subject: EDEP
title: Nonparametric Methods for Behavioral Science
description: Conditions for valid applications of nonparametric statistical techniques in education and behavioral sciences; theoretical and methodological perspectives.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Educational Research
description: Fundamental design and evaluation procedures in educational research. Topics include an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research, the review of literature, developing research questions, research design, instrumentation, data collection, and writing a research proposal.
prerequisites: EDEP 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B or higher) or consent.

subject: EDEP
title: Graduate Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Graduate level introduction to educational psychology theories, research, and topics.

subject: EDEP
title: Multilevel Modeling for Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data
description: Theories and applications of multilevel model to analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal data. Topics include two-level and three-level models, growth models, and multilevel logistic regression.
prerequisites: EDEP 604, PSY 610, PSY 612 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or consent.

subject: EDEP
title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education
description: Introduction to methods of qualitative research in education. (Meets PhD common core requirement.) (Cross-listed as EDEA 604)

subject: EDEP
title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
description: Measurement and psychometric theories and applications using psychometric programs. Topics include classical test theory, reliability, validity, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, item bias, and item response theory.

subject: EDEP
title: Categorical Data Analysis
description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables; analysis of contingency tables, loglinear models, introduction to generalized linear models for binary, nominal, ordinal, and count outcomes in cross-sectional and longitudinal data sets.

subject: EDEP
title: Structural Equation Modeling
description: Theories and applications to test models with manifest and latent variables. Topics include path analysis, factor analysis, latent variable model, multi-group analysis, latent means model, and other advanced topics in SEM.

subject: EDEP
title: Psychometric Methods
description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, and current issues in psychometrics.
prerequisites: EDEP 604 (with a minimum grade of B+) or consent.

subject: EDEP
title: Adolescence and Education
description: Discussion-based course presenting an overview of educational psychology applied to teaching adolescents, including theory and research on human learning, adolescent development and its social context, and student assessment.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Program Evaluation
description: Introduction to concepts and issues related to program evaluation. Topics include preparing for an evaluation, formative and summative uses, and qualitative and quantitative design approaches. A-F only.

subject: EDEP
title: Development and Learning
description: Theories and research on learning and development and their educational applications. Analysis of how learning and development are interrelated.

subject: EDEP
title: Social Context of Learning
description: Analysis of the social context in the learning process and education, including peer, family, community, and cultural influences.

subject: EDEP
title: Models of Cognitive Learning
description: Cognitive models of knowledge acquisition, organization, and utilization; theory and research relating learning and cognition to interactive instructional models.

subject: EDEP
title: Instructional Psychology
description: Application of learning theory and cognitive skills training in instructional settings.

subject: EDEP
title: Social Cognition and Competence
description: Systematic analysis of social reasoning abilities conjunctive with or prerequisite to effective social interaction in educational settings.

subject: EDEP
title: Capstone Project in Educational Psychology
description: To be taken in the final semester or the second to last semester to complete the certificate. Students are expected to integrate, extend, critique and apply knowledge learned in the certificate program. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: EDEP
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable ten times.

subject: EDEP
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable seven times.

subject: EDEP
title: Educational Research Methods
description: Research techniques and thesis development.

subject: EDEP
title: Practicum in Educational Psychology
description: Supervised practicum in teaching or program evaluation as each is reflected by professional activities of the members of the faculty. Repeatable six times.

subject: EDEP
title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
description: Analysis of psychology of adult learner; forces that affect learning in dynamics of individual, group, and organizational behavior; concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities. (Cross-listed as EDEA 745 and NURS 745)

subject: EDEP
title: Seminar in Educational Psychology
description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology. Repeatable nine times. Seminar may be repeated for credit as topics vary.

subject: EDEP
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECE
title: Electrical Engineering Skills
description: Electrical engineering subjects in a skill acquisition context at the freshman level. Learning, creative problem solving, brainstorming, technical information assimilation, and presentation skills development. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Engineering Computation
description: Engineering problem solving using MATLAB. Basic programming concepts include input/output, branching, looping, functions, file input/output, and data structures such as arrays and structures. Matrix operations for solving linear equations. Engineering computations and visualization. ECE and CENG majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Programming for Engineers
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to computer programming and modern computing environments with an emphasis on algorithm and program design, implementation, and debugging. Includes a hands-on laboratory to develop and practice programming skills. BENG, CE, CENG, ECE, ME, PREN, CNST, and ENGS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Freshman Project
description: Freshman level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. This project provides early student entry into ECE hands-on project activity providing practical skills, ECE subject exposure and experience. Second semester freshman standing required. Repeatable unlimited times. CENG, ECE, and PREN majors only. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Object Oriented Programming
description: Second programming for computer engineers. System programming language, such as C. Object-oriented programming paradigm, definition and use of classes, fundamentals of object-oriented design, such as C++. Common data structures. Common searching and sorting algorithms. CEE, ECE, ME, PREN majors only. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Basic Circuit Analysis I
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Linear passive circuits, time domain analysis, transient and steady-state responses, phasors, impedance and admittance; power and energy, frequency responses, resonance. BENG, CE, CENG, ECE, ME, PREN, and ENGS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253 (or concurrent), and PHYS 272 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Basic Circuit Analysis II
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Laplace transforms and their application to circuits, Fourier transforms and their applications to circuits, frequency selective circuits, introduction to and design of active filters, convolution, and state space analysis of circuits. A-F only.
prerequisites: ECE 211, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the design of digital systems with an emphasis on design methods and the implementation and use of fundamental digital components.
prerequisites: ECE 160 or ECE 110 or ICS 111 or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Sophomore Project
description: Sophomore level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. Repeatable unlimited times. CENG, ECE, and PREN majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ENGR 296)

subject: ECE
title: Signal and Systems Analysis
description: Discrete-time and continuous time signals and systems, linear systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transform, sampling.
prerequisites: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I
description: Semiconductor structures, operating principles and characteristics of diodes and amplifying devices. Their application as circuit elements in building basic digital, analog, and

subject: AMST
title: Material Culture
description: Physical artifacts considered as documents of American cultural and regional development.

subject: AMST
title: Environment and Society
description: Technological development in cultural perspective; its relation to the American environment, science, capitalism, public policy, and values.

subject: AMST
title: Mass Media
description: Appraisal of major media of communications in American society with attention to political, educational, cultural, and ethical implications.

subject: AMST
title: Technologies of War and Media
description: Critical examination of the relationship between war and media with particular attention to the overlapping histories of technologies of perception and destruction in the modern era and to the military-entertainment complex today.

subject: AMST
title: Public History and Commemoration
description: Approaches to public presentations of history and examination of various ways in which historic memory is constructed in sites such as museums, memorials, and theme parks.

subject: AMST
title: American Punishment
description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 638)

subject: AMST
title: Writing for Publication
description: Advanced seminar designed to convert graduate research projects into publishable scholarly articles. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: AMST
title: Revolutions and Social Movements
description: Examines the role of social movements in transforming American society and culture.

subject: AMST
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only) (Cross-listed as ANTH 645 and ARCH 645)

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: Social/Cultural/ Intellectual
description: Readings and research on American social and intellectual history. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as HIST 639B)

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: Business/Labor/ Technology
description: Readings and research on American business, labor, and technological history. Repeatable one time. (Crosslisted as HIST 639K)

subject: AMST
title: American Intellectual Traditions
description: Examination of intellectual figures and movements in American history.

subject: AMST
title: Field Mastery
description: Prepares students to achieve specialization in an American Studies-related academic field. Repeatable two times with different contents. A-F only.

subject: AMST
title: Film in America
description: Examination of various roles of motion picture film in America with particular respect to art form, cultural artifact, document, and myth.

subject: AMST
title: Arts in America: Modern to PostModern
description: Survey of the literature of the field.

subject: AMST
title: Transpacific Studies
description: Critical analysis of regional formation in and across the Pacific and the role of the U.S. therein; migrations within and across the Pacific; political, military, economic, cultural, and environmental dynamics of transpacific exchanges.

subject: AMST
title: Globalization and Transnationalism
description: Examines the socioeconomic and cultural meanings of globalization and transnationalism. Emphasis on how the deployment and flows of power beyond the nation-state have an impact on regional, national, and/ or local communities and cultures.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: America and the World
description: Historical and contemporary issues in America’s global relationships.

subject: AMST
title: Comparative Methods in American Studies
description: Examines approaches to American studies that use comparison as a primary method. Comparison of histories, institutions, of phenomena between the U.S. and another country as well as among communities in the U.S. (Every 2-3 years)
prerequisites: Graduate standing only. Co-requisite: AMST 600 or AMST 601 or AMST 602, or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Curation and Museums: Practice Meets Theory
description: Seminar explores the history, evolution, and contemporary movement towards indigenous curation within museums, emphasis on the Americas and Oceania, as shaped by colonialism, globalization, multiculturalism, selfdetermination, and nationalism. (Fall only)

subject: AMST
title: 20th Century U.S. Literature
description: Selected works of 20th-century literature as cultural documents.

subject: AMST
title: African American Literature
description: Cultural and social imagination of blacks and whites as revealed in literature, poetry, and drama.

subject: AMST
title: Elements of Style
description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present. (Cross-listed as ARCH 679)

subject: AMST
title: Historic Building Technology
description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600–c.1960. (Cross-listed as ARCH 680)

subject: AMST
title: Vernacular Architecture
description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes, and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas. (Cross-listed as ARCH 650)

subject: AMST
title: Museums: Theory, History, Practice
description: History and theory of museums and related institutions (art galleries, historic houses, zoos, parks). Relationship between museums, collections, and communities. Introduction to governance, planning, legal, and ethical concerns.

subject: AMST
title: Museums and Collections
description: Work of museums and professionals (registrars, collections managers, conservators, curators and others) in the care of collections, interpretive studies of museum displays; field trips.

subject: AMST
title: Museums and Education
description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects. (Cross-listed as EDCS 685)

subject: AMST
title: Museum Studies Practicum
description: Applies coursework in museum studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. A-F only.
prerequisites: Museum studies certificate students only. Pre: consent.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Studies Practicum
description: Applies course work in Indigenous studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: AMST
title: Research Seminar
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies graduate courses; emphasis upon research methods. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: AMST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: AMST
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: AMST
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANAT
title: (Alpha) Unit VII Anatomy Electives
description: Advanced study of human anatomy by dissection and individual observation of surgical procedures. (C) topics in reproductive biology. Repeatable two times. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532; or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: Independent Study in Anatomy
description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology. CR/NC only. Repeatable three times.

subject: ANAT
title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as KRS 603)
prerequisites: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.
degrees: Biomedical Sciences - Anatomy/Reproductive Biology and Physiology

subject: ANAT
title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as KRS 604)
prerequisites: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.
degrees: Biomedical Sciences - Anatomy/Reproductive Biology and Physiology

subject: ANAT
title: Human Embryology
description: Systematic study of human development, including implantation, placentation, basics of development of each organ system with reference to pertinent congenital anomalies and their surgical repair. Recommended: gross anatomy course.

subject: ANAT
title: Seminar in Anatomy Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses in anatomical sciences, development and evaluation of exams, experience in teaching with audiovisual/ computer aids. Open to graduate students in physiology or KRS. CR/NC only. Repeatable eight times, up to 32 credits.

subject: ANAT
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANAT
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANAT
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Animals, and Agriculture
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to animal agriculture, animal science, and the use of animals by humans. Ethics and importance of human use of animals in agriculture are emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Principles and Practices of Animal Science
description: DB Biology, behavior, and management of animals of economic and social import

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Economics
description: One semester survey of the principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics to enable students in all disciplines to understand current economic events.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: An introduction to macroeconomics–the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: An introduction to macroeconomics–the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

subject: ECON
title: Data Analysis and Visualization
description: Develops basic techniques of data analysis and visualization. Introduces sources of economic data; methods of preparing data from various file/data formats for analysis; methods of visualization: bubble plots, scatterplot matrices, heatmaps, hexbins, rug plots, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts used to study the overall macroeconomy and policies that affect it. Study the determinants of national income and long-run growth; causes and consequences of unemployment, inflation, and business cycle fluctuations; determination of foreign exchange rates and current account imbalances, and the role of government policy in various settings.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Microeconomics
description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory. Learn to use economic reasoning to understand the social consequences of decisions made by individual consumers, producers, and governments. Analyze the nature of market outcomes under alternative market structures, and further discuss possible welfare-improving government policies when markets fail to be efficient. Special attention is paid to the analysis of strategic behavior and markets with public goods and externalities.

subject: ECON
title: The Economy of Hawai‘i
description: Descriptive understanding of the history of development of Hawai‘i’s economy; current economic problems; future prospects. Emphasizes the written communication of the intuition behind economic concepts in practice in Hawai‘i.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: The Japanese Economy
description: Analysis of Japan’s growth past and present. Does Japan’s economy look different in terms of its international trade structure, industrial structure, labor market, savings patterns, government policies, etc.? Does it matter?

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development. (Cross-listed as TIM 320)
prerequisites: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131; consent.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Statistics
description: Basic elements; descriptive statistics, probability, inference, distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and correlation analysis.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Global Climate Change
description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation. (Cross-listed as SUST 332)
prerequisites: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131, or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources. (Cross-listed as SUST 336)

subject: ECON
title: Financial Markets and Institutions
description: The determination of asset prices; the risk and term structure of interest rates; efficient markets hypothesis; risk management and financial derivatives, asymmetric information models of financial market structure, innovation, regulation and deregulation; and financial crises.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Comparative Economic History
description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions. (Cross-listed as HIST 340)

subject: ECON
title: The History of Economic Thought
description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy. (Cross-listed as HIST 342)

subject: ECON
title: Sustainable Development
description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawai‘i. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls. (Cross-listed as SUST 350)
prerequisites: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131, or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Network Economics
description: Fundamental questions about the connections in the social, economic, and technological worlds. Topics include: matching markets, traffic, financial and social networks; and the political and economic consequences of the internet and other large networks.

subject: ECON
title: Games and Economic Behavior
description: Introduces students to the study of strategic behavior with applications to economics, business, and public policy. Simple economic models of strategic decision making are used to analyze provision of public goods; competition, cooperation, and coordination among firms; bargaining between employers and labor unions; international trade negotiations; reputation as a competitive advantage, and others.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Economics
description: Nature and causes of environmental degradation/economic solutions, with emphasis on relevant ethical issues and decision-making. Topics include air and water pollution, toxic waste, deforestation, soil erosion, biodiversity, global warming, and sustainable development.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Seminar: Women and International Development
description: Women’s role, status, work and treatment in the Third World; economic development, changing work/family roles, and improvement/ deterioration in gender equity across the Third World; global feminization of poverty; efforts to promote gender equity. Open to non-majors. (Cross-listed as WGSS 361)
prerequisites: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Trade Policy and Globalization
description: Political economy of the world trading system. Case studies of trade cooperation and conflict under the World Trade Organization and other institutions. Future challenges, including investment policies, environmental and labor standards.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130 or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Internship for Economics
description: Economics majors and minors work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. Students combine academic work with practical experience. Repeatable two times.

subject: ECON
title: Cooperative Education
description: Economics majors and minors, under the supervision of faculty members, work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations.

subject: ACC
title: Income Taxation
description: Examines federal income tax concepts, such as gross income, exclusions, deductions, exemptions, and tax credits, especially for sole proprietors. Introduces taxation of property transactions. Development of professional writing skills is integral to this course.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 200 and ACC 210, or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better).

subject: ACC
title: Taxation of Business Entities
description: A survey of the general concepts, rules, and practices involved in the taxation of sole-proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, and subchapter S corporations.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 401 with C- or better.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Accounting systems analysis, control and design in manual and computerized environments. Knowledge and skills of information technology for auditing AIS systems. Hands-on experience with microcomputers and a computerized accounting system. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 323 (with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 (with C or better).

subject: ACC
title: Law for the Accountant
description: Intensive study of areas of law of importance to accountants. Particular attention is given to principles of law relating to contracts, sales, commercial paper, secured transactions, property, legal entities, agency, securities, and accountant’s legal liability.

subject: ACC
title: Advanced Financial Accounting
description: Accounting topics relating to consolidation requirements and introduction to the fundamentals of fund accounting, including the general fund, restricted funds, debt service funds, enterprise funds, general long-term account group, general fixed assets accounting group, and accounting entries for encumbrances.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 323 with C- or better.

subject: ACC
title: Special Topics in Accounting
description: Addresses current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits.

subject: ACC
title: Auditing
description: Auditing concepts including standards, objectives and ethics for external auditors. Emphasis on reporting standards, internal control, evidence, statistical sampling, IT audits and assurance. Development of professional writing skills is an integral part of this course.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 323 and ACC 409, both with C- or better.

subject: ACC
title: Forensic Accounting
description: Theoretical and real life aspects of forensic accounting. Includes discussions of the legal environment, types of forensic engagements such as, lost earnings, business valuations, fraud, and real world forensic cases. Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Capstone (Alpha)
description: Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Lectures, discussions, case analysis. (B) managerial-tax-ethics; emphasis on instruction in writing; (C) financial-auditing-accounting information systems. ACC majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 401 (or concurrent) and ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (B); ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (C).

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-Audit and Attestation
description: Auditing and Attestation (AUD) section covers the entire auditing process, including auditing procedures, generally accepted auditing standards, standards related to attest engagements, and the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct. CR/NC only.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-The Business Environment and Concepts
description: The Business Environment and Concepts (BEC) section focuses on business concepts and the significance of a CPA’s professional duties and responsibilities within the larger context of the business environment. CR/NC only.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-The Financial Accounting and Reporting
description: The (FAR) section focuses on U.S. GAAP, including concepts and standards for financial statements, typical items in financial statements, specific types of transactions and events, accounting and reporting for governmental and other entities. CR/NC only.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-The Regulation
description: The Regulation section focuses on federal taxation, especially taxation of business entities; individuals, and property taxation, but also tests on business law, business ethics, and professional and legal responsibilities. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: ACC
title: International Corporate Governance
description: Understanding of complex and critical issues of international corporate governance, financial reporting, and ethical conduct. Includes corporate governance in the U.S., major European markets, and Asia. Emphasis on internal and external stakeholders, regulators, and gatekeepers. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Theory and Development
description: History and theoretical background of accounting standards. Including accounting theories, formulating and testing theories; scientific, pragmatic, syntactic and semantic theories; normative and positive theories. Literature supportive and critical of accounting theories and standards.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 323 with C- or better, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Information and Assurance and Analytics
description: Focus on auditing processes, standards, and guidance specific to IT risks. Exposure to advanced IT audit software and its practical application and real world IT audit issues.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 418 with C- or better, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Global Accounting
description: Theory and fundamental causes of international variations in accounting. Special emphasis on problems such variations create for financial reporting, control, and decision-making within multinational business enterprises.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 323 with C- or better, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting and Tax Research
description: In depth examination of tax and accounting research, IRC, and SEC procedures. Extensive practice in issue identification, reading and analyzing primary authority, and communicating results. Credit not given for both 606 and 625.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 401 or ACC 584 with C- or better, orientation program, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Tax of Partners/Partnerships
description: Examines advanced topics in federal taxation of partners and partnerships regarding the contribution, operation, and distribution from partnerships and transfers of partnership interests.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 407 with C- or better, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Advanced Public Sector Accounting
description: Provides the tools necessary for understanding the principles of fiscal accountability and reporting in governmental and not-for-profit organizations. ACC majors only.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 415 with C- or better, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Estate and Gift Taxation and Planning
description: Examines estate and gift tax provisions and basic estate planning techniques to save taxes and avoid probate. Overviews generation-skipping transfer taxes and income taxes on estates and trusts.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 401 with C- or better, or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Multijurisdictional Taxation
description: Examines international, state, and local tax issues. Topics include U.S. International taxation of in- and out-bound transactions, sourcing of income and deductions and nexus.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 401 with C- or better.

subject: ACC
title: Financial Statements Analysis
description: Analyses of a firm’s profitability, liquidity, and solvency using ratios and common size financial statements. Students are expected to find strengths and weaknesses of the firm based on their analysis. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Data Analytics for Accountants
description: Introduction to visual analytics. Tableau and Power BI for Excel. Introduction to data processing and blending, data visualization and other visualization techniques. Introduction to PowerQuery, PowerPivot, PowerView, and PowerMap. Repeatable two times, up to three credits.

subject: ACC
title: Analysis and Decision-Making
description: Integrates learning through analysis and communication of comprehensive business problems. Stresses research, critical thinking, and analytical and communication skills applied to contemporary accounting and tax issues.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 625 with C- or better (or concurrent), no waiver. Co-requisite: ACC 648.

subject: ACC
title: Current Topics in Accounting
description: Concentration on current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Internship
description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Necessary evaluation reports and meetings with faculty advisor required. ACC majors only.

subject: ACC
title: Thesis Research
description: Required for Plan A candidates only; six credit hours required, one must be taken during semester that degree is being awarded. Repeatable up to six credits. ACC majors only. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.
prerequisites: Pre: MAcc student and School of Accountancy Director approval.

subject: ACC
title: Financial Accounting Research
description: Provides an overview of financial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. Repeatable one time. A-F only. PhD students in Business Administration only. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Managerial Accounting Research
description: Provides an overview of managerial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. A-F only. PhD students in Business Administration only. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Behavioral Accounting
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in behavioral accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Accounting Information Systems
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in accounting information systems topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only. A-F only.

subject: BOT
title: Sophomore Seminar
description: Presentations by faculty highlighting research in tropical ecosystems. Topics include alien species, biodiversity, ecosystem services, ethnobotany, marine ecology, plant-animal interactions, and systematics of Hawaiian species. Assigned reading and writing exercises from papers in current journals. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity
description: DB. Significance of evolutionary trends in the plant world, including reproductive, morphological, and life history adaptations by algae, fungi, and vascular plants.
prerequisites: Pre: 101 or college general biology. Co-requisite: 201L.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Lab exercises in the morphology and systematics of land plants, fungi, and algae.

subject: BOT
title: Biostatistics
description: FQ. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R. A-F only. (Cross-listed as BIOL 220)
prerequisites: Pre: 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam.

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Ethics
description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 310)
prerequisites: Pre: any DB course or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Conservation Biology
description: DB. Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-inpractice in Hawai‘i and elsewhere. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 313)

subject: BOT
title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
description: DY. Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 313L)

subject: BOT
title: Ecology
description: DB. General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment. A-F only. (Cross-listed as BIOL 305)

subject: BOT
title: Field Botany
description: DB DY. Combined lecturelaboratory with intensive field experience for observational and experimental field work in native/impacted Hawaiian ecosystems. Field experience typically held during spring break. Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine habitats considered. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Resource Management and Conservation in Hawai‘i
description: DB. Management of native Hawaiian organisms and terrestrial ecosystems with particular attention to strategies, planning, research, and management actions necessary to control alien influences and promote native species.

subject: BOT
title: Tropical forest Ecology
description: DB. Introduction to the ecological processes and principles of tropical ecosystems, and to conservation issues facing tropical forests, with a particular emphasis on the neotropics. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172, or BOT 101; and BIOL 265.

subject: BOT
title: Senior Seminar
description: Current research themes in botany presented in discussion format; reading current research papers. Oral presentations of primary research. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: BOT majors only. Senior standing and consent.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Form and Function
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lecture/laboratory to examine the anatomy, physiology, morphology, and functional ecology of plants. Labs will develop skills in microscopy, experimental techniques for studying plant physiology, and basic functional ecology. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: BOT
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: DB. Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts. (Spring only) (Crosslisted as BIOL 430 and TPSS 432)
prerequisites: Pre: (201, BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as BIOL 430L and TPSS 432L)
prerequisites: Pre: (430 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C. or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Medical Ethnobotany
description: DB. Survey and theory of plants used as medicines, cultural perspectives of herbal medicine, and the botanical/ chemical basis of allopathic and naturopathic medicine. Lecture/discussion, term paper or project.

subject: BOT
title: Ethnoecology and Conservation
description: DB. Ecological implications of cultural uses of plants. Examines the biological basis for, and ecological effects of traditional and local resource management systems. (Crosslisted as SUST 445)
prerequisites: Pre: BOT 305 or BIOL 265/265L or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: DS. (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork. (Cross-listed as SUST 446)

subject: BOT
title: Plant-Animal Interactions
description: DB. Interdependence of plants and animals, emphasizing the influence of animals on plant fitness and evolution. Topics include pollination, fruit/seed dispersal, herbivory, and ant-plant mutualisms.
prerequisites: Pre: 201 or 305 or BIOL 265 or BIOL 305.

subject: BOT
title: ‘Āina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.
prerequisites: Pre: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356.

subject: BOT
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
prerequisites: Pre: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/ SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356.

subject: BOT
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356.

subject: BOT
title: Systematics of Vascular Plants
description: DB DY. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) “Hands-on” experience with Hawai‘i’s unique tropical flora; emphasis on recognition and identification of vascular plant families and the principles and methodologies that define them; evolution of biodiversity.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Ecology
description: DB DY. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ecological principles and process that determine patterns of plant distribution and abundance. Lectures cover theory and examples from primary literature. Labs cover study design, descriptive and experimental techniques, field skills, and data analysis and interpretation. A-F only.

subject: BOT
title: Algal Diversity and Evolution
description: DB DY. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of algal diversity, structure, and evolution. Identification of common Hawaiian algae. Develops written communication skills with significant attention paid to developing writing skills and emphasis on writing instruction.
prerequisites: Pre: one of 101, BIOL 172, MICR 351, ZOOL 101; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Grant Writing and Your Career in Science
description: Scientific grant writing from inception through management to completion; students will write a DDIG and participate in a panel. Professional skills including “rules,” job applications, interviews, transitioning from graduate student to academic or non-academic job. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: current standing as a graduate student, or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Foundations of Current Botany I
description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in history of science, plant diversity, plant interactions with the environment, and plant integration. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Pre: graduate standing in BOT or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Foundations of Current Botany II
description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in ecology, plant interactions with other plants or animals, and ecosystem functioning. (Spring only)
prerequisites: BOT majors only. Pre: graduate standing in BOT or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Darwin’s Origin of Species
description: Study and discussion of Charles Darwin’s Origin of Species, 1st edition 1859, and related current literature. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: Pre: BA or BS in BOT, BIOL, GEOL, or related field; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Graduate Research Skills
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Survey of major research areas in the botanical sciences with emphasis upon research opportunities in Hawai‘i and an overview of 1) skills needed by botanical researchers including writing scientific papers and proposals, practicing ethical research procedures, and collection of specimens; and 2) equipment used by botanical researchers including c

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar in Educational Foundations-Selected Topics
description: Multi-disciplinary (historical, philosophical, social/cultural and comparative/international focus on topical issues in education. (B) general; (C) leadership and governance in education; (D) educational reform; (E) foundations of teaching; (F) foundations of curriculum; (G) globalization in education; (H) moral political education. Repeatable one time for (H). A-F only for (H).

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Comparative/ International Education
description: Introduction to basic methods of comparative studies, focusing on schooling, but also treating broader educational issues. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Topics in Comparative Education
description: Educational institutions, structures, processes, policies, and problems viewed within the context of political, social, and cultural milieus. Geographic region or theme focus. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Educational Policy Studies
description: Examines theories and models of educational policy and policy-making and the contribution of policy analysis to the policy-making and change processes. A-F only. (Crosslisted as EDEA 675)

subject: EDEF
title: The Politics of Education
description: Examination of the ways in which education can be viewed as political, arising from its connection to the larger political system including local, state, and federal governments. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEA 676)

subject: EDEF
title: Approaches to Educational Inquiry
description: Overview of different research methods in educational inquiry with an opportunity to explore through practice one or more methods (ex: case study, interviewing, narrative construction, practitioner inquiry. Preparation for MEd or PhD proposals.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar on Race, Law, and Education
description: Introduction to educational law and the way it relates to issues of race and ethnicity. Particular focus on how the U.S. courts have dealt with the question of educational inequality in a multiracial/multiethnic society. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
description: Focuses on the interplay of class, race, gender and ethnicity in school and community settings. Social praxis, educational reform and policy are considered. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Education and World Order
description: Focuses on the challenges educators face in identifying appropriate pedagogical frameworks and practices in global education that address the impact of globalization in our society today. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: International Development Education
description: Introduction to international development education in Asian and Pacific nations. Students explore links between education and development. Emphasis is on cross-cultural perception of development.

subject: EDEF
title: Environmental Education
description: Focuses on the development of an ecological consciousness through a cultural and environmental approach to teaching and learning in schooling and everyday life.

subject: EDEF
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDEF
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDEF
title: Education and Social Change
description: Study of classical and contemporary theories of social change as these relate to school, the profession of teaching, planning of change, and social stability.

subject: EDEF
title: Recent History of American Education
description: Contemporary American education in recent historical perspective; focuses on the educational changes brought about by WW II, the Cold War, civil rights and other social movements. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: History of American Higher Education
description: Genesis and evolution of college and university from

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar on the Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
description: Examination of social, political, and cultural issues affecting educational policy with special emphasis on methods of inquiry and theoretical constructs. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Advanced Seminar in Philosophy of Education
description: Advanced studies in philosophical inquiry. Examination of philosophically based methods of analysis and interpretation and their influence in educational research and practice. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar in History of Education
description: Aspects of the history of education. Application of historiography to educational problems and policy. Repeatable with different content. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar on the Educational System
description: Examination of the structure and dynamics of educational system. Particular focus on how educational policy interacts with principles that explain educational system behavior. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEA 767)

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar in Comparative/International Education
description: Advanced reading, research and writing in selected topics dealing with comparative and international education, including such themes as policy studies, minority education and educational reform. A-F only.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Teaching as a Career
description: An experience-based introduction to teaching as a career. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: DS Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research. Develops knowledge and written communication skills through an introduction to classroom, assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing. (Cross-listed as PSY 301)

subject: EDEP
title: Self-Regulated Learning
description: Theory and use of self-regulated learning strategies in academic contexts.

subject: EDEP
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual reading or research.

subject: EDEP
title: Fundamentals of Research in Education
description: DS Introduction to the methodology of systematic study of problems in education: principles of research design, data processing, technical writing, and evaluation of research proposals and reports.

subject: EDEP
title: Seminar in Contemporary Perspectives in Educational Psychology
description: DS In-depth analysis of contemporary issues in education from the theoretical and methodological perspectives of the faculty in educational psychology. Focuses on oral communication and intensive writing skills. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEP
title: Student Assessment
description: Introduction to basic concepts and issues in assessment and measurement, development of formative and summative assessment procedures, descriptive statistics, scales of measurement, and standardizing testing.

subject: EDEP
title: Introductory Statistics
description: DS Introduction to concepts and logics of statistical reasoning and statistical literacy. Topics include descriptive statistics, sampling distribution, and inferential statistics such as z-test, t-tests, correlation, and one-way ANOVA.

subject: EDEP
title: Human Motivation and Education
description: Application of motivation theory and research to understanding and increasing human motivation for education.

subject: EDEP
title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: DS Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research. Repeatable to six credit hours. (Crosslisted as PSY 489)

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods
description: Introductory graduate-level statistics in education and social sciences. Topics on descriptive and inferential statistics including central tendency, variability, sampling distribution, z-test, t-test, correlation, simple linear regression, and one-way ANOVA. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: EDEP
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models. (Cross-listed as EDEA 608 and SOC 608)

subject: EDEP
title: Design and Analysis of Psychological Experiments
description: Analysis of variance and other models of assessing results of experiments. Relation of analysis to design.

subject: EDEP
title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.
prerequisites: 601 or EDEA 629 (with a grade of B+), or consent.

subject: EDEP
title: Multivariate Methods
description: Builds on prior knowledge of multiple regression and will include applications of MANOVA, canonical correlation, logistic regression, discriminant function analysis, cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling, and mixture models.

subject: EDEP
title: Nonparametric Methods for Behavioral Science
description: Conditions for valid applications of nonparametric statistical techniques in education and behavioral sciences; theoretical and methodological perspectives.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Educational Research
description: Fundamental design and evaluation procedures in educational research. Topics include an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research, the review of literature, developing research questions, research design, instrumentation, data collection, and writing a research proposal.
prerequisites: 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B or higher) or consent.

subject: EDEP
title: Graduate Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Graduate level introduction to educational psychology theories, research, and topics.

subject: EDEP
title: Multilevel Modeling for Cross-Sectional and Lo

subject: ACC
title: Managerial Accounting Research
description: Provides an overview of managerial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Behavioral Accounting
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in behavioral accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Accounting Information Systems
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in accounting information systems topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Auditing and International Accounting
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in Auditing and International Accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in an area of accounting under the direction of faculty member(s). Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: AS
title: Foundations of the United States Air Force
description: Study of the total force structure, strategic offensive and defensive, general purpose, and aerospace support forces of the Air Force in the contemporary world. A-F only.

subject: AS
title: Initial Military Training I
description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps. Course is open to all majors. CR/NC only.

subject: AS
title: Foundations of the United States Air Force
description: Continuation of 101. A-F only

subject: AS
title: Initial Military Training II
description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps. Course is open to all majors. CR/NC only.

subject: AS
title: Evolution of USAF Air and Space Power
description: Study of Air Force heritage, Quality Air Force principles, ethics, and an introduction to leadership and group leadership problems. Application of written and verbal communication skills is included. A-F only.

subject: AS
title: Field Training Preparation I
description: Laboratory consists of preparing second-year AFROTC cadets with the skills needed to successfully complete AFROTC Field Training. Students will learn basic military skills, Field Training skills, and participate in physical fitness training. CR/NC only.

subject: AS
title: Evolution of USAF Air and Space Power
description: Continuation of 201. A-F only.

subject: AS
title: Field Training Preparation II
description: Continuation of 201L. CR/NC only.

subject: AS
title: Leadership Laboratory
description: Laboratory on the basic skills of leadership and followership. Lab includes application of leadership/followership skills, various field trips to military installations, group projects, and physical training. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: AS
title: Leadership Laboratory II
description: Continuation of 251L. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. Sophomore standing or higher. Open to all majors. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: AS
title: Air Force Leadership Studies
description: Focuses on an examination of ethical Air Force leadership and management concepts. Continued emphasis is given to the refinement of ethical thought through writing and debate. A-F only.

subject: AS
title: Intermediate Cadet Leader I
description: Laboratory consists of demonstration of leadership and management skills needed to successfully function as an Air Force officer. Instruction will include lessons covering planning, organizational and communication skills, and the ability to use available resources to complete an assigned task. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent.

subject: AS
title: Air Force Leadership Studies II
description: Continuation of 301. Focuses on an examination of Air Force leadership and management concepts. Continued emphasis is given to the refinement of both written and oral communicative skills. A-F only.

subject: AS
title: Intermediate Cadet Leader II
description: Continuation of 301L. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent.

subject: AS
title: National Security Affairs
description: Study of the national security process, regional studies, advanced leadership, ethics, and Air Force doctrine. Special focus placed on preparation for active duty and current issues affecting professionalism. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Pre: must have completed 301 and 302; or consent.

subject: AS
title: Senior Cadet Leader I
description: Laboratory consists of providing prospective Air Force officers opportunities to continue to develop leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills. Instruction will include preparation for active duty. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: must have completed 301 and 302L; or consent.

subject: AS
title: National Security Affairs
description: Continuation of 401. A-F only.

subject: AS
title: Senior Cadet Leader II
description: Laboratory consists of providing prospective Air Force officers opportunities to continue to develop leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills. Instruction will include preparation for active duty. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: must have completed 301 and 302L; or consent.

subject: AREC
title: Biosystems Modeling
description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system modes, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models. (Crosslisted as BE 638)
prerequisites: Pre: one of MATH 215, MATH 241, MATH 251A; or consent.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: AREC
title: Econometrics I
description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.
prerequisites: Pre: NREM 310 or ECON 321, and MATH 241; or consent.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: AREC
title: Econometrics II
description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference, and forecasting of economic models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series. (Cross-listed as ECON 629)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: ASL
title: Elementary American Sign Language I
description: Development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Elementary American Sign Language II
description: Continued development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Intermediate American Sign Language I
description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Intermediate American Sign Language II
description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Advanced American Sign Language I
description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL). (Fall only)

subject: ASL
title: Advanced American Sign Language II
description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL). (Spring only)

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies
description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing through analyses of contemporary American culture and to the main themes and approaches used in American studies and the humanities.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies Writing
description: Introduction to different types of college level writing and information literacy with a focus on American culture and society. A-F only.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: Examines America’s role in

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology (Alpha)
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational. Repeatable two times.

subject: ANTH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only) (Cross-listed as AMST 645 and ARCH 645).

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology
description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology with a focus on South Africa and its relevance for the Pacific and U.S. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence.

subject: ANTH
title: Advances in Extinctions
description: To delve deeply into the primary literature that focuses on the subjects of extinction and conservation broadly speaking, with particular emphasis on the 6 mass extinction events, including the Anthropocene. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Paleoanthropology of Asia
description: Survey of the Asian paleoanthropological record, particularly in its paleoenvironmental setting; Out of Africa I; modern human origins. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: graduate standing and relevant background in anthropology or related field

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Perspectives on Southeast Asia
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia, and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, india, Australia, and Oceania.
prerequisites: background in archaeology or Southeast Asian history or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Aid
description: Examines ideologies of development, humanitarian, and global health interventions from an anthropological perspective. Explores the disjuncture between discourses that portrays global aid as easing suffering and those that accuse it of maintaining relationships of domination. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Hawaiian Archaeology
description: An advanced theoretical and methodological examination of past and current archaeological research in the Hawaiian Islands. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Data Analysis
description: Advanced introduction to the fundamental principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies, and practices of modern medicine. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology Field Methods
description: (5 7-hr Lab) Laboratory and field training in the principles and practice of methods of archaeology—survey, mapping, excavation, conservation. Repeatable one time, up to 12 credits.

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Household Archaeology
description: Focus on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between the households that comprised ancient communities, and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change. Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Archaeology Practicum
description: Applies course work in archaeology to handson activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. MA track in Applied Archaeology students only. Repeatable one time, up to 12 credits.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Method and Theory in Hawaiian Archaeology
description: Graduate seminar focused on method and theory in the practice of applied archaeology in Hawai‘i. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures. Graduate students only or consent. (Cross-listed as ARCH 676 and PLAN 676)

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Cultural Anthropology
description: Theory, methods, and results of application of cultural anthropological concepts to practical problems. Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Cultural Anthropology Practicum
description: Applies course work in cultural anthropology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Repeatable one time. ANTH majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Professional Skills Develop in Anthropology
description: Seminar prepares graduate students for entry into profession, including employment opportunities, research, presentations, ethics and outreach. Required of all Plan B students.

subject: ANTH
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable nine times, up to 12 credits.

subject: ANTH
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable nine times, up to 12 credits.

subject: ANTH
title: Seminar in Research Methods in Cultural Anthropology
description: Ethnographic research methods. Introduction to the approaches and techniques of participatory research, including the collection, analysis, and interpretation of social and cultural data. Politics and ethics of research practice. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: graduate standing in anthropology or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Seminar in Research Design and Proposal Writing
description: Research design and proposal writing. For students preparing for advanced research.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Japan
description: Japan examined through three dimensions of cultural anthropology: cultural/symbolic, social/organizational, and individual/psychological. Selected topics analyzed and interpreted in terms of conjunctions of these dimensions.

subject: ANTH
title: Research Seminar (Alpha)
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological. Repeatable nine times.

subject: ANTH
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable nine times.

subject: ARAB
title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
description: HSL Designed to provide students with basic knowledge of Modern Standard Arabic. Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language, as well as formal spoken Arabic.

subject: ARAB
title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
description: HSL Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language as well as formal spoken Arabic. It introduces a wide range of situation-based texts and topics that build vocabulary, grammar, and general communicative competence.

subject: ARAB
title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
description: HSL Designed for students who have successfully completed a year of Elementary Arabic. Focus is on acquisition of more complex grammatical structures, expanding vocabulary, and developing competence in a wide range of communicative situations. (Fall only)

subject: ARAB
title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
description: HSL Designed for students who have successfully completed three semesters of Arabic. Focus is on intensive practice of interactive functional skills such as listening comprehension and fundamental conversation strategies.

subject: ARAB
title: Third-Level Arabic I
description: Develop proficiency in reading/listening comprehension in Modern Standard Arabic. The instructional materials consist of authentic written, visual and audio materials. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

subject: ARAB
title: Third-Level Arabic II
description: Continuation of third-level Arabic I. Emphasis on developing writing and interaction ability at advanced levels of proficiency. Course includes extensive reading, composition exercises, listening skills, conversation practice and extensive review of Arabic grammar. Developing fluency is the main objective of this course. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to the Built Environment
description: DS Introduction to the breadth of design in today’s global culture. Exploration of human responses to place, climate, culture, communication, and technology, with emphasis on the impact of scientific knowledge on environmental design. Open to nonmajors. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Fundamentals Studio I
description: DA Introduction to creative design processes focusing on the investigation of composition within defining perceivable space. Hands-on exploration of materials and structures as an introduction to design processes. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Fundamentals Studio II
description: DA Continued exploration of design processes. Introduction to CAD technologies, material exploration, and creative exploration including the relationship between digital, physical, and materials aspects of design. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Collaboration in Environmental Design
description: Investigation of the various disciplines in the environmental design field, including architecture, landscape architecture, interiors, historic preservation, urban design, and construction management. Emphasis given to collaborative methods to address critical issues. Open to non-majors. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio I
