description: DA Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, represent, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and computer graphic techniques. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ANTH
title: Quantitative Archaeology
description: Combined lecture/lab. Introduction to the basic principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. Exploratory data analysis approach. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: A-F only. ANTH majors only. Junior standing or higher. Pre: 210.

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: DS Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies and practices of modern medicine. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Pre: junior standing or higher, 152, or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Field Mapping
description: DS Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data. (Cross-listed as GEO 472)
prerequisites: Pre: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Ceramic Analysis in Archaeology
description: DH Concepts, methods, and approaches used in the analysis of ancient pottery. Emphasis placed on ceramic technology, stylistic analysis.

subject: ANTH
title: Lithic Artifact Assemblage Analysis
description: DS Combined lecture/lab on the manufacture and analysis of stone tools. Students work with experimental collections and engage in stone tool production. The ways in which lithics enlighten us about past human behavior are discussed.

subject: ANTH
title: Faunal Analysis in Archaeology
description: DH Analysis of archaeologically recovered faunal collections with emphasis on identification and interpretation of nonhuman vertebrate remains.

subject: ANTH
title: Spatial Analysis in Archaeology
description: Lecture/lab. Introduction to the use of Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistics in archaeological research. Topics include: map creation; spatial database management; spatial analysis; image processing, data reporting; and data display. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: 466 or 666, or instructor approval.

subject: ANTH
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: DH Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as LAIS 478 and REL 478)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites. Pre: LAIS 360, or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Anthropology
description: DS The application of anthropological methods and concepts to solving practical human problems such as homelessness, domestic violence, maternal morbidity, conflict over resources, and the loss of indigenous languages. Includes a significant service-learning component.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
description: DS Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature. (Alt. years) (Crosslisted as SUST 482)

subject: ANTH
title: Japanese Culture and Behavior
description: DS Sociocultural factors in Japanese behavior. Social structure; traditional institutions

subject: ANTH
title: Japanese Popular Culture
description: DS Explores contemporary Japanese popular culture through themes such as gender, consumerism, globalization and nostalgia. Rather than a survey of popular culture genres, the course is organized thematically around issues and problematics.

subject: ANTH
title: Pre-European Hawai‘i
description: DH Pre-European society and culture from an anthropological viewpoint.

subject: ANTH
title: Peoples of Hawai‘i
description: DS Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawai‘i using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ES 486)

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Okinawa and Its Diaspora
description: Explores the ties of identity that exist within and between Okinawa and its diasporic populations. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Chinese Culture: Ethnography
description: DS Critical interpretations of ethnographic and biographic texts depicting individual and family lives in different socioeconomic circumstances, geographical regions, and historical periods of modern China.

subject: ANTH
title: History of Anthropology
description: DS Development of anthropological ideas, focusing on theoretical issues concerning culture, society, and human nature. Required of majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History: Monuments and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
description: DH Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. Monuments and nationalism in Southeast Asia. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ART 490D)
prerequisites: A-F only. Pre: ART 175, or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
description: DH Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project. (Cross-listed as ES 493)

subject: ANTH
title: Senior Thesis I
description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. First semester of a two-semester sequence with 496. May be taken concurrently with 496. Optional for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Senior Thesis II
description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. Second semester of a two-semester sequence with 495. May be taken concurrently with 495. Optional for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnology
description: Survey, in historical perspective, of theory in social and cultural anthropology, from the origin of anthropology to 1976. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Linguistic Anthropology
description: Investigation of mutual influences of linguistic theory and methodology and anthropological theory and methodology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology
description: Development of critical and analytical skills in assessment of archaeological literature; emphasis on the science, theory, explanation, and paradigms that comprise archaeology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Biological Anthropology Core
description: Human evolution and human variability in extant and previously existing populations; emphasis on history of physical anthropology, evolutionary systematics, primate biology and behavior, paleontology, anthropological genetics, climatic adaptation, growth, and nutrition. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Discursive Practices
description: Emphasizes linguistic, semantic, and interactional aspects of culture, exploring ways that discourse constructs social action and social realities, examining processes by which culture is produced as meaningful behavior in actual situations.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Infectious Disease
description: The role of human behavior, including its social and cultural determinants, in understanding the distribution of infectious diseases and in shaping preventive and therapeutic strategies.

subject: ANTH
title: History and Memory
description: History and collective memory as culturally formed and politically contested realities. The role of narrative, ritual, and media technologies in shaping representations of the past.

subject: ANTH
title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation. (Cross-listed as GEO 610)

subject: ANTH
title: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
description: Graduate seminar that examines the history of theory in sociocultural anthropology from 1960 to present. Designed to be taken in sequence after 601. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology
description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced. Repeatable nine times.

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Pacific Islands Archaeology
description: Advanced theoretical and methodological examination of archaeological research in Oceania, a region including the islands of Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia. (Fall only)

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational. Repeatable two times.

subject: ANTH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only) (Cross-listed as AMST 645 and ARCH 645).

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology
description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology with a focus on South Africa and its relevance for the Pacific and U.S. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence.

subject: ANTH
title: Advances in Extinctions
description: To delve deeply into the primary literature that focuses on the subjects of extinction and

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Culture
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in regard to cultural studies and the reading and interpretation of cultural texts. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Comparative Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in the field of comparative literature. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Medieval Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in Old/Middle English literature from 500-1500, including works in modern translation. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 16th and 17th Century Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written during the period 1500-1700. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 18th Century Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written during the period 1660-1830, the “long” 18th century. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 19th Century Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written during the 19th century. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 20th and 21st Century Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written from the 20th century to the present. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Single Author
description: DL. Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of a single author considered significant by most scholars in English Studies. The English Department maintains a list of versions focusing on specific authors. Repeatable one time for a different author, with consent.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Geoffrey Chaucer
description: DL. Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of Geoffrey Chaucer.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: William Shakespeare
description: DL. Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of William Shakespeare. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: John Milton
description: DL. Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of John Milton.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: DL. Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities. (Cross-listed as AMST 455 and WGSS 445)

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Film
description: DH. Intensive study of selected topics in film, e.g.: genres, major filmmakers, film theory/criticism, or film and literature. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Life Writing
description: DL. Intensive study of forms and theories of life writing in forms such as biographies, autobiographies, oral histories, diaries, journals, letters, film, drama, and portraiture with a focus on the ethical questions these materials present. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literary Forms, Genres, and Media
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, or movements in literary forms, genres, and media. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Asian American and Asian Diaspora Literatures
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, genres, or writers relating to Asia. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Postcolonial Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of postcolonial literatures and of historical, cultural, and theoretical issues such as colonialism, migration, assimilation, national identity, or transnationalism. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Cultural Identities and Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, genres, and writers in relation to cultural identities such as race, ethnicity, class as the basis for literary inquiry. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Cultural and Literary Geographies
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, genres, or writers relating to space and place as the basis for literary inquiry. Topics may include migration, diaspora, and local histories. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, writers, movements, and genres in the field of Hawaiian and/or Pacific literature. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as PACS 474)

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Folklore
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, or genres in folklore and oral traditions and their performance and transformations within specific social and cultural contexts. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Popular Culture
description: DL. Intensive study of selected problems, issues, traditions, writers, movements, or genres in the field of popular literature and/or popular culture. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions and issues in the construction and representation of sexuality and gender in specific genres, social and cultural contexts, or thematic/figurative clusters. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as WGSS 483)
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Study Abroad
description: DL. Intensive study in the English language of selected topics, issues or writers from the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Internship
description: Faculty supervised participation in the operations of an organization. A-F only.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses, junior standing, or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Directed Reading
description: Repeatable up to six credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: HWP Summer Writing Institute
description: Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: HWP Summer Institute WAC
description: Practicum in the current best approaches to teaching writing across the curriculum. Participants write, read published theory and research in composition, and demonstrate effective writing lessons. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Old English
description: Structure of the language, relation to present English; reading of selected prose and poetry.

subject: ENG
title: Theory and Practice of Teaching Composition
description: Major contemporary theorists and classroom practices that evolve from their theories; observation and applications. A-F only.

subject: ENG
title: Elements of Creative Writing
description: Intensive discussion of the craft and technique of creative writing through readings in poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and creative writing pedagogy. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ENG
title: Graduate Writing Workshop
description: Advanced practice and critical evaluation of the writing of poetry, fiction, or creative nonfiction. (B) poetry; (C) fiction; (D) nonfiction. Repeatable one time in each English graduate degree.
prerequisites: graduate standing plus 411 for (B); 414 for (C); 412 for (D); or consent

subject: ENG
title: Theories and Methods
description: Required course in the MA student’s area of concentration. (B) theories and methods of literary study; (C) introduction to composition and rhetoric; (D) foundations of creative writing; (E) theories in cultural studies. Repeatable in different alphas. ENG majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ENG
title: Literary Theory and Criticism
description: (B) classical period through 18th century; (C) Romantic and post-Romantic.

subject: ENG
title: Biography
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American literature. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: MA Final Project
description: Individual reading and research towards preparation of MA project. 3 credit hours required. CR/NC only. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Supervised Practicum
description: Applies course work in literature, creative writing, cultural studies, or composition and rhetoric to hands-on activities engaging publics outside of the university under direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. ENG majors only. A-F only.

subject: ENG
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual reading or research. Repeatable with consent of Graduate Director.

subject: ENG
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Composition Studies
description: In

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology
description: The study of the structure and functions of the head and neck with emphasis on structures in or related to the oral cavity; of tooth morphology. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: PHYL 141, PHYL 141L, PHYL 142, PHYL 142L, and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161. Co-requisite: 231L.

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of DH 231 didactic concepts to laboratory activities and practices. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: PHYL 141, PHYL 141L, PHYL 142, PHYL 142L, and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161. Co-requisite: 231.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene I
description: Relationship to dentistry, problems, trends, issues; role and functions of dental hygienists to prevent and control chronic oral diseases; preliminary dental hygiene clinical, includes team concepts in dentistry. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene I Lab
description: Application of preliminary dental hygiene clinical and support procedures including instrumentation, vital signs, and team concepts in dentistry. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene II
description: Basic dental hygiene theory and skills including competencies in health history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, plaque control and support procedures. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene II Lab/Clinic
description: Laboratory and clinical experiences in basic dental hygiene skills and competencies including history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, and clinic procedures. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: General Histology
description: Cells, tissues, the organs they make up, and their embryologic origin. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Oral Histology and Embryology
description: Cells and tissues as they relate to the oral cavity and the embryological development of the head, neck, and related oral structures. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Dental Radiography
description: Basic principles of radiation and fundamental information to understand and safely use radiation in dental radiography. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Dental Radiography Lab/Clinic
description: (1 3-hr Lab/Clinic) Preparation and evaluation of radiographic survey of patients with varying dentition; methods, and indications of safety considerations in clinical application of roentgen rays. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Health Education and Promotion
description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups and the larger public. Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as NURS 361)
prerequisites: Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: DH
title: General Pathology
description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases an tissue alterations associated with the human body organ systems. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Oral Pathology
description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases affecting the teeth and the structures of the oral cavity. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Dental Materials
description: Science of dental materials and its application to dentistry and dental hygiene. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Dental Materials Lab/Clinic
description: Laboratory and clinical application of concepts in the science of dental materials. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene
description: Basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene Lab/Clinic
description: (2 1.5-hr Lab/Clinic) Application of basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I
description: Development of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I Clinic
description: Clinical instruction and application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing, and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II
description: Continued development of dental hygiene concepts, skills, emergency procedures, team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating oral hygiene care of patients. Review and analyze dental periodicals and conduct a case study. Emphasis on writing. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
description: Continuation of 375. Clinical application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care to patients. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Pain Control and Local Anesthesia in Dentistry
description: Basic concepts of pain control and local anesthesia in dentistry with appropriate emphasis on psychological preparation, pharmacological preparation, and safe and effective administration of anesthesia in the practice of dental hygiene. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Periodontology I
description: Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Periodontology II
description: Continuation of DH 390. Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Community Health
description: Introduction and application of the principles of health education and dental public health into practice in schools, community agencies, and private dental offices (inclusive of problem assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation processes); epidemiology and biostatistics. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene I
description: An in-depth knowledge and clinical application of expanded function in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior. A-F only.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Dental Hygiene I Clinic
description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II
description: In-depth knowledge, communicated via oral delivery, on development of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modifications in behavior. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Pediatric Growth and Development
description: Focus on the normal growth and development of children based on current clinical practice guidelines and evidence in pediatric research. DH majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Advanced Health and Diagnostic Assessment for Pediatric Patients
description: Focus on advanced health and diagnostic assessment for pediatric patients. Includes behavior management techniques as well as oral habits and subsequent malocclusions and speech difficulties. DH majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Pharmacological Principles and Clinical Therapeutics in Pediatric Dental Care
description: Focus on pharmacological principles and clinical therapeutics in pediatric dental care. DH majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Simulation Lab
description: Focus on interprofessional practice principles and competencies while providing students an opportunity to participate in interprofessional team simulations to address health care issues of children. DH majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical I
description: Field experience.

subject: EDCS
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as SUST 623)

subject: EDCS
title: School Mathematics Curriculum
description: Analysis of research related to teaching and learning school mathematics, application of research to classroom practices. Appraisal of recent curriculum trends; critical examination of assumptions underlying proposed curriculum changes.

subject: EDCS
title: Social Studies Curriculum
description: Examination and evaluation of social science content, societal values and research findings as basis for development and revision of social studies materials, texts, curriculum guides, methodology.
prerequisites: STE 322 or equivalent, social studies teaching experience, or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Art Education K-12
description: Principles, goals, and objectives in teaching and learning art K-12; curriculum, instruction, and assessment in art education; laboratory experiences in art media.

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning with Art Objects, Museums, Collections, and Site Visits
description: Interdisciplinary inquiry and examination of the role of physical objects and site visits in schools and other educational contexts, through visits to local art museums and related sites.

subject: EDCS
title: Function of Play in Early Childhood Education
description: Review of research and theory illuminating the nature, purposes, and meaning of play as a critical aspect of early childhood education. (Summer only)

subject: EDCS
title: Cultural Diversity and Education
description: Examines issues, theories, perspectives and practices in multicultural education and promotes awareness, encourages knowledgeable reflection and develops skills necessary for multicultural practitioners. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEF 630)

subject: EDCS
title: Qualitative Research Methods
description: Methods of qualitative research in education or related social science from an interdisciplinary framework.

subject: EDCS
title: Autoethnography in Education
description: Exploration and application of autoethnography as a self-reflexive research method that utilizes the retelling of lived experience and emotion to examine historical, critical, and social topics. Graduate students only.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum and Instruction in Studio Art
description: Understanding art methods and materials related to art education for teachers grades K-12. Writing curricula, integrating visual arts across the curriculum, developing evaluation methods observing stages of artistic growth among students of multiple ages/abilities. (B) painting, drawing, printing; (C) fiber arts, ceramics, sculpture; (D) photography, technology, collage; (E) Combination of any three of B, C, and/or D. Previous BA, BS, BEd, and BFA only. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: EDCS
title: Business and Marketing Education Curriculum
description: Theory, philosophy, objectives, and development of business and marketing education curriculum.

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field. (C) English; (H) mathematics; (I) literacy; (J) science; (K) social studies; (M) interdisciplinary education; (N) art; (P) place-based education. Each alpha repeatable two times. COE-related majors only for (P). (K Cross-listed as PACE 640, P Cross-listed as SUST 641)
prerequisites: teaching experience or consent for all alphas except for (P); graduate and/or undergraduate courses in education and/or social sciences or consent for (P).

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar in Foreign Language
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation of language education instruction. (B) French; (C) German; (D) Japanese; (F) Spanish.

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar in Diversity Issues
description: Examination of principles in multicultural education and diversity. (D) middle level; (G) K-14; (R) reading K-12. Each alpha repeatable five times. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Multilingual/EL Pedagogy
description: Examines practices, theories, research, and perspectives on multilingual/EL teaching approaches. Topics include culturally and linguistically responsive approaches, collaboration, lesson planning, and adapting materials to promote the growth and development of multilingual/ EL learners. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as SLS 644)

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar In Multicultural Literacy
description: Interdisciplinary examination of research and issues in the teaching and learning of literacy in diverse multicultural settings. A-F only.
prerequisites: course in teaching language arts of multicultural education, teaching experience, or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Literacy Assessment, Instruction, and Intervention
description: Application of formative assessments to better monitor/guide struggling readers and writers. Topics include diversity and state/national initiatives. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Classroom and School Literacy Assessment
description: Advanced use of formative and summative assessments to monitor/lead classroom and school literacy programs. Focus on diversity, leadership, state/national initiatives, and practical applications in schools or other educational contexts. (B) general; (C) multilingualism. May take each alpha one time only.

subject: EDCS
title: Reading for English Language Learners
description: Presents key concepts and theories in teaching reading to K-12 English language learners. Topics include instructional decisions in teaching reading to ELLs, the interrelationship of language skills, strategies, and teaching academic content. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Theory/Practice in Cooperative Occupational Education
description: Theory and practices of coordinating cooperative education in high school and community college.

subject: EDCS
title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawai‘i and our global community. A-F only. (Summer only) (Cross-listed as DIS 650 and KRS 650)

subject: EDCS
title: Mathematics in the Schools
description: School mathematics, K-12 content, curricula, pedagogy, and standards; trends and issues; theory and research. (B) number and operation; (C) patterns, functions and algebra; (D) geometry and measurement; (E) probability and statistics; (F) integrated math content. Each alpha represents a different K-12 content area. Repeatable three times for (F).

subject: EDCS
title: Ethnomathematics
description: Research and practice in ethnomathematics from an interdisciplinary framework. Analysis of ethnomathematics content knowledge and pedagogy; connections among curriculum, standards, and classroom practice; examination of theory and research; and building sustainable campus-community networks. Topics vary. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar in Issues in ECE
description: Concepts and inquiry regarding the application of early childhood educational principles and approaches to programs serving children between birth and age five. Study and discussion of topics and problems presented in required summer courses and by invited experts in early childhood education. Restricted to masters in Early Childhood Education. Repeatable six times. A-F only. (Two times a year)

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar in Curriculum
description: Curriculum trends and issues related to school organization, program, administration, faculty. Required for Plan B MEd candidates in their final semester or summer session. Repeatable one time. (B) early childhood; (D) middle-level; (G) K-14.
prerequisites: EDCS 622 (any alpha), and EDCS 606 or EDEF 678 or EDEP 408, and EDCS 632 or EDEA 604 or EDEP 429 or EDEA 608; or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Indigenous and Postcolonial Perspectives in Education
description: Examination of historical impacts of U.S. and European imperialism and Western education on Indigenous communities across the globe. Additional emphasis on contemporary Indigenous efforts towards cultural reclamation and educational sovereignty.

subject: EDCS
title: Contemporary Native Hawaiian Education
description: Explores the landscapes, purposes, successes, and challenges of contemporary Native Hawaiian education. Emphasizes educational kīpuka, resurgence, liberation and educational sovereignty. Topics include Hawaiian immersion education, Hawaiian-focused charter schools, ‘āna and community education, and virtual learning.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum Design in Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to help classroom teachers understand sources and principles of curriculum in early childhood education and to provide experience in evaluating, selecting, and developing appropriate curriculum for young children.

subject: EDCS
title: Museums and Education
description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects. (Cross-listed as AMST 685)

subject: EDCS
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices in effective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure. A-F only.
degrees: MEd in Curriculum Studies (School Library Science track)

subject: ASAN
title: Law and Society in China
description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as LWPA 586)

subject: ASAN
title: Conflict and Cooperation in Asia
description: Explores conflict and cooperation among Asian nations. Topics may include economic integration, business networks, space and cyberspace, military alliances, territorial disputes, transnational crime, environmental cooperation, soft power, and regional institutional architecture. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Foreign Policy
description: Examination of China’s rise and world view, review of China’s regional relations, China and U.S. relations, formation of a new world order.

subject: ASAN
title: International Relations in Asia
description: How well do international relations theories explain interstate relations in Asia? How do international issues interact with domestic politics? Covers Japan, China, Korea, ASEAN nations, India, and touches on Russia, Australia, and New Zealand. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Field Study in Asia
description: With prior consent and supervision of an Asian Studies faculty, students design, conduct, and write the results of a field research project. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Buddhist Studies
description: Seminar on selected topics in Buddhist studies. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: PHIL 360, PHIL 406, REL 475, or REL 490; or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Studies Master’s Plan B Culminating Experience
description: Students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend a portfolio of work produced in seminars before a three-person faculty committee. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. ASAN majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Directed Research
description: Individual problems and research. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ASAN
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable nine times.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
description: Bibliography, reference tools, and research methods in sources on Asia in Western and Asian languages. Discussion of published and archival repositories. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as LIS 645)

subject: ASAN
title: MAIA Capstone
description: Capstone experience for MAIA students that emphasizes practical applications of Asia knowledge. Should be taken in final semester or after completion of all or most of MAIA core requirements. MAIA majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism. A-F only. (Alt. 2-3 years) (Cross-listed as ART 792)

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy
description: DP. Introduction to the astronomical universe: sky and celestial objects, planetary motion, planets and the Solar System, Sun and stars, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology and the universe.

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy
description: DP. Introduction to the astronomical universe: sky and celestial objects, planetary motion, planets and the Solar System, Sun and stars, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology and the universe.

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy Laboratory
description: DY. Observations of constellations and the night sky, the sun and moon, planets, stars, and deep-sky objects; laboratory and observational experiments illustrating basic concepts in astronomy. Offered in the evening.

subject: ASTR
title: Introduction to Archaeoastronomy
description: DP. Astronomy and celestial lore in ancient cultures: Neolithic Europe, Mayan, Mesoamerican, Egyptian, Mesopotamian, American Indian, Chinese, and Polynesian. Concepts of the cosmos, calendars, eclipse predictions, motion of celestial bodies, and navigation. Construction of simple observing tools.

subject: ASTR
title: Voyage through the Solar System
description: DP. An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip. (Cross-listed as ERTH 105)

subject: ASTR
title: Introduction to Astronomical Research
description: Introduction to astronomical research, including literature resources, basic computing skills, software tools, data analysis, scientific communication, and research opportunities. Prepares students for effective internships and directed research projects. ASTR and ASTP majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astronomy
description: DP. A rigorous overview of modern astronomy: solar system, stellar, galactic and extragalactic astronomy and cosmology. For science and engineering students.

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astrophysics I: The Solar System
description: DP. Solar system astrophysics. Dynamics of planets, satellite systems, asteroids and comets; planetary atmospheres and internal structure; thermal balance; the Sun as a star. Introduces numerical computing. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: PHYS 170, MATH 242 or 252A, and PHYS 272 (or concurrent). (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astrophysics II: Galaxies and Stars
description: DP. Stellar and galactic astrophysics. Stellar magnitudes, colors, distances, and spectra. Galactic structure and evolution, active nuclei, large-scale structure, Big-Bang cosmology. Stellar interiors, nuclear “burning,” main-sequence and evolved stars. Introduces computer programming. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: 241, PHYS 274 (or concurrent), and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent). (Spring only)

subject: ASTR
title: Evolution of the Universe
description: DP. The Big Bang, origin of the elements, formation and evolution of galaxies and stars.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrobiology
description: DP. Are we alone in the universe? Modern astronomical, biological, and geological perspectives on this fundamental question. Searches for life on Mars, oceans on Europa, planets orbiting other stars. Space exploration and colonies, interstellar spaceflight and communication. (Spring only)

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy
description: DP. Principles and techniques of optical and near-infrared astronomical observation. Astronomical coordinate systems. Telescopes, cameras, spectrographs, and detectors. Astrometry, photometry, and spectroscopy of astronomical objects. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 210 or 242; PHYS 152 or 274; MATH 216, 242, or 252A. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy Laboratory
description: DY. Optical and near-infrared astronomy laboratory. Error analysis, properties of light, data, and image processing. Astrometric, photometric, and spectroscopic measurement. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or 274; PHYS 152L or 274L; MATH 216, 242, or 252A. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy Projects
description: DY. Astronomical observational research projects. Students use astronomical data and process telescopic observations to produce scientific results, and present these orally and in writing. Students prepare for independent research projects and present research plans orally. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomical Spectroscopy
description: DP. Introduction to astronomical spectroscopy. Stellar atmospheres, line formation, elements of radiative transfer. Phases of interstellar medium. Emission line diagnostics. Doppler shift and kinematics. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: 210 or 242; PHYS 152 or 274; MATH 216 or 242 or 252A. (Spring only)

subject: ASTR
title: Modern Extragalactic Astronomy
description: DP. Use of astronomical surveys to map large-scale distribution of galaxies. Internal structure & dynamics of galaxies. Evolution of galaxy populations over cosmic time. Theoretical understanding of galaxy formation in context of modern Big Bang cosmology. Recommended: 280. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: 210 or 242; and 300 (or concurrent); and PHYS 152 or PHYS 274.

subject: ASTR
title: History of Cosmology and Scientific Thought
description: History and intellectual context of astronomical discovery; the evolution of ideas of space, time, and motion from the Babylonians to relativistic cosmologies; emphasis on the interaction of astronomy with the history of ideas. (Spring only)

subject: ASTR
title: Directed Study
description: Individual reading, observation, or experimentation in astronomy and astrophysics. Repeatable four times.

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Astrophysics
description: DP. Advanced survey of stellar astrophysics, including application of astrometry, photometry, and spectrometry to determine fundamental stellar properties; stellar structure and evolution of single and binary stars; astrophysical distance determination methods; stellar nucleosynthesis.

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies & Cosmology
description: DP. Survey of extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, including: galaxy morphology and kinematics; luminosity functions; dark matter; properties of galaxy groups/ clusters; gravitational lensing; redshifts; cosmological models; the Big Bang; thermal history of the Universe; structure formation. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274; MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A.

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: DP. Observations and physical nature of planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and other small bodies; formation of the Solar System; discove

subject: CHN
title: Fourth-Level Mandarin I
description: Extensive reading in academic topics. Meets one hour a day, three times a week.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Fourth-Level Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 401.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Mandarin
description: Content of 401 and 402 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, three times a week.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Fourth-Year Chinese for Business Professionals
description: Accelerated, intensive advanced course focusing on specialized advanced listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: High-Advanced Chinese I
description: Authentic reading, writing, speaking, and listening with Advanced-high and Superior level discourse, content, and genres to build Superior Chinese proficiency and broaden knowledge of Chinese culture. Significant attention paid to developing Chinese writing skills.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: High-Advanced Chinese II
description: Aims to build Superior Level Chinese proficiency in reading, speaking, writing, and listening using authentic texts covering Chinese education, and economy, philosophy, while broadening and deepening knowledge of Chinese culture. (Spring only)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Advanced Mandarin Conversation I
description: Systematic practice on academic topics of conversation. Lab work.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Advanced Mandarin Conversation II
description: Continuation of 411.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Chinese Translation
description: Training in techniques; theory of translation. (B) Chinese–English; (C) English–Chinese.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Media Analysis in Chinese
description: Use authentic materials, including texts, videos, and postings from social media with Advanced and Superior level discourse and content to build Superior Chinese proficiency and social media literacy, and understand society and contemporary issues.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Fourth Year Reading and Writing: Advanced Topics
description: Asynchronous web-based course with focuses on (i) reading selected texts across a broad range of genres, and (ii) writing expository and argumentative essays by referencing and reflecting on the readings, along with interacting with peers. (Fall only)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Fourth Year Reading and Writing: Contemporary Social Issues
description: Asynchronous web-based course with focuses on (i) authentic texts covering a variety of contemporary social issues, and (ii) writing expository/argumentative essays by referencing and reflecting on the readings, along with interacting with peers. (Spring only)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Language and Linguistics
description: Covers major areas of linguistic description as applied to Chinese language, with significant attention paid to developing writing skills on demonstrating knowledge of the basics of Chinese linguistic features and analyzing Chinese language phenomena. DH
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Structure of Chinese
description: Introduction to syntax and semantics of Mandarin Chinese; some discussion of usage and linguistic geography. DH
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Study of Chinese Characters I
description: Origin, structure, and evolution. (Alt. years)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Study of Chinese Characters II
description: Continuation of 453. (Alt. years)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Pragmatics and Discourse
description: Introduction to pragmatics and discourse analysis of Mandarin Chinese; some discussion of usage and linguistic geography. DH
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Semantics and Communication
description: Study of the meaning of Chinese sentences in isolation, in discourse contexts, and in written texts. Pays equal attention to theoretical issues and practical problems in Chinese semantics and communication. (Once a year)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Words and the Lexicon
description: Defines properties of the Chinese lexicon, introduces its principles, approaches, and methodologies in Chinese lexicology, outlines similarities and differences between the Chinese and English lexicons, and advances students’ Chinese language proficiency. (Alt. years: fall)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Introduction to Classical Chinese
description: Analysis of basic structural patterns through selected readings in various texts.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Language and Culture of China
description: Extensive exposure–chiefly through tape recordings, classroom conversation, and outside readings–to history, culture, and institutions. DH
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Professional Chinese
description: Focus on professional reading, writing, speaking, and listening in order to train students to the Superior (according to ACTFL standards) level of language proficiency. Repeatable one time when taken in China as part of the UH Chinese Flagship Program.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Academic
description: Focus on academic reading, writing, speaking, and listening with emphasis on writing instruction in order to train students to the Superior (according to ACTFL standards) level of language proficiency. Repeatable one time when taken in China as part of the UH Chinese Flagship Program.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Readings in 20th Century Chinese Literature
description: Representative works of writers from People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. (B) short stories; (C) poetry and drama; (D) novels and essays. Repeatable two times. DL
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Flagship Rhetoric and Composition Abroad
description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of and ability to use Chinese to effectively communicate in writing. A-F only.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Flagship Media and Society Abroad
description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of Chinese media, how it operates, and its effects on Chinese society. A-F only.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Flagship Experience Abroad
description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will take two courses taught in Chinese in their field at Nanjing or Beijing Union University. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. CR/NC only.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Oral Fluency Through Chinese Films
description: Increasing Chinese proficiency through film, which offers authentically rich cultural contexts. Focus on oral communication. DH
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Internship Program
description: Faculty supervised participation in the operations of an organization in a position making use of students’ Chinese language skills in Hawai‘i. Students must achieve a grade of B- in CHN 302 to take this course. Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. CHN majors only. Junior/senior standing only.
prerequisites: 302 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Overseas Internship in China
description: Supervised internships in a Chinese-speaking institution in China. Students must pass 486 with a B- or higher and be accepted to the Flagship Capstone Year in China to take this. Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: 461 and 485 and 486 (with a minimum grade of B- or better) and proficiency assessment and acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. CR/NC only. Repeatable three times. Primarily for graduate students from other departments.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Introduction to Study of Contemporary Chinese Linguistics
description: Panoramic overview of major perspectives in contemporary Chinese linguistics. Readings on recent developments of fields. Report on selected research papers and present analysis of linguistic phenomena of interest. (Alt. years)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Chinese Poetry
description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th–10th century).
prerequisites: 461 or consent for (B), 610B or consent for (C).
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Traditional Chinese Fiction
description: Formal and thematic analysis of short stories, historical romances, and novels. Repeatable one time with consent.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) History of Chinese Language
description: (B) phonology; (C) syntax.
prerequisites: 451, LING 421, or consent for (B); 452 or consent for (C).
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Dialects
description: Synchronic description of a Chinese dialect other than Cantonese and Mandarin; contrastive and comparative studies with Mandarin. Repeatable one time with consent.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Syntax and Semantics
description: Verbal categories, aspects, focus devices, resultative and directional compounds, coverbial constructions. Interaction between syntax and semantics.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Contrastive Analysis of Mandarin and English
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Methods in Teaching Chinese as Second Language
description: Problems in language learning and teaching. Practice in preparing and presenting lessons with materials based on comparative linguistic analysis. Materials, teaching aids, test construction.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Practicum: Teaching Chinese Language
description: For graduate students pursuing teach
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: ANTH
title: Sex and Gender
description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual differences; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status. (Crosslisted as WGSS 315)

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Tourism
description: Anthropological perspectives on the subject of the global phenomenon of tourism. Includes issues of cultural performance, identity, and commoditization. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ANTH
title: Pacific Islands Archaeology
description: Origins of Pacific peoples; chronology of settlement; sequences of culture in Australia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia.

subject: ANTH
title: Origins of Cities
description: Combined lecture/ discussion on the emergence and development of ancient cities in comparative perspective and the dynamics of (pre)modern urban life. Examples are drawn from the Near East, Mediterranean, Africa, India, China, and the Americas. A-F only.

subject: ANTH
title: American Folklore and Folklife
description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism. (Cross-listed as AMST 326)

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnohistory
description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e., the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history. A-F only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as IS 322)

subject: ANTH
title: Food Origins, Food Culture
description: Lectures and discussion offer an anthropological introduction to how humans created and transformed food through time. (Spring only)

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Peoples and Cultures of North America
description: Survey of Indigenous peoples of North America. Integrates documentary records, ethnography, and archaeology to explore variability among native communities. Contemporary topics include political recognition and self-determination, health and education, and natural resources and economic development.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Surfing
description: Applies cultural anthropology to assess surfing as an indigenous Hawaiian and modern globalized activity. Discusses the history of surfing, surfing culture, and the impacts of surfing tourism on coastal development, reef ecology, and ocean safety. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ANTH
title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as SUST 333)

subject: ANTH
title: Society and Environment
description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems. (Cross-listed as SUST 335)

subject: ANTH
title: Historical Ecology
description: Examines the recursive relationship between humans and the environment across deep time. (Fall only)

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Virtual Worlds
description: Anthropological study of computer mediated interaction. Focus on the ethnography of massively multiplayer online games, text-based chat rooms, and blogs. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Aggression, War, and Peace
description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace. (Cross-listed as PACE 345)

subject: ANTH
title: Pacific Island Cultures
description: Introduction to cultures of Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia from time of first settlement to emergence of modern nation states.

subject: ANTH
title: Primate Behavioral Ecology
description: As primates are our closest living relatives, studying the range of variation in areas like life history, diet, communication, and social systems within the order primates can inform on how we ourselves evolved.

subject: ANTH
title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households. (Cross-listed as LAIS 368)

subject: ANTH
title: Household Archaeology
description: Focuses on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between households that comprised ancient communities and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change. A-F only.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnographic Field Techniques
description: Problems and techniques of social-cultural anthropological fieldwork; ethnographic literature; work with informants. Repeatable one time.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America. Repeatable one time for different alphas. (Cross-listed as LAIS 372 (Alpha))

subject: ANTH
title: Race and Human Variation
description: Human genetic and physical variation; latitudinal, longitudinal, and altitudinal variation across human populations; history of racism; contemporary issues in race and racism. (Once a year)
prerequisites: Pre: sophomore standing, recommend 152 and 215; or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology Practicum
description: Students will gain practical archaeological experience (e.g., materials processing, analysis, documentation, conservation) under the direction of practicing archaeological professionals in the local community and in collaboration with supervising archaeological faculty. Repeatable two times, up to 6 credits. ANTH majors or minors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: ANTH majors or minors only. Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: 210 or consent of instructor.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Lab Techniques
description: Laboratory analysis and evaluation of field data; preservation and restoration of artifacts. Preparation for publication. Repeatable two times. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Field Techniques
description: Archaeological survey and excavations; field trips, mapping, photography. May focus on terrestrial or underwater. May be taught entirely in the field at a national or international archaeological site. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: ANTH
title: How Archaeology Works
description: Uses archaeological examples to illustrate social science research techniques. Students learn how to create, analyze, and evaluate data through lab-based exercises, and examine ethical issues inherent in anthropological practice. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: 210 or instructor consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Skeletal Biology
description: Introduction to the human skeleton and methods for analyzing archaeological human remains including age, sex, ethnicity, paleodemography, skeletal and dental variation, paleopathology, population studies.

subject: ANTH
title: Skeletal Biology Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany 384.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological. Repeatable nine times.

subject: ANTH
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable nine times.
prerequisites: Pre: major or minor in Anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethics in Anthropology
description: Seminar surveying ethical cases, problems, issues and questions from the inception of anthropology to the present.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Museum Anthropology
description: Anthropological study of museums and related sites of cultural production (historic sites, memorials, theme parks). (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Evolutionary Anthropology
description: Lecture discussion providing an overview of evolutionary theory in anthropology: focus on the evolution of culture, behavioral ecology, and cultural diversity; emphasis on archaeological and ethnographic research and explanatory models. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Language and Gender
description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required. A-F only. (Cross-listed as LING 415)

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as LING 414 and IS 414)

subject: ANTH
title: Wealth, Culture, and Economic Anthropology
description: Analysis of economic activities in non-Western, non-industrial societies; production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a variety of cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: Political Anthropology
description: Character of political institutions and their development in nonWestern and non industrial societies.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Anthropology
description: Exploration of how anthropology studies indigenous groups throughout the world. An examination of the role of anthropology in representing and engaging with indigenous communities.

subject: ANAT
title: Seminar in Anatomy Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses in anatomical sciences, development and evaluation of exams, experience in teaching with audiovisual/ computer aids. Open to graduate students in physiology or KRS. CR/NC only. Repeatable eight times, up to 32 credits.

subject: ANAT
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANAT
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANAT
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Animals, and Agriculture
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to animal agriculture, animal science, and the use of animals by humans. Ethics and importance of human use of animals in agriculture are emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Principles and Practices of Animal Science
description: DB Biology, behavior, and management of animals of economic and social importance. Topics include physiology, genetics, nutrition, reproduction, behavior, care, and management to achieve productivity, performance, and welfare. (lecture, discussion, and field trips)

subject: ANSC
title: Comparative Nutrition
description: DB Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors. (Cross-listed as FSHN 244) DB
prerequisites: Pre: (ANSC 200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161/161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C.
degrees: Food Science and Human Nutrition BS

subject: ANSC
title: Anatomy of Domestic Animals
description: DB Micro and gross anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C. Co-requisite: 301L.

subject: ANSC
title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
description: DY Laboratory to accompany 301, with an emphasis on teaching scientific and technical writing. Dissection and identification of anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C. Corequisite: 301.

subject: ANSC
title: Applied Animal Nutrition
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of the principles of nutrition to feeding of farm animals; composition and nutritional value of feed stuffs; nutritional requirements of beef cattle, dairy cattle, horses, poultry, and swine.
prerequisites: Pre: (ANSC 201 (or concurrent), and ANSC 244 or FSHN 244) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives. A-F only. (Cross-listed as FSHN 350)
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 200 or ANSC 201 or FSHN 181 or FSHN 185.
degrees: Food Science and Human Nutrition BS

subject: ANSC
title: Horses and Horsemanship
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Origin of species, breeds, nutrition, care, management. Lab on management practices with work on light horses.

subject: ANSC
title: Laboratory Skills in Animal Science
description: Provides students with basic and essential laboratory skills required in various fields of animal science such as nutrition, genetics, reproductive physiology, meat science, clinical pathology, parasitology, and animal handling. ANSC majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Pre: (ANSC 200 or ANSC 201, and BIOL 171 and 171L and CHEM 161) with a minimum grade of D-.

subject: ANSC
title: Poultry Production
description: DB Students will learn about poultry health and hygiene, husbandry, production, biosecurity, hands-on skills, and recent advances in poultry farming systems for meat and egg production. ANSC majors only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANSC
title: Beef Production
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of economic beef production, including beef breeds, selection, breeding, management systems, feeding, and marketing under tropical conditions.

subject: ANSC
title: Swine Production
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of efficient pork production, including comparative breed evaluation, breeding, feeding, management, marketing, and business aspects. Problems and practices associated with tropical environment emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Tropical Dairying
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles involved in economical milk production in the tropics, including management, recordkeeping, breeds, breeding, selection, culling, feeding, housing, milking, quality control, and raising young animals.

subject: ANSC
title: Genetics and Animal Breeding
description: DB Review and application of genetic principles to livestock, poultry, companion, aquatic, and laboratory research animals. Current practices and future developments. Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent.
prerequisites: Pre: (BIOL 171/171L or ZOOL 101/101L, and MATH 140X or higher) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Genes and Animal Biology
description: An understanding of animal biology at the level of genes and their regulations; emphasis on gene structure, recombinant DNA, transgenic animals and functional genomics being used for agricultural, nutritional and biomedical sciences. Open to nonmajors. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (ANSC 301, BIOL 171 or ZOOL 101) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Production
description: DB Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery. (Crosslisted as OCN 450)
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445: or BIOL 172/L and CHEM 162/L or higher.

subject: ANSC
title: Physiology of Domestic Animals
description: DB Functions and relationships of organs and organ systems of domestic animals excluding reproduction and lactation. Problem-based learning and case studies are emphasized.
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Animal Diseases and Their Control
description: DB Disease problems of livestock, poultry, and companion animals; their economic significance, causes, public health implications, and control.
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 200 (or concurrent), and BIOL 171/L or ZOOL 101/L.

subject: ANSC
title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology
description: DB Development, growth, function, carcass evaluation of muscle tissue.

subject: ANSC
title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology Lab
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Livestock and poultry slaughter, carcass evaluation, meat chemistry, muscle physiology and biochemistry, meat microbiology, and meat processing.

subject: ANSC
title: Companion Animals and Society
description: Explore human and companion animal relationships in biological, social, cultural, economic, legal, health, and welfare contexts to prepare students for careers in the various animal-related fields in Hawai‘i, the Pacific rim, and worldwide. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Biology and Culture of Shrimp and Prawns
description: Aspects of the biology and culture of the freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii and marine shrimp Penaeus (sp) species. Scientific research results and case studies presented and analyzed.

subject: ANSC
title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination
description: DB Introductory exploration of anatomy, development, and physiology of reproduction of domestic animals and artificial insemination. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C).

subject: ANSC
title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination Lab
description: Reproductive anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, estorus synchronization, breeding soundness, and artificial insemination laboratory, field trips. One week offisland field trip. Repeatable one time. ANSC majors or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Production Laboratory
description: Intensive, hands-on course involving the culture of larvae and juveniles of marine shrimp, freshwater prawns, molluscs, fish, and their food. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing and flexible time for continuous live animal care. Lab fee required.

subject: ANSC
title: Comparative Endocrinology
