description: DB Structure and function of endocrine systems across vertebrate groups, surveying how hormones mediate adaptive responses to dynamic environments and coordinate key aspects of growth, development, metabolism, osmoregulation, and stress.
prerequisites: Pre: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C).

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Business Planning and Entrepreneurship
description: Practical aspects of planning and developing an aquaculture business from conceptualization to a final business plan. Topics include species/technology, project planning, business structuring, permitting, contracts, production plans, financial planning and analysis, market/competition analysis, capital acquisition, intellectual property and legal issues. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care.

subject: ANSC
title: Topics in Animal Sciences
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs. Repeatable five times, up to 18 credits.

subject: ANSC
title: Field Experience
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report. A-F only. (Cross-listed as FSHN 492)
degrees: Food Science and Human Nutrition BS

subject: ANSC
title: Directed Study or Research
description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students, generally with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major. Exceptions may be granted for students with high achievement in last three semesters. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECON
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDUC
title: Action Research in Education
description: Theory and practice in collaborative action research; critical inquiry into current educational work in schools with goals of improvement of teaching and participation in school and curriculum reform.

subject: EDUC
title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Consultancy Project
description: Practicum in the EdD program in professional practice; involves a group consultancy project requiring independent research and reflective activity embedded in a group project dealing with a problem of practice. Repeatable three times. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice. A-F only.
degrees: Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice

subject: EDUC
title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Individual Applied Research Project
description: Practicum in conducting individual practitioner research within the EdD. Includes the formulation of individual applied research project, developing a plan of action, selection of appropriate methods, implementation of plan and composition of practitioner research report. Repeatable three times. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice. A-F only.
degrees: Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice

subject: EDUC
title: EdD Conference
description: Capstone for the Doctoral Degree in Professional Education Practice. Involves a conference presentation of research project results to an audience of faculty, fellow graduate students, and interested members of the public. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice. CR/NC only.
degrees: Doctoral Degree in Professional Education Practice

subject: EDUC
title: Field Project
description: Practicum experience in area of specialization. Variable credit: minimum of 3 credit hours, maximum of 6 credit hours. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: EDUC
title: Internship in College Teaching
description: Introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as apprentices to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, planning and evaluation. Repeatable up to six credits. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: admission to PhD candidacy and consent

subject: EDUC
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: EDEA
title: Dynamics of Student Leadership
description: Theoretical approaches and an experimental orientation toward leadership in student organizations via classroom activities and practicum experiences with student organizations.

subject: EDEA
title: Peer Leadership Education and Mentoring
description: Theoretical explorations and a supervised practicum experience in student peer leadership education and mentoring in a variety of curricular and co-curricular contexts.

subject: EDEA
title: (Alpha)Topics in Emergent Paradigms of Leadership
description: Exploration, application, analysis and synthesis of advanced leadership concepts including emergent theories, issues, trends and empowering approaches. (B) survey of emergent paradigms; (C) Asian Pacific American leadership; (D) gender and leadership; (E) ethics and leadership; (K) issues and problems in leadership. Repeatable one time per alpha.

subject: EDEA
title: Directed Reading
description: Planned individualized study, reading, research, teaching, and/ or projects under direct supervision of instructor. A-F only. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: EDEA
title: Introduction to Education Administration
description: Develops view of administrative process and organization elements in context of system of personal, social, and physical variables. Emphasis on role and functions of school administrator. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Research in Education Administration
description: Develops basic concepts of research on educational administration: methodology, status of particular topics, communication, and application of findings to problems of school administration. (Meets PhD common core inquiry methods requirement.) Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education
description: Introduction to methods of qualitative research in education. (Meets PhD common core requirement.) (Cross-listed as EDEP 613)

subject: EDEA
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models. Pre: consent. (Cross-listed as EDEP 602 and SOC 608)

subject: EDEA
title: School-Community Relations
description: Application of principles, techniques, policies, organization of school-community information program. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: (Alpha) Education Finance
description: Educational revenues, apportionments, budgetary procedures, costs, business management, economics of education, measures of productivity. (H) higher education: specific for higher education students; (K) K-12: specific for K-12 students. A-F only.

subject: EDEA
title: Administration in Kinesiology
description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings. Repeatable one time. Pre: consent. (Cross-listed as KRS 623)

subject: EDEA
title: Educational Statistics
description: Statistical inference including applications of parametric and nonparametric methods to educational problems.

subject: EDEA
title: (Alpha) Education Law
description: Status and functions of educational institutions and personnel relative to their legal rights and responsibilities. Includes interpretation of important court decisions, statutes, equity measures. (H) higher education: specific for higher education students; (K) K-12: specific for K-12 students. A-F only.

subject: EDEA
title: Principles of School Leadership
description: Examine the emergent theories, issues, practices, and problems relevant for educational leaders in school organizations. Integrates the aspects of management and administration within the context of leadership.

subject: EDEA
title: College Student Development Theory
description: Study of psycho-social characteristics of the American college student and college environment, from viewpoint of student personnel work. Repeatable one time. EDEA majors only.

subject: EDEA
title: Organizational Leadership in Education
description: Analysis of the nature of organizations, human nature and needs, and their relationship to leadership, staffing, and staff development. Implications of group structure and human conflict, communications, and supervision and evaluation considered. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Conflict Management for Educators
description: Conflict resolution theory and practice for administrators, faculty and staff in educational organizations. K-12, community colleges and universities. Application and theory of negotiation, mediation, facilitation and hybrid ADR processes. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as PACE 652)

subject: EDEA
title: Intercultural Interactions
description: Theory-based frameworks and training methods of intercultural interaction and their applications to educational administration situations. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Introduction to Higher Education
description: Salient historic, social, and organizational aspects of higher education; history, philosophy, purposes, governance, administration, structures, financing, faculty and student selection, curricula, legal and social issues. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Leadership in Higher Education
description: Trends, research, and problems in college and university management. Repeatable one time. EDEA majors only.

subject: EDEA
title: Leadership in Student Affairs
description: Philosophy, history, organization, and administration of student personnel services at college and university levels, including admissions, housing, student activities, financial aids, placement, counseling, health services. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Curriculum in Higher Education
description: Traditional and contemporary curriculum issues. Development of performance competencies in curriculum design and evaluation using systems and design theory as central paradigms. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Community College Leadership
description: Development and changing missions of community colleges; in-depth study of emerging leadership issues: planning, financial management, decision-making, governance, and student personnel. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Teacher Development and Evaluation
description: The role of teacher evaluation in the development of teachers and learning communities and to support effective teaching. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDEA
title: Introduction to Educational Policy Studies
description: Examines theories and models of educational policy and policy-making and the contribution of policy analysis to the policy-making and change processes. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEF 675)

subject: EDEA
title: The Politics of Education
description: Examination of the ways in which education can be viewed as political, arising from its connection to the larger political system including local, state, and federal governments. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEF 676)

subject: EDEA
title: Curriculum Administration
description: Master’s level course in curriculum administration and leadership, focusing on fundamental theories underlying curriculum development, as well as the implementation of curriculum policy at the school level.

subject: GEO
title: Geography and Contemporary Society
description: FGC Elements of economic geography and resource management, population and urban geography; application to current problems of developed and underdeveloped worlds.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Climatology
description: DP Elements and controls of climate. World patterns of insolation, temperature, evaporation, precipitation, atmospheric circulation. Climatic classifications.
prerequisites: 101 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 314)

subject: GEO
title: General Geomorphology
description: DP Introduction to geomorphological concepts, process mechanics, and relationships between forms and processes. Emphasis on various subdisciplines of geomorphology: coastal hillslopes, fluvial, aeolean, and glacial.

subject: GEO
title: Water and Society
description: DS Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives. (Cross-listed as SUST 315)
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Biogeography
description: DB Introduction to ecosystem concept; environmental adaptations for energy and nutrient transfer; characteristics, dynamics, productivity, and distribution of principal vegetation communities. Human dominance.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Planning
description: DS Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawai‘i planning–research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.

subject: GEO
title: Tropical Agrarian Systems
description: DS Analysis of environmental potential and constraints and of spatial organization of economy and society of tropical agrarian systems. Emphasis on change through colonial and post-colonial periods.

subject: GEO
title: Economic Geography
description: DS Examines how factors of production like land, labor and capital; economic activities like consumption, trade, production, and investments; and institutions like state, markets, and corporations alter economic space. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: GEO
title: Globalization and Environment
description: DS Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change. (Cross-listed as SUST 322)

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Global Tourism
description: DS Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. (Cross-listed as TIM 324)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: GEO
title: Geography, Environment, and Society
description: DS Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems. (Cross-listed as SUST 326)

subject: GEO
title: Culture and Environment
description: DS Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures. (Cross-listed as SUST 330)

subject: GEO
title: Islands and Archipelagos
description: DS Applies an island studies perspective to critically evaluate the commonalities and differences across islands and archipelagos in several world regions. Examines how island geographies influence social identities and movements and are impacted by environmental conditions. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PACS 333)

subject: GEO
title: Politics, Nations, and States
description: DS Examines the political organization of space in the sovereign state system. Contemporary and historical analyses of boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, nations, nationalism, and territory.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of North America
description: DS Overview of the physical and cultural geography. Regions and characters. Patterns of population, natural resources, industry, agriculture, and transportation/ communication networks.

subject: GEO
title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
description: DS Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as WGSS 343)

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Japan
description: DS Regional synthesis of physical and cultural features; economic, social, political geography; origins and development of cities.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of China
description: DS Topics: environmental parameters and resource base, ecological control and resource management, institutional and technological transformation of agriculture, industrial potential and industrial location, settlement patterns and rural urban symbiosis.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of South Asia
description: DS Introduction to physical and human geography of India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Himalayan kingdoms. Environmental, economic, social, cultural, and political factors in development.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description: DS An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change. (Cross-listed as ASAN 356)

subject: GEO
title: Geography of the Pacific
description: DS Physical character of the Pacific; cultural, political, economic geography of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia (except Hawai‘i).

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Honolulu
description: DS Development of Honolulu and O‘ahu from 1778. Evolution of function, land use, and social patterns. Contemporary planning and environmental issues arising from urban growth.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Hawai‘i
description: DS Regional, physical, cultural geography. Detailed study of people and resources.

subject: GEO
title: UAV and Aerial Photography
description: DY (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle systems) and the measurement, interpretation, analysis, and use of photography acquired by UAV and other aerial systems.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Cartography and Air Photo
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of cartography: compilation and measurement from aerial photographs, alternate forms of data presentation, symbolism, design, and map projection.

subject: GEO
title: Map Design and Production
description: (3 2-hr Lab) Compilation, design and production of maps for presentations, research, and illustration using artists and mapping software.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Statistical Methods in Geography
description: Quantitative statistical methods will be explored for describing and interpreting geographic/environmental phenomena. Topics will include data display, measurement, sampling, spatial statistics, dimensional analysis, nonparametric and parametric models.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to GIS
description: Design, implementation, and use. Database construction and documentation. Techniques for spatial data manipulation and display. Evaluation of existing systems. Student research projects.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Reading
description: Limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in geography.

subject: GEO
title: Vegetation and the Climate System
description: DP Role of vegetation in the climate system; links to hydrology and biogeochemical cycling; vegetation and climate history; evolution of terrestrial ecosystems; effects of global warming.
prerequisites: 101 or 300 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Climate Change
description: DP Approaches to the study of past and future climate change.
prerequisites: 101 or 300 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Agricultural Climatology
description: DP Analyzing climatic data; relation to photosynthesis, phenological development, and crop yields. Crop-weather models as guides to improved land-use planning and agronomic practices.
prerequisites: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Fluvial Geomorphology
description: DP Introduction to the single most important geomorphic agent shaping the terrestrial environment. Focus on fluvial process, fluvial dynamics, fluvial landforms, and sediment transport.

subject: GEO
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: DS Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control. (Cross-listed as SUST 404)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Water in the Environment
description: DP Water fluxes in the environment. Occurrence and movement of water; methods of quantification. Water balance of soil-plant system: precipitation, interception, infiltration, runoff, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and groundwater recharge.
prerequisites: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Conservation and Evolutionary Biogeography
description: Theories and techniques for the analysis of spatial microevolutionary patterns, taught from an interdisciplinary perspective. Examples and readings emphasize Hawai

subject: CAAM
title: Nutrition for Clinicians
description: Provides in-depth lectures and case studies reviewing the role of nutritional therapy in health and illness. MD majors only. CR/NC only. Pre: MDED 554 or consent. (Fall only)
department: Department of Complementary and Alternative Medicine
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years)
description: Emphasizes interrelated historical and philosophical roots and socio-cultural context and their influence on policy and practice in early childhood education settings. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years) Lab
description: Direct experience with children in early childhood settings in order to apply concepts from 415 and gain perspective on the role of the practitioner in ECE settings.

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
description: Continuation of 415: focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children (pK-3). (Cross-listed as STE 416)

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
description: Continuation of 415L. Co-requisite: 416. (Cross-listed as ITE 416L)

subject: EDCS
title: STEM Pedagogy
description: Introduction to STEM education pedagogy with emphasis on ethical issues and effective oral communication. Designed to integrate educational theory, pedagogy, content, and practical concerns into teaching practices in the STEM fields. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: EDCS
title: Collaborative Language and Learning
description: Examination of language (talking, reading, and writing) processes within a collaborative teaching framework in the secondary curriculum. Field experience may be required. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Adolescent Literature and Literacy
description: Selection and interpretation of young adult literature, including multicultural literature for middle level and high school students. Theory and teaching strategies for integrating literacy instruction in the literature program for diverse student populations. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as SUST 433)

subject: EDCS
title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education
description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawai‘i as our place of learning and teaching. (Cross-listed as STE 440)

subject: EDCS
title: Methods and Materials in Science
description: Selecting and using methods and materials, demonstrations and simulations, open-ended experimentation, inquiry and discovery, task analysis measurement tools and techniques, activities from various curricula, opportunity for individualized goals and projects. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: STE 323, STE 404(H), teaching experience; or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers, including criteria for evaluation and planning. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SPED 451)
prerequisites: (HDFS 230 (or concurrent), HDFS 331 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: DS Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper. (Cross-listed as EDEF 453 and WGSS 453)

subject: EDCS
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education. (Cross-listed as STE 480)

subject: EDCS
title: Problem Solving in Mathematics Education
description: Experiencing and learning to teach heuristics of solving mathematical problems; designing curricula, classroom organization, evaluative measures for problem solving.

subject: EDCS
title: Difficulties in Learning Mathematics
description: Identification, analysis, and remediation of difficulties in learning mathematics.

subject: EDCS
title: Language, Learning and Teaching
description: Examines the role that language plays in the social construction of knowledge within various disciplines, K–adult. Collaborative group learning strategies will be modeled. A-F only.
prerequisites: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Advanced Topics in Reading
description: Current theories and teaching strategies of reading throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Topics include psychological, sociological, and cultural foundations of reading; 21st century literacies; emergent literacy; diversity; multilingual learners, formative assessment; state/national initiatives.
prerequisites: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Advanced Topics in Writing and Oral Language
description: Current theories and teaching strategies of writing and oral language throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Focus on teaching writing and oral language as tools for learning and to demonstrate learning.
prerequisites: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Children’s Literature in the Elementary Curriculum
description: In-depth examination of traditional and current books/media, birth through young adult, with emphasis on applications in schools or other educational contexts. Focus on use of narrative, exposition, and other genres across the curriculum. A-F only.
prerequisites: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Effective Writing Practices
description: Analysis and practical application of principles and strategies of effective writing and informed writing instruction in K-12 classrooms. (Summer only)

subject: EDCS
title: Literacy Coaching and Leadership
description: Exploration and application of literacy specialist roles. Includes teaching, coaching, providing resources, advocating for all students, and collaborating with other professionals. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, action research, mixed methods, and curriculum based assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal. (Cross-listed as DIS 606)

subject: EDCS
title: New Literacies Leadership +
description: New approaches to analyzing 21st century literacies K-12, including visual, media, digital, and critical literacies as well as developing leadership practices in multi-literacies pedagogy. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 608)

subject: EDCS
title: Early Career Teaching, K-12
description: Focuses on research and practice related to the first five years of teaching. Especially recommended for beginning teachers and graduate students interested in this stage of teaching development. Repeatable one time.

subject: EDCS
title: Early Literacy and Language Development
description: Theory and practice for PK-3 early literacy and language development. Focus is on content knowledge and pedagogical strategies that support the optimal development of oral language, reading, and writing skills in PK-3 classrooms. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Early Childhood Education: Advanced Topics
description: Analysis and practical application of selected early childhood education program and/ or instructional materials. Restricted to majors. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Social and Cultural Constructions of Childhood
description: Seminar examines the interrelated socially constructed concepts of children and childhood and places them in the larger contexts informed by sociological, anthropological, historical, critical, and technological perspectives. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum Leadership (Alpha)
description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

subject: EDCS
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as SUST 623)

subject: EDCS
title: School Mathematics Curriculum
description: Analysis of research related to teaching and learning school mathematics, application of research to classroom practices. Appraisal of recent curriculum trends; critical examination of assumptions underlying proposed curriculum changes.

subject: EDCS
title: Social Studies Curriculum
description: Examination and evaluation of social science content, societal values and research findings as basis for development and revision of social studies materials, tex

subject: ACC
title: Introduction to Accounting I
description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part I. A-F only.

subject: ACC
title: Introduction to Accounting II
description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part II.

subject: ACC
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
description: Accounting process and the application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of cash, receivables, inventories, property plant and equipment, depreciation and depletion, intangibles, and current liabilities.
prerequisites: 200 and 210, or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better)

subject: ACC
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
description: Application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of long-term liabilities, investments, contributed capital, retained earnings, accounting changes and errors, income recognition, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and statement of cash flows.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Internship
description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Term paper and meetings with faculty advisor required. CR/NC only.

subject: ACC
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research of a special area in major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated.
prerequisites: Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

subject: ACC
title: Federal Individual Income Taxation
description: Examines federal income tax concepts, such as gross income, exclusions, deductions, exemptions, and tax credits, especially for sole proprietors. Introduces taxation of property transactions. Development of professional writing skills is integral to this course.
prerequisites: 200 and 210, or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better)

subject: ACC
title: Taxation of Business Entities
description: A survey of the general concepts, rules, and practices involved in the taxation of sole-proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, and subchapter S corporations.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Accounting systems analysis, control and design in manual and computerized environments. Knowledge and skills of information technology for auditing AIS systems. Hands-on experience with microcomputers and a computerized accounting system. A-F only.
prerequisites: 323 (with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 (with C or better)

subject: ECE
title: Communication System Performance
description: Fundamental performance limits, signal detection and estimation, modulation, intersymbol interference, equalization adaptive filtering, sequence detection, synchronization, fading multipath channels, spread spectrum.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: Fundamentals of computer communication networks including modeling, performance evaluation, routing, flow control, local area networks, distributed algorithms, and optimization algorithms.

subject: ECE
title: Machine Learning
description: Learning theory, pattern recognition and regression; gradient based algorithms and least square algorithms; Kernel methods; Bayesian learning algorithms; ensemble learning and boosting; principal component analysis; independent component analysis, and clustering; reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Information Theory
description: Measure of information, coding for discrete sources, discrete memoryless channels and capacity, the noisy channel coding theorem, source coding with fidelity criterion, rate-distortion theory, multiuser channels.

subject: ECE
title: Source Coding
description: Theory and applications of source coding, rate-distortion theory, companding, lattice coding, tree coding, trellis coding, entropy-constrained coding, asymptotic theory, predictive and differential encoding, combined source/channel coding, vector quantization.

subject: ECE
title: Error-Control Coding I
description: Linear block codes, soft and hard decision decodings, correction of random errors, cyclic codes, BCH codes, Reed-Solomon codes, majority logic decodable codes, burst-error correcting codes, concatenated codes.

subject: ECE
title: Error-Control Coding II
description: Convolutional codes, Viterbi algorithm, coded modulation, multistage decoding, concatenated coded modulation, probabilistic decoding, turbo codes, low density parity check codes and iterative decoding.

subject: ECE
title: Linear System Theory
description: State space theory of linear systems, controllability, observability, stability, irreducible realizations.

subject: ECE
title: Nonlinear Control Systems
description: Digital simulations, phase-plane analysis, limit cycles and amplitude bounds, Lyapunov’s theorem, circle criterion of stability, lure systems, Popov’s stability theorem.

subject: ECE
title: Optimal Control Systems
description: Optimal controls introduced through parametric optimization, calculus of variations, Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton-Jacobi equations, Pontryagin’s maximum principle, minimum-time and minimum-fuel problems, dynamic programming, applications.

subject: ECE
title: Robust Control
description: Multivariable frequency response design, signals and systems, linear fractional transformations, LQG Control, Full Information H-infinity Controller Synthesis, H-infinity filtering, model reduction, the four-block problem.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Architecture I
description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs. (Cross-listed as ICS 660)

subject: ECE
title: Computer Systems
description: Modern operating system software, process communication, distributed systems, device drivers. Software development and maintenance, integration of software packages. Projects reflecting special interests of faculty.

subject: ECE
title: Telecommunication Networks
description: Telecommunication-network architecture; switching, broadcast, and wireless networks; protocols, interfaces, routing, flow- and congestion-control techniques; intelligent network architecture; service creation capabilities; multimedia, voice, data, and video networks and services.

subject: ECE
title: Wireless and Mobile Security
description: Security and privacy design principles and application in wireless and mobile devices, networks, and services, as well as research methodology in wireless and mobile security. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Electromagnetic Theory and Applications
description: Solutions of Maxwell’s equations and applications to radiation and propagation of electromagnetic waves.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Microwave Engineering
description: Advanced RF and microwave circuit design for wireless applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
description: Develop comprehensive understanding of computations techniques for solving engineering electromagnetic problems formulated in terms of integral or differential equations. Eigenvalue problems, radiation, and electromagnetics scattering problems will be discussed and computer programming is required. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: ECE 471 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Systems
description: Systems analysis and electronic instrumentation methods in biomedicine. Network and control-loop modeling, computer simulation, biological transducers, and analysis of electronic and physiological systems.
prerequisites: ECE 326, ECE 326L, and ECE 371; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Biosensors and Bioelectronics
description: Advanced topics in the design of biological detection technologies. Topics include fundamentals of electrochemistry, electrochemical biosensors, DNA and protein biochips, and bioelectronics for bio-signal conditioning and processing. (Once a year)

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Microdevices
description: Design and fabrication of micro- and nanodevices for biomedical applications. Topics include micro- and nanoscale physics, microfluidic physics and microfluidic devices, and micro- and nanoscale fabrication techniques. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Signal Processing and Analysis
description: Biomedical signals, digital filters and filter banks, spike train analysis, time-scale and time-frequency representations, nonlinear techniques, Lomb’s algorithm and the Hilbert transform, modeling, Volterra series, Wiener series, Poisson-Wiener series, multichannel data, causality. (Spring only)
degrees: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: ECE
title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (Alpha) (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECE
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: ECE
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for MS in electrical and computer engineering.

subject: ECE
title: Directed Instruction
description: Student assists in classroom instruction under direction and close supervision of faculty member. CR/NC only.

subject: ECE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD in electrical and computer engineering.

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Freshman Seminar
description: Overview of the engineering field, the different disciplines, and opportunities. Success strategies for studying engineering. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Engineering
description: Topics include the engineering disciplines, the development of problem solving and technical communication skills, the design process and analysis methods using a team design project, and introduction to programming in Matlab for engineering applications. Freshman standing only.

subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors. Freshmen only. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as BUS 102)

subject: ENGR
title: Freshman Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for freshman-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a sophomore (ENGR 296). Repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: ENGR
title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders. (Cross-listed as IS 250)

subject: ENGR
title: Sophomore Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for sophomore-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a junior (ENGR 396). Sophomore standing or higher. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ECE 296)

subject: ENGR
title: Career Development Seminar
description: Introduction to career development as it pertains to engineering and business industry; client relations, networking, job skills, career assessment and direction. Repeatable one time. (Fall only)

subject: ENGR
title: Junior Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for junior-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue w

subject: AMST
title: Food, Culture, and Empire
description: DS. Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 466)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.

subject: AMST
title: Victims, Virtue, and Violence
description: DH. Examination of the history and significance of melodrama as a dominant mode of American cultural production from the early republic to the present, with a focus on issues of race, gender, and national identity. (Cross-listed as ES 450 and WGSS 450)

subject: AMST
title: Popular Culture
description: DH. Major themes, modes, and media of popular or mass culture in the U.S.; emphasis on cultural trends and social implications.

subject: AMST
title: The ’20s and ’30s
description: DH. Novelists, painters, poets, jazz musicians as examples of culture of the 1920s and 1930s in America.

subject: AMST
title: Culture, Society, and Literature
description: DL. Literary and non-fictive exploration of the intellectual and moral response of Americans to institutions and culture of 20th-century marketplace economy.

subject: AMST
title: Fashioning America
description: DS. Examines linkages between American identity, representation, labor and capital through fashion theory, clothing discourses and other practices of textile production over history.

subject: AMST
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: DL. Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities. (Cross-listed as ENG 455 and WGSS 445)

subject: AMST
title: Art of the United States
description: DH. Emphasis on the 18th and 19th centuries. (Cross-listed as ART 472)

subject: AMST
title: Museum Interpretations
description: DH. Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used by museums to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Considers how interpretations contribute to cultural knowledge. Repeatable one time. (Crosslisted as ART 481)

subject: AMST
title: Film in American Culture
description: DL. Comprehensive survey of varieties of film experience from historical and contemporary points of view.

subject: AMST
title: Sports in America
description: DS. Sports as reflected in literature, films, and TV. Focus on ethical dimensions of sports and sporting cultures; writing emphasis.

subject: AMST
title: Early 20th Century American Art
description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as ART 460)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: ART 176 or consent.

subject: AMST
title: America’s World Role
description: DS. Examination of America’s role in modern world affairs, against the background of history, perceptions, and values.

subject: AMST
title: America and Africa
description: DH. American attitudes toward Africa, as well as how Africa has functioned within the dynamics of American culture and history.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience in Asia
description: DH. Examination of various forms of U.S. engagement with Asia, with particular attention to the role of Hawai‘i as the site, agent, and object of engagement. Emphasis on developing critical reading and expository writing skills.

subject: AMST
title: Religion, Sex, and Gender in the U.S.
description: DH. Examines religious and ethical conflicts about sexuality and gender nonconformity in contemporary America. Students gain knowledge, practical wisdom, and communication skills to negotiate moral disagreement in a pluralistic society.

subject: AMST
title: Preservation: Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific
description: DH. Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions. (Cross-listed as ARCH 474)

subject: AMST
title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/ Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/ HAER). Repeatable three times, up to 24 credits. (Cross-listed as ARCH 472)
prerequisites: AMST, ARCH, and HIS majors only. Pre: consent.

subject: AMST
title: Senior Capstone Project
description: Capstone course for American studies students to undertake a major research-based project.

subject: AMST
title: World Maritime History
description: DH. Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples. (Cross-listed as HIST 489)

subject: AMST
title: (Alpha) Topics in American Studies
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment. Repeatable one time.

subject: AMST
title: Readings in American Studies
description: Directed readings and research for majors.

subject: AMST
title: Approaches to American Studies
description: Introductory survey of methodological issues underlying research in American studies.

subject: AMST
title: Patterns of American Cultures
description: American cultural origins and development.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Research and Professional Development
description: Prepares advanced graduate students to present original research findings to colleagues, write for peer review, design undergraduate classes in their areas of expertise, and participate actively in their fields. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: (AMST 600 and AMST 601) with a minimum grade of B-.

subject: AMST
title: Early America
description: Interdisciplinary approach to understanding early American culture and history. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as HIST 632B)

subject: AMST
title: Asian America
description: The Asian American experience from an interdisciplinary and humanities perspective. Asian American history, literature, media, and theater arts. Comparative study of Hawai‘i and the Continental U.S.

subject: AMST
title: Women in American Culture
description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method. (Cross-listed as WGSS 612)

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: American West
description: Examination of the U.S. colonization of the American West. Topics include: European-indigenous relations, migration and labor, regional literature, frontier ideology, ethnic conflict, and new community formation. A-F only. (Cross-listed as HIST 639F)

subject: AMST
title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts. (Cross-listed as WGSS 614)

subject: AMST
title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 616)

subject: AMST
title: Social and Cultural Diversity in America
description: Examination of selected subcultures in America.

subject: AMST
title: American Sexualities
description: Aspects of sexual identity within the context of American culture.

subject: AMST
title: Slavery and Modern Memory
description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts. A-F only. (Cross-listed as HIST 619)

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Identity
description: Interdisciplinary and comparative focus on how Indigenous identity is constructed, negotiated, asserted, ascribed, and deconstructed within and without Indigenous communities with attention to the U.S.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: graduate level standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: American Architecture
description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations. (Cross-listed as ARCH 623)

subject: AMST
title: Wilderness in America
description: American wilderness as both physical setting and social construction. A-F only.

subject: AMST
title: Material Culture
description: Physical artifacts considered as documents of American cultural and regional development.

subject: AMST
title: Environment and Society
description: Technological development in cultural perspective; its relation to the American environment, science, capitalism, public policy, and values.

subject: AMST
title: Mass Media
description: Appraisal of major media of communications in American society with attention to political, educational, cultural, and ethical implications.

subject: AMST
title: Technologies of War and Media
description: Critical examination of the relationship between war and media with particular attention to the overlapping histories of technologies of perception and destruction in the modern era and to the military-entertainment complex today.

subject: AMST
title: Public History and Commemoration
description: Approaches to public presentations of history and examination of various

subject: DH
title: Advanced Health and Diagnostic Assessment for Pediatric Patients
description: Focus on advanced health and diagnostic assessment for pediatric patients. Includes behavior management techniques as well as oral habits and subsequent malocclusions and speech difficulties. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Pharmacological Principles and Clinical Therapeutics in Pediatric Dental Care
description: Focus on pharmacological principles and clinical therapeutics in pediatric dental care. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Simulation Lab
description: Focus on interprofessional practice principles and competencies while providing students an opportunity to participate in interprofessional team simulations to address health care issues of children. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical I
description: Field experience. Clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: DH
title: Management of Pediatric Dental Emergencies
description: Focus on the management of dental emergencies in children. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Community-Based Dental Hygiene Care of Vulnerable and Special Needs Children
description: Emphasizes community-based oral health promotion, dental disease risk reduction and management in children 0-5 years of age with a focus on vulnerable and special needs populations. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Community-Based Practice Capstone
description: Provides an opportunity to synthesize, analyze, and develop solutions to an oral health care problem affecting children ages 0-5 years. Requires one credit to be spent in fieldwork to meet course requirements. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical II
description: Advanced clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DH
title: Directed Reading, Field Work, or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading, field work, or research for major under supervision in related areas of dentistry and dental hygiene.

subject: DRB
title: Fertilization and Early Development
description: Lecture on the basics of vertebrate and invertebrate fertilization and early embryonic development. Open to all graduate students. (Fall only)

subject: DRB
title: Seminar in Developmental and Reproductive Biology I
description: Presentations of current research carried out by developmental and reproductive biology graduate program faculty.

subject: DRB
title: Developmental and Reproductive Biology Scientific Investigations
description: Discussion of current research in developmental and reproductive biology. A-F only.

subject: DRB
title: Stem Cell Biology
description: Seminar designed to teach graduate students and advanced undergraduate students about current topics relating to stem cell biology, as well as the application of stem cells to modern medicine. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DRB
title: Applied Developmental and Reproductive Biology
description: Combined lecture-lab on current technologies and methods for mammalian reproduction and developmental biology. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: DRB
title: DRB Research Rotation
description: Introductory laboratory research experience under the supervision of faculty. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: DRB
title: Directed Research
description: Research experience in developmental and reproductive biology. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: DRB
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: DRB
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: DIS
title: Foundations in Disability and Diversity
description: Focuses on disability as a category of diversity and identity, as well as diversity within disability. Different strategies used to increase the freedom or liberty of people with disabilities are critically examined. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Accessible Learning Technology
description: Focuses on creating accessible technology and instructional media, developing long-term resources, advancing accessible social interaction between students and students with instructors, and using case studies as examples of good practices. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Disability History and Culture: From Homer to Hip Hop
description: How have people over many centuries, and from broad geographical perspectives perceived and treated individuals with disabilities? An overview of the history of the conditions in which people with disabilities lived. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, Action Research, mixed methods, and Curriculum Based Assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal. (Cross-listed as EDCS 606)

subject: DIS
title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawai‘i and our global community. A-F only. (Summer only) (Cross-listed as EDCS 650 and KRS 650)

subject: DIS
title: Sexuality & Health
description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health. (Cross-listed as KRS 651)

subject: DIS
title: Supporting Multilingual Learners
description: Strategies for identifying and adopting best practices that support all students in inclusive learning environments with an emphasis on STEM curriculum for English Language Learners; (B) science; (C) technology; (D) math. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Practicum in Applied Behavior Analysis
description: Supervised field experience in applied behavior analysis. The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings. Repeatable four times or up to 15 credits. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Disability History Through the Ages
description: A historical overview of disability that visits diverse perspectives, attitudes, and treatment toward individuals with disabilities through many centuries, societies, and cultures throughout the world; and how people with disabilities perceived themselves. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Multicultural Issues in Disabilities
description: Provide background and understanding of various Pacific Rim cultural issues in the conceptualization and treatment of individuals with disabilities and their families. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Special Topics in Disability and Diversity Studies
description: Explores disability and diversity across time to gain an understanding and context of issues such as difference, culture, identity, community, privilege, and oppression and how the past affects the present and future. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Disability and Diversity Issues
description: Develop understanding of current issues faced by individuals with disabilities and their families within the disability paradigm and across cultures.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Team Development
description: Develop knowledge and skills to participate effectively on interdisciplinary teams for the common goal of promoting service integration and coordination of education, social, health, mental health, and other services with individuals with disabilities and their families. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Assessment
description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS). A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Advanced Interdisciplinary Assessment
description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS). A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Seminar on Disability Issues
description: In-depth explorations of current and compelling interdisciplinary topics related to advancing the social, political, educational, and economic integration of individuals with disabilities of all ages. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Portfolio/Field Work
description: Interdisciplinary community experience and portfolio in disability and diversity studies. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Directed reading and/or research. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. Repeatable one time. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as EDCS 780 and LTEC 780)

subject: EPET
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written co

subject: ENGR
title: Sophomore Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for sophomore-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a junior (ENGR 396). Sophomore standing or higher. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ECE 296)

subject: ENGR
title: Career Development Seminar
description: Introduction to career development as it pertains to engineering and business industry; client relations, networking, job skills, career assessment and direction. Repeatable one time. (Fall only)

subject: ENGR
title: Junior Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for junior-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a senior. Repeatable unlimited times. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ECE 396)

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Management
description: Introduction to engineering management of projects and its outcomes. Development of professional skills for the systematic formulation of problems and solutions to efficiently deduce project viability. Emphasis on collaborative teamwork and performance evaluations and improvements. Senior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: ENGR
title: Field Experience
description: Supervised internship in engineering practice under professional and faculty direction. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: junior standing in engineering and consent

subject: ENG
title: Composition I
description: Introduction to the rhetorical, conceptual and stylistic demands of writing at the university level; instruction in composing processes, search strategies, and writing from sources. Students may not earn credit for both ENG 100 and 190.

subject: ENG
title: Composition I
description: Introduction to the rhetorical, conceptual and stylistic demands of writing at the university level; instruction in composing processes, search strategies, and writing from sources. Students may not earn credit for both ENG 100 and 190.

subject: ENG
title: Composition for Transfer Students to UHM
description: Introduction to the rhetorical, conceptual and stylistic demands of writing at the university level; instruction in composing processes, search strategies, and writing from sources. Restricted to students with more than 24 credits. Students may not earn credit for both ENG 100 and 190. A-F only.

subject: ENG
title: Composition II
description: Further study of rhetorical, conceptual, and stylistic demands of writing; instruction develops the writing and research skills covered in Composition I.

subject: ENG
title: Business Writing
description: Practice in informative, analytical, persuasive writing. Students may not earn credit for both ENG 209 and BUS 209.

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to Literature: Literary History
description: Study of significant works of selected historical periods. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction. Repeatable one time. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to Literature: Genre
description: Study of significant works of selected genres. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction. Repeatable one time. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to Literature: Culture and Literature
description: Study of significant works of selected cultures and cultural formations. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction. Repeatable one time. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to Literature: Creative Writing and Literature
description: Study of significant works through analytical and creative writing. Repeatable one time. No waiver.

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to Literature: Rhetoric and Literature
description: Study of significant works of literature and rhetoric through a rhetorical analytical lens. A significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to Rhetoric
description: History of theory and practices of rhetoric from Classical to contemporary periods; e.g., Plato, Aristotle, Cicero, Quintilian, Augustine, Sidney, K. Burke, DeMan; (B) Classical-Renaissance; (C) EnlightenmentContemporary. Repeatable one time for different alphas.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: History of the English Language
description: Basic concepts and methods for the study of the English language; general history of the language; grammar and usage, issues of language diversity and standardization; English as a world language.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Modern English Grammar
description: Introduction to the structure of present-day English for native speakers and others with advanced competency.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Argumentative Writing
description: Theory and practice of written argument; emphasis on the role of invention in argumentative discourse and on the nature of rhetorical proof.
prerequisites: FW and either 200 or one ENG DL course, or consent

subject: ENG
title: Rhetoric, Composition, and Computers
description: Introduction to computer-based writing and reading technologies. Study of principles of traditional and online composition. Writing traditional and multimedia essays.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Technical Writing
description: Combined lecture/ lab preparing students to write about technical subjects for specialists and laypersons. Introduces theory of technical communication and document design and teaches students to make use of relevant technology. A-F only.
prerequisites: FW and either 200 or one ENG DL course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Autobiographical Writing
description: Writing clear, effective prose based on the writer’s own experiences and ideas with a focus on the ethical questions such writing entails.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Creative Writing
description: Basic principles of the craft as developed through writing in two of the following genres: fiction, poetry, drama, screenwriting, and creative nonfiction.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Introduction to English Studies
description: Introduction to English Studies, including reading and writing about the purpose, practice, and potential of literary and rhetorical study of texts; consideration given to Hawaiian and/or Pacific texts in cultural and historical context. Restricted to ENG majors/minors and Secondary Education-English majors only. Prerequisite to 400-level work for ENG majors.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Backgrounds of Western Literature
description: Sources of European and American literary themes and allusions; myth, legend, and folklore of Western cultures; e.g., Classical texts, Arthurian romances, King James Bible.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Literatures of the World
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the transhistorical, transnational, and/or comparative study of literatures in English and in translation from regions around the world.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Medieval Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literature before 1500.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Renaissance British Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry, and drama in English from 1500 to 1660.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: Restoration/18th Century British Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry, and drama in English from 1660 to 1780, exclusive of Milton.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: 19th Century Literature in English (Except American)
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of 19th century prose and poetry in English.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: British Literature After 1900
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry, and drama in English from 1900 to the present.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: American Literature to Mid-19th Century
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry, and drama in American literature through the middle of the 19th century.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ENG
title: American Literature Mid-19th to Mid20th Century
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry and drama in American literature from the middle of the 19th

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Astrophysics
description: DP Advanced survey of stellar astrophysics, including application of astrometry, photometry, and spectrometry to determine fundamental stellar properties; stellar structure and evolution of single and binary stars; astrophysical distance determination methods; stellar nucleosynthesis.

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies & Cosmology
description: DP Survey of extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, including: galaxy morphology and kinematics; luminosity functions; dark matter; properties of galaxy groups/ clusters; gravitational lensing; redshifts; cosmological models; the Big Bang; thermal history of the Universe; structure formation. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274; MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A.

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: DP Observations and physical nature of planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and other small bodies; formation of the Solar System; discovery of other planetary systems; solar activity. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 300; and PHYS 152 or 274; and MATH 216, 242, or 252A.

subject: ASTR
title: General Relativity & Cosmology
description: DP Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as PHYS 470)
prerequisites: PHYS 274; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: 242.

subject: ASTR
title: Senior Research Project
description: Seminar focusing on development of professional skills for astronomical research, and on scientific writing as a tool for organizing research. A final paper describing a supervised research project is required. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ASTR
title: Being a Professional Astronomer
description: Seminar for beginning graduate students focusing on professional skills needed for astronomy and discussing possible research opportunities. Repeatable one time. ASTR majors only. Graduate students only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: The Interstellar Medium
description: Astrophysics of diffuse matter, HII regions, molecular clouds, etc. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Interiors and Evolution
description: Structure and evolution; energy sources, radiative processes; relations to observables. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies
description: Observations and stellar dynamics of elliptical and spiral galaxies including our galaxy, globular clusters, and dark matter. Galaxy formation and evolution. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ASTR
title: Cosmology
description: Geometry and evolution of the universe. Dark matter. Early universe. Formation of large–scale structure, galaxies, and clusters. Cosmological models. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: Survey of observational data and physical concepts on planets and smaller bodies; formation of planetary systems; solar activity. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Radiative Transfer Stellar Atmospheres
description: Excitation, ionization, and radiative transfer in stellar atmospheres; model atmospheres, formation of line and continuum radiation. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Astrophysical Techniques
description: Telescopes, positional astronomy, photon detection, error analysis, photometry, spectroscopy. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomical Instrumentation
description: Design and operation of astronomical instrumentation. Physics of optical and infrared detectors. Wavefront sensors and adaptive optics. Radio and infrared interferometry. Optical design: methods and software. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ASTR
title: Fundamentals of Astrophysics
description: Applications of fundamental physics to astrophysical situations. Elements of general relativity. Basics of hydrodynamics and shock waves. Radiative processes, high energy astrophysics. Modern dynamics. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: General Relativity
description: Introduction to gravity and general relativity. Tensor basics, classical scalar, vector and tensor field theories. Exact symmetric Einstein equation, gravito-magnetic weak field, and radiation solutions. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Active Galaxies
description: Phenomenology of active galactic nuclei, black holes, accretion flows and jets, emission mechanisms, host galaxies, and cosmic evolution. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ASTR
title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as CHEM 657 and ERTH 657)

subject: ASTR
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ASTR
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar I
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar II
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar III
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrobiology Seminar: Origin, Evolution and the Role of Water for Life in the Universe
description: Interdisciplinary research topics in astrobiology as they relate to the theme of water: formation in space, role in creating pre-biotic molecules, delivery to earth, and terrestrial planet habitability. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: graduate level sciences and ideas, or consent.

subject: ASTR
title: Scientific Grant Writing
description: Principles of scientific grant writing are taught by working on draft proposals through a mix of lectures, discussions, and hands on activities. The final proposal will be reviewed and evaluated via a review panel. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: Programming and Algorithms for Astronomers
description: Distillation of modern computer science fundamentals and paradigms, with applications to astronomy. Common algorithms and essential programming techniques.
