Assignments include extensive Python programming practice. Open to graduate students in any physical science. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques. Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as PHYS 760)

subject: ASTR
title: Star Formation
description: Molecular clouds, collapse processes, physics of circumstellar disks and accretion, properties of young stars, outflows and jets, formation of binaries, extrasolar planets and planet formation, meteorites and the early solar system. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ASTR
title: Astro-ph Seminar
description: Seminar discussions of the most recent research papers covering all areas of astronomy. Student lead discussion sessions and discuss papers of their choice during the semester. ASTR majors only. Graduate students only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: ASTR
title: Cosmology Seminar
description: Students and researchers will review and discuss the most important and exciting cosmological results in depth. ASTR and PHYS majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Stars and Planets Lunch and Talks (SPLAT) Seminar
description: Seminar for graduate students and researchers discussing the latest results on solar, stellar, and exoplanet research. Repeatable one time. ASTR majors only. Graduate students only. CR/NC only.

subject: ASTR
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
description: DP Introductory physical science course for all undergraduates in any major. A non-mathematical introduction to basic atmospheric variables, Earth’s past climates, global warming, air pollution, El Nino, hurricanes, tornadoes, and forecasting weather in Hawai‘i.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate Lab
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Exercises with meteorological data and measurement systems. Characteristics of Hawaiian winds, temperatures, and rainfall

subject: ATMO
title: Pacific Climates and Cultures
description: Highlights the interface between the observed weather and climate of the Pacific and the past and future culture of the people of the Hawaiian and Pacific islands. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: FQ Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real- world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ERTH 150 and OCN 150)
prerequisites: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X).

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to MET Undergraduate Directed Research
description: Students gain familiarity with ATMO research. Students can select 1-3 credits per semester for maximum 6 credits over 4 semesters. Students must pre-arrange research and reading content with instructor. Repeatable three times, up to six credits. Freshman and sophomore standing only. CR/NC only.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Processes and Phenomena
description: DP Atmospheric variables, gas laws, radiation processes, ther

subject: BIOL
title: Population Genetics
description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations. (Cross-listed as CMB 650)

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: To provide elective courses for undergraduates in the biomedical sciences specialties.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Research Review
description: Research elective for medical students.

subject: BIOM
title: Global Health and Medicine: Emerging Problems and Impact
description: Analysis of emerging problems and impact in countries on a multidimensional perspective.

subject: BIOM
title: Introduction to Clinical Nutrition
description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions.
prerequisites: BIOL 171 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or ZOOL 141 or consent

subject: BIOM
title: Introduction to Clinical Research
description: Instruction in developing clinical research questions and creating a concise protocol that includes a literature review, study design, subject recruitment and sampling, instruments, other measures and bioinformatics, sample size, consent form, budget and timetable.

subject: BIOM
title: Legal and Regulatory Issues and Bioethics
description: Ethical dilemmas in clinical research are identified and resolved in cases, research on human subjects regulation are discussed. Research misconduct is defined. Ethical considerations in protocol developed in the Designing Clinical Research course are resolved. (Cross-listed as CMB 626)

subject: BIOM
title: Translational Research Methods
description: Lectures focus on translational research methods through selected genetic and acquired diseases including cancer, neurodevelopmental, inflammatoryimmune, and metabolic conditions with insight into analyses of DNA, RNA, genomics-proteomics, cell and animal models, and advanced imaging.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Protocol Development
description: Provides training in proposal development. Governance structures of funding agencies; funding opportunities and decisions; review processes; NIH application and processes; reading RFAs; compliance issues; cultural sensitivity; and types of questions using databases are addressed.

subject: BIOM
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective.

subject: BIOM
title: Foundations of Biomedical Ethics
description: Explores the foundations of biomedical ethics via small group seminars and discussion, presentations.

subject: BIOM
title: Advanced Ethics in Biomedical Research II
description: Develop biomedical ethics through case studies to incite discussions on topics such as gene therapy, gene enhancement, genetic counseling, informed consent, health care professional/patient and investigator/student participant communication, advanced directives and living wills, clinical research in developing countries, clinical research in ethnic minority and socio-economically disadvantaged populations, and non-discrimination in health care and research settings.

subject: BIOM
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research II
description: Explore topics in cultural competence in greater depth, encouraging trainees to address issues from a unified yet flexible conceptual framework. Involves building knowledge, skills and action plans to address a range of learning styles and to appreciate and benefit from diversity.

subject: BIOM
title: PhD Team Building Seminar
description: Seminar focuses on teaching participants to work independently and collaborate in order to accomplish specific results. Students will be exposed to group dynamics, communication, healthy competition, conflict resolution, and innovative means of crossing boundaries between departments, organizations, industries and disciplines.

subject: BIOM
title: Medical Genetics
description: Focus on heritable disorders, genetic mechanisms, patterns of inheritance, phenotype-genotype correlations, genetic/ environmental factors, clinical diagnoses, genomic and precision medicine.

subject: BIOM
title: Mentored Research Practicum
description: Conduct research under the direction of a mentor. Participants will be responsible for submission of a proposal, acquisition of IRB approval, and conduct of the project.

subject: BIOM
title: Advanced Biostatistics for Clinical Research
description: Current methods for analyzing longitudinal and clustered, clinical data through lectures, discussions, and a group analysis. Topic areas include multi-level, multi-state, multi-process, and structural equation models.

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research
description: Students may register on approval of department.

subject: BIOM
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: BIOM
title: Disasters and Pandemics: Medical and PH Management and Risk Communication
description: Assess impact on health in disasters and diseases. Enhances research skills related to management and communication.

subject: BIOM
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: BOT
title: Freshman Seminar
description: Discussion of hot topics in botany, including conservation of rare plants, invasive species, marine botany, ethnobotany, poisonous plants, evolution in action, fungal networks, and careers in botany with emphasis on Hawaiian examples. Students should enroll in BOT 100 and 101/101L, or BOT 100 and BIOL 171/171L.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany
description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany
description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany Lab
description: Lab observations and experiments illustrating basic principles of plant biology.

subject: BOT
title: Plants, People, and Culture
description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

subject: BOT
title: Plants, People, and Culture
description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance
description: Introduction to the native flora of Hawai‘i, its origin, evolution and ecology, and the observation, identification, and systematics of the Hawaiian flora.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance Lab
description: The exploration of concepts and the process of science through hands-on experience in studying Hawaiian and introduced plants, their ecology, and cultural significance.

subject: BOT
title: Magical Mushrooms and Mystical Molds
description: Impact of fungi in nature and on humankind. Selected historical events in which fungi played a significant role, their activities as decomposers and pathogens, and their uses as sources for mind altering drugs in religious ceremonies and in food and beverage production in various societies.

subject: BOT
title: Campus Plants
description: Nontechnical course emphasizing recognition of the many interesting tropical plants seen on campus; origin, status in Hawai‘i, and cultural and economic uses of campus plants.

subject: BOT
title: Sophomore Seminar
description: Presentations by faculty highlighting research in tropical ecosystems. Topics include alien species, biodiversity, ecosystem services, ethnobotany, marine ecology, plant-animal interactions, and systematics of Hawaiian species. Assigned reading and writing exercises from papers in current journals.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity
description: Significance of evolutionary trends in the plant world, including reproductive, morphological, and life history adaptations by algae, fungi, and vascular plants.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity Lab
description: Lab exercises in the morphology and systematics of land plants, fungi, and algae.

subject: BOT
title: Foundations of Current Botany II
description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in ecology, plant interactions with other plants or animals, and ecosystem functioning. BOT majors only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: graduate standing in BOT or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Darwin’s Origin of Species
description: Study and discussion of Charles Darwin’s Origin of Species, 1st edition 1859, and related current literature. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: BA or BS in BOT, BIOL, GEOL, or related field; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Graduate Research Skills
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Survey of major research areas in the botanical sciences with emphasis upon research opportunities in Hawai‘i and an overview of 1) skills needed by botanical researchers including writing scientific papers and proposals, practicing ethical research procedures, and collection of specimens; and 2) equipment used by botanical researchers including computers, cameras, measuring and monitoring equipment, and global positioning systems. Lecture/ discussion, laboratory. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: graduate standing in biological science or approval.

subject: BOT
title: Botanical Seminar
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in botany. Repeatable three times.

subject: BOT
title: Advanced Botanical Problems
description: Investigation of any botanical problem; reading and laboratory work. Repeatable nine times.

subject: BOT
title: Perspectives in Modern Botany
description: Lectures by distinguished visiting professor on contemporary botanical topics in the lecturer’s area of expertise. No more than 6 credit hours may be counted toward the MS degree requirements. Repeatable five times.

subject: BOT
title: Ecohydrology: Theory and Modeling
description: Vegetative response to hydrologic controls and nutrient cycles; quantitative linkages between hydrological dynamics and ecological patterns/ processes. MatLab is used to develop and simulate ecohydrological models. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Quantitative Ethnobotany
description: Modern ethnobotanical field research project design, execution, data analysis, and documentation methods. Intended for students preparing to conduct field research studies. Lecture/discussion, term paper.
prerequisites: 105 and one of 201, 461, ANTH 200, or BIOL 172.

subject: BOT
title: Ethnoecological Methods
description: Field techniques for assessing the ecological effects of cultural uses of plants. Emphasis on documenting traditional and local patterns of plant use and measuring the effects on plant individuals, populations, communities, and landscapes.
prerequisites: previous course work in anthropology or biology.

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Ethnobiology
description: Practical field training experience for a scientific career conducting ethnobiological research. Repeatable one time. (Summer only)

subject: BOT
title: Invasion Biology
description: Theories, models, patterns, and predictive methods relating to the introduction, establishment, and spread of introduced organisms. Application of principles of invasion biology to conservation and natural resource management.
prerequisites: 456 or MICR 485; and BIOL 375; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Population Biology
description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology. (Cross-listed as ZOOL 652)
prerequisites: one of 456, NREM 680, PEPS 671, ZOOL 620, ZOOL 623; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Population Dynamics Models with R
description: Learn advanced modeling techniques to investigate the dynamics of size-structure populations (using matrix and integral population models in R), and discuss various applications in ecology and conservation biology. Recommended: students have working knowledge of calculus. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: BOT
title: Advances in Plant Ecology
description: A researchoriented course focusing on recent advances in all areas of plant ecology. Involves critical review of recent literature, independent research project, oral and written presentation of project results. Repeatable three times.

subject: BOT
title: Ecological Statistics with R
description: Learn how to choose appropriate statistical methods to test hypotheses in ecology, evolution, and conservation biology and applications using R as a platform. Lecture/discussion, term paper. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips. (Cross-listed as SUST 661)

subject: BOT
title: High Throughput Sequencing Approaches to Ecology and Evolution
description: Fundamentals of experimental design, lab techniques and data analysis to conduct research using high throughput sequencing. Students will work in groups to conduct an amplicon sequencing study with ten samples. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: BOT
title: Nomenclature and Practical Systematics
description: Modern issues of naming and classifying of organisms, with a botanical emphasis. Includes lectures, discussions, class projects, and field trips. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution
description: Molecular approaches to evolution, phylogenetics, and systematics. Basic use of chloroplast DNA, mitochondrial DNA, nuclear DNA, and electrophoresis. Phylogenetic analysis using parsimony, distance, and comparative methods. Repeatable two times. Recommended: 201.

subject: BOT
title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques. BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as ZOOL 670)

subject: BOT
title: Environmental Physiology Seminar
description: Environmental stress; pollution; salinity, geobotany, and other interactions between the environment and plant processes. Current literature emphasized at multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary levels.
prerequisites: graduate status in a biological science, geosciences, etc.; consent for well-prepared undergraduates.

subject: BOT
title: Marine Macrophytes Seminar
description: Discussion of current literature in physiological ecology, cellular and molecular adaptations to environmental factors by marine plants. Repeatable four times.

subject: BOT
title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants
description: Discussion of current studies in morphological, physiological, cellular, and molecular adaptation to marine environments by macroalgae, phytoplankton, and seagrasses. A-F only. Co-requisite: 682L.
prerequisites: upper division ecology class recommended, 480 (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants Lab
description: Field and laboratory research techniques and projects in the physiological ecology of algae and seagrasses. A-F only. Co-requisite: 682.
prerequisites: upper division ecology class recommended, 470L (or equivalent), 480 (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Biology
description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution, and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions. (Cross-listed as NREM 690 and ZOOL 690)

subject: BOT
title: Directed Research
description: Research preliminary to thesis or dissertation research. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: BOT
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for MS degree and approval of thesis proposal.

subject: BOT
title: Topics in Conservation Biology
description: Advanced topics in conservation and environmental biology. Repeatable three times, up to twelve credits. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ZOOL 750)

subject: BOT
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD and approval of dissertation proposal.

subject: BUS
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program. Repeatable four times. CR/NC only.

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors. ENGR and BUS majors only. Freshmen only. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ENGR 102)

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Business
description: Introduction to each of the functional areas of business. Intends to help students understand the interrelationships of business functional areas and the role of business in society. Stresses written communication in business. BUS majors only. Freshman or sophomore standing only. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Written Communication in Business
description: An interactive writing class stressing persuasive writing in the context of memos, letters, and business reports. A-F only. Students may not earn credit for both BUS 209 and ENG 209.

subject: BUS
title: Applied Math in Business
description: FQ Provides problem-solving and quantitative skills essential in business. Reviews algebra, mathematics of finance, calculus in business applications, probability, introductory statistics, and hypothesis testing.

subject: BUS
title: Statistical Analysis for Business Decisions
description: Problem recognition and formulation; stress on cross-disciplinary complex pr

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
description: Topics on production, consumption, labor market, asset market, economic growth, and business cycles are discussed with emphasis on real-economy applications and policy analysis. Implications of monetary, fiscal, and international finance and economic policies are explored. (Spring only)

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory I
description: Theory of the firm: production, costs, duality; theory of the market: competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition; theory of the consumer: preferences, expenditures, duality; expected utility theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory I
description: Neoclassical theory of real and monetary equilibrium, economics of J. M. Keynes, standard IS/LM models and aggregate demand/supply analysis in the closed and open economy, theory of rational expectations.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory II
description: General equilibrium analysis: production, consumption and Walrasian equilibria; Pareto efficiency, fundamental theorems of welfare economics; externalities; public goods; game theory; information theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory II
description: Models of economic growth and fluctuations; stochastic and dynamic macroeconomic models; econometric testing of rational expectations models; theory of public debt; current topics in macroeconomic theory.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development
description: Nature and causes of economic growth and structural change. Roles of macroeconomic policy and foreign trade.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development Policy
description: Analysis of policies for the promotion of industrial and agricultural development. Project evaluation, industrial regulation, public administration, investment and capital market policies, land-use policies, trade policies, pricing, and stabilization.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development of Japan
description: Analysis of growth from Meiji period to present. Problems of population change, capital formation, income distribution, industrial structure.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory III
description: Game theory and strategic behavior. Economics of information and incentives principal-agent theory. Economic design. Applications include: theory of contracts; incentive compatible mechanism for provision of public goods; auction theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory III
description: Will equip students with the ability to understand, undertake, and critically evaluate theoretical and quantitative research in modern macroeconomics with a focus on the application of the search and matching methodology. (Alt. years)

subject: ECON
title: Mathematics for Economics
description: Sets, functions, limits, convexity, continuity; constrained and unconstrained optimization; difference and differential equations; matrix algebra; simultaneous equations; comparative statics; Kuhn-Tucker theory; game theory; mathematical programming.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics I
description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics II
description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference and forecasting of econometric models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series. (Cross-listed as AREC 634)

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics III
description: Will equip students with the ability to undertake, understand, and critically assess empirical research using state-of-the-at econometric methods. (Alt. years)

subject: ECON
title: Disasters and Economic Policy
description: Economic analysis of disasters. The economics of prevention and mitigation, as well as post-disaster economic consequences and policy, will be examined. Graduate students only.

subject: ECON
title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options. (Cross-listed as SUST 636)
prerequisites: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development. (Cross-listed as NREM 637 and SUST 637)

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Resource Economics
description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development. (Cross-listed as SUST 638)

subject: ECON
title: Marine Resource Economics
description: Seminar on the economics of the marine environment. Topics include fisheries management, ocean recreation, shipping, and coral reef protection. (Once a year)

subject: ECON
title: Foundations of Public Policy
description: Microeconomic principles for expenditure and tax policies. Externalities, public goods, non-convexities, regulation; cost-benefit analysis, general equilibrium, shadow-pricing; rent-seeking, corruption; optimal taxation, incidence, excess burden; dynamic public finance, national debt, social security.

subject: ECON
title: Public Economics
description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of public-sector allocation. Adverse selection, moral hazard, networks, auctions, public choice and political mechanisms; tax and mandate incidence; economics of education and local public goods; social insurance programs.

subject: ECON
title: International Trade and Welfare
description: Classical and new theories of international trade: why nations trade, gains from trade, patterns of trade, and trade policy effects under perfect and imperfect competition. Empirical trade and other special topics.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced International Trade and Investment
description: Surveys theoretical and empirical research on topics such as regionalism and multilateralism, trade and wages, foreign direct investment and multinational firms, trade and the environment, and trade and economic growth. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECON
title: International Macroeconomics
description: Advanced international monetary and macroeconomic theory: balance of payments, output, price and exchange rate determination, international aspects of growth and economic fluctuations, alternative exchange rate regimes, international capital flows.

subject: ECON
title: Applied International Finance
description: Surveys empirical research in international macroeconomics, finance and econometric methods: including balance of payments adjustment, international equilibrium, international prices, interest rates and exchange rates, models of exchange rate determination, capital flows, balance of payments crises. (Fall only)
prerequisites: ECON 607 and ECON 629 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics and Policy
description: Supply of and demand for labor; implications for labor markets and unemployment level.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Population
description: Economic determinants and consequences of population change.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics and Policy
description: Economic analysis of health-care policy; efficient design of health-care financing schemes; private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; provider behavior.
prerequisites: ECON 604 (or concurrent) or ECON 606 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Strategic Behavior and Experimental Economics
description: Experimental economics: methodology. Experimental game theory. Market experiments. Applications include: topics in industrial organization, provision of public goods, asset markets, auctions. Repeatable one time.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced Topics in Economics
description: Reflects interests of visiting and permanent faculty, focusing on specialized methods or topics in economics. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECON
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECON
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECON
title: Research Seminar
description: Selected issues emphasizing research techniques. Required for students who have passed the two theory qualifying exams and have not passed the comprehensive exam. CR/NC only.

subject: ECON
title: MA Capstone Research
description: Student applies theoretical and quantitative techniques, critical thinking, and communicative skills to prepare a written and oral presentation of original research on a topic of his or her choice. A-F only.
prerequisites: ECON 606, ECON 607, ECON 627, ECON 628, and consent of graduate chair.

subject: ECON
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDUC
title: Action Research in Education
description: Theory and practice in collaborative action research; critical inquiry into current educational work in schools with goals of improvement of teaching and participation in school and curriculum reform.

subject: EDUC
title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Consultancy Project
description: Practicum in the EdD program in professional practice; involves a group consultancy project requiring independent research and reflective activity embedded in a group project dealing with a problem of practice. Repeatable three times. Restricted to students in the EdD program.

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Chinese Development
description: Development and planning in contemporary China: economic policy and institutional structure in the development and urbanization process; urban and rural transformation in a socialist economy.

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Topics in Asian Studies
description: Selected topics in Asian studies. (C) China; (G) Asia; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other. Each alpha is repeatable two times.

subject: ASAN
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons. (Cross-listed as HIST 492 and WGSS 492)

subject: ASAN
title: Food, Culture, and Politics in Asia
description: Examines Asia’s role in the development of global foodways. Topics include the relationship between spices and imperialism, global popularity of Asian cuisines, Asian-influenced “hapa” cuisine in Hawai‘i, McDonaldization in Asia, and food security and sustainability. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Religions of Island Southeast Asia
description: A comparative, interdisciplinary examination of indigenous beliefs, Islam, Christianity, and Hinduism in island Southeast Asia, and how they have been adjusted because of economic and social change.

subject: ASAN
title: Directed Reading
description: Repeatable three times.

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Approaches to Asian Studies
description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Advanced Research and Writing in Asian Studies
description: Provides a structured overview of research and writing process, focused on Asia. Topics include research questions, abstracts, literature reviews, arguments, conceptualization, incorporating evidence, research ethics, and style. Students are required to produce a research paper.

subject: ASAN
title: Practicum in Asian Studies
description: Repeatable with consent up to nine credits.

subject: ASAN
title: Politics and Development: China
description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice. (Cross-listed as POLS 645C and PLAN 608)

subject: ASAN
title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required. Repeatable one time with consent. (Cross-listed as EALL 611)

subject: ASAN
title: Problems/Issues of Contemporary Asia
description: Analysis from multidisciplinary perspective: rural development, urbanization, international relations, ethnicity, religion, language, etc. Repeatable one time with different topics.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender in Asian Performing Arts
description: Performance is a rich site for gender construction, critique, and articulation in Asia. This seminar examines gender reflected in traditional music, dance, and theatre, including character role and performer persona; approaches of performance and culture studies, and an “Asian way.” A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ASAN
title: Culture and Colonialism
description: Analysis of theories and debates (cultural studies, feminist writings, post-colonial issues). Case studies of the transformation and creation of “traditional” cultures under colonialism.

subject: ASAN
title: Capitalism in Contemporary Asia
description: Historically grounded theoretical examination of capitalism in 20th-century Asia; multidisciplinary approach to fundamental change in political and economic structures and institutions, prospects for the future.

subject: ASAN
title: Ethnic Nationalism in Asia
description: Contemporary theories of ethnic and cultural nationalism from perspective of Asia. Issues of nationstate, power hierarchies, modernity, and identity in contemporary societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Security Cultures
description: Comparative study of conceptualizations, practices and institutions of national security in Asia in light of their geographic and historic contexts. (Once a year)

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asia Now
description: Examines the ways global influences are shaping the cultural developments in the diverse societies of contemporary Southeast Asia. (Spring only)

subject: ASAN
title: Seafood in Southeast Asia
description: Seafood production in Southeast Asia, including both regional fisheries and aquaculture. Case studies used to illustrate challenges to the implementation of sustainable seafood production and emerging approaches, such as community supported seafood. (Cross-listed as GEO 633)

subject: ASAN
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals. (Cross-listed as ARCH 687 and PLAN 636)

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Japanese Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics in Japanese literature, primarily of the modern period. English translations of original texts will be provided whenever available. Repeatable unlimited times with consent. (Cross-listed as JPN 640)

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as PLAN 649)

subject: ASAN
title: Marriage and Family in East Asia
description: Examines gendered/generational practices, expectations, and ideologies of marriage, childrearing, and caregiving; state’s role in legitimizing certain kinds of families; how transnational marriage migration is changing notions of belonging, relatedness, and national identity in East Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: East Asia Now
description: Views East Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic and political themes including various experiences with the West. Focus upon present state of the region. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Major Authors in Modern Korean Literature
description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature. Repeatable one time.

subject: ASAN
title: South Asia Now
description: Views South Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic, and political themes, including global interactions. Focus upon present state of the region. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ASAN
title: Telecom and the Internet in East Asia
description: Offers interdisciplinary approach to study of internet and telecommunications in East Asia. Examines growth and development of telecommunications networks in China, Japan, South and North Korea. Focuses on contemporary social media and government policy. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ASAN
title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical sociocultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history. Repeatable one time.

subject: ASAN
title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective. Repeatable two times in different topics, but need consent for second repeat. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EALL 665)

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asia and its Neighbors
description: Examines how Southeast Asian nations have recalibrated their international relationships in accordance with past experience and new concerns, focusing on interactions with Japan, China, and India, while integrating both global and domestic imperatives.

subject: ASAN
title: Law and Society in China
description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as LWPA 586)

subject: ASAN
title: Conflict and Cooperation in Asia
description: Explores conflict and cooperation among Asian nations. Topics may include economic integration, business networks, space and cyberspace, military alliances, territorial disputes, transnational crime, environmental cooperation, soft power, and regional institutional architecture. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Foreign Policy
description: Examination of China’s rise and world view, review of China’s regional relations, China and U.S. relations, formation of a new world order.
prerequisites: ASAN 600, ASAN 608, or POLS 645C, or consent

subject: ASAN
title: International Relations in Asia
description: How well do international relations theories explain interstate relations in Asia? How do international issues intera

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology III
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results, counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: COMG
title: Everyday Communication with Numbers: A Survival Guide
description: Understanding, communicating, and evaluating quantitative information in everyday contexts. Topics include describing and interpreting data, basic statistics, and evaluating the validity of results.

subject: COMG
title: Personal and Public Speech
description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

subject: COMG
title: Personal and Public Speech
description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

subject: COMG
title: Introduction to Nonverbal Communication
description: Beginning course on the fundamental components of nonverbal communication. Aspects of body movements, facial expressions, eye behavior, physical appearance, voice, touch, space, smell, time, and environmental features will be examined in a lecture/discussion format. Extensive practice in skills.

subject: COMG
title: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication
description: Introduction to basic principles of interaction between two people. Emphasis is on enhancement of skills in a variety of interpersonal contexts.

subject: COMG
title: Multicultural Communication Skills
description: Expose students to practical skills needed for effective intercultural communication. Offer guidelines for improvement in diverse cultural settings such as business, education, counseling, and healthcare.

subject: COMG
title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

subject: COMG
title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

subject: COMG
title: Interviewing
description: Principles and practice; training in informational, persuasive, employment, appraisal, and research interviewing.

subject: COMG
title: Introduction to Communicological Theories
description: Introduction to the theoretical perspectives that are the foundations of the communication discipline. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Research Methods
description: Introduction to methods of inquiry in the field of communication. Topics include research design and problem formulation, sampling, analytic and observational techniques, and data interpretation. Ethical issues in communication research will be discussed. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Instructional Communication
description: Analysis of and practice in using models of communication in the classroom. Extends application of oral communication skills to various instructional and teaching contexts. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

subject: COMG
title: Professional Presentations
description: Extends application of public speaking skills to professional contexts: group sales, press conferences, and corporate annual reports. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

subject: COMG
title: Group Decision-Making and Leadership
description: Study of decision-making within the small group. Effects of organization, leadership, membership, and goals on achieving group purposes. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Argumentation and Debate
description: Adapting communication theory to forensic strategies for social action. Practice in formal argument. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits

subject: COMG
title: Leadership and Organizational Communication
description: Principles and practices of organizational communication and its relationship to networks, leadership, power, conflict, cultures, and other contemporary views of organizational work, change, and development. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Persuasion
description: Theories, concepts, strategies, and processes of persuasion and social influence in contemporary society. Focus on analyzing, developing, and resisting persuasive messages. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Creating Understanding
description: Introduction to theory and research on human communication, comprehension, and creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories. Topics include prediction, inference-making, communication systems, and deception. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Family Communication
description: Focuses on the role of interaction patterns (both constructive and destructive) in the evolution of family communications. The impact of family dynamics upon these interaction patterns is given equal attention. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Interpersonal Relations
description: Theory and research on the development, maintenance, and termination of interpersonal relationships. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Culture and Communication
description: Survey of major factors affecting interpersonal communication between members of different cultures. Emphasis upon interaction between U.S. and Asian-Pacific peoples. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Special Topics in Culture and Communication
description: Contemporary research and theory on intercultural communication. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Interrogation and Interviewing
description: Survey of theory and research on the communicative demands of obtaining reliable information from others. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Evolution and Human Communication
description: Analysis of the role of human communication in mate attraction, intrasexual competition, cooperation, family dynamics, and coalition formation; discussion on the biological function of language, laughter, yawning, and emotion expressions. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Research on Communication Behavior
description: Survey of research on communication behavior. Verbal and nonverbal data collection; analysis of research data. Students design and implement a research project. Repeatable three times.

subject: COMG
title: Internship
description: Analysis and application of communication knowledge and behaviors in organizational settings. Repeatable up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: COMG
title: Social Identity and Intergroup Communication
description: Surveys theory and research on communication between members of different social groups, highlighting how communication influences and is influenced by social identity. Applies concepts to intergenerational, health, family, educational, multilingual, and computer-mediated contexts. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Political Communication
description: Survey of interpersonal and mass communication theories in the political context. Topics may include communication in public opinion processes, elections, debates, political campaigning and advertising. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Conflict Management
description: Examination of the theories, assumptions, practices, models, and techniques of managing interpersonal conflicts. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Science Communication
description: Introduction to principles for communicating science information effectively to a variety of audiences including the general public, policy makers, and profession peers. Application of these principles to create written and oral science communication products. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits. A-F only.

subject: COMG
title: Human Communication and Technology
description: Analysis of evolving communicative exchanges in the Internet age including how people communicate with computer technology: focus on personal, interpersonal, and cultural effects associated with technology use.

subject: COMG
title: Theories and Research in Strategic Communication
description: An in-depth overview of theories related to strategic communication and scientific approaches to attitude formation and changes. Junior standing or higher.

subject: COMG
title: Nonverbal Communication
description: Understanding communication beyond the words themselves. Review of theory and research on gestures, facial expressions, touch, personal space, and physical appearance. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Verbal Communication
description: Roles of language in human communication and social relationships; language variation, change, and social consequences. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Deceptive Communication
description: Survey of major social scientific theories, concepts, and research findings on deceptive communication, in a lecture/discussion format. Emphasis is on how people create deceptive messages, induce deception, and strategies used to detect deception. Restricted to studen

subject: COA
title: Introduction to Applied Gerontology: Helping Yourself and Others to Thrive in Later Life
description: Introduction to essential information on aging and the field of gerontology. Counters ageist stereotypes, develops skills for translating research into practice, and provides an introductory survey course for the undergraduate certificate in aging. A-F only. (Crosslisted as IS 206)

subject: COA
title: Ethics, Aging & Society
description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging. A-F only. (Cross-listed as IS 305)

subject: COA
title: Middle Age and Aging
description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences. (Cross-listed as HDFS 334)

subject: COA
title: Adult Development and Aging
description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death. Recommended: 240. (Cross-listed as PSY 342)

subject: COA
title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research. (Cross-listed as SOC 353)
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: COA
title: On Death and Dying
description: Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves. (Crosslisted as REL 394)

subject: COA
title: Directed Reading and Research for Freshmen and Sophomores
description: Individual reading or research under supervision of COA-affiliated faculty. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits. Freshmen and sophomores only. A-F only.

subject: COA
title: Aging and Disability Policy: Intersections in Health
description: Examines health programs and policies that help kupuna and persons with disabilities stay healthy and independent, including Medicare. Will engage with local community partners for meaningful intergenerational activities and project-based learning. A-F only.

subject: COA
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PH 435 and SW 435)
prerequisites: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent.

subject: COA
title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as NURS 449)

subject: COA
title: Directed Reading and Research forJuniors and Seniors
description: Individual reading or research under supervision of COA-affiliated faculty. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits. Juniors and seniors only.

subject: CHAM
title: Elementary Chamorro
description: Introduction to Chamorro, emphasis on listening and speaking, language structure. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Elementary Chamorro
description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills; emphasis on oral and reading proficiency. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Intermediate Chamorro
description: Continuation of 102. Emphasis on comprehension and language production (speaking). Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Intermediate Chamorro
description: Continuation of 201. Emphasis on comprehension and language production.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry and Society
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of basic chemistry concepts and their application to everyday life. No credit for science and engineering majors. A-F only. Students who successfully completed 110/SUST 120 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 110/SUST 120 without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry and Society Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany CHEM 100, 110, or SUST 120. Lab introduces fundamental applications of chemistry, with special emphasis on relevant topics and how chemistry relates to the real world. (For students in non-science fields.) A-F only.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and manmade chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. A-F only. Students who successfully completed 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 110/SUST 120 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 110/SUST 120 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override. (Cross-listed as SUST 120)

subject: CHEM
title: Preparation for General Chemistry
description: For students lacking preparation in chemistry. Provides background in algebra and elementary concepts of chemistry in preparation for entering the General Chemistry sequence. A-F only.

subject: CHEM
title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry
description: Nonrigorous but adequate background in fundamentals. Preparation for technical training in life sciences.

subject: CHEM
title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments introducing laboratory techniques and illustrating chemical principles.

subject: CHEM
title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry
description: Structure, nomenclature, properties, reactions of organic compounds emphasizing those of practical importance in related fields.

subject: CHEM
title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Techniques of preparation, purification, identification of organic compounds.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry I
description: Basic principles of chemistry, including stoichiometry. Introduction to solution phase chemistry. Gas phase chemistry. Thermodynamics, including enthalpies of formation and reaction. Atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular structure. Students who successfully completed 171 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 161 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 or 181A without instructor override.
prerequisites: C (not C-) in 131 or C (not C-) in 151 or successful completion of placement exam, or consent.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry Lab I
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed 171 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 161 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 or 181A without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry II
description: Continuation of 161. Liquids and solids. Solutions and colligative properties. Continuation of thermodynamics, including entropy and free energy. Principles and applications of chemical equilibrium, including acidbase chemistry (titrations, buffers). Kinetics. Redox reactions and electrochemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry Lab II
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 161L and 162 (or concurrent).

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Chemistry
description: Principles, theories, elementary analytical methods of chemistry. Intended for physical science majors and engineers. Co-requisite: 171L. Students who successfully completed 161 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 or 181A without instructor override. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Satisfactory Placement Exam score, and MATH 241 or MATH 242 or MATH 243 or MATH 251A or MATH 252A or MATH 253A.

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3.5- hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed 161L or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161L or 181A without instructor override. (Fall only)

subject: CHEM
title: Honors General Chemistry
description: Rigorous, in-depth introduction to chemical principles with emphasis on experimental and applied aspects of modern chemistry. Students who successfully completed 161 or 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 181A without instructor override.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Topics in Marine Biology
description: Current themes in marine biology and experience in scientific assessment. Emphasis on teaching writing and oral communication. Repeatable two times. MBIO majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 301/301L or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of Marine Organisms
description: Biology, physiology, and ecology of marine organisms and marine ecosystems, and the physical and chemical factors, which influence them. Cannot be used to satisfy BS-MB major requirements. Credit granted for only one of ZOOL 200, BIOL 301, or BIOL 406. Junior standing or consent. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Cell Biology I
description: Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level. (Cross-listed as MCB 407)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 275/275L and CHEM 273, or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
description: Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules. (Cross-listed as MBBE 408 and MCB 408)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 407; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Biology Laboratory
description: (2 3-hr Lab) A laboratory to accompany 407 and 408. (Cross-listed as MCB 408L)

subject: BIOL
title: Human Role in Environmental Change
description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability. (Cross-listed as GEO 410)
prerequisites: with a minimum grade of B, one of 101, 123 or GEO 101 and either 310 or GEO 322; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Corals and Coral Reefs
description: The biogeography, evolution, ecology, and physiology of corals and coral reefs, and the application of this information to the management of coral reefs. Emphasis will be placed on processes such as dispersal, the evolution and operation of mutualisms, calcification, reproduction, and the maintenance of diversity. (Spring only)

subject: BIOL
title: Wildlife and Plant Conservation
description: Principles of conservation biology and wildlife management techniques, illustrated with animal, plant, and ecosystem examples. Examination of ethical, cultural, legal, political, and socio-economic issues impinging on conservation policy and practice. Group project and field trips.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 265/265L or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts. (Spring only) (Crosslisted as BOT 430 and TPSS 432)
prerequisites: (172, BOT 201) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as BOT 430L and TPSS 432L)
prerequisites: (430 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Psychoactive Drug Plants
description: Taxonomy, ecology, biochemistry, distribution, cultural history, and contemporary use of mind-altering drug plants; examples from primitive, traditional, and modern societies.
prerequisites: junior standing, one semester of biological science, and either ANTH 200 or GEO 151; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota. (Cross-listed as SUST 450)
prerequisites: one semester of biological sciences at college level.

subject: BIOL
title: Fish Diversity
description: Survey of fish biodiversity focusing on major lineages, their phylogenetic relationships, and their geographic distribution in light of evolutionary history. Taught spring semester in alternate years. Junior standing or higher. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: BIOL
title: Fish Diversity Laboratory
description: (2 2-hr Lab) Overview of the major orders and families of fishes of the world; introduction to local Hawaiian fishes; coverage of basic fish anatomy; introduction to field and laboratory techniques in fish research. Junior standing or higher. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: BIOL
title: The Rise of Fishes: An Evolutionary History
description: The origins and early evolution of fishes, with a focus on morphological innovations that have led to lineage divergence and adaptive radiation, and the nature of underlying processes associated with novel character trait evolution. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: BIOL
title: Evolutionary Biology
description: Process of evolution: genetic basis, natural selection, population genetics, speciation, the fossil record. Recommended: a BIOL or ZOOL course at 300 or 400 level.

subject: BIOL
title: The Biology of Cancer
description: Integrative, in-depth focus on the genetics, cell biology, and molecular basis of cancer. Combination of classroom lectures and problem-based discussions in small groups. Addresses ethical implications of cancer research and treatment. A-F only. MCB or BIOL majors only. Senior standing or higher. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as MCB 472)

subject: BIOL
title: Life in the Soil Environment
description: An interdisciplinary study of the diverse life in the soil beneath our feet that includes bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, invertebrate, viruses, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as TPSS 480)
prerequisites: 375 or TPSS/PEPS/SUST 371, or MICR 351, or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Life in the Soil Environment Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany 480. Technical examination of bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, and other invertebrate, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet. Repeatable one time. (Crosslisted as TPSS 480L)
prerequisites: 171L and 172L, or MICR 351L, or consent. Co-requisite: 480.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Topics for Biologists
description: Focuses on the use of computational tools and approaches to analyze the enormous amount of biological data (DNA, RNA, protein) available today. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as MBBE 483)
prerequisites: (171 (or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Invertebrates
description: Body plans, development, cellular construction, physiological integration, natural history, and ecology of invertebrate animals. Emphasis on marine species, especially local ones.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Invertebrates Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab)

subject: BIOL
title: Biogeography and Evolution
description: Study of the fundamental role that geography plays in evolution and maintenance of species diversity. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 171 and one of BIOL 172 or BOT 101.

subject: BIOL
title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as MATH 490)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biological Directed Research
description: Development and completion of a research project under the direction of a faculty advisor. Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits, up to 6 credits apply towards BA and BS BIOL major requirements. A-F only.
prerequisites: 2.5 GPA minimum, written proposal and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: (Alpha) Biology Workshop for Science Teachers
description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology. A-F only. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: BIOL
title: Life Sciences Colloquium
description: Seminars presented with the School of Life Sciences; topics will vary across the biological sciences. Repeatable up to four credits. BOT, MBIO, MICR, ZOOL graduate students only.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Ecology
description: Practical introduction to molecular methods used to address ecological and evolutionary questions. Advanced undergraduate/graduate level. Focus on methods and application to independent research project. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 265/265L (or equivalent) or 275/275L (or equivalent), and 375/375L, and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Population Genetics
description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations. (Cross-listed as CMB 650)

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: To provide elective courses for undergraduates in the biomedical sciences specialties. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Research Review
description: Research elective for medical students. MD students only. CR/NC only.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II
description: DB Anatomy, physiology, and systematics of plants and animals; behavior; ecosystems, populations, and communities.
prerequisites: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172L (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 172.
prerequisites: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biostatistics
description: FQ (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R. A-F only. (Cross-listed as BOT 220)
prerequisites: BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or BOT 101; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam.

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: DB Principles of ecology and evolution for life science majors stressing integrated approach and recent advance. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171/171L, BIOL 172, BIOL 172L (or concurrent).

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Lab
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 265. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 (or concurrent).

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology
description: DB Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology. A-F only. (Cross-listed as MCB 275)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171/171L and CHEM 272.

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology Lab
description: DY (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory for Cell and Molecular Biology. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 (or concurrent) and CHEM 272.

subject: BIOL
title: Service Learning for Biology Majors
description: Directed participation on tutorials and related activities in public schools and approved community and UH Mānoa organizations. A-F only. Repeatable one time.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Ecology and Evolution
description: DB Ecological and evolutionary factors creating and maintaining patterns of biological diversity in major marine ecosystems. Emphasis on the biphasic life histories of many marine organisms. The development of quantitative skills and critical thinking. MBIO majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265, BIOL 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Ecology and Evolution Lab
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 301. MBIO majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 (or concurrent).

subject: BIOL
title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering. (Cross-listed as MBBE 304)
prerequisites: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology
description: DB General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment. A-F only. (Cross-listed as BOT 305)

subject: BIOL
title: Ethology
description: DB Introduction to animal and human ethology and sociobiology; emphasis on social and interspecific behavior, its causes and adaptive significance. Lab optional.
prerequisites: BIOL 171 and BIOL 171L and BIOL 172 and BIOL 172L or ANSC 201; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Ethology Lab
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Application of methods in the study of animal behavior by demonstrations, labs and projects.

subject: BIOL
title: Environmental Issues
description: DB Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views. (Cross-listed as SUST 309)
prerequisites: one of BIOL 101, BIOL 123, or GEO 101; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Vertebrates
description: DB Introduction to the evolution and systematics of vertebrates, with emphasis on comparative morphology, physiology, and ecology.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Vertebrates Lab
description: DY (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 325.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Mammal Biology
description: DB Overview of marine mammal science, significance and roles of marine mammals in their ecosystems, and marine conservation issues. Current research topics in marine mammal science will also be covered.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171/171L, BIOL 172/172L, and BIOL 265, BIOL 265L; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
description: DB The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society. Not a BIOL major elective. (Cross-listed as CMB 351)
prerequisites: one semester of biological science at college level or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Parasitology
description: DB Animal parasites of man, and domestic and wild animals; systematics, comparative morphology, life history, pathology, treatment, control.

subject: BIOL
title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
description: DB Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging. (Cross-listed as WGSS 350)
degrees: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies BA

subject: BIOL
title: Island Ecosystems
description: DB Characteristics of island biota; examples from Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Impact of island and continental cultures; policy and ecosystem endangerment; contemporary legislation, policy, and management practices. Not a BIOL major elective.
prerequisites: one semester of biological science or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biological Field Studies
description: DB Biological survey, collection, and analysis techniques will be reviewed and applied through field studies. Students will be introduced to the uniqueness of the Hawaiian environment and its diversity of life. Emphasis on diversity, evolution and ecology. Repeatable up to six credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265/265L (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics
description: DB Genetic concepts at advanced undergraduate level; genetic transmission, recombination, gene action, mutation, population and evolutionary genetics. A-F only.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics Laboratory
description: DY (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments with a variety of organisms to illustrate principles discussed in BIOL 375.

subject: BIOL
title: Communicating in Biological Sciences
description: Combined lecture/lab impart essential knowledge and skills in technical writing, poster design, and oral presentations for effective communication for life science majors. Research papers, lab reports, project proposals, conference presentations are covered. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171/171L, BIOL 172/172L, and ENG 100.

subject: BIOL
title: (Alpha) Teaching Internship
description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication. Repeatable one time.

subject: BIOL
title: Ocean Internships and Research
description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Crosslisted as IS 400)
prerequisites: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100/BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Biotechnology
description: DB General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues. (Cross-listed as MBBE 401)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
