description: DY (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 401. Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as MBBE 401L)
prerequisites: BIOL 275L, or BIOL 375L, or MBBE 304, or MBBE 375; or consent. Co-requisite: BIOL 401.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Biochemistry
description: DB Molecular basis of living processes in bacteria, plants, and animals; emphasis on metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. (Cross-listed as MBBE 402)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275/275L, and CHEM 273; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Field Problems in Marine Biology
description: DB Integrated program of intensive lectures, laboratory experiments, and field research that focus on the biological processes that shape the lives of marine organisms. A-F only. Limited space; enrollment by consent; GPA considered.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301/301L and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Topics in Marine Biology
description: DB Current themes in marine biology and experience in scientific assessment. Emphasis on teaching writing and oral communication. Repeatable two times. MBIO majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301/301L or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of Marine Organisms
description: DB Biology, physiology, and ecology of marine organisms and marine ecosystems, and the physical and chemical factors, which influence them. Cannot be used to satisfy BS-MB major requirements. Credit granted for only one of ZOOL 200, BIOL 301, or BIOL 406. Junior standing or consent. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Cell Biology I
description: DB Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level.

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk. (Cross-listed as ORE 621 and SUST 621)
prerequisites: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics
description: Theory of fluid dynamics in differential form, covering equation of motion, vortex generation, flow in rotating frame, potential theory, laminar flow, and introduction to turbulence.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ERTH 656)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change. (Cross-listed as ORE 624 and SUST 624)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as BE 664 and NREM 660)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Surface Water Hydrology
description: Deterministic and probabilistic methods include reliability of empirical distributions, multiple regression analysis, extreme value analysis and domain of attraction. Short-memory models for stochastic simulation of streamflows include autoregressive, Markov chain and moving average models. Time series analysis of hydrologic data is discussed. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Hydrology
description: Groundwater occurrence, movement, quality, and resource evaluation, development, and management. Emphasis on saltwater encroachment, well evaluation, aquifer protection, recharge with wastewater, and Hawai‘i type hydrology.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Physical and Chemical Treatment
description: Introduction to physical and chemical processes for water and wastewater treatment: Review of momentum and mass transfer, chemical reactions, colloidal chemistry, coagulation and flocculation, granular filtration, sedimentation, carbon adsorption, gas transfer, disinfection and oxidation. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Biological Treatment
description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as BE 634)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Chemistry
description: Basic concepts of chemistry as related to the environment, with more emphasis on water. Topics include chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acid-base, precipitation and dissolution redox reactions, sorption, organic chemicals in the environment. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Combined lecture-discussion on major topics in environmental microbiology, microbial ecology, and a broad understanding of microbial processes in natural and engineered environments. CEE majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: graduate standing in CEE or consent.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mathematics for Engineers
description: Application of advanced mathematics to engineering phenomena; linear algebra, Eigen systems; partial differentiation and multiple integrals; vector/tensor analysis; Fourier series/transforms and Laplace transform; ordinary/partial differential equations; probability and statistics. CE, ME, ORE, and ECE majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Hazardous Waste Remediation
description: Introduces the national problems dealing with the contamination of groundwater and presents remedial measures. Such measures include pump and treat (PAT) technology, in-situ bioremediation, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, electrokinetics, hydraulic fracturing, reactive walls, and phytoremediation. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Water Quality Modeling
description: Mathematical formulation of pollutant transport and mixing in the water environment. Kinetics formulation and parameter identification, model calibration and verification. Design projects. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Membrane Separations
description: Applications of membrane separations to desalination, power generation, and ultrapure water systems. Discussion of reverse osmosis, osmosis-driven processes, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, electrodialysis and ion exchange technologies. Membrane fouling and concentration polarization from practical/theoretical standpoints. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Seepage, Drainage, and Dewatering
description: Theory of seepage, field and laboratory methods of measurement; graphical and numerical methods; design of drainage structures; construction dewatering. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Deep Foundations
description: Analysis and design of deep foundations; driven piles and drilled shafts. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and 455 (with a minimum grade of D).
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Numerical Methods in Geotechnical Engineering
description: Finite element and finite difference formulation and analyses to solve problems in geotechnical engineering. Also covers constitutive modelling. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 355 (with a minimum grade of C) and 455 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
description: Soil continuum mechanics principles; elastic, plastic, and Cam clay soil behavior; critical state and strength; interpretation of laboratory test results. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Alt. years)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Slope and Earth Structures
description: Classification of landslides and triggering mechanisms; field investigation procedures; limit equilibrium slope stability methods; numerical techniques; seepage and dynamic considerations; case studies. A-F only. (Alt. years)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Marine Geotechnics
description: Principles of geotechnical engineering applied to marine environments; marine geology; surveying and sampling methods; seabed sediment types, properties, and behavior; coastal and offshore foundations. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Earth Pressures
description: Estimation of lateral earth pressures; analysis and design of retaining walls and excavation support systems. A-F only.
prerequisites: 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and 455 (with a minimum grade of D).
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Systems Analysis for Engineers
description: Optimization used in design and management of systems for minimizing resources or optimizing outcomes. Evaluation of alternatives, economic efficiency and effectiveness analysis. Logistics. Open to engineering students. Computer applications and labs.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
description: Definition, technologies and their attributes. Analysis and implementation based on FHWA’s User Services. Automated incident detection algorithms. Machine vision applications to traffic engineering. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Transportation Modeling and Statistics
description: Demand modeling, discrete choice and activity-based modeling. Demand forecasting by simulation. Transportation surveys and sampling methods. Application of cluster, factor, regression, logistic and ARIMA analyses to transportation. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Pavement Design and Rehabilitation
description: Pavement engineering with emphasis given to understanding fundamental issues such as historical development of pavement design, approaches used for design of new pavements and overlays, understanding of construction issues and their effects on pavement performance, and various design factors: environmental, loading and materials characterization. Introduction of pavement management systems. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Continuum Mechanics
description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics; coordinate transformations; analysis of stress and strain; principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations; constitutive relations; field equations. Problems in elasticity. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ME 671)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Project Management Systems
description: Project integration and PMIS; organizational power; conflict, strategic, and life-cycle management in construction management; matrix structure compared to projectized structure; project success; team building; change and culture in construction organizations; competitive bidding. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations. (Cross-listed as MGT 660)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics I
description: Response of single and multi degree-of-freedom systems due to dynamic forces. Direct integration of equations of motion. Response spectrum analysis. Application to earthquake loading. Systems with distributed mass and elasticity. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture History
description: Specialized work on the history and theory of architecture. Repeatable unlimited times. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction. Repeatable unlimited times. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics. Repeatable unlimited times. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Explore Furniture Design
description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice and an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience. Repeatable one time. BEnvD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Writing
description: Reading, research, and work on topics in architecture and design. Includes an intensive writing component. May include specialized research and/or studio experience in architecture, design, and the history and theory of architecture and design. ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: American Architecture
description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations. (Cross-listed as AMST 623)

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy. (Cross-listed as PLAN 675)

subject: ARCH
title: Design Communication for Landscape Architects
description: Theory and application in design communication, including drawing and presentation skills; emphasis on the design process and critical thinking through analog and digital media, diagramming, three-dimensional modeling, and various other presentation techniques. LAND majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Computer Applications in Landscape Architecture
description: Introduction to the use of computers in landscape architecture, emphasizing two- and three dimensional computer-aided drawings and graphics suitable to landscape architectural design and practice. LAND majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawai‘i and the tropics. LAND majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TPSS 634)

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Materials and Construction
description: Examination of materials and methods of landscape construction from source, extraction, and manufacturing, to use and reuse. Assignments include drawing standard construction details and a report on the history of material use, properties, and qualities. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Architectural Professional Practice
description: Introduction of practices and core methods of the landscape architecture profession. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, professional relationships, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Land Use Planning
description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making. A-F only. (Crosslisted as PLAN 645)

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only) (Cross-listed as AMST 645 and ANTH 645)

subject: ARCH
title: Vernacular Architecture
description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas. (Cross-listed as AMST 681)

subject: ARCH
title: Fundamentals of Landscape Design Studio
description: Theory and application of foundational landscape design principles, programming, and physical analysis to site-based design problems. Visual, formal, spatial, and functional design principles are applied to ecological and cultural influences in landscape design. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Site Design Studio
description: Landscape project design at the site scale; from concept development through detailed design. Synthesis of foundational skills into more complex, layered spatial, and functional problems. Emphasis on site research and design methods. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design. LAND and TPSS majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TPSS 656)

subject: ARCH
title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes. LAND majors only. A-F only. (Crosslisted as TPSS 658)

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Seminar
description: Provides participants with basic knowledge of the field of historic preservation as well as the fundamental knowledge of how to document, conserve, and preserve both tangible and intangible cultural properties. Repeatable three times. (Summer only)

subject: ARCH
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures. Graduate students only or consent. (Cross-listed as ANTH 676 and PLAN 676)

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation Planning
description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building. (Cross-listed as PLAN 677)

subject: ARCH
title: Elements of Style
description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/ cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present. (Cross-listed as AMST 679)

subject: ARCH
title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises. LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Crosslisted as PLAN 682)

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Study
description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawai‘i; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific. Each alpha repeatable up to 18 credits.

subject: ARCH
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals. (Cross-listed as ASAN 636 and PLAN 636)

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Seminar on a wide range of architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty. Repeatable three times. ARCH and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation at an advanced level of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Intensive work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Furniture Design and Fabrication
description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice, an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience. Additionally, a survey of 20th Century furniture design. Repeatable one time. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. ARCH and LAND majors only, or consent. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 695)

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Landscape Architecture
description: Seminar on a wide range of landscape architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty. Repeatable three times. ARCH and LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Technical Ceramics
description: DA. Clay body development, glaze development, empirical and calculation methods. Emphasis on glaze maturity, surface, and color. A-F only.
prerequisites: 242, and one of 343, 344, or 345; or consent.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Figure Modeling
description: DA. Figure modeling, mold making, and casting. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Kinetic Sculpture
description: DA. The design and construction of objects incorporating movement as an integral element of their content. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Metal Fabrication
description: DA. Metal fabrication and development of associated practices, concepts, and historical references. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Small-Scale
description: DA. Fabrication and casting of forms on a small scale such as jewelry. The development of related practices, concepts, and historical references. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Utilitarian Sculpture
description: DA. The design and construction of objects intended for use/interaction. Emphasis on wood and synthetic materials. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Contemporary
description: DA. Contextualization of late 20th/early 21st century sculptural practice, including stylistic and theoretical frameworks, with references to influences of various historical Western and Asian traditions and applying this knowledge in the creation of sculpture.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Exhibition Design and Gallery Management
description: DA. Design theory and techniques for presentation of artworks and mounting exhibitions.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art Museums and Preservation Practices
description: Introduction to collections management and preservation techniques, incorporating both theoretical and practical approaches, and including hands-on work with the collections of the John Young Museum. A-F only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio II
description: DA. Intermediate graphic design. Emphasis on communication problems involving process and analysis. Introduction to modernist precedents and information theory. A-F only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio II Lab
description: Intermediate instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, software, and peripheral devices, including intermediate layout. Introduction to graphic design industry standard multi-media and web design programs. CR/NC only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography II
description: DA. Intermediate typographic design, exploration of word and text composition in the context of multiple-page structures. A-F only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Study Abroad-Studio Art
description: DA. Intensive study of topics in studio art at a UH Mānoa approved study abroad institution. (B) introductory; (C) upper-division. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Medieval Art
description: DH. Arts of Europe from early Christian era to Renaissance.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Greece and Rome
description: DH. Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome. (Cross-listed as CLAS 373)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of the 19th Century
description: DH. Architecture, sculpture, and painting of Europe.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Early Art of Japan
description: DH. Major developments, prehistoric through Kamakura; architecture, painting, sculpture.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Later Art of Japan
description: DH. Major developments, Muromachi to modern period; painting, sculpture, architecture.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Philippine Visual Art from Burial Jars to Burning Effigies
description: DH. Introduction to the arts and material culture of the Philippines from the pre-colonial to the contemporary period through the examination of sculpture, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, and painting from various ethnolinguistic groups. (Cross-listed as IP 382)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Korea
description: DH. Ceramics, sculpture, painting, and architecture; neolithic through Yi periods.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art and Culture of Early China
description: DH. A culturally oriented study of Chinese visual arts; emphasis on jade, bronze, secular and religious sculptures, and paintings from prehistory to the 9th century.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art and Culture of Late China
description: DH. A culturally oriented study of Chinese visual arts; emphasis on the rise of literati painting and theory individualism in art and theory, garden, and architecture, and the Chinese pursuit of modernity and post-modernity in art.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Sculpture of China
description: DH. Thematic introduction to sculpture in China from the Neolithic period through the present day. A-F only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Study Abroad-Art History
description: DH. Intensive study of advanced topics in art history at a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad institution. (B) introductory; (C) upper-division. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Africa, Pacific, North America
description: DH. Contextual study of art from selected areas in Africa, the Pacific, and North America.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Southeast Asia
description: DH. Critical analysis of the historical and cultural development of Buddhist and Hindu art in Southeast Asia; (B) island Southeast Asia; (C) mainland Southeast Asia. Repeatable one time for different alphas.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of India and South Asia
description: DH. Art and architecture of South Asia in historical and cultural context. Art of India and South Asia.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art Historical Methodology
description: DH. Introduction to the methods and approaches of art history. Students will develop skills in perception and comprehension of visual art forms, and a critical understanding of the methods used by art historians to analyze them. A-F only.
program: Art History and Theory Core Courses
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: History of Photography
description: DH. History of photography from its beginnings to the present; emphasis on the evolution of photography as an art form; (B) nineteenth century, from the invention of photography through pictorialism; (C) twentieth century, from World War I to the present. Repeatable one time for different alphas.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Directed Work
description: Individual projects; tutorial. Maximum: 3 credit hours per semester; total 3 for BA, 6 for BFA.
prerequisites: two 200-level or above art courses in area of directed work, as well as consent of instructor and department associate chair
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Special Topics
description: Intensive and specialized work at advanced level in fields of special interest of visiting or resident faculty; (B) studio art; (C) art history. Repeatable three times per alpha, up to 12 credits.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher and instructor consent only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Advanced Electronic Arts Studio
description: DA. Tutorial studio that encourages exploration in combined and new media through independent work within an environment of theoretical and critical discourse. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Professional Practice in the Arts: Creative, Career, and Leadership
description: Examination of the role of the artist in society, the artist as self, as community member, as teacher. Professional Practice skills in the arts; planning, grantsmanship, fundraising, budgeting, marketing, outreach, and media relations. A-F only.
prerequisites: ART majors only. Senior standing or graduate students only.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Graduation Portfolio (BA)
description: Required graduation portfolio for BA Art History and Art Studio students. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: BA ART majors only. Undergraduates only. To be taken during the semester prior to expected graduation.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: BFA Capstone Seminar/Studio
description: In conjunction with the production of art for the BFA annual exhibition, this seminar will examine, critique, and evaluate the student’s art within the context of contemporary art, professional practices, exhibition theory, and integrate theoretical and practical issues in the life of an artist. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: BFA majors only. Pre: BFA major or consent.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: DA. Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 436)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Installation/Performance–Material in Context
description: DA. Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological, etc.).
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: Continuation of 343: 20th century. (Cross-listed as HIST 374)
prerequisites: 150 or 201 or 202 or 211 or 212 or HIST 151 or HIST 152; or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Conflict in American History
description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion. (Fall only) (Crosslisted as REL 345)

subject: AMST
title: American Design: An Historical Survey
description: Examination of design in American culture over the last century. Readings in industrial, graphic, interior, architectural, landscape, and user interface design used to study issues of gender, race, and class in the U.S. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Design
description: Investigates design in contemporary American culture. Graphic, industrial, urban, and user-interface design practices are situated within broader social and economic forces. Modes of design practice, production, and consumption studied as reflection of American society today. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: Culture and the Arts in America
description: Study of the role of the arts in American society and diverse cultural practices in historical and contemporary contexts.

subject: AMST
title: Screening Asian Americans
description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship. SCA majors: A-F only. (Cross-listed as CINE 352)

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Lands and Waters
description: Examines indigenous practices born of and located in Indigenous places. Analyzes how indigenous knowledge of place informs Indigenous cultural, linguistic, intellectual, and political survivance and sovereignty, and resistance.

subject: AMST
title: American Travel Writing
description: Survey examines the roles that travel writing plays in American identity- and nation-formation, from early colonial history to the present. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: American Cinema
description: Introductory history of American cinema from the silent to the digital era, with an emphasis on criticism, genre and style, as well as cultural and sociopolitical context.

subject: AMST
title: American Empire
description: Examines the interplay between an “American culture of empire” and the rise of the U.S. as a superpower. Topics: imperialism and political culture, social movements and international affairs, race, gender and class relations. (Cross-listed as HIST 379)

subject: AMST
title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics. (Cross-listed as ES 373)

subject: AMST
title: Critical Research Methods
description: Overview of methods and methodologies drawn from various fields (including history, politics, literature, art, law and race, Indigenous, gender, and sexuality studies) for conducting interdisciplinary research. Models of writing from AMST faculty; emphasis on writing.

subject: AMST
title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered. (Cross-listed as ES 443)

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Literature and Film
description: Interdisciplinary, comparative course examining native literary texts (novels, short fiction, poetry), films, etc. that address issues of representation and how native peoples actively resist colonial ideology.

subject: AMST
title: Asian American Music Cultures
description: An exploration of how Asian American music making is related to community formation, labor migration, and cultural sensibilities throughout the 20th century.

subject: AMST
title: Japanese Americans: Research Topics
description: Research and thematic seminar on Japanese American culture, issues, and history.

subject: AMST
title: Regionalism: The South
description: Definition of a Southern identity and its relation to the larger U.S. culture, using literary and polemical works of 19th- and 20th-century.

subject: AMST
title: Hawai‘i’s Multiculturalism
description: A multidisciplinary examination of the dynamics of the Hawaiian Islands’ racial and cultural diversity from the perspectives of historical trends, social processes, and contemporary political, social, and economic issues as they impact interracial relations.

subject: AMST
title: American Ideas of Nature
description: The natural world in American thought from Native Americans to modern ecologists.

subject: AMST
title: History of American Architecture
description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning. (Cross-listed as ARCH 473)

subject: AMST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present. (Cross-listed as HIST 480 and SUST 481)

subject: AMST
title: History of American Workers
description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century. (Cross-listed as HIST 477)

subject: AMST
title: Slavery and Freedom
description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World. (Cross-listed as HIST 473)

subject: AMST
title: Islands, Empires, and the Arts
description: Colonialism, neocolonialism, and cultures of resistance in the Caribbean and its North American diaspora through literature, film, and the arts. Focus on political dissent; nation building; historical memory; construction of gender, race. Writing emphasis. A-F only

subject: AMST
title: Politics in Hawai‘i
description: Discussion of modern politics against the background of recent history and major contemporary issues.

subject: AMST
title: History of Crime and Punishment
description: History of American crime and punishment from 18th century to the present. Topics: changing crime patterns, evolving punishment methods, penal reform movements, convict resistance, growth of prison industrial complex, racism, class, and gender.

subject: AMST
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 368 and WGSS 436)
prerequisites: one of WGSS 151, WGSS 175, WGSS 176, WGSS 202, WGSS 360, WGSS 381, or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration. (Cross-listed as WGSS 493)

subject: AMST
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory. (Cross-listed as POLS 372 and WGSS 462)
prerequisites: one of 310, 316, 318, 373, 455, POLS 339, WGSS 360, WGSS 361, WGSS 439; or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Race and Racism in America
description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history. (Cross-listed as HIST 476)

subject: AMST
title: Social Movements
description: Examination of mass mobilization in U.S. history from the Revolution forward, including abolitionism, feminism, civil rights, labor, and more. Concludes with analysis of various community organizing efforts today.

subject: AMST
title: Racism, American Culture and Film/ Media
description: An exploration of the critique of racial ideologies in American film. The course also examines how aggrieved communities develop cultural sensibilities, aesthetic choices and politicized identities through film, video and media work.

subject: AMST
title: Gender in Action Cinema
description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. (Cross-listed as WGSS 466)

subject: AMST
title: Food, Culture, and Empire
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ES 450 and WGSS 450)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.

subject: AMST
title: Victims, Virtue, and Violence
description: Examination of the history and significance of melodrama as a dominant mode of American cultural production from the early republic to the present, with a focus on issues of race, gender, and national identity.

subject: AMST
title: Popular Culture
description: Major themes, modes, and media of popular or mass culture in the U.S.; emphasis on cultural trends and social implications.

subject: AMST
title: The ’20s and ’30s
description: Novelists, painters, poets, jazz musicians as examples of culture of the 1920s and 1930s in America.

subject: ANSC
title: Topics in Animal Sciences
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs. Repeatable five times, up to 18 credits.
department: Department of Human Nutrition, Food and Animal Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: ANSC
title: Field Experience
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report. A-F only. (Cross-listed as FSHN 492)
department: Department of Human Nutrition, Food and Animal Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: ANSC
title: Directed Study or Research
description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students, generally with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major. Exceptions may be granted for students with high achievement in last three semesters. Repeatable unlimited times.
department: Department of Human Nutrition, Food and Animal Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: ANSC
title: The Science of Food Systems
description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as FSHN 601)
department: Department of Human Nutrition, Food and Animal Sciences

subject: ECON

description: DS Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 412)

subject: ECON
title: Economic History of the United States
description: DS U.S. economy from colonial times: government policies, institutions, industries, financial markets, economic growth, economic crises.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Global Economic Crisis and Recovery
description: DS Causes and consequences of financial and economic crises: crisis origins and global transmission; macroeconomic and regulatory policy responses; recovery challenges.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Asian Economic Development
description: DS History and economic development. Resources, population, and income, saving, investment, and consumption patterns. Role of government and private enterprise.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: The Chinese Economy
description: DS The Chinese economy during the imperial and republican periods, under Mao, and into the present reform era, with a brief comparison to Taiwan and Hong Kong.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Pacific Island Economies
description: DS Historical and current economic development of the Pacific islands (excluding Hawai‘i). Analysis of selected economic issues such as tourism, population growth, etc.
prerequisites: ECON 120, ECON 130, or ECON 131; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Mathematical Economics
description: DS Mathematical techniques applied to theories of the consumer, the firm, markets. Linear programming, input-output analysis.
prerequisites: ECON 300, ECON 301; MATH 203, MATH 215, MATH 241, or MATH 251A.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Econometrics I: Data Exploration and Regression Analysis
description: DS Types of data, exploratory data analysis, generalizing from random samples, simple and multivariate regression, non-linear relationships, measurement error, extreme values, weights, correlated and heteroskedastic errors, instrumental variables, models for binary or discrete dependent variables. A-F only.
prerequisites: ECON 321 or MATH 241 or BUS 310 or NREM 310 or (MATH 251A and NREM 203) or (MATH 371 and MATH 373) or (MATH 471 and MATH 472); or consent.

subject: ECON

A-F only.
prerequisites: ECON 425 (with a minimum grade of B- or better).

Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as NREM 429)
prerequisites: ECON 130 or NREM/SUST 220, and ECON 321 or NREM 310; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics
description: DS Economic analysis of labor market. Investment in human capital, education, health, migration, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Population
description: DS Determinants and consequences of growth and structure of human populations. Relationships between economic factors and fertility, population growth and economic growth.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics
description: DS Private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; efficient production and utilization of services; models of hospital and physician behavior; optimal public policy.

subject: ECON
title: Monetary Theory and Policy
description: DS Micro-foundations and critical analysis of monetary and macroeconomic theory and policy. Topics include the causes and consequences of inflation, optimal monetary policy and international monetary systems, bank risk and insurance, and national debt and taxation.

subject: ECON
title: Development Economics
description: DS Theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for analyzing key issues facing today’s developing world. Topics include characteristics of underdeveloped economies, economic growth, structural change, poverty, inequality, education, population growth, foreign aid and financial sector.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Happiness
description: DS Topics covered include: measuring happiness, what individual and country characteristics contribute to individual well-being, what are the consequences of happiness on behavior, and whether happiness is a cause or an effect.

subject: ECON
title: Public Economics
description: DS Welfare economics, public expenditure and policy evaluation, public finance by debt and taxes.

subject: ECON
title: State and Local Finance
description: DS Fiscal institutions, operations, and policy questions within state and local governments in U.S. grant programs and other links with central government.

subject: ECON
title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
description: DS Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources. (Cross-listed as SUST 458)

subject: ECON
title: International Trade and Welfare
description: Theory of international specialization and exchange; general equilibrium, tariffs, quotas, common markets.

subject: ECON
title: International Macroeconomics
description: DS The determination of output, price levels, exchange rates and the balance of payments for economies that are integrated with the global economy; theory and application to historical and/or contemporary policy issues.

subject: ECON
title: Industrial Organization
description: DS Theoretical and empirical analysis of contemporary topics in industrial organization. Uses economic theory to analyze important issues facing firms, and examines the practical challenges of empirical applications of theory.

subject: ECON
title: Law and Economics
description: DS Legal issues of property rights, contracts, torts, and crime. Efficiency of U.S. legal process. Economics of law enforcement, juries, prosecutors; evolution of legal rules.

subject: ECON
title: Land and Housing Economics

subject: ECON

description: DS Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester, e.g., environmental pollution, crime control, racial discrimination, traffic congestion.

subject: ECON

subject: ECON

subject: ECON

(Alt. years: spring)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Niño/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 666)

prerequisites: ATMO 600 or OCN 620; MATH 407 or 408; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
description: Theory, observations, large-scale analyses, and global model simulations that describe characteristic large-scale circulation of the Earth’s atmosphere. Includes zonally averaged climatology, asymmetric features of the general circulation, and El NinoSouthern Oscillation phenomenon. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Special Topics in Meteorology
description: Concentrated studies on selected atmospheric problems. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Seminar in Meteorology
description: Participation in departmental seminars and presentation of a seminar on research results. Includes written critiques of departmental seminars. Repeatable three times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: BIOC
title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
description: DP. Biological chemistry stressing integration of concepts of general, inorganic, and biochemistry and application to life chemistry.
prerequisites: beginning algebra and high school science.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: BIOC
title: Elements of Biochemistry
description: DP. Biochemical principles and concepts as applied to living systems, including sufficient organic chemistry to understand these principles.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: BIOC
title: Basic Biochemistry
description: DB. Principles of biochemistry, applicable to medicine and real-life situations, involving metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Taught by biomedical researchers. Evaluated based on exams, quizzes, homework, and group presentation.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: BIOC
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: Independent research or selected reading of current literature in the area of biochemistry and biophysics. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: BIOC
title: Topics in Biochemistry
description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students take an in-depth study of selected topics in biochemistry.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: BIOC
title: Highlights of Organ-System Biochemistry
description: Provides highly interactive, small group discussions on concepts of biochemistry important to the various organ systems; such as cardiac, respiratory, hematology, gastrointestinal, endocrine, musculoskeletal and neurological systems, and relevant to clinical medicine. CR/NC only. (Fall only)
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Sustainable Engineering
description: Sustainability and its social and technical significance; global population growth; resource management and quantification; designs for sustainable society; challenges interfacing technology and culture/religion; green and ecological engineering; life cycle analyses; engineering ethics; selected case studies. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Quantitative Biology
description: DB. Quantitative approach to applied topics in biology including synthesis and metabolism, kinetics, physiological systems, cellular processes and signaling, informatics, and emerging technologies for health, biological production/processing, and discovery. (Once a year)
prerequisites: MATH 241 (or concurrent) and CHEM 162 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Biological Engineering
description: DY. Discussion and experimental investigation of physical and chemical principles underlying representative biological processes and systems. Bioproduction, energy conversion processes, physiological systems, biological treatment, biosensors, biomechanics, and related natural and engineered systems. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Applications in Biological Engineering
description: Discussion and investigation of special topics, problems and applications of biological engineering.

subject: BE
title: Mass and Energy Balances
description: DP. Introduction of the principles of mass and energy conservation; development of systematic approaches to apply these principles in calculations for design and analysis of biochemical, chemical, and physical processes.
prerequisites: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or 171 or 181A, PHYS 170, and MATH 242 or 252A) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Dynamic Systems Modeling
description: DP. Introduction to analytical and numerical solutions for systems of differential equations. Modeling and computer simulation of representative dynamic systems encountered in biological engineering. A-F only.
prerequisites: (BE 260, ECE 110 or 160, MATH 243 or 253A, CEE 270) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent. Co-requisite: BE 350L.

subject: BE
title: Dynamic Systems Modeling Laboratory
description: DY. Industry field trips and lab experiences to illustrate behavior of representative dynamic systems in biological engineering. Data acquisition and model validation. A-F only.

subject: BE
title: Transport Phenomena
description: DP. Fundamental principles and applications relating to mass, momentum, and energy transfers in biosystems and other systems for engineers and scientists.
prerequisites: BE 260, CEE 270, MATH 243 or 253A, ME 311 (or concurrent).

subject: BE
title: Engineering Economics
description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CEE 405)
prerequisites: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing.

subject: BE
title: Biomass Conversion to Biofuels and Bioenergy
description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production; fundamental concepts in biofuel/ bioenergy production; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel/bioenergy; biodiesel production; environmental impacts, economics and life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: BE 373 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

subject: BE
title: Food Engineering
description: DP. Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as FSHN 411 and MBBE 411)
prerequisites: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: DP. Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems. (Cross-listed as MBBE 420)
prerequisites: (ECE 160, ECE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: ART
title: Methods in Contemporary Art
description: Examines processes of inquiry and experimentation within studio practice. Students explore a range of research methods as a way to challenge habitual methodologies and expand notions of art and art making. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ART
title: Materials in Contemporary Art
description: Explores the physical, historical, symbolic, and contextual capacity of materials, as well as the mutually constitutive roles of artist and materials within the creative process. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ART
title: Graduate Studio Teaching Practicum
description: Observation, analysis and participation in teaching a lower division course under the direction of an instructor in the student’s area of concentration. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: ART 690, admitted to candidacy for MFA in art, and consent

subject: ART
title: Art Historical Methodology
description: An introduction to art historiography, analytical techniques, and research methods and materials.

subject: ART
title: Art of Oceania
description: Arts from Polynesia, Melanesia, Micronesia explored in context of issues involving belief systems and cultural change. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Topics in the Art of China
description: Research topics in the history of Chinese sculpture, ceramics, bronzes, jade, and textiles. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Contemporary Critical Theory
description: Research and discussion seminar supporting advanced critical theory in the context of contemporary art and other creative practice.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Global Contemporary Art
description: Selected topics in global contemporary art history. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Western Art History
description: Selected topics in European and American art history.

subject: ART
title: Directed Work
description: Advanced individual projects; advanced tutorial. Maximum: 3 credit hours per semester; total 6 for MA Plan A, 9 for MA Plan B, MFA students must petition OGE for permission to apply toward degree requirement. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and department chair

subject: ART
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Japanese Art
description: Selected topics in Japanese art history.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in South/Southeast Asian Art History
description: Selected topics in South and/or Southeast Asian art and architectural history with an emphasis on Hindu and Buddhist traditions. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ART
title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism. A-F only. (Alt. 2-3 years) (Cross-listed as ASAN 792)

subject: CALL
title: Exploring Expression: Foundations in Arts, Languages & Letters
description: First-year seminar for majors in the College of Arts, Languages & Letters that includes emphasis on the introduction to studies in a liberal arts curriculum and emphasizes the importance of writing in this discipline. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: CALL majors only, or consent. Freshmen only.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies
description:
DH
Introductory course focuses on change and continuity in the history, culture, values, and political institutions of South, East, and Southeast Asia, and the region’s interrelationships with the rest of the world. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Asia
description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in Asia through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions. A-F only.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Research and Writing in Asian Studies
description:
FW
Introduction to research and writing in Asian Studies provides a structured overview of the research and writing process from an interdisciplinary perspective, focused on Asia. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies: East Asia
description:
DH
Understanding East Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies: South/ Southeast Asia
description:
DH
Understanding South and Southeast Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

subject: ASAN
title: East Asian Popular Cultures
description:
DS
East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 259)

subject: ASAN
title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
description:
DA
Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as IP 303)

subject: ASAN
title: Career Pathways in Asian Studies
description: Explore the range of careers related to Asian Studies and develop skills and materials to build your academic success into a meaningful career. Students create a job search portfolio they can share with prospective employers.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Political Economy
description:
DS
Interdisciplinary review and analysis of the social and political issues in contemporary China, the interchange between state and society in national policies, the relationship between cultural tradition and technological modernization in the social transformation process. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 308)

subject: ASAN
title: Studying Asia Culturally
description:
DH
Multidisciplinary. Classics of literature, philosophy, and religion shaping Asian beliefs and values.
prerequisites: ASAN 201 and ASAN 202 are recommended, but not required

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Asia
description:
DS
Multidisciplinary examination of problems and issues affecting peoples and institutions of contemporary Asia: ethnic, language, religious, and cultural differences; population growth; public health; economic development; political and social change; environmental problems; etc.
prerequisites: ASAN 201 and ASAN 202 are recommended, but not required

subject: ASAN
title: Asia Past and Present
description:
DS
Multidisciplinary examination of major Asian countries; cultural, social, economic, and political lives of their peoples. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (O) Okinawa; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other. Repeatable three times in different alphas.

subject: ASAN
title: The Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
description:
DH
History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills. (Cross-listed as HIST 323)

subject: ASAN
title: Chado-the Way of Tea Practicum
description:
DA
Actual practice of the tea ceremony as history and culture of Japan. Repeatable one time.

subject: ASAN
title: Japanese Film: Art and History
description:
DH
Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics. (Cross-listed as EALL 325)

subject: ASAN
title: Media, Advertising & Desire in East Asia
description:
DH
Examines concepts of beauty and desire in East Asian cultures within historical and contemporary media contexts. Uses critical theory and in-depth case studies to explore how images, language, and branding work in contemporary Asian societies. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Film: Art and History
description:
DH
Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (Cross-listed as EALL 330)

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course. (Cross-listed as THEA 336)

subject: ASAN
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description:
DS
An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change. (Cross-listed as GEO 356)

subject: ASAN
title: Buddhist Philosophy
description:
DH
Survey of central thinkers and schools. (Cross-listed as PHIL 360)

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
description:
DL
Survey in English traditional and modern literatures of Southeast Asia. A-F only. (Cross-listed as IP 361)

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Chemistry Lab
description: DY (1 3.5- hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed 161L or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161L or 181A without instructor override. (Fall only)

subject: CHEM
title: Honors General Chemistry
description: DP Rigorous, in-depth introduction to chemical principles with emphasis on experimental and applied aspects of modern chemistry. Students who successfully completed 161 or 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 181A without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 or 171 without instructor override. (Fall only)
prerequisites: satisfactory placement exam score and MATH 215 (or concurrent) or MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: CHEM
title: Honors General Chemistry Laboratory
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating chemical principles involving advanced techniques and modern instrumentation. A-F only. Students who successfully completed 161L or 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 181L without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 181L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161L or 171L without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry I
description: DP Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 162 or 171 or 181A.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry I Lab
description: DY (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 162L, 171L, or 181L; and C (not C-) or better in 272 (or concurrent).

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry II
description: DP Continuation of 272. Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry II Lab
description: DY (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 272L and 273 (or concurrent).

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry
description: DP Selected methods and principles, e.g., phase equilibria, ionic equilibria, electrode equilibria, separations, spectroscopy, automation, and process control.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 162 or 171 or 181A, MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A.

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry Lab
description: DY (2 3-hr Lab) Phase separations, chromatography, titrimetry, spectrophotometry, etc.
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in 162L or 171L or 181L; and 274 (or concurrent).

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Chemistry I
description: DP Principles and theories; physico-chemical procedures.
prerequisites: 274, 274L, PHYS 272, PHYS 272L, and MATH 243 or MATH 253A.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Chemistry II
description: DP Continuation of 351.

subject: CHEM
title: Physico-Chemical Measurements
description: DY (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory on instrumentation, measurements, and data analysis in thermodynamics, spectroscopy, and other areas of physical chemistry. Emphasis on instruction in scientific reporting writing.

subject: CHEM
title: Bioorganic Chemistry
description: DB Mechanism of biochemical reactions, biophysical structure, techniques for studying biochemical reactions. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 273 (with a grade of C or better) or graduate standing with consent, or departmental approval.

subject: CHEM
title: Professional Ethics for Chemists
description: Student team-led discussions of contemporary ethical issues and ethical decision making in chemistry using case studies and additional examples from the media. CHEM or BIOC majors only. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: CHEM
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading and discussion of scientific journal articles culminating in a written literature review. Repeatable unlimited times. CHEM or BIOC majors only.
prerequisites: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0.

subject: CHEM
title: Directed Research
description: Directed laboratory research culminating in a written research report. Repeatable unlimited times. CHEM or BIOC majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0.

subject: CHEM
title: Synthesis and Analysis of Inorganic Compounds
description: DP Lecture on advanced methods of preparation and characterization of inorganic compounds and materials. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CHEM
title: Preparation and Analysis of Inoraganic Compounds Laboratory
description: DY Laboratory on preparative methods and analytical techniques and instruments in inorganic chemistry. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: DP Classification, description, fundamental theory.

subject: CHEM
title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods—theory and hands-on experience. (Crosslisted as ME 435)

subject: CHEM
title: Synthesis and Analysis of Organic Compounds
description: DP Introduction to multi-step synthesis and instruments/analytical techniques used to characterize organic compounds. Retrosynthesis and diastereoselective reactions; spectroscopy (optical methods, NMR), mass spectrometry. Chromatography (GC, HPLC) and coupled techniques (GCMS, LCMS). CHEM or BIOC majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: 273 with a grade of C (not C-) or better, or departmental approval.

subject: CHEM
title: Preparation and Analysis of Organic Compounds Laboratory
description: DY Laboratory on the preparation of organic compounds and physical methods for their characterization. Includes optical methods (UV-vis, IR), chromatography (HPLC, GC), mass spectrometry (GCMS and LCMS) and NMR. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: 273L with a grade of C (not C-) or better, or departmental approval. Co-requisite: 445.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Biochemistry
description: DP Biochemical thermodynamics, chemical and enzyme kinetics, biomolecular structure, and biomolecular spectroscopy. A-F only.
prerequisites: 162, PHYS 272, and MATH 242 or 252A with a grade of C or better for prerequisites.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Biochemistry
description: Advanced topics in biochemistry including nucleic acid replication, transcription, and translation; genetic and epigenetic regulation; bioenergetics and control of metabolism; alternative metabolic strategies; and enzyme structure and mechanism. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Biochemistry Lab
description: Advanced biochemistry lab techniques: protein purification and characterization, identification of unknown proteins, enzyme kinetics, ligand binding, enzyme kinetics, protein structure, and spectroscopy, with instruction in writing scientific reports. A-F only.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Research
description: Introduction to field-specific methods and skills needed for success in graduate research. Includes training modules for safety, ethics, and library resources. Short faculty research overviews may also be given.CHEM majors only. Graduate students only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: CHEM
title: Theory of Chemical Bonding
description: Application of quantum mechanics and symmetry principles to descriptions of chemical bonding.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Applications of Spectroscopy
description: Introduction to magnetic resonance, infrared, UV, and visible spectroscopy, emphasizing applications to organic and inorganic chemistry. Three topics each semester–1 credit hour per topic. Repeatable unlimited times in different topics.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallics I
description: Reactivity and reaction mechanisms of compounds containing metalcarbon bonds.

subject: CHEM
title: Coordination Chemistry
description: Survey of Lewis acids and bases, coordination numbers, geometries, stereochemistry, ligand field theory, formation constants, and bioinorganic chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallics II
description: Introduction to the principles of catalysis and the classes of catalytic reactions effected by organometallic compounds. A-F only.
prerequisites: 622 and a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B.

subject: CHEM
title: Methods of Instrumental Analysis
description: Theory, instrumentation, applications. Three areas each semester-one credit hour per area. Repeatable unlimited times in different areas.
prerequisites: 333 and graduate standing in CHEM or consent.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Structure Determination
description: Interpretation of chemical and physical (primarily spectral) data in the identification of organic compounds.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Synthesis I
description: Modern synthetic methods with emphasis on the design and execution of multi-step sequences.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Organic Chemistry
description: Theory of molecular structure, stereochemistry, and reaction mechanisms.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Synthesis II
description: Continuation of 642, and is the second half of a two-semester course in Modern Organic Synthesis.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Derivatives
description: Will familiarize the students with the mathematical foundation and the application of Futures, Swaps, and Options. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Forecasting
description: Focus on financial forecasting and financial econometrics as volatility and correlation modeling. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Insurance and Risk Management
description: Introduces students to topics in the actuarial science and latest developments in risk management. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Interest Rate/Credit Models
description: Addresses specific properties of interest rate modelling as mean reversion as well as latest developments in credit risk modelling. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Modelling
