description: Addresses advanced techniques in financial modelling and related fields. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Mortgage/Weather Derivatives
description: Covers the real estate market, mortgage backed securities (MBSs) and real estate derivatives. Focuses on modelling weather, climate change, and weather derivatives. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Seminar in Finance
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. May be repeated with change in topic.

subject: FIN
title: Research Seminar
description: Students either program a model or write a paper with high practical or scientific merit. Outcome enhances the chances for employment. Represents the culminating experience for students in this program. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Healthcare Financial Management
description: Focus on important accounting and financial management principles relevant to management of health services organizations. Designed around a series of cases that examine the issues that confront healthcare managers. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall only)

subject: FIN
title: Foundations of Finance
description: First PhD course in finance. Covers basic theory and empirical methodology in asset pricing, provides a concise framework of conceptual knowledge to understand the literature on financial theory and related empirical evidence. A-F only.

subject: FIN
title: Seminar in Investments
description: Covers research issues in investments. Topics include empirical asset pricing tests, characteristics of asset returns, behavioral finance, and investment issues that overlaps with corporate finance, accounting, and economics, etc. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in business administration, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Corporate Finance
description: Covers research issues in corporate finance and financial markets. Topics include capital structure theory, corporate governance, corporate innovations, and mergers and acquisitions, etc. Student develop academic research papers that lead to dissertation work. A-F only.
prerequisites: student status in PhD in business administration, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Asian Finance
description: Provides in-depth review of scholarly journal articles and working papers relevant to Asian-Pacific financial markets to prepare PhD students for scholarly research work focusing on market microstructure, corporate finance, investments. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in business administration, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by department chair and the faculty advisor. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in international management, or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Safety and Sanitation
description: Principles and procedures of sanitation and safety in the food service industry, including the study of foodborne illnesses, biological, chemical, physical hazards and cross-contamination as they may occur during the flow of food.

subject: FSHN
title: Culture and Cuisine: The Global Diversity of Food
description: A timeline of the world history of food and how it relates to culture, diversity, ethnicity, and religion. International food demonstrations and tastings included.

subject: FSHN
title: Introduction to Food Preparation
description: Lectures, discussions, and demonstrations on how food components contribute to the functional, sensory, and safety characteristics of foods, and what changes occur in foods due to preparation, processing, and storage.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Preparation Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments in foods emphasizing ingredient function and standard preparation methods for food groups.

subject: FSHN
title: The Science of Human Nutrition
description: Integration of natural science concepts basic to the study of human nutrition. Emphasis on nutrient requirements of healthy individuals, food sources, functions of nutrients.

subject: FSHN
title: Comparative Nutrition
description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors. (Cross-listed as ANSC 244)
prerequisites: (ANSC 200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161/161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Systems Management
description: Critical and essential aspects of management and effective leadership practices to direct and delivery quality foodservices. Focus on the role and competencies of the Registered Dietitian (RD) working in these environments.
prerequisites: (181 and 181L (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Production and Operations
description: Principles and procedures of menu planning, quantity food production, production scheduling, recipe adaptation, equipment operation, and formula costing. Principles of procurement including purchasing, selection, storage of equipment and quantity foods.
prerequisites: (181 and 181L) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Marketing Nutrition and Food
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental marketing principles applied to nutrition and food. Will include concepts such as the psychology of food purchasing decisions and consumer behavior. Field trips and group projects included. Open to non-majors.

subject: FSHN
title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ANSC 350)

subject: FSHN
title: Applied Professional Skills in Nutrition
description: Will apply skills in technology, research, and career development to nutrition. Students will identify evidence-based nutrition information and demonstrate their academic skill sets for future professional success through technology. (Summer only)

subject: FSHN
title: Lifespan Nutrition
description: Physiological changes and nutritional requirements during human life stages: prepregnancy, pregnancy, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
prerequisites: B or better in 185; C or better in CHEM 161/161L; C or better in PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent)

subject: FSHN
title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental approach to study food preparation problems. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports. Subject matter used to practice critical thinking and problem solving skills. A-F only.
prerequisites: (181/181L, CHEM 161/161L) with a minimum grade of C. Co-requisite: 381L.

subject: FSHN
title: Experimental Foods Laboratory
description: Experimental approach to study food preparation, food formulation, and sensory evaluation with laboratory exercises in a certified kitchen environment. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports. A-F only.
prerequisites: (181/181L, CHEM 161/161L) with a minimum grade of D. Co-requisite: 381.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Assessment
description: Addresses concepts and uses of nutrition assessment tools at individual and community levels. Students will be introduced to national surveys and new, more sophisticated body composition measurements. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.
prerequisites: (185 and 370 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: FSHN
title: Microbiology of Foods
description: Microorganisms encountered in foods; types of food spoilage; microbial hazards in food; methods of food preservation.
prerequisites: (MICR 130 and MICR 140L, or MICR 351 and MICR 351L) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Engineering
description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as BE 411 and MBBE 411)
prerequisites: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design c

subject: COM
title: Communication and Gender
description: Theories and issues related to gender and communication applied to organizational, intercultural, and technology mediated communication. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Building Communication Theory
description: Major theories of communication in terms of requirements for a theory, theory development, associated research, and application.
prerequisites: COM major and junior standing, or consent.

subject: COM
title: Special Topics in Communication
description: Topics of relevance to the focus areas of Communication in Communities, Media Arts, and ICTs & Policy; taught by regular and visiting faculty. Repeatable on different topics to six credit hours. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Political Communication in the Digital Era
description: An examination of how various aspects of digital media platforms, such as affordances and communication processes impact political outcomes. COM majors or consent. Sophomore standing or higher. (Fall only)

subject: COM
title: Capstone in Media Arts Design and Development
description: Design, development, and evaluation of computer-based media arts communication. Emphasizes authoring and production of such media elements as video, audio, and graphics. COM majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: COM 310 and COM 320 and COM 330 and COM 337, or consent.

subject: COM
title: Capstone in Communication in Communities
description: Synthesize knowledge, apply research findings in service to community, and develop proposal for intervention or campaign through assignments that emphasize the development of writing skills. COM majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: COM 310 and COM 320 and COM 330; and COM 340 or COM 421; or consent.

subject: COM
title: Capstone Project in ICTs and Policy
description: Written research or media project focused on specific ICT and policy problems, including social media, digital games, and the internet. COM majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: COM 310 and COM 320 and COM 330; and COM 432 or COM 438; or consent.

subject: COM
title: Communication Seminar
description: Application of theoretic and methodological criteria to researchable questions. Topics will vary.
prerequisites: COM 201 and senior standing, or consent.

subject: COM
title: Communicating Creativity
description: The role of communication in fostering or inhibiting creativity. Exploration of theoretical bases for shared scientific or artistic creativity in communication research. COM major or consent. (Once a year)
prerequisites: COM 201 and senior standing, or consent.

subject: COM
title: Senior Thesis Project
description: Completion of the thesis project appropriate to the selected focus area within the context of a seminar. Emphasis on ongoing process of writing, editing, review, and revision.
prerequisites: COM major and senior standing, or consent.

subject: COM
title: Communication Internship
description: Application of communication skills and knowledge. Under faculty supervision, interns participate in operations of an organization and analyze communication processes and effects; (B) community setting; (C) Communication program activity. Maximum of three credits per semester; six credits total toward major; each alpha repeatable up to three credits.

subject: COM
title: Special Problems
description: Independent study of selected topics under faculty supervision. Repeatable up to three credits.
prerequisites: COM major and junior standing, or consent.

subject: COM
title: Communication Theories
description: Systematic study of major theories of communication and current status of communication research.

subject: COM
title: Communication Inquiry
description: Introduction to inquiry and the array of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication.

subject: COM
title: Strategic Organizational Communication
description: Theories, concepts, and applications of strategic communication and public relations to achieve organizational goals.

subject: COM
title: Information and Communication Technologies
description: Information and communication technologies, structures, processes, and networks as an area of research and study in the social sciences.

subject: COM
title: Social Media
description: Systematic study from a social science perspective of current and emerging social media. Attention to user needs and impact.

subject: COM
title: Intercultural Communication
description: Problems and opportunities of intercultural communication from theory and research, consulting and training, and policy and program perspectives.

subject: COM
title: Global Communication and Journalism
description: Analysis of the emerging global media landscape as digital technologies enable the sharing of news, information, and commentary across geographical and cultural borders. Focuses on causes, characteristics, and consequences.

subject: COM
title: Digital Storytelling
description: Focus on development of narrative-based creative activities in all mediums (text, audio, video, etc.) within communication contexts, i.e., journalism, film, public relations, etc. COM majors only. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Intervention in Multicultural Organizations
description: Describes the array of communication-related intervention programs designed to enhance effectiveness in multicultural organizations at home and abroad. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Media Effects
description: Critical examination of major media effects theories and topic areas. Must be enrolled in one of the following majors: COM, CIS majors only. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Public Diplomacy and Communication
description: Analysis of the emerging trends in international relations from communication and public relations perspectives. Focuses on factors, characteristics, and processes. COM majors only. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: ICT Policy and Planning
description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives. (Cross-listed as PUBA 628)

subject: COM
title: Communication Topics
description: Coverage in depth of some area of theory and research. Repeatable one time.

subject: COM
title: Communication Research Seminar
description: General research seminar in communication. In-depth coverage of specific research methods to develop, refine, or interpret graduate students’ thesis or dissertation projects. COM, CIS majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: COM 611 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: COM
title: Communication Practicum
description: Supervised work experience, study of an organization, and career planning. Required of Plan B students in the main communication program. Repeatable up to six credits. CR/NC only.

subject: COM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: COM
title: Thesis
description: Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: CIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Theories of Society
description: A critical review of major theoretical and empirical traditions in communication and information sciences. Focus on European, American, Third World, and applied research.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Technologies
description: Technological concepts underlying data communications; information processing and computers; communication channels and networks, information storage and retrieval, and computer hardware and software.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Research Methods
description: Current research methodologies in decision sciences, computer science, library science, and communication. Emphasis on methodologies suitable for interdisciplinary analysis.

subject: CIS
title: Special Topics in Communication and Information Sciences
description: Seminar reflecting research interests of faculty and current interdisciplinary topics in communication and information sciences. Repeatable unlimited times. Graduate students only.

subject: CIS
title: Data Science Foundations
description: All aspects of data science: the methodology and processes; ethics and regulatory issues; programming tools; data acquisition, cleaning, analysis and mining; visualization, publication, curation, and preservation; applications in various fields. Graduate students only.

subject: CIS
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Communication and Information Sciences
description: Exploration of relationships between disciplines in social sciences, science and technology, and humanities. Faculty and student presentations. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: CIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Repeatable unlimited times. Plan must include goals and rationale.

subject: CIS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CSD
title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
description: Will overview anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing. Students gain exposure to structures and functions of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, deglutition, and hearing systems required for normal communication and swallowing. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CSD
title: Phonetics
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of phonetic and phonological development. International Phonetic Alphabet Transcription of English speech sounds; phonological developments and m

subject: COMG
title: Nonverbal Communication
description: Understanding communication beyond the words themselves. Review of theory and research on gestures, facial expressions, touch, personal space, and physical appearance.
prerequisites: Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Verbal Communication
description: Roles of language in human communication and social relationships; language variation, change, and social consequences.
prerequisites: Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Deceptive Communication
description: Survey of major social scientific theories, concepts, and research findings on deceptive communication, in a lecture/discussion format. Emphasis is on how people create deceptive messages, induce deception, and strategies used to detect deception.
prerequisites: Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Relational Management
description: Survey and critical discussion of current theory and research in relational management. Focus on written analysis of the role of communication in the initiation, maintenance, decline, and dissolution of different types of relationships.

subject: COMG
title: Communicating Social Support
description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships. (Cross-listed as PSY 477)

subject: COMG
title: Teaching Speech
description: For communicology majors who lead, under supervision, a freshman seminar section of communicology.

subject: COMG
title: Health Communication
description: Develop understanding of the process through which communication influences health outcomes, and learn how to design effective health communication programs using theory and research.
prerequisites: Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Directed Reading
prerequisites: Pre: consent of department chair and instructor.

subject: COMG
title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
description: Enrollment for degree completion. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: master’s Plan B candidate and consent.

subject: COMG
title: Theories in Communicology
description: Major theoretical foundations; humanistic and social scientific perspectives. Examination of the research and the development of different models of human communication. A-F only.

subject: COMG
title: Research Methods in Communicology
description: Design and analysis of quantitative research in communicology. Focus on measurement issues, research design, descriptive and inferential statistics. A-F only.

subject: COMG
title: Advanced Research Methods in Communicology
description: Advanced focus on survey, laboratory, and field study design, data collection, and data analysis. Emphasis on control of variance through design and statistical analysis. Appropriate preparation for graduate theses and dissertations. A-F only.

subject: COMG
title: Practicum for Instructional Communication
description: Combined seminar and lecture/ discussion format on techniques and procedures for teaching communication skills and their related components in a laboratory setting. CR/NC only. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: COMG majors only. Pre: COMG GTA or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Business Communication
description: Analysis of communication issues in business through discussion of verbal/nonverbal messages, interpersonal relationships, conflict, and persuasion. Focus on interviewing, group communication, and public speaking skills. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) or 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Persuasion and Social Influence
description: Theories of persuasion and resistance to persuasion; assessment of attitudes and measurement of change. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) or 602 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Creating Understanding
description: Theory and research on human communication, social cognition, comprehension, and creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories, metacognition, prediction, inference-making, and communication systems. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) or 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Relational Communication
description: Major models and theories of interpersonal communication; research on interpersonal relationships; interaction and functions of human communication. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Foundations of Intercultural Communication
description: Major models, theories, and concepts of intercultural communication; basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to intercultural communication; research on intercultural communication. Graduate standing only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. Only three credits can count toward degree.

subject: COMG
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable three times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: COMG
title: Approaches to Instructional Communication
description: Seminar on communication theories and models in instructional environment; emphasis on message processing, classroom dynamics, cognitive and metacognitive processes associated with learning, and learning assessment. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) or 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Research in Intergroup Communication
description: Theory, concepts, research, and application of communication processes between members of different social groups. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) or 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Special Topics in Communicology
description: Substantive areas in communication that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addresed in other COMG courses. Topics vary each semester. Content to be announced. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Persuasion and Influence
description: Contemporary research in persuasion and influence. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Issues in Message Processing
description: Contemporary research in verbal and nonverbal message processing. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Relational Communication
description: Contemporary research in interpersonal relations. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Research on Intercultural Communication
description: Functional approach to the study of communication in intercultural settings. Examination of culture-based variables and their impact on social influence, relational management, and message processing. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Artificial Intelligence and Communication
description: Comprehensive understanding of the role and function of computer technology (including. A.I.) within the field of communication. Basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to semi-intelligent artifacts as information source or receiver. A-F only.
prerequisites: COMG majors or consent. Graduate students only. Pre: 601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Health Communication Research
description: Contemporary interpersonal and/ or public communication issues in health communication research. Topics include communication functions such as information management, interpersonal influence, relational management, emotional management, social influence. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: CAAM
title: Mindfulness Meditation and Stress Reduction
description: Practice mindfulness meditation to reduce burnout and live life in the present moment. Learn life skills to handle life better and be more resilient. Respond rather than react to life. Repeatable nine times.

subject: CAAM
title: Clinical Nutrition
description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations, and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Junior standing and higher. Pre: CHEM 151 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or BIOL 171 or approval from instructor; highly encouraged: FSHN 185 or any other basic nutrition course.

subject: CAAM
title: Introduction to Integrative Medicine
description: Overview of integrative (complementary) medicine covering Traditional Chinese Medicine, Ayurvedic medicine, naturapathy, traditional healing practices, homeopathy, nutrition and diet, herbs and dietary supplements, environmental health, mind-body, energy, spiritual, and positive psychology. Repeatable one time.

subject: CAAM
title: Nutrition for Clinicians
description: Provides in-depth lectures and case studies reviewing the role of nutritional therapy in health and illness. CR/NC only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: MD majors only. Pre: MDED 554 or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years)
description: Emphasizes interrelated historical and philosophical roots and socio-cultural context and their influence on policy and practice in early childhood education settings. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years) Lab
description: Direct experience with children in early childhood settings in order to apply co

subject: CINE
title: Global Media
description: Close textual analysis and strategic analysis of global media dynamics with an emphasis on transnational media corporations.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Arts Internship
description: Internship in professional cinematic, television, animation and/or digital media production company under professional and faculty supervision. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: CINE
title: Directed Study
description: Independent research or creative project under the supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of 399/499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: CINE
title: Classical 2D Full Animation
description: Hand drawn full animation techniques; rough animation, inbetweening, clean up animation and digital color processes. Digital line testing, sync dialog and other advanced skills for classical 2D full animation.

subject: CEE
title: Surveying/Geodesy/Geomatics
description: Plane surveying for cadastral, engineering, and construction applications including taping, leveling, traverses, bearings and azimuths, areas and volumes, EDM. Geodesy, map projections, satellite geodesy (GPS), geodetic surveying and photogrammetry. Field lab in notes and procedures. Repeatable one time.

subject: CEE
title: CAD/BIM/3D Visualization
description: Computer-aided drafting (CAD) tools using AutoCAD and Revit. AutoCAD interface, titleblocks, model/paper space, viewports, texts and annotation, dimensioning. Basics of BIM, toolbox, modeling techniques, annotating, dimensioning. CAD drafting to real-world engineering applications. Repeatable one time.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mechanics I
description: Forces, resultants, and equilibrium; analysis of trusses, frames, and machines; centroids, moments of inertia; friction.
prerequisites: grade of C or better in all of the following: PHYS 170; MATH 242 or 252A; and either MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mechanics II
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy. (Cross-listed as ME 271)
prerequisites: C or better in 270; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

subject: CEE
title: Applied Probability and Statistics
description: Description of sample data; correlation and regression; probability and statistical distributions; estimations of population parameters; fitting distributions to histograms; hypothesis testing.

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics Fundamentals
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Compressible and incompressible fluid properties; fluid statics; kinematics, energy and momentum considerations in steady flows; application of steady flow concepts to various fluid processes; with an emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Engineering
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Parameters and indices of environmental quality; materials balances; chemical kinetics; ideal reactor models; water and air pollution control; solid and hazardous waste management; emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering I
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to geotechnical engineering: soil characterization, index properties, seepage and flow in soil, stresses in soils, compressibility, consolidation, shear strength. Substantial emphasis on writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Fundamentals of Transportation
description: Transportation modes: land, air, water, pipelines. Tourist, urban transportation. Geometric design, human factors, vehicular flow models, capacity analysis. Overview: traffic impact, air quality, parking studies.

subject: CEE
title: Mechanics of Solids
description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, constitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading. (Crosslisted as ME 371)
prerequisites: C or better in all of the following: 270; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

subject: CEE
title: Mechanics of Materials Lab
description: Tension, compression, and torsion of bars, and bending of beams.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Materials
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Concrete properties, role of aggregates, concrete mix design, supplementary cementitious materials, chemical admixtures, behavior of concrete, concrete testing, field practices. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prerequisites: 305 (or concurrent); and 370 with a minimum grade of C or better

subject: CEE
title: Structural Analysis
description: Analysis of statically determinate plane and space trusses and frames; deflections; introduction to matrix methods; computer applications.
prerequisites: 370 with a minimum grade of C or better

subject: CEE
title: Engineering Economics
description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis. (Cross-listed as BE 405)
prerequisites: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing

subject: CEE
title: Computer Methods in Engineering Systems
description: Numerical solutions of engineering problems using digital computers. Regression analysis; numerical differentiation and integration; solutions of algebraic, transcendental, and differential equations; and analysis of large structural systems.

subject: CEE
title: Engineering Hydraulics
description: Hydraulics of closed conduits and open channels with emphasis on engineering applications. Topics also include pump hydraulics, bridge hydraulics, urban drainage engineering, and flood plain management.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
description: Introduction to basic concepts of pollutant transport phenomenon through theoretical modeling, lab and field experiments and observations. Specific topics include mass balance, jets and plumes, mixing and transport in rivers, reservoirs, groundwater and estuaries; non point course pollution. (Alt. years)

subject: CEE
title: Applied Hydrology
description: Surface water hydrology topics include hydrologic cycle, hydrographs, regression methods, urban rain-runoff process, flood frequency analysis, flood routing and hydrology for detention basin design. Groundwater hydrology topics include seawater intrusion, theory of groundwater flow and solutions to steady and unsteady aquifer flows.

subject: CEE
title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
description: Hydrologic fundamentals of water demand and supply; water and wastewater distribution; collection systems; quality characterization; analytical methods for water quality management.

subject: CEE
title: Water/Wastewater Treatment Design
description: Physical operations, chemical and biological processes, design flow and process loading rates, pilot plant testing, and treatment plant design.

subject: CEE
title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 440)

subject: CEE
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as OCN 441 and SUST 441)

subject: CEE
title: Infrastructure: Project Impacts, Policy and Sustainability
description: Evaluation of infrastructure impacts. Impacts regulation and mitigation. Effects of environmental and other policies on infrastructure. Infrastructure relations to sustainability. Energy consumption, transportation efficiency and infrastructure recycling. Lectures and presentations by experts and enrolled students. (Cross-listed as SUST 444)
prerequisites: senior standing, open to engineering, science, urban planning, and economics majors

subject: CEE
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. (Cross-listed as ATMO 449 and SUST 449)
prerequisites: Senior standing or higher, or consent

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering II
description: Continuation of 355 field exploration, lateral earth pressures, bearing capacity theory,

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
description: Major writers: emphasis on Homer, drama, and philosophy. Assignments are essay-based and attention is given to developing academic writing skills.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher or consent

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Roman Literature in Translation
description: Major writers: emphasis on Vergil, satire, and novel.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher or consent

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Epic
description: A survey of Greek and Roman epic literature, beginning with Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey and proceeding through the Hellenistic Greek and Roman periods.

subject: CLAS
title: Topics in Ancient Greek Thought
description: Explore a central aspect of ancient Greek philosophy and literature. This may be a theme, such as tragedy or emotions; a thinker, such as Aristotle; or a since monumental text, such as Plato’s Republic. (Cross-listed as PHIL 332)

subject: CLAS
title: Archaeology of Ancient Greece
description: Introduction to the field of Greek archaeology and methods of archaeological research in the Mediterranean.

subject: CLAS
title: Archaeology of Ancient Rome
description: Examines the archaeology of the Roman world from the Etruscan period to the reign of the emperor Constantine.

subject: CLAS
title: Literatures of Ancient India
description: Survey of South Asian literature from ancient times to the early medieval period; focusing on Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Tamil poetry traditions. Readings in English translation. (Cross-listed as IP 366)

subject: CLAS
title: Art of Greece and Rome
description: Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome. (Cross-listed as ART 373)

subject: CLAS
title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
description: Historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states, Macedonia, the Hellenistic, and Roman Empires. (Cross-listed as HIST 430)

subject: COM
title: Introduction to Communication
description: An overview of communication emphasizing intercultural, organizational and international communication and media arts with introduction to multimedia, ICTs, and public relations perspectives.

subject: COM
title: Media Arts
description: Combined lecture-discussion on theories and criticism of visual media, covering aesthetic development and delivery through multimedia and cinematic principles. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Communication and Communities
description: Combined lecture-discussion on communication within organizational communities and between organizations and their communities with attention to intercultural issues in local, global, and online interactions.

subject: COM
title: Communicating Sustainability
description: Application of scientific communication theory, strategic communication, and multimedia techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability. (Crosslisted as SUST 325)
prerequisites: COM 201 or consent. COM majors only. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Information and Communication Technology Concepts
description: Combined lecture discussion on basic technical concepts related to ICTs embedded in sociocultural context.

subject: COM
title: Techniques of Video and Digital Cinema
description: Orientation to techniques of production. Emphasis on history, language, and theory of the creative process and application to media productions.

subject: COM
title: Media Arts Techniques
description: Combined lecture-lab providing an orientation to, and examination of, procedures and techniques of media arts production. Emphasis on new media literacy, human-computer interaction, and basic electronic media tools for communication design.

subject: COM
title: Public Relations Writing
description: Enhance students’ professional writing skills in the contemporary public relations field and equip students with the foundations of essential techniques for persuasive communication.
prerequisites: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B). COM majors or consent. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Intercultural Communication
description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of intercultural contexts. Focus on theory, research, and managing intercultural effectiveness.

subject: COM
title: Information Technology and Health Communication
description: Combined lecture-discussion on the application of ICTs for health communication from the aspect of technologies, systems, services, and policies.

subject: COM
title: Computer-Mediated Communication
description: Combine lecture-discussion on the evolution of computer-mediated communication from the 1970s to current day. Examines the development of online communities, technologies, and their networked online and offline social practices.

subject: COM
title: Digital Cultures
description: Introduction to the social, cultural, and ethical implications of information and communication technologies by studying new and emerging media including games, interactive media, and virtual worlds.

subject: COM
title: Esports and Society
description: Introduction to professional and collegiate esports (electronic sports) in global context, including theories related to leisure and gaming, and current academic and industry developments. No previous technical or gaming experience is required.
prerequisites: COM major or consent. COM majors only. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Media Communications and Conflict
description: Mass communication and conflict; deals with understanding the role of news media in influencing conflict, and introduces students to conflict-sensitive communications working to assist in resolving conflicts. (Cross-listed as PACE 380)
prerequisites: any 200-level DS course. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: COM
title: Emerging Topics in Communication
description: Emerging communication topics of interest to faculty and students. Repeatable one time on different topics, up to six credits.

subject: COM
title: Survey of Inquiry Methods in Communication
description: Exploration of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication studies and related professional work.

subject: COM
title: Communication in Multicultural Organizations
description: Cultural diversity in multicultural and multinational organizations is examined regarding communication-related aspects of working life.

subject: COM
title: Public Relations Strategies
description: Exploring the practice and effects of public relations. Strategic management functions, including use of communication technologies, communication with diverse publics, ethics and social responsibility will be emphasized.
prerequisites: COM majors only or consent. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Public Relations Campaigns
description: Synthesizing and applying the principles and techniques of public relations to create comprehensive campaigns.
prerequisites: COM 421 or consent. COM majors only. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Filming Social Change
description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects. (Cross-listed as ES 425)
prerequisites: one DH or DS course, or consent. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Environmental Storytelling Through an Indigenous Lens
description: Through media arts storytelling techniques, will focus on reframing perspectives and creativity from an Indigenous lens to communicate environmental-centric stories geared toward improving our communities’ quality of life.

subject: COM
title: Studio Production
description: Studio production ranging from three-camera studio production to broadcast and magazine show formats to on-line web production. Fundamental knowledge of lighting, sound, blocking, and equipment competency.

subject: COM
title: Social Media
description: Combined lecture-discussion on the sociocultural, political, psychological, historical and policy dimensions of social media for societies past, contemporary, and future.
prerequisites: COM majors only or consent. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Video Scriptwriting
description: Application of communication theory to creating and revising commercial and dramatic script material for video production.

subject: COM
title: Media Effects
description: Social, political, economic, and cultural effects of mediated communication are examined to understand their impact on human behavior.

subject: COM
title: Telecommunication in the Pacific Hemisphere
description: Development of international telecommunication, with special emphasis on the wireless communication, the internet, and emerging technologies.
prerequisites: COM majors only or consent. A-F only.

subject: COM
title: Communication and Gender
description: Theories and issues related to gender and communication applied to organizational, intercultural, and technology mediated communication.

subject: COM
title: Building Communication Theory
description: Major theories of communication in terms of requirements for a theory, theory development, associated research, and application.
prerequisites: COM major and junior standing, or consent

subject: COM
title: Special Topics in Communication
description: Topics of relevance to the focus areas of Communication in Communities, Media Arts, and ICTs & Policy; taught by regular and visiting faculty. Repeatable on different topics to six credit hours.

subject: CAM
title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare II
description: Continuation of 203. Intermediate level online course familiarizes students with basic language, cultures and customs through study of classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare, “Judge Rabbit,” one of the most famous figures in oral folktale stories. (Spring only)

subject: CAM
title: Advanced Khmer I
description: Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the web-based instruction. (Fall only)

subject: CAM
title: Advanced Khmer II
description: Continuation of 301. Provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and a textbook to complement the online instruction. (Spring only)

subject: CAM
title: Accelerated Third-Level Cambodian
description: Continuation of 212. Practice in idiomatic conversation and extensive reading. Integrated development of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Meets 10 hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Fourth-Level Khmer
description: Continuation of 302. Computer assisted learning. Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of social and cultural issues; advanced conversation and composition.

subject: CAM
title: Fourth-Level Khmer
description: Continuation of 401. Computer assisted learning.

subject: CAM
title: Khmer Language in the Media
description: Focus on advanced reading, writing, aural comprehension and speaking skills through the study of Khmer newspaper, radio, TV, audio/video clips and film. Repeatable one time.

subject: CMB
title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society. Not a BIOL major elective. (Cross-listed as BIOL 340)
prerequisites: one semester of biological science at college level or consent.

subject: CMB
title: Human Genetics
description: Principles of human genetics. Designed for pre-medical or pre-dental students or others who require a course with emphasis on human genetics.

subject: CMB
title: Genetical Problems
description: Directed reading and research in genetics. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CMB
title: Unit V Topics in Genetics
description: First-year elective course in which medical students may take an in-depth study of genetics. Repeatable six times.

subject: CMB
title: Bioethics
description: Prepare medical students to identify and resolve ethical dilemmas in medical career and biomedical research, and to maintain integrity and professionalism in accordance with relevant ethical principles, policies, and laws. Repeatable one time. MD majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: CMB
title: Research Topics in Cell Molecular Biology
description: Research elective for medical students. MD majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: CMB
title: Evolutionary Genetics
description: Genetic changes involved in the processes of adaptation and in species formation. Recommended: population and/or quantitative genetics.

subject: CMB
title: Introduction to Neurosciences
description: An interdisciplinary overview of the central nervous system, drawn from current knowledge and research on vertebrate and invertebrate neurobiology. Repeatable one time.

subject: CMB
title: Public Health Biology
description: Writing intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as PH 610)

subject: CMB
title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
description: Presentation and discussion of research topics in biomedical science. Repeatable nine times. CR/NC only. (Cross-listed as REPR 611)

subject: CMB
title: Cell Molecular Biology I
description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals. Recommended: CHEM 351.
prerequisites: BIOL 402 or MBBE 402; and BIOC 441, BIOL 408, and graduate standing; or consent.

subject: CMB
title: Cell Molecular Biology II
description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
prerequisites: 621, BIOC 441, and BIOL 408; and either BIOL 402 or MBBE 402; or consent.

subject: CMB
title: Advanced Topics in Genetics
description: Advanced treatment of frontiers in genetics.
prerequisites: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

subject: CMB
title: Ethics in Biomedical Research
description: Topics include responsible data management, recording, reporting, misconduct and scientific fraud, conflicts of interest, critical use of animals and human issues and subjects in research, genetic screening, stem cell and gene therapy and patenting. (Cross-listed as BIOM 641)

subject: CMB
title: Research Rotations
description: Individualized research project in three laboratories of CMB faculty with a written report on each project. Faculty laboratories will be selected by consultation with student’s graduate committee and individual faculty. Repeatable two times.

subject: CMB
title: Neuropharmacology
description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PHRM 640)
prerequisites: 606, or consent from the course director.

subject: CMB
title: Introductory Biostatistics for the Bench Biologist
description: Lecture and example-based introduction to the critical biostatistics skills commonly required of the bench life scientist. Technical literacy and basic practical application are the goals. Problem sets will be scored. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: CMB
title: Introductory Bioinformatics for the Bench Biologist
description: Modern biomolecular and genomic concepts are explored through brief guided hands-on web-based bioinformatic projects using public domain resources. Understanding key concepts and algorithms, technical literacy, and operational confidence are goals. Programming skill development is student-optional. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CMB
title: Population Genetics
description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations. (Cross-listed as BIOL 650)

subject: CMB
title: Literature Analysis and Scientific Writing
description: Aims to improve the skills of graduate students in Biomedical Sciences in literature search, analysis, and management, as well as in scientific writing and other forms of scientific communication. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CMB
title: (Alpha) Genetics Seminar
description: Research and topical literature reports in genetics. May be repeated. (B) molecular genetics; (C) molecular biology of cancer; (D) human genetics; (E) cytogenetics; (F) evolutionary genetics; (G) molecular biology of the cell; (H) drosophila genetics; (I) population/statistical genetics; (J) developmental genetics; (K) insect molecular biology; (M) genetics and molecular biology of fungi. Repeatable unlimited times for (G).
prerequisites: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

subject: CMB
title: Essentials in Grant Writing
description: (1 2-hr Lec) Presentation and discussion of hypothesis-driven research and grant writing. Topics include the process of proposal, submission, and review. Course work includes writing, critiquing, and revising a proposal. Graduate students only. Repeatable two times. CR/ NC only.

subject: CMB
title: Techniques in Genetics
description: Laboratory training in procedures used in diagnosis of genetic diseases, cytogenetics, immunogenetics, and dermatoglyphics. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

subject: CMB
title: Techniques in Genetics
description: Continuation of 671.

subject: CMB
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CMB
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CMB
title: Special Topics in Neurosciences
description: Advanced topics in neuroscience, from basic neurobiology to clinical neurology and psychiatry. Emphasis on current investigations at the cellular or molecular level. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CMB
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: COA
title: Introduction to Applied Gerontology: Helping Yourself and Others to Thrive in Later Life
description: Introduction to essential information on aging and the field of gerontology. Counters ageist stereotypes, develops skills for translating research into practice, and provides an introductory survey course for the undergraduate certificate in aging. A-F only. (Crosslisted as IS 206)

subject: COA
title: Ethics, Aging & Society
description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging. A-F only. (Cross-listed as IS 305)

subject: COA
title: Middle Age and Aging
description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social a

subject: ARCH
title: Capstone Studio (Alpha)
description: Advanced landscape architectural design inquiry and applied research investigation. Serves as a capstone experience, synthesizing theory, values, and practice. Limited to MLA students under Plan B. (D) design (6 credits); (R) research (3 credits). Repeatable one time per alpha, up to 18 credits. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture History
description: Investigation of architectural history and theory in the world from antiquity to present. Examining social, political, technological, material, and environmental forces. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Research Methods and Design Inquiry
description: Individual development of a Doctorate Project or MArch Capstone proposal that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Case Study and Analysis
description: Individual development of a case study project that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions. ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: MArch Capstone Studio (Alpha)
description: Advanced capstone architectural design research synthesizing theory and practice. (D) design; (R) research. MArch students only. A-F only. Co-requisite: (R) for (D); (D) for (R).

subject: ARCH
title: Doctorate Project I (Alpha)
description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji. Repeatable one time for (H). ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Doctorate Project II (Alpha)
description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji. Repeatable one time for (H). ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Doctorate Project II Extension
description: Extension of the development of a doctorate project with an approved committee that advances architectural knowledge through research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions. Repeatable one time. ARCH majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice. (Not for art majors or minors)

subject: ART
title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice. (Not for art majors or minors)

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Foundation explorations in the processes of relief, intaglio, and stencil printmaking. Direct workshop studio experience in the basic techniques and concepts of wood cut, linoleum cut, drypoint, monotype, and basic stencil processes.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Photography (Alpha)
description: Studio/lecture combining history, theory and practice of photography. (B) film and darkroom, students must have 35mm film-based camera with adjustable shutter speed, aperture, and light meter; (D) digital, students must have digital camera with manual control and image editing software.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Drawing
description: Descriptive, expressive, and formal aspects of visual language through drawing practice.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Three-Dimensional Composition
description: Basic concepts, elements, and principles of art.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Painting
description: Theory and practice of painting; material and technical procedures. A standalone course aimed at non-majors. ART majors should start with ART 223 after taking ART 113.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Glass
description: Basic techniques of working with cold and molten glass. Theory of glass studio operation and introduction to glass theory.

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art I
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles. (Fall only)
program: Art History and Theory Core Courses

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art I
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles. (Fall only)
program: Art History and Theory Core Courses

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art II
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles. (Spring only)
program: Art History and Theory Core Courses

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art II
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles. (Spring only)
program: Art History and Theory Core Courses

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Art
description: Integrated beginning studio art course, which offers students the opportunity to understand and express Hawaiian cultural perspectives through contemporary art practice. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Electronic Arts
description: Theory and practice course investigating language common to all arts activity particularly as related to the contemporary arts.
prerequisites: any studio art course; or consent

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Digital Imaging
description: Combined theory and practice examining major techniques, concepts, and aesthetics in contemporary digital image production. Direct studio experience in essential software, printing techniques and hardware necessary in producing the gallery quality inkjet print. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Photo (Black and White Darkroom)
description: Black and white photography emphasizing communication and self-expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and projects. Student must supply camera and material.

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Drawing
description: Extension of the observational foundation established in 113 to address contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches to drawing.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Life Drawing
description: Investigations of the figure concerning anatomical construction, light, space, diagramatic analysis, and thematic content.

subject: ART
title: Intaglio Printmaking
description: Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from metal plates including etching, engraving, aquatint, and drypoint. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Screenprinting
description: Studio practice in screenprinting on paper. Copy camera and basic photo-stencil techniques introduced. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Relief Printmaking
description: Studio practice in the techniques and concepts of woodblock, linoleum cut, monotype, and calligraph printmaking. Emphasis on both traditional and contemporary practices. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Approaches to Painting
description: Theory and practice of painting; contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches.

subject: ART
title: Painting/Water-Based Media
description: An introduction to water-based media. Traditional transparent color, gouache and acrylics.

subject: ART
title: Glass Casting: Sand and Metal Molds
description: Expressive explorations in glass casting with wet sand, bonded sand, and metal molds. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Cold Glass Fabrication
description: Expressive explorations using architectural sheet glass. Development of 2D and 3D forms using engraving, sandblasting, and cold joinery techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Ceramics
description: Three-dimensional concepts in clay; hand-building and wheel-throwing techniques. Projects, lectures, and demonstrations.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Metal Casting
description: Metal casting and development of as

subject: ANTH
description: DS The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required. A-F only. (Cross-listed as LING 415)

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: DS Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as LING 414 and IS 414)

subject: ANTH
title: Wealth, Culture, and Economic Anthropology
description: DS Analysis of economic activities in non-Western, non-industrial societies; production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a variety of cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: Political Anthropology
description: DS Character of political institutions and their development in nonWestern and non industrial societies.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Anthropology
description: DS Exploration of how anthropology studies indigenous groups throughout the world. An examination of the changing contexts of anthropological practice as calls for reflexivity lead anthropology of all backgrounds to bring insights from their “homes.” Issues include the question of objectivity, the emicetic distinction, and the ethics of different kinds of anthropological research and the role of anthropologists in indigenous self-determination. Repeatable one time.

subject: ANTH
title: Communication and Culture
description: DS Anthropological introduction to communication; intercultural and interspecies comparisons; verbal and nonverbal. Ethnography of communication, discourse and structural analyses, ethnomethodology.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
description: DH Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies. (Cross-listed as REL 422)

subject: ANTH
title: Social and Cultural Change
description: DH Various approaches to examples of social and cultural change in non-literate societies; evolution, diffusion, acculturation, revolution, etc. Historical features and social processes of colonialism.

subject: ANTH
title: Islands as Model Systems: Human Biogeography of the Pacific
description: DS Applying the concept of islands as “model systems;” explores the impacts of human populations on the natural ecosystems of oceanic islands, and the reciprocal effects of anthropogenic change on human cultures. A-F only.

subject: ANTH
title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
description: DS Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 426)

subject: ANTH
title: Food, Health, and Society
description: DS How human groups identify, collect, create, and transform foods; how they shape those into dietary behaviors, and the influence of those behaviors on health.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of the Body
description: DS Exploration of the history and development of theories of the body via topics such as phenomenology, perception, bodily rituals, gender, sex, race, colonialism, power, pain, medicalization, immunology, reproductive health and cyborgs.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Consumer Cultures
description: DS Examines the practices and meanings of consumption in the contemporary world. Topics include social class, branding, fandom, global-local nexus. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: ANTH
title: The Agriculture of Identity: Food and Farming in Anthropological Perspective
description: DS Exploration of agriculture from the perspective of anthropology, with a focus on alternatives to industrial agriculture, especially in the context of Hawai‘i. Readings include academic writing and also literary non-fiction and journalism. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Globalization and Identity in the Himalayas
description: DS Examines the influence of local culture and global flows on identity formation in the Himalayan region. Topics include: Hindu caste and gender, constructions of ethnicity, Tibetans and tourists, Sherpas and mountaineers, development ideologies, and consumerism. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Buddhism
description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as REL 443)

subject: ANTH
title: Spiritual Ecology
description: DS Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism. (Cross-listed as REL 444)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Sacred Places
description: DS Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as REL 445)

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Cultures
description: DS Cultures of Southeast Asia from hunting and gathering groups to high civilizations; kinship, economic, political, and religious systems; recent developments.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Cultures
description: DS Analysis of Polynesian cultures from their origins to contemporary states.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Melanesia
description: DS Close study of cultures of Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Fiji through anthropological ethnography. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology Through South Africa
description: DS Decolonizing approaches to anthropology explored through the archaeology and ethnography of South Africa. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence. (Alt years)

subject: ANTH
title: Forensic Anthropology
description: DB (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of physical anthropology to problems in human identification. Determination of age, sex, ancestry, etc., of the skeleton and preparation of reports for legal medicine.

subject: ANTH
title: Extinctions
description: DB An extraordinary number of plants and animals have gone extinct. Delves deeply into the primary literature that focuses on extinction and conservation from the beginning of the earth to the present day. (Alt. yrs: fall)

subject: ANTH
title: Asian Paleoanthropology
description: DB Neogene-Quaternary paleoenvironmental reconstructions; human evolution in East Asia during the Pleistocene; Out of Africa I; modern human origins. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
description: DH Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania. (Crosslisted as ASAN 461)

subject: ANTH
title: East Asian Archaeology
description: DH Prehistory and protohistory of China, Japan, and Korea from earliest human occupation to historic times. Geographical emphasis may vary between China and Japan/Korea.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Health and Development
description: DS Seminar explores the definitions and histories of development and global health initiatives in developing countries from an anthropological perspective. Reading materials include scholarly and popular texts that propose and critique solutions to global poverty. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: 152 or 301.

subject: ANTH
title: Hawaiian Archaeology
description: DH Archaeological perspective in Hawai‘i’s past; origins of Hawaiians; early settlement and culture change; settlement patterns and material culture; historic sites preservation.

subject: ANTH
title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
description: DS Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as WGSS 465)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: 152 or 301 or WGSS 151.

subject: ANTH
title: Quantitative Archaeology
description: Combined lecture/lab. Introduction to the basic principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. Exploratory data analysis approach. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: ANTH majors only. Junior standing or higher. Pre: 210.

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: DS Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies and practices of modern medicine. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, 152, or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Field Mapping
description: DS Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data. (Cross-listed as GEO 472)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Ceramic Analysis in Archaeology
description: DH Concep

subject: BE
title: Food Engineering
description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
prerequisites: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as FSHN 411 and MBBE 411)

subject: BE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prerequisites: (ECE 160, ECE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. (Cross-listed as ECE 422 and MBBE 422)

subject: BE
title: Environmental Biotechnology
description: Environmental impact and control; the microorganism and its nutrition and growth conditions; microbial growth and substrate removal kinetics; bioreactors; biological treatment systems; biodegredation of xenobiotic organic chemicals; case studies. A-F only.

subject: BE
title: Biosystems Unit Operations
description: Introduction to unit operations in biological, environmental, food, and manufacturing processes. Integration of biology and chemistry into engineering using basic concepts in mass and energy conservation and transport in reacting and non-reacting systems. A-F only.
prerequisites: (373; and either CEE 320 or ME 322) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Bioremediation: Principles and Practices
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Soil environment, fate and transport of contaminants; microbial ecology, metabolism, and energy production; biodegradation of selected compounds. In situ treatment, solid-phase bioremediation, slurry-phase bioremediation, and vapor-phase biological treatment. Open to nonmajors. Repeatable one time.

subject: BE
title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
description: Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures.
prerequisites: 373 or CEE 320 or ME 322; or consent. (Cross-listed as MBBE 460)

subject: BE
title: Bioprocess Design and Analysis
description: Combined lecture/computer lab on theory and practice of bioprocess design and analysis, involving biological basics and engineering principles of bioprocessing, computer-aided unit operations, process integration, and economic evaluation. A-F only.
prerequisites: 373, or 437 (or concurrent) or 460 (or concurrent); or consent. (Alt. years)

subject: BE
title: Senior Engineering Design I
description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) First course in a two-semester major open-ended design experience for senior students in biological engineering, with heavy emphasis on teaching written/oral engineering communication. Design process; project management; methodology; modeling; optimization; engineering economics. A-F only.
prerequisites: (350/350L, 373, CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent), ME 311, ECE 211) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Senior Engineering Design II
description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Continuation of 481 with emphasis on written/oral communication and engineering ethics. Properties of biological materials; risk and reliability; guest lectures on design by engineers; project completion with submission of a final design report. A-F only.
prerequisites: 481 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

subject: BE
title: Biological Engineering Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs. Repeatable nine times.

subject: BE
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. A-F only.

subject: BE
title: Directed Research
