description: Research in the area of biosystems engineering.

subject: BE
title: Instrumentation and Measurement
description: Measurement concepts and operating principles applied to the selection and use of instruments important to scientists and engineers dealing with biological systems, including automatic data acquisition and processing.
prerequisites: CHEM 151, MATH 241, and ME 311; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Biofuel and Bioenergy
description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production, biorefinery concept; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel; biodiesel production; algal-biofuel; environmental impacts, life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies; term paper and presentation. A-F only.

subject: BE
title: Experimental Methods in Cause-Effect Modeling
description: Factorial designs and fractional factorial designs for screening variable and response optimization. Response surface methodology. Experimental designs appropriate to building and testing multi-variable behavior relationships. Sequential experimental designs.

subject: BE
title: Biological Instrumentation
description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers.

subject: BE
title: Biological Treatment
description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil. A-F only.

subject: BE
title: Biosystems Modeling
description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system models, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
prerequisites: one of MATH 215, MATH 241, MATH 251A; or consent. (Crosslisted as AREC 610)

subject: BE
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling. Recommended: CEE 424 or consent. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as CEE 625 and NREM 660)

subject: BE
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: BE
title: Seminar
description: Use of computer and video technology in technical presentation, review of current biosystems engineering research.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology and Society
description: Characteristics of science, historical development of scientific concepts, and interaction of society with science illustrated by topics from biological science. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology & Society Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawai‘i. Not a BIOL major elective. (Cross-listed as SUST 111L)

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Option Program Seminar
description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective. (Cross-listed as IS 100)

subject: BIOL
title: Current Topics in Biomedical Research Seminar
description: Overview of contemporary laboratory- and population-based studies of disease. Discussion of career pathways in human health sciences. Public health and epidemiology of cancer. A-F only.

subject: BIOL
title: Hawaiian Environment Science
description: Characteristics of science and interaction with society illustrated by topics in geology, astronomy, oceanography, and biology of Hawaiian Islands. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology I
description: Introductory biology for all life science majors. Cell structure and chemistry; growth, reproduction, genetics, evolution, viruses, bacteria, and simple eukaryotes.
prerequisites: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 171L (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology I Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 171. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prerequisites: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 171 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II
description: Anatomy, physiology, and systematics of plants and animals; behavior; ecosystems, populations, and communities.
prerequisites: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172L (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 172.
prerequisites: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biostatistics
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R. A-F only.
prerequisites: 171 or 172 or BOT 101; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam. (Cross-listed as BOT 220)

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Principles of ecolog

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, Gender in Popular Culture
description: Contemporary issues of race, class, and gender in popular culture (film, television, music, social media, sports, etc.). Introduction to critical media analysis and social science theories and methods.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society. (Cross-listed as SOC 214)

subject: ES
title: Hawaiians
description: The sustainable social system, culture, spirituality, language, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians. Transformation of the sustainable Hawaiian social system by a capitalist economy. Resiliency, land issues, and Native Hawaiian quest for sovereign governance. (Cross-listed as SUST 222)

subject: ES
title: Filipinos in Diaspora
description: Introduction to Filipinos in diaspora. Topics include: race, empire, migration, representation, cultural production, identity formation, and decolonization.

subject: ES
title: Ethnic Identity
description: Individual and group problems of identity, identity conflict, culture conflict, inter-ethnic relations. Critical review of available material on Hawai‘i.

subject: ES
title: African American Experience I
description: Afrocentric perspective. Analysis of the black political/cultural diaspora, including ancient African kingdoms, the slavery experience, organized resistance, emancipation struggles, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

subject: ES
title: African American Experience II
description: Black sociopolitical perspectives of the Reconstruction period, Jim Crow, intellectual and cultural awakenings, civil rights movements, and contemporary issues as examined through students’ written analysis and creative projects.

subject: ES
title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity. (Cross-listed as SUST 318)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Ethnicity and Community: Hawai‘i
description: Site visits to museums, social welfare units, etc., as well as guest lecturers from the community including police, health, education. (Summer only)

subject: ES
title: Asian America
description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation. (Cross-listed as AMST 318)

subject: ES
title: Hawai‘i and the Pacific
description: Hawai‘i as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples. (Cross-listed as SUST 321)

subject: ES
title: Japanese in Hawai‘i
description: Issei roots in Japan; the role of Japanese in labor, politics, and business; sansei and perspectives on local identity and culture. The Japanese in light of changing economic, social, and political conditions in Hawai‘i today.

subject: ES
title: Power and Place: Chinatowns
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of Chinese in Hawai‘i and the U.S. continent with a focus on Chinatowns; urbanization; economic development, community organizing; comparative racialization.

subject: ES
title: Filipinos in Hawai‘i
description: Historical and contemporary experiences; immigration; traditional culture and values; plantation experience; labor organizing; development of Filipino community; racism; discrimination; and ethnic identity.

subject: ES
title: American Indian Experience
description: Provides a comprehensive look at the indigenous foundation of life and society in the Americas and elaborates on historical and contemporary importance of American Indian rights issues.

subject: ES
title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as WGSS 339)
prerequisites: one ES or WGSS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent

subject: ES
title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawai‘i
description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities. (Cross-listed as SUST 341)

subject: ES
title: The Sounds of Race and Inequality
description: Explore inequality as manifested and contested in silence, music, dialect, nature, voice, and acoustic space by listening through a matrix of race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexualities. Combination of hands-on work and current scholarship.

subject: ES
title: Economic Change and Hawai‘i’s People
description: Hawai‘i’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy. (Cross-listed as SUST 351)

subject: ES
title: Immigration to Hawai‘i and U.S.
description: Historical overview: “push and pull factors”; effect of changing economy; experiences of various ethnic groups; problems of recent immigrants; immigration policies in the U.S. and Hawai‘i.

subject: ES
title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawai‘i
description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawai‘i; feminist anthropological and historical analysis. (Cross-listed as WGSS 360)
prerequisites: one ANTH, SOC, or WGSS course

subject: ES
title: Literatures of Hawai‘i
description: Writings of various ethnic groups in Hawai‘i, ancient to contemporary. Songs, stories, poetry, fiction, essays that illustrate the social history of Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as ENG 370)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ES
title: Asian American Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Asian American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds. (Cross-listed as ENG 372)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ES
title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics. (Cross-listed as AMST 373)

subject: ES
title: Issues of Diversity in Higher Education
description: Examines issues of diversity within higher education. Examines different dimensions of diversity including ethnicity, gender, national origin, age, and sexual orientation. Will utilize national and local case studies. Junior class standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Fieldwork in Ethnic Studies
description: Supervision of individual student research projects pertinent to ethnic studies, including service learning, civic engagement, internship, oral history, or supervised practicum experience in teaching select ethnic studies courses. Repeatable to total of 6 credit hours.

subject: ES
title: Social Movements in Hawai‘i
description: Examines, through writing and collaboration, interethnic movement building among Native Hawaiian, other Pacific Islander, and Asian peoples of Hawai‘i through intersectional theories of social change to evaluate strategies to create just and sustainable futures.

subject: ES
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: Historical and sociological studies of race and gender in U.S. society; grassroots feminist and racial/justice activism on the continent and in Hawai‘i. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 390)

subject: ES
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as WGSS 371)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Change in the Pacific—Polynesia
description: Impact of cultural and physical change and their interrelationship.

subject: ES
title: Multiethnic Popular Culture: Hip Hop
description: Historical, social, cultural, and political aspects of the formation and development of Hip Hop culture in Hawai‘i and other Pacific islands. Special attention to the significance of Hip Hop in faci

subject: ARCH
title: Collaboration in Environmental Design
description: Investigation of the various disciplines in the environmental design field, including architecture, landscape architecture, interiors, historic preservation, urban design, and construction management. Emphasis given to collaborative methods to address critical issues. Open to non-majors. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio I
description: DA Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, represent, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and computer graphic techniques. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio II
description: DA Development of designs and processes to study precedents and explore solutions responding to human needs in built and natural environments. Analysis and representation of architectonic space and form using hand and computer techniques. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to Environmental Systems A
description: Introduction to building systems, including structural, environmental, life-safety, building envelope, building materials and building assemblies. Development of design skills with emphasis on elevating skills in assessing and selecting appropriate building systems. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: World Architecture and Urbanism A
description: DH Investigation of the history and theory of architecture in the world’s major cultural regions, from early agricultural settlements to 1500 C.E. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: World Architecture and Urbanism B
description: DH Investigation of the history and theory of architecture from the 15th century C.E. to the present. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to Environmental Systems B
description: Introduction to environmentalism; focusing on the impact of building systems of the global environment; the role of environmental regulations/certifications, and understanding of sustainable principles (economic, social, and natural systems). ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Intermediate Design Studio I
description: Building and site design with emphasis on site development, analysis, and climatic response. Introduction to sustainable design, land use ordinances, description and delineation of property and land features, and urban and community design influences. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Intermediate Design Studio II
description: Architectural design with emphasis on space planning, building materials, technology, climatic responses, and codes including complex functional requirements, multi-story design issues, vertical transportation, structure, and finishes. Production of complete schematic design documents. Detailed writing instruction. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Architecture History
description: DH Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes. ENVD and LAND majors only. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as TPSS 352)

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Graphics Studio
description: DA Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics. ARCH and ENVD majors only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as TPSS 353)

subject: ARCH
title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
description: DA Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale. Repeatable one time. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as TPSS 354)

subject: ARCH
title: Design Theory
description: Examination of theories, movements, and periods in architectural history focusing on contemporary issues. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of writing, and three oral communication assignments. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landform and Water
description: Essential topographic site design concepts and skills needed to reshape the land for human use, circulation, water management, and resilience. Topics will be reinforced through problem sets and analytical, computational, graphical, and technical exercises. ENVD and LAND majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Directed Work
description: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Concentration Design Studio
description: Professional experience combined with scholarly and research activity occurring in an off-campus location with a focus on architectural concentration areas. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Capstone Design Studio
description: Culminating design studio with focus on the development of a comprehensive design project integrating all major aspects of prior environmental design education. BEnvD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Construction Project Management
description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CEE 472)

subject: ARCH
title: Professional Practice Law and Ethics
description: Knowledge of professional standards and a broad understanding of the practice of architecture, including professionalism; ethical conduct; public, client, consultant, contractor, and government relations; project administration, contracts, procedures, and compensation; land use and construction law. ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Digital Design Synthesis
description: Investigation of processes for generating architectonic form using current digital technologies. Making advanced geometric models including investigation of morphological transformations. Study of design optimization, digital fabrication, information modeling, and generative algorithms. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Exchange
description: Seminar centered on academic and cultural exchanges, focused on advanced topics related to the design of built environments. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, and sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER). Repeatable three times, up to 24 credits. ARCH, ENVD, and AMST majors only. (Cross-listed as AMST 475)

subject: ARCH
title: History of American Architecture
description: DH History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning. ARCH and ENVD majors only. (Cross-listed as AMST 423)

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation: Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific
description: DH Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions. ARCH and ENVD majors only. (Cross-listed as AMST 474)

subject: ARCH
title: Urban Ecological Analysis and Design
description: Applied urban and landscape ecology principles and strategies for analysis, design, and management of urban regions and sites; emphasis on structure, functions, and processes that form urban landscapes at multiple scales and in diverse contexts. ENVD and LAND majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Plants in Design
description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples. ENVD and LAND majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in any aspect of architecture. Content to be announced. Repeatable four times. ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture History
description: Specialized work on the history and theory of architecture. Repeatable unlimited times. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction. Repeatable unlimited times. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics. Repeatable unlimited times. ARCH and ENVD majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Explore Furniture Design
description: Exploration of design and building princip

subject: ASL
title: Advanced American Sign Language II
description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL). Pre: 301. (Spring only)

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies
description: DH Introduction to different types of college-level writing through analyses of contemporary American culture and to the main themes and approaches used in American studies and the humanities.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies Writing
description: FW Introduction to different types of college level writing and information literacy with a focus on American culture and society. A-F only.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: FGB Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: FGB Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Institutions and Movements
description: DH Emergence and transformation of laws, ideologies, institutions, and social movements from the 17th-21st centuries. Emphasis on relationships among structures of power, representational practices, belief systems, and social action. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives. DH

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
description: DH Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives. DH

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Domestic Issues
description: DS Current debates in the U.S. over individual rights and nationalism; civil rights, citizenship, and sovereignty; sexuality, law, and religion; economic, racial, and gender equality; public health and environmental justice. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Global Issues
description: DS Interdisciplinary and transnational perspectives on global issues including international law and diplomacy; war, diaspora, and refugees; economic underdevelopment and environmental racism; globalization, race, and the feminization of poverty. Writing emphasis

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: DH Interdisciplinary survey that examines the histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of the indigenous peoples of the U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, and Samoans.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: DH Interdisciplinary survey that examines the histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of the indigenous peoples of the U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, and Samoans.

subject: AMST
title: Art and Social Change
description: DH Will analyze examples from the visual and performing arts, including murals, digital art, film, poetry, and music, paying particular attention to the connections and influence upon social and political movements, both historically and today. A-F only

subject: AMST
title: Hip-Hop and American Culture
description: DH Survey tracing hip-hop from its Afro-Carribean musical beginnings to contemporary adaptations and interpretations. Students will analyze various materials and will pay attention to the relationships between hip-hop and contemporary social forms.

subject: AMST
title: Justice and Asian America: Social Movements and the Law in American History
description: DH Examination of demands for and the changing nature of justice, historical and contemporary, through court cases, legislation, presidential orders, and social movements that address legal, social, and political definitions of Asian America.

subject: AMST
title: Japanese Americans: History, Culture, Lifestyles
description: DH Explores experiences of Japanese Americans in Hawai ʻi and the U.S.: historical and cultural heritage, biographical portraits, changing family ties, ethnic lifeways, gender relations, local identity, and the future of island living. Emphasis: oral communication skills. DH

subject: AMST
title: African Americans: Issues, Culture, History
description: DH Traces the history and culture of African Americans and outlines contemporary issues. Topics include: slavery and racism, community formation and resistance, cultural expression, African American diversity, civil rights, gender and class relations.

subject: AMST
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: DH History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women. (Cross-listed as HIST 361 and WGSS 311)

subject: AMST
title: American Music and Culture
description: DH Analysis of a variety of American musical genres and histories through focused writing assignments (record and performance reviews, personal narratives, interviews, research proposals, research papers). (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Pre: second year standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Asian America
description: DH History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation. (Cross-listed as ES 318)

subject: AMST
title: America, Hawai‘i and World War II
description: DH Examines WWII as a watershed in American and Hawai‘i history and culture. Topics include: Pearl Harbor, Japanese American internment, sex and racial tensions, Anti-Semitism and the Holocaust, and the dawn of the Atomic Age.

subject: AMST
title: American Environments: Survey
description: DS Survey of social, political, and cultural relations in diverse, contemporary American environments, including: island societies, urban centers, suburbs, Indian reservations, farming communities, and national parks. Special emphasis on contemporary environmental issues in Hawai‘i.

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Law in the U.S.
description: DH Surveys church-state jurisprudence since the 1940s, with special attention to difficulty of defining religion, and applies the religion clauses to current issues. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as POLS 325)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: AMST
title: American Folklore and Folklife
description: DH Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism. (Cross-listed as ANTH 326)

subject: AMST
title: Digital America: Online Communities and Virtual Worlds
description: DH Seminar on the impact of the digital revolution and virtual communities on American culture and society, with an emphasis on questions of identity and participatory democracy. Open to non majors.
prerequisites: Pre: one DH, DA, or DL course, sophomore standing, or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Religions in America
description: DH Examination of American religious traditions, both historical and contemporary, with an emphasis on the principles of religious liberty, non-establishment, and pluralism.

subject: AMST
title: War and Media
description: DH Examination of a range of media, including photography, film, print journalism, television, video games, and the internet, as they have shaped popular representations and experiences of war in America from the Civil War through the present. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
description: DH Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship with the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of Reconstruction. (Cross-listed as HIST 373)

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: DH Continuation of 343: 20th century. (Cross-listed as HIST 374)
prerequisites: Pre: 150 or 201 or 202 or 211 or 212 or HIST 151 or HIST 152; or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Conflict in American History
description: DH Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion. (Fall only) (Crosslisted as REL 345)

subject: AMST
title: American Design: An Historical Survey
description: DH Examination of design in American culture over the last century. Readings in industrial, graphic, interior, architectural, landscape, and user interface design used to study issues of gender, race, and class in the U.S. Open to all class standings. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Design
description: DH Investigates design in contempo

subject: DNCE
title: Field Experiences in Dance
description: DA Field experiences in relevant contexts under professional and faculty supervision. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: DNCE
title: Topics in Dance
description: Readings, research, and/or field and movement experiences. Repeatable if topic changes unlimited times.

subject: DNCE
title: Teaching Dance Technique
description: Principles, techniques, and materials used in the teaching of dance technique. A-F only.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Performance
description: DA Performance in various dance styles and settings. Repeatable eight times.

subject: DNCE
title: Improvisation II
description: Advanced-level dance improvisation. Repeatable two times.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Repertory
description: DA Preparation of standard and new works for performance. Repeatable three times.

subject: DNCE
title: Creative Dance
description: DA Dance activities for young people. Appropriate for teachers, group workers, recreation majors, and others working with children. Also adults with special needs. Supervised field activities.

subject: DNCE
title: Senior Project
description: DA Individual choreographic project; student choreographs, performs, and oversees all technical aspects of a creative project; tutorial. A-F only.

subject: DNCE
title: Directed Work
description: Individual projects, tutorial.

subject: DNCE
title: Performance Theory
description: Introduction to key texts and concepts of performance studies. (Cross-listed as THEA 615)

subject: DNCE
title: Seminar in Performance Studies
description: Special topics. Repeatable up to two times when topics change. (Cross-listed as THEA 617)

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Topics in Performance
description: Readings, discussion, research, and/or performance work. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits. THEA and DNCE majors only. (Cross-listed as THEA 626)

subject: DNCE
title: Seminar in Dance Research
description: Research materials and methods; preparation for thesis and scholarly research reporting. Required for graduate concentrations in dance. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Seminar: Dance Theory and Criticism
description: Major theories of dance and dance criticism; emphasis on Western ideas.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance and Performance Theory: Asia
description: Dance content and historico-social context of principal dance traditions. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Dance and Performance Theory: Oceania
description: Dance content and historico-social context of principal dance traditions. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Business for the Arts
description: Seminar offering overview and foundation for launching or advancing enterprises in the arts. A focus on the processes and method for creating economically successful grants and project development applications. (Cross-listed as THEA 658)

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Topics in Dance
description: Readings, research, and/or field movement experiences. Repeatable one time if topic changes.

subject: DNCE
title: Movement Analysis
description: Movement analysis in indigenous, critical race, critical dance frameworks for enhancing scholarly and artistic abilities.

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Topics in Performance in Hawai‘i
description: Analysis of Hawai‘i’s indigenous performance traditions, the contemporary multicultural landscape of theatre in Ko Hawai‘i Pae ‘āina, and the representation of Kanaka Maoli and settler voices on Hawai‘i’s stages. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as THEA 668)

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Choreography
description: Advanced analytic and creative study. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Performance
description: Graduate performance in various dance styles and settings. By audition only. Repeatable six times.

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Dance Technology and Live Performance
description: Advanced skills in dance and technology in live performance. Emphasis on New Media. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: DNCE
title: Interdisciplinary Collaborations
description: Hybrid performance works for dancers, musicians, actors, visual artists, poets, and writers to explore the nature of the collaboration process in various settings. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. THEA, DNCE, MUS, ART, ENG majors only. (Cross-listed as THEA 674)

subject: DNCE
title: Seminar in Choreographic Methods
description: Graduate level course designed for students with prior choreographic experience. Students will research, create, revise, and perform new works based on a variety of choreographic methodologies. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Directed Choreography
description: Concert choreography for selected performance settings under the direction of a faculty advisor. Repeatable six times.

subject: DNCE
title: Seminar in Teaching Dance/Theater
description: Pedagogy and classroom experience in teaching technique and theory. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as THEA 691)

subject: DNCE
title: Practicum in Teaching
description: Supervised teaching experience at the introductory or undergraduate level. Students will teach an appropriate level course in their field of expertise under faculty supervision. Repeatable up to nine credits. THEA or DNCE majors only. (Cross-listed as THEA 692)

subject: DNCE
title: Internship: Youth Theater/Dance
description: Supervised leadership experiences in dance/theater program with children. Students spend nine hours per week in supervised setting and three hours in weekly class meeting. (Cross-listed as THEA 693)

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Colloquium
description: Forum for presentation and discussion of current intellectual and artistic activities in the dance field. Repeatable three times.

subject: DNCE
title: (Alpha) Professional Internship
description: Internship program where students will work for or with a professional theatre company under supervision of a UH faculty member, plus possible supervisor(s) from the theatre company. Students must participate hands-on in production activities of that company and receive a satisfactory (or better) review from their supervisor(s); (B) entertainment design: costume, lighting, scenery, props, sound, or other related disciplines; (C) performance: acting, directing, dance, choreography, or other related disciplines. Repeatable eight times per alpha, up to nine credits per alpha. A-F only. (Cross-listed as THEA 696 (Alpha))
prerequisites: 345 or 353 or 356 for (B); 621 or 682 or DNCE 371 for (C).

subject: DNCE
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual projects: tutorial. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: DATA
title: (Alpha) Introduction to Computer Programming
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; ((P) Python. Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. ((P) Cross-listed as ICS 110P)

subject: DATA
title: Machine Learning Methods
description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ICS 235)

subject: DATA
title: Network Science Methodology
description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages. (Cross-listed as ICS 422)

subject: DATA
title: Data Science Fundamentals
description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ICS 434)

subject: DATA
title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory. Recommended: MATH 307. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ICS 435)

subject: DATA
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as CINE 484 and ICS 484)

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology
description: DB The study of the structure and functions of the head and neck with emphasis on structures in or related to the oral cavity; of tooth morphology. A-F only. Co-requisite: 231L.
prerequisites: PHYL 141, PHYL 141L, PHYL 142, PHYL 142L, and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161.

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology Lab
description: DY (2 3-hr Lab) Application of DH 231 didactic concepts to laboratory activities

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Actor on Screen
description: Introduction of the screen-director to the craft of acting for the camera. Students will develop communication skills and learn practical techniques to elicit spontaneous and relaxed performances with actors from the Theatre program. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Editing for Cinema
description: Advanced course examining the theory, techniques, and practices of motion picture editing; use of non-linear digital editing systems; and practical experience in digital editing projects. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Post Production Sound
description: Practical course on the theory, art, and techniques of sound recording, editing, and design for cinema. Students work on projects involving dialogue and sound effects in post-production. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Camera for the Screen
description: Detailed analysis of cinematic grammar, placement, movement, focus, and effects of the camera to create the mise-en-scene. Practical exercises to apply theory to individual creative work and in collaboration with actors from the Theatre program. ACM majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Genre and Narrative Theory in Creative Media
description: Focus on the concept of genre, genre films, genre film criticism, and popular genres such as the Western, film noir, documentary, and Chinese martial arts. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Documentary Studies
description: In-depth study of the nature, history, and impact of documentary filmmaking traditions around the world, focusing on the interplay between filmmaker, subject, and audience. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Authors in Cinematic Arts
description: In-depth study of the auteur theory and specific application to authors in cinematic arts, such as film directors, animators, screenwriters, or game designers. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Study Abroad
description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or digital media production in the host country in a UH Manoa-approved study abroad location. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Topics in Cinematic Arts
description: Topics of study and critical inquiry in a variety of areas in the cinematic arts. Taught by regular and visiting faculty. Repeatable one time on different topics. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Techniques in Cinematic Arts
description: Specialized techniques in the creation of digital media: taught by regular and *visiting faculty. Repeatable one time on different topics. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Workshop in Cinematic Arts
description: Intensive workshop in focused area of cinematic arts production. Repeatable up to six credits. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Independent Group Project
description: Participation in a group research or creative project under supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of 399/499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major. A-F only. Repeatable up to six credits. SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Documentary Production
description: Analysis and practical knowledge of the documentary process including, but not limited to, research, organization and story structure, shooting, camera coverage, and editing. SCA majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: 310, 350, and one of the following: 312, 330, 370, 372, or 374.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Cinematic Production
description: Production of a major cinematic/digital narrative project. Working in groups, each student takes on creative and technical role and responsibilities of a principle crew position. Emphasis on artistic form in narrative development; timely execution from pre- to post-production. Repeatable one time. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Cinematography
description: Applies the basic foundations, techniques, and theory of cinematography (covered in CINE 312) to a more informed and crafted practice with Camera and Lighting Scene study workshops, and research exercises and film projects. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Animation Production I
description: Students work independently to produce a short, animated film. Emphasis on visual storytelling and character animation. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course. (Cross-listed as ICS 486).

subject: CINE
title: Animation Production II
description: Student teams produce a short, animated film. Prior knowledge of 2D and 3D media authoring tools and animation techniques is necessary. Repeatable one time. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Screenwriting
description: Application of narrative principles of character development, story structure, and thematic spine to screenplays for live action and animated short films, television, or transmedia projects. ACM majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: (Alpha) History and Film
description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (E) world/ comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures. Repeatable one time for different alphas. (C Cross-listed as HIST 452C; E Cross-listed as HIST 452E)

subject: CINE
title: Indigenous Filmmaking
description: Theories and studies of indigenous films and creation of a cinematic project based in indigenous cultural and value systems. SCA majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: 310, 350, and one of the following; 312, 330, 370, 372, or 374.

subject: CINE
title: Ethics and Film
description: Ethical theory and dilemmas as reflected in film and filmmaking. Social responsibility for filmmakers. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Motion Picture
description: Students direct a narrative live-action short film from pre- through post-production, learning how to develop a directorial vision and how to implement it through storyboarding, scheduling, and collaborative skill sets. SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Screenwriting Capstone
description: Culmination of beginning and advanced screenwriting classes. Students will write a treatment and first act for a feature-length project or pilot script and series bible for a television project. Repeatable one time. SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Oceanic Media and Culture
description: Involves close textual analysis of film, TV and multimedia content. The course includes cinematic and television screenings. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as DATA 484 and ICS 484)

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in Cinematic Arts
description: Intellectual issues in cinematic arts. Conducted by regular and visiting faculty with extensive student participation and scholarly presentation. Repeatable one time on different topics. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Capstone Creative Production
description: Emphasis on advanced production skills in creating a capstone project in live-action fiction film, animation, documentary, or new media. Screenwriting students may also develop a feature screenplay or television pilot and series bible. Repeatable one time. SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Video Game Design and Development
description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as ICS 485)

subject: CINE
title: Global Media
description: Close textual analysis and strategic analysis of global media dynamics with an emphasis on transnational media corporations. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Arts Internship
description: Internship in professional cinematic, television, animation and/or digital media production company under professional and faculty supervision. Repeatable up to six credits. SCA majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: CINE
title: Directed Study
description: Independent research or creative project under the supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of 399/499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major. Repeatable up to six credits. SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Classical 2D Full Animation
description: Hand drawn full animation techniques; r. Cross-listed as ACM 318.

subject: BUS
title: Business, Government, and External Environment
description: Important issues related to the external environment of business. This includes international trade and finance, regulatory environment, social impacts of business. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Ethics
description: Assists students in developing an awareness of major ethical issues which affect business decisions, and encourages a socially responsible consideration of those issues and being able to express their views. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Managerial Finance
description: Financial management theories and tools for business professionals; asset management; capital budgeting; capital structure and dividend policies. MBA students only or advisor approval. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Managing Information Technology for Strategic Advantage
description: Theory, practices, techniques for managing information technology resources for innovation and for strategic advantage in global business environment. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
description: Theory, practices, techniques for managing operations and supply chains for global integration of firms and organizations. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Business Policy and Strategy
description: Integration of learning through analysis of comprehensive business problems, resolution of policy issues, and the study of competitive strategies in the international setting. MBA students only or advisor approval.
prerequisites: Pre: MBA core courses completed or taken concurrently; or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Business Study Abroad
description: Study abroad experience emphasizing international business issues. Content varies depending on course of study and educational institution selected. Course qualifies as an international business elective(s). Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: business core or permission of academic advisor.

subject: BUS
title: International Business Topics
description: Analysis of the business environment and business issues through study of businesses, governmental entities, and/or non-governmental organizations in specific geographic areas, in non-U.S. settings. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: BUS
title: International Business Field Experience
description: Analysis of the business environment and business issues through study and direct observation of businesses, governmental entities, and/or nongovernmental organizations in non-U.S. settings. Involves group travel to selected international business cities. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: BUS
title: Field Study in Asia
description: Industry observations conducted entirely in Asian countries for three and a half weeks. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Internships
description: On-the-job experience in the business community. Project paper and meetings with faculty advisor required. A-F only. Repeatable one time.

subject: BUS
title: MBA Consulting Practicum
description: Final MBA requirement for those candidates not writing a thesis. Candidates will form consulting teams to perform a meaningful, strategic study for a client organization. MBA students only or advisor approval.
prerequisites: Pre: 632 and at least 12 credits of MBA electives.

subject: BUS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Outline (including methodology or sources, results expected and means of measurement) must be prepared by student and approved by supervisor and chair of graduate programs before registration. Repeatable up to 12 credits.

subject: BUS
title: Thesis Research
description: Required for Plan A candidates only; six credit hours required, one of which must be taken during semester in which degree is awarded. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: BUS
title: Advanced Research Methods
description: Analysis of current theories in international business; design research studies in areas of possible dissertation research through application of scientific method; includes formation of research questions and testable hypothesis, identification of data sources, and analysis. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: two graduate level courses (six credits) in statistics and methodology, or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Research Seminar in Business
description: Covers research topics including research projects currently underway by Shidler College faculty, advanced PhD students, distinguished visiting faculty, and research contemplated by new PhD students. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: student status in PhD in business administration or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Seminar in International Business
description: Developing research and teaching skills in international business, preparation for teaching college-level courses in “international business,” give presentation on recent research in most selective business journals, integrating expectations of university teaching, research, and service. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: student status in PhD in business administration or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: Pre: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: BLAW
title: Legal Environment of Business
description: Introduction to the legal environment of business operations with particular attention to business law and ethics and to principles of law relating to contracts, agency, partnerships, and corporations.

subject: BLAW
title: Business Enterprise and Government
description: Critical study of the legal environment of business administration including competition, monopolies, mergers, securities, taxation, and regulatory agencies.

subject: BLAW
title: International Business Law
description: Overview of international and national law as it applies to international trade. Readings and case studies focus on the legal environment of selected areas in the Asia Pacific region and strategies for doing business overseas.

subject: BLAW
title: Social and Legal Aspects of Management
description: Study of the legal environment of management with particular attention to the sources, principles, and form of the law; contracts, business organizational structures, agency, and partnership.

subject: CAM
title: Introductory Khmer I
description: HSL. Face to face course aims to develop students’ proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the introductory level, with structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Introductory Khmer II
description: HSL. Continuation of 101. Face to face course continues to develop students’ proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the introductory level, with structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Conversing in Khmer I
description: HSL. Online course aims to develop students’ proficiency in speaking and listening to Khmer at the introductory level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

subject: CAM
title: Conversing in Khmer II
description: HSL. Continuation of 103. Online course continues to develop students’ proficiency in speaking and listening to Khmer at the introductory level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

subject: CAM
title: Reading/Writing in Khmer I
description: HSL. Online course aims to develop proficiency in reading and writing Khmer at the introductory level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Reading/Writing in Khmer II
description: HSL. Continuation of 105. Online course continues to develop proficiency in reading and writing Khmer at the introductory level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Intensive Elementary Khmer
description: HSL

subject: CAM
title: Intermediate Khmer I
description: HSL. Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse, and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the intermediate level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the online instruction. (Fall only) HSL

subject: CAM
title: Intermediate Khmer II
description: HSL. Continuation of 201. Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the intermediate level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the online instruction. (Spring only) HSL

subject: CAM
title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare I
description: HSL. Intermediate level online course familiarizes students with basic language, culture and customs through study of classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare, “Judge Rabbit,” one of the most famous figures in oral folktale stories.

subject: CAM
title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare II
description: HSL. Continuation of 203. Intermediate level online course familiarizes students with basic language, cultures and customs through study of classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare, “Judge Rabbit,” one of the most famous figures in oral folktale stories. (Spring only)

subject: CAM
title: Intensive Intermediate Khmer
description: HSL

subject: CAM
title: Advanced Khmer I
description: Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the web-based instruction. (Fall only)

subject: CAM
title: Advanced Khmer II
description: Continuation of 301. Provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the online instruction.

subject: ART
title: BFA Capstone Seminar/Studio
description: In conjunction with the production of art for the BFA annual exhibition, this seminar will examine, critique, and evaluate the student’s art within the context of contemporary art, professional practices, exhibition theory, and integrate theoretical and practical issues in the life of an artist. (Spring only)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis. (Cross-listed as SUST 436)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Installation/Performance–Material in Context
description: Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as SUST 439)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Early 20th Century American Art
description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher. (Alt. years: fall) (Crosslisted as AMST 460)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio III
description: Advanced graphic design. Emphasis on postmodernist theory, context, audience, and alternative media.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ART 365, ART 365L, and ART 366; or consent. Co-requisite: ART 465L.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio III Lab
description: Advanced instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including software and peripheral devices. Instruction in image manipulation and editing still video images for the web, CD, DVD, and portable interface devices.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ART 365, ART 365L, and ART 366; or consent. Co-requisite: ART 465.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography III
description: Advanced typographic design. Exploration of 2D, 3D, electronic, and intermedia. Emphasis on contemporary typographic models.
prerequisites: ART 365, ART 365L, and ART 366; or consent
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Production Techniques
description: Advanced techniques in design production from printed and digital media. (Spring only)
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ART 465, ART 465L, and ART 466; or consent. Co-requisite: ART 467L.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Production Techniques Lab
description: Advanced study of digital media for graphic designers. Focuses on skills and specific technical information to complement material covered in 467. (Spring only)
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ART 465 and ART 465L and ART 466. Co-requisite: ART 467.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Design: Advanced Studio
description: Individual and team investigations of complex problems in graphic design. Emphasis on projects with actual clients (when available) and/or independent investigations addressing advanced and current questions in the graphic design field. (Spring only)
prerequisites: with a minimum grade of B- for (ART 465 and ART 466) and credit for ART 465L
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Renaissance Art (Alpha)
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture: (B) early Renaissance in Italy; (C) northern Europe; (D) High Renaissance and mannerism in Italy. Repeatable one time for different alphas.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Baroque and Rococo Art
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of Europe in the Baroque and Rococo periods.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of the United States
description: Emphasis on the 18th and 19th centuries. (Cross-listed as AMST 456)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of the First Half of 20th Century
description: Development of modern art in Europe 1900–1939.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art Since 1945 (Alpha)
description: Art since 1945, with a focus on the global expansion of the avantgarde; (B) contemporary art 1945-2000; (C) global contemporary art since 2000.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of the Pacific (Alpha)
description: Visual form and function of the arts in cultural context: (B) Melanesia and Australia; (C) Polynesia and Micronesia; (D) North Pacific coast Indian, Eskimo. Repeatable one time for different alphas.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Tribal Africa
description: Visual form and function of arts in cultural context. Mali, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Guinea, Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, Congo, Zaire.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Indonesia
description: Architecture, sculpture, and textile traditions of indigenous Indonesia in cultural context.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Topics in Contemporary Art
description: Thematic approaches to contemporary art and visual culture. Course themes may include identity, local/global issues, and appropriation. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Hawai‘i
description: Stylistic and aesthetic characteristics of art of ancient Hawai‘i; relationship to art from other parts of Polynesia.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Museum Interpretations
description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used by museums to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Considers how interpretations contribute to cultural knowledge. Repeatable one time. (Crosslisted as AMST 457)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Applied Art of Japan
description: Ceramics, metalwork, lacquer, and textiles throughout Japanese history.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning. (Cross-listed as SUST 484)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Contemporary Art in Hawai‘i
description: History of contemporary art in Hawai‘i: the institutions, artists, critics, and historians that have shaped it. Strong focus on oral history of Hawai‘i artists.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Traditional Chinese Painting
description: Stylistic and historic development of two-dimensional arts; painting and calligraphy from prehistory through 18th century.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Modern and Contemporary Art of China
description: Introduction to the arts of China in the modern and contemporary periods, in all media and genres, from 1840 to the present.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Genres of Japanese Cinema
description: History of Japanese cinema, including silent films, samurai films, monster films, and literary adaptations, analyzed through the lens of genre theory. Students demonstrate mastery of assigned readings and lecture content via weekly writing assignments. (Summer only)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History (Alpha)
description: Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. (B) Angkor & art of Khmer civilization; (C) art & architecture of Thailand; (D) monuments & nationalism in Southeast Asia. Repeatable one time for up to two different alphas. (Once a year) (D Cross-listed as ANTH 491)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Hindu Visual Culture
description: Art and architecture of South Asia in historical and cultural context. Hindu visual culture.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Art of Islam
description: Major developments in art and architecture.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Photography: Critical Issues
description: Seminar on theoretical, ethical and aesthetic issues relating to the practice of photography, past and present.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: History of Modern Design
description: Major design movements in Europe and America from late 19th century to present; arts and crafts movement, art nouveau, modernist trends of the 20th century.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Topics in the History of Cinema
description: Specific period or national style of cinema studied in its historical context. Repeatable two times.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Graduate Studio Seminar in Art
description: Selected topics in art. A critique-based course with emphasis on the development of critical analysis, artistic research, and practice. Repeatable six times.
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Methods in Contemporary Art
description: Examines processes of inquiry and experimentation within studio practice. Students explore a range of research methods as a way to challenge habitual methodologies and expand notions of art and art making. (Fall only)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Materials in Contemporary Art
description: Explores the physical, historical, symbolic, and contextual capacity of materials, as well as the mutually constitutive roles of artist and materials within the creative process. (Spring only)
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ART
title: Graduate Studio Teaching Practicum
description: Observation, analysis and participation in teaching a lower division course under
department: Department of Art and Art History

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ERTH 150 and OCN 150)
prerequisites: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X).
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to MET Undergraduate Directed Research
description: Students gain familiarity with ATMO research. Students can select 1-3 credits per semester for maximum 6 credits over 4 semesters. Students must pre-arrange research and reading content with instructor. Repeatable three times, up to six credits. Freshman and sophomore standing only. CR/NC only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Processes and Phenomena
description: Atmospheric variables, gas laws, radiation processes, thermodynamics, conservation laws, dynamic approximations, clouds and precipitation, convection, atmospheric circulations, mid-latitude and tropical weather systems, forecasting, climate.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Physics
description: Energy and thermodynamics, statics and stability, physical processes of cloud formation, radiation and Earthatmosphere heat balance, kinetic theory, optical effects.
prerequisites: ATMO 200, MATH 242, and PHYS 272; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Atmospheric Dynamics
description: Scalar and vector development of basic laws of hydrodynamics, equations of motion, kinematics, divergence and vorticity, viscosity and turbulence, introduction to numerical weather prediction, general circulation.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawai‘i. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only. A-F only. (Alt years: Spring) (Cross-listed as GES 304 and SUST 304)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Meteorological Instruments and Observations
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Each week targets a different meteorological instrument and culminates in a lab exercise and report. The focus is on accurate measurement and scientific-style writing. A-F only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Global Environmental Change
description: Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc. (Cross-listed as OCN 310)
prerequisites: ATMO 200, OCN 201, ERTH 101, ERTH 103, or ERTH 170; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Programming for Meteorologists
description: Scientific programming in Fortran 77, graphics software and meteorological applications. A-F or Audit.
prerequisites: ATMO 302 (or concurrent) and MATH 241; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only. (Fall only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Directed Reading
description: Individual reading in Atmospheric Sciences. Repeatable one time, up to three credits. ATMO students only. Junior and senior standing only. A-F only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Applied Atmospheric Dynamics
description: Advanced concepts in dynamics: vorticity, cyclogenesis, jet streams, fronts, mesoscale circulations.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Synoptic Satellite Meteorology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Satellite applications to synoptic meteorology and forecasting, including orbital elements, ephemerides, viewing geometry, radiation, satellite sensors, and interpreting satellite data.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Meteorology
description: History; tropical clouds and hydrometeors; typhoons; monsoons; local and diurnal effects.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Meteorological Analysis Lab
description: (2 4-hr Lab) Techniques and methods of forecasting extratropical systems with analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems. Students will be instructed on how to communicate and discuss a weather forecast and how to present a research paper. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Analysis Lab
description: (2 Lec 2 3-hr Lab) Techniques of portraying and analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems in tropical and equatorial regions; forecasting tropical systems.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis, and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers.
