Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CEE 449 and SUST 449)
prerequisites: Senior standing or higher, or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Capstone for senior Meteorology majors. Undergraduate thesis project includes literature review, experiment or research design, data collection and analysis, technical writing of a final thesis paper and oral presentation of the paper. Junior and senior standing only. A-F only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Dynamics I
description: Governing equations for moist atmospheric motions, approximations, basic theoretical models, boundary layer dynamics, atmospheric waves, quasi-geostrophic theory for mid-latitudes.
prerequisites: ATMO 402, and either MATH 402 or MATH 405; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Dynamics II
description: Overview of dynamic meteorology, numerical weather prediction, geophysical fluid instabilities, approximate dynamical systems, atmospheric general circulation, stratospheric dynamics. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Cumulus Dynamics
description: Dynamics of convective systems: tornadoes, waterspouts, squall lines. Interactions with synoptic scale. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Mesoscale Meteorology
description: Scale analysis. Observational and theoretical aspects of mesoscale circulation systems. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Climate and Weather
description: Climate and general circulation of the tropics; El Niño and Southern Oscillation; intraseasonal oscillation; trade winds; tropical weather systems; energy balance; typhoons.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Satellite Data Applications
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Principles and practices of satellite remote sensing as used in the atmospheric sciences, specifically clouds, aerosols, precipitation, ocean and land cover datasets from various satellites. Develop skills including data manipulation, analysis, and visualization using Matlab. A-F only. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Cyclones
description: Lecture covering fundamentals of tropical cyclone structure, motion, and impacts on society. Observations from satellites, aircraft, ships and buoys, and numerical simulations focusing on storm structure and track. Some forecasting exercises. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Monsoon Meteorology
description: Synoptic components of monsoons, regional and temporal variability, numerical models, research exercises. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Physical Meteorology
description: Molecular kinetics, atmospheric thermodynamics, cloud physics, precipitation processes, atmospheric electricity, scattering and absorption of solar radiation, absorption and emission of infrared radiation, radiative transfer.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Radar Meteorology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Radar hardware, electromagnetic propagation and scattering, radar equation, signal processing, precipitation estimation and polarimetric applications, Multi-Doppler wind synthesis, mobile and spaceborne radars, forecasting, and data assimilation applications. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: ATMO 620 (with a minimum grade of B- or higher) or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Statistical Meteorology
description: Probability; frequency distributions of atmospheric variables; linear models; time series analysis (frequency and time domain); principal component analysis; statistical weather forecasting and verification. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Advanced Statistical Methods in the Geosciences
description: Methods for numerous multivariate analyses will include singular spectrum, extended empirical orthogonal function, singular-value decomposition, canonical correlation, discriminant and cluster analysis. Other advanced topics include wavelet analysis, statistical downscaling and Bayesian analysis. A-F only and audit. (Every 3rd year)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Paleoclimate Model-Proxy Synthesis
description: Basics of Earth System Model development, parameterizations, intermodel variability and design of paleoclimate simulations. Types of proxies, tools and techniques for paleoclimate record development and reconstructions. Hypothesis testing and methods for proxy-model comparison studies. ATMO, GEO, EPET, NREM, OCN, and ORE majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 665)
prerequisites: MATH 402 and 403 (or their equivalents) and either ATMO 600 or OCN 620; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ATMO
title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the stateof-the-art theories and observatio
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Dialects

department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Syntax and Semantics
description: Verbal categories, aspects, focus devices, resultative and directional compounds, coverbial constructions. Interaction between syntax and semantics.

subject: CHN

subject: CHN

description: For graduate students pursuing teaching Chinese language. Students gain practical skills and hands-on experiences in creating instructional and assessment materials and teaching an actual Chinese language class using the self-developed materials effectively. (Alt. years: fall)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN

department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

prerequisites: CHN 452, CHN 455, or CHN 456; or consent.
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Second Semester Classical Chinese
description: Builds on the foundation laid in 461; introduces complex syntactic patterns, advanced vocabulary; teaches sophisticated reading strategies and cultural literary contexts; exposes students to a wide range of intermediate level texts. Repeatable two times. (Spring only)
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN

description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

prerequisites: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Literature (Alpha)
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional. Repeatable one time for (M). A-F only for (M). (Cross-listed as WGSS 753 (Alpha))
prerequisites: EALL 611, WGSS 613, WGSS 615, or WGSS 650; or consent for (M); 612, or consent for (T).
department: Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures

subject: CINE

description: Introduction to the basic techniques of cinematic digital production and allows them to explore their personal voice in this process. A-F only.

subject: CINE

description: A basic overview of the 3D animation production process, including modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, lighting, and rendering. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to 2D Animation
description: Introduction to traditional styles and methods of hand drawn 2D, digital, and stop motion animation through theory and practice. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Cinema and Digital Media

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Narrative Production
description: Production-intensive course with collaborative as well as individual projects. Theories and application of basic digital cinema productions, including camera, lighting, sound, and editing. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematography
description: Comprehensive course in visual styles supporting screen narratives through a study of principles of camera elements, operations, lighting, color and composition. Professional role and responsibilities of cinematographer. Project-oriented. SCA majors only. A-F only.

description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation. SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only. (Cross-listed as ART 315 and THEA 314)
prerequisites: CINE 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or CINE/DNCE/THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE/DNCE/THEA 356 (or concurrent).

subject: CINE
title: 3D Modeling
description: Essential principles of 3D modeling in order to create both organic character models and hard surface models. Students will create high-quality, animation-ready 3D models with textures and poses. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: 3D Animation
description: Creating the illusion of life through the principles of animation. Repeatable one time for different alphas. SCA majors only. A-F only.

title: 3D Lighting, Camera, and Rendering

subject: CINE

description: Visual design and development for animated characters and environments. Students will create concept art, character, and prop designs; movements styles; backgrounds; and layouts for animation pre-production. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Movement Study for Animation
description: Creating the illusion of life and expressive movement through the principles of 2D animation: timing, spacing, physics, staging, anatomy, attitude, and acting. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Motion Graphics
description: A project-based introduction to motion graphics using Adobe After Effects. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Independent Producing
description: Fundamentals of producing for independent filmmaking, focusing on business acumen and role of the producer through various stages of production. Topics include proposal writing, script breakdowns, budgeting, scheduling, legal issues, festival strategy, and distribution. SCA majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: CINE 255; and CINE 310 or (CINE 215 and CINE 216).

subject: CINE
title: Screenwriting
description: Introduction to the basics of writing a short narrative screenplay for film or animation. Students learn the fundamentals and format of screenwriting as well as basic elements of storytelling and character development. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Screening Asian Americans
description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship. SCA majors: A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 352)

subject: CINE
title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
description: Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process. (Consent required for production experience option) (Cross-listed as DNCE 353 and THEA 353)
prerequisites: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent.

subject: CINE
title: Oral Tradition to Screenplay
description: Adapting the stories, styles, and cultural values of oral tradition storytelling to cinematic narratives. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as DNCE 356 and THEA 356)

subject: CINE
title: Indigenous Aesthetics
description: Aesthetic theories and practices of indigenous cultures of the Pacific and their adaptation to the screen in cinematic storytelling. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Actor on Screen
description: Introduction of the screen-director to the craft of acting for the camera. Students will develop communication skills and learn practical techniques to elicit spontaneous and relaxed performances with actors from the Theatre program. SCA majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: CINE 310 or (CINE 215 and CINE 216); and CINE 350 (or concurrent).

subject: CINE
title: Editing for Cinema
description: Advanced course examining the theory, techniques, and practices of motion picture editing; use of non-linear digital editing systems; and practical experience in digital editing projects. SCA majors only. A-F only.

subject: CINE
title: Post Production Sound
description: Practical course on the theory, art, and techniques of sound recording, editing, and design for cinema. Students work on project

subject: ARCH
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. ARCH and LAND majors only, or consent. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 695)

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Landscape Architecture
description: Seminar on a wide range of landscape architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty. Repeatable three times. ARCH and LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH

subject: ARCH

subject: ARCH

description: Study of the history and theory of culture and the built environment with particular focus on the Asia-Pacific region. ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH

description: Detailed investigation of major theories in architecture and urban design and examination of their impact on contemporary architectural practice in varied geo-political contexts. Open to non-majors. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems I: Introduction to Systems
description: Study of building materials, assemblies, and integrated design including structural, environmental, life-safety, and building envelope systems. Development of ability to design, analyze and assess appropriate systems. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems II: Qualitative Bioclimatic and Structural Performance
description: Introduction to the theory of bioclimatic principles and structural systems and the ability to analyze, assess, select, design, and integrate them as initial determinants into the building design. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems III: Quantitative Structural Analysis and Design
description: Introduction to procedures and wood, steel, concrete, and masonry material properties used for structural analysis and design of individual structural elements and building structural systems. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems IV: Environmental Technology, Sustainability, and Analysis
description: Application and analysis of highperformance building design principles. Emphasis on climate-appropriate passive design, energy-efficient lighting and conditioning strategies, innovative water systems, and renewable energy production. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems V: Building Systems Integration
description: Properties, evolution, and range of building materials, assemblies, and systems and their applications in integrated high-performance building design with a focus on the role of detail and systems in the design process. ARCH majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: ARCH 724, ARCH 725, and ARCH 733. Co-requisite: ARCH 744.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communication I
description: (Lec, Lab) Exploration of digital technologies, their relationship to design, and their application to architectural analysis, conceptualization, design processes, communication, representation, and construction. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communication II
description: (Lec, Lab) An interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to digital technology and its applications to current developments in practice and research within architecture and design. ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Forms and Frames of Practice
description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice within the global context with emphasis on the Asia Pacific region. Exploration of information technology systems, materials and design process research, construction technology, computer aided manufacturing, and entrepreneurial approaches. ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communications III
description: Interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to architectural presentation techniques, particularly oral and written, to current developments in architectural practice. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Research Methods Seminar
description: Comprehensive assessment of objectives and function of research in architecture and landscape architecture. Lecture, seminar, independent work with emphasis on research project topic and proposal development. ARCH and LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio I: Intro to Design
description: Design theories and systematic analytic and synthetic methodologies applied to creation of building and site spaces responsive to environmental and human needs. Several individual projects. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio III
description: Design of complex, large scale building and site engaging social, cultural, code, sustainable systems, and acoustic issues. Production of schematic and design development documents. ARCH majors only. Graduate standing only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio IV: Urban Design
description: Urban design focused on Asian cities investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response. ARCH and LAND majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio V: Comprehensive Design
description: Design and programming for a moderately complex building and site. Production of design development and partial construction documents describing sustainable building assemblies and construction cost. ARCH majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: ARCH 724, ARCH 725, ARCH 733, and ARCH 743. Co-requisite: ARCH 726.

subject: ARCH

description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

(Alpha) (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawai‘i; (P) practicum; (T) China. Repeatable one time per alpha. ARCH majors only. Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T). A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: ARCH 744, and ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (B), (G), and (T); ARCH 744 and ARCH 745 for (H); ARCH 726, ARCH 744, ARCH 745, ARCH 750G, and ARCH 781 for (C), (E), and (P).

subject: ARCH
title: Research Studio in Professional Setting
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off campus location. (Alpha) (C) China; (G) global. ARCH majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH

subject: ARCH

description: Varied topics furthering knowledge and ability needed for professional design practice emphasizing communication methods for collaborative and integrated design using digital technologies. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH

description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law. A-F only.

subject: ARCH

description: Exploration of the interaction of landscape and community necessities in urban ecological design. Studio problems, design research projects, lectures, and discussion applied to the integration of ecological and social factors in urban contexts. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Project Design Studio: Comprehensive
description: Design and programming for a complex, medium-scale, multi-layered urban landscape architecture project. Iterative, advanced design inquiry and materials exploration. Production of in-depth, comprehensive design development and partial construction documents. LAND majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: ARCH
title: Capstone Studio
description: Advanced landscape architectural design inquiry and applied research investigation. Serves as a capstone experience, synthesizing theory, values, and practice. subject: ARCH
title: Architecture History
description: Investigation of architectural history and theory in the world from antiquity to present. Examining social, political, technological, material, and environmental forces. ARCH majors only. A-F only.

title: Advanced Research Methods and Design Inquiry

title: Introduction to Costume Construction
description: Workshop on basic principles of costume construction for theatre and dance. Professional practices, materials, and methods. (Cross-listed as THEA 354)

subject: DNCE
title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as CINE 356 and THEA 356)

subject: DNCE
title: Queer Dance Exploratory
description: Queer dance exploration in movement practices and performance. Repeatable two times. Open to all majors. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 357)

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Kinesiology
description: Practical information for dance students on diet and nutrition, anatomy, training and conditioning, and injury prevention.

subject: DNCE
title: Visual Media for Dance
description: Introductory theory of dance for camera. Includes emphasis on practical applications in digital media, choreography, performance, documentation, and feedback in oral communication. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Movement Improvisation
description: Introduces movement improvisation to all levels and disciplines. Movement studies will explore improvisation approaches, devices, elements, exercises, and implications to gain skills in and appreciation for the art of improvisation. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as THEA 370)

subject: DNCE
title: Choreography I
description: Elementary techniques and theories for dance-making; includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

subject: DNCE
title: Choreography II
description: Intermediate techniques and theories for dance-making; includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

subject: DNCE
title: (Alpha) Advanced Practicum
description: Advanced workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography. Repeatable up to four credits per alpha. (Cross-listed as THEA 400)
prerequisites: audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production for (B); 200C for (C); 200D for (D); 200E for (E); 200B or 200C or 200F, and consent for (F)

subject: DNCE
title: Asian Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable up to eight credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Chinese Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Japanese Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Balinese Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable up to eight credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Korean Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Okinawan Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Philippine Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Oceanic Dance II
description: Performance and techniques at intermediate level. Repeatable up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Hula/Chant Ensemble II
description: Ancient style. (Cross-listed as MUS 412)

subject: DNCE
title: Hula/Chant Ensemble III
description: Ancient style; hālau protocol. Repeatable nine times. (Cross-listed as MUS 413)

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Ballet Technique
description: Advanced ballet technique. Repeatable six times.

subject: DNCE
title: Hawaiian Performance Workshop
description: Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Hawaiian performance forms and Hawaiian medium theatre. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as THEA 424)
prerequisites: one of: 312, 411, 412, HAW 202, HAW 321, HAW 384, HAW 486, THEA 101, THEA 221, THEA 224, THEA 468; or consent

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Contemporary Dance Technique
description: Advanced contemporary dance technique. Repeatable six times.

subject: DNCE
title: Movement Workshop
description: Special workshops in movements relating to specific departmental theatrical productions beyond the scope of movement taught in 437 and 438. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as THEA 433)
prerequisites: one of 435 or THEA 435, or consent

subject: DNCE
title: Taiji (T’ai Chi) for Actors II
description: Intermediate-level Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) movement training. Repeatable two times. (Cross-listed as THEA 434)

subject: DNCE
title: Movement for Actors
description: Training actors to discover experientially the sources of movement; to teach skills for analyzing movement for its mechanical, anatomical, spatial, and dynamic content; and then to apply these skills in a role. (Cross-listed as THEA 435)

subject: DNCE
title: Advanced Movement for Actors
description: Detailed development of material presented in 435. Focus on Bartenieff fundamentals and movement analysis as it applies to the physical interpretation of theatrical roles. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as THEA 436)

subject: DNCE
title: Musical Theater Dance Forms
description: Theatrical dance forms used in 20th-century musical theater. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as THEA 439)
prerequisites: 100 level or above dance technique class, 421, or consent

subject: DNCE
title: Topics in Costume Construction
description: Costume production techniques, both Western and Asian, for theatre and dance. Topic rotation includes: understructures and armatures, patterning, tailoring, dyeing, fabric modification, millenery and crafts, within the context of current industry practice. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as THEA 446)

subject: DNCE
title: Indigenous Dance Studies
description: Lecture/ discussion about choreographies of indigeneity and identity with an intersectional emphasis on Native Hawaiian, Pacific, and Asian dance cultures. Repeatable two times.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Histories I
description: Development of selected dance histories prior to 1900.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Histories II
description: Development of selected dance forms from 1900 to present, emphasis on writing and ethics.

subject: DNCE
title: Costumes II: Intermediate Costume Design
description: Advanced costume design for theatre and dance. Introduction to collaborative process in costume. Intensive work on rendering skills, applied to various design problems. Cost analysis and organizational techniques. (Cross-listed as THEA 456)

subject: DNCE
title: Field Experiences in Dance
description: Field experiences in relevant contexts under professional and faculty supervision. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: DNCE
title: Topics in Dance
description: Readings, research, and/or field and movement experiences. Repeatable if topic changes unlimited times.

subject: DNCE
title: Teaching Dance Technique
description: Principles, techniques, and materials used in the teaching of dance technique. A-F only.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Performance
description: Performance in various dance styles and settings. Repeatable eight times.

subject: DNCE
title: Improvisation II
description: Advanced-level dance improvisation. Repeatable two times.

subject: DNCE
title: Dance Repertory
description: Preparation

subject: EDEA
title: Introduction to Educational Policy Studies
description: Examines theories and models of educational policy and policy-making and the contribution of policy analysis to the policy-making and change processes. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEF 675)

subject: EDEA
title: The Politics of Education
description: Examination of the ways in which education can be viewed as political, arising from its connection to the larger political system including local, state, and federal governments. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEF 676)

subject: EDEA
title: Curriculum Administration
description: Master’s level course in curriculum administration and leadership, focusing on fundamental theories underlying curriculum development, as well as the implementation of curriculum policy at the school level.

subject: EDEA
title: Capstone Project in Educational Administration
description: Required for higher education Plan B option. 3 credits required for program completion. Taken in final semester or second to last semester in program. A-F only.
prerequisites: 602 and 657, and consent of instructor and chair.

subject: EDEA
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and department chair.

subject: EDEA
title: Thesis Research
description: Research master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDEA
title: Advanced Qualitative Research
description: Study in trends, research, and problems.

subject: EDEA
title: Internship in Education
description: Supervised intern experience in school and university administration. Emphasizes the development of leadership skills through program and project management. A-F only.
prerequisites: approval of cooperating agencies and department.

subject: EDEA
title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
description: Analysis of psychology of adult learner; forces that affect learning in dynamics of individual, group, and organizational behavior; concept of lifelong learning vis-a-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities. (Cross-listed as EDEP 745 and NURS 745)

subject: EDEA
title: Seminar on the Educational System
description: Examination of structure and dynamics of the educational system. Particular focus on how educational policy interacts with principles that explain educational system behavior. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDEF 767)

subject: EDEA
title: Seminar on the Principalship
description: Series of planned seminar experiences on problems and issues confronting school principals, such as contract administration, program planning and budgeting systems (PPBS), teacher evaluation. Topic to be announced. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDEA
title: Seminar (Alpha)
description: Study in trends, research, and problems. (B) policy formulation; (C) organizational change; (D) evaluation and research management (meets PhD common required advanced methodology course); (G) school governance; (H) college student affairs administration; (I) higher education administration; (J) administrative theories; (K) administrative problems and issues; (M) engaging diverse student populations; (N) exploring Indigeneity in higher education. (K) is repeatable two times in different topics. EDEA majors only for (I) and (K). A-F only for (M).

subject: EDEF
title: Education in American Society
description: Interrelated historical, philosophical, and sociocultural contexts of education with an emphasis on identifying, analyzing, and deliberating on contemporary ethical issues, problems, and applications. Students enrolled in colleges other than the College of Education are asked to confer with the College of Education director of student services before enrolling in 310. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: The History of Education in Hawai‘i From Pre-contact to Statehood
description: History of educational though and practices from pre-contact Hawaii through statehood. Social, intellectual, political, and cultural influences on indigenous, territorial, and state educational institutions; emphasis on white-settler colonialism, multiculturalism, assimilation, resistance, indigenous, and immigrant experiences. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Spring only.)

subject: EDEF
title: The History of Education in Hawai‘i From Pre-contact to Statehood
description: History of educational though and practices from pre-contact Hawaii through statehood. Social, intellectual, political, and cultural influences on indigenous, territorial, and state educational institutions; emphasis on white-settler colonialism, multiculturalism, assimilation, resistance, indigenous, and immigrant experiences. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Multicultural Education
description: Concepts and methods to develop sensitivity and awareness of cultural influences on behavior as these relate to the schooling process. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual reading or research.
prerequisites: senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in education, and consent of instructor and department chair.

subject: EDEF
title: Community and Culture
description: Theoretical and practical approaches to understanding the constitution of community life. A focus on the social construction of normative values, social dynamics of organizations, and school-community relations. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Sociology of Education
description: Introduction to sociological frameworks of analysis of the institutional, cultural and social dynamics of schooling, classroom management, school reform, social group and individual role behavior. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper. (Cross-listed as EDCS 453 and WGSS 453)

subject: EDEF
title: Ethnic Groups and Education in Hawai‘i
description: Identity and learning within and among Hawai‘i ethnic groups; study of prejudice and inter-ethnic hostilities as these impact education and teaching. College of Education majors only. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Anthropological Applications
description: Education as cultural and cross-cultural learning; universal aspects of the process. Ethnographic study. Applied anthropological theory and practice for educators. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Foundations of Educational Theory
description: An in-depth review of social, philosophical, and historical views underlying various theories of education and their applications in teaching and learning. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Cultural Diversity and Education
description: Examines issues, theories, perspectives and practices in multicultural education and promotes awareness, encourages knowledgeable reflection and develops skills necessary for multicultural practitioners. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDCS 630)

subject: EDEF
title: Field Studies in Educational Foundations
description: Field-based participant research projects, including analysis of educational problems and issues. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Education in the Classical Tradition
description: Classical European, Chinese, Indic, and Islamic traditions in the history of education; emphasis on ways in which they shift, interact, and collide from the early modern period to the present.

subject: EDEF
title: History of Education in America
description: History of educational thought and practice from European colonialism to revolutionary nationalism to the present. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: History of Education in Hawai‘i
description: From pre-contact, ancient Hawai‘i to the present. Social and intellectual influences on the development of national, local, and indigenous educational institutions; emphasis on multicultural as well as monocultural directions in Hawai‘i’s schools. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Higher Education
description: Salient historic, social, and organizational aspects of higher education; history, philosophy, purposes, governance, administration, structures, financing, faculty and student selection, curricula, legal and social issues.

subject: EDEF
title: Philosophy of Education
description: Readings of the original texts of major philosophers impacting American education. Considerations about the conditions of knowing and their extension in everyday practices in education. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar in Educational Foundations-Selected Topics (Alpha)
description: Multi-disciplinary (historical, philosophical, social/cultural and comparative/international focus on topical issues in education. (B) general; (C) leadership and governance in education; (D) educational reform; (E) foundations of teaching; (F) foundations of curriculum; (G) globalization in education; (H) moral political education. Repeatable one time for (H). A-F only for (H).

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Comparative/ International Education
description: Introduction to basic methods of comparative studies, focusing on schooling, but also treating broader educational issues. A-F only.

subject: EDEF
title: Topics in Comparative Education
description: Educational institutions, structures, processes, policies, and problems viewed within the context of political, social, and cultural milieus. Geographic region or theme focus. Repeatable

subject: ECE
title: Sophomore Project
description: Sophomore level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. Repeatable unlimited times. CENG, ECE, and PREN majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ENGR 296)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Signal and Systems Analysis
description: Discrete-time and continuous time signals and systems, linear systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transform, sampling.
prerequisites: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I
description: DP. Semiconductor structures, operating principles and characteristics of diodes and amplifying devices. Their application as circuit elements in building basic digital, analog, and integrated circuit subsystems.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments on linear and logic properties of diodes and transistor networks.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Physical Electronics
description: DP. Review of quantum mechanics fundamentals, H-atom, and chemical bonding. Introduction to band structure models and materials. Semiconductor doping, charge carrier statistics and charge transport, including ambipolar transport. Metal-semiconductor and PN junctions.
prerequisites: MATH 243 or MATH 253A, and PHYS 274; or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits II
description: DP. Principles and design of linear electronic circuits including differential, operational, feedback, and tuned amplifiers; integrated circuits, current mirrors, signal generators, filters, and stability.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits II Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 326, experiments on linear and analog electronics. Includes an emphasis on writing laboratory reports.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Theory and Design of IC Devices
description: DP. Band structure models and carrier transport physics review. Theory and design of semiconductor IC devices: Schottky diodes, bipolar devices (PN junction diodes, BJTs), FETs (MOSFETs, JFETs, and MESFETs).
prerequisites: ECE 324 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A; or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microcircuit Fabrication
description: DP. Technology principles, materials, and methods for the design and fabrication of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, and microelectromechanical systems.
prerequisites: Pre: ECE 327 or consent. Co-requisite: ECE 328L.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microcircuit Fabrication Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on laboratory where students make various electronic and electromechanical micro-devices using IC technology. Devices are also tested and analyzed.
prerequisites: Pre: ECE 324 or consent. Co-requisite: ECE 328.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Probability and Statistics
description: Probability, statistics, random variables, distributions, densities, expectations, limit theorems, and applications to electrical engineering.
prerequisites: ECE 315 (or concurrent) and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Communication Systems
description: Signal representation, Fourier analysis; amplitude and angle modulated systems; sampling theorems, pulse and digital modulation systems; carrier modulation by digital signals.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Communication Systems Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of communication systems. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Networking I
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Covers 4 semesters from the Cisco Networking Academy plus supplementary material; hands-on experience with routers and switches; prepares students for the CCNA. Topics include TCP/IP, LANs, WANs, routing protocols, network security; PPP; ISDN, frame relay. A-F only.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Linear Algebra and Machine Learning
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Mathematical and algorithmic fundamentals of linear algebra and their applications and illustrations to machine learning. Lab introduces programming with data and uses machine learning libraries for an introduction to commonly used technologies. MATH, ECE, CENG, CECE, ME, ICS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems
description: Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Provides experience in applying theoretical tools to analyze linear systems. Extensive use is made of computer-aided analysis and design packages study system performance.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Digital Systems and Computer Design
description: Design methodology, processor design, control design, memory organization, system organization.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Digital Systems and Computer Design Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 361, experiments on digital systems and interfacing. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Discrete Math for Engineers
description: Logic, sets, number theory, properties of functions, properties of relations, methods of proofs, recursion, counting, probability, trees, graphs, analysis of algorithms, finite state autonoma.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: CMOS VLSI Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the design of very large scale integrated (VLSI) systems and use of CAD tools and design languages. Lab includes hands-on use of CAD tools and experiments with field programmable logic devices.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of data structures and algorithms, including correctness and performance. Topics include time complexity, hash tables, sorting, search trees, self-balancing trees, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 367. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Cyber-Physical Systems and the Internet of Things
description: Topics include General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO), serial communications, sensors, actuators, low-power wireless communications. TCP/IP networking, dynamic service discovery, distributed network messaging, machine-to-machine communication and cloud-computing interaction. A-F only. Engineering majors only.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns. ECE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ICS 369)
prerequisites: ECE 160 or ICS 111 or instructor approval.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
description: Transient and steady-state waves on transmission lines. Plane wave solutions of Maxwell’s equations. Application of Maxwell’s equations under static and time-varying conditions.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
description: Solution of Maxwell’s equations under various boundary conditions. Introduction to radiation, guided waves, and principles of optics.
prerequisites: ECE 371 and PHYS 274 (or concurrent); or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of electromagnetics and optics.
prerequisites: Pre: ECE 371 and PHYS 274 (or concurrent), or consent. Co-requisite: ECE 372.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Junior Project
description: Junior level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. It may be a continuation of ECE 296 or a new project. Repeatable unlimited times. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ENGR 396)
prerequisites: Pre: ECE 296 or consent. Junior standing or higher.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Computer and Network Security
description: Review basic network mechanisms, introduce basic cryptography concepts, and study algorithms and protocols used in computer and network security. Discuss practical security mechanisms. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: ECE 361 or ICS 312 or ICS 331 or instructor consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Digital Signal Processing
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Discrete-time signals and systems, sampling, Z-transform, transform, transform analysis of linear time-invariant systems, filter design, discrete Fourier transform, and computation of discrete Fourier transform.
prerequisites: ECE 315 and ECE 342 (or concurrent), or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
description: Digital image representation, intensity transformations, spatial filtering, filtering in the frequency domain, image restoration, color spaces and transformations, the fast wavelet transform, image compression.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Optimization
description: Application of linear, nonlinear and integer optimization models and algorithms to communications, control, signal processing, computer networking, financial engineering, manufacturing, production and distribution systems. CE, ECE, ME, or CBA majors only. (Alt. years)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: DY. Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum Design in Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to help classroom teachers understand sources and principles of curriculum in early childhood education and to provide experience in evaluating, selecting, and developing appropriate curriculum for young children.

subject: EDCS
title: Museums and Education
description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects. (Cross-listed as AMST 685)

subject: EDCS
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure. A-F only. (Cross-listed as LTEC 686 and LIS 686)

subject: EDCS
title: School and District Literacy Leadership
description: Exploration and application of school and district-wide roles of the literacy specialist, such as collaborating with other educators to: (1) design and implement literacy programs, and (2) provide research-supported professional development. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A-F only.

subject: EDCS
title: Graduate Certificate Capstone
description: Independent study and/or seminar for students working on a capstone for a graduate certificate. Repeatable three times. CR/NC only.

subject: EDCS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EDCS
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable up to 36 credits.

subject: EDCS
title: Qualitative Data Analysis
description: Advanced seminar in qualitative research methods with an emphasis upon qualitative data analysis, theory construction, data presentation and reporting.
prerequisites: 632, a course in introduction to qualitative research methods; or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Research on Teaching and Teacher Education
description: Examination of alternative approaches and multidisciplinary perspectives on research on teaching and learning in and out of school, on educational change, and on teacher education and professional development.

subject: EDCS
title: Dissertation Research and Writing
description: Intended for doctoral students at any point of their doctoral program to develop their dissertation prospectus, proposals, comprehensive examinations, and/or initial dissertation drafts. Repeatable unlimited times. (Once a year)

subject: EDCS
title: Issues and Trends in Curriculum
description: Uses problem-centered approach and field experiences. Topics include historical review of curriculum development since 1900, examination of current curriculum practices at all levels of education, and prediction of future directions in curriculum theory and design.

subject: EDCS
title: Seminar in Curriculum and Instructional Theories
description: Analysis and critical examination of models and curriculum theory and theories of instruction leading to generation of theories by seminar members.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum and Program Evaluation
description: Critical examination of theoretical and methodological positions on curriculum and educational program evaluation.

subject: EDCS
title: Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. Repeatable one time. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as DIS 780 and LTEC 780)

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Stage, Screen, and New Media Writing
description: Introduction to college level writing and information literacy for and about the stage (theatre, dance, performance), the screen (film, television), and new media (digital platforms, social media). A-F only. (Cross-listed as THEA 100)

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Japanese Dance
description: Beginning techniques of Japanese dance. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Balinese Dance
description: Beginning techniques of Balinese dance. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Korean Dance
description: Beginning techniques of Korean dance. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Okinawan Dance
description: Beginning techniques of Okinawan dance. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Philippine Dance
description: Beginning techniques of Philippine dance. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Oceanic Dance
description: Beginning techniques of Oceanic dance. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits

subject: DNCE
title: Beginning Ballet Technique
description: Introduction to classical ballet technique. Repeatable three times.

subject: DNCE
title: Beginning Contemporary Dance Technique
description: Introduction to contemporary dance technique. Repeatable three times.

subject: DNCE
title: Hip Hop Dance
description: Introductory lecture/lab geared towards those with or without Hip Hop dance experience. Students will learn the fundamentals of various Hip Hop dance styles. Repeatable two times.

subject: DNCE
title: Jazz Dance Technique
description: Introduction to jazz dance technique. Repeatable two times.

subject: DNCE
title: Ballroom Dance
description: Introduction to those with or without ballroom dance experience. Students will learn the fundamentals of various ballroom dances. Repeatable five times.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Dance
description: Survey the development of major dance styles and their relationship to contemporary choreography, emphasis on teaching writing.

subject: DNCE
title: Music Theory for Dancers
description: Elements of music and relationship to dance; emphasis on rhythmic analysis. (Alt. years)

subject: DNCE
title: Live on Stage
description: Students view locally produced theatre and dance productions and write performance reviews. Readings, writing, and class discussion will guide students to understand each performance. Performances include theatre, dance, musical theatre, opera, and performance art. Repeatable one time. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as THEA 152)

subject: DNCE
title: (Alpha) Beginning Practicum
description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography. Repeatable up to four credits in each alpha. (Cross-listed as THEA 200)
prerequisites: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

subject: DNCE
title: Low Intermediate Ballet Technique
description: Low intermediate ballet technique. Repeatable three times.

subject: DNCE
title: Intermediate Contemporary Dance Technique
description: Low intermediate modern dance technique. Repeatable three times.

subject: DNCE
title: Introduction to Stage Production
description: Survey class introducing theater management, lighting, costuming, scenery, and other aspects of theatre that relate to producing stage performances. (Cross-listed as THEA 240)

subject: DNCE
title: Intermediate Hip Hop
description: Hip Hop studio practice, technique, and performance at the intermediate level. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Principles of of Design
description: Introduction to general design principles as applied to theatre. Will introduce the language and tools of visual literacy and visual communications via individual projects and collaboration. Repeatable two times. (Cross-listed as THEA 245)

subject: DNCE
title: Global Perspectives on Dance
description: Overview of global perspectives on dance, with emphasis on Asia and the Pacific, and related concepts. Includes practical dance performance workshop. Develops written communication skills.

subject: DNCE
title: Topics in Dance
description: Readings, research, and/or field and movement experiences. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Movement Fundamentals
description: Organized somatic systems as a framework for understanding movement and dance techniques. Required for majors. Repeatable two times.

subject: DNCE
title: Asian Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level. Repeatable up to eight credits.

subject: DNCE
title: Chinese Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Japanese Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Balinese Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Korean Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Okinawan Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Philippine Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Oceanic Dance I
description: Performance and techniques at the introductory level.

subject: DNCE
title: Hula/Chant Ensemble I
description: Ancient style. A-F only. (Cross-listed as MUS 312)

subject: DNCE
title: Intermediate Ballet Technique
description: Intermediate ballet technique. Repeatable four times.

subject: DNCE
title: High Intermediate Contemporary Dance Technique
description: Intermediate modern dance technique

subject: ART
title: Approaches to Painting
description: DA Theory and practice of painting; contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches.

subject: ART
title: Painting/Water-Based Media
description: DA An introduction to water-based media. Traditional transparent color, gouache and acrylics.

subject: ART
title: Glass Casting: Sand and Metal Molds
description: DA Expressive explorations in glass casting with wet sand, bonded sand, and metal molds. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Cold Glass Fabrication
description: DA Expressive explorations using architectural sheet glass. Development of 2D and 3D forms using engraving, sandblasting, and cold joinery techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Ceramics
description: DA Three-dimensional concepts in clay; hand-building and wheel-throwing techniques. Projects, lectures, and demonstrations.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Metal Casting
description: DA Metal casting and development of associated practices and concepts. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Carving, Mixed Media
description: DA Investigations of traditional and contemporary carving concepts and methods. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio I
description: DA Introduction to graphic design. Explorations of rhetorical and semiotic structures and their relationship to visual form and content. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio I Lab
description: Beginning instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including hardware, software, and lab networking as it relates to graphic design production. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite. CR/NC only.

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography I
description: DA Introduction to typography. Exploration of letterform and word compositions in the context of single-page structures. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Electronic Arts Studio
description: DA (6 Lec/ Lab) Combined theory and practice studio course(s) that investigate language, processes, and personalized composing systems related to the use of technological media and its application to a variety of contemporary art areas and related disciplines. (B) imaging systems; (C) sound; (D) interactive systems.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Contemporary Critical Theory
description: DH Examination of the significant themes and issues in contemporary critical theory as they relate to the production and reception of art.
program: Art History and Theory Core Courses

subject: ART
title: Kiln-Formed Glass
description: DA Expressive explorations in the use of kiln-formed, fusible-sheet glasses and enameling on glass. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Digital Imaging: Professional Printing
description: DA Combined theory and practice. Investigates industry standard methods for archival pigment printing. Techniques include: device calibration and profiling, black and white, coating techniques, mounting and adhesive techniques, professional portfolio presentation. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Digital Imaging: Alternative Printing
description: DA Combined theory and practice. Merges digital printing, mark-making, photography, and traditional printmaking. Includes image transfers, lifts, precoating techniques, as well as printing on alternative substrates such as watercolor papers, metals, and cloth. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Lost Wax Glass Casting
description: DA Glass kiln casting techniques, lost wax fuse casting, pâte de verre. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Lighting
description: DA Emphasis on aesthetic and critical analysis. Techniques covered include continuous light, strobe and handheld flash. Repeatable one time with consent.
prerequisites: 107D and 202 with a minimum grade of B

subject: ART
title: Advanced Photographic Techniques
description: DA Emphasis on aesthetic and critical analysis. (B) digital color photography and printing; (C) hand-applied emulsion. Each alpha is repeatable one time with consent.
prerequisites: 107D and 202 with a minimum grade of B for (B); 202 and 207 with a minimum grade of B for (C)

subject: ART
title: Sound Design and Video Art
description: DA Combined theory and practice studio art course examining the techniques, concepts, and aesthetics of congtemporary sound design and video art. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ART
title: Advanced Drawing
description: DA Studio practice in drawing emphasizing contemporary developments in art. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Life Drawing
description: DA Further investigations of the figure concerning anatomical and diagramatic construction, light, space, and thematic content. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Experimental Art and Animation
description: DA Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation. SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only. (Cross-listed as CINE 314 and THEA 314)
prerequisites: 113 or CINE 216 (or concurrent) or CINE/DNCE/THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE/DNCE/THEA 356 (or concurrent)

subject: ART
title: Lithography
description: DA Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from lithographic limestone and plates.
prerequisites: (with a minimum grade of B) 215 or 217 or 218

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Printmaking
description: DA Intermediate level specialization in either intaglio, lithography, screenprinting, or relief printmaking. Concentration on the techniques and formats of color printing and sequential image development. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: (with a minimum grade of B) two of 215, 217, 218, or 316

subject: ART
title: Advanced Color
description: DA Theory and application of color as related to studio practice.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Painting I
description: DA Studio practice in painting emphasizing contemporary developments in art. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Painting from Life
description: DA Painting from the model; a survey of the figurative tradition. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Glass
description: DA Glass as an expressive medium. Individual problems; construction of studio equipment. Readings and discussions of contemporary glass issues. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Papermaking
description: DA Studio emphasis on handmade papermaking techniques, conceptual exploration in two and three dimensions. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Fiber Sculpture—Endurance and Impermanence
description: DA Studio exploration in contemporary dimensional fiber using both conventional and nonconventional materials and processes. Emphasis on concept development, sensitivity to the evocative potential of materials, context, surface treatment and its relationship to concept and structure. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ART
title: Inter-woven Structures
description: DA Studio investigation of threads under tension. Thematic lens of environmental vulnerability and resiliency. Explores art practice as embodied knowledge. Specific attention to weaving as meaning and place-making. Engages writing as a significant tool for analysis. A-F only. (Cross-listing as SUST 338)

subject: ART
title: Ceramics—Sculpture
description: DA Sculptural concepts and techniques specifically related to the medium of clay; advanced hand-building, throwing, glazing, and firing techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Ceramics—Vessels
description: DA Exploration of the ceramic vessel as function, metaphor, and expression. Advanced hand-building, throwing, glazing, and firing techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Ceramics—Low Temperature
description: DA Form and surface problems related to earthenware clay bodies and low-temperature glazes; mold-making for ceramics. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: History of Western Ceramics
description: DH Western ceramics history from chronological, developmental, contextual, and theoretical standpoints; influence of Asian ceramics.

subject: ART
title: Technical Ceramics
description: DA Clay body development, glaze development, empirical and calculation methods. Emphasis on glaze maturity, surface, and color. A-F only.
prerequisites: 242, and one of 343, 344, or 345; or consent

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Figure Modeling
description: DA Figure modeling, mold making, and casting. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Kinetic Sculpture
description: DA The design and construction of objects incorporating movement as an integral element of their content. Repeatable one time.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Metal Fabrication
description: DA Metal fabrication and development of associated practices, concepts, and historical references. Repeatable one time.

subject: ES
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: Historical and sociological studies of race and gender in U.S. society; grassroots feminist and racial/justice activism on the continent and in Hawai‘i. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 390)

subject: ES
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as WGSS 371)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Change in the Pacific—Polynesia
description: Impact of cultural and physical change and their interrelationship.

subject: ES
title: Multiethnic Popular Culture: Hip Hop
description: Historical, social, cultural, and political aspects of the formation and development of Hip Hop culture in Hawai‘i and other Pacific islands. Special attention to the significance of Hip Hop in facilitating cultural interactions. Junior standing or higher.
prerequisites: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable up to 6 credits.

subject: ES
title: Ethnic Studies in the Digital World
description: The digitally networked world mediates race and ethnicity– and vice-versa. We will challenge racism and discrimination manifested in social media, changing notions of identity and group belonging, ewaste, gaming, big data, and more.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, and the Law
description: Historical context and implications of landmark court decisions and legal issues affecting social change in ethnic communities in Hawai‘i and the continental U.S.
prerequisites: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Women and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global. (Cross-listed as SOC 418 and WGSS 418)
prerequisites: one 300-level ES or WGSS course, or SOC 300; or consent.

subject: ES
title: American Ethnic and Race Relations
description: Surveys ethnic and race relations in the U.S. Focus on historical conflicts and critical issues such as racism, immigration, affirmative action, changing economic structures, and the role of government.

subject: ES
title: Mixed Race Identities, Multiracial Experiences
description: Critically examines historical and contemporary issues surrounding mixed race identities and experiences through themes that resonate in localized contexts within the continental U.S. and Oceania.
prerequisites: one DH or DS course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Filming Social Change
description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects. A-F only. (Cross-listed as COM 425)
prerequisites: one DH or DS course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Contemporary Diasporas in Comparative Perspective
description: Compares the circumstances under which contemporary Asian, Pacific Islander, or African migrants form diasporas across the globe; focus on a particular ethnic group to examine its site-specific experiences. A-F only.

subject: ES
title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered. (Cross-listed as AMST 401)

subject: ES
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 448 and WGSS 450)
prerequisites: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.

subject: ES
title: Raciolinguistics
description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere. (Cross-listed as LING 418)

subject: ES
title: (Alpha) Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context. ((C) Cross-listed as SUST 455)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

subject: ES
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
description: The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as SOC 456)
prerequisites: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 456)
prerequisites: one of WGSS 151, WGSS 175, WGSS 176, or WGSS 202; or consent.

subject: ES
title: Global Ethnic Conflict
description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher. (Crosslisted as SUST 461)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Latinx Experience in Hawai‘i
description: Examines historical, socio-cultural, and contemporary Latinx presence; relations among Latinx, other immigrant, and Indigenous communities; causes and patterns of immigration; racism and discrimination; ethnicity and identity issues; struggles for justice.
prerequisites: one DH or DS course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Practices and Methods in Oceanic Ethnic Studies
description: Engagement with theoretical elements and qualitative and quantitative research methods of Oceanic Ethnic Studies: theories of class, race, indignity, migrancy, diaspora and political economy; community-based and participatory research methods. A-F only.
prerequisites: one upper division ES or SOCS course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Peoples of Hawai‘i
description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawai‘i using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ANTH 486)

subject: ES
title: Politics of Multiculturalism
description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 492)
prerequisites: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project. (Cross-listed as ANTH 493)

subject: ES
title: Hawai‘i’s Labor History
description: Conditions of work under varying political, social, and economic transformations in Hawai‘i; anthropological, sociological, and historic data.
prerequisites: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Special Topics in Ethnic Studies
description: Selected themes in ethnic studies exploring current issues and new topics; taught by regular and visiting faculty. Repeatable two times.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment I: Social and Cultural Contexts for Learning
description: Knowledge and skills related to the context of teaching. Teacher candidates will examine the impact of culture, family, school, classroom, and individual characteristics on learning, and orally present, in varied formats, acquired knowledge and competencies. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment II: Classroom and Behavior Management
description: Teacher candidates explore the ethical implications for establishing, maintaining, and restoring the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment III: Behavior Project Implementation
description: Teacher candidates demonstrate the ability to establish, maintain, and (when necessary) restore the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning. Candidates demonstrate ability to identify maladaptive student behaviors and implement effective, research-based interventions. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment I: Foundations of Assessment
description: Introduction to foundational aspects of assessment and emphasizes the importance of linking assessment with planning and instruction. Candidates develop knowledge, skills, and dispositions important for designing, implementing, and analyzing effective assessments for diverse learners. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment II: Formal Assessment
description: Understand techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities.
