Inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment is stressed. Significant instruction on writing individualized education programs. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Introduction to Inclusive Teaching
description: Teacher candidates engage in reflective, procedural, and research writing to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Science
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to the teaching and learning of science in elementary settings, K-6. Candidates learn to

subject: BUS
title: Written Communication in Business
description: An interactive writing class stressing persuasive writing in the context of memos, letters, and business reports. A-F only. Students may not earn credit for both BUS 209 and ENG 209.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 200 or ACC 210, and ENG 100.

subject: BUS
title: Applied Math in Business
description: FQ Provides problem-solving and quantitative skills essential in business. Reviews algebra, mathematics of finance, calculus in business applications, probability, introductory statistics, and hypothesis testing.
prerequisites: Pre: two years high school algebra.

subject: BUS
title: Statistical Analysis for Business Decisions
description: Problem recognition and formulation; stress on cross-disciplinary complex problem solving and communication; computer intensive. Coverage of descriptive statistics, probability and hypothesis testing with emphasis on quality, productivity, and regression analysis. Must be taken in first semester of BBA program.

subject: BUS
title: Information Systems for Global Business Environment
description: Skills and strategies for using information resources applied to local and global business issues; advanced skills in computer-based analytical techniques and information management; impact of information technology on business operations and business strategies. Must be taken in first semester of BBA program.
prerequisites: Pre: ICS 101, or LTEC 112 and 113, or equivalent, or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Principles of Marketing
description: Concepts, problems, and opportunities in marketing within its competitive, political-legal, economic, social and global environments. Social responsibility and ethics. Marketing research. Consumer and businessto-business segmentation and positioning. Strategic marketing planning. Students may not earn credit for BUS 312 and TIM 304.

subject: BUS
title: Economic and Financial Environment of Global Business
description: DS International trade, financial flows, and direct investment. Public and private institutions including government policies and capital markets. Emphasis on Asia Pacific issues, with attention to the cultural differences among countries.
prerequisites: Pre: ECON 130 and ECON 131 or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Business Finance
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of financial management: analysis and decision making for asset management, capital budgeting, capital structure, and dividend policy. Prerequisite for all other finance courses.
prerequisites: Pre: ACC 200 and ACC 210, ECON 130 and ECON 131; or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Global Management and Organizational Behavior
description: Analysis of theories and concepts underlying domestic and global organizational management, including behavioral and personnel issues. Emphasis on leadership, team-work, cultural differences in the Asia Pacific region. Prerequisite to all other advanced management courses. Students may not receive credit for BUS 315 and TIM 303.

subject: BUS
title: Strategic Management
description: Applications of strategy to domestic and global business problems using an interdisciplinary approach. Emphasis on AsiaPacific business, assessment of risk, integration of all business core disciplines. Extensive writing expected.
prerequisites: Pre: all core courses and graduating senior standing.

subject: BUS
title: Business Study Abroad
description: Study abroad experience emphasizing international business issues. Content varies with courses taught; (C) accounting; (D) management of informational systems; (F) finance; (G) management; (I) international business; (K) marketing; (M) human resources; (R) real estate. Each alpha repeatable three times, up to 16 credits.

subject: BUS
title: Internship
description: On-the-job experience in the business community. Term paper and meetings with faculty advisor required. (D) MIS; (F) finance; (G) management; (I) international business; (K) marketing; (M) human resource management; (R) real estate. CR/NC only. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: consent and RE 300 for (R) only.

subject: BUS
title: Data Analytics for Business
description: Introduction to data analytics techniques and tools, builds on foundational business analysis and quantitative methods knowledge. Modules include preparing relevant data, conducting analysis, visualizing results, and storytelling with data.

subject: BUS
title: Asia Pacific Business
description: Analysis of business environment and business issues through study of businesses, governmental entities, and nongovernmental organizations in specific geographic areas in non-U.S. settings. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Asia Pacific Field Trip
description: Analysis of business environment and business issues through study and direct observation of businesses, governmental entities, and non-governmental organizations in non-U.S. settings. Involves group travel to selected international business cities. Travel sites will vary. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Dynamics of Asian Finance
description: Analysis of selected key industries of Asian countries: business/ economic trends, shifting product mix, technological changes, joint ventures, international competition, and productivity strategy, including contrasting management styles, worker/management relationships, and decision-making processes under different cultural settings. Industry observations conducted in Asian countries for three weeks during the summer.
prerequisites: Pre: 6 credit hours of economics or business, PAMI participant; or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Professional Development
description: Professional development course designed to focus and improve the career development and leadership skills of MBA students. Students learn from guest speakers through site visits, intensive workshops, and hands-on experience. No grading.
prerequisites: MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Data Analytics and Statistics for Business
description: Data analytical and statistical tools for the MBA with emphasis on descriptive and predictive quantitative analytical methods, including time series and regression. Completing an additional six contacthour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. A-F only.
prerequisites: MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Micro- and Macro-economic Foundations for Managers
description: Applications of micro- and macro-economic principles to managerial decisions. Microeconomic focuses on economic foundations of business strategies. Macroeconomics focuses on the external economic environment including regulatory and international trends and issues. Complete an additional 3 contacthour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. MBA students only or advisor approval. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: BUS
title: Business Statistics
description: Statistical tools for the MBA with emphasis on quality control, time series, and forecasting using regression. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Economic Foundations of Strategy
description: Microeconomic principles that provide structure to solve managerial problems, and to suggest strategies for success. Evaluation of the microeconomic competitive environment in which organizations operate. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Marketing Management
description: Concepts and issues in marketing within the global environment of business. Ethical dimensions and social responsibilities; market research; consumer segmentation and positioning. Strategic marketing planning. A-F only.
prerequisites: MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Accounting for Decision-making
description: Accounting tools for business professionals focusing on the role of accounting information in capital markets, managerial decision-making and corporate governance. A-F only. Completing an additional 12 contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. With instructor approval, the tutorial requirement may be waived if student has successfully completed an accounting course (ex. ACC 200 (with a minimum grade of C-) or 201 (with a minimum grade of C-) or an approved online tutorial.

subject: BUS
title: Digital Transformation with Information Systems and Technology
description: Practices, techniques, and tools for managing digital innovation in markets, firms, and enterprise systems through information technologies and applications. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.
prerequisites: MBA students only or advisor approval. (Pre: 619 and 620 or consent. Spring only)

subject: BUS
title: Leadership and Organizational Behavior
description: Personal leadership and communications development and the contributions of the behavioral sciences to understanding human behavior in organizations with a focus on leading organizations in times of change.
prerequisites: MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Business, Government, and External Environment
description: Important issues related to the external environment of business. This includes international trade and finance, regulatory environment, social impacts of business. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Ethics
description: Assists students in developing an awareness of major ethical issues which affect business decisions, and encourages a socially responsible consideration of those issues and being able to express their views. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Managerial Finance
description: Financial management theories and tools for business professionals; asset management; capital budgeting; capital structure and dividend policies. MBA students only or advisor approval. A-F only.

subject: BUS
title: Managing Information Technology for Strategic Advantage
description: Theory, practices, techniques for managing information technology resources for in

subject: EALL
title: Japanese Literature in Translation– Traditional
description: Survey of all major forms from the earliest era to mid-19th century.

subject: EALL
title: Japanese Literature in Translation– Modern
description: Survey from mid-19th century to present; emphasis on fiction.

subject: EALL
title: Survey of Japanese Literature–KIC
description: Survey of traditional and modern Japanese literature in translation, covering all major genres. Only offered at Konan University in Japan.
prerequisites: Not open to students with 271 or 272.

subject: EALL
title: Korean Literature in Translation– Traditional
description: Survey of Korean literature from earliest times with emphasis on development and cultural context; all readings in English translation. Students write essays about the readings.

subject: EALL
title: Korean Literature in Translation– Modern
description: Survey of 20th-century Korean literature with emphasis on development and cultural context; all readings in English translation. Students write essays about the readings.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Korean Culture
description: Multi-disciplinary and historically-located study of Korean culture through the examination of literary and visual texts. Topics will depend upon the term. Repeatable one time with consent. (Spring only)

subject: EALL
title: Japanese Film: Art and History (Alpha)
description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics. (Cross-listed as ASAN 325)

subject: EALL
title: Chinese Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (Cross-listed as ASAN 330)

subject: EALL
title: Literary Traditions of East Asia
description: Selected works of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean literature in English; relationships and parallels.
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Chinese Literature: Ancient
description: Survey of all major genres from antiquity until the ninth century.
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Chinese Literature: Pre-modern
description: Survey of all major genres from the ninth century till the end of the Qing.
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: 20th-Century Chinese Literature and Culture (Alpha)
description: Survey of 20th-century Chinese literature in translation. Includes a variety of genres from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong: (B) 1919–1949; (C) 1949–present; emphases on writing instruction.
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent

subject: EALL
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film. (Crosslisted as ASAN 364 and WGSS 346)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Traditional Chinese Fiction in Translation (Alpha)
description: Survey of pre-modern Chinese fiction in translation. (B) short story; (C) novel.
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: The City in Modern Chinese Literature and Visual Arts
description: Study of the fictional and visual representations of the city in the changing contexts of Chinese modernization from the late imperial age to the beginning of the 21st century. (Once a year)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Traditional Japanese Literature
description: Reading and analysis of English translations of selected important works in the classical tradition. No knowledge of Japanese required. Repeatable two times in different topics with consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Modern Japanese Literature
description: Reading and analysis of English translations of selected important works in modern Japanese literature. No knowledge of Japanese required. Repeatable two times in different topics with consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Japanese Cultural Studies
description: Multi-disciplinary and historically located study of Japanese culture through the examination of literary and visual texts. Specific topics will depend upon the term. Repeatable one time with consent. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Modern Korean Women Writers and Culture
description: Study of fiction by modern Korean women writers in the changing context of Korean culture. A-F only.

subject: EALL
title: East-West Cultural Encounters
description: Critical examination of encounters between Western and East Asian cultures across time. In addition to literary texts, the course may use sources from other media, and focus on a specific era, region, or genre.
prerequisites: an EALL course at 200 level or above; or a DH or DL course at 200 level or above; or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture–Chinese Diaspora
description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term. Repeatable one time with consent. (Cross-listed as ASAN 473)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism. (Cross-listed as ASAN 474)
prerequisites: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course.

subject: EALL
title: Perspectives on Chinese Cinema
description: Introduction to Chinese cinema studies, with emphasis on the theoretical and critical approaches to Chinese film. (Once a year)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Senior Colloquium in East Asian Literature
description: Comparative perspectives; some works studied in the original.

subject: EALL
title: Current Issues in East Asian Language Pedagogy
description: Survey on East Asian language pedagogy designed to develop students’ familiarity with and facility in addressing the major issues, initiatives, and innovations in the field.

subject: EALL
title: Introduction to East Asian Linguistics
description: Introduction to cross-linguistic comparison of the writing systems, dialects, history, phonology, morphology, and syntax of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. (Once a year)
prerequisites: CHN 451 and 452, or JPN 451, or KOR 451 and 452; or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Bibliographical and Research Methods (Alpha)
description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
prerequisites: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

subject: EALL
title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required. Repeatable one time with consent. (Cross-listed as ASAN 612)

subject: EALL
title: Contemporary Chinese Documentary: Record, Expression, Cultural Space
description: Introduction to contemporary Chinese independent documentary with these goals: to achieve in-depth understanding of Chinese society through documentary; be familiar with theoretical debates on documentary form; and understand documentary as a cultural discourse. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: EALL
title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective. Repeatable two times in different topics, but need consent for second repeat. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ASAN 665)

subject: EALL
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: EALL
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EALL
title: Seminar in Comparative East Asian Literature
description: Comparison of authors, modes, topics, and genres in poetry and prose; theoretical and practical criticism.

subject: EALL
title: Seminar in Comparison of East Asian Languages
description: Comparison of lexicon, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, etc., of two or more East Asian languages, contact influence on them.
prerequisites: CHN 451, CHN 452, or JPN 451; or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Economics
description: One semester survey of the principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics to enable students in all disciplines to understand current economic events.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Contemporary Literature: 1980s-Present
description: Survey of literature from the 80s (1986) to the present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

subject: FIN
title: Personal Financial Planning
description: Focuses on principles and techniques for handling personal financial decisions, including: personal budgeting, obtaining credit, life and casualty insurance, buying a home, buying an automobile, savings and investments, and retirement planning.

subject: FIN
title: Problems of Business Finance
description: Application of financial principles to cases involving important financial decisions; emphasis on writing.

subject: FIN
title: Corporate Financial Management
description: Development and analysis of modern financial theory and its implications for management decisions: market efficiency, capital asset pricing, firm investment decisions, capital structure, dividend policy, and cost of capital.

subject: FIN
title: Investments
description: Introduction to various investment media and capital markets. Topics include the analysis of security returns using techniques such as beta, filter rules, and portfolio theory.

subject: FIN
title: International Business Finance
description: Financial management of foreign and international business operations: the regulatory environment of international finance, financing international transactions, international capital markets, taxation. Financial decision-making in the firm.

subject: FIN
title: International Banking
description: Commercial, investment, and merchant banking. Includes theory and practical applications. Topics include international lending, Euromarkets, global gap management, Forex activities, and global risk management.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Aspects of New Ventures
description: Examination of underlying business models for new ventures, how to determine corresponding financial requirements, and approaches to resource acquisition. Students explore a range of financing sources and related issues of valuation and deal structure. College restriction: Shidler students only.
prerequisites: junior standing and BUS 314, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: Approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

subject: FIN
title: Options and Other Derivatives
description: Options and other derivatives. Equity options, index options and options on futures. Black-Scholos Model. Trading strategies and tactics. Contemporary developments in financial engineering. A-F only.

subject: FIN
title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
description: Security analysis and portfolio management from standpoint of the professional analyst and institutional investor. Recent advances in security valuation models, portfolio selection, and techniques for appraising portfolio performance. College restriction: Shidler students only. A-F only.

subject: FIN
title: Bank Financial Management
description: Analysis of financial institution management within the domestic economy and regulatory environment. Topics include federal reserve activities, interest rates, regulation, lending, investments, and asset/liability management.

subject: FIN
title: Banking and Capital Markets
description: Covers the analytical skills necessary to work in the financial services industry, in particular in the bank treasury department or the fixed income capital market sector. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: FIN
title: Asian Finance
description: Financial systems, regulatory structure over financial institutions in the Asia-Pacific region. Major financial policy issues for financial sector reforms in the region. Seminar format. A-F only.

subject: FIN
title: Enterprise Risk Management
description: Overview analyzing various primary risks faced by corporations and developing important risk management techniques with an emphasis on enterprise risk management. Combined lectures, case studies, and discussions. BUS majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: FIN
title: Sustainable Finance
description: Explores criticism and defense of the traditional profit maximization business model. Economic theory, recent trends, and case studies will refine students’ understanding of this cutting-edge field. Repeatable one time.

subject: FIN
title: Special Topics in Finance, Real Estate or Insurance
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of finance and finance-related fields. Repeatable two times in different topics.
prerequisites: BUS 314 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: FIN
title: Seminar in Financial Planning
description: A capstone course for financial services and planning track. This is a case study course intended to provide students the opportunity to integrate concepts from earlier courses and develop a comprehensive view of the financial planning process. A-F only.
prerequisites: FIN 301 and FIN 311 and two of the following courses: FIN 490E, FIN 490F, ACC 401, INS 300

subject: FIN
title: Advanced Topics in Finance
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. (B) equity research and corporate valuation methods; (C) Japanese financial management; (D) financial analysis; (E) retirement and employee benefit planning; (F) finance estate planning. Repeatable four times for (D). Shidler College of Business students only. A-F only for (E) and (F). (Fall only for (B))
prerequisites: FIN 311 and BUS 314 for (B); BUS 314 or BUS 629 for (C); FIN 311 or FIN 629, or consent for (D); FIN 301 for (E) and (F).

subject: FIN
title: International Monetary Systems and Global Financial Markets
description: Supply and demand for capital in national and international markets. Nature of capital movements and role of capital in industrialization of regions and nations.

subject: FIN
title: Problems in Business Finance
description: Application of financial principles and analytical techniques to financial problems. Case method.

subject: FIN
title: Investment Analysis and Management
description: Techniques of security analysis, theories of investment, and the analysis of investment decisions related to portfolio planning.

subject: FIN
title: Advanced Topics in Finance
description: Major current financial issues and problems. (C) Japanese financial management; (D) portfolio management theory; (F) stocks, bonds, and modern instruments.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Analysis and Valuation
description: Introduces the standard financial analysis framework and develops skills in analysis of financial information, evaluation of firms’ business risks and earnings prospects, and related applications in valuation. Repeatable one time.

subject: FIN
title: International Financial Management
description: Financial decision-making in an international setting: analysis of direct foreign investment; economic, accounting, and regulatory environments, including taxation; international money and capital markets; import and export financing; multinational working capital management; and risk aspects of international finance.

subject: FIN
title: International Banking
description: Commercial, investment, and merchant banking in the international arena. Includes international lending, Euromarkets, global gap management, Forex activities, and international risk management.

subject: FIN
title: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: Assessment of financial needs, arranging venture financing, assessing value to the entrepreneur and the investor(s), financial aspects of strategic planning, analyzing the tradeoffs between alternative financing choices and flexibility and control, harvesting the investment.

subject: FIN
title: Advanced Capital Markets
description: Regulatory structure over capital market institutions, market developmental issues, market microstructure issues, and corporate governance, and creation of capital market infrastructure. Seminar format.

subject: FIN
title: PDEs and Stochastic Calculus
description: Covers PDEs (Partial Differential Equations) and calculus in a stochastic environment. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Programming in Finance
description: Addresses programming principles, and programming languages used in financial modeling. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Portfolio Optimization
description: Introduces students to principles of capital markets, classical portfolio theory, and focus on portfolio optimization. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Financial Derivatives
description: Will familiarize the students with the mathematical foundation and the application of Futures, Swaps, and Options. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Financial Forecasting
description: Focus on financial forecasting and financial econometrics as volatility and correlation modeling. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Insurance and Risk Management
description: Introduces students to topics in the actuarial science and latest developments in risk management. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in Financial Engineering program, or consent

subject: FIN
title: Interest Rate/Credit Models
description: Addresses specific properties of interest rate modelling as mean reversion as well as latest developments in credit risk

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Measurement of bioelectrical signals, computer and electronic simulation of biological systems, design and evaluation of electronic circuits for biomedical measurements, evaluation of instruments for patient safety.

subject: ECE
title: Bioelectric Phenomena
description: Study of electrical phenomena in living systems. Mechanisms underlying bioelectric activity. Membrane and transepithelial potentials, skin impedance, electrocardiography, neuroelectric signals, diagnostic considerations, laboratory demonstrations.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Instrumentation
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, applications, and design of biomedical instrumentation. Transducers, IC and microcomputer applications, patient safety.

subject: ECE
title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty; to be oriented toward juniors and seniors. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (G) computer vision; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECE
title: Provisional Topics
description: Upper division course with subject matter to be announced.

subject: ECE
title: Ethics in Electrical Engineering
description: Equip electrical engineers with the necessary background for ethical reasoning, as it pertains to technology, society, workplace issues, and the environment. ECE majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ECE
title: Capstone Design Project
description: Significant project integrating the design content of previous courses and incorporating engineering standards and realistic constraints. Written report must document all aspects of the design process: reliability, safety, economics, ethics. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Directed Reading
description: Investigation of advanced engineering problems. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ECE
title: Graph Theory and Its Applications
description: Graphs and subgraphs, trees and treelike graphs, planar graphs, connectivity and edge-connectivity, applications.

subject: ECE
title: Algorithm I
description: Design and evaluation of machine representations, techniques and algorithms for sorting, pattern processing, computational geometry, mathematical computations, and engineering applications. Introduction to computational issues of time, space, communication, and program correctness.

subject: ECE
title: Artificial Intelligence
description: LISP for machine intelligence applications, or related constraint object and logic-oriented languages.

subject: ECE
title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ICS 606)
prerequisites: 467 or ICS 313 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Network Algorithms
description: Network algorithms, protocols, and packet switching systems for the internet including TCP/IP, routing algorithms, transmission scheduling, link management, buffer management, and simple network management.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Networks
description: Propagation of signals in fibers, components, modulation and demodulation, transmission system engineering, network systems and architectures, network design, control and management and packet switching.

subject: ECE
title: Computer and Network Security
description: Basic security theory, current practices, and emerging research issues. First covering the fundamentals of computer and network security, then will work on research projects on computer and network security.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing
description: An advanced course in digital processing. Topics include fast DFT algorithms, multirate systems and filter banks, power spectrum estimation, linear prediction, optimum linear filters, and adaptive filtering. A-F only. Open to nonmajors for CR/NC only.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Image Processing
description: Human visual perception, image formation, sampling and quantization, enhancement and restoration, color image processing, wavelets and multiresolution representations, image and video compression.

subject: ECE
title: Linear and Convex Optimization
description: Algorithms for linear, nonlinear, and convex optimization. Emphasis is on methodology and the underlying mathematical structures. Topics include simplex method, network flow methods, optimality conditions, duality, Newton’s method and interior point methods. ECE, ME, MIS and MATH majors only. (Alt. years)

subject: ECE
title: Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control
description: Sequential decision-making via dynamic programming. Optimal control of stochastic dynamic systems. Applications in linear-quadratic control, inventory control, resource allocation, scheduling, and control of queues. Rollout and other suboptimal methods. Value and policy iteration.
prerequisites: 342 or MATH 371 or MATH 471, or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Electronic Circuits
description: Electronic circuits for precision measurement, computation, and signal processing. Low noise and interference reduction techniques. High-frequency and high-speed techniques. Micro-processor and biomedical applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Solid-State Devices
description: Advanced physical principles and design of modern solid-state electronic devices. Heterostructures, photodetectors, LED, junction lasers, and other devices of current importance identified from the current literature. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Electronics I
description: Fundamentals of optical radiation, including stimulated and spontaneous processes. Optical electronics including optical resonators, lasers, optical detectors, light-guiding, and applications. A-F only.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Electronics II
description: Electro-optics, noise detection, light and sound dielectric waveguide phenomena, lasers, optics, phase conjugation.

subject: ECE
title: Microsensors and Microactuators I
description: Technology methods and physical principles of microsensors and microactuators. Vacuum technology, thin film deposition and characterization techniques, solid mechanics, micromachining, acoustics, piezoelectricity and principles of current microtransducers.

subject: ECE
title: Rapid Prototyping of Electrophysical Devices
description: Hands on experience in designing, fabricating, testing, and iterating according to rapid-prototyping principles. Students learn state-of-the-art equipment for making their designs, software for simulating designs, and working in design teams. ECE majors only. Graduate students only. (Spring only)

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Topics in Physical Electronics
description: Recent developments in phenomena and devices of physical electronics.

subject: ECE
title: Analysis and Design of Integrated Circuits
description: Fabrication constraints and design guidelines for integrated circuits. Nonlinear model of integrated circuit transistor. Design and analysis of integrated logic circuits and linear circuits.

subject: ECE
title: Smart Grids and Renewable Energy Integration
description: Challenges and solutions for integrating intermittent renewable energy sources into the power system, with a focus on “smart grid” approaches and demand-response. Using linear programming and other modeling techniques to answer policy-relevant questions. Graduate students only. (Spring only)

subject: ECE
title: Applied Random Processes
description: Random variables, multivariate distributions, random sequences, stochastic convergence, stationary and nonstationary processes, spectral analysis, Karhunen-Loeve expansion, Markov processes, mean square estimation, Kalman filters.

subject: ECE
title: Queueing Theory
description: Poisson, Markov, and renewal processes, M/G/1 queue, G/M/1 queue, queueing networks, simulation, and performance evaluation of computer systems and communication networks. ECE, ICS, MATH majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Detection and Estimation Theory
description: Fundamentals of signal detection and estimation theory. Hypothesis testing, parametric and nonparametric detection, sequential detection, parametric estimation, linear estimation, robust detection and estimation, and applications to communication systems.

subject: ECE
title: Communication System Performance
description: Fundamental performance limits, signal detection and estimation, modulation, intersymbol interference, equalization adaptive filtering, sequence detection, synchronization, fading multipath channels, spread spectrum.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: Fundamentals of computer communication networks including modeling, performance evaluation, routing, flow control, local area networks, distributed algorithms, and optimization algorithms.

subject: ECE
title: Machine Learning
description: Learning theory, pattern recognition and regression; gradient based algorithms and least square algorithms; Kernel methods; Bayesian learning algorithms; ensemble learning and boosting; principal component analysis; independent component analysis, and clustering; reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming. ECE, ME, ICS, MATH majors only.

subject: ENG
title: 19th Century Literature in English (Except American)
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of 19th century prose and poetry in English.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: British Literature After 1900
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry, and drama in English from 1900 to the present.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: American Literature to Mid-19th Century
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry, and drama in American literature through the middle of the 19th century.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: American Literature Mid-19th to Mid20th Century
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of prose, poetry and drama in American literature from the middle of the 19th century to the middle of the 20th century.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: American Literature Since Mid-20th Century
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of American literature since approximately 1950.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Film, Literature, and Adaptation
description: Comparative analysis of literary texts and their screen adaptations.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Poetry
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the analysis of imagery, sound, language, form, and structure in poems.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Drama
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the form, function, and development of the genre of drama. Emphasis on types of writing and revision, and oral presentation.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Film
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the form, function, and development of cinematic narrative techniques.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Non-fiction
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of non-fiction such as essays, biographies, autobiographies, speeches, political and legal documents, conversion and captivity narratives, testimonials, science writing, and travel writing.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Fiction
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the form, function, and development of fiction genres such as short story and the novel in English. Repeatable one time for different topics.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Film History
description: Introduction to the history of film as art, industry, and socio-cultural representation from the invention of the moving picture to 1965.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Literatures of Hawai‘i
description: Writings of various ethnic groups in Hawai‘i, ancient to contemporary. Songs, stories, poetry, fiction, essays that illustrate the social history of Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as ES 370)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Literature of the Pacific
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the literature of the Pacific, including Pacific voyagers and contemporary writings in English by Pacific Islanders. (Cross-listed as PACS 371)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Asian American Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Asian American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds. (Cross-listed as ES 372)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: African American Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of African American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Race, Ethnicity, and Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of race and ethnicity as the basis for literary inquiry.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Philippine Contemporary Literature in English
description: Critical survey of 20th-century Philippine literature written in English; cultural values. (Cross-listed as IP 363)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Philippine Literature and Folklore in Translation
description: Philippine folk literature translated into English: epics, myths, legends, and other folklore. Classic works of vernacular writers. (Cross-listed as IP 396)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Native Hawaiian Literature in English
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Native Hawaiian literature, ancient to contemporary, in translation and in English, that demonstrate the depth and breadth of the Native Hawaiian literary tradition.

subject: ENG
title: Folklore, Wonder Tales, and Oral Traditions
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of folktales, legends, ballads, wonder tales, and other folklore genres in various cultures; consideration given to folklore/literature relationships.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Popular Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of popular literature genres, such as detective fiction, science fiction, the thriller, the romance, and westerns.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Gender, Sexuality and Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literary constructions of gender and sexuality; emphasis on teaching gender and sexuality through writing and oral communication. (Cross-listed as WGSS 381)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Children’s Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of children’s literature; may include study of children’s book illustration.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Fairy Tales and Their Adaptations
description: Comparative analysis of selected tales of magic and their adaptations across history, cultures and media such as book illustration and film.
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Literature and the Environment
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of intersections between literature and the environment, including issues such as climate change, technology, pollution, land and land use, interspecies relationships.
prerequisites: One ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Theories and Methods of English Studies
description: Intensive study of questions, issues, traditions, and movements in the field of English Studies. Recommended for students planning to pursue postbaccalaureate degrees.
prerequisites: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: English in Hawai‘i
description: English language in Hawai‘i viewed historically and in a multicultural context, with attention to politics, religion, race, and education, from 1820 to present.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Teaching Composition
description: Theory, observation, and practice in teaching writing, especially the use of one-on-one and small group instruction. Recommended: 306.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Advanced Argumentative Writing
description: Advanced study of both the philosophical and practical dimensions of written reasoning. Emphasis on argument as a process of inquiry.
prerequisites: FW and either 200 or one ENG DL course, or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Writing for Digital Media
description: Combined lecture/lab on writing and rhetoric in computermediated communication. May include online technical writing, courseware development, social media content creation.
prerequisites: two ENG DL courses or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Professional Editing
description: Discussion and practice in the professional editing of articles, reports, books; logic, clarity, coherence, consistency of tone and style, grammar and punctuation.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Composition/Rhetoric/ Language
description: Intensive study of selected topics, questions, themes, issues, and/or writers in composition, rhetoric, and/or English language. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Form and Theory of Poetry
description: Poetic theories and techniques for students interested in writing poetry.

subject: ENG
title: Poetry Workshop
description: Writing, evaluating poems. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Nonfiction Writing
description: Workshop analysis of nonfiction as a literary form. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Form and Theory of Fiction
description: Narrative techniques for students interested in writing fiction.

subject: ENG
title: Fiction Workshop
description: Writing, evaluating fiction. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Creative Writing
description: Intensive study of selected topics, questions, themes, writers, or modes of creative writing in a workshop setting. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Culture
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in regard to cultural studies and the reading and interpretation of cultural texts. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Comparative Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in the field of comparative literature. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Medieval Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in Old/Middle English literature from 500-1500, including

subject: CEE
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ATMO 449 and SUST 449)
prerequisites: Senior standing or higher, or consent.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering II
description: DP. Continuation of 355 field exploration, lateral earth pressures, bearing capacity theory, slope stability, use of geosynthetics. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Pavement Engineering
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design principles of flexible and rigid pavements; HMA mixture design, equipment and construction; and application of life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) in pavement engineering. Includes laboratory sessions for aggregate testing and Superpave mix design. A-F only.
prerequisites: CEE 355 (or concurrent), CEE 375 (or concurrent), and CEE 361.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Traffic Engineering
description: Design/analysis of signalized, unsignalized intersections, urban networks. Traffic impact studies; analysis steps and applications. Design/redesign options. Parking studies: demand, alternative designs (lot layouts).
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Urban and Regional Transportation Planning
description: Application of travel demand forecasting models to transportation planning. Evaluation and decision-making. Term projects.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Methods
description: Methods of construction, primarily buildings. Construction types: light and heavy wood; steel; plain, reinforced, and prestressed concrete; masonry. Foundations; associated details of frames, walls, roofs, floors, openings, finishes. Disasters, failures, and their causes. Industrialization of the building process.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Project Management
description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ARCH 432)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Equipment and Methods
description: Methods and equipment used on horizontal/ heavy engineering projects. Available equipment, their production, and how they are used to excavate, move, process, and place the earth.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Estimating and Bidding
description: Estimating science; techniques of estimating quantities and pricing of work for construction contracting; classification of costs, analysis of plans and specifications for estimating; computerized estimating; cash flow, bidding strategy, preparation and submission. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
description: To teach the theory and the practice of planning, scheduling, and reporting a construction project through the use of bar chart and CPM. Format to include lectures, text, outside speakers, site visits, discussions, case study, and computers.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Safety
description: Safety and health concepts, laws and requirements for civilian and contractor personnel in construction, including applications in project management and construction activities. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Construction Law
description: In-depth exploration of the legal regimes governing construction. Construction contracts, contractors, and subcontractors. Breach of contracts, claims and litigation in construction projects. Senior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Undergraduate Structural Research
description: Individual research project for undergraduate students in the structures track. Topic to be determined by consultation with structural faculty advisor. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Field Experience
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Structural Loads
description: Introduction to the minimum load requirements for buildings and other structures used in current structural design codes. Derive and apply dead, live, rain, soil, snow, wind, earthquake, flood, inundation, and other loads to structural systems. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Reinforced Concrete Design
description: DP. (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Behavior and design of reinforced concrete beams, one-way slabs and columns. Laboratory section includes design and hands-on manufacturing and testing of reinforced concrete members. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Structural Steel Design
description: Basic properties of steel; behavior and design of steel beams, columns, and connections; introduction to rigid frames.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Senior Design Project & Professional Ethics
description: Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills are assessed through multiple presentations to an industry. Engineering ethics, ethical decision making and deliberation. A-F only. Senior standing only. (Fall only)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Senior Design Project
description: (Lec/Lab) Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills will be assessed through multiple presentations to an industry panel. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: senior standing in CEE or CNST and CEE 489B
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Will reflect special interests of visiting and/or permanent faculty. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: junior or senior standing, and consent
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Special Problems
description: Individual investigation in civil and environmental engineering topics as approved by instructor.
prerequisites: senior standing, and minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum GPA of 3.0 in engineering
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
description: CR/NC only
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Operations Management
description: Linear programming, simplex method, graphical representation: dual; degeneracy; transportation problem; assignment problems; data envelopment analysis; applications; case studies; managerial reporting; LINDO software. Graduate students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: CEE 476 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and consent.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Cost Engineering and Quality Control
description: Study and applications of cost/schedule control systems criteria, earned value analysis, probabilistic cost estimating, construction risk management, construction quality control, and operations research in construction. Recommended: CEE 472 or CEE 474, or consent.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Machine Learning in Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Science
description: Statistical machine learning and deep learning methods. Script languages for data-driven model training, validation and test. Analysis with linear algebra and statistics. Applications to engineering and earth science problems. Knowledge of Python Programming desirable. (Alt. years: fall)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Risk Analysis and Decision Making
description: Risk analysis and decision making are fundamental areas of construction and project management. Students will benefit from analyzing risks and learning various decision making techniques for real-time applications. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice-negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR. (Cross-listed as LAW 508)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Parallel Computing for Engineers
description: Concepts and techniques in high performance parallel computing. Topics include parallel language and algorithms, parallelizing pre-existing serial codes, statistical analysis, and techniques up to increase computational speed and accuracy for problems requiring large memory size. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Organizations: Theory and Change
description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as PUBA 603)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk. Knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable. (Cross-listed as ORE 621 and SUST 621)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics
description: Theory of fluid dynamics in differential form, covering equation of motion, vortex generation, flow in rotating frame, potential theory, laminar flow, and introduction to turbulence.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment II: Formal Assessment
description: Understand techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment is stressed. Significant instruction on writing individualized education programs. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Introduction to Inclusive Teaching
description: Teacher candidates engage in reflective, procedural, and research writing to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Science
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to the teaching and learning of science in elementary settings, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, using evidence-based practices. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Mathematics in Inclusive Settings
description: Prepares beginning elementary school teachers of mathematics, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: STEM
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to teaching and learning of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) content for inclusive elementary classrooms, K-6. Teacher candidates focus on planning, teaching, and assessing STEM. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Integrating Social Studies and the Performing Arts
description: Social Studies and Performing Arts integrated content in diverse K-6 classrooms. Teacher candidates engage with social issues through collaborative, expressive, aesthetic, creative, and critical pedagogy. Candidates perform, present, and teach to develop oral communication skills. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy I: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, K-3
description: Overview of principles and practices for teaching reading (phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) to diverse students, grades K-3; including planning, instruction, and assessment. Writing assignments include lesson reflections, case studies, modules, and reading responses. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy II: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, Grades 4-6
description: Teacher candidates demonstrate essential reading comprehension strategies, engaging students in complex text by planning, instructing, and assessing elementary students in grades 4-6, in inclusive settings. Emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy III: Writing and Visual Arts in Inclusive Settings, K-6
description: Methods, programs, and strategies for planning, teaching, and assessing writing for elementary students in inclusive settings, grades K-6. Visual arts methods are integrated to develop visual literacy. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience I: Response to Intervention in Reading
description: Teacher candidates in this field based course will use an evidencebased practice in reading within a response to intervention (Rtl) framework. Supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Rounds
description: Field-based course engages teacher candidates in a variety of purposeful observation and reflection activities aligned with course work. Field settings are appropriate to concurrent classes; supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience II: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience III: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Student Teaching in Elementary and Special Education Classrooms
description: Full-time student teaching in grades K-6 in an elementary school inclusion classroom, or a combination of general education and special education settings. The experience is directed by a qualified mentor teacher and has university-provided supervision. A-F only.

subject: ESEE
title: Seminar for Student Teaching
description: Seminar to support student teaching experiences and prepare teacher candidates to transition into a full time teacher, examine ethical issues in the field, prepare for employment, and demonstrate ability to meet professional standards. A-F only.

subject: FMCH
title: Family Medicine and Community Health Longitudinal Clerkship
description: 5.5-month ambulatory clerkship. Students learn history taking, physical exam skills, and management of family medicine patients. Emphasis on behavioral care, caring for the underserved, sports medicine, preventive care, and common acute/chronic ambulatory problems. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Co-requisite: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.

subject: FMCH
title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health
description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6). MED majors only for (G). CR/NC only. (Spring only for (G))

subject: FMCH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: FDM
title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
description: Introduction to the fields of apparel design and merchandising including theories of fashion change, apparel industry operations, current industry issues, literature of the field, professional competencies, careers in apparel and related businesses. A-F only.

subject: FDM
title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
description: DS. Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance. Repeatable one time. Open to nonmajors. (Cross-listed as WGSS 200)

subject: FDM
title: Basic Apparel Construction
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, concepts, and procedures for quality construction and custom fitting of clothing.

subject: FDM
title: Western World Fashion History
description: Historic study of dress as related to customs and cultures in the Western world, in sociohistorical and contemporary contexts. Emphasis on 19th and 20th centuries.

subject: FDM
title: Flat Pattern Design
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of pattern making for women’s apparel through manipulation of pattern blocks.

subject: FDM
title: Fashion Illustration
description: DA. (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles and techniques of sketching the fashion figure including garment details and fabric drape. Development of a personal style of illustration. Introduction to use of computers for illustration.

subject: FDM
title: Textiles I
description: DP. Introduction to fibers, fabric structure, and finishes related to selection and care. Interrelationship between textile characteristics, properties, and end uses. Open to non-majors. A-F only.

subject: FDM
title: Costumes/Cultures of East Asia
description: Development of ethnic dress of China, Japan, and Korea as a visual manifestation of culture. Students will be trained in written communication skills to describe and report important designs of these ethnic dresses related to culture.

subject: FDM
title: Fashion Forecasting/Marketing
description: Principles and practices in fashion trend forecasting, including environment in analysis, consumer research, competitive analysis, color and textile forecasting, style directions, and digital marketing trends. Adapting fashion trend forecasts to apparel lines. Sophomore standing or higher.
prerequisites: Pre: one FW or FG course, or consent.

subject: FDM
title: Draping Essentials
description: Principles of pattern making through draping muslin models on standard garment forms. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Specialty Market Design: Group Collection Development
description: Advanced study in the specialty market design, pattern making, and construction for fashion design majors. Different specialty designs, such as swimwear, menswear, or others, will be offered each semester. Repeatable five times. Recommended: 315, 330. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Textiles Quality Assurance
description: DP. Chemical nature and structure of fibers and fabrics, their properties and finishes. FDM majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Textiles Quality Assurance Laboratory
description: DY. Examination of textile properties through standardized textiles testing laboratory equipment. FDM majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Advanced Apparel Design and Construction Techniques
description: Principles of advanced techniques for garment construction with emphasis on

subject: CHEM
title: Methods of Instrumental Analysis
description: Theory, instrumentation, applications. Three areas each semester-one credit hour per area. Repeatable unlimited times in different areas.
prerequisites: 333 and graduate standing in CHEM or consent.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Structure Determination
description: Interpretation of chemical and physical (primarily spectral) data in the identification of organic compounds.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Synthesis I
description: Modern synthetic methods with emphasis on the design and execution of multi-step sequences.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Organic Chemistry
description: Theory of molecular structure, stereochemistry, and reaction mechanisms.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Synthesis II
description: Continuation of 642, and is the second half of a two- semester course in Modern Organic Synthesis. (Spring only)
prerequisites: 642 and a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
description: Includes statistical thermodynamics, with application to chemical systems.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Kinetics and Reaction Dynamics
description: Kinetics and chemical reaction dynamics of elementary reactions relevant to combustion processes, astrochemistry, chemical vapor deposition and planetary sciences. (Spring only)

subject: CHEM
title: Quantum Chemistry
description: Rigorous introduction to quantum mechanics, including operator formalism, matrix formation, group theory, and perturbation theory; introduction to the electronic structure of atoms and molecules.

subject: CHEM
title: Astrochemistry–A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ASTR 657 and ERTH 657)

subject: CHEM
title: Crystallography
description: Crystal symmetry. Elementary x-ray physics. Diffraction theory and its application to crystal and molecular structure determination.

subject: CHEM
title: Enzyme Reaction Mechanisms
description: The chemical mechanisms of reactions catalyzed by enzymes in biochemical pathways, with an emphasis on the major types of cofactor and metal catalyzed reactions.

subject: CHEM
title: Computational Modeling in Chemistry
description: Theory and application of computational modeling in chemistry. Statistical theory behind molecular dynamics simulations, application to modeling chemical systems, computer programming, and analysis of results. Graduate students only.

subject: CHEM
title: (Alpha) Chemistry Seminar I
description: Current topics in (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CHEM
title: (Alpha) Chemistry Seminar II
description: Continuation of 691. Current topics in: (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CHEM
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CHEM
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for MS degree and consent of thesis chair.

subject: CHEM
title: Special Topics: Inorganic Chemistry
description: Theory and applications. Repeatable unlimited times in different topics.

subject: CHEM
title: Special Topics: Organic Chemistry
description: Theory and applications. Repeatable unlimited times in different topics.

subject: CHEM
title: Special Topics: Physical Chemistry
description: Theory and applications. Repeatable unlimited times in different topics.

subject: CHEM
title: Special Topics: Biochemistry
description: Theory and applications. A-F only. Repeatable unlimited times in different topics.

subject: CHEM
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD degree and consent of dissertation chair.

title: Directed Third-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in their area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. CR/NC only. Repeatable three times.

title: Fourth-Level Mandarin I

title: High-Advanced Chinese I

subject: GEO
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: DS. Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control. (Cross-listed as SUST 404)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Water in the Environment
description: DP. Water fluxes in the environment. Occurrence and movement of water; methods of quantification. Water balance of soil-plant system: precipitation, interception, infiltration, runoff, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and groundwater recharge.
prerequisites: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Conservation and Evolutionary Biogeography
description: Theories and techniques for the analysis of spatial microevolutionary patterns, taught from an interdisciplinary perspective. Examples and readings emphasize Hawai‘i and the Pacific region. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: either 309, BIOL 265 or BIOL 487, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Cultural Biogeography
description: DS. Coevolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens. A-F only.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Human Role in Environmental Change
description: DB. Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability. (Cross-listed as BIOL 410)
prerequisites: with a minimum grade of B, one of 101, BIOL 101, BIOL 123 and either 322 or BIOL 310; or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
description: DP. Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes. (Cross-listed as SUST 413)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
description: DS. Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ASAN 413)

subject: GEO
title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
description: Investigation of the forces behind natural and technological hazards, and human actions that reduce or increase vulnerability to natural disasters. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: DS. Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as TIM 415 and SUST 415)

subject: GEO
title: Urban Geography
description: DS. Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings.
