Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities. (Cross-listed as PLAN 421)

subject: GEO
title: Agriculture, Food and Society
description: DS. Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to non-majors. (Cross-listed as SUST 423)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Marine Policy
description: DS. Introduction to the law and policies concerning the marine environment, commerce and security. Role of science, law and politics in historical and current policies for maritime trades, navigation safety, marine resources, and marine exploration.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Regional Analysis
description: DS. Spatial dynamics and environmental implications of urban and rural development. Concepts of regions, process of regional development, patterns of spatial interaction, and theoretical bases for development strategies; emphasis on Hawai‘i.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Geographies of Popular Culture
description: DH. Examines contemporary geographical debates related to concepts of discourse, identity, space/place, power, representation, and popular culture. Considers various landscapes of popular culture and how popular culture mediate a sense of place, geopolitics, and identity formation.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Environment, Resources and Society
description: DS. Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues. (Cross-listed as SUST 426)

subject: GEO
title: Tea and Culture
description: DS. Examines cultural practices of tea in different parts of the world, focusing on history and culture of tea in China, Japan, and England. Also includes changing technologies and economies of tea worldwide. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
description: DS. Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication. A-F only. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as WGSS 433)

subject: GEO
title: Political Geography of Oceans
description: DS. The geopolitics of the oceans and the law of the sea as applied to regions of conflict and cooperation in marine resource development and preservation. Focus on Indo-West Pacific, South China Sea, Arctic Ocean.
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Peace and War
description: DS. Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world. (Cross-listed as PACE 436)
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Environment and Society in China
description: DS. Explores the relationship between environment and society in the Chinese society, including both traditional nature-culture connections and modern human-environmental issues. Examines China’s long-range cultural change, environmental transformations, and modern development challenges.

subject: GEO
title: Topics in Geography
description: Selected topics in geography not offered in the regular geography curriculum.

subject: GEO
title: Remote Sensing
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the principles of remote sensing and image processing skills. Topics include electromagnetic spectrum, sensors, aerial photo and satellite imagery interpretation, geometric and radiometric correction, digital image processing. Research project, lab.

subject: GEO
title: 3D Mapping and Analysis
description: DY. Environmental mapping and analysis using 3-dimensional geographical data acquired from high resolution remote sensing systems. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: GEO
title: Field Mapping
description: DS. Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data. (Cross-listed as ANTH 471)
prerequisites: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Web Mapping
description: (3 2-hr Lab) Introduction to interactive web mapping techniques for sharing and visualizing various forms of geospatial data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

subject: GEO
title: GIS and Spatial Analysis for Social Sciences
description: DS. Introduction to spacial analysis and GIS for social science studies, using open-source GIS tools to collect, visualize, and analyze social data; public health, socio-economic and social media data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

subject: GEO
title: GIS for Environmental Sciences
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr lab) Applications of GIS technologies to solve real-world problems in natural and environmental sciences. Research project, lab.

subject: GEO
title: Senior Thesis
description: Preparation of research paper under individual faculty supervision. Recommended for admission to graduate program.

subject: GEO
title: Practicum in Geography
description: Internship in applied geography under professional and faculty supervision. Field placement integrated with academic study. Repeatable up to six credit hours maximum.

subject: GEO
title: Capstone Undergraduate Seminar
description: Current and historical geographic literature provides a background for local and global issues. Through discussion, written reviews, and research reports, the geographic perspective in modern life will be explored.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Research
description: Geography majors conduct research under faculty supervision on a topic of their choice. Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent. Repeatable two times, up to six credits. GEO majors only. Senior standing only.
prerequisites: Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent. GEO majors only. Senior standing only.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Climatology
description: Methods of determining energy budget and water balance; applications in agriculture, hydrology, climatic classifications. Theory of climatic change. Bibliography.
prerequisites: 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 or ATMO 320; or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Project Management Systems
description: Project integration and PMIS; organizational power; conflict, strategic, and life-cycle management in construction management; matrix structure compared to projectized structure; project success; team building; change and culture in construction organizations; competitive bidding. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations. (Cross-listed as MGT 660)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics I
description: Response of single and multi degree-of-freedom systems due to dynamic forces. Direct integration of equations of motion. Response spectrum analysis. Application to earthquake loading. Systems with distributed mass and elasticity. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics II
description: Elastic and inelastic response of structures due to earthquakes. Seismic design criteria. Code design procedures. Advanced topics in time- and frequency-domain dynamic analysis of structures. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Smart Structures Technology
description: Fundamentals of sensor technologies for structural engineering applications. Control devices and strategies for protection of structures against extreme events, i.e. earthquakes, strong winds, etc. Structural health monitoring and smart sensor networks. Smart materials for civil structures. CE majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Modern Structural Analysis
description: Fundamentals of modern structural analysis theory, with emphasis on frame structures. Virtual work. Member stiffness/flexibility. Matrix formulation of stiffness and flexibility methods. Computer modeling issues. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Design
description: Slender columns; biaxial bending; combined shear and torsion. Building lateral load resisting frame analysis and design—shearwalls, rigid frames. Floor system analysis and design—flat slabs, joist systems. Computer applications. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
description: Load and resistance factored design (LRFD); steel building modeling and analysis; moment-resisting frames; bracing systems; beam-columns; moment connections; composite construction; and plate girders. A-F only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Finite Elements in Structures
description: Finite element method in structural engineering. Extension of structural theory. Virtual work. One- two-, and three-dimensional elements; axisymmetric elements; plate bending. Application to linear problems.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Prestressed Concrete
description: Behavior of prestressed concrete members, including prestress losses. Analysis and design of prestressed beams, slabs, and composite sections. Anchorage zone design; continuous systems.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Concrete Technology
description: Composition and hydration of concrete, chemical, and mineral admixtures, fresh and hardened properties, mix proportions, high performance concretes, durability and retrofitting technology, non-destructive testing, and advanced material characterization techniques. A-F only. CEE majors only. Graduate students only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: CEE 375 (with a minimum grade of C)
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Seminar in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Discussions and reports on literature, research, developments and activities in civil engineering. One unit of all graduate students for each graduate degree. Student presentations are required. Repeatable two times. CR/NC only.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: graduate standing in CEE or consent
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Selected Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Highly specialized topics in structures, soils, hydraulics, sanitary, water resources, applied mechanics, transportation. Repeatable unlimited times.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Directed Readings or Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CEE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD in civil engineering
department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Egypt: Mummies, Pharaohs, and Gods
description: An overview of ancient Egyptian civilization through lectures and class discussion on Egyptian literature, archaeology, history, religion and society.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek, Roman, and Ancient Mythology
description: Combines readings and analyses of myths from the ancient world including Europe, Asia, Africa, and Hawai‘i, with an emphasis on comparative analysis of cultures and religions.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Latin Elements in English
description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a literary vocabulary.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Latin Elements in Scientific Terminology
description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a scientific vocabulary.

subject: CLAS
title: World Myth to 1500 C.E.
description: Reading and analysis of myths and legends from around the globe, from before the dawn of writing to 1500 C.E. Students will learn to interpret traditional stories from several theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives. A-F only.

subject: CLAS
title: Understanding Ancient Religions
description: Comparative and historical survey of the religious beliefs and practices in ancient times throughout Egypt, Mesopotamia, Syria-Canaan, Anatolia, Persia, Greece, and Rome. A-F only. (Cross-listed as REL 211)

subject: CLAS
title: Myth, Religion, and Society
description: Theories and methods used in the study of myth, ritual, and religion. (Cross-listed as REL 300)

subject: CLAS
title: Biblical Hebrew I
description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as REL 301)

subject: CLAS
title: Biblical Hebrew II
description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; essay-based analysis of literary forms, with attention given both to stories important to the development of the Abrahamic religions and writing-based interpretation of religious traditions. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as REL 302)
prerequisites: REL 301 or CLAS 301 with C- or better

subject: CLAS
title: Indigenous & Decolonial Approaches to Religion and Culture
description: Introduction to indigenous and decolonial approaches to the study of religion and culture. Includes a critical assessment of tools and terminology traditionally used in academia. (Cross-listed as REL 304)

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics I
description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts. (Fall only)

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics II
description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts, including Tale of Sinuhe. (Spring only)

subject: CLAS
title: History of the Written Word
description: A hands-on history of writing beginning in Ancient Greece and Rome. Content includes the development of the alphabet, scripts, books, libraries, and writing in ancient culture.

subject: CLAS
title: Classics Ancient and Modern
description: Provides an in-depth introduction to a major work of classical literature and its impact on both ancient and modern poetry, prose, art, and intellectual history.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Drama
description: Survey of Greek and Roman drama, both tragedies and comedies, tracing the history of a genre that contains some of the wittiest and most agonizing moments in ancient literature.

subject: CLAS
title: Nature in the Ancient World
description: Study of the relationship between the Greeks and Romans and the natural environment. Particular attention will be given to the place of nature in ancient science, philosophy, literature, and “real life.” Assignments are essay-based.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman War Literature
description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world. (Cross-listed as PACE 325)
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: CLAS
title: The Greek and Roman Novel
description: Survey of Greek and Roman novels, a collection of highly entertaining texts that offer windows into various aspects of life in the ancient world.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
description: Major writers: emphasis on Homer, drama, and philosophy. Assignments are essay-based and attention is given to developing academic writing skills.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher or consent

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Roman Literature in Translation
description: Major writers: emphasis on Vergil, satire, and novel.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher or consent

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Epic
description: A survey of Greek and Roman epic literature, beginning with Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey and proceeding through the Hellenistic Greek and Roman periods.

subject: CLAS
title: Topics in Ancient Greek Thought
description: Explore a central aspect of ancient Greek philosophy and literature. This may be a theme, such as tragedy or emotions; a thinker, such as Aristotle

subject: ENG
title: Biography
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American literature. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: MA Final Project
description: Individual reading and research towards preparation of MA project. 3 credit hours required. CR/NC only. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Supervised Practicum
description: Applies course work in literature, creative writing, cultural studies, or composition and rhetoric to hands-on activities engaging publics outside of the university under direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. ENG majors only. A-F only.

subject: ENG
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual reading or research. Repeatable with consent of Graduate Director.

subject: ENG
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Composition Studies
description: Intensive study of selected issues in composition studies. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Rhetoric
description: Intensive study of selected topics in the history of rhetoric, rhetorical theory, or rhetorical criticism; topic to be announced. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Creative Writing
description: Advanced study in creative writing focused on thesis and dissertation projects. Repeatable one time in each English graduate degree.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Techniques in Contemporary Literature
description: The study, from the point of view of the creative writer, of works written within the last 25 years. (B) techniques in fiction; (C) techniques in poetry; (D) techniques in creative nonfiction. Repeatable one time in each ENG graduate degree.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Literary Criticism
description: Intensive study of selected topics in literary theory and its practical application; topics to be announced. Repeatable two times.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in English Literature
description: Study of authors or a period. (C) re-reading Chaucer; (N) 14th century poetry; (P) extended Victorian lyric; (Q) modern British fiction; (R) early 17th century poetry; (S) dominant Victorians: the 1840s; (T) Baroque and English literature; (U) literature and social change; (X) literature and history; (Y) studies in satire. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in American Literature
description: Study of authors or a period. (B) American modernism; (C) race in American literature; (D) 19th century American poetry; (E) American literature naturalism; (F) African American literature and theory; (G) American transcendentalism; (H) 19th century American novel; (J) contemporary American poetry; (N) poetry by 20th century American women; (P) women writers and multiculturalism; (Q) Asian American literature and theory; (R) relocating American literature; (S) early American literature; (T) H. Melville and T. Morrison. Repeatable one time for different alphas.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Major Author
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American. (C) George Eliot; (D) Emily Dickinson; (M) Milton; (S) Chaucer and his backgrounds; (T) Austen; (U) Yeats and his circle; (X) Beowulf; (Y) Faulkner’s narrative; (Z) Virginia Woolf. Repeatable one time for different alphas. A-F only.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Shakespeare
description: Intensive study of Shakespeare.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Literary Genres
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American literature. (C) neoclassicism; (D) tragedy; (E) modern American short story; (F) sonnet and sonnet sequences; (G) Rest., 18th century dramatic comedy; (H) 18th century literature and art; (I) medieval drama; (J) narrative theory and criticism; (K) reinventing the author; (M) laughter and the comic arts; (N) nature of romance; (O) Victorian novel; (P) Jacobean drama; (Q) science fiction; (R) essay, past and present; (S) Eng. hymn in Western culture; (W) 18th century British women novelists; (Y) English romanticism; (Z) English novel and criticism. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Film Theory and Criticism
description: Classic theories of representation and aesthetics; modern and contemporary cultural, psychoanalytic, and aesthetic theories as they apply to film.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Life Writing
description: Intensive study of critical and theoretical issues raised by various forms of life writing (biography, autobiography, oral history, diaries, etc.) and of their history and methodology. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Cultural Studies in Asia/ Pacific
description: Intensive study of selected issues in cultural studies in Asia and the Pacific; topics to be announced. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Pacific Literatures
description: Intensive study of selected issues in the literatures of the Pacific in English, or translated into English. Topics to be announced. Repeatable one time. (Spring only)

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Literatures of Hawai‘i
description: Introduction to comparative literature; relationship of Hawaiian to other literatures; sources and influences. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Hawaiian Literature
description: Intensive study of selected issues, genres, and traditions in Hawaiian literature written in English or translated from Hawaiian into English. Repeatable one time. (Fall only)

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Cultural Studies
description: Intensive study of selected issues in cultural studies and cultural and social theory; topics to be announced. Repeatable one time.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Comparative Literature
description: Introduction to comparative literature; relationship of English to other literatures; sources and influences. (B) African lit. and literary theory; (F) folklore and literature; (G) theory/practice of poetry; (H) contemporary drama; (I) mythic method; (J) postmodern fiction; (M) modernism; (N) colonial/ postcolonial; (P) postmodernism and postcolonialism; (W) medieval women writers. Repeatable one time for different alphas.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Special Topics
description: Content to be announced. Repeatable five times.

subject: ENG
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable nine times.

subject: ESL
title: Composition I for Second Language Writers
description: FW Extensive practice in writing expository essays; linguistic devices that make an essay effective. (Fulfills composition requirement for nonnative speakers of English only.)

subject: ELI
title: Intermediate Academic Listening and Speaking
description: Introduction to the academic English language listening/speaking demands required at the university. Instruction and practice of effective note-taking skills, listening strategies, delivery of presentations, and participation in academic discussions. Designed as a bridge to ELI 080. CR/ NC only.

subject: ELI
title: Intermediate Academic Literacy
description: Introduction to the academic English-language literacy demands required at the university. Extensive practice in academic reading, writing, and vocabulary development. Designed as a bridge to advanced-level ELI courses in reading and writing. CR/NC only.

subject: ELI
title: Advanced Academic Listening and Speaking
description: Further development of the academic English-language listening/speaking skills and strategies required at the university. Instruction and practice of effective note-taking skills, critical listening strategies, delivery of effective academic presentations and leading of academic discussions.

subject: ELI
title: Advanced Academic Reading
description: Further development of skills and strategies for dealing with the high demands of academic reading by focusing on becoming efficient and autonomous readers. Instruction and practice of developing critical reading strategies and building field-specific vocabulary. CR/NC only.

subject: ELI
title: Advanced Academic Writing for Graduate Students
description: Introduction to academic writing conventions common at the graduate level. Students explore academic writing in their disciplines, develop clarity of written expression, and improve command over textual, rhetorical, and discursive conventions common in academic writing.

subject: ELI
title: Practicum for International Teaching Assistants
description: Extensive practice for international teaching assistants in speaking in classroom situations with emphasis on oral skills, American cultural expectations and classroom management. CR/NC only.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: DS Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: DS Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, Gender in Popular Culture
description: DS Contemporary issues of race, class, and gender in popula

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course. (Cross-listed as THEA 336)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description: DS. An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change. (Cross-listed as GEO 356)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Buddhist Philosophy
description: DH. Survey of central thinkers and schools. (Cross-listed as PHIL 360)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
description: DL. Survey in English traditional and modern literatures of Southeast Asia. A-F only. (Cross-listed as IP 361)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: DL. A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film. (Crosslisted as EALL 364 and WGSS 346)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course, or consent
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Field Study in Asia
description: Students may submit proposals to have academic course work, field research, or work experience in Asia. See specific center for guidelines and procedures. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other. Repeatable one time. A-F only for (C), (I), (J), (S), and (Z).
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Modern Philippines
description: DH. Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic. (Cross-listed as HIST 406)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawai‘i
description: DH. History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as PACE 407)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 410)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
description: DH. Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies. A-F only. (Alt. years)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
description: DS. Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GEO 413)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Korean Cinema
description: DH. Develop an understanding of Korean culture and society through visual, narrative, and contextual analysis of Korean films. Topics include post-Korean War experience, compressed modernity, authoritarianism, and postauthoritarian transformation. Special attention to independent films. A-F only.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Contested Issues Korea and Japan
description: DH. In-depth understanding of Korean-Japanese relations in the past and present by examining conflicting views and interpretations by Japanese, Korean, and Western scholars on important issues that divide the people of East Asia. A-F only.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
description: DS. Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning. (Cross-listed as PLAN 438)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape. (Cross-listed as PLAN 449)
prerequisites: 310 or PLAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
description: DH. Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania. (Cross-listed as ANTH 461)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Contested Issues in Contemporary Japan
description: DS. Familiarizes students with public discourse in Japan by analyzing key current issues widely debated in the Japanese media and in public forums in light of their political, historical, cultural, social and economic contexts. A-F only. Previous course work related to Japan or Asia will be helpful.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
description: DS. Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g., with class, religion, ethnicity). (Cross-listed as WGSS 463)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: K-pop and J-pop: Korean and Japanese Popular Music and Society
description: Examines modern Japan and South Korea through popular music. Examines genres from early popular music, today’s K-pop and J-pop music. A-F only. (Summer only)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Japan Cool: Anime, Manga, and Film
description: DH. Focus on Japanese anime, manga, and films with an emphasis on oral communication. What can one learn about Japanese issues of gender, national identity, and race? A-F only. (Summer only)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Transpacific Youth Pop Culture: From K-pop to Tiktok
description: DH. Examines ties between East Asian and Asian American digital media, including comics, movies, TV shows, music, and video games, to examine the dreams, fears, and aspirations of young Asians and Asian Americans. A-F only (Summer only)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Contemporary Asian Cinema
description: DH. Acquaint students with significant films from the major countries in Asia and how these films reflect and comment on profound social, political, and historical changes that have occurred in recent decades.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture–Chinese Diaspora
description: DH. Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term. Repeatable one time with consent. (Cross-listed as EALL 473)
prerequisites: one DH or DL course or consent
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
description: DH. Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism. (Cross-listed as EALL 474)
prerequisites: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Music Cultures: India
description: Approaches the cultural study of music and performance through a specific focus on South Asia. (Cross-listed as MUS 478H)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: consent
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Culture and Economy of Southeast Asia
description: DH. An exploration of the cultural and economic development of the countries of Southeast Asia from early times to the present day, with an emphasis on the effects of outside influences.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Film, Culture, and Modernity in Southeast Asia
description: DH. Examines interplay between tradition and modernity; religion and secularism; individual and collective; youth, wisdom, and the world; and role of gender identification/community response as they find articulation in medium of film across Southeast Asia. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Asia Through Fiction
description: DH. Explores core values and cultural principles of the four major Asian region as represented in major works of fiction from those regions. (Spring only)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Imperialism, Colonialism, and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
description: DH. Theoretical and historical analysis of a global, nineteenth, and twentieth century phenomenon using an interdisciplinary approach organized around lectures, readings, and discussions. (Fall only)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Political Violence in Modern Southeast Asia
description: Why do Southeast Asian governments and political movements engage in mass killings? How do their perpetrators justify these atrocities? How do survivors deal with their trauma and get their voices heard? A-F only. (Fall only)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Chinese Development
description: DS. Development and planning in contemporary China: economic policy and institutional structure in the development and urbanization process; urban and rural transformation in a socialist economy.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Asian Studies
description: DS. Selected topics in Asian studies. (C) China; (G) Asia; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other. Each alpha is repeatable two times.
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Women and Revolution
description: DH. Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons. (Cross-listed as HIST 492 and WGSS 492)
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ASAN
title: Food, Culture, and Politics in Asia
description: DH. Examines...
college: School of Pacific and Asian Studies

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
description: Digital image representation, intensity transformations, spatial filtering, filtering in the frequency domain, image restoration, color spaces and transformations, the fast wavelet transform, image compression.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Optimization
description: Application of linear, nonlinear and integer optimization models and algorithms to communications, control, signal processing, computer networking, financial engineering, manufacturing, production and distribution systems. CE, ECE, ME, or CBA majors only. (Alt. years)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: DY. Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems. (Cross-listed as BE 420 and MBBE 422)
prerequisites: (ECE 160, ECE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Instrumentation Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 422.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computer-Aided Analysis and Design
description: Algorithms and techniques used in computer-aided analysis and design of electronic circuits. Circuit simulation with interactive computers.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Electronic Instrumentation II
description: DP. Instrumentation systems and circuits for measurement, control, signal processing, transmission, and detection. Noise and interference, ADC/DAC, modulation demodulation, high-frequency and high-speed techniques, IC applications.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Si IC and Solid State Devices
description: DP. State of the art Si-based devices including advanced bipolar and MOS devices, heterojunction devices, new device trends. Topics from the most current literature included.
prerequisites: ECE 327 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A, or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computer-Aided Circuit Design
description: DP. Application of the computer to the analysis, design, simulation, and construction of analog and digital circuits.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Electric Power Systems
description: Design/operation of “the grid.” History of electric power systems, three-phrase power, real and reactive power, transformers, transmission, distribution, circuit analysis, protection, load flow, load frequency control, optimal power flow, and renewable energy integration. (Fall only)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Renewable Energy
description: DP. Fundamentals of power, electric power grid and conventional electricity generation. Wind and solar power systems. Photovoltaic materials and systems. Distributed generation and energy storage. ENGR majors only. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: ECE 213 or consent. Junior standing or higher.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Digital Communications
description: Baseband transmission, intersymbol interference and pulse shaping, partial response signaling, equalization, bandpass modulation and demodulation, channel coding, synchronization, multiplexing and multiple access, spread spectrum techniques.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Foundation for algorithms, practice, and theory behind common machine-learning applications. Includes projects, statistical programming, and an introduction to the unique challenges of high-dimensional problems. ECE, CENG, CEE, ME, MATH, ICS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Information Theory and Coding
description: Models of communication systems. Channel noise, measurement, and coding of information. Intrinsic limits of performance of communication systems.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: ISO Reference Model. Physical Layer, Data Link Layer, Network Layer and Transport Layer protocols. Wired and wireless local-area networks. Structure and operation of the Internet including routing, congestion control and flow control.
prerequisites: ECE 315 and one of ECE 342, or MATH 371 or MATH 471; or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Digital Control Systems
description: Sampling/reconstruction, Z-transform, DT transfer function. Reachability/observability. State and output feedback, observer design, input-output models, diophantine equations. Implementation procedures.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Modern Control Theory
description: Analysis and synthesis of nonlinear control systems by means of Lagrange’s equation, state space techniques, maximum principle. Lyapunov’s theorems, the phase plane, and Z-transform techniques. Optimization and adaptation by means of gradient methods, calculus of variations, dynamic programming.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Design of Intelligent Robots
description: DP. Study of the design principles of computer-controlled, intelligent robots such as roving vehicles, hand-eye systems.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computer Architecture
description: Structure of stored program machines, data flow machines, pipelining, fault-tolerant computing, instruction set design, effects of compilation on architecture, RISC vs. CISC architecture, uses of parallelism.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Object-oriented Software Engineering
description: Introduction to advanced techniques for designing, implementing, and testing computer software with a particular focus on using object-oriented design, analysis, and programming to produce high-quality computer programs that solve non-trivial problems. A-F only.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Operating Systems
description: Computer system organization; multiprocessor systems, memory hierarchies, assemblers, compilers, operating systems, virtual machine, memory management, processor management; information management. Emphasis on written communication through written assignments on relevant topics.
prerequisites: ECE 361 (or concurrent) and ECE 367 or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Wireless Data Networks
description: Mobile agent’s platforms and systems, mobile agent-based service implementation, middleware, and configuration, wireless local area networks, wireless protocols, network architecture supporting wireless applications, routing protocols in mobile and wireless networks, handoff in mobile and wireless networks.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Physical Optics
description: DP. Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics. (Cross-listed as PHYS 460)
prerequisites: ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-) or PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C), or consent.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
description: Introduction to computational methods used to simulate/solve engineering design problems focusing on electromagnetics. Finite difference, method of moments, and finite elements methods will be described; students will write computer programs in each. A-F only. BE, ECE, ENGR majors only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Microwave Engineering
description: DP. Passive and active microwave devices and circuits for RF and wireless applications. Scattering parameters, signal-flow graphs, and computer-aided design.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Antennas
description: DP. Electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and ionized media. Geomagnetic and solar effects on the ionosphere. Absorption and dispersion. Antenna arrays, apertures, horns, impedance. Design of antenna systems.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Optical Communications
description: DP. Principles and applications of optical fibers and waveguides. Fundamentals of optical communication systems (optical links, high-speed systems, wavelength-division-multiplexing networks, and network elements) and optical components (guided-wave circuits, lasers, detectors, and optical amplifiers). System and network integration issues. A-F only.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Fundamentals of Radar, Sonar, and Navigation Systems
description: DP. Discussion of basic radar detection and position- and velocity-measurement principles. Applications to various types of radar and sonar systems. Modern navigation aids.
prerequisites: ECE 371 (or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Biomedical and Clinical Engineering
description: Application of engineering principles and technology to biological and medical problems. Introduction to human anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, clinical measurements. Systems modeling, physiological control systems, computer applications, health-related problems.
prerequisites: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Measurement of bioelectrical signals, computer and electronic simulation of biological systems, design and evaluation of electronic circuits for biomedical measurements, evaluation of instruments for patient safety.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Bioelectric Phenomena
description: Study of electrical phenomena in living systems. Mechanisms underlying bioelectric activity. Membrane and transepithelial potentials, skin impedance, electrocardiography, neuroelectric signals, diagnostic considerations, laboratory demonstrations.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Instrumentation
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, applications, and design of biomedical instrumentation. Transducers, IC and microcomputer applications, patient safety.
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: ECE
title: Special Topics in Electrical
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

subject: FSHN
title: Microbiology of Foods
description: DB. Microorganisms encountered in foods; types of food spoilage; microbial hazards in food; methods of food preservation.
prerequisites: (MICR 130 and MICR 140L, or MICR 351 and MICR 351L) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Engineering
description: DP. Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as BE 411 and MBBE 411)
prerequisites: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: DP. Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prerequisites: (ECE 160, ECE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Chemistry
description: DP. Chemical properties of food constituents studied in relationship to their effects on processing, nutrition, and spoilage.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Chemistry Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical methods in the study of food constituents—proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, pigments, enzymes, etc.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Safety
description: DB. Discussion of potential microbiological, parasitic, chemical, and natural food hazards; food laws and standards; and related aspects of consumer protection.
prerequisites: (FSHN 181, BIOL 171, and CHEM 272) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Quality Control
description: Fundamental principles of quality control in the food industry: measurement of quality parameters, utilization and integration of the individual test procedures into grades and standards of quality, sampling, and reporting results.

subject: FSHN
title: Community Nutrition and Nutrition Education
description: (4 Lec) Concepts and methods of nutrition program planning and nutrition education; analysis of nutritional problems of local, national, and international communities; strategies used to educate groups or individuals. A-F only.
prerequisites: (FSHN 370 and either HDFS 380 or NREM 310) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Foundation of Childhood Obesity Prevention in the Pacific
description: Provide students with a basic overview of the causes and effects of childhood obesity, evidence-based approaches, community-based research, and policies to prevent childhood obesity as it relates to the Pacific region. (Summer only)
prerequisites: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

subject: FSHN
title: Childhood Anthropometric and Dietary Assessment Field Techniques
description: Teaches techniques for measuring anthropometry and collecting dietary intake in children. Online course imitates hands-on training through partnering with local organizations and the use of technology. Repeatable one time. (Summer only)
prerequisites: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

subject: FSHN
title: Child Health and Nutrition Monotiring
description: Covers topics related to health and nutritional status monitoring and surveillance, including epidemiology, biostatistics, health and nutrition surveillance systems, and the uses of technology for conducting these activities. Repeatable one time. (Summer only)
prerequisites: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

subject: FSHN
title: Culture and Child Health in the Pacific
description: In-depth study of Pacific culture, land, people, and history and its relationship to child health. Explores cultural competency, cultural safety, and multidisciplinary approaches to promote a healthy Pacific. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing. (Summer only)
prerequisites: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

subject: FSHN
title: Food Processing Operations
description: Principles and applications of food dehydration, thermal processing, low temperature preservation, chemical and biochemical preservation, irradiation, packaging, manufacturing, plant sanitation, water and waste management.

subject: FSHN
title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
description: DB. Development of dietary, anthropometric and clinical lab assessment skills measuring nutritional status. Understanding pathophysiology of disease processes, medical terminology and nutritional intervention, utilizing case studies. Dietetics majors only.
prerequisites: (FSHN 389 and FSHN 486) with a minimum grade of C or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
description: DB. Understanding of the pathophysiology of disease processes and nutritional intervention, using medical terminology and case studies. Dietetics majors only.
prerequisites: FSHN 467 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutrition Counseling Skills
description: Theory and practice in nutritional counseling. Combined lecture and discussion on nutrition/dietary counseling. Knowledge and theories. Application through lab experiences including role playing, case presentations, and performing actual counseling sessions. A-F only.

subject: FSHN
title: Applied Human Nutrition
description: DB. Application of basic nutrition principles; includes sources and functions of essential nutrients and food patterns compatible with nutrient needs, health, disease prevention, and sustainability. Intended for undergraduate and graduate students.
prerequisites: CHEM 161 (or higher) or BIOC 241 (or higher); PHYL 141, BIOL 171; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Cultural Aspects of Food Habits
description: Study of eating from behavioral perspectives. Implications for health practitioners and health education.
prerequisites: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher or SOC 100 or higher or PSY 100 or higher.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Analysis
description: Principles of sample preparation and chemical and physical analysis of food components using current methodology.
prerequisites: FSHN 430; and CHEM 162 or higher; and BIOL 402 or MBBE 402 or PEPS 402.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Analysis Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical and physical methods for the identification and quantitation of food components.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
description: DB. Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance. (Cross-listed as KRS 480)
prerequisites: (FSHN 185, and PHYL 103 or 141 or 301) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Biochemistry I
description: DB. Metabolism and biochemistry of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, cellular/molecular functions in human nutrition; integration of metabolic pathways; energy metabolism and balance, including relevance to chronic disease.
prerequisites: FSHN 185; PHYL 142/142L or PHYL 302/302L; BIOC 341 or higher (or concurrent) or MBBE 402 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Biochemistry II
description: DB. Metabolism and biochemistry of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, and cellular/ molecular functions in human nutrition; relevance to establishing nutrient requirements and to mechanisms of chronic disease.
prerequisites: FSHN 485 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Obesity, Science, and Issues
description: In-depth study of obesity, including research, etiology, treatment, and prevention.
prerequisites: FSHN 485 with a minimum grade of C.

subject: FSHN
title: Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems, or laboratory experiments. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: FSHN
title: Field Experience
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ANSC 492)

subject: FSHN
title: Food Science Capstone
description: Field practicum designed to integrate knowledge from previous FSHN courses to develop novel and innovative food products. Students deal with shelflife, marketing, packaging, labeling, sensory evaluation, and quality assurance. Repeatable one time. FSHN majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: (FSHN 381 and FSHN 460) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: FSHN
title: The Science of Food Systems
description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ANSC 601)

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Food Science I
description: Advanced topics in chemical and physical characteristics of foods as well as their role in human nutrition. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as MBBE 607)
prerequisites: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Food Science II
description: Advances in sensory quality and evaluation, deterioration of foods and food safety, as well as food processing technology. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Food Safety
description: Real and perceived food hazards, their ethical issues and imp

subject: DIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Directed reading and/or research. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: DIS
title: Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. Repeatable one time. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as EDCS 780 and LTEC 780)

subject: EPET
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ME 201)

subject: EPET
title: Space Science and Instrumentation
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation. A-F only. (Fall only) (crosslisted as ME 301)
prerequisites: EPET 201, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272

subject: EPET
title: Introduction to Human Spaceflight
description: Effects of spaceflight conditions on human physiology and psychology. Astronaut selection, training, crew composition. Ethics of space exploration. Politics & sociology of public and private human space flight. Selection of capstone project. Significant written communication. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: EPET
title: Space Mission Design
description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ME 400)

subject: EPET
title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ME 401)

subject: EPET
title: Human Spaceflight Mission Elements
description: Engineering aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, and budgets for human spaceflight missions. Design of environmental control and life support systems. Capstone project design. Significant oral and written communication. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip. (Cross-listed as SUST 101)

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on study of minerals, rocks, and topographic maps. Examine volcanism, hydrology, coastal processes and hazards, geologic time and earthquakes. Field trips to investigate landslides, beaches and O‘ahu geology. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 113)

subject: ERTH
title: Geology of the Hawaiian Islands
description: Hawaiian geology and geologic processes: origin of Hawaiian islands, volcanism, rocks and minerals, landforms, stream and coastal processes, landslides, earthquakes and tsunamis, groundwater, geologic and environmental hazards. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Volcanoes in the Sea
description: Lecture with field trips covering the manner in which geological conditions, resources, and events have affected past and present circum-Pacific societies.

subject: ERTH
title: Voyage through the Solar System
description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip. (Cross-listed as ASTR 150)

subject: ERTH
title: Humans and the Environment
description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 116)

subject: ERTH
title: Solar System Studio
description: Explore the wonders of the Solar System through hands-on experience of science. Will study satellite images, evaluate planetary surface observations, analyze data of objects in our Solar System, conduct experiments, and communicate their findings. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Volcanoes
description: Examines the origin and classification of volcanoes, volcanic eruptions, and volcanic deposits. Includes the history of volcanic studies, myths, and legends. Emphasis on volcanic eruptions, eruptive products, volcanic hazards, and risk management. (Spring only)

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Hazards
description: Introductory course covering the causes of, and effects from, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, landslides, rockfalls, and other natural geologic phenomena. Open to non-majors. Field trips. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters and Human History
description: Examines how natural hazards have affected the course of human culture and societies from pre-history to the present in Hawai‘i/Oceania, Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ATMO 150 and OCN 150)
prerequisites: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X)

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Geology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Structure, composition and evolution of Earth; processes responsible for formation, deformation and transformation of rocks; plate tectonics. Emphasis on quantitative methods, problem solving and critical thinking to geology. Laboratory and field trips required.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Directed Research
description: Lower division reading and research in any area of ERTH under the direction of a faculty member. Repeatable four times or up to six credits. CR/NC only.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Inquiry
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Origin and age of the solar system and earth: interior of the earth; plate tectonics and records of biological evolution and past environments. Development of critical thinking and writing skills. ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors.
prerequisites: ERTH 101L and one of ERTH 101, ERTH 103, ERTH 104, ERTH 106, or ERTH 130; or consent. ERTH 101L may be taken concurrently.

subject: ERTH
title: Climate Change
description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors. (Fall only)
prerequisites: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102, or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Scientific Programming
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to solving scientific problems by computer programming. Overview of the MatLab programming language and environment. Emphasis placed on good style, logical reasoning, and applied mathematics.

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Volcanology
description: Volcanic eruptions and their consequences. Includes models for volcanic eruptions including explosive eruptions and lava flows, monitoring of active volcanoes, evaluation and impacts of volcanic hazards, and mitigation of volcanic risk. Field trips. Normally fall. ERTH and GEOL majors or consent.
prerequisites: (ERTH 200 or ERTH 201) with a minimum grade of B+ or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Mineralogy
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the chemistry, crystalline structure, geologic occurrence, and physical properties of minerals. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
prerequisites: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 and (CHEM 162/162L or CHEM 171/171L) or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Igneous Petrology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Survey of composition, classification, and occurrence of igneous rocks. Hand-specimen identification and optical petrography of igneous rocks. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Hazards & Geomechanics
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Dynamic behavior of Earth’s surface, physical processes driving geohazards, and the risks pposed to society. Theory, practical techniques, and data visualization to measure, analyze, and interpret hazards and implications.
prerequisites: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 130, MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A, and PHYS 151 or PHYS 170; or consent

subject: HIST
title: The Samurai of Japan
description: A social, military, and cultural history of Japan’s samurai (warrior) class.

subject: HIST
title: History of Premodern Korea
description: Survey of political, economic, social, and cultural developments from earliest times to 1400. Ethical issues in nationhood, central hegemony, myth-making, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

subject: HIST
title: History of Modern Korea
description: Continuation of 327. From 1400 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of North Korea
description: History of North Korea in terms of industrialism, militarism, nationalism, and state power, from 1945 to today. Focus on construction of national sovereign identity and comparison with postcolonial world.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece I
description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Minoan, Mycenean, and Archaic periods.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece II
description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Classical and Hellenistic periods.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Rome: The Republic
description: Political, social, cultural history from the Etruscans to Augustus. Emphasis on discussion of literary and archaeological materials. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Rome: The Empire
description: Political, social, and cultural history from Augustus to 476 A.D. Emphasis on literary and archaeological materials. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: Early Medieval Europe 300–1050
description: Formation of European societies in relation to Byzantine and Islamic cultures. Writing exercises develop historical thinking and the analysis of primary sources through workshops with peer and instructor feedback on drafts and revisions.

subject: HIST
title: Medieval Europe 1050–1350
description: Main trends in European economy, society, religion, politics, thought, and the arts; interactions with Byzantine and Islamic worlds.

subject: HIST
title: European Intellectual History
description: Undergraduate seminar on great debates in Western thought. Discussion of primary source materials; the scientific revolution and Enlightenment.

subject: HIST
title: European Intellectual History
description: Continuation of 337. European thought from French Revolution to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Renaissance and Reformation
description: Political, social, cultural, and intellectual developments in Europe from 1300 to 1600. Emphasis on cultural and intellectual history and its impact on social and political developments; humanism and its influence on thought and reforming movements, Protestant and Catholic Reformations. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: Comparative Economic History
description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions. (Cross-listed as ECON 341)

subject: HIST
title: The History of Economic Thought
description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ECON 342)

subject: HIST
title: Reacting to the Past
description: Exploration of moments of crisis and the clash of ideas in their historical context through the use of simulation games. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Germany
description: Political, social, economic, and cultural history since 1547. Rise of Austria and Prussia, unification, Bismarckian era, World War I and Weimar Republic, Hitler’s Third Reich, post-World War II.

subject: HIST
title: France in the Old Regime
description: Major social, political, and intellectual developments: Renaissance, Reformation, religious wars, Richelieu, Louis XIV, Enlightenment, and Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Modern France
description: Political, social, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments in France from Revolution and Napoleon to the present. Assignments emphasize engagement with course concepts through oral communication and individual and group presentation.

subject: HIST
title: Tudor-Stuart Britain
description: Traces major developments in British politics, society, and culture between the late Medieval and Modern Eras.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Britain 1688-1945
description: Interaction of 17th-, 18th-, and 19th-century intellectual, political, economic, and social changes, which together produced the British Empire and modern Britain.

subject: HIST
title: British Empire
description: Origins and expansion of the British empire between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries. Includes imperial policies affecting Britain, Australia, India, Ireland, and Southern Africa. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Iberia in Asia and the Pacific
description: Comparative exploration of the Iberian empires–Spain and Portugal–and their political, economic, and cultural interactions with indigenous societies in Asia and the Pacific. A-F only.

subject: HIST
title: France and Empire
description: Lecture/discussion exploring the history of France’s relationship with imperialism from the Renaissance to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to Islamic History
description: Muhammad, the Arab conquests, the Caliphate; fundamentals of Islam; classical Islamic civilization; development of Islam into modern times with emphasis on the Middle Eastern heartland.

subject: HIST
title: The Making of the Modern Middle East
description: Survey of developments that created the system of nation-states in the Middle East. History of the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Turkey; Egypt; the Arab world; Israel and Iran.

subject: HIST
title: Survey of African History
description: The history of Africa from earliest times to the present: the rise of indigenous civilizations, European and Muslim impact, colonialism and nationalism, and current issues.

subject: HIST
title: The World of Mekong
description: Historical survey, from BC period to present, of the peoples of the Mekong region, an area covering southwestern China, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and southern Vietnam. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women. (Cross-listed as AMST 316 and WGSS 311)

subject: HIST
title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. (Once a year) (Crosslisted as CLAS 362)

subject: HIST
title: Women in Oceania
description: Uses research and writing to explore historical processes that have impacted the lives of Indigenous women in Oceania and women’s engagements with those processes over time, with a focus on women’s voices, agency, and empowerment.

subject: HIST
title: Global History of Sport
description: Explores the relationship between sport and society in historical perspective. Analyzes global processes of imperialism, nationalism, globalization, and international relations, and studies themes such as the politics of race, class, and gender.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Foreign Relations to 1898
description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from initial encounters between Europeans and Native Americans through the 1890s.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Foreign Relations From 1898
description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from the wars of 1898 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship within the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of the 19th century. (Cross-listed as AMST 343)

subject: HIST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: Continuation of 373: the 20th century. (Cross-listed as AMST 344)

subject: HIST
title: History of American Business
description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development. (Cross-listed as MGT 348)

subject: HIST
title: American Empire
description: Examines the interplay between an “American culture of empire” and the rise of the U.S. as a superpower. Topics: imperialism and political culture, social movements and international affairs, race, gender and class relations. (Cross-listed as AMST 365)

subject: HIST
title: Caribbean History
description: Survey of the history of the Caribbean region from 1500 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: The Asia-Pacific War
description: Explores WWII in the Asia-Pacific region, focusing on the intersection of the grand strategy, military operations, and war crimes. Involves source analyses and discussions.

subject: HIST
title: History of Warfare to 1850
description: Classical and guerrilla warfare, revolution, and military systems and institutions.

subject: HIST
title: War and Peace Since 1850
description: Continuation of 391, from 1850 to present.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Military History
