description: Survey of development of American military forces from War of Independence to war in Vietnam.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science to 1700
description: Evolution of scientific thought and its cultural context. Antiquity to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science Since 1700
description: Continuation of 394; science, technology, and society since 1700.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Historical Theories and Methods
description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

subject: HIST
title: Digital History in the Global Village
description: History of the digital age in global perspective connecting people, media, and technology

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics–Solid, Fluid, and Wave Mechanics
description: Continuum mechanics in geophysics, as applied to the deformation of Earth materials (elastic, viscous, viscoelastic, and plastic deformations) and seismic wave propagation (body waves, surface waves, anisotropy, and attenuation). (Fall only)
prerequisites: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent).

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics–Gravity, Magnetics, and Heat Transfer
description: Fundamental theory and practical applications of the use of gravity, magnetics, and heat conduction to probing the structure of the Earth; heat transfer via mantle convection is a major control on Earth’s internal structure. (Spring only)
prerequisites: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent).

subject: ERTH
title: Seismology
description: Elasticity, wave equations, body waves, surface waves, free oscillations, seismometry, seismogram interpretation, tectonics, inversion, source theory, and waveform modeling.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth System Science and Global Change
description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmospheric-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as OCN 638)
prerequisites: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Stable Isotope Biogeochemistry
description: Stable isotope geochemistry applied to questions of biogeochemical cycling in the oceans, sediment diagenesis, paleoceanography, environmental geochemistry and ecology. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geochemistry
description: Geochemistry at the land-ocean interface: coastal hydrology, subterranean estuaries and coastal mixing and their importance in governing the distribution of selected radiotracers, trace metals and nutrients. Combined lecture-lab with field trips and group projects. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: CHEM 162, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 641)

subject: ERTH
title: Elemental Composition Changes
description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 642)

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 644)
prerequisites: CHEM 171, or CHEM 161 and CHEM 162; PHYS 152; and MATH 242 or MATH 252A; and consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Geomagnetism and Cosmic Magnetism
description: Magnetic fields of Earth, planets, stars, and galaxies; dynamo theories; paleomagnetism; terrestrial and lunar rock magnetism; planetary, regional, and local geomagnetic sounding. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater Contamination
description: Principles of groundwater chemistry; chemical evolution in natural groundwater flow systems; sources of contamination; mass transport processes; hydrochemical behavior of contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CEE 623)

subject: ERTH
title: Astrochemistry–A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ASTR 657 and CHEM 657)

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary Surfaces
description: Comparative geology of terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, geomorphology; remote sensing; manned and unmanned space exploration. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Cosmochemistry
description: Formation and evolution of planets as astrophysical objects, geologic bodies, and abodes of life; current understanding from studies of the Solar System, star formation, meteorites, exoplanets; theory of formation and dynamics; atmospheres, oceans, habitability, biosignatures. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: (Alpha) Remote Sensing
description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

subject: ERTH
title: Seminar in Tectonics
description: Evolution of ocean basins, margins, foldbelts, and platforms, from plate tectonics and regional syntheses of structure, petrology, geophysics, and stratigraphy. Repeatable eight times. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: (Alpha) Extraterrestrial Material
description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

subject: ERTH
title: Paleoceanography
description: Study of the paleoceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere and biosphere. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 674)

subject: ERTH
title: The Generic Mapping Tools
description: Introduction to the Generic Mapping Tools (GMT). Processing of scientific data and the automated preparation of maps and illustrations using GMT on UNIX workstations, with introduction to UNIX and the C shell environment.

subject: ERTH
title: Data Exploration and Processing
description: Time- and frequency analysis, filtering, factor and cluster analysis, interpolation, quantitative map analysis, and introduction to wavelets and fractals.

subject: ERTH
title: Bayesian Data Analysis
description: Linear and nonlinear techniques for model selection, parameter estimation, simulation and forecasting, from Bayesian principles with particular attention to large data sets and sparse noisy data. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: ERTH
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ERTH
title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
description: Interpretation of geophysical and laboratory data to understand elastic and anelastic properties, composition, phase relationships, temperature distribution in the Earth. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Fractures and Faults
description: Lecture on elasticity theory, fracture mechanics and boundary element modeling, with application to faults and fractures in the Earth.

subject: ERTH
title: Selected Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
description: Content to be announced. Repeatable eight times.

subject: ERTH
title: Special Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
description: Content to be announced. Repeatable eight times.

subject: ERTH
title: MGeo Seminar
description: Seminar to improve student awareness of trends and practices in geoscience professions, and develop ability to prepare, deliver, and evaluate a professional scientific presentation. Targets abstract writing, oral presentation, and technical criticism. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: ERTH
title: MGeo Professional Project
description: Practical hands-on professional experience, typically with a local company or agency, and involving a final written report and an oral presentation. A grade of credit is assigned when the internship presentations are satisfactorily completed. Repeatable up to six credits. MGEO majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: ERTH
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: EALL
title: Writing East Asia
description: FW An introduction to writing analytically and cross-culturally about East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) and various aspects of East Asian culture. (Fall only)

subject: EALL
title: Introduction to Chinese Language and Culture
description: DH Provides students with interesting perspectives on and some general knowledge of Chinese language, literature, and culture.

subject: EALL
title: Japanese Literature in Translation– Traditional
description: DL Survey of all major forms from the earliest era to mid-19th century.

subject: EALL
title: Japanese Literature in Translation– Modern
description: DL Survey from mid-19th century to present; emphasis on fiction.

subject: EALL
title: Survey of Japanese Literature–KIC
description: DL Survey of traditional and modern Japanese literature in translation, covering all major genres. Only offered at Konan University in Japan. Not open to students with 271 or 272.

subject: EALL
title: Korean Literature in Translation– Traditional
description: DL Survey of Korean literature from earliest times with emphasis on development and cultural context; all readings in English translation. Students write essays about the readings.

subject: EALL
title: Korean Literature in Translation– Modern
description: DL Survey of 20th-century Korean literature with emphasis on development and cultural context; all readings in English translation. Students write essays about th

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Aquatic Medicine
description: Identification, extraction and preparation of complexes of aquatic herbs to formulate a healing combination to contribute to maintaining overall health. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: HWST
title: Senior Seminar in Hawaiian Studies
description: Critical examination of existing research; individual or team development, execution, and evaluation of selected projects. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: senior major in Hawaiian studies or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Senior Capstone Project in Hawaiian Studies
description: Capstone seminar designed to provide a culminating academic experience through in-depth examination, analysis, articulation, and projects relevant to a HWST area of concentration. Repeatable one time. HWST majors only. Senior standing only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 341, 342, [343 or 390 or 490 (or concurrent)] and [207/SUST 217 or 285 or 307/SUST 317 or 356/SUST 356] and [222 or 224 or 225 or 372 or 478].

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Political Speech: Ha‘i ‘Ōlelo Ku‘e
description: Senior seminar in short, extemporaneous speeches in persuasive, passionate and dynamic styles of Native Hawaiian orators. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Modern Pacific Women’s Poetry
description: DL. Critical examination of modern indigenous women’s poetry from the Pacific Islands. Thematic concentration on land, family, sexual and national oppression.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kānāwai: Western Law and Hawai‘i
description: DH. The rise of Western law in Hawai‘i, its contribution to nation building and colonialism.

subject: HWST
title: Kānāwai II: Practical Application of Rights
description: Historical analysis of land use, race and self-determination; introduced to legal case briefing, analysis of legal precedent, practical impacts of rules and regulations and the sociopolitical factors that influence law and law enforcement. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading/research.

subject: HWST
title: Indigenous Research Methodologies
description: Reading seminar for developing a Native Hawaiian epistemology from sources in comparative indigenous thought. A-F only.
prerequisites: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Archival Research
description: Research seminar aimed at familiarizing students with the rich historical primary sources existent in various archives in Honolulu. A-F only.
prerequisites: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Review of Hawaiian Literature
description: Seminar in review of Hawaiian literature to understand the significance of secondary sources in Hawaiian subjects. This makes up part of the Hawaiian Studies graduate core. A-F only.
prerequisites: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Writing a Hawaiian Thesis
description: Seminar to help fashion student’s research and thesis proposal. To be taken by all HWST MA students as they begin designing their capstone project. Course will be team-taught by HWST faculty. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: ‘Ike Pono-Visual/Cultural Interpretations
description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that examines (from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint) colonial imaging; collecting and site of contestation; resilience and resistance; and re-righting. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 107, and one course from 220-225, and one course from 320-325; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: ‘Ike Maka-Visual/Cultural Knowledge
description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that carefully examines and develops critical consciousness–from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint–visual hegemony, rhetorical tropes; and representation–imag(in)ing and reimag(in)-ing. HWST majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: HWST
title: Pono Science: Ethical Implications of Science in Hawai‘i
description: Support student dialogue on the foundations of pono science. Through discussions and structured guidance, students will explore Hawaiian ethics, implications of research, and decolonizing methodology. Repeatable three times. Graduate students only.

subject: HWST
title: Mo‘olelo ‘Ōiwi: Historical Perspectives
description: Research seminar for developing interpretations of the past from Native Hawaiian and foreign world views with particular emphasis on understanding the meaning of culturally-based knowledge systems. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Mele Hawa‘i: Mele as Systems of Knowledge
description: Seminar on Mele Hawai‘i (Songs, Poetry, Chants) as systems of knowledge that record, communicate, and critique historical, political, environmental, and cultural information. Will include learning and analysis of mele, culminating with a research project.
prerequisites: HAW 302 and (HWST 478 or HAW 384 or HAW 484).

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Geography and Resource Management
description: Seminar in geography of Hawai‘i from a Native Hawaiian perspective that will enable the researcher to define and develop resource management methods consistent with Native Hawaiian understandings and traditions. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent).

subject: HWST
title: ‘Āina Waiwai: Water, Food Sovereignty, and Ancestral Abundance
description: Topical graduate seminar focuses on indigenous perspectives on water, food sovereignty, Hawaiian terrestrial and marine food production systems, and ancestral abundance. Seminar perspective to change each term. Repeatable two times.

subject: HWST
title: Kānāwai Lawai‘a: Hawa‘i’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance. (Alt. years: Fall) (Cross-listed as SUST 652)

subject: HWST
title: Historic Preservation Law
description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as LAW 503)

subject: HWST
title: He Ali‘i Ka ‘Āina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ‘Āina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ‘Āina future. (Cross-listed as SUST 659)

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kahiki: Comparative Hawaiian and Tahitian Cosmogonies
description: Seminar comparing Gods/myths from Ancient Tahiti by Teiura Henry (600 pages) with the six volumes of Hawaiian historians Kamakau and Malo. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kahiki: Pacific Life Narratives in Mixed Media and Literature
description: Research seminar in relevant literary traditions, histories of interaction, colonization, and literary politics in the Pacific region through the examination of life narratives in mixed media and literature. A-F only. HWST majors only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Indigenous Futurisms: Hawai ʻi, Polynesia, and Beyond
description: Seminar on Indigenous Futurisms as developed in Hawai ʻi, Polynesia, and other Indigenous contexts, and expressed through art, literature, film, music, and scholarship.

subject: HWST
title: Huaka‘i Huli Heiau Hawai‘inuiākea: Study Abroad on Polynesian Temples
description: Comparative study of Hawaiian/Polynesian temple design taught over a 3-week period in Hawai‘i and Polynesia. Travel costs to be paid by student. (Summer only)
prerequisites: 670 (with a minimum grade of B) and HAW 302 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Envisioning the Nation
description: A research seminar designed to provide an overview of community activism and Native Hawaiian empowerment in Hawai‘i in contexts that range from local to international, and to provide a foundation for further study and professional growth. A-F only.
prerequisites: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Sovereign Hawaiian State, Domestic Kingdom Law, Governance and Politics
description: Research seminar on the subject of domestic law, governance, and politics of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the historical relevance of this to the contemporary case for independent, sovereign state continuity under public international law. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: HWST
title: Practicum Research Plan B
description: Practicum for Plan B. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: HWST
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. (F) Full-time. S/U for (F) only. Repeatable up to six credits; Repeatable unlimited times for (F).

subject: HSSW
title: Southeast Asian Cultures in Health/ Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in Southeast and South Asian region.

subject: HSSW
title: Pacific Cultures in Health/Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in the Pacific region.

subject: FR
title: Intermediate French Abroad
description: Continuation of 258.

subject: FR
title: French Phonetics
description: Analysis of phonological system; methods of teaching pronunciation; understanding various types of spontaneous speech. Drills in pronunciation, intonation, stress, and rhythm.

subject: FR
title: Reading in French
description: Development of language skills through reading of cultural and literary texts.

subject: FR
title: Structure of French
description: Structure of contemporary French as analyzed by descriptive linguists.

subject: FR
title: Business French
description: Reading and writing commercial materials.

subject: FR
title: Conversation
description: Systematic practice for control of spoken French. Further development of vocabulary for accurate, mature expression.

subject: FR
title: Composition
description: Emphasis on strengthening facility with language through further training in syntax, structure, and composition writing.

subject: FR
title: Advanced Conversation
description: Systematic and advanced practice for control of spoken French, advanced development for accurate, mature expression.

subject: FR
title: Survey of French Literature
description: Major authors and movements.
prerequisites: 311 (or concurrent) and 312; only 311 may be concurrent.

subject: FR
title: Survey of French Literature
description: Continuation of 331.
prerequisites: 311 (or concurrent) and 312; only 311 may be concurrent.

subject: FR
title: Third-Level French Abroad
description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in French language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a French-speaking country.

subject: FR
title: Third-Level French Abroad
description: Continuation of 358.

subject: FR
title: Intensive Third-Level French Abroad
description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in French language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a French-speaking country.

subject: FR
title: Contemporary French Civilization
description: Survey of culture and institutions of modern France.

subject: FR
title: Survey of French Civilization
description: A historical survey of the development of French culture. The course is interdisciplinary, focusing on the relations between politics, literature, science, and the arts. A-F only.

subject: FR
title: Topics in French Literature
description: (B) French film; (C) the Fantastic; (D) Francophone literature. Repeatable two times with consent.

subject: FR
title: Directed Reading
description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: FR
title: Advanced Oral and Written Expression
description: Further development of listening, comprehension, speaking, and writing skills through viewing of French videotapes, reading French newspapers, frequent oral and written reports.
prerequisites: 311 and 312, or 306, or 358, or 360; or consent.

subject: FR
title: French-English Translation
description: Practice in techniques based on contrastive linguistics. Translation of texts from various fields from French into English and the reverse.

subject: FR
title: Masterpieces of Medieval Literature
description: Samplings from epic, novel, verse and prose, tale, lyric poetry, chronicle, theater, didactic literature. Elementary readings in original text in editions giving modern French translation.

subject: FR
title: Advanced Language Study: French
description: Advanced course in spoken and written French with intensive review of alternative grammatical structures and shades of meaning in the modern language. Graduates who have not taken prerequisites may request consent.

subject: FR
title: Masterpieces of 16th-Century Literature
description: Samplings from all major writers of the period. Readings in original text in editions giving modern French equivalents for difficult words.

subject: FR
title: Masterpieces of 17th-Century Literature
description: Principal works of major dramatists: Corneille, Moliere, Racine. Principal movements and major authors of non-dramatic prose and poetry.

subject: FR
title: 19th Century French Prose and Poetry
description: Study of representative prose and poetry of the major trends of 19th century France: romanticism, realism, symbolism, aestheticism.

subject: FR
title: 20th-Century French Theater
description: Major French playwrights and their works: Claudel, Giraudoux, Anouilh, Sartre, Camus, etc.

subject: FR
title: 20th Century French Prose and Poetry
description: Study of representative prose and poetry of the major trends of 20th century France: modernism, surrealism, existentialism, postmodernism and multiculturalism.

subject: FR
title: Fourth-Level French Abroad
description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the fourth-year level in French linguistics, civilization, culture, and literature in a French-speaking country.

subject: FR
title: Fourth-Level French Abroad
description: Continuation of 458.

subject: FR
title: Intensive Fourth-Level French Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourthyear level in French language, culture and literature in a French-speaking country. For semester programs only.

subject: FR
title: Seminar in French Literature
description: (B) French literature by period; (C) Francophone literature; (D) French film; (E) topic in French literature. Repeatable two time per alpha.

subject: FR
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: FR
title: French for Reading Proficiency
description: Reading of scholarly and technical French for graduate students; open to undergraduates with consent of department chair. Not applicable to undergraduate language requirement. Repeatable two times with consent. CR/NC only.

subject: FR
title: Seminar in 20th-Century French Literature
description: Authors and movements of modern period.

subject: FR
title: French Renaissance
description: Poetry, theater, prose. Emphasis on Montaigne and Rabelais. Lectures, discussions, reports.

subject: FR
title: Masterpieces of the 17th Century
description: Dramatic or prose works of the classical period.

subject: FR
title: Philosophic Currents in 18th Century
description: Philosophic movements and their impact on the social, political, and literary life of the period and the modern era.

subject: FR
title: Advanced French-English Translation: Practice and Theory
description: Advanced practice in translation into French and from French to English in various fields (literature, business, medicine, other), with reflection on choices. Readings in translation theory. Repeatable one time.

subject: FR
title: History of the French Language
description: Origins and development of French language in its cultural context. Contrastive analysis.

subject: FR
title: Seminar in Medieval Literature
description: Genesis and evolution of literary genres from the 12th to 15th centuries. Epic, romance, lyric poetry, prose, and drama.

subject: FR
title: Seminar: The Novel in France
description: Novels which have influenced movements or established techniques. Repeatable two times with consent.

subject: FR
title: The Theater in France
description: Historical development; major dramatists who have influenced movements or established techniques.

subject: FR
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: FR
title: Seminar in French Literature
description: Study of authors or a period. Repeatable two times with consent.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and French graduate advisor.

subject: GEO
title: The Natural Environment
description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards. (Cross-listed as SUST 102)

subject: GEO
title: The Natural Environment Lab
description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers. (Cross-listed as SUST 102L)

subject: GEO
title: World Regional Geography
description: World’s major cultural regions; geographic aspects of contemporary economic, social, political conditions.

subject: GEO
title: Digital Earth
description: Cartographic representation and meaning in a digital age. Earth models, map projections, coordinate systems, scale, distance, and direction. Data types and transformations in graphic and digital representation. Manual, automated, and web-based map making and analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Geography and Contemporary Society
description: Elements of economic geography and resource management, population and urban geography; application to current problems of developed and underdeveloped worlds.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Climatology
description: Elements and controls of climate. World patterns of insolation, temperature, evaporation, precipitation, atmospheric circulation. Climatic classifications.
prerequisites: 101 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 314)

subject: GEO
title: General Geomorphology
description: Introduction to geomorphological concepts,

subject: FDM
title: Specialty Market Design: Group Collection Development
description: Advanced study in the specialty market design, pattern making, and construction for fashion design majors. Different specialty designs, such as swimwear, menswear, or others, will be offered each semester. Repeatable five times. Recommended: 315, 330. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Textiles Quality Assurance
description: DP. Chemical nature and structure of fibers and fabrics, their properties and finishes. FDM majors only. A-F only. Co-requisite: 321L. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Textiles Quality Assurance Laboratory
description: DY. Examination of textile properties through standardized textiles testing laboratory equipment. FDM majors only. A-F only. Co-requisite: 321. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Advanced Apparel Design and Construction Techniques
description: Principles of advanced techniques for garment construction with emphasis on new, difficult-to-handle fabrics. Repeatable one time.

subject: FDM
title: 2D/3D Computer Aided Design
description: DA. Exploration of CAD applications from the design to the pattern-making process. Use of Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop for fashion illustration. Use of OptiTex PDS pattern design software featuring 2D and 3D CAD. Repeatable one time.

subject: FDM
title: 3D Retail Store Design
description: Visual merchandising concepts and planning; use of a virtual 3D store modeling software package. Visual Retailing/Mockshop, to design store interiors, fixtures, lighting, signage, window displays, and planograms. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Writing for the Fashion Industry
description: Analysis and creation of different types of writing in the fashion industry, with emphasis on creating a professional writing style. A-F only.

subject: FDM
title: Branding
description: Study of principles and practices in brand architecture and effective brand-building strategies; analysis of a case study and application of the concepts of brand management. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Retail Buying and Merchandising
description: Theories and procedures in selecting, buying and selling apparel and textiles. Types of merchandising organizations, analysis of consumer demand, brick-and-click opportunities and challenges, development of an image, operation location, store and floor layout. FDM majors only.

subject: FDM
title: Merchandise Planning and Control
description: Theories, problems, and procedures of financial and assortment planning and control of merchandise inventories. FDM majors and merchandising minors only.

subject: FDM
title: Product Lifecycle Management
description: Application of principles of apparel production management, including methods engineering (detail construction for ordering), story boards and color tables, production measurements, costing, and PLM computer applications. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: FDM
title: Runway Design Collection Studio
description: Development of runway collection. Topic includes: inspirational research, developing aesthetic design, sketching, draping, drafting, patternmaking, muslin proofs, fittings, garment construction, and portfolio. FDM 420 enrollment required to showcase a collection in an annual fashion show. Repeatable three times. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Fashion Show Production
description: Application of principles and procedures related to the promotion of fashion apparel. Preparation and presentation of fashion information through shows, displays, media, and written communications. Repeatable one time. (Spring only)

subject: FDM
title: Entrepreneurship in Retail
description: Application of principles, procedures and techniques of organizing a small retail business in a brick-and-click world. Students develop, write, and evaluate business plans creatively using low and high tech resources and oral communication skills. Junior standing or higher. FDM majors only; open to non-majors with instructor’s consent.
prerequisites: Pre: one FS or FQ course, or consent.

subject: FDM
title: Costume Museum Management
description: Investigation of skills and techniques needed for handling textile and apparel artifacts in museums and other collections. Active involvement in documenting, researching, interpreting, and exhibiting costumes and textiles. Involves written work and oral presentations. Repeatable one time. FDM majors only. A-F only.

subject: FDM
title: International Apparel Trade Issues
description: Theories, concepts, problems of international trade of textile and apparel products. Issues of importing and exporting apparel products globally. Social, economic, and ethical factors affecting textile and apparel trade.

subject: FDM
title: Topics in Fashion
description: Study and discussion of special topics, problems. Offered by staff and visiting faculty. Repeatable five times.

subject: FDM
title: Internship
description: Examination of issues and opportunities associated with careers in fashion and related businesses and industries. Topics include interpersonal skills development, job search and interview strategies, and ethical issues in the workplace. FDM majors only. A-F only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: FDM
title: Capstone Portfolio
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Includes extensive instruction in writing and communication.

subject: FDM
title: Field Study in the Fashion Industry
description: Study tours to various centers of the world to examine historical and modern apparel and textiles. Merchandising and design methods and operations examined. Repeatable up to 12 credits.

subject: FDM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable up to 15 credits.

subject: FIL
title: Beginning Filipino
description: HSL. Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Beginning Filipino
description: HSL. Continuation of 101.

subject: FIL
title: Intermediate Filipino
description: HSL. Continuation of 102. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Intermediate Filipino
description: HSL. Continuation of 201.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino for Education
description: HSL. Continuation of 102. Lessons focus on various aspects of Philippine culture and specialized topics that cater to the needs of teachers intending to teach Filipino immigrant students or teach Filipino as a second language. Meets five hours a week; daily lab work.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino for Education
description: HSL. Continuation of 202 or 224.

subject: FIL
title: Third-Level Filipino I
description: Conversation, advanced reading and composition on traditional culture and indigenous knowledge. Includes emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Third-Level Filipino II
description: Conversation, advanced reading, and composition on contemporary issues. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Aural Comprehension
description: Training in comprehension of spoken authentic/ simulated authentic materials presented in news broadcasts, songs, documentary narration, formal lectures, radio and television soap operas, etc.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Film: Art and History
description: DH. Study and analysis of Filipino films: its history, forms, development and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic context.

subject: FIL
title: Fourth-Level Filipino I
description: Advanced reading in traditional literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced oral communication and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Fourth-Level Filipino II
description: Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced conversation and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Advanced Filipino Aural Comprehension
description: DL. Continuation of 315. Training in comprehension and analysis/criticism of spoken authentic materials through films.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Translation Techniques
description: Techniques of bilingual translation: Filipino to English and English to Filipino. A-F only.

subject: FIL
title: Structure of Filipino
description: DH. Introduction to phonology, morphology, syntax.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Contemporary Literature
description: DL. Selected readings in poetry, short stories, and plays from early 1900s to present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Contemporary Literature: 1980s-Present
description: DL. Survey of literature from the 80s (1986) to the present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

subject: FIN
title: Personal Financial Planning
description: Focuses on principles and techniques for handling personal financial decisions, including: personal budgeting, obtaining credit, life and casualty insurance, buying a home, buying an automobile, savings and investments, and retirement planning.

subject: FIN
title: Problems of Business Finance
description: Application of financial principles to cases involving important financial decisions; emphasis on writing.

subject: FIN
title: Corporate Financial Management
description: Development and analysis of modern financial theory and its implications for management decisions: market efficiency, capital asset pricing, firm investment decisions, capital structure, dividend policy, and cost of capital.

subject: CIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Repeatable unlimited times. Plan must include goals and rationale.

subject: CIS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CSD
title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
description: Will overview anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing. Students gain exposure to structures and functions of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, deglutition, and hearing systems required for normal communication and swallowing. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CSD
title: Phonetics
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of phonetic and phonological development. International Phonetic Alphabet Transcription of English speech sounds; phonological developments and models; cultural variations; analysis interpretation and other considerations related to speech sound development and production. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CSD
title: Speech and Language Development
description: Will develop an understanding of children’s acquisition of speech, language, and normal communication development from birth through adolescence. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CSD
title: Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Speech and Hearing
description: Provides an understanding of the fundamental processes underlying the production and perception of speech. Students gain an understanding of the physical and psychological aspects of sound and their measurement. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Clinical Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Provides observation and discussion of the clinical management of individuals with communication disorders, and practical experience related to clinical procedures and requirements. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Information and theoretical foundations serve as an introduction to the field of communication disorders. Will provide an overview of the normal processes and disorders of speech, language, hearing, and swallowing. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Audiometry and Auditory Disorders
description: Covers anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, acoustic, basic knowledge of auditory disorders and testing procedures, and introduction to rehabilitative audiology. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: CSD
title: Basic Statistics for Health-Related Professionals
description: Provides students from behavioral sciences and health-related professions with an overview of normal distribution, central tendency, variability, sampling, hypothesis testing, frequency distribution, correlation, regression, and t-test. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: CSD
title: Research Methods
description: Research methods applicable to the field of speech-language pathology and audiology; analysis and reporting of data. Required of all CSD graduate students.
prerequisites: previous coursework in inferential statistics and consent

subject: CSD
title: Neuroscience in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Explores the neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the human nervous system as it relates to communication and swallowing and how neurological pathologies lead to behavioral deficits in those areas. CSD majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: CSD
title: Audiological Foundations for SpeechLanguage Pathology
description: Instrumentation; special tests of hearing.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Motor Speech Disorders
description: Provides in-depth examination of various motor speech disorders, including apraxia of speech and dysarthria. Emphasis is on assessment/treatment of these diagnoses. Review of current treatment literature, anatomy/physiology, practical exercises in treatment planning. A-F only.

subject: CSD
title: Disorders of Phonology and Articulation
description: Study of the etiology, assessment, and remediation of disorders and articulation. A-F only.

subject: CSD
title: Child Language Disorders
description: Study of the etiology, behavioral characteristics and treatment methods for child language disorders. Examination of methods, test, and instruments employed in diagnosis of child language disorders. Includes identification of language deficits and writing intervention goals. A-F only.

subject: CSD
title: Language Development for Children with Hearing Deficiencies
description: Language acquisition by hard-of-hearing and deaf children; methods of stimulating growth.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology I
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings. Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned for six credits only.

subject: CSD
title: Audiology Practicum for SpeechLanguage Pathology
description: Clinical practice in administering tests, interpreting results; counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CSD
title: Voice Disorders
description: Contemporary development and theoretical issues in the diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of vocal system disorders in children and adults; current literature and clinical practice issues are addressed. A-F only.

subject: CSD
title: Adult Neurogenic Language and Cognitive-Communication Disorders
description: Study of acquired adult language and cognitive communication disorders associated with stroke, traumatic brain injury, and dementia. Application of evidence-based procedures and strategies for assessment and intervention, review of current literature, and discussion of professional issues. A-F only.

subject: CSD
title: Research–Speech Pathology
description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing speech-language pathology. Repeatable three times.

subject: CSD
title: Research–Audiology
description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing audiology.

subject: CSD
title: (Alpha) Directed Study
description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area. Repeatable unlimited times. (B) language pathology; (C) audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CSD
title: Amplification: Assessment and Applications
description: Comprehensive study of amplification. Assessment, fitting, evaluation, electroacoustic evaluation, dispensing. Personal instruments and instructional-educational systems.

subject: CSD
title: Disorders of Fluency
description: Contemporary developments and theoretical issues in diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of disorders of fluency such as stuttering in both children and adults.

subject: CSD
title: Electrophysiologic Audiometry
description: Study of early, middle, and late auditory evoked potentials with emphasis on the auditory brainstem response.

subject: CSD
title: Dysphagia: Disorders of Swallowing
description: Explores the dynamics of normal and disordered swallowing across the life span with emphasis on the adult population. CSD majors only. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: CSD
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology
description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology. Repeatable for credit for different alphas unlimited times.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology II
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings. Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned for 12 credits only

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology II
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results; counseling individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Audiology–Diagnostic Procedures
description: Study of diagnostic procedures as reflected in current literature.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Audiology–Rehabilitative Procedures
description: Procedures and philosophies presented in recent literature dealing with rehabilitative phases of audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology III
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedure with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings. Repeatable unlimited times, up to 18 credits.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology III
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results, counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: COMG
title: Everyday Communication with Numbers: A Survival Guide
description: FQ Understanding, communicating, and evaluating quantitative information in everyday contexts. Topics include describing and interpreting data, basic statistics, and evaluating the validity of results.

subject: COMG
title: Personal and Public Speech
description: DA Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

subject: COMG
title: Personal and Public Speech
description: DA Develops communication skills necessary to func

subject: HWST
title: Practicum Research Plan B
description: Practicum for Plan B. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: HWST
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. (F) Full-time. S/U for (F) only. Repeatable up to six credits; Repeatable unlimited times for (F).

subject: HSSW
title: Southeast Asian Cultures in Health/ Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in Southeast and South Asian region.
department: Health Sciences and Social Welfare Department

subject: HSSW
title: Pacific Cultures in Health/Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in the Pacific region.
department: Health Sciences and Social Welfare Department

subject: HNDI
title: Elementary Hindi I
description: HSL. Learn to express yourself in Hindi-a language that comes with a beautiful script, ancient philosophy, spicy food, and Bollywood! The course is communicative, creative, flexibly personalized for student interests. No textbook to buy.

subject: HNDI
title: Elementary Hindi II
description: HSL. Build on your 101 skills. Content includes Bollywood Film Festival at Honolulu Museum of Art. Create your own audiovisual projects–make movie trailers, write children’s books, or perform at South Asian events.

subject: HNDI
title: Intermediate Hindi I
description: HSL. Improve your communicative and cultural proficiency. Make Bollywood your language coach. Talk about cross-cultural values and practices of food, family, and friendship. Project-based course that builds bridges to your majors, minors, and other interests.

subject: HNDI
title: Intermediate Hindi II
description: HSL. Prepare your proficiency for traveling to India. Create audio-visual presentations, documentaries, movie parodies, poetry, plays, dance, or projects from your majors/minors. Develop critical, cross-cultural, and creative skills. Bollywood built into course content.

subject: HNDI
title: Third-Level Hindi: Culture
description: Continuation of 202. Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected cultural themes.

subject: HNDI
title: Third-Level Hindi: Film
description: Continuation of 202. Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected Hindi-Urdu films.

subject: HIST
title: World History to 1500
description: FGA. Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from prehistory to 1500; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: World History since 1500
description: FGB. Continuation of 151. Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from 1500 to present; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: Issues in World History
description: In examining aspects of the histories of Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe and Oceania, this course highlights the myriad ways in which global contact has transformed our world and narratives of the past.

subject: HIST
title: World History of Human Disease
description: FGC. Examines how disease has affected humans in terms of society, culture, politics, religion, and economics. Explores the impact over a broad range of time periods, from pre-history to the present/future.

subject: HIST
title: Global Environmental History
description: FGC. Explores the influence of nature–climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms–on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them. (Cross-listed as SUST 157)

subject: HIST
title: Global History of Food
description: FGB. Exploration of food and eating from historical, cultural, economic, and geopolitical perspectives. Includes both historical and contemporary issues.

subject: HIST
title: World Cultures in Perspective
description: FGA. Development of civilizations from prehistoric origins to 1500. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for 151 and 152; students in Honors program only.

subject: HIST
title: World Cultures in Perspective
description: FGB. Continuation of 161A. Development of civilization from 1500 to the present. Offered as discussion and/ or problems course. Alternative for 151 and 152; students in Honors program only.

subject: HIST
title: Early European Civilization
description: DH. Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states before 1500, including classical and medieval eras. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: European Civilization 1500-1800
description: DH. Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states. 1500–1800.

subject: HIST
title: Modern European Civilization 1800-
description: DH. Continuation of 231. Major political, social, economic, and cultural trends from Napoleon to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Civilizations of Asia
description: DH. Survey of major civilizations of Asia from earliest times to 1500; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

subject: HIST
title: Civilizations of Asia
description: DH. Continuation of 241. Survey of major civilizations of Asia from 1500 to the present; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

subject: HIST
title: Atlantic History: Colonies to Revolutions
description: DH. Comparative and historical survey of colonialism and revolutions in the Atlantic World from 1500 to 1830. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to American History
description: DH. Interpretive survey from earliest settlement to 1865. A-F only.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to American History
description: DH. Interpretive survey from 1865 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Hawaiian Islands
description: DH. Survey of state and local history from Polynesian chiefdoms to Hawaiian Kingdom to American territory and state.

subject: HIST
title: Oceania Survey
description: DH. Survey of major events, themes, and issues that make up the diverse histories of Oceania, including Hawai‘i, from ancestral origins to the present, with an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Philippines
description: DH. Traces developments in Philippine history and society from precolonial to contemporary times and explores ways in which the peoples of the Philippines embraced, resisted or negotiated new modes of thought, behavior and social organization influenced by the Spanish, American, and Japanese regimes as well as the postcolonial global order.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in History
description: DH. Introduction to methods of historical inquiry; current issues in World, American, European, or Pacific history. Emphasis on teaching writing. Repeatable one time. A-F only

subject: HIST
title: History of Early India
description: DH. Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century. (Cross-listed as IP 300)

subject: HIST
title: History of Modern India
description: DH. Historical survey of India and South Asia from the Mughal Empire to the new millennium, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from the 18th century to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Early Modern Southeast Asia
description: DH. Traces the development of Southeast Asia from early beginnings to the 19th century. Ethical issues and effective writing based on essays and ethical responses will form an important part of the course. DH

subject: HIST
title: Modern Southeast Asia
description: DH. Continuation of 305, from 18th century to the present.

subject: HIST
title: East Asian Civilizations
description: DH. Characteristics of East Asian civilizations as they developed in pre-modern China; variant patterns in Japan and Korea; the modernization process to 1500.

subject: HIST
title: East Asian Civilizations
description: DH. Continuation of 309. Period after 1500.

subject: HIST
title: History of China
description: DH. Chinese civilization to the 17th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of China
description: DH. Continuation of 311. Period since the 17th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japan
description: DH. Survey of culture, government, economics, and institutions, to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japan
description: DH. Continuation of 321. Period from 1700.

subject: HIST
title: Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
description: DH. History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills. (Cross-listed as ASAN 323)

subject: HIST
title: The Samurai of Japan
description: DH. A social, military, and cultural history of Japan’s samurai (warrior) class.

subject: HIST
title: History of Premodern Korea
description: DH. Survey of political, economic, social, and cultural developments from earliest times to 1400. Ethical issues in nationhood, central hegemony, myth-making, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

subject: HIST
title: History of Modern Korea
description: DH. Continuation of 327. From 1400 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of North Korea
description: DH. History of North Korea in terms of industrialism, militarism, nationalism, and state power, from 1945 to today. Focus on construction of national sovereign identity and comparison with postcolonial world.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece I
description: DH. Political, social, and cultural history of the Minoan, Mycenean, and Archaic periods.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece II
description: DH. Political, social, and cultural history of the Classical and Hellenistic periods.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i–Political Thought in Hawaiian
description:
DH
Intensive study of Hawaiian political thought in writing and speech. (Cross-listed as POLS 303C)

subject: HAW
title: Ka Hō‘ike Honua
description: Study of Hawaiian land tenure practices through readings and discussions of audiotapes, written primary sources, maps, wind names, rain names, ‘Ōlelo no‘eau (wise sayings), and mele (poetry). Readings are drawn from 19th and 20th century Hawaiian newspapers and other primary sources.

subject: HAW
title: Ma Ka Hana Ka ‘Ike
description: Study of traditional Hawaiian language and cultural practices through hands-on applications and lectures.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Mo‘olelo–Creative Writing in Hawaiian
description: Study and composition of written works in various creative genres of Hawaiian storytelling, with a focus on the adaptation and maintenance of a Hawaiian voice and worldview in writing.

subject: HAW
title: I Pa‘a Ke Kahua
description: An experiential approach to the acquisition of vocabulary, which will allow students to broaden and deepen their knowledge of language and the range of domains to perpetuate Hawaiian as a living language. Repeatable one time.

subject: HAW
title: E Pū Pa‘akai Kākou: A Study of Traditional Hawaiian and Contemporary Food Culture
description: A study of traditional Hawaiian and contemporary food culture through hands-on applications and lectures.

subject: HAW
title: (Alpha) Problems in Translation
description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

subject: HAW
title: Na Politika ma ka Nuhou Hawai‘i– Politics in Hawaiian Language Media
description:
DH
Study of Hawaiian news media with emphasis on political content. Includes field trips to various archives. (Cross-listed as POLS 344)

subject: HAW
title: Structure of Hawaiian
description:
DH
Descriptive linguistic analysis. Intensive exercises in advanced grammar.

subject: HAW
title: ‘Ōlelo Ni‘ihau I
description:
DH
Basic study of ‘Olelo Ni‘ihau. Speaking and listening comprehension will be developed through listening to audio recordings, watching video recordings, and participating in faceto-face conversations with Ni‘ihau native speakers.

subject: HAW
title: History of the Hawaiian Language
description:
DH
Development from proto-Polynesian. Phonology, morphology, and grammar; history of research.

subject: HAW
title: (Alpha) Ha‘uki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian
description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball. Repeatable for other topics.

subject: HAW
title: Language for the Classroom
description: Examination of language needs in various classroom settings and introduction to new vocabulary in school content areas.

subject: HAW
title: Kuleana Kula Kaiapuni
description: Examination of the political struggles of the Kula Kaiapuni (Hawaiian Immersion Program)–past and present. Special attention given to federal and state governments, Department of Education, and internal political struggles.

subject: HAW
title: Ho‘omōhala Ha‘awina Kaiapuni Curriculum Development
description: Examination of curricular issues of indigenous language programs; weekly participation in an immersion classroom; development of materials. Repeatable one time.

subject: HAW
title: Teaching in Hawaiian Language Immersion Program
description: Explore the knowledge base needed for teaching in the Hawaiian Language Immersion Program and initiate inquiry into the nature and social context of teaching, learning and schooling.

subject: HAW
title: Teaching Residency
description: Full-time student teaching in a Hawaiian language classroom. CR/NC only.

subject: HAW
title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
description: Analysis and resolution of issues in teaching residency; teaching strategies and techniques; curriculum planning, professional growth and development.

subject: HAW
title: Papa Mele Wahi Pana
description: Will provide students with the opportunity to learn mele, mainly poetry and song, composed specifically for a certain area of Hawai‘i.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Poetry
description:
DL
Historical survey and analysis of poetry found in traditional chants, folk songs, modern poetry written in Hawaiian. Interpreting and composing Hawaiian poetry.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Hanakeaka–Hawaiian Language Playwriting
description:
DA
The creation and authoring of Hawaiian language play scripts based on traditional motifs. Repeatable one time.

subject: HAW
title: Kahua Hanakeaka (Hawaiian Medium Stage Production)
description: From design to performance, students mount an original production based on traditional motifs. Repeatable one time.

subject: HAW
title: ‘Ōlelo No‘eau
description: Survey and analysis of traditional proverbs and their kaona or symbolic meanings. A-F only.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Mākau‘Ōlelo A‘o Kula Kaiapuni Hawai‘i
description: Assess the linguistic competence of prospective Hawaiian language immersion teachers to assure that all teachers entering the state DOE Hawaiian Immersion Program meet the requirements of the program with respect to Hawaiian language proficiency. CR/NC only.

subject: HAW
title: Analyzing Immersion Hawaiian
description: Analysis and acquisition of features in Hawaiian spoken by Hawaiian speaking children in Hawaiian immersion education.

subject: HAW
title: Learning Hawaiian Through Immersion
description: Learning Hawaiian in the immersion setting: cultural context, behavioral patterns, and learning concerns.

subject: HAW
title: Directed Studies
description: Study of Hawaiian language through vernacular readings in various academic fields. Repeatable up to 6 credits.

subject: HAW
title: Kākau Mo‘olelo
description: Analyzes various genres of written Hawaiian literature. HAW majors only.

subject: HAW
title: Kākā‘ōlelo Oratory
description: A survey of oral performance styles to build increased oral skills.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Palapala Noi Laeo‘o/Writing a Hawaiian Master’s Proposal
description: Seminar to select and develop students’ research topic, proposal, and organizational plan for Plan A or B completion. Majors are encouraged not to take this course in their first semester of the program. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HAW
title: Ka Hana Noi‘i (Research Methods)
description: Research methodology course utilizing active research in the major repositories of Hawaiian language materials and Hawaiian-related knowledge. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HAW
title: Nā Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i (Hawaiian Political Thought)
description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods. (Cross-listed as POLS 612)

subject: HAW
title: Kuana‘ike
description: The examination of Hawaiian ways of speaking, as contrasted with English focusing on those features that are uniquely Hawaiian and can be said to constitute a Hawaiian worldview. Section 1 taught in Hawaiian; Section 2 taught in English.

subject: HAW
title: Mo‘olelo Hawai‘i
description: Intensive study, research, and analysis of Hawaiian history. Repeatable two times with consent of advisor.

subject: HAW
title: (Alpha) Nā Mea Kākau/Nā Haku Mo‘olelo
description: Intensive study of an individual author, his/her works and nuances of his/her works. (E) J. H. Kanepu‘u; (I) S. M. Kamakau. (Once a year)

subject: HAW
title: Ke A‘o ‘Olelo Hou ‘Ana (Teaching Hawaiian As a Second Language)
description: Survey of existing texts and teaching resources; analysis of student clientele and needs; review of pedagogical approaches for heritage and non-heritage learners; syllabus and materials development; practicum.

subject: HAW
title: Pilina ‘Ōlelo
description: In-depth examination and research into the grammar of Hawaiian including discussion of theories of language and incorporation of meta-language. (Once a year)

subject: HAW
title: ‘Ōlelo Ni‘ihau
description: Intensive, advanced study and analysis of traditional Hawaiian Ni‘ihau dialect through face-to-face conversations with Ni‘ihau native speakers, listening to audio recordings and watching video recordings of Ni‘ihau native speakers.
prerequisites: (402 and 453) with a minimum grade of B- or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Noi‘i Mele
description: Intensive study focusing on original compositions of Hawaiian poetry and song.

subject: HAW
title: Papahana Laeo‘o
description: Research for Plan B project/non-thesis. May include but not limited to internship with cultural practitioner. Repeatable up to six credits. HAW majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: HAW
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and graduate chair.

subject: HAW
title: Noi‘i Pepa Laeo‘o (Thesis)
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: GER
title: Elementary German
description: Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: GER
title: Elementary German
description: Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Elementary German
description: Combined content of 101 and 102 covered in one intensive course. (Summer only)

subject: GER

description: Conversation, grammar, reading and writing.

subject: GER
title: Intermediate German
description: Conversation, grammar, reading and writing.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Intermediate German Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the second-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

subject: GER
title: Phonetics and Pronunciation Practice
description: Analysis of the German phonological system and practice in pronunciation.

subject: GER
title: Structure of Modern German
description: Study of syntactic and morphological structures and basic pragmatic principles. Focuses on spoken and written Modern German.

subject: GER
title: Reading and Writing
description: Further development of reading and writing skills through the study of short texts, focusing on modern German short stories, fairy tales, poems and song lyrics.

subject: GER
title: Business German
description: Advanced German conversation, reading, and writing with a special emphasis on the vocabulary and cultural context of the German business world.

subject: GER
title: Contemporary Topics in Media
description: Development of listening and speaking, reading and writing skills through analysis and discussion of media: newspaper articles, radio, and television programs and online sources.

subject: GER
title: Conversation
description: Intensive practice in spoken German designed to increase vocabulary and improve oral proficiency.

subject: GER
title: Modern Readings: Wanderlust, Love, and Desire
description: Development of reading skills through the study of authentic modern texts (short stories; articles from newspapers, magazines, and the internet) with topics relating to culture, society, and history.

subject: GER
title: German for Reading II
description: Further development of reading skills through the study of short scholarly, technical, and literary texts.

subject: GER
title: Introduction to German Literature 1750- 1914:
description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1750 to 1914.

subject: GER
title: Introduction to German Literature 1914- Present
description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1914 to present.

subject: GER
title: German Cinema
description: Study of German film history, film analysis, film theory, and film study. Lecture/discussion. Repeatable one time, or take LLEA 320 one time, for different topics. 6 cr. limit on GER/LLEA 320 courses.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Third-Level German Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the third-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

subject: GER
title: Germanic Civilization to World War II
description: German cultural heritage and history in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland until World War II.

subject: GER
title: Modern German Culture
description: Modern culture in post-World War II Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

subject: GER
title: Practical German for use in Hawai‘i
description: Use of German in practical situations in Hawai‘i, e.g., in travel industry.

subject: GER
title: Enlightenment—Sturm und Drang
description: Lessing and his contemporaries; early dramas of Goethe and Schiller; Goethe’s early lyrics.

subject: GER
title: Classicism
description: Classical writings of Goethe and Schiller; some reference to other writers.

subject: GER
title: Romanticism
description: Novalis, Tieck, E. T. A. Hoffmann, Eichendorff, etc.

subject: GER
title: Culture of Two Germanies: 1945-1989
description: (taught in German) Literature, culture, and film of East and West Germany, 1945-1989. Credit cannot be earned for both LLEA 415 and GER 415.

subject: GER
title: German Literature, Culture and Film: 1989 to Present
description: Study of German literature, culture and film, 1989 to present. Credit cannot be earned for both 416 and LLEA 416.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Fourth-Level German Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-level in German language and culture in a German-speaking country.

subject: GES
title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST. Restricted to GES majors. CR/NC only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as OCN 100)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability. Repeatable one time. A-F only. ((Cross-listed as OCN 102 and SUST 112)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment. A-F only. (Cross-listed as OCN 102L and SUST 112L)
prerequisites: 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent) or SUST 112 (or concurrent).
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: GES Thesis Proposal
description: Supports GES majors in producing a thesis proposal that outlines and describes the timeline, required resources, etc. of the degree-required project. CR/NC only. GES majors only. Sophomore standing or higher.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawai‘i. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only. A-F only. (Alt years: Spring) (Cross-listed as ATMO 304 and SUST 304)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: The Changing Earth and Climate System
description: Covers the Earth system, including mass and energy transfers, biogeochemical cycles, natural and anthropogenic changes on regional and global scale. GES majors only.
prerequisites: MATH 241, and GES 302 (or concurrent) and OCN 201 (or concurrent).
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311. Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling. GES majors only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as OCN 319L)
prerequisites: 311, MATH 242, PHYS 170/170L, and CHEM 161/161L; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Aquatic Pollution
description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives. GES majors only. (Cross-listed as OCN 320)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Environmental Data Science
description: Provides an introduction to environmental data science by applying python-based programming techniques to Earth science datasets. GES majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: MATH 242, and ICS 110P or ICS 110C or ERTH 250.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science. Repeatable up to 6 credits. GES majors only. (Cross-listed as OCN 399)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Biogeochemical Systems
description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills. GES majors only. Senior standing only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as OCN 401)
prerequisites: OCN 201, GES 311, BIOL 172/172L, CHEM 162/162L, ERTH 101/101L, GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES/OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome
description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Alt years: Fall) (Cross-listed as OCN 454)
prerequisites: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Alt years: Fall) (Cross-listed as OCN 454L)
prerequisites: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory. GES majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as OCN 463)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GES
title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: GEO
title: Capstone Undergraduate Seminar
