description: Current and historical geographic literature provides a background for local and global issues. Through discussion, written reviews, and research reports, the geographic perspective in modern life will be explored.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Research
description: Geography majors conduct research under faculty supervision on a topic of their choice. Repeatable two times, up to six credits.
prerequisites: Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent. GEO majors only. Senior standing only.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Climatology
description: Methods of determining energy budget and water balance; applications in agriculture, hydrology, climatic classifications. Theory of climatic change. Bibliography.
prerequisites: GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 or ATMO 320; or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation. (Cross-listed as ANTH 610)

subject: GEO
title: Human Environment Systems
description: Role and potential of systems science in analysis of human environment interaction, especially resource management. Framework and methodology for problem structuring; overview of techniques.
prerequisites: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing with consent.

subject: GEO
title: Theories and Policies of Development
description: Will critically examine what constitutes progress, advancement, or betterment in this highly uneven world, where inter-regional, inter-class, inter-group, and inter-gender differences in development are expanding. Graduate standing only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: GEO
title: Coastal Planning and Management
description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture. Repeatable one time with consent. (Crosslisted as PLAN 623)

subject: GEO
title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment. (Cross-listed as PLAN 622)

subject: GEO
title: Seafood in Southeast Asia
description: Seafood production in Southeast Asia, including both regional fisheries and aquaculture. Case studies used to illustrate challenges to the implementation of sustainable seafood production and emerging approaches, such as community supported seafood. (Cross-listed as ASAN 633)

subject: GEO
title: Environment and Development
description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era. (Cross-listed as PLAN 637)

subject: GEO
title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy. (Cross-listed as PLAN 639)

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geography of Southeast Asia
description: Repeatable with consent of instructor.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geography of the Pacific
description: Investigation of geographic problems of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia. Repeatable with consent of instructor.

subject: GEO
title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TPSS 680)
degrees: Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences MS

subject: GEO
title: Human Geography Research Methods
description: Introduction to research methods in human geography. Explores and provides guided practical experience with research methods and analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Graduate seminar required of all department MA students and PhD students. Single credit course in which faculty present ongoing research in their fields. Co-requisite: GEO 695.

subject: GEO
title: Technology and Natural Risks Methods of Analysis
description: Survey of tools for evaluating risks to human health from technological and natural hazards. Historical and international context of methods.

subject: GEO
title: Concepts and Theories in Geography
description: Concepts, theory, models. Geographic approaches to spatial and environmental problems. Required of entering graduate students unless waived by department.

subject: GEO
title: Research Design/Methods in Geography
description: Elements of research design, practical field experience, exposure to research and ideologies, broad exposure to heritage and ethos of the discipline.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: GEO
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: GEO
title: Geomorphology
description: Current understanding of geomorphological concepts, processes, and the dynamic relationship between human landscape modification and system response.

subject: GEO
title: (Alpha) Special Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis. Repeatable two times.

subject: GEO
title: Political Ecology
description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Resource Management in Asia-Pacific
description: Examination of resource management problems in Asia and the Pacific. Problems of resource use—agriculture, forestry, energy, minerals, ocean, air quality.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Political Geography
description: Topics vary; may include borders, boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, identity politics, nations and nationalism, social categorization, the sovereign state system, territoriality. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Geographies of Migration
description: Topics vary; may include immigration, borders, refugees, asylum, climate change, and displacement. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: GEO
title: Research Seminar: Agricultural Geography
description: (Cross-listed as SUST 763)

subject: GEO
title: Society and Space
description: Advanced seminar on social production of space. Topics include spatial metaphor in social theory; western spatiality from the renaissance through the enlightenment, modernity and post modernity; and geography of the body, home, landscape, and nation.

subject: GEO
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric and Palliative Care
description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric Medicine Research
description: Medical students will have the opportunity to complete a research project in the field of epidemiology of aging, and present an abstract at a local meeting. Basic principles of epidemiology and statistics will be taught. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric and Palliative Medicine Elective
description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers. CR/NC only.

subject: GERI
title: Medical Student Training in Aging Program
description: Introduces medical students to clinical, research, and academic experiences in geriatrics, under the mentorship of faculty members. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: GERI
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: One-on-one independent study for students interested in geriatrics and/or palliative medicine. Students will work with a faculty mentor to define an area of interest and meet regularly for guidance and feedback. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: GER
title: Elementary German
description: HSL. Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: GER
title: Elementary German
description: HSL. Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Elementary German
description: HSL. Combined content of 101 and 102 covered in one intensive course. (Summer only)

subject: GER
title: Intermediate German
description: HSL. Conversation, grammar, reading and writing.

subject: GER
title: Intermediate German
description: HSL. Conversation, grammar, reading and writing.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Intermediate German Abroad
description: HSL. Intensive course of formal instruction abroad.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Military History
description: Survey of development of American military forces from War of Independence to war in Vietnam.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science to 1700
description: Evolution of scientific thought and its cultural context. Antiquity to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science Since 1700
description: Continuation of 394; science, technology, and society since 1700.

subject: HIST
title: Historical Theories and Methods (Alpha)
description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

subject: HIST
title: Digital History in the Global Village
description: History of the digital age in global perspective connecting people, media, and technology. Faculty and students will use digital media to introduce innovative approaches to doing history. (Fall only)

subject: HIST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as SUST 401)

subject: HIST
title: Vietnam: History and Memory
description: Survey of Vietnamese history with particular attention to the multiple ways that the Vietnamese past has been remembered and represented by different peoples. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Rivers, Seas, and Society in Southeast Asia
description: The rivers, seas, and extensive coastlines are a dominant environmental feature in Southeast Asia. Focuses on the dynamic interaction of water and society in shaping the history of the region.

subject: HIST
title: Themes of War in History
description: Explores cross-cutting themes of war from ancient times to the present, such as concepts of just war and unjust war, valor and heroism, and war trauma among combatants and civilian populations in conflict zones.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Philippines
description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic. (Cross-listed as ASAN 406)

subject: HIST
title: Modern Malaysia
description: History of Malay peninsula and northern Borneo, emphasizing developments since 18th century: trade, commerce, foreign migrations, pluralism, nationalism, and Islam.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Indonesia
description: Indonesia from 14th century to present. Emphasis on period from late 18th-century Western colonial impact to struggle for independence and problems of nationhood.

subject: HIST
title: History of Islamic Southeast Asia
description: History of the coming of Islam to Southeast Asia, the spread of its ideas, and its role in the lives of Muslim communities living in the region. (Spring only)

subject: HIST
title: Twentieth-Century China
description: An examination of the political, intellectual, economic, cultural, and social transformations of China in the twentieth century. This lecture studies critical events in the making of modern China and explores important issues in the modernization of Chinese life in the twentieth century.

subject: HIST
title: Society and Culture in Traditional China
description: Ch’ing government and Chinese society from local and regional perspectives; modes of control and disorder during the 19th century.

subject: HIST
title: Local History of 20th-Century China
description: Sociopolitical change and continuity at local and regional levels since 1900, stressing provincial reform, Hsien and sub-Hsien politics, warlordism, Kuomintang tutelage, and the Chinese Communist movement and rule.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Intellectual History
description: An interpretive survey of Chinese ideas and values in their cultural, social and political settings from classical age to 1600.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Intellectual History
description: Interpretive survey of Chinese thought from 1600 to the contemporary period, with special emphasis on the themes of cultural collision and change.

subject: HIST
title: China’s Foreign Relations
description: Systematic review from traditional times, with emphasis on modern and contemporary history, analyses of foreign policy formulation, objectives, and implementation.

subject: HIST
title: The Search for Modern China
description: Origins, development, and meaning of modern revolution in China, 19th century to People’s Republic.

subject: HIST
title: People’s Republic of China
description: Salient developments from 1949 to the present. Social revolution and modernization, critically relevant foreign relations.

subject: HIST
title: China in World History
description: Interpretative survey of China’s changing position, significance, and function in the evolution of world history as a way to provide a better understanding of its past and present.

subject: HIST
title: Tokugawa Japan
description: Japanese history and culture, 1600–1867.

subject: HIST
title: Okinawa
description: Survey of social, cultural, economic, and political history from earliest times to present.

subject: HIST
title: Twentieth Century Japan
description: Problems of Japan’s political, economic, and social development since institutional consolidation of Meiji state (c.1890).

subject: HIST
title: Women in East Asian History
description: Survey of the changing political, social, economic, and cultural positions of women in China, Japan, and Korea from ancient times to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japanese Cuisine and Foodways
description: Explores the history of Japanese cuisine and investigates the cultural, economic, and geopolitical aspects of food-ways in Japanese domestic and international identity.

subject: HIST
title: Topics on Transitional Justice
description: Explores how societies in the wake of armed conflict, repression, or mass human rights abuses build institutional capacities for promoting justice, human rights, and the rule of law

subject: HIST
title: War Crimes Trials in History
description: Explores war crimes trials in history since the end of WWII to the present. Involves extensive source analysis, discussion, research, and writing. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
description: Historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states, Macedonia, the Hellenistic, and Roman Empires. (Cross-listed as CLAS 430)

subject: HIST
title: Crisis and Conflict in the Middle East
description: In depth study and analysis of major crises and conflicts in the Middle East since World War II: the Arab–Israeli Wars, revolutions in the Arab countries, the Turkish experiment with secularism, the Iranian/ Islamic revolution, Afghanistan, the Gulf War.

subject: HIST
title: Medieval Cultures
description: Topical study of cultural and cross-cultural issues in the medieval period (circa 300-1500). Class discussion and written work emphasize analysis of primary source documents using cultural and world history theories. Regional focus and readings vary by semester. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: History of Christianity to 1500
description: Historical analysis of the main traditions of Christianity and elements of diversity within Europe and in relation to other parts of the world. Focus on the interpretation of primary sources and discussion of cultural issues. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: World Environmental History, 1500 to Present
description: Explores interactions between humans and the natural world from early modern era to the present. Topics include invader species and biotic exchange; environmental politics; and the ecological impact of industrialization, urbanization, science, technology, war, etc.

subject: HIST
title: The Darwinian Revolution
description: Social and intellectual origins of evolutionary thought and its continuing impact; emphasis on Darwin and the Victorian scientific community.

subject: HIST
title: 20th-Century Europe
description: Contemporary problems and their historical background.

subject: HIST
title: Expansion of Europe
description: Historical processes in modern European colonization from 16th to 20th century; impact on non-Europeans in Asia and Africa. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: War and Violence in Early Modern Europe
description: History of the intellectual, social, and cultural causes and consequences of violence, including military conflicts.

subject: HIST
title: Nazi Germany
description: Origins, establishment, and impact of Hitler’s Third Reich. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: The History of the Holocaust
description: The origins and progression of the Holocaust, the almost complete destruction of European Jews, and other Nazi genocidal policies. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: French Revolution and Napoleon
description: Causes, course, and conduct of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods, their impact upon Europe; emphasis on the conflict of ideologies inherent in the Revolutionary process.

subject: HIST
title: Europe, 1914-1945: War, Peace, and Revolution
description: Explores war and peace in Europe, from the start of the Great War through the formal end of World War II. Topics include key battles, civilians, peace movements, treaties, the Shoah, Fascism, and Soviet Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Imperial Spain and Portugal
description: The influence of Spain and Portugal on people and cultures in Europe, Africa, America, and Asia; Portugal’s captivity and the defeat of the Spanish Armada.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in African History
description: Selected themes important in African history, including political, social, and economic developments.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning
description: Introduction to key theoretical concepts of machine learning. Practical experience with decision free methods, artificial neural networks. Bayesian belief networks and contemporary statistical methods including regression, clustering and classification. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Information Theory in Machine Learning
description: Basics of information processing and learning in the brain; neural networks; learning algorithms based on information maximization; applications in molecular biology and bioinformatics. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in computer science or mathematics background, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Deep Learning with Neural Networks
description: Graduate course on deep learning with artificial neural networks. Provides practical techniques for modeling image, video, text, and graph data with supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches. Includes instruction in the latest software frameworks. Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
description: Covers the latest developments in human-centered artificial intelligence, including ethics, bias, explainability, privacy, fairness, and usability. Involves discussion, writing assignments, and a final project. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Theory of Computation
description: Advanced topics in formal languages, automata, computability, computational complexity.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Parallel Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of parallel algorithms, with emphasis on advanced techniques and latest advances in parallel algorithms.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Networks
description: Elementary principles of modern computer networking. Detailed coverage of overall architecture and the physical, data link, and network layers, with emphasis on the network layer. ICS majos only.
prerequisites: graduate standing in ICS, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust III: Cyber Security and Commerce
description: Tools and methods for security managers. Tools and methods to secure and monetize services and applications. Network as a computer and as a market. Problems of cyber war, cyber crime, cyber bullying. Graduate students only. (Spring only)

subject: ICS
title: Computer Architecture I
description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs. (Cross-listed as ECE 660)

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence
description: Current issues in artificial intelligence, including expert systems, knowledge representation, logic programming, learning, natural language processing.

subject: ICS
title: Pattern Recognition
description: Nature of the problem in pattern recognition and clustering; explanation of various algorithms.

subject: ICS
title: Human-Computer Interaction II
description: Studies of human performance in designing and using information systems. Emphasizes concepts and methodologies from human factors, psychology, and software engineering relating to human performance.

subject: ICS
title: User Interfaces and Hypermedia
description: Advanced concepts in construction of interfaces between computers and their users. Hypermedia information structures, guidelines, problems, and tradeoffs. Discussion of selected readings, implementation of prototypes.

subject: ICS
title: HCI Design Methods
description: Advanced analytical and empirical methods for the design and evaluation of usable, useful, and robust human computer interfaces. Students will apply selected methodologies to a major system design project.

subject: ICS
title: Social Informatics
description: An advanced introduction to the design of human-computer systems and other technological artifacts for supporting human collaboration in learning, work and social contexts, and to theoretical perspectives and empirical studies of collaboration that inform such design. A-F only.
prerequisites: 464 or 465 or 664 or 665 or 667 or LIS 677; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Social Computing
description: Participative analysis of online communities and user-generated content collections. Theoretical and practical aspects of online interaction, identity, trust, and virtual social capital. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Evolutionary Computation I: Survey of Methods
description: Evolutionary computation surveys in the field to prepare students for research. Topics include diverse engineering applications, theory, and concepts including search spaces, representation, objective functions, variation operators, selection, and population based search. (Once a year: fall)
prerequisites: 211 (B or better) and 241 (C or better) and admitted to a graduate program or capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics: Sequences Analysis
description: To expose students to bioinformatics at the biological sequences analysis level (DNA, RNA, proteins). Several bioinformatics methods and algorithms are introduced. Students are required to present one paper and to participate in a small group project. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics: Microarrays
description: Introduction to the basic principles of biology relevant for microarray gene expression data and to Bio-conductor. Collaborative open-source project to develop a modular general framework for the analysis of cDNA arrays and gene chips. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: 311 or background in biology, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Computer Graphics
description: Selected advanced topics in computer graphics. Substantial project required.

subject: ICS
title: Numerical Computation
description: Selected topics in numerical analysis, mathematical software, and scientific computation; examples include sparse matrix methods, finite element methods, mathematical programming.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Computer Vision
description: Fundamental problems and core concepts and techniques in computer vision, covering both theoretical and practical issues in the field. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Data Visualization
description: Explores advanced techniques in data visualization by surveying visualization techniques from the past 5-10 years, and designing and developing data visualizations leveraging those techniques. Graduate students only. (Fall only)

subject: ICS
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
description: Students will learn the science, engineering, art, and applications of virtual reality and augmented reality, with an emphasis on the construction of working virtual environments. Graduate students only. (Fall only)

subject: ICS
title: Digital Video Information
description: Principles and techniques of technical and context analysis of digital video information. Video capture and editing tools, compression and analysis algorithms, visual culture, narrative structure, juxtaposition of multimedia elements and their effects on information transmission. (Alt. years)

subject: ICS
title: Seminar in ICS
description: Series of talks on advanced research topics. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: ICS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Computer Science
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general. Repeatable unlimited times in different topics and different areas.

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Seminar discussing special topics in information and computer science. Topics and number of credits vary. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Special Topics in Security
description: Current topics and upcoming issues relevant to the field of information assurance and cyber security. Repeatable unlimited times. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ICS
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ICS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ICS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable eight times.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD in computer science

subject: ITM
title: Using Computers and Applications
description: Using Windows computers browsers, Microsoft Office (or equivalent) and other applications. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Project Management
description: Project management application and techniques such as planning methods; PERT/CPM forecasting; risk analysis; application in information technology projects and other areas.

subject: ITM
title: Supply Chain Processes
description: Improving organization productivity with an emphasis on analyzing supply chain processes and principles in terms of scheduling, inventory, quality control techniques, through most current practices.

subject: ITM
title: Programming Application Systems
description: Introduction to applications programming. Fundamentals, essential logic, file handling, report writing. Emphasis on systems development and disciplined programming. A-F only.
prerequisites: ICS 101, or LTEC 112 and 113, (or equivalent), or consent

subject: ITM
title: Information Systems Analysis and Design
description: Analysis and design of systems in organizations. Includes role of general systems concepts, systems development life cycle, identifying systems requirements, logical and physical design. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Database Systems
description: Introduction to database management and data structures, including database planning and design, normalization, relational and network data models, and physical organization and implementation. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Current Topics in ITM
description: Repeatable three time

subject: HIST
title: Directed Research
description: Individual research topics. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean. Restricted to plan A (thesis) students. Maximum 2 credit hours. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: HIST
title: Institutional History of Korea
description: Major political, economic, and social institutions. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Historical Literature
description: Reading and use of numerous genres of Chinese historical literature and documents. Chinese bibliography. Knowledge of Chinese required. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Teaching History
description: HIST 100-level faculty supervisors mentor their Teaching Assistants who teach the discussion labs. Course addresses issues of teaching strategy, grading and historical content. Enrollment limited to current Teaching Assistants in the World History Program. Repeatable seven times.
prerequisites: History graduate Teaching Assistants assigned to 151-152

subject: HIST
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: HON
title: Introduction to Research and Creative Work at Mānoa
description: Combines lectures by instructors and faculty guests with workshops and hands-on experience in small group projects, including bibliographic searches, laboratory science, social surveys and interviews. A significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. A-F only.

subject: HON
title: Sophomore Seminar
description: DA DB DH DL DP DS. Special inquiry-based study of multi-disciplinary topics in particular historical, cultural, geographical, environmental, or other contexts. Emphasis on primary sources and/or fieldwork and extensive instruction in writing. (B) biological science; (H) humanities; (P) physical science; (R) arts; (S) social science; (T) literature. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as IS 291) DB for (B); DH for (H); DP for (P); DA for (R); DS for (S); DL for (T)

subject: HON
title: Transformational Research Experiences for Early Undergraduates
description: Introduction to exploring discover-based investigation, with hands-on experiences in a wide range of science fields. Divided into 4-week learning modules led by researchers at several UH Mānoa research facilities on and off campus. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only. (Cross-listed as UROP 299)

subject: HON
title: Public Policy-Making
description: Students develop understanding of theory, practice, and ethical issues of public policy-making. Combines lecture/discussion and fieldtrips. Students develop policy analysis and strategic plans that identify issues, interests, and methods of influence. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 386)
prerequisites: HON 101 or HON 291(Alpha), or departmental approval

subject: HON
title: Civic Engagement and Social Justice
description: Seminar on history, theory, and practice of civic engagement in the U.S. and abroad. Involves comparative study of social justice movements, historically and today. Focus on role of university students in social justice movements. Repeatable one time. A-F only. DS
prerequisites: HON 101 or HON 291, or departmental approval

subject: HON
title: Off Campus Study Project
description: Honors students participating in off campus study (via Study Abroad Center, MIX, or NSE) enhance their experience through a project at the host site, designed with and approved with consultation with Honors advisor. Repeatable one time, up to three credits.
prerequisites: Honors students only. consent of Honors director and Study Abroad director.

subject: HON
title: Experiential Learning and Scholarly Engagement
description: Students develop an understanding of theory and practice of experiential learning through direct engagement and focused scholarly reflection while assimilating and synthesizing new knowledge and developing critical thinking skills. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: HON
title: From Ideas to Page: Learn The Publication Process
description: Learn the publication process through a “hands on” experiential learning, emphasizing diverse knowledge systems, writing, and ethics. Learn how to solicit contributions, review, and edit articles as part of the Horizons Undergraduate Journal publication cycle. Repeatable one time. (Spring only)
prerequisites: Honors students only. consent of Honors director and instructor.

subject: HON
title: Peer Mentoring
description: Students develop understanding of dynamics of leadership skills within the contexts of paired to large groups. Significant portion is dedicated to writing and oral communication instruction. Pre-semester training sessions, on-going training and supervision. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: HON 101 or departmental approval. Honors Program students only.

subject: HON
title: Junior Seminar
description: Project-based experiential learning involving community-based research or creative work. Focus on project design, practical skills, and teamwork. Significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. Multi-disciplinary topics vary each semester. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: HON
title: Honors Colloquium
description: Weekly meetings for discussion of enduring issues and problems of an interdisciplinary nature. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Limited to candidates for Honors degree

subject: HON
title: Honors Workshop
description: Supplemental workshop for students beginning independent work on their senior honors thesis. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: HON students only. Junior or senior standing only.

subject: HON
title: Honors Thesis Proposal
description: Library research skills; scholarship of research and creative work; methodological and ethical issues; development of individual proposal or prospectus for Senior Honors Project. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Limited to candidates for the Honors degree

subject: HON
title: Senior Honors Project
description: Original research, creative work, performance or other form of scholarly project appropriate to a major and supervised by a faculty member. Repeatable one time for each major. A-F only.
prerequisites: Limited to candidates for Honors degree

subject: HON
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Directed reading and/or research. Repeatable 3 times or up to 12 credits.

subject: HDFS
title: Human Development
description: DS. Concepts, issues, theories of human growth and development from conception to death; systems approaches to inquiry into factors affecting growth and development.

subject: HDFS
title: Infancy and Early Childhood
description: DS. Growth and development from prenatal period to age 5. Historical and current issues and research based on ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on optimal development.

subject: HDFS
title: Childhood
description: DS. Intensive investigation into developmental aspects of 6–12 year old children. Historical and current issues, research, and examination of the role of schools and other community resources. Focus on optimal development.

subject: HDFS
title: Adolescence and Early Adulthood
description: DS. Problems, concepts, and research related to development from puberty through early adulthood. Examination of biological, cognitive, social, and cultural factors affecting the individual.

subject: HDFS
title: Middle Age and Aging
description: DS. Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences. (Cross-listed as COA 334)

subject: HDFS
title: Intimacy, Marriages and Families
description: DS. Study of intimate relationships, marriages and families, their dynamics, strengths, growth and development, challenges, choices and opportunities, in the context of social change and cultural diversity.
prerequisites: HDFS 230 or PSY 100 or SOC 100; or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Parenting
description: Parenting theories, methods, skills, issues, and resources; parent-child relations in various cultural contexts.

subject: HDFS
title: Leadership and Group Process
description: Exploration of leadership research and theories and their application to leadership development; designed to enhance personal and interactive leadership.

subject: HDFS
title: Community Needs and Resources
description: DS. Theory and practice in determining community needs and resources; community resources development based on needs identification.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Resource Management
description: Concepts, principles, and practices in managing family and household resources.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Financial Planning
description: Analytical approach to family financial planning from the perspective of changing family demands over the life cycle.
prerequisites: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Economics
description: Consumer rights, responsibilities, and resources; consumer decision-making; factors affecting consumer functioning within economy.
prerequisites: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Soft Skills for Success in the Workplace
description: Employers regard soft skills as key criteria when hiring and retaining employees. Students learn critical skills essential to work place success. This class prepares students to be work ready.

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology
description: DS. Fundamental scientific

subject: HIST
title: French Revolution and Napoleon
description: Causes, course, and conduct of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods, their impact upon Europe; emphasis on the conflict of ideologies inherent in the Revolutionary process.

subject: HIST
title: Europe, 1914-1945: War, Peace, and Revolution
description: Explores war and peace in Europe, from the start of the Great War through the formal end of World War II. Topics include key battles, civilians, peace movements, treaties, the Shoah, Fascism, and Soviet Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Imperial Spain and Portugal
description: The influence of Spain and Portugal on people and cultures in Europe, Africa, America, and Asia; Portugal’s captivity and the defeat of the Spanish Armada.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in African History
description: Selected themes important in African history, including, for example, the politics, economics, societies, and cultures of pre-colonial, colonial, or modern Africa. Topics to be pre-announced. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History and Literature
description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/ Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics. Repeatable one time for different alphas, not repeatable for (C).

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History and Film
description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (B) United States; (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) world/ comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures. Repeatable one time for different alphas. (Once a year for (D))(C Cross-listed as CINE 452C); (E Cross-listed as CINE 452E)

subject: HIST
title: Colonial Medicine
description: Evolution of Western medical traditions; challenges created by European expansion and colonial interactions; development of modern racial and gender theories. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: HIST
title: Modern Russia
description: Creation of the Soviet Union, Stalinization, the Cold War, the collapse of the empire, the post-Soviet era.

subject: HIST
title: Russia in Asia and the Pacific
description: Russian/Soviet Siberia and Central Asia; Russian American Company and the Pacific; evolving relations with Asian and Pacific powers.

subject: HIST
title: The American Revolution
description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins, development, and consequences of the American Revolution, explored within the context of the broader revolutionary Atlantic world.

subject: HIST
title: African American History
description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins of racial slavery, slave and free black culture, slave resistance and antislavery, post-emancipation black life, the rise of Jim Crow, the Harlem Renaissance, and the Civil Rights Movement.

subject: HIST
title: Native American History
description: Lecture/ discussion on the history of North American Indians from the seventeenth century to the present. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Early America
description: Lecture/discussion on Native Americans, Africans, and Europeans in North America from contact to independence. Social, cultural, and economic themes and intersections of race, class, and gender explored.

subject: HIST
title: The Early American Republic
description: Lecture/discussion on the Constitution, the growth of partisan politics, the market revolution, religious revivalism, abolitionism and the expansion of slavery in the U.S. during the age of Jefferson and Jackson.

subject: HIST
title: American Civil War Era 1841–1877
description: The crisis of the Union: antebellum society and culture, slavery, reform, sectionalism, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

subject: HIST
title: Transformation of America 1877–1920
description: Selected themes that explain major changes in American life during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including the westward movement, consolidation of capitalism, world power diplomacy, popular culture, progressivism, and World War I.

subject: HIST
title: The United States 1920–1948
description: The Roaring Twenties, the Depression, New Deal, coming of World War II, America during the war, origins of the Cold War.

subject: HIST
title: The U.S.: 1948 to the Present
description: The atomic age and the Cold War, the age of anxiety, the 1960s, the Vietnam War, the Reagan-Bush era, and beyond.

subject: HIST
title: American Television History
description: Lecture/discussion examining the impact of television on American society, culture and politics. Analyzed in depth are family sitcoms, presidential politics, Vietnam and the presentation of gender and ethnicity. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Viva Las Vegas!
description: Upper-division lecture on the historical and cultural significance of Las Vegas in twentieth-century America. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: The Cold War
description: Cold War as a global struggle. Topics will include U.S.-Soviet economic and political rivalry, Capitalism vs. Communism as practical policy and ideology, and the force of Third World anti-colonial nationalism.

subject: HIST
title: Music, Industry, and Society
description: History of U.S. music and recording industry. How industry relates to economy as a whole, and how it reflects broad patterns and trends in American culture and society. (Cross-listed as MUS 440)

subject: HIST
title: Slavery and Freedom
description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World. (Cross-listed as AMST 432)

subject: HIST
title: The American West
description: Lecture/ discussion surveying the conquest, colonization, and consolidation of North American frontiers and the post-frontier development of the American West.

subject: HIST
title: Constitutional History of the U.S.
description: Origins, development of Constitution, Colonial to modern times.

subject: HIST
title: Race and Racism in America
description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history. (Cross-listed as AMST 440)

subject: HIST
title: History of American Workers
description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century. (Cross-listed as AMST 431)

subject: HIST
title: Colonial Latin America
description: PreColumbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social, and religious evolution to 1810; independence. (Cross-listed as LAIS 468)

subject: HIST
title: Latin America Since Independence
description: Political, economic, and social development since 1825; case studies from Brazil, Mexico, and Cuba.

subject: HIST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present. (Cross-listed as AMST 425 and SUST 481)

subject: HIST
title: Histories of Oceania I
description: Explores the diverse, interconnected histories of Oceania from ancestral origins through the early colonial period. Topics include voyaging, orality, land, gender, power, exchange, cross-cultural encounter, disease, colonization, resistance, and historiography. Additional focus on oral communication.

subject: HIST
title: Histories of Oceania II
description: Examines Oceania’s histories of protest during the colonial and post-colonial eras as responses to empire expansion. Explores ethical issues concerning these movements, emphasizing Hawai‘i experiences and their intersection with those across Oceania.

subject: HIST
title: United States in the Pacific
description: Growth of economic and political interests and policies.

subject: HIST
title: The Hawaiian Kingdom 1819–1893
description: Transformation of Hawai‘i into a state influenced by American and European ideas and institutions and Asian peoples, with an emphasis on instruction on writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of 20th-Century Hawai‘i
description: Formation of an American Hawai‘i with its unique local culture from 1898 to the present. Pre: upper division standing.

subject: HIST
title: World Maritime History
description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples. (Cross-listed as AMST 489)

subject: HIST
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons (Cross-listed as ASAN 492 and WGSS 492)

subject: HIST
title: Library Treasures: Exploring Special Collections & Archives
description: Conduct original research using general library materials, special collections, rare books, archives, and manuscripts, maps, and other historical documents that are uniquely available at libraries and archives at UH and beyond. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History Colloquium
description: Extensive or intensive treatment of special problems. (B) Philippines and Indonesia; (C) U.S. foreign relations; (D) history in Oceania; (E) Chinese traditional government. Recommended for honors students. Pre: 372 (or concurrent) or consent for (C); consent for (B) and (E).
prerequisites: 372 (or concurrent) or consent for (C); consent for (B) and (E).

subject: HIST
title: Senior Tutorial in History
description: Analysis of sources and evaluation of methods of historical writing. Students undertake a major research and writing project in field of special interest. Capstone

subject: ERTH
title: Mineralogy
description: DP DY. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the chemistry, crystalline structure, geologic occurrence, and physical properties of minerals. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
prerequisites: 200 or 201 and (CHEM 162/162L or CHEM 171/171L). or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Igneous Petrology
description: DP. (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Survey of composition, classification, and occurrence of igneous rocks. Hand-specimen identification and optical petrography of igneous rocks. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Hazards & Geomechanics
description: DP. (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Dynamic behavior of Earth’s surface, physical processes driving geohazards, and the risks pposed to society. Theory, practical techniques, and data visualization to measure, analyze, and interpret hazards and implications.
prerequisites: ERTH 101 or 103 or 104 or 106 or 130, MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A, and PHYS 151 or PHYS 170; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Field Methods
description: DP. Methods used in geological investigations in the field. Eight hours on Saturday in the field. (Spring only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Work of Water
description: DP DY. Physical properties of water, geological aspects of surface water and ground water occurrence, surface water and groundwater resources, use, and problems. (Spring only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Processes and Environments
description: DP DY. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Modern and past terrestrial and oceanic processes and environments that form sediments and sedimentary rocks, and their interpretation in Earth history. Incorporates properties, principles and applications of sedimentology, sedimentary petrology, geochemistry and stratigraphy. Repeatable one time. (Spring only)
prerequisites: 200 or 201 or consent, and 333 or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods. (Cross-listed as OCN 312)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Plate Tectonics and Geodynamics
description: Mechanics of lithosphere deformation related to plate convergence, rifting and strike-slip faulting, and the evolution of mountain belts. Use of theory and skillbuilding techniques to measure, describe, analyze, and interpret structures on Earth. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 200 or 201; and 250; and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; and PHYS 170.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Physics of Earth and Planets
description: DP DY. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Essentials of geophysics: application of physics understanding Earth, planetary, and solar dynamics. Topics include heat flow, gravity, geodesy, electromagnetism, seismology. Applications to core and mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, volcanoes, hydrology, environmental concerns, and archaeology.
prerequisites: 250, 303, 313, MATH 242, and PHYS 272, PHYS 272L; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Geochemistry
description: DP. Theory and applications of chemical principles and chemical analysis to Earth, ocean and environmental sciences; chemistry of hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere system, origin/ differentiation of Earth/Solar system, volcanic processes, natural radioactivity, organic/inorganic chemistry. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 200 or 201, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A, and CHEM 162 (or concurrent); or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Earth Materials and Structures
description: DP DY. (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lecture and lab that covers formation, occurrence, and identification of common minerals, rocks, and geologic structures. Lab work will include study of hand-samples, thin-sections, and field experiences. A-F only. (Fall only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Research in Earth Sciences
description: Research experience for Earth Science undergraduates. Under the guidance of a mentor, the student will conduct research and write a report on the background, methods, data, interpretations, and conclusions of the work. Repeatable one time only. Earth Sciences majors only. Junior standing or higher. CR/NC only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth sciences. Repeatable up to six credits. Junior/ Senior standing only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to mineral Physics
description: DP. Scientific study of the materials that make up the Earth. Properties of minerals on micro- and macro-scales; their properties and behavior. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Hawaiian Geology
description: DP. Consists of lectures, discussions, and field trips on the geologic processes and geologic history of the Hawaiian islands, with emphasis on writing communication.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Remote Compositional Analysis: Spectroscopy, Mineralogy, and Geochemistry of Planetary Surfaces
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces. Comparative studies of fundamental planetary science phenomena. Planetary surface science discoveries. Sustainability of planetary environments. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: (101 or 105 or 107 or ASTR 150; and CHEM 161; and MATH 241 and 242 and PHYS 272) with a minimum grade of C+; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters: Geoethics and the Layman
description: Evaluates ethical practice of geoscience as it relates to studies of natural disasters that result from geological and meteorological phenomena and the means that earth scientists interact with the laymen. (Once a year)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Energy and Mineral Resources
description: DP. Lecture and discussion on the origin, distribution and exploitation of fossil fuels, renewable energy resources and ore deposits. Coverage and detail will depend partly on student interest and background.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar
description: Gain professional training and practical experience giving scientific presentations emphasizing Earth and planetary sciences, including analysis of associated ethical issues. Grading is distributed 60/40 between three oral communication assignments and related ethics content.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
description: DP. Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites. Repeatable one time. Junior standing or higher, or consent. (Cross-listed as SUST 427)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Marine Geology
description: DP. Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins. (Cross-listed as OCN 423)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Environmental Geochemistry
description: DP. Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 425)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geochemistry
description: Covers aqueous geochemistry at the land-ocean interface, including the distribution of major and minor ions, trace metals, organic chemicals, and nutrients. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: 200 or 201, CHEM 162, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Plate Tectonics
description: DP. (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as OCN 444)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Earthquakes and Crustal Deformation
description: DP. Earthquakes and crustal deformation through modern seismological and geodetic observations; elastic properties of rocks, seismic waves, causes, detection, and location of earthquakes; crustal motions of the earthquake cycle; tsunami generation, liquefaction, and planetary observations. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Engineering Geology
description: Solutions of geotechnical problems by geologists and engineers through recognition, characterization, evaluation, and assessment of geologic processes that impact people, engineering structures, and engineering operations. Group format. ERTH, GEOL, and CEE majors only. Junior standing and higher. (Spring only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Hydrogeology
description: DP. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Occurrence, characteristics, movement, quality, development, and contamination of water in the Earth’s crust.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Remote Sensing
description: DP. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab on the concepts behind, geologic uses for, and techniques of satellite and airborne remote sensing. Lab work will consist of computer image processing. Field trips. Open to non-majors. (Alt. years: Spring)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Geospatial Information
description: Combined lecture/lab covering the collection, analysis and use of geospatially registered field data. (Fall only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: HDFS
title: Family Resource Management
description: Concepts, principles, and practices in managing family and household resources.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Family Financial Planning
description: Analytical approach to family financial planning from the perspective of changing family demands over the life cycle.
prerequisites: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Economics
description: Consumer rights, responsibilities, and resources; consumer decision-making; factors affecting consumer functioning within economy.
prerequisites: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Soft Skills for Success in the Workplace
description: Employers regard soft skills as key criteria when hiring and retaining employees. Students learn critical skills essential to work place success. This class prepares students to be work ready.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology
description: Fundamental scientific methodology, design and data collection; introduction to statistics and program evaluations, analysis of ethical issues.
prerequisites: HDFS 230 or FDM 200 or TPSS 200/SUST 211, or consent. Co-requisite: HDFS 380L.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Test design, computer use, data analysis.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, prepares students for direct, educational work with parents and children and for continued graduate work in child and family studies, counseling, psychology, social work and/or family life education. A-F only.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Mindfulness and Skillful Living
description: Lecture, discussion, and experiential activities of principles and practice of an evidence-based contemplative science discipline. Focuses on development of writing skills and ethical applications to daily life, with implications for youth, families, and society.
prerequisites: completed DS course (with a minimum grade of C).
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Marriage Development
description: Marital interaction and development; divorce and remarriage; resources and techniques for marital adjustment, enrichment, and growth.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Contemporary Family Issues
description: Investigation of current issues with impact upon family quality of life, with emphasis on the interdependent nature of families and their environments. A-F only.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Family Life Education Methodology
description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, with service learning on Family Life Education Methodology. Repeatable one time.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Community Program Development
description: Concepts and theories of community program development; principles, practices, and procedures in administration and supervision of volunteer services surveyed and analyzed.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Family Public Policy
description: Cross-national survey of family public policy; analysis, revision, and development of family public policy; impacts of policy on consumers and families.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Communications
description: Development, production, analysis, and evaluation of consumer materials for print media. Use of desktop publishing computer programs.
prerequisites: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Family Economics
description: Study of personal family resources and its interaction with the economy. Focuses on contemporary economic problems that affect the welfare of families.
prerequisites: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Topics in Family Resources
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs. Repeatable.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills in supervised work at an approved internship site and through analytical writing assignments and class discussions. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: (HDFS 230, 340, 360, 380, and 380L) with a minimum grade of C.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Capstone Portfolio
description: Preparation of a senior portfolio to be used as assessment of competence relative to national FCS standards. Includes extensive instruction on writing.
prerequisites: (HDFS 230, 340, 360, 380, 380L, and 492 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HDFS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent reading and research on a topic, done under supervision of a faculty member; outcomes contracted in writing with faculty member at beginning of semester. Repeatable two times or up to nine credits.
department: Human Development and Family Studies Department

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management
description: Survey of the field covering recruitment, selection, training, appraisals, grievance handling, communications, discipline, safety, compensation, and benefits.

subject: HRM
title: Leadership and Group Dynamics
description: Explore frameworks leaders can use to get things done in their teams. Examine how leaders can engage employees, improve decision-making, manage interpersonal dynamics, and adapt to changing internal and external contexts. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: HRM
title: Organizational Change and Effectiveness
description: Identify and evaluate methods to promote an effective change transition through efficient integration of corporate goals with the organizational culture.

subject: HRM
title: Labor Problems
description: Problems and economics of labor; history, structure, government, activities of trade unions.

subject: HRM
title: Labor and Social Legislation
description: Evolution, interpretation, and application of labor and social welfare legislation with special emphasis on impact of labor-management relations.

subject: HRM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

subject: HRM
title: Personnel Compensation
description: Selected topics. Emphasis on trends, recent issues, job evaluation, incentive systems, salary administration, executive compensation, profit sharing, benefit programs, retirement plans.

subject: HRM
title: The Staffing Process
description: Contemporary practices and trends in personnel planning for a competent work force; legal constraints, recruitment and selection, differential placement, training, career programming.

subject: HRM
title: Negotiation and Workplace Dispute Resolution
description: Theory and practice in negotiating; design and operation of different kinds of workplace dispute resolution (such as mediation, arbitration, and various alternatives); features exercises on bargaining and negotiation and advocacy and decision skills. (Spring only)

subject: HRM
title: Labor Management Relations
description: Review and analysis of basic factors that distinguish employment relations; examination of the development of recent legislation and programs at federal, state, and municipal levels. Specific consideration given to current problems on the mainland and Hawai‘i.

subject: HRM
title: Training and Development
description: Analysis of the current concepts and practices in the design, delivery, and assessment of training. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Seminar in HRM
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in HRM. Repeatable one time for different topics.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management
description: Analysis and critical evaluation of basic issues, policies, and trends in personnel administration. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Training and Development
description: Covers issues in design, delivery, and assessment of training, theoretical background of training and development process, types of training process, cross cultural and other types of diversity training and development of training modules. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Advanced Organizational Behavior
description: Organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Finance for Human Resource Management
description: Intends to give HR professionals a basic overview of the vocabulary and concepts of financial decision-making. Topics include: understanding financial information, budgeting, the finance of retirement and employee benefit and business valuation. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Compensation
description: Survey of compensation methods and procedures including job evaluations, incentive systems, salary administration, fringe benefits, appropriate legislation, policies and strategy issues of compensation systems. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: The Staffing Process
description: Recruiting and selection to optimize organizations including job design, job analysis, recruitment and selection methods, such as types of interviews and assessment centers, within legislative environment. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Negotiations and Labor Relations
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: International Human Resources
description: Exploring global trends in human resources with focus on the Asia Pacific region. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management-Topics
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in human resources. Repeatable four times with change in topics. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management Capstone
description: The final course in the MHRM c

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Genealogies
description: Survey of major Hawaiian chiefly lineages from the four main islands: Hawai‘i, Maui, O‘ahu and Kaua‘i. Political history from the Kumulipo to Western contact.

subject: HWST
title: Chiefs of Post-Contact Hawai‘i
description: Survey of Hawaiian chiefs from 1778 to the present, including genealogy, political function, and historical impact.

subject: HWST
title: Myths of Hawaiian History
description: DL. Thematic exploration of some common myths of Hawaiian history, including infanticide, slavery, feudalism, constant warfare, human sacrifice, and a limited pre-contact population, to determine the role of myth making in perceptions of Hawaiian history. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Mahi‘ai Kalo I: Taro Cultivation
description: Historical, cultural and philosophical foundations of the cultivation and uses of taro. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Mahi‘ai Kalo II: Advanced Taro
description: In depth-study of taro cultivation techniques and systems. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Mālama Loko I‘a
description: Study of traditional Hawaiian fishpond management with hands-on experience at He‘eia fishpond near Kāne‘ohe, merging traditional Native knowledge and ways of seeing with Western science. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as SUST 356)

subject: HWST
title: Pana O‘ahu: Famous Place Names
description: A survey of the famous place names in each ahupua‘a of O‘ahu, including accounts of mythical heroes, heiau, fishponds, wind, rain names, and their metaphoric value in Hawaiian literature.

subject: HWST
title: Pana Paemoku o Kanaloa: The Northwestern Hawaiian Islands
description: Will look at the use of the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands during pre-contact times, the historical period of the Kingdom of Hawai‘i, after the islands were ceded to the U.S., and the contemporary politics that surround the region today. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: La‘au Lapa‘au: Ho‘i Ka Mana i Loko
description: (3 Lec, 1 Lab) Advanced study and preparation of Hawaiian medicinal herb combinations.

subject: HWST
title: Issues in Modern Hawai‘i
description: DH. Cultural and political aspects of the current Hawaiian movement; historical colonization; conflicts over tourism, the military, and agriculture; forms of native self-determination. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Native Hawaiian Rights and Practices
description: DH. Students will strengthen their cultural, political, and legal foundations by: (1) reviewing Hawai‘i’s historical traditions and customs, (2) learning legal analysis techniques, and (3) applying those techniques to issues that govern native Hawaiian “rights” today. Sophomore or higher standing. (Fall only)
prerequisites: HWST 107, HWST 270, and HWST 341 (or concurrent) and HAW 102

subject: HWST
title: Visiting Artist Seminar
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Explore indigenous concepts through the media of a visiting indigenous master artist by looking at traditional media in indigenous cultures, and the possibilities for contemporary expression in other media. Repeatable one time. HWST majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: HWST 107, one course in HWST 220 level (HWST 222, HWST 224, HWST 225), one course in HWST 320 level (HWST 322, HWST 324, HWST 325); or consent

subject: HWST
title: Ka Mana Mo‘olelo: Topics in Hawaiian and Indigenous Mo‘olelo
description: Advanced course of study focusing on pressing topics connected with Hawaiian and Indigenous literatures, such as land struggle, climate change, or issues of governance and sovereignty. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: HWST
title: Māhele Land Awards
description: Practical guide to the researching of land awards and change in title for a single ahupua‘a, 1848 to present. Focus on field trips.

subject: HWST
title: Ceded Lands: Focus on Crown and Government Lands (1848 to Present)
description: Inventorying “Ceded Lands” in Hawai‘i with emphasis on historical, legal, and cultural changes from the Kingdom through statehood. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Research Methods
description: Survey course introduces students to a range of methods by beginning with a critical analysis of dominant research methodologies from the perspective of Indigenous scholars. Junior/senior standing only.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Institutions
description: Comprehensive analysis of institutions like Bishop Estate/Kamehameha Schools, OHA, Lili‘uokalani Trust, Department of Hawaiian Home Lands and The Queen’s Hospital.

subject: HWST
title: Wehe Ka ‘Āina: Cultivating a Sovereign Land Base
description: A Mālama ‘Āina and Kukulu ‘Aupuni course that identifies modern options in land access for reestablishing or resuming Hawaiian traditional and customary practices relating to food sovereignty and self-sustainability. HWST majors only. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: HWST 207/SUST 217 and HWST 343 and HWST 351; HAW 202 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: Ola I Ka Wai; Water and Sovereignty in Hawai‘i
description: Focus on Hawaiian relationships with Ka Wai Ola a Kane (water), traditional and contemporary water management practices, as well as contemporary resource management issues and native Hawaiian community advocacy for water.
prerequisites: HWST 307 and HAW 202 (or concurrent) or consent

subject: HWST
title: Kia‘i Kanaloa–Guarding Our Ocean Resources
description: Students will actively monitor and practice coastal and ocean stewardship in support of local communities and practitioners while also exploring how the Hawaiian worldview can plan a role in aloha ‘āina conservation movements. Repeatable one time. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: HWST
title: ‘Āina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as SUST 457)

subject: HWST
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies. (Cross-listed as NREM 458 and SUST 456)

subject: HWST
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 459)

subject: HWST
title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawai‘i. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 460)
