subject: HWST
title: Hawai‘i & Indigenous Economies
description: Students will map out indigenous economies by articulating cultural similarity and diversity between academic experience and professional experiences. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Mālama ‘Āina Field Methods Course
description: Intensive field methods program to research Mālama ‘Āina strategies. Introduces students to a variety of field techniques including land research, historical documents, ecological surveys, and Papakūmakawalu. Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. Junior standing or higher. (Summer only)
prerequisites: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356, or consent

subject: HWST
title: ‘Ike Akua Papakū Makawalu: Ancestral Understanding of Elements
description: Uses Dr. Pualani Kanahele’s Papakū Makawalu methodology to analyze akua as elements and as a paradigm for understanding ancestral knowledge. Senior standing or higher.
prerequisites: HWST 270, HWST 372 (or concurrent), and HAW 301 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: Mele Au Hou: Music and Native Identity
description: Presents Hawaiian music as it has been an avenue for native social, cultural and political expression in traditional and contemporary society. A-F only.
prerequisites: HWST 107 or HWST 343 or HWST 390; or consent

subject: HWST
title: Mahi Lā‘au Lapa‘au: Hawaiian Medicinal Horticulture
description: The science of planting and harvesting Hawaiian medicinal plants and exploring production and marketing strategies.
prerequisites: HWST 107, HWST 285 and HWST 385; or consent

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Aquatic Medicine
description: Identification, extraction and preparation of complexes of aquatic herbs to formulate a healing combination to contribute to maintaining overall health. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: HWST
title: Senior Seminar in Hawaiian Studies
description: Critical examination of existing research; individual or team development, execution, and evaluation of selected projects. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: senior major in Hawaiian studies or consent

subject: HWST
title: Senior Capstone Project in Hawaiian Studies
description: Capstone seminar designed to provide a culminating academic experience through in-depth examination, analysis, articulation, and projects relevant to a HWST area of concentration. Repeatable one time. HWST majors only. Senior standing only. A-F only.
prerequisites: HWST 341, HWST 342, [HWST 343 or HWST 390 or HWST 490 (or concurrent)] and [HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 285 or HWST 307/SUST 317 or HWST 356/SUST 356]

subject: HAW
title: Noi‘i Mele
description: Intensive study focusing on original compositions of Hawaiian poetry and song.

subject: HAW
title: Papahana Laeo‘o
description: Research for Plan B project/non-thesis. May include but not limited to internship with cultural practitioner. Repeatable up to six credits. HAW majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: HAW
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and graduate chair.

subject: HAW
title: Noi‘i Pepa Laeo‘o (Thesis)
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: HWST
title: Hawai‘i: Center of the Pacific
description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawai‘i and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

subject: HWST
title: Hawai‘i: Center of the Pacific
description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawai‘i and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupua‘a
description: Examination of the ahupua‘a system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the mālama ‘āina track designed to build critical writing skills. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 217)

subject: HWST
title: ‘A‘a Ka Hula: Introduction to Hula
description: Introductory-level, performance-based Hula (Dance) exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures). A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Kūnihi Ka Mauna: Introduction to Oli
description: (2 1-hr Lec, 1 2-hr Lab/practice) Introductory-level, performance-based Oli (Chant) exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Mo ʻolelo (History and Literatures).

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Visual Culture Studio
description: Introduction to a variety of material (fiber, bone, wood, and stone) and skills in the media used in the Hawaiian culture. Research and explore basic techniques within the media with emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses, and conservation. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio-Hana No‘eau Ma‘awe
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to a variety of fibers used in the Hawaiian culture. Emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses and conservation of the fibers. Areas explored are kapa, plaiting, netting and twining. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
description: Research and express personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through Hawaiian visual culture. Introduction to painting and drawing media and exploration of various materials and techniques as applied to individual student styles. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to Native Hawaiian perspective and world view in images used in print and the basic material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery through the indigenous eyes. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to the Literature of Native Hawaiians and Other Indigenous People Written in English
description: Surveys literature of Native Hawaiians and other Indigenous Peoples, especially to focus on the situational impetus from which these texts were created. (Fall only)

subject: HWST
title: Native Hawaiian Composition
description: Focus on studying and Applying Native Hawaiian composition practices from the nineteenth century into the present day.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Mythology
description: Survey of gods, ‘aumākua, kupua, mythical heroes, heroines, and their kinolau as the basis of traditional Hawaiian metaphor.

subject: HWST
title: Papahulilani Hawaiian Astronomy I
description: Introduction to Hawaiian ancestral understandings of the movements of the sun, moon and stars, and their use in ordering the Hawaiian year in planting, fishing, and ceremony. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: (107 and 270) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: HWST
title: Ho‘okele I: Hawaiian Astronomy
description: Introduction to Hawaiian views of astronomy and the stars used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators. Introduction and comparison to various Pacific island non-instrument navigation systems and star names. Restricted to majors.

subject: HWST
title: Ho‘okele I Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Stargazing laboratory to accompany 281.

subject: HWST
title: Ho‘okele II: Hawaiian Navigation
description: Hawaiian and other Oceanic canoe design, navigation, Pacific weather, sailing dynamics for canoes, and sail planning strategies used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators for long voyages.

subject: HWST
title: Ho‘okele II Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands on experience on voyaging skills and sailing canoes to accompany 282.

subject: HWST
title: Lā‘au Lapa‘au: Hawaiian Medicinal Herbs
description: Presentation of Hawaiian medicinal herbs including basic philosophy, identification, utilization, and preparation of such herbs for human ailments.

subject: HWST
title: Perspectives in Hawaiian Studies
description: Interdisciplinary lectures and discussions examining traditional and contemporary experiences in Hawaiian society and setting; resources, methods, and techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: HWST
title: Malama ‘Āina Resource Management Visual Technologies
description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies. (Cross-listed as SUST 317)

subject: HWST
title: Ke Ha ʻa Lā: Intermediate Hula
description: Intermediate-level, performance-based Hula (Dance) course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).

subject: HWST
title: Kū Ka Pūnohu: Intermediate Oli
description: Intermediate-level, performance-based Oli (Chant) course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures). A-F only.

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Art Media
description: Examine and explore advance techniques within the media and the customary and contemporary uses of a variety of material and skills used in traditional Hawaiian everyday life. Repeatable six times. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio-Hana No‘eau Ma‘awe
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Examine the customary and contemporary use of fiber materials and the skills used in Hawaiian culture. Research and explore advanced techniques within the media used in traditional Hawai‘i. A-F only. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
description: Advanced research and expression of personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through visual culture and language. Students will further their definitions, analysis skills, research, and understandings through painting and drawing media. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Advanced Native Hawaiian perspective in imagery in print and the material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery. Lecture-lab with studio work time. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Native Hawaiian Traditions in Literature
description: Discusses theoretical frameworks, main features, and cultural contexts of Hawaiian literature.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian and Indigenous Digital Media
description: Focus on studying, analyzing, and creating various forms of Hawaiian and Indigenous digital storytelling.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Genealogies
description: Survey of major Hawaiian chiefly lineages from the four main islands: Hawai‘i, Maui, O‘ahu and Kaua‘i. Political history from the Kumulipo to Western contact.

subject: HWST
title: Chiefs of Post-Contact Hawai‘i
description: Survey of Hawaiian chiefs from 1778 to the present, including genealogy, political function, and historical impact.

subject: HWST
title: Myths of Hawaiian History
description: Thematic exploration of some common myths of Hawaiian history, including infanticide, slavery, feudalism, constant warfare, human sacrifice, and a limited pre-contact population, to determine the role of myth making in perceptions of Hawaiian history. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Mahi‘ai Kalo I: Taro Cultivation
description: Historical, cultural and philosophical foundations of the cultivation and uses of taro. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Hydrogeology
description: DP (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Occurrence, characteristics, movement, quality, development, and contamination of water in the Earth’s crust.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Remote Sensing
description: DP (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab on the concepts behind, geologic uses for, and techniques of satellite and airborne remote sensing. Lab work will consist of computer image processing. Field trips. Open to non-majors.

subject: ERTH
title: Geospatial Information
description: Combined lecture/lab covering the collection, analysis and use of geospatially registered field data.

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary Geology
description: DP Comparative geology of the terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, tectonism, geomorphology, weathering; manned and unmanned space exploration.

subject: ERTH
title: Lunar Geology
description: Introduction to the basics of the geology and spectroscopy of our Moon. A-F only. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ERTH
title: Origin of the Solar System
description: Exploration of the origin and evolution of our solar system. Understanding the composition of the universe and its constituents (planets, asteroids, stars, comets, and meteorites). A-F only.
prerequisites: 101 or 103 or 104 or 106 or 130 and CHEM 161 and PHYS 170. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article. Repeatable one time.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth and Planetary Sciences Workshops
description: Designed for in-service school professionals to learn new approaches and concepts in the fields of earth and planetary sciences. Repeatable for credit. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: ERTH
title: Equations of Geophysics
description: Least-square approximation of functions by orthogonal series; potential, wave heat flow equations; boundary value problems; Bessel Hankel functions, spherical harmonics, potential theory, plane waves, spherical waves; emphasis on geophysics application.
prerequisites: MATH 244 or MATH 253A, PHYS 400, or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Explosive Volcanism
description: Explosive volcanic eruptions: from causes to consequences. Review of current physical volcanology including ascent and fragmentation of magma, transport and deposition processes in pyroclastic eruptions, volcanic crisis management and volcanic eruption scenarios. Seven-day field trip. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Theoretical Petrology
description: Derivation of phase diagrams from basic thermodynamics principles. Equilibria of natural silicate systems. Crystal chemistry, kinetics, diffusion, etc., Applied to igneous and metamorphic petrology.
prerequisites: 302, 325, and CHEM 351 (or concurrent); or consent. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Petrology of Ocean Lithosphere
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Petrogenesis of the oceanic lithosphere, including mantle processes and rocks from mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, oceanic hotspots, back-arc basins, and intra-oceanic arcs.

subject: ERTH
title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
description: Combined lecture/ discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and and planning.
prerequisites: PLAN 670 or consent. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as PLAN 671)

subject: ERTH
title: Lava Flow Rheology and Morphology
description: Effusion eruptions: from eruption to final flow form. Includes: rheology, effusion rate, heat loss, and field measurements, followed by inflation, flow forms, lava lakes, domes, flow hazard and modeling. Field trips to Kilauea and Makapuu. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Current Events in Volcanology
description: Discussion of active areas of volcanism and new publications on volcanology. Repeatable four times.

subject: ERTH
title: Submarine Volcanoes
description: Seminar exploring different aspects of submarine effusive and explosive volcanism, hydrothermal activity, and volcano-hosted ecosystems. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Isotopes and Trace Elements
description: Principles of radiogenic and stable isotope, and trace element geochemistry as applied to igneous petrology, mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, and terrestrial evolution.

subject: ERTH
title: Graduate Teaching Geology
description: For ERTH graduate students who lead, under faculty supervision, a scheduled class in Geology and Geophysics. The instructor will define the student’s responsibilities when offering ERTH 609, and these responsibilities must be met for a passing grade. As the consent to take the class must also be granted by the department chair, the chair will also review the responsibilities required by the instructor. ERTH graduate students only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and department chair

subject: ERTH
title: Graduate Seminar
description: Seminar in which students present a 15- to 20-minute talk on their research or a related topic. Meets once a week with two to three talks per meeting. Graduate students are required to register for this course once per year. Repeatable eight times.

subject: ERTH
title: Accelerated Introduction to Earth Sciences I
description: Lecture presenting a rapid-paced survey of earth sciences for graduate students. Includes origin of the Solar System, tectonics, volcanology, whole-earth composition, phase transformations, petrology (igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary), historical geology, and hydrology. Saturday field trips. (Fall only)

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data. Credit earned only one time for either 413 or 613.
prerequisites: 250 and MATH 242 (or concurrent), or consent. (Fall only)

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Field Study
description: Shipboard and land-based projects. Repeatable eight times.

subject: ERTH
title: Literate Programming With R and RStudio
description: Literate programming with R, RStudio, and R Markdown for data analysis and research. Introduction to Matlab for rapid modeling. Emphasis on the preparation of research papers for scholarly publication in the Earth and environmental sciences.
prerequisites: competence in basic differential and integral calculus. (Fall only)

subject: ERTH
title: How to Write a Scientific Paper
description: Designed for students who have collected data and want to know how to publish their work in a scientific journal. Covers the essential parts of paper preparation and submission. ERTH students only. A-F only.

subject: ERTH
title: Summer Fieldschool Program: Hydrogeophysics in Volcanic Environments
description: Will cover the full hydrogeophysical workflow including theory, acquisition design, field data acquisition, data processing, data inversion, and hydrogeological interpretation. Methods include ambient seismic, 3D electrical resistivity tomography and induced polarization, and self-potential.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geology
description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning. Repeatable one time, credit earned one time. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 627)

subject: ERTH
title: Electron Microprobe Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab on the principles of geochemical analysis by electron microprobe and X-ray fluorescence. Hands-on experience with the electron microprobe. Required to operate the UH electron microprobe.

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere- atmosphere system and remediation methods. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase and isotope chemistry of environmental contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Numerical Modeling of Physical Systems
description: Finite difference, finite element, and other modeling techniques applied to geological and geophysical problems. Physical modeling of heat flow, molecular diffusion, solidification and melting, deformation, fluid flow, wave propagation, and other phenomena. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics–Solid, Fluid, and Wave Mechanics
description: Continuum mechanics in geophysics, as applied to the deformation of Earth materials (elastic, viscous, viscoelastic, and plastic deformations) and seismic wave propagation (body waves, surface waves, anisotropy, and attenuation).
prerequisites: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent). (Fall only)

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics–Gravity, Magnetics, and Heat Transfer
description: Fundamental theory and practical applications of the use of gravity, magnetics, and heat conduction to probing the structure of the Earth; heat transfer via mantle convection is a major control on Earth’s internal structure.
prerequisites: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent). (Spring

subject: HRM
title: Negotiations and Labor Relations
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: International Human Resources
description: Exploring global trends in human resources with focus on the Asia Pacific region. A-F only.
prerequisites: HRM majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management-Topics
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in human resources. Repeatable four times with change in topics. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management Capstone
description: The final course in the MHRM curriculum. It provides students opportunity to integrate and apply previous course content to their professional organization offering a value-added opportunity to enhance organizational performance. A-F only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resources Leadership in Healthcare Organizations
description: Builds on previous leadership and management courses, focus on development of individual leadership skills emphasizing ethical and critical decision making, effective working relationships, and a systems-perspective relevant to healthcare organizations. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: ILO
title: Beginning Ilokano
description: HSL. Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets four hours weekly.

subject: ILO
title: Beginning Ilokano
description: HSL. Continuation of 101.

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano for Health Sciences
description: Development of listening, speaking, reading, writing and other communication skills designed specifically for Nursing, Dentistry, Dental Hygiene, Public Health and Social Work students. Culture integrated with language study.

subject: ILO
title: Intermediate Ilokano
description: HSL. Continuation of 102. Meets four hours weekly; three of four hours devoted to drill and practice.

subject: ILO
title: Intermediate Ilokano
description: HSL. Continuation of 201.

subject: ILO
title: Third-Level Ilokano
description: To further acquire and develop Ilokano language skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing, utilizes ethnographic and sociolinguistic approaches in order to further examine and interrogate the relationship of language and culture.

subject: ILO
title: Third-Level Ilokano
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano Aural Comprehension
description: Training in listening comprehension of different authentic and simulated materials as presented in documentaries, soap operas, radio and television news and other broadcasts, formal lectures, plays, natural conversations, songs, and student-created sitcoms and dramas.

subject: ILO
title: Contemporary Ilokano Literature
description: Conducted in Ilokano, this course explores the literary landscape of Ilokano literature from the perspective of Ilokano writers based in the Philippines as well as those outside of the country.

subject: ILO
title: Fourth-Level Ilokano
description: Continuation of 302. Conducted in Ilokano. Advanced reading, writing, and conversation. Contemporary Ilokano literature; cultural and historical topics.

subject: ILO
title: Fourth-Level Ilokano
description: Continuation of 401.

subject: ILO
title: Introduction to Ilokano for Interpreters
description: Techniques for interpreting Ilokano into English and vice versa. A-F only.

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano Interpretation Field Practicum
description: Provide extensive practical training in consecutive, simultaneous, sight and telephonic interpreting. It requires observation and study of interpretation strategies and techniques in relevant situations.

subject: ILO
title: Structure of Ilokano
description: DH. Introduction to phonology, morphology, and syntax.

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano for the Mass Media
description: Ilokano as the medium for print journalism, for radio show programming, and for television production. (Fall only)

subject: IP
title: Directed Elementary Language Study
description: Directed study of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or Pacific language not regularly listed by the department.

subject: IP
title: Directed Elementary Language Study
description: Continuation of 101.

subject: IP
title: Introductory Language Study
description: Introductory study of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or Pacific language. Contact hours and credits determined by student interests and faculty resources. Repeatable up to eight credit hours.

subject: IP
title: Directed Intermediate Language Study
description: Continuation of 102.

subject: IP
title: Directed Intermediate Language Study
description: Continuation of 201.

subject: IP
title: Topics in Indo-Pacific Literature/Culture
description: Study of a literature or culture of the Indo-Pacific area through readings in various fields in English. Repeatable up to six credit hours.

subject: IP
title: (Alpha) Introduction to Indo-Pacific Language and Culture
description: DH. Introduction in English to language(s) and culture(s) of Indo-Pacific country or region. (B) Indian; (C) Southeast Asian; (D) Polynesian; (E) Philippines.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher for (C). IP 101 and 102 courses in relevant language or consent for (B), (D), and (E).

subject: IP
title: Intermediate Language Study
description: Intermediate study of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or Pacific language. Contact hours and credits determined by student interests and faculty resources. Repeatable up to eight credit hours.
prerequisites: at least six credit hours of elementary study in the same language.

subject: IP
title: History of Early India
description: DH. Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century. (Cross-listed as HIST 301)

subject: IP
title: Directed Third-Level Language Study
description: Continuation of 202.

subject: IP
title: Directed Third-Level Language Study
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: IP
title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
description: DA. Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ASAN 303)

subject: IP
title: (Alpha) Southeast Asian Food, Music, and Rituals
description: DH. Study and analysis of the art and culture of Southeast Asian food, music, and rituals—history, forms, social development, influences, and impact, with an emphasis on oral and written communication. (P) Philippine; (V) Vietnamese. A-F only.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or consent for P.

subject: IP
title: Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
description: DL. Survey in English of traditional and modern literatures of Southeast Asia. (Cross-listed as ASAN 361)

subject: IP
title: Philippine Drama: History, Art, Culture
description: DL. Survey of Philippine drama from the perspective of sociocultural and historical experiences of the people in the country and in the diaspora. Emphasis is on ethical inquiry and the teaching of writing and oral communication. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: Philippine Contemporary Literature in English
description: DL. Critical survey of 20th-century Philippine literature written in English; cultural values. (Cross-listed as ENG 375)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: IP
title: Philippine Popular Culture
description: DH. Explores the ethics of Philippine popular culture forms; teaches students how to produce, act, and perform in a select media form; and engages students in writing a critical analysis of these pop cultural expressions. A-F only.

subject: IP
title: South Asian Literature in Translation
description: DL. Survey of traditional and modern literatures of South Asia; literature written originally in English.

subject: IP
title: Literatures of Ancient India
description: DL. Survey of South Asia literature from ancient times to the early medieval period; focusing on Sanskrit, Prakrit and Tamil poetry traditions. Readings in English translation. (Cross-listed as CLAS 366)

subject: IP
title: Introduction to South/Southeast Asian Film, History, Theory and Appreciation
description: DH. Study and analysis of South/Southeast Asian films– history, forms, development, theoretical framework and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical and aesthetic context. (B) Filipino. A-F only for (B).
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: (Alpha) Study Abroad
description: (B) Samoa; (C) Tahiti; (E) Vietnam. Repeatable one time for (B) and (C).

subject: IP
title: (Alpha) Southeast Asian Travelogue: People, Places, and Practices
description: DH. A virtual guided tour of Southeast Asia that explores its multiculture diversity through its people, places, and practices. (P) Philippines; (V) Vietnam. A-F only.

subject: IP
title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
description: DH. Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as REL 373)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: Classical Hindu Mythology
description: DH. Study of major myths of Epic Sanskrit literature, primarily with focus of the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Literary sources will be tapped

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science II
description: Overviews leadership fundamentals such as setting direction, problem-solving, listening, presenting briefs, providing feedback and using effective writing skills. Explores leadership values, attributes, skills, and actions in the context of practical, hands-on, and interactive exercises. Cadre role models and building stronger relationships among cadets through common experience and practical interaction are critical.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science II Lab
description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

subject: MSL
title: Intermediate Military Science I
description: Explores creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles through historical case studies and engaging in interactive student exercises. Cadets practice aspects of personal motivation and team building by planning, executing, and assessing team exercises. Focus is on continued development of leadership values and attributes through understanding of rank, uniform, customs and courtesies.

subject: MSL
title: Intermediate Military Science II
description: Challenges of leading complex, contemporary operational environments. Dimensions of cross-cultural challenges of leadership in a constantly changing world are highlighted and applied to practical Army leadership tasks and situations. Cadets develop greater self awareness as they practice communication and team building skills, and tactics in real world scenarios. Provides a smooth transition to MSL 301.

subject: MSL
title: ROTC Basic Camp
description: Four-week summer course conducted at Ft. Knox, Kentucky. Substitutes for ROTC basic course (101, 102, 201, and 202) and fulfills course requirement for admission to ROTC advanced courses. Credit will be given for 203 or basic courses, but not both.

subject: MSL
title: Leading Small Organizations I
description: (2 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Challenges cadets to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills with demands of the ROTC Advanced Camp. Challenging scenarios related to small unit tactical operations will develop self-awareness and critical thinking skills. Cadets will receive systematic, specific feedback on their leadership abilities, and analyze/evaluate their leadership values, attributes, skills and actions. A-F only.

subject: MSL
title: Leading Small Organizations II
description: (2 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Intense situational leadership challenges to build awareness and skills in leading small units. Decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members under fire are explored, evaluated, and developed. Military operations are reviewed to prepare for the ROTC Advance Camp. Cadets apply principles of Law of Land Warfare, Army training, and motivation to troop leading procedures; and are evaluated on what they know and do as leaders. A-F only.

subject: MSL
title: ROTC Advanced Camp
description: Five-week summer field training exercise conducted at Fort Knox, Kentucky. Arduous and intensified leadership training is conducted throughout the five-week period. Required for U.S. Army commissioning.

subject: MSL
title: History of Military Warfare
description: Lecture/discussion on the art and science of warfare concentrating on U.S. military history from the Colonial Period to present. Generally restricted to Army ROTC students, requiring twenty pages of graded writing assignments. A-F only.

subject: MSL
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Limited to military science students who have had at least one previous military science course for which a grade of B or higher was earned and a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or better.

subject: MSL
title: Fundamentals of Leadership
description: Introduces students to the fundamentals of leadership. Activities challenge students to connect theory to practice, develop positive relationships through application of effective leadership concepts for leader development, and team-building. A-F only.

subject: MSL
title: Leadership Challenges and Goal Setting
description: (3 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Develops proficiency in planning, execution, and assessment of complex operations; students will learn to assess risk, make ethical decisions, function as a staff member, and provide leadership performance feedback to subordinates; emphasis on oral communication. A-F only.

subject: MSL
title: Transition to Lieutenant
description: (3 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Explores dynamics of leading in complex situations of current military operations. Examines differences in customs and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism. Interaction with nongovernment organizations, civilians on the battlefield, and host nation support are examined and evaluated. Case studies, scenarios, and What Now, Lieutenant? exercises prepare cadets to lead as commissioned officers in the U.S. Army. A-F only.

subject: MSL
title: Advanced Military Research
description: Directs the student to conduct detailed research on a military topic and present to the department leadership plus assist MSL 400 series students on a battle analysis. Repeatable up to eight credits. Must be in Military Science and Leadership Program or Military Service member in junior or greater standing.

subject: MCB
title: Cell and Molecular Biology
description: DB. Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology. A-F only. (Cross-listed as BIOL 275)
prerequisites: Pre: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171/171L and CHEM 272.

subject: MCB
title: Research Ethics
description: DS. Introduction to the ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Based on case studies, students will discuss and write about ethical issues in research. Issues include humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data, genetic technologies and record keeping. This course is designed for students with majors in the natural sciences. A-F only. (Cross-listed as MICR 314)
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 171 (or concurrent), or MATH 307 (or concurrent), or MATH 311 (or concurrent), or PHYS 170 (or concurrent), or CHEM 272 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MCB
title: Molecular Cell Biology I
description: DB. Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level. (Cross-listed as BIOL 407)
prerequisites: Pre: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275/275L and CHEM 273, or consent.

subject: MCB
title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
description: DB. Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules. (Cross-listed as BIOL 408 and MBBE 408)
prerequisites: Pre: C (not C-) or better in 407; or consent.

subject: MCB
title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Biology Laboratory
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) A laboratory to accompany 407 and 408. (Cross-listed as BIOL 408L)
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 407 (or concurrent) or BIOL 408 (or concurrent).

subject: MCB
title: Immunology
description: DB. Structure and biological actions of antigens and antibodies; fundamentals of antibody synthesis; the relation of immunology to biology and medical sciences. Recommended: BIOL 275/275L. (Cross-listed as MICR 461)
prerequisites: Pre: MICR 351 or BIOL 171; or consent.

subject: MCB
title: Immunology Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Basic exercises and experiments in immunology, immunochemistry, immuno-biology to illustrate principles of 461. (Cross-listed as MICR 461L)

subject: MCB
title: The Biology of Cancer
description: Integrative, in-depth focus on the genetics, cell biology, and molecular basis of cancer. Combination of classroom lectures and problem-based discussions in small groups. Addresses ethical implications of cancer research and treatment. A-F only. MCB or BIOL majors only. Senior standing or higher. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as BIOL 472)
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 407 (or concurrent) and BIOL 408 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: MCB
title: Bacterial Genetics
description: DB. Genetic analysis and molecular basis of transmission replication, mutation, and expression of heritable characteristics in prokaryotes. (Cross-listed as MICR 475)
prerequisites: Pre: MICR 351 or BIOL 275, or consent.

subject: MCB
title: Bacterial Genetics Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of transfer and expression of prokaryotic genes: transformation, conjugation, transposon mutagenesis, preparation and analysis of plasmid and chromosomal DNA. (Cross-listed as MICR 475L)

subject: MBBE
title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering. (Cross-listed as BIOL 304)
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Essential Biochemistry
description: Introduction to basic concepts of cellular biochemistry and metabolic pathways as applied to nutritional, medicinal and environmental biochemistry. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: (CHEM 152 or CHEM 272) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Biotechnology
description: DB. General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues. (Cross-listed as BIOL 401)
prerequisites: Pre: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
description: DY. (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 401. Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry. (Cross-listed as OCN 454L)
prerequisites: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: GES
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory. GES majors only. (Cross-listed as OCN 463)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: GES
title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with Bayesian inference, make predictions using artificial neural networks, and analyze data in space and time using the Python language with biological and geophysical datasets. GES majors only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: GES
title: Communication of Research Results
description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material. GES majors only in their final semester. (Cross-listed as OCN 490)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: GES
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article. GES majors only. (Cross-listed as OCN 499)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: GRK
title: Elementary Greek
description: Grammar and vocabulary, with reading of simple Greek.

subject: GRK
title: Elementary Greek
description: Continuation of 101.

subject: GRK
title: Intermediate Greek
description: Development of reading and translation skills. Emphasis on prose.

subject: GRK
title: Intermediate Greek
description: Continuation of 201: emphasis on poetry.

subject: GRK
title: Greek Historians
description: Selections from Herodotus, Xenophon, and others.

subject: GRK
title: Greek Epic
description: Selections from Homer, Hesiod, and others.

subject: GRK
title: Greek Philosophy
description: Selections from Plato, Aristotle, and others.

subject: GRK
title: Greek Drama
description: Selections from Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides.

subject: GRK
title: Greek Lyric
description: Selections from Sappho, Alcaeus, and others.

subject: GRK
title: Seminar in Greek Studies
description: Study of an author or phase in Greek studies.
prerequisites: any two 300-level GRK courses, or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Language in Hawai‘i: A Microcosm of Global Language Issues
description: Survival kit for life in Hawai‘i: Introduction to Hawaiian and language related issues enhancing communicative experience in Hawai‘i. Examination of social, cultural, political, and linguistic cross-cultural interaction locally and globally. Taught in English/Hawai‘i Creole English.

subject: HAW
title: Elementary Hawaiian I
description: Introductory course in Hawaiian language focused on the foundational skills of language acquisition: speaking, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding.

subject: HAW
title: Elementary Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of 101.

subject: HAW
title: Intensive Elementary Hawaiian
description: Content of 101 and 102 (Elementary Hawaiian I & II) covered in one semester.

subject: HAW
title: I Ka ‘Olelo No Ke Ola
description: Accelerated lecture/lab to bridge fluent speakers mainly from Kula Kaiapuni into Kawaihuelani’s system of Hawaiian that reflects a Hawaiian worldview, including HAW 101-201 content, grammar, writing, and spelling conventions. Students matriculate into HAW 202.

subject: HAW
title: Intermediate Hawaiian I
description: Continuation of 102 with continued development in the foundational skills of language acquisition: speaking, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Increased emphasis on reading or traditional texts.

subject: HAW
title: Intermediate Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of 201.

subject: HAW
title: Intensive Intermediate Hawaiian
description: Content of 201 and 202 covered in one semester. Meets two hours daily, plus lab work.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Literature in Translation
description: Survey of Hawaiian literature, including prose narration and poetry with reference to Polynesian and Western themes and forms.

subject: HAW
title: Papa Mele I (Mele in the Hawaiian Language Classroom)
description: The incorporation of mele and the performance thereof for the enhancement of second language acquisition in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Third-Level Hawaiian I
description: Continuation of 202 with emphasis on increasing proficiency in speaking/conversation, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Conducted in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Third-Level Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Conversation
description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Mo‘olelo Pōkole
description: Development of reading comprehension, pronunciation, vocabulary, and Hawaiian cultural knowledge through reading of Hawaiian language short stories. Short stories are from primary and secondary sources written by a variety of authors across different time periods.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Composition
description: Intensive work in the grammatical, semantic, and pragmatic dimensions of composition writing in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Listening Comprehension and Transcription
description: Development of listening comprehension through transcription and discussion of tape recordings.

subject: HAW
title: Ulu ka Hoi
description: Lecture offering focused study and creation of Hawaiian language newspapers with a concentration on the characteristics of writing in this genre. Students will produce a monthly newsletter in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Mo‘omeheu Hawai‘i
description: A survey course on the study of traditional Hawaiian culture including origins, the socioeconomic system, land tenure, religion, values, and the arts. The course will be taught in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Hana ‘Oe a Kani Pono-Hawaiian Radio Broadcasting
description: Combined lecture/lab involving students in the planning and production of a weekly Hawaiian language radio broadcast. Includes research, writing, and voicing of mele and their stories on live radio.
prerequisites: 302 or 384 (or concurrent with consent), or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Haku Mele
description: Composers and Their Compositions. Provides a venue which will allow students to analyze, dissect and discuss mele (song, poetry and chant), paying close attention to the style of composition by identifying reoccurring nuances found in mele composed by the same as well as various authors.

subject: HAW
title: Fourth-Level Hawaiian I
description: Advanced speaking/conversation, discussion, listening comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Conducted in Hawaiian. Transcribing and translating recordings of native speakers in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Fourth-Level Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of 401.

subject: HAW
title: Mo‘olelo Hawai‘i
description: Survey of the major works by Hawaiian scholars writing about the history and culture of Hawai‘i including David Malo, Kamakau, Kepelino, and John Papa Î‘i.

subject: HAW
title: Ka‘ao Hawai‘i
description: Survey of the core literature written by Hawaiian scholars, including both historical and mythological epics and folk tales.

subject: HAW
title: I Le‘a Ka Hula I Ka Ho‘opa‘a (Mo‘olelo, Ka‘ao, Mele and Hula)
description: The incorporation of mele and hula performance with mo‘olelo and ka‘ao.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i–Political Thought in Hawaiian
description: Intensive study of Hawaiian political thought in writing and speech. (Cross-listed as POLS 303C)

subject: HAW
title: Ka Hō‘ike Honua
description: Study of Hawaiian land tenure practices through readings and discussions of audiotapes, written primary sources, maps, wind names, rain names, ‘Ōlelo no‘eau (wise sayings), and mele (poetry). Readings are drawn from 19th and 20th century Hawaiian newspapers and other primary sources.

subject: HAW
title: Ma Ka Hana Ka ‘Ike
description: Study of traditional Hawaiian language and cultural practices through hands-on applications and lectures.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Mo‘olelo–Creative Writing in Hawaiian
description: Study and composition of written works in various creative

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust I: Resource Protections
description: Security and trust in computers, networks, and society. Security models. Access and authorization. Availability and Denial-of-Service. Trust processes and network interactions.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Programming
description: Introduction to the theory of Artificial Intelligence and the practical application of AI techniques in Functional (Common LISP and/or Scheme) and Logic (Prolog) programming languages. Students gain practical experience through programming assignments and projects. A-F only.
prerequisites: (215 or 212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns. ECE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ECE 369)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Computing Ethics for Lab Assistants
description: A lecture/discussion/internship on ethical issues and instructional techniques for students assisting a laboratory section of ICS 101. The class uses multiple significant writing and oral presentation activities to help students learn course content.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Junior Project
description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in intermediate-level design, implementation and presentation of a software project that may have been initiated in ICS 296. CS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Software Engineering II
description: Continuation of 314. Project management, quality, and productivity control, testing and validation, team management. Team-oriented software-implementation project.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Programming for the Web
description: Introduction to emerging technologies for construction of World Wide Web (WWW)-based software. Covers programming and scripting languages used for the creation of WWW sites and client-server programming. Students will complete a medium-sized software project that uses languages and concepts discussed in class.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: The Science, Psychology and Philosophy of Systems Design
description: Scientific, psychological and philosophical bases of systems design, including a survey of human-factors and ergonomic standards; the nature of innovation and creativity as it relates to systems design. Web-enhanced course. (Once a year)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Database Systems II
description: Very large database systems, data integration, data warehousing, designing big data systems, parallel query processing, distributed transactions.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Network Science Methodology
description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages. (Cross-listed as DATA 422)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Data Security and Cryptography I
description: Secret communication and confidentiality data storage. Elements of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Classical ciphers. Symmetric key cryptography. Public key cryptography. Data security in cyber space.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Application Frameworks
description: Experience producing applications with at least two different applications frameworks. A-F only.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Computer Security and Ethics
description: Theoretical results, security policy, encryption, key management, digital signatures, certificates, passwords. Ethics: privacy, computer crime, professional ethics. Effects of the computer revolution on society. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Computer System Security
description: Information flow, confinement, information assurance, malicious programs, vulnerability analysis, network security, writing secure programs. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Programming Approaches to Software Quality Assurance
description: Examination of best practices associated with developing and supporting software applications with respect to potential security risks. Will augment software engineering practices learned in other courses with the basic principles of cybersecurity.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Digital Forensics
description: Provides students with the knowledge of underlying principles and skills to identify, preserve, and extract electronic evidence for further analysis.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Computer Architecture
description: Memory management, control flow, interrupt mechanisms, multiprocessor systems, special-purpose devices.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Concurrent and High-Performance Programming
description: Principles of concurrent and high performance programming. Multi-threading in C and Java for shared-memory programming. Distributed memory programming with Java. Introduction to cluster computing. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205) and 332 and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Data Science Fundamentals
description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist. A-F only. (Cross-listed as DATA 434)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory. Recommended: MATH 307. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as DATA 435)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Big Data Analytics
description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Theory of Computation
description: Grammars, sequential machines, equivalence, minimalization, analysis and synthesis, regular expressions, computability, unsolvability, Gödel’s theorem, Turing machines.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Analytical Models and Methods
description: Applications of mathematical methods in computer science with emphasis on discrete mathematics, numerical computation, algebraic models, operations research.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Parallel Algorithms
description: Introduction to parallel models of computation and design and analysis of parallel algorithms. (Fall only)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Data Networks
description: Network analysis, architecture, digital signal analysis and design; circuit switching, packet switching, packet broadcasting; protocols and standards; local area networks; satellite networks; ALOHA channels; examples.
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Software Design for Robotics
description: Sensors, actuators, signal processing, paradigms of robotic software design, introduction to machine learning, introduction to computer vision, and robot-to-human interaction. A-F only. Recommended: 312 and 313. (Once a year: spring)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust II: Information Assurance
description: Channel security. Trojan and noninterference. Basic concepts of cryptology. Cryptographic primitives. Protocols for authentication and key establishment.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Artificial Intelligence
description: Survey of artificial intelligence: natural language processing, vision and robotics, expert systems. Emphasis on fundamental concepts: search, planning, and problem solving, logic, knowledge representation.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Artificial Intelligence for Games
description: Techniques to stimulate intelligence in video games: movement, pathfinding with A* search, decision/behavior trees, state machines, machine learning, tactics. Extend games with your own AI implementations; experience “shootout” contests for the best AI algorithm/implementation. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314 and (PHYS 151 or PHYS 170).
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Human Computer Interaction I
description: Application of concepts and methodologies of human factors, psychology and software engineering to address ergonomic, cognitive, and social factors in the design and evaluation of human-computer systems.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Hypermedia
description: Basic issues of interactive access to information in various formats on computers. Available hardware and software: editing, integration, programming. Implementation of a sample information system.
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Design for Mobile Devices
description: Lecture introducing design issues, programming languages, operating systems and mark-up languages for internet-enabled mobile devices, such as cell phones and PDAs. A-F or Audit. (Spring only)
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: ICS
title: Cognitive Science
description: Introduces basic concepts, central problems, and methods from cognitive science. Identifies contributions from disciplines such as cognitive psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosop
department: Department of Information and Computer Sciences

subject: HIST
title: Library Treasures: Exploring Special Collections & Archives
description: DH Conduct original research using general library materials, special collections, rare books, archives, and manuscripts, maps, and other historical documents that are uniquely available at libraries and archives at UH and beyond. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: History Colloquium
description: DH Extensive or intensive treatment of special problems. (B) Philippines and Indonesia; (C) U.S. foreign relations; (D) history in Oceania; (E) Chinese traditional government. Recommended for honors students.
prerequisites: 372 (or concurrent) or consent for (C); consent for (B) and (E).

subject: HIST
title: Senior Tutorial in History
description: Analysis of sources and evaluation of methods of historical writing. Students undertake a major research and writing project in field of special interest. Capstone course requires a 20-25 page minimum final research paper. A-F only.

subject: HIST
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual projects in various fields. Maximum 5 credit hours. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Historiography
description: History of history and historians; philosophies of history.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Digital History
description: Examines the various ways that the production, presentation, and learning of history through digital media is changing the way people access and process information about the past.

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Topics in Environmental History
description: Introduction to leading themes, methodologies, and topics in world environmental history. Drawing on new and influential scholarship, readings explore the diverse forces that shape humans’ adaptation to and impact on the natural world. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar on Water in History
description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history. (Cross-listed as SUST 610)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in World History
description: Analysis, research, and discussion of themes and issues in study of history of humankind. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in World History
description: Selected themes— feudalism, economic and industrial development, etc.— important in global history. Topics pre-announced. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Readings in European History
description: Selected topics for advanced reading; (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years: spring for (D)); (Alt. years: fall for (E))

subject: HIST
title: Ethnographic History
description: Critical inquiry into historical representations of the “other” and ways in which modern historians have used culture and other anthropological concepts to write and think about the past.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to Cultural Studies
description: Graduate seminar designed to introduce history students to the multidisciplinary theories that are appropriate to cultural studies. A-F only. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Research in European History
description: Selected topics for advanced research. (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: HIST
title: Topics in European Colonialism
description: Selected topics for comparative advanced reading and research. (D) early modern; (E) modern. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Topics in Historical Methods and Theory
description: Seminar covering one specific approach to historical methods or theory. The goal is a deep engagement with a particular historical approach via research and reading not bounded by region, time, or specialty. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Atrocity Crimes: Law and History
description: Seminar on history of mass atrocity and international justice in the modern world. Topics include postWWII Allied war crimes prosecution, post-cold war ad hoc international criminal tribunals, and contemporary international law and national legal systems. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Readings in Russian History
description: (B) early Russia; (C) modern. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Slavery and Modern Memory
description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts. A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 619)

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Readings in American History
description: Interpretations and literature of important themes and problems. (B) early America; (C) the Republic to 1877; (D) industrial America; (E) recent America. Repeatable one time per alpha. (Alt. years for (B)) ((B) Cross-listed as AMST 610)
prerequisites: appropriate 400-level U.S. history course or consent for (D) and (E); graduate standing or consent for (B) and (C).

subject: HIST
title: Research in American History
description: (B) early America; (C) the Republic to 1877; (D) industrial America; (E) recent America; (F) foreign relations. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Topics in American History
description: Seminar in advanced research and readings: (B) social and intellectual; (C) foreign relations; (F) the West; (K) business, labor, and technology. Repeatable one time for (B), (C) and (K). ((B) Cross-listed as AMST 646); ((F) Cross-listed as AMST 614); ((K) Cross-listed as AMST 647)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar: Comparative Asia
description: This reading seminar in the comparative history of modern Asia will introduce graduate students to themes, particularly in social, cultural, and intellectual history, which lend themselves to comparison across the region. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Topics in Southeast Asia
description: Reading and research seminar on themes about the past and present of Southeast Asia in a comparative framework.

subject: HIST
title: Historiography of Southeast Asia
description: Examination of contested boundaries of Southeast Asia, the various historiographic traditions, the colonial legacy, and the current issues emerging from a dialogue of historians from the “region” and the outside world. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Modern Southeast Asian History
description: Graduate level reading seminar in modern Southeast Asian history. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: The Seas in Southeast Asian History
description: Seminar on the seas in Southeast Asian history. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar: Vietnamese History
description: Reading and research seminar on Vietnamese history. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Chinese History
description: Problems and readings in political, social, and cultural history. (B) early; (C) middle; (D) modern. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar: Islam and Islamic Civilization
description: Readings on the rise, spread, and development of Islamic cultures and civilizations throughout the world down to modern times. Repeatable one time. Recommended: 354.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in South Asian History
description: Graduate-level reading and research seminar on topics in Indian and South Asian history. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Japanese History
description: Problems, principal sources of bibliographic information. (B) traditional period to c.1600; (C) early modern 1600–1868; (D) 1868 to present; (E) 20th-century diplomatic. Repeatable one time per alpha.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Korean History
description: Reading major interpretive works, and research in selected topics. (B) reading; (C) research. Repeatable one time per alpha.

subject: HIST
title: Topics on War in History
description: Research seminars on topics on war in history. Repeatable one time.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in Histories of Oceania
description: Reading and research on major issues, topics, and themes in the history of Oceania. Repeatable three times. (Cross-listed as PACS 675)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in History of Hawai‘i
description: Reading seminar with short papers required. Covers Kingdom of Hawai‘i and 20th-century Hawai‘i in alternate years. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: Hawaiian Historical Research: Documents and Methods
description: Research and writings emphasizing the interpretation of Hawaiian and English language primary sources. Development of source materials, approaches, and methods in Hawaiian history. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate standing only. HAW 301 with a B or better, or instructor consent.

subject: HIST
title: Directed Research
description: Individual research topics. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean. Maximum 2 credit hours. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Restricted to plan A (thesis) students. consent.

subject: HIST
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: HIST
title: Institutional History of Korea
description: Major political, economic, and social institutions. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Historical Literature
description: Reading and use of numerous genres of Chinese historical literature and document

subject: PDET
title: Technology Skills for Educators
description: Exploring technology resources needed for integration into classroom instruction. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology I
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology II
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology III
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology IV
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: LTEC
title: Theory and Practice in Educational Technology
description: The profession of educational technology and the role of instructional designers. Theoretical and philosophical foundations underlying practice that include instructional systems theory, needs assessment, change theory, and relevant learning models. Practical applications of these theories to solve instructional problems in real-life settings. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Innovations in Educational Technology
description: Innovative technological advances and new media in the field of educational technology and their application in instruction. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Educational Technology Research and Evaluation
description: Review of existing research in media/ed technology, with activities leading to the preparation of final study or project proposal. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Introduction to Online Learning
description: Introduction to principles of online learning and their application in formal and informal instructional settings. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Instructional Design and Development
description: Basic concepts and techniques of instructional design and development, for application to solving instructional problems in real-life situations. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Visual Design
description: Theory and practice involved in planning educational/instructional graphic and photographic material for print and computer-based media. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: E-learning Theory and Design
description: Principles of e-learning theory as well as design and development for instruction. Application to new media and web authoring. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Digital Video Design
description: Development and utilization of digital video for the purpose of improving the teaching-learning process. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Developing Online Learning
description: Design and development of online instruction for educational and training settings. Implementation of online course elements and strategies for content delivery, course management, student interaction, course evaluation and assessment of student learning. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: LTEC 673 or consent; LTEC majors only or consent

subject: LTEC
title: Emerging Technologies for K-12 Teaching
description: Exploration and impact of emerging technologies in K-12 classroom teaching and learning and ramifications of these technologies on administrative structure of schools. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Facilitating E-learning Communities
description: Exploration of tools and design considerations for effective online communication and development of learning communities.

subject: LTEC
title: Educational Technology in Informal Learning Environments
description: Exploring the nature, application, and use of educational technology in informal learning environments, such as museums, cultural institutions, tourist attractions, and visitor information centers. Focusing on the analysis, selection, and development of various media choices. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Learning with Emerging Technologies (Alpha)
description: Exploration and evaluation of new tools and strategies for teaching and learning. (B) mobile learning; (C) free/open software; (D) educational games and simulations; (E) critical trends. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only. (Fall only for (B) and (D)) (Spring only for (C) and (E))

subject: LTEC
title: Interactive Multimedia Production
description: The utilization and application of advanced authoring tools, combining video, animation, graphics, and sound to develop student-centered learning. Primarily for advanced LTEC students.

subject: LTEC
title: Authoring E-learning Environments (Alpha)
description: Conceptualization of instructional design and its application to the development for e-learning environments: (B) assisted instruction (CAI); (C) managed instruction; (D) virtual reality; (E) animation. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Programming for Games and Simulations
description: Project-based exploration of the breadth of programming in the context of educational games and simulations. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Design Thinking for Creative Problem Solving
description: Using real-world problems, students learn an agile design and problem-solving process that is human-centered, iterative, and cultivates individual and group creativity. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Assessment and Evaluation in Educational Technology
description: Evaluation and assessment processes, sources, and instruments applicable to systematic appraisal of learning with technology. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Research Design: Multiple Methods and Traditions
description: Explores research methods used in educational technology with a focus on developing a design for dissertation research. Emphasis is on the use of digital technologies in data collection and analysis. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: LTEC
title: Qualitative Research in Educational Technology
description: Introduction to qualitative research traditions and designs. Emphasis will be on the use of digital technologies in data collection and analysis. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: LTEC PhD majors only. EDUC PhD majors only with consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Quantitative Research in Educational Technology
description: Application of methodological and statistical concepts in a projects-based classroom framework. Formative and summative evaluation, measurements, descriptive, and inferential statistics. A-F only.
prerequisites: LTEC PhD majors only. EDUC PhD majors only with consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Distance Education Technology
description: Technical and instructional considerations for developing, delivering, managing, and evaluating distance education including voice, video, print, hypermedia and data transmissions.

subject: LTEC
title: Designing Online Learning
description: Planning, needs assessment, standards and learning theory applied to the design of online learning and assessment plans.

subject: LTEC
title: Technical Issues in Educational Technology (Alpha)
description: Applying theory of management in instructional technology support services and delivery systems. (B) management; (C) systems; (D) networks. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Social and Ethical Issues in Educational Technology
description: Examination of social and ethical issues as they relate to technology in instructional settings. Focus on social justice and societal impact. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Cognition and Technology
description: Interdisciplinary course that introduces a range of empirical research examining aspects of cognition such as attention, memory and learning, and how technologies can enhance and/or hinder these cognitive processes. Repeatable 3 times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDCS 686 and LIS 686)

subject: LTEC
title: Learning Design Studio
description: Practicum in instructional design, development, and technology in academic and non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings in seminar format. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
