title: LTEC Training and Evaluation Practicum
description: Practicum in educational technology training and evaluation in formal and informal settings, under close supervision, plus class meetings in hybrid format. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: LTEC majors only or consent; instructor consent

subject: LTEC
title: Seminar in Technology Leadership
description: Supervised activity in application of research in learning design and technology to teaching/training experiences. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Practicum in E-learning
description: Practicum in e-learning in academic or non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable for 3 credit hours maximum each time.

subject: CUL

Discussion of illusion, identity, time, the future, the bizarre and major concepts in fantasy literature. (B) fairies, devils and fantasy; (C) the fantastic, the strange and science fiction. Repeatable one time in different alphas.
department: Department of Languages and Literatures of Europe and the Americas

prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

A-F only. (Once a year)

description: Selected topics in international management and industrial relations: (B) Chinese management systems; (C) Japanese management systems; (D) management of multinational corporations; (F) contemporary issues in international business foreign direct investment; (G) cross-cultural communication in international business; (H) interactive strategies in Asian culture; (I) international human resource management; (J) international joint ventures; (K) international management of technology; (M) Korean management systems; (N) multinational corporation and environmental issues; (O) strategy of the multinational corporation; (P) international transfer of technology. Repeatable four times per alpha.
prerequisites: MBA or MAcc students only (except for (D). Pre: consent.

subject: MGT

subject: MGT

subject: MBIO

prerequisites: MATH 215 or 216, or MATH 241 or 242, or consent.

description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research. (Cross-listed as OCN 682)

subject: MKT

subject: MKT

subject: MKT

subject: MKT

prerequisites: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Marketing Strategy
description: Focuses on theories of strategic marketing and planning. Explores the theoretical principles of marketing concepts, tools, and processes that can be used to help an organization develop a sustainable competitive advantage. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Selected Marketing Topics
description: Selected topics in any aspect of marketing to increase exposure to the range of issues researchers commonly confront. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Directed Research
description: Reading and research in an area of marketing under the direction of faculty member(s). A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Survey of Mathematics
description: FQ Selected topics designed to acquaint nonspecialists with examples of mathematical reasoning. May not be taken for credit after 215 or higher.

subject: MATH
title: Math for Elementary Teachers I
description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas, problem solving, and reasoning. Number systems, place value, fractions, and properties of operations. Prospective elementary education majors only.

subject: MATH
title: Math for Elementary Teachers II
description: FQ Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas; problem solving; reasoning and proof; and using symbolism. Patterns and algebraic thinking, place value and decimals, geometry, and mathematical modeling.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus: Elementary Functions
description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational exponential and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing. A- F only.
prerequisites: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus
description: FQ Algebra review. Polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing. Trigonometric functions, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, and related topics.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus and Elements of Calculus for Economics and the Social Sciences
description: FQ Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, algebra of functions, techniques of graphing, differentiation and integration of algebraic functions, applications in economics and social sciences. A-F only.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Programming
description: (3 hr) Introduction to numerical algorithms and structured programming using Fortran, MATLAB, or other appropriate language.
prerequisites: one semester of calculus (203, 215, 241, 242, 243, 244, 251A, 252A, or 253A) (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for Business and Social Sciences
description: FQ Basic concepts; differentiation and integration applications to management, finance, economics, and the social sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Calculus I
description: FQ Basic concepts; differentiation, differential equations and integration with applications directed primarily to the life sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Calculus II
description: Differential calculus for functions in several variables and curves, systems of ordinary differential equations, series approximation of functions, continuous probability, exposure to use of calculus in the literature.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus I
description: FQ Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations.
prerequisites: 241 or 251A or a grade of B or better in 215; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus III
description: Vector algebra, vector-valued functions, differentiation in several variables, and optimization.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus IV
description: Multiple integrals; line integrals and Green’s Theorem; surface integrals, Stokes’s and Gauss’s Theorems.

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus I
description: FQ Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Compared to 241, topics are discussed in greater depth.
prerequisites: assessment and consent, or a grade of A in 140X

subject: KRS
title: Practicum in Health and Exercise Science
description: Culminating 160 hours of supervised practicum experience in health, wellness, fitness assessment, lifestyle management, and/or exercise leadership. Qualifying hours are contingent upon instructor’s approval in the registered semester. Health and Exercise Science majors only.
prerequisites: current CPR and First Aid Certification, 152, 332, 353, 354, and 463; or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Program Design in Strength Training and Conditioning
description: Designed to provide theoretical and practical experience in supervision of a strength training center. Content includes program design, exercise techniques, organization, testing, evaluation, methods of strength development, facility design and special populations. Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Athletic Training Clinic
description: Introduction to the Professional Athletic Training Education Program and the Clinical Education Plan. Students are required to document all requirements and demonstrate proficiency in basic clinical skills. Repeatable one time. A-F only. ATEP Program students only. (Once a year)

subject: KRS
title: AT Practicum I
description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: AT Practicum II
description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Practicum III
description: Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Practicum IV
description: (5 2-hr Practicum) Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Counseling in the Schools
description: History, philosophy, and organization of school counseling programs. Counselor role and functions, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, current methodology and resources. (Meets EdD common core elective.)

subject: KRS
title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen with emphasis on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Repeatable one time. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ANAT 603)
prerequisites: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Repeatable one time. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ANAT 604)
prerequisites: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Human Growth and Development—Life Span
description: Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Major theories and related research on human development; applications in policy planning and service delivery in counseling.

subject: KRS
title: Counseling: Theory and Practice
description: Theory and techniques of counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

subject: KRS
title: Scientific Principles of Physical Conditioning
description: Application of physiological principles to physical conditioning and athletic performance.

subject: KRS
title: Muscular Strength and Power Development
description: Interpretation of scientific principles of muscular strength and power development. Examination of muscular adaptations to increased and decreased use.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience I
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Must be completed during first semester post admission into program. Athletic Training majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience II
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum includes duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Practicum must be completed during second semester post admission to the program. Athletic Training majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience III
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required. Athletic Training majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience IV
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required. Athletic Training majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Clinical Practicum
description: (V) (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced clinical practicum in which the BOC certified or certification eligible graduate student experiences an enhancement of athletic training knowledge and refinement of athletic training skills. Repeatable up to 10 credits. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Research Practicum
description: (V) (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced research practicum in which the BOC certified or certification eligible graduate student deepens their understanding and enhances their critical thinking abilities in order to contribute to the advancement of the discipline and the athletic training profession. Repeatable four times, up to 12 credits. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Clinical Examination of Pathology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body. Athletic Training majors only. A-F only.

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Orthopedic Assessment
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Advanced knowledge and skills of athletic training as they are specifically applied to the understanding, treatment, and rehabilitation of sport-related injuries. (e.g. epidemiology, legal, ethical concerns, sports psychology, pharm, drug abuse, health issues)

subject: KRS
title: Therapeutic Interventions: Modalities
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Physiology principles and operational procedures of contemporary therapeutic modalities as they relate to the care and treatment of athletic injuries. Athletic Training majors only. (Fall only)

subject: KRS
title: Therapeutic Interventions: Rehabilitative Exercise
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Concepts and principles of comprehensive rehabilitation programs (therapeutic goals and objectives, exercise selection, methods of evaluation and recording progress, progression and return to competition criteria, and physiological effects of tissue trauma and inactivity). Athletic Training majors only. (Spring only)

subject: KRS
title: General Medical Conditions in Sports Medicine
description: An examination/evaluation of general medical conditions associated with sports medicine including pathology, care and treatment. Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Seminar in Athletic Training
description: Designed to provide the student with analytical skills and practical experience relative to research as it applies to sports related injuries. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Therapeutic Exercise
description: Advanced concepts and evidence-based principles of rehabilitation programs. Enhancement of previously learned therapeutic exercise techniques and integration of therapeutic modalities and therapeutic exercise, including objective and functional goal setting and evaluation for appropriate progression and expedited return to activity. KRS majors only.
prerequisites: 617 and 618 or basic therapeutic exercise and therapeutic modalities courses, or consent

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Capstone Experience
description: Capstone culminating experience preparing the student for the computer-based BOC Exam and for a career in athletic training. Follows the students’ didactic and clinical preparation in the 12 competency areas of athletic training. Repeatable one time. KRS majors only. A-F only. Co-requisite: 612. (Spring only)

subject: KRS
title: Administration in Kinesiology
description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as EDEA 623)

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Community Counseling
description: Philosophy, organization, and function of community service agencies, programs, and institutions as related to professional work in counseling.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Practicum
description: Pre-practicum training for supervised experiences in school, community, and human service organization.

subject: IS
title: Introduction to Environmental Humanities
description: Introduction to the environmental humanities, which rests at the intersection of the arts, humanities, and environmental studies. (Cross-listed as SUST 260)

subject: IS
title: Sophomore Seminar
description: Special inquiry-based study of multi-disciplinary topics in particular historical, cultural, geographical, environmental, or other contexts. Emphasis on primary sources and/or fieldwork and extensive instruction in writing. (B) biological science; (H) humanities; (P) physical science; (R) arts; (S) social science; (T) literature. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as HON 291) DB for (B); DH for (H); DP for (P); DA for (R); DS for (S); DL for (T)

subject: IS
title: Field Study
description: Pre-arranged systematic field investigation of selected topics. Pre: written proposal approved by Honors director and appropriate faculty member. Repeatable up to 16 credits.
prerequisites: written proposal approved by Honors director and appropriate faculty member.

subject: IS
title: Ethics, Aging & Society
description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging. A-F only. (Cross-listed as COA 305)

subject: IS
title: Independent Study Tutorial
description: Independent study tutorial. A-F only.

subject: IS
title: Native Americans and Native Hawaiians
description: Comparative-contrastive examination of similarities and differences between Native Americans and Native Hawaiians as the only indigenous peoples of the U.S. with special attention to sociohistorical parallels and mutual contacts since contact with Europeans. Perspective is explicitly interdisciplinary by drawing not only on sociology and history, but also on archaeology, ethnology, linguistics and still other disciplines. A-F only. Pre: HIST 152 and an introductory course in cultural anthropology, political science or sociology; or consent. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: HIST 152 and an introductory course in cultural anthropology, political science or sociology; or consent.

subject: IS
title: Ethnohistory
description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e. the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history. A-F only. Pre: HIST 152, or consent. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ANTH 327)

subject: IS
title: Information Technology and Culture
description: Investigation of the impact of information technologies on contemporary culture from a variety of perspectives. A-F only. Pre: upper division or consent.

subject: IS
title: Science and Culture
description: Cultural studies of science from historical, philosophical, sociological and literary perspectives. Examination of intersections of science, race, gender and environment. A-F only. Pre: upper division or consent.

subject: IS
title: Human Values and the Environment
description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts–literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics–in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature. A-F only. Pre: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as SUST 340)
prerequisites: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent.

subject: IS
title: Pidgin and Creole Languages
description: Nature, history, structure, and geographic distribution of pidgins and creoles. Pre: LING 102 or consent. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as LING 347)

subject: IS
title: One Health: Preparing for the Next Pandemic
description: Focuses on the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study of a global health problem that is optimally approached from a One Health perspective. A-F only. Pre: ANSC 200, BIOL 101, MICR 130, PH 201, or consent of instructor. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as TRMD 350)
prerequisites: ANSC 200, BIOL 101, MICR 130, PH 201, or consent of instructor.

subject: IS
title: People, the Ocean and the Environment
description: People’s impact on quality of coastal and ocean environments, especially Hawaiian; scientific, legal, socioeconomic aspects. Ocean pollution, ocean technology. Pre: OCN 201, ORE 202, or ZOOL 200; or consent.
prerequisites: OCN 201, ORE 202, or ZOOL 200; or consent.

subject: IS
title: British Life and Culture
description: For Study Abroad Program students participating in the UH Mānoa Semester in London. Emphasis is placed on understanding within historical contexts important issues for contemporary British society—particularly those of class, power, gender, and race. A-F only. Pre: participation in London Semester Program.

subject: IS
title: One Health Journal Club
description: Students gain critical reading skills in the presentation and discussion of published literature on One Health-related topics. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. Pre: PH 441. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as TRMD 395)

subject: IS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Directed reading and research. Repeatable two times.

subject: IS
title: Ocean Internships and Research
description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Pre: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100/BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal. (Cross-listed as BIOL 400)
prerequisites: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100/BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal.

subject: IS
title: The Humboldt Brothers’ Legacy
description: Life and thought of the two Humboldt brothers. Alexander (1769-1859) helped to lay the foundations of modern science, including geology, geography, botany, zoology, physiology and anthropology. Older, less well-known Wilhelm (1767–1835) was an influential statesman, classical scholar, man of letters, humanist, political philosopher, anthropologist and linguist, and founded the University of Berlin. Review of the two polymaths’ impact on modern science in the Americas, the Pacific and Asia. A-F only. Pre: upper-division or consent.

subject: IS
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language. Pre: ANTH 152. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ANTH 414 and LING 414)

subject: IS
title: One Health Practicum
description: Provide certificate students with real-world experience and opportunity to integrate and apply classroom learning in a professional environment. Intended for students who prefer to pursue a supervised, practical experience rather than a research-based project. A-F only. Pre: PH 441. (Cross-listed as TRMD 485)

subject: IS
title: Environmental Practicum
description: Field experience in study and abatement of environmental problems under faculty direction. Project proposal, narrative activity log, and documentary report are required. Pre: upper division standing, courses in appropriate discipline, and consent.
prerequisites: upper division standing, courses in appropriate discipline, and consent.

subject: IS
title: One Health Seminar
description: Weekly presentations and discussions on current events and research in the field of One Health. Presentation topics may include research progress, literature reviews, or research proposals. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. Pre: PH 441. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as TRMD 490)

subject: IS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Directed reading and research. Repeatable one time.

subject: IS
title: Field Study in Gerontology
description: Individually designed field experience for advanced certificate in gerontology students. Placements arranged at community programs, research sites, and special projects at the Center on Aging. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: IS
title: Integrative Seminar in Gerontology
description: Integrative seminar. A-F only. Pre: graduate standing or consent.

subject: IS
title: Principles of Applied Evolutionary Ecology: Biodiversity Loss, Biological Invasions and Emerging Disease
description: Combined lecture-discussion on the ecological and evolutionary underpinnings of the coupled process of biological invasion, disease emergence and biodiversity loss. A-F only. Pre: consent. (Once a year)

subject: IS
title: Laboratory A in Applied Evolutionary Ecology: Biodiversity Loss, Biological Invasions and Emerging Disease
description: Combined lecture-laboratory on the ecological and evolutionary underpinnings of the coupled process of biological invasion, disease emergence and biodiversity loss. A-F only. Pre: consent. (Once a year)

subject: IS
title: Laboratory B in Applied Evolutionary Ecology: Biodiversity Loss, Biological Invasions and Emerging Disease
description: Practical laboratory/ field rotation on the ecological and evolutionary underpinnings of the coupled process of biological invasion, disease emergence and biodiversity loss. Continuation of 650 and 651L. A-F only. Pre: 650 and 651L, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: IS
title: Topics in Biocultural Diversity and Conservation
description: Biological, cultural, and linguistic conservation are intimately linked, but rarely studied simultaneously. Adopts a trans-disciplinary view of diversity and conservation of nature, cultures, and languages, along with issues in anthropology, law, and ethics. (Fall only)

subject: CUL
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Seminar consists of a series of presentations by certificate faculty on topics of ongoing research. Presentations will open current debates about theory and method in cultural studies. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: CUL
title: International Cultural Studies: History and Theory
description: Seminar on the history and theory of interdisciplinary cultural studies. The politics of culture are examined in comparative perspective, focusing on their significance for identity formation, intercultural relations, and global flows of images, people and capital. Approaches to the study of media and popular culture are taken up in terms of their relevance for contemporary issues, especially in Hawai‘i and the Asia/Pacific/U.S. region. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychometrics
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Experimental Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Experimental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Physiological Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Comparative Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Developmental Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Developmental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Social Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Social Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Child Treatment
description: Psychological interventions for youth, as well as parent training. Repeatable two times.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Treatment: Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy
description: Training in cognitive-behavioral strategies for treating adults. Repeatable one time. Enrolled in Clinical Studies Program only. PSY major only.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Psychopathology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Clinical Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Psychological Therapies
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Health Psychology: Behavioral and Biological Bases
description: Psychological and biological bases of health psychology and behavioral medicine. Overview of cognitive, behavioral, and psychophysiological mechanisms; theories and methods of prevention in physical disease.

subject: PSY
title: Internship in Clinical Psychology
description: Repeatable one time.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Clinical Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable 30 times.

subject: PSY
title: Community Psychology Seminar
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Community Psychology Research
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PUBA
title: Survey of Public Policy and Analysis
description: Students will learn about the policy making process, the results of policy decisions and how public policy is assessed, analyzed, and responded to. Also discusses important policy issues that currently fill the political landscape. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Research Methods for Policy Evaluation
description: Explores methodological approaches to the evaluation of public policies and strengths and weaknesses of various social science research methods. Students will learn how to employ them to determine the effectiveness of various public policies. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Foundations of Nonprofit Management
description: Broad overview of nonprofit organizations, including what it means to be a nonprofit, strategies of nonprofit organizations, and the management of nonprofits. Topics include advocacy, leadership, and evaluating success. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Multicultural Leadership in Public Service
description: Develop students’ culturally agile leadership to allow them effectively lead in work on international, regional, and local projects and problems of compelling public interest that cross cultures. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Practicum and Internship
description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses. (Cross-listed as PACE 495)
prerequisites: any two other PACE courses or consent

subject: PUBA
title: Directed Reading and Research in Public Administration
description: Independent research and reading on topics in public administration, public service, and community development. Repeatable one time.

subject: PUBA
title: Program Evaluation for Public and Nonprofit Organizations
description: Methods for evaluating the effectiveness of programs in the public and nonprofit sectors; performance measurement to inform managerial decision making. (Fall only)

subject: PUBA
title: Introduction to Public Administration
description: Develop a comprehension of the history and foundation of public administration. Topics include economic, political, and social dynamics; decision-making and leadership theories, management challenges, human resources, budgeting, program evaluation, policy, and technology. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PUBA
title: Organizations: Theory and Change
description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as CEE 620)

subject: PUBA
title: Leadership and Ethics
description: Applies leadership and ethical theories to public and non-profit sectors, focusing on ethical leadership; emphasizes critical thinking to address value conflicts; and teaches moral reasoning as a practical professional skill. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PUBA
title: Effective Communication in Public Administration
description: Knowledge and skills to effectively communicate in the public sector. Focus on communication foundations and skills, levels and contexts of public sector communication, and handling challenges such as diverse and multi-cultural settings. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PUBA
title: Public Administration Personnel Management
description: Understand the pivotal role that effective human resource management (also known as personnel management) plays in improving organizational effectiveness. Topics include managing diversity, employment law and discrimination, performance appraisal, and labor-management relations. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PUBA
title: Public Administration Research Methods
description: Introduction to research methods for public administrators to understand the principles and methods used to conduct and analyze valid research. Examples are oriented to the field; theory and hands-on practice utilized. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PUBA
title: Public Budgeting
description: Institutions and issues related to public-sector budgeting at federal, state, and local levels. Process of developing public budgets and constraints on public policy reflected in budgets. PUBA majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PUBA
title: Policy Analysis and Implementation
description: Explore contemporary policy issues relating to public administration practice. Develop analytic techniques and models of public policy-making processes, administrative rules, and policy implementation strategies. Learn how social forces, political, and economic pressures influence policy orientation. PUBA majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PUBA
title: Reforming Public Organizations
description: Looks at the challenges and opportunities for changing public organizations so that they may be more successful in meeting their public responsibilities and better places for people to work. Focus is on the creation of positive images of organization and effective change strategies. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: The Political Environment of Public Organizations
description: Seminar on the role of public managers in shaping public opinion and public policy. Using evidence from theory and practice presents students with tools for understanding management roles within a political context.

subject: PUBA
title: Strategies of Change: Leaders and Leadership
description: Explores the key elements of leadership in public settings by examining what leaders actually do, looking at popular media portrayals of leadership, and talking together with guests about the challenges of leadership, effective followership, and positive change. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Law, Economics, and Public Administration
description: Explore U.S. law as applied to public instituti

subject: ITM
title: Programming Application Systems
description: Introduction to applications programming. Fundamentals, essential logic, file handling, report writing. Emphasis on systems development and disciplined programming. A-F only.
prerequisites: ICS 101, or LTEC 112 and 113, (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: ITM
title: Information Systems Analysis and Design
description: Analysis and design of systems in organizations. Includes role of general systems concepts, systems development life cycle, identifying systems requirements, logical and physical design. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Database Systems
description: Introduction to database management and data structures, including database planning and design, normalization, relational and network data models, and physical organization and implementation. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Current Topics in ITM
description: Repeatable three times with permission of department chair.

subject: ITM
title: Information Systems in Organizations
description: Practice of information systems in organizations. Capstone course for MIS majors. A-F only.
prerequisites: ITM 353 and ITM 354 (or concurrent), and BUS 311.

subject: ITM
title: Electronic Commerce
description: Survey of electronic commerce technologies and business strategies, with an emphasis on technology and application development. The development of web-based and multimedia applications; the impacts of EC on business strategy; legal and ethical issues. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: (Alpha) Advanced Topics in Information Systems
description: Computerized management information systems, operations research or business statistics: (B) software systems economics; (C) advanced topics in programming; (D) web-based application development; (E) advanced technology in MIS; (F) systems development; (G) database systems; (H) advanced business applications; (J) ethics of technology; (K) business intelligence. Repeatable with permission of department chair.

subject: ITM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

subject: ITM
title: Networking and Security
description: Basic concepts in networking and security. Network standards and technologies. Network planning and design. LANs and WANS, wireless networking. Security threats and countermeasures. Security planning and policies. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Advanced Security
description: Designed around the plan-protect-respond cycle. Security threats, cryptographic security, access control, identity management, firewalls, intrusion detection systems, host hardening, and application security. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: ITM
title: Current Topics in Information Systems
description: Selected current practices and trends in decision sciences and MIS. Repeatable three times. ACC, CIS, and BUS majors only.

subject: ITM
title: Project Management, Information Technology and Change
description: Lectures and discussions to contextualize knowledge and techniques of project management in organizational change, globalization and outsourcing, global teamwork, intercultural awareness, negotiation and leadership. Semester long group project. Open to all graduate students. (Once a year)

subject: ITM
title: Enterprise Data and Information Management
description: Framework of policies, people, processes, and technologies to control, protect, deliver, and enhance the organizational data assets; best practices and technologies for database management, data warehousing, and data curation; support of enterprise data governance. MIS, ICS, MIS-BBA majors only. Senior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Business Intelligence and Data Analytics
description: Addresses business intelligence and data analytics at operational, tactical, and strategic levels using basic data science techniques, including visual, descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics methods and hands-on learning using current software tools. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Enterprise System Architecture and Management
description: Foundations of enterprise information systems design and architecture to support business strategy, processes, data, and IT/IS services; integrating cloud-based and loT infrastructure; management and maintenance of organizational IS/IT infrastructure and operations. MIS, ICS, MIS-BBA majors only. Senior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Digitally-Enabled Business Processes
description: Business process analysis, design, and implementation of new business processes enabled by digital platforms. Concepts, methods, and techniques to support prototyping and user interface design are considered. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ITM
title: Management of Health Information Technology and Population Health
description: Covers latest trends/innovations in HIT designed to reduce costs, improve quality/access, and reduce outcome disparity through population health management. Includes management of financial, organizational, and professional barriers to effective HIT. A-F only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)

subject: ITM
title: Capstone Course
description: Individual- or team-based project with a client organization, conducted under faculty supervision, as capstone project to complete masters level work in the Masters of Science in Information Systems. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. Graduate students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: students must complete 15 semester hours and core masters courses before capstone.
degrees: Masters of Science in Information Systems

subject: ITM
title: Directed Research
description: Reading and research in ITM under the direction of a faculty member. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Doctoral Seminar in Information Systems
description: Extensive and critical review of the IS research literature. Can be retaken for credit. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: ITM
title: Research Seminar in E-Business in the Asia Pacific Region
description: Overview of the current research issues in e-business with focus on the Asia Pacific region. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: ITM
title: International IT Organizational Research Methods
description: Overview of current survey methodology and analysis in global information systems research. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: ITM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in an area of information technology management under the direction of faculty member(s). A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: INS
title: Principles of Insurance
description: Risk management and insurance application to business and personal financial decision-making. Introduction to basic risk management concepts and techniques. Analyze various types of insurance: including life, property, casualty, liability, health, disability, and long-term care.

subject: INS
title: Property and Casualty Insurance
description: Treatment of risk of financial loss of personal and business property and resulting loss of income occasioned by fire and allied perils. Forms of insurance used by individual business executives and firms including crime, transportation, liability, and worker compensation.

subject: INS
title: Life Insurance
description: Treatment of the risk of premature death through use of various life insurance policies. Policy forms, calculation of premiums, reserves, non-forfeiture values, underwriting, regulation of policy provisions, related coverage.

subject: IS
title: Mānoa International Exchange
description: Designed for students accepted for participation in an international exchange program while enrolled at UH Mānoa. Repeatable unlimited times, credit for 12 credits only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: admittance to an international exchange program.

subject: IS
title: Marine Option Program Seminar
description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective. (Cross-listed as BIOL 104)

subject: IS
title: Introduction to Applied Gerontology: Helping Yourself and Others to Thrive in Later Life
description: DS Introduction to essential information on aging and the field of gerontology. Counters ageist stereotypes, develops skills for translating research into practice, and provides an introductory survey course for the undergraduate certificate in aging. A-F only. (Crosslisted as COA 206)

subject: IS
title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders. (Cross-listed as ENGR 250)

subject: IS
title: Introduction to Environmental Humanities
description: DH Introduction to the environmental humanities, which rests at the intersection of the arts, humanities, and environmental studies. (Cross-listed as SUST 260)

subject: IS
title: (Alpha) Sophomore Seminar
description: DA DB DH DL DP DS Special inquiry-based study of multi-disciplinary topics in particular historical, cultural, geographical, environmental, or other contexts. Emphasis on primary sources and/or fieldwork and extensive instruction in writing. (B) biological science; (H) humanities; (P) physical science; (R) arts; (S) social science; (T) literature. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as HON 291) DB for (B); DH for (H); DP

subject: LWPA
title: International Criminal Law
description: Designed to give an understanding of international criminal law. Will review all aspects of international criminal law from substantive international crimes to criminal liability and sentencing by domestic and international tribunals. LAW majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in Korea
description: Provides students with an understanding of the law, society, and legal systems in Korea. Areas of law including constitutional, civil, criminal, and business are discussed. Emphasis on South Korea. Law majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Human Rights in Asia
description: A survey of human rights norms, institutions, and implementation mechanism of international human rights law in light of the rapid development of regional cooperation and integration in Asia. Offered to provide advanced human rights courses at the Law School. The purpose is to convey an understanding of the current situation concerning human rights in Asia, and to facilitate a chance to think about what the future may bring.

subject: LWPA
title: (Alpha) Topics in International Legal Studies
description: Selected topics presented by faculty members or visiting scholars, focusing upon subjects in the Pacific and Asian area. (B) business; (C) China; (G) global; (H) Philippines; (I) India; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Pacific; (S) Southeast Asia; (T) Topic 10; (U) Topic 11; (V) Topic 12; (W) Topic 13; (X) Topic 14. LAW majors only for (B) and (H). Repeatable six times for (C), (I), (J), (K), (P), (S), (T), (U), (V), (W), (X); repeatable five times, up to 18 credits for (B), (H); not repeatable for (G).

subject: LWPA
title: International Business Transactions
description: An examination of the law, rules, and practices relating to transborder commercial transactions. Roughly half of the semester focuses on international sales transactions, the remaining portion focuses on domestic and multinational governance of the international business arena.

subject: LWPA
title: Native Hawaiian Rights
description: Status and evolution of rights of Native Hawaiians to the land and its usufructs. Potential of utilizing native rights based on statute, custom, and use to develop new and expanded rights.

subject: LWPA
title: (Alpha) Topics-Native Hawaiian Law
description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawai‘i, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability. Repeatable up to 9 credits. LAW students only.

subject: LWPA
title: Legal History of Hawai‘i
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the unique legal history of Hawai‘i, emphasizing particular legal controversies that have shaped the law of our island society. LAW majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Emerging Hawai‘i Water Issues
description: Introduction to the legal framework for water resource management in Hawai‘i; case studies illuminate the litigation process and evolution of the public trust, precautionary principle, and other legal, scientific, and policy areas.

subject: LWPA
title: International Law
description: Evolving process of formulating rules to govern nations and peoples of the world in their attempts to solve problems recognized as requiring global solutions.

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in China
description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ASAN 686)

subject: LWPA
title: Comparative Law
description: Introduction to the civil law tradition, particularly as exemplified by the legal systems of East and Southeast Asia. After a brief review of comparative law study and the historical development of the civil law, the course will examine the structure and role of the courts, judicial process, the legal profession and constitutional law and administrative law in Western Europe and in the Asian civil law countries.

subject: LWPA
title: International Human Rights Advocacy
description: Applying international human rights law and legal skills to promote and protect human rights by way of United Nations Charter-based human rights mechanism, treaty-based mechanism, or other international human rights institutions.

subject: LWPA
title: International Economic Law
description: Problem-based course teaches theory and practice of interrelated global private regulation and public development consequences, as situated in cross-border transactions and dispute resolution in world law, international investment law, and international financial law.

subject: LWPA
title: Pacific Islands Legal Systems
description: Study of substantive rules of one or more Pacific Islands jurisdictions, development of legal systems, relationship of legal systems to culture and tradition.

subject: LWPA
title: International Intellectual Property
description: Primer on the World Intellectual Property Organization and the treaties it administers. Will explore the various international legislative and judicial developments in intellectual property as well as analyze international methods to harmonize several regional and national laws to protect rights in trademarks, patents, and copyrights. Students will be exposed to issues of territoriality and jurisdiction, international antitrust issues, and international dispute resolution, and human rights implications of international intellectual property rights protections.

subject: LWUL
title: American Legal Systems
description: Introduces foundational concepts in American legal systems. Engages students in legal analysis and techniques of legal advocacy. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: LWUL
title: American Legal Systems II
description: Introduces conceptual and historical foundations of systems of public and private ordering in the U.S. and its territories. Subjects include federalism, constitutional democracy, separation of powers, and the common law. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: LTEC
title: Technologies for Academic Success
description: Virtual and hands-on analysis of technology resources and utilization in learning.

subject: LTEC
title: Technologies for Academic Success– Business
description: Virtual and hands-on analysis of technology resources and utilization in learning with an emphasis on business education. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Educational Media Technology
description: Introduction to educational technology theory and practice with an emphasis on meaningful integration of technology and media into a variety of face-to-face and online learning environments for diverse populations. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Technology for Teachers
description: Introduction to the application of educational technology in teaching and learning using strategies in design, selection, development, integration, and evaluation. Interactive delivery via distance education technologies. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Video Technology
description: Overview of video uses in educational contexts. Includes video planning, production, and simple editing procedures, as well as selection, evaluation, and integration into learning plans.

subject: LTEC
title: Technology in Education
description: Planning and implementation of computer systems and applications for effective integration into classroom settings. Emphasis is on methods and strategies for using digital technologies to enhance standards-based learning by K-12 students.

subject: LTEC
title: Social Media: Links to Lifelong Learning
description: Exploration of social media and effects on individuals, communities, and world. Analysis and evaluation of impacts and ethical implications of social media, with emphasis on writing. Includes service learning and research project.

subject: LTEC
title: Foundations in Design Thinking
description: Using real-world problems, students learn a creative problem-solving process that is human-centered and iterative, and practice design thinking mindsets (embracing ambiguity, learning from failure, and bias toward action) as they tackle the problem. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: LTEC
title: Directed Activity
description: Individual work, supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, and/or projects. Repeatable two times, up to six credits.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development in Educational Technology: Technology Skills for Educators
description: Exploring technology resources needed for distance learning and classroom integration. Repeatable two times.

subject: LTEC
title: PDET: Technology Skills for Educators
description: Exploring technology resources needed for integration into classroom instruction. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology I
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology II
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: LTEC
title: Professional Development Education Technology III
description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course. Repeatable one time.

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nursing Practice
description: Essential principles of pharmacology using a pathophysiologic approach with emphasis on administering medications and evaluating their effects. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Assessment
description: Concepts/theories of health assessment, data collection, and analysis to distinguish between health/wellness, risk factors or health deviations across the lifespan. Attention to principles of communication and interviewing. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Assessment Lab
description: Application of assessment skills in dry lab and clinical settings, with attention to principles of communication, interviewing and physical examination skills. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Foundations of Nursing Science
description: Nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Foundations of Nursing Science and Practice Lab
description: Application of the nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing
description: Biopsychosocial theories of human behavior related to function, alteration, and/or disruption of mental processes; reviews current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing Clinic/Lab
description: Application of current knowledge regarding human behavior related to function, alteration, and/or disruption of mental processes; applies current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families
description: Introduction to the theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care of the perinatal family. Women’s and men’s health issues are discussed. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families Clinical/Lab
description: Application of the nursing care of the mother and family. The student will apply clinical and theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care for women experiencing customary and complicated perinatal processes. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Children and Families
description: Examines the bio/psycho/social response of the child and family to health and illness, as well as nursing care for acute and chronic conditions. Lab course taken concurrently. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Children and Families Clinical/Lab
description: Accompanies and supports Pediatric Nursing to provide educational experiences in the hospital and outpatient or community settings. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Acute Care Nursing
description: Addresses the bio/psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatment in the acute setting will be covered. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Acute Care Nursing Lab
description: Application of the bio/psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Application of health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatments in the acute care setting. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice
description: Examination of continuity of care for clients with complex needs. Emphasis on application of leadership, management, and quality improvement in the clinical setting. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice Lab
description: Deliver comprehensive nursing care to clients with complex needs in community and/or acute care settings. Leadership, management, and quality improvement competencies are stressed. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing
description: Introduces community and public health nursing with an emphasis on application to nursing practice in the community and public health settings. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing Lab
description: Application of health promotion, risk reduction, and disease prevention and detection and nursing care treatments in the community setting. NURS majors only or consent. CR/NC only. (Spring only)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Epidemiology for Advanced Nursing
description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods, with an emphasis on its application to nursing practice. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and prevention of common health and illness conditions with culturally diverse individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes didactic (30 hrs) and fieldwork (45 hrs). Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: classified graduate student status in the SONDH.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Applied Biostatistics and Epidemiology for Nurses in Advance Practice
description: Investigation of epidemiologic and biostatistical methods for advance practice nurses within healthcare settings and complementary roles of epi/biostatistics in shaping advance nurse practice. Application of epi/biostatistical approaches to the design and analysis of DNP projects. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Genetics and Health Care
description: Addresses the scientific, psycho-social, ethical, cultural, and spiritual issues surrounding genetic disease, genetic testing, and living with an inherited condition. Repeatable one time.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Politics & Policy
description: Review of contemporary national health policies, issues and concerns; and international comparison of health policy evolution; includes didactic and 45 hours of fieldwork experience learning.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Assessment and Diagnosis
description: Identification and synthesis of pertinent biopsychosocial and cultural data to complete advanced psychiatric-mental health assessments and diagnoses.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning
description: Provides a framework for the development of advanced skills for systematic and comprehensive data collection, organization, precise recording, accurate assessment and communication of data reflecting the biopsychophysical status of individuals across the life span. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning Lab
description: Clinical lab and practicum for advanced practice nursing. Emphasis on integration of knowledge, skills and outcome evaluation. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Pathophysiology for Advanced Practice
description: Provides an understanding of normal physiological mechanisms and pathological processes to serve as a foundation for clinical assessment, decision making, and clinical management across the lifespan. NURS majors only or consent.
prerequisites: Pre: enrollment as a classified student in a graduate program in the SONDH.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Skills and Procedures for Advanced Practice Nursing
description: Clinical laboratory that focuses on clinical skills and procedures performed by advanced practice nurses (nurse practitioners and/or clinical nurse specialists). Topics will vary by section and semester. CR/NC only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Mental Health in Primary Care
description: Augment APRN students’ understanding, evaluation, treatment plan development, and competence to care for patients with mental health and psychiatric disorders treatment plans across the lifespan in the primary care settings. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-A
description: The first of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis, and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-B
description: Second of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis and management of common acute and chronic adult healt
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: KRS
title: Prevent/Care of Athletic Injuries
description: DB An examination of the most recent practices and procedures in the prevention and care of athletic and sports injuries. Observational field experiences in athletic training will be required. KRS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 353.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Fundamentals of Ergonomics
description: Introduction to ergonomics principles and their application in understanding and prevention of Muscular Skeletal Disorders encountered in the working environment including introduction to legal aspects of ergonomics. Post-Master’s Certificate in Nursing majors only. Pre: 463 or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Administration in Athletic Training, Exercise Science, Allied Health
description: An examination of organization and administration in Athletic Training, Allied Health and Exercise Science. Content includes leadership and motivation models, legal liability, ethical considerations and management strategies for all aspects of Health Care Administration. KRS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Lower Extremity Assessment
description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the lower extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals. KRS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 353, 415; or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Upper Extremity Assessment
description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the upper extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only. A-F only. Pre: 353 and 415, or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Curriculum and Supervision
description: Effective program development, planning, and supervision, including issues in legal liability and administration of all aspects of physical education programming in grades K-12. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Pre: 270 or consent. Majors only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Current Issues in Leisure Services
description: Philosophical foundations and current and emerging issues in leisure services management and programming. Coverage of leisure research and its implications to practice. Repeatable one time. Pre: 238, 249, and 329; or consent.
prerequisites: KRS 238, KRS 249, and KRS 329; or consent
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Evaluating and Marketing Leisure Services
description: Basic methods in marketing, planning, evaluating programs and problem-solving methods, survey research, research design, data analysis, and report generation for park, recreation, and tourism systems. A-F only. Pre: 329 (or concurrent), or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Emergency Care for the Professional Rescuer
description: Combined lecture-lab on advanced emergency care for injuries and illnesses and includes certifications for CPR/First Aid/AED. Class size of approximately 20 students. Open to all majors. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Pre: consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Coaching Athletics
description: Combined lecture-lab with emphasis on scientific principles, theory and practice, and professional qualities of the coach. Writing is integrated with the intent that students will enhance their communication skills through writing. KRS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. Pre: consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Camp Resources and Planning
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab for camp counselors and camp leadership. Plan and evaluate camp experiences for children and youth, including those with disabilities. Includes field trips. Pre: 331 and 332, or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Practicum in Camping
description: Supervised leadership at a camp setting with children and youth, including those with disabilities. Day or residential camps. One full week camping for each credit hour. Maximum of four credit hours. Pre: 437 (or concurrent) or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience. KRS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Sport Biomechanics
description: DB Concepts and scientific principles essential to efficient human movement; proper application of biomechanical principles to fundamental movements and selected complex motor skills. KRS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 353, and either PHYS 100, PHYS 151, or PHYS 170; or consent.
prerequisites: KRS 353, and either PHYS 100, PHYS 151, or PHYS 170; or consent
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Fitness for Life
description: Students will gain knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to plan, implement, and evaluate Fitness for Life curriculum. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication. KRS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Methods in Health Education
description: Experiences in developing standards-based, interactive learning opportunities to teach quality health education in schools. Focus on creating curriculum and assessments aligned with the National and State Standards for Health Education. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Learning Communities
description: Theory, basic research, interactive process, and methodology of the cooperative learning process known as Tribes. Will develop participants’ abilities to foster and facilitate learning communities in a variety of settings. Repeatable one time. (Summer only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Sociocultural Issues in Physical Activity
description: DS Contemporary and historical perspective on socio-cultural issues that influence health and physical activity settings. Understanding ethics and culturally responsive practice around race, gender, sexuality, class, etc. Emphasis on ethics and teaching writing for the profession. Sophomore standing or higher.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Statistics
description: Basic elements for: descriptive statistics, probability, inference, regression, and correlation analysis. KRS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Motor Learning and Performance
description: Basic consideration is kinesthesis, motor ability, fatigue, developmental factors, practice, motivation in relation to motor learning and human performance. Repeatable one time. Pre: EDEP 311 or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Motor Development and Learning
description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Motor development through the lifespan with an emphasis on fundamental principles and patterns. Areas such as memory, knowledge of performance, and motivation are incorporated and demonstrated through multiple writing assignments. Required field experience. Primarily for KRS majors. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Adapted Physical Activity in Early Childhood
description: Concepts of developmentally appropriate practice, importance of movement in overall development, and design of physical activity sessions and environments for young children with and without disabilities are covered. A-F only. Pre: consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
description: DB Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance. Pre: (FSHN 185, and KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or (PHYL 141/141L and 142/142L) or PHYL 301) with a minimum grade of C. (Cross-listed as FSHN 480)
prerequisites: (FSHN 185, and KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or (PHYL 141/141L and 142/142L) or PHYL 301) with a minimum grade of C
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Research in KRS
description: Research methods in the study of physical activity, types of research, statistical concepts and techniques, and reporting research results. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Commercial Recreation
description: Overview of leisure services and trends in commercial, private and employee recreation, and resort and recreational tourism. The social, economic, and environmental significance is examined. Pre: 428 or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Recreation Planning and Maintenance
description: Examination of social, economic, and environmental factors of recreation and tourism development. Emphasis on methods, processes, citizen participation, design issues/regulations, and land use. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Pre: 238 and 329; or consent.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Drug Abuse, Violence, and Injury Prevention
description: Standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment on the scientific, socio-cultural, and attitudinal aspects of drug abuse, violence, and injury prevention. Focus on incidence and prevalence, roles, prevention, and high-risk populations. KRS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Sexual Health Education
