description: Program planning, curriculum development and classroom teaching strategies in the areas of human sexuality, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Focus on research-based curriculum and strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Exercise Assessment and Conditioning Lab
description: Designed to provide knowledge of laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of aerobic and anaerobic testing results, and individual exercise program/prescription. A-F only. Pre: 480 and EDEP 429, or consent. (Fall only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Practicum in Health and Exercise Science
description: Culminating 160 hours of supervised practicum experience in health, wellness, fitness assessment, lifestyle management, and/or exercise leadership. Qualifying hours are contingent upon instructor’s approval in the registered semester. Health and Exercise Science majors only. Pre: current CPR and First Aid Certification, 152, 332, 353, 354, and 463; or consent.
prerequisites: current CPR and First Aid Certification, KRS 152, KRS 332, KRS 353, KRS 354, and KRS 463; or consent
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Program Design in Strength Training and Conditioning
description: Designed to provide theoretical and practical experience in supervision of a strength training center. Content includes program design, exercise techniques, organization, testing, evaluation, methods of strength development, facil
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: LIS
title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
description: Literature of Asia in Western and Asian languages; bibliography, reference tools, research methods, sources, published and archival repositories. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ASAN 705)

subject: LIS
title: Government Documents
description: Survey of government documents at the federal, state/local and international levels in all formats. Covers methods of acquisition and organization, including depository arrangements. Current issues of government information dissemination policies and practices discussed.

subject: LIS
title: Management of Libraries and Information Centers
description: Theories and principles of administration for effective management of libraries and information centers, with emphasis on planning, resource allocation, team skills, project management, assessment, leadership, outreach, and advocacy.

subject: LIS
title: Archival Arrangement and Description
description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope and content.

subject: LIS
title: Records, Archives and Memory
description: Introduction to records, archives, and memory including the global history and nature of records, archives, and the archival profession. Topics include cultural memory, ethics and values, tribal and indigenous records, archival theory, practice and perspectives.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Archives
description: The role of technology in archival theory and practice. Topics include digital preservation, authenticity assessment, arrangement and description, content management, and access systems. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Moving Image Archives
description: Principles and technologies of processing, preservation, and accessibility of archival audiovisual materials in moving image archives. Topics include moving image repositories, critical analysis of archival footage, format identification, digitization strategies, equipment, and vendor considerations. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Records Management
description: Management of records in all media formats. Selection of media format based on government and internal records requirements. Problems associated with electronic media such as legality and shelf life.

subject: LIS
title: Archival and Special Collections Management
description: Management of archives, manuscript collections, and special collections using approaches and best practices from archival studies. Topics include management theory, appraisal theory, facilities issues, privacy, intellectual property, records management, advocacy, fundraising, reference, and educational outreach. Graduate standing only. A-F only.

subject: LIS
title: Archival Access, Representation and Use
description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope, and content. LIS majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Informatics
description: Sociotechnical concepts and processes underlying information systems, services, and use. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Asian Informatics
description: Lecture/discussion on the transformative effects of information and communication technologies in East Asia. Topics include media, mobile devices, social media, publishing, e-government, and e-commerce. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Instruction
description: Study and application of principles and practices that influence digital instruction related to information literacy in libraries and other information environments. Focus on application of instructional design and standards-based outcome assessment. Field research component.

subject: LIS
title: Technology for Libraries and Information Centers
description: Survey of theories, concepts, methods and practices relating to the application of information technology to support the administration and use of information resources. Includes digital, printed and audiovisual materials.

subject: LIS
title: Media Technology and Resources
description: Overview of the use of media technology and the development of media collections and services in libraries. Use and integration of new emerging technologies, including problems and issues.

subject: LIS
title: Database Design and Creation
description: Designing and creating textual and/or directory databases from the viewpoint of information specialists and content providers. Needs analysis, file design, record content and structuring, software choice. Students implement prototype database.

subject: LIS
title: Creating Digital Libraries
description: Principles, techniques, and technologies supporting the creation of user-centered digital libraries. Selection, organization, maintenance, access, and retrieval of digital collections. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Human Dimension in Information Systems
description: Lecture/discussion on human element in information systems, including physical, cognitive and affective behavior in interaction with information systems. Information retrieval, human-computer interaction and cognitive science research, quantitative and qualitative research methods. Research component.

subject: LIS
title: Books and Media for Children
description: History and criticism of children’s literature. Contemporary books and media. Trends in book publishing and media production. Developmental needs and interests of children. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

subject: LIS
title: Books and Media for Young Adults
description: History and criticism of literature for young adults. Contemporary books and media. Trends in media for young adults. Developmental needs and interests of adolescents. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

subject: LIS
title: Services in Public Libraries
description: Planning and implementing services and programming in public and school libraries. Trends, issues, networking, public relations, outreach, competencies, services for the disabled and other special groups.

subject: LIS
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDCS 686 and LTEC 686)

subject: LIS
title: Internship
description: Field experience in library or information agency settings with supervision of professional librarians or information specialists. Available to classified students only. Selection based on academic advisor approval, application form, interview and possession of required competencies. Students must apply and be accepted before registration. Selection is by agency. Repeatable up to six credits. CR/NC only.

subject: LIS
title: Masters Seminar
description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio and preparation for professional practice. Peer mentoring and student presentations. MLISc degree Plan B required course. CR/NC only.

subject: LIS
title: Masters Seminar II
description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio or thesis. Peer mentoring, faculty, and student presentations. MLISc degree required course. Graduate students only. CR/NC only.

subject: LIS
title: Special Topics in Information Studies
description: Includes issues of topical interest in the information professions. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as services for specific groups and special collections. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge. Repeatable unlimited times if course content is different.

subject: LIS
title: Special Topics in Information Technology
description: Includes issues of topical interest in information technology. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as digital archives, content management systems and informatics. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge. Repeatable unlimited times if course content is different.

subject: LIS
title: Practicum School Librarianship
description: Skill development and application of academic study through observation and practice in a fieldwork program with accompanying seminar. Required for school library certification in Hawai‘i. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. LIS majors only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: 12 credits in LIS degree program and consent of practicum coordinator required

subject: LIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/ or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Enrollment requires approval before end of previous semester, with specification of goals, work requirements, number of credits, rationale. Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned up to six credits.

subject: LIS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable nine times.

subject: LIS
title: Seminar in International Librarianship
description: International and comparative librarianship; professional organizations; comparative methodology; research; periodicals; international agencies; influence of literacy and social, cultural, political factors.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to the Study of Language
description:
DS
Non-formal introduction to language, emphasizing the everyday use of language, its relevance to contemporary issues in society, and local language issues. Content studied through lecture, readings, and writing; emphasis on writing as a grading criterion

subject: LING
title: Language and Symbolic Reasoning
description: Introduction to language as a formal symbolic system and to the techniques of analysis and reasoning that re

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Education & Leadership Capstone Practicum
description: A culminating experience in nursing education and leadership program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program. NURS majors only.
prerequisites: (NURS 732 and NURS 747) with a minimum grade of B-.

subject: NURS
title: Curriculum Evaluation & Accreditation in Nursing Education
description: Current trends of planning for evaluation and critical analysis and application of curriculum evaluation in nursing curriculum. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: NURS 474 with a minimum grade of B-.

subject: NURS
title: Foundation of Health Systems and Translation Science
description: Integrate scientific findings from various fields of study to the leadership and management of healthcare systems to ensure the delivery of quality and safe care. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NURS
title: Concept Development and Analysis
description: First course offering in-depth analysis of specific concepts and theoretical formulations of nursing and other disciplines pertinent to the student’s area of research interest. Addresses human responses to health in culturally diverse populations. NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Statistics I
description: Advanced application of general linear model theory to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations. NURS majors only. A-F only. Once a year.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Statistics II
description: Advanced application of multivariate statistics to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations. A-F only. Once a year.
prerequisites: NURS 741 and NURS 752 or equivalent courses, or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Trends in Healthcare
description: Evaluates the historical foundations of healthcare systems and their relationship to current issues and trends in healthcare services. Analyzes the variations in healthcare delivery systems across nations and the impact on health outcomes. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NURS
title: Translation Science
description: Synthesis and analysis of interventions and variables that influence the rate of adoption of innovations. Application of concepts to patient populations and systems of healthcare. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NURS
title: Culturally Competent Research Methods
description: Analysis of concepts, issues, and methods in conducting culturally competent research in the health field.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Clinical Economics and Finance
description: Theory and practice of financial management to achieve high quality and cost effectiveness in healthcare. Hybrid course which combines face-to-face with online learning. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: NURS
title: Dissertation Proposal Writing Seminar
description: Provides students with advanced study and critique from faculty leading to the development of a draft dissertation proposal. Peer exchange facilities individual scholarship, research topic mastery, and ability to conduct rigorous critique. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: NURS
title: Best Practices in Leading Healthcare Patient Safety and Quality
description: Examination of quality of health care, the process of managing healthcare outcomes and costs in the delivery of care through the interdisciplinary process. NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Capstone Field Study
description: Supervised experience in executive nursing leadership to address important health issues for high-risk or under-served populations utilizing an interdisciplinary systems-based approach. NURS majors only.
prerequisites: NURS 664 and NURS 774 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Doctor of Nursing Practice Project
description: Under the guidance of their DNP Project Team members, students will synthesize, integrate, and translate newly acquired knowledge and skills in the implementation and evaluation of their DNP Project. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Research Practicum
description: Faculty guided research opportunity to gain mastery of research skills and techniques through participation in mentored research. Repeatable one time. NURS majors only. PhD students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: NURS 741 (with a minimum grade of B-), NURS 742 (with a minimum grade of B-), NURS 751 (with a minimum grade of B-) and a quantitative methods course.

subject: NURS
title: Grant Writing and Grant Management
description: Designed to introduce students to grants, grant writing, and grant management. Combined lecture discussion, seminar, and exercises on grants, grant writing, and grant management for health sciences. Open to NURS students only, others with approval. Repeatable one time. NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable nine times. NURS majors only.

subject: OBGN
title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in outpatient setting, covering assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and/or management of common gynecologic problems and normal and complicated pregnancies. Emphasis on prevention and health maintenance. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: third-year standing, and concurrent registration in 532 courses. Co-requisite: FMCH, MED, PED, PSTY, and SURG 632.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN (Alpha)
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (C) outpatient clinic at Queen’s; (D) Sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives; (J) urogynecology and pelvic reconstructive surgery. Repeatable twice for each alpha. CR/NC only.

subject: OEST
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program. Repeatable three times. GES, ERTH, and MET majors only. CR/NC only.

description: Science of natural hazards: impact on human civilization of events in the lithosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere (e.g., earthquakes, hurricanes, red tides, and floods), and impact of humans on their exposure to and mitigation of the hazards.

title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Introduction to the principles of sustainability analysis through execution of Life Cycle Analysis applied to products, processes, or systems. LCA and the evaluation of environmental impact will be presented. Personal computer or laptop (Word 97 or higher) OS, and minimum of 4GB RAM. Repeatable one time. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Fall only)

title: Earth Sciences Professional Development Education
description: Specialized Earth Science topics workshops designed for in-service teachers who wish to learn new approaches and content areas in geology and geophysics, meteorology and oceanography. Repeatable up to 12 credits. Credits earned cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

department: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: OEST
title: Communicating Ocean Sciences
description: Application of current learning theory and pedagogical practices in formal and informal learning environments to improve communication and instructional skills. Graduate students from multiple science disciplines welcome. Requires knowledge of biology, earth sciences, and/or chemistry. Repeatable one time, up to 3 credits.
prerequisites: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry or marine science, an interest in ocean science, and enthusiasm for teaching science; or consent.

department: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: OEST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Selected interdisciplinary ocean/earth-related topics involving science, technology, engineering, and/or policy. Repeatable one time.

department: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

title: Ocean Policy and Management
description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Video Journalism
description: Advanced experience in field and studio production of short and long form video journalism; with emphasis on social media fundamentals and content distribution across multiple digital platforms. A-F only.

subject: JOUR
title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Journalism
description: Exploration of the leading edge of the journalistic ideology today as well as a projection of future forms, styles, and strategies, with writing skills as the foundation of such exploratory activities. A-F only.
prerequisites: JOUR majors only. Junior standing or higher. 150, 200, 250, 300, and 330.

subject: JOUR
title: Internship
description: Internship in media or PR operations under professional and faculty supervision. Repeatable two times. JOUR majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: JOUR
title: Directed Research
description: Individual research projects.
prerequisites: senior standing and consent of department chair.

subject: KRS
title: Physical Fitness
description: Conditioning exercises and activities to develop and maintain physical efficiency. Motor fitness tests administered to measure status and progress. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Aerobic Fitness
description: Aerobic fitness improvement upon completion of course by regularly attending and practicing safe workout routines. Learn fitness components, names of muscles and exercises associated with each one. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Beginning
description: Adjusting to and immersing in water, floating, sculling; correct arm stroke, leg kick, breathing techniques and their coordination. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Intermediate
description: Perfecting and integrating basic strokes with added emphasis for speed and distance. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Advanced
description: Correct techniques used in competitive swimming, racing starts, correct turning techniques, long-distance swimming. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: SCUBA Diving: Beginning
description: Learning watermanship, equipment handling skills, and the knowledge to become safe divers. Additional costs for equipment, diver manual, dive tables, and certification fee. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Aqua-Aerobic Fitness
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on aerobic fitness improvement through total body aquatic workouts with music, and development of individualized aquatics fitness program. Open to all students. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, stance, drive, normal iron shots, approach shots, putting. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Intermediate
description: Corrective work on basic swing mechanics and rhythm; adjustments for bunker play, uphill lies, downhill lies, short game around and on the green; handicapping and match play competition. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Advanced
description: Improving drive, fairway wood shots, long iron shots, control shots, trouble shots, putting, course management, competitive strategy, problems in rules. Greens fees paid by students for play on courses. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of those interested in pursuing health-related careers. Structure and function of major systems examined (gross anatomy, microanatomy, physiology, and pathology). (Spring only)

subject: KRS
title: Bowling
description: Rules, etiquette, arm swing, approach, execution, scoring, spare pickups. Students pay charge for use of alley. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Badminton
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, smash, drive, net play, offensive and defensive strategy; singles and doubles play. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Folk and National Dances
description: Popular dances of various national groups, including square dances. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Dances of Hawai‘i
description: Background and fundamentals of hula. Selected dances with and without instruments. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Dances of Hawai‘i: Advanced
description: Advanced techniques in hula movements. Selected dances taught will be more complex, including work with instruments. Individual choreography will be emphasized. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Social Dance: Ballroom
description: Social dances including fox trot, waltz, swing, and other popular dances. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Social Dance: Latin
description: Social dances of a Latin flavor including rhumba, cha-cha, tango, samba, and others. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, volleying; singles and doubles play. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Intermediate
description: Corrective work in three basic strokes and in net play; the lob, drop shot, overhead smash, and half-volley; applying spin in basic strokes; basic strategy in singles and doubles play. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Advanced
description: Improving upon the strokes introduced in 130 and 131; advanced competitive strategy; problems in rules; officiating; elements of tournament play. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Volleyball: Beginning
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on beginner skills and knowledge relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy. Open to all students. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Volleyball: Intermediate
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on improving skills and knowledge through practice and cognitive activities relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy. Open to all students. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Basketball
description: Rules, passing, shooting, dribbling, rebounding, individual defensive and offensive maneuvers; team offense and defense. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Adapted and Prescribed Exercises
description: Small group and individual guidance and instruction for students recommended by student health service. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Weight Training
description: Kinesiology of lifting and weight training, various types of exercises and methods of training with resistance. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Olympic and Power Lifting
description: Exercise technique and prescription with an emphasis on anaerobic exercise. Explores advanced periodization models and their utilization, mastery of Olympic lifts, and plyometric programs. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Tumbling and Rebound Tumbling
description: Single and combination stunts on tumbling mats and trampoline, balancing stunts; techniques of spotting; safety procedures. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Heavy Apparatus
description: Single and combination stunts on side horse, horizontal bar, parallel bars, still rings; techniques of spotting; safety procedures. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Judo
description: Rules, etiquette, method of falling and breaking the fall, simple throws and their counters, simple holds and breaking of such holds, randori. (Student to provide own gi.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Aikido
description: Rules, etiquette, basic rolls, simple holds and the breaking of such holds, specific physical conditioning exercises. (Student to provide own gi.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: T’ai Chi Ch’uan
description: Classic

subject: LAW
title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as PH 673)
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Internet Law and Policy
description: Explores the development and use of new technologies in the global economy, social culture, copyright law, cyberspace, e-commerce, privacy, security, trademarks, domain names, tort liability, criminal activity, speech, and social and ethical issues.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Independent Study
description: Designed for law students participating in an international exchange program, visiting student program, or independent study while enrolled at UH Mānoa. Student must obtain departmental approval prior to registering. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Student must obtain departmental approval prior to registering.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LSJD
title: SJD Dissertation
description: Research and writing of SJD dissertation under supervision of dissertation advisor. Repeatable four times, up to 60 credits. LAW students only. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LSJD
title: SJD Directed Reading
description: Individual reading and research for SJD dissertation under supervision of faculty instructors. Repeatable two times, up to 36 credits. LAW students only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LSJD
title: SJD Legal Scholarship
description: Provides SJD students with an overview of legal scholarship in a series of related fields. Students will be introduced to different research approaches and areas of legal analysis through presentations by instructor and other faculty. Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. LAW students only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LSJD
title: SJD Legal Writing Seminar
description: Provides SJD students with an overview of fundamentals for academic writing skills and opportunity to improve their writing of dissertations. Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. LAW students only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Wildlife and Natural Resources Law
description: Seminar covering federal and Hawai‘i laws that govern the management of wildlife resources, with a particular focus on wildlife conflicts arising in Hawai‘i.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Conservation Transactions
description: Real estate transactions are an important and growing conservation strategy; examines land transactions within the environment of conservation. (Once a year)
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Environmental Compliance and Regulated Industries
description: In depth study of the federal and state environmental laws that impact modern businesses and industries, and exploration of the compliance issues that arise under the statutes, regulations, and case law.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Topics in Environmental Law
description: Study of contemporary topics in environmental law to change periodically as to issues and topics. (B) advanced environmental law; (C) regulatory; (D) legislature; (E) policy; (F) judicial. Repeatable six times.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: International Environmental Law
description: Study of the international regulation of activities and processes used to prevent environmental degradation and to preserve resources of environmental value.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Environmental Litigation Seminar
description: Seminar on the techniques, law, and strategy involved in federal and state court environmental litigation.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Climate Change Law and Policy
description: Climate change is a core challenge that will influence law and policy well into the future. Students will study climate change science, litigation, law and policy at state, national, and international levels. (Once a year)
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Hazardous Waste Law
description: Examination of major federal statutes, regulatory and case law, and Hawai‘i counterparts. Policies behind hazardous waste laws and their impact on individuals, community, and businesses.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Environmental Law
description: Basic statutory law and policy questions and problems concerning the environment. Focus on federal Hawai‘i issues.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Legal Aspects of Water Resources and Control
description: Legal aspects of water and water rights with focus on Hawai‘i.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: Domestic Ocean and Coastal Law
description: Examination of U.S. and Hawai‘i ocean and coastal law covers modern issues concerning the protection and use of the native environment including challenges in Hawai‘i.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWEV
title: International Ocean Law
description: Examination of the history of international ocean law, including comprehensive coverage of modern problems and issues concerning the laws of the sea.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWJT
title: Moot Court Team
description: An honors program for students who prepare for and compete in national advocacy. Travel/registration fees required. (B) Black Law Students Association; (C) client counseling; (D) Hispanic Bar Association; (E) environmental law; (H) Native American; (J) Jessup international; (K) international environmental law; (M) intellectual property; (N) labor; (O) other; (S) space law; (T) trial team. Repeatable one time; up to four credits for (S) and (T). CR/NC only. Pre: selection by competition.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWJT
title: Law Review
description: Students selected for the Law Review editorial board have responsibility for editorial research, writing, and production of the Law Review published by the School of Law. Repeatable four times. CR/NC only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWJT
title: Asian-Pacific Law Journal
description: Students selected for the Asian-Pacific Law and Policy Journal editorial board have writing, researching, editorial and production responsibility for publication of the journal. Repeatable five times. CR/NC only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLR
title: Legal Research
description: Provides a theoretical understanding of the process of law making and of developing and implementing a research plan. LAW majors only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLR
title: Scholarly Research Methods
description: Learn to plan the prewriting process for such scholarly assignments as Second Year Seminar (SYS), writing for law review, moot court competitions, and in any course involving a scholarly approach to research and writing. LAW majors only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLR
title: Advanced Legal Research
description: Designed to meet the needs of students who require an advanced course on research in a specific area of law. (E) environmental law research; (F) foreign law research; (H) Hawai‘i law research; (I) international and foreign law research; (P) prepare to practice; (Q) topic 5; (R) topic 6; (S) topic 7; (T) topic 8; (U) topic 9; (V) topic 10. Each alpha repeatable four times, up to 15 credits. LAW students only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLW
title: Law Thesis
description: Intensive writing that satisfies the law school’s upper division writing requirement and results in advanced law paper of publishable quality, extending over two consecutive semesters of study. Repeatable one time, up to 4 credits. LAW majors only. A-F only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLW
title: Law Teaching Seminar I
description: Interdisciplinary seminar used LP 1 assignments and additional readings to discover and deliver the theoretical and practical underpinnings of substantive law assignments and the methodology used to teach them. Instructor approval required. Repeatable up to eight credits.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLW
title: Law Teaching Seminar II
description: Interdisciplinary seminar uses LP II assignments and additional readings to discover and deliver the theoretical and practical underpinnings of appellate advocacy and negotiation the methodologies used to teach them. Instructor approval required. Repeatable one time. (Spring only)
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLM
title: Introduction to American Law
description: General introduction to the fundamental principles and distinctive aspects of the American legal system and its institutions.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWLM
title: U.S. Legal Research and Writing
description: Introduction to the basic principles of American legal research and writing. Students review techniques of case and statutory analysis and learn to write a professional legal memoranda and client opinion letters. LL.M. students only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in Japan
description: An extended historical review of the foundations of Japanese law in society: Japan’s adoption and adaptation of Chinese legal doctrines, continental European legal structures and ideas, and American influences. Consideration of the structure of contemporary law in Japan: a look at the various players in the legal system, some important legal doctrines, and the real-world operation of Japan’s laws today.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWPA
title: Asian Pacific Insolvency Law
description: Comparison of corporate insolvency law of selected Asian and Pacific island countries, with a focus on recently enacted laws and pending proposals that have followed the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis. Law students only. Recommended: LAW 515, LAW 554, LAW 562. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Law students only. Recommended: LAW 515, LAW 554, LAW 562.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWPA
title: Asian Comparative Labor Law
description: Area studies of Asian legal systems and issues, focusing on administration of Asian labor laws in a comparative context. Possible effects on foreign direct investment and foreign migrant contract workers. Comparison of Chinese, Japanese and other legal approaches in dealing with common issues.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWPA
title: International Criminal Law
description: Designed to give an understanding of international criminal law. Will review all aspects of international criminal law from substantive international crimes to criminal liability and sentencing by domestic and international tribunals. LAW majors only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in Korea
description: Provides students with an understanding of the law, society, and legal systems in Korea. Areas of law including constitutional, civil, criminal, and business are discussed. Emphasis on South Korea. Law majors only.
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LWPA
title: Human Rights in Asia
description: A survey of human rights norms, institutions, and implementation mechanism of international human rights law in light of the rapid development of regional
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Discussion of politics as an activity and of political problems, systems, ideologies, processes.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Discussion of politics as an activity and of political problems, systems, ideologies, processes.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to World Politics
description: Power and contemporary world politics since 1945 with emphasis on the U.S. role.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to American Politics
description: American political processes and institutions, as seen through alternative interpretations. Emphasis on opportunities and limitations for practical political participation.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Indigenous Politics
description: Foundations in Indigenous politics from diverse cultural perspectives and across regions. Addresses political issues facing Indigenous peoples at global and local levels, with attention to Indigenous epistemologies, languages, movements, and institutions. A-F only.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Global Politics
description: Foundations in global politics from political, historical, and multicultural perspectives. A-F only.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
description: Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawai‘i and the Asia-Pacific region. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 180)

subject: POLS
title: Politics and Public Policy
description: Perspectives on the role of government in guiding economies and civil societies with particular emphasis on the recent U.S.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Political Futures
description: Introduction to political future studies. Using science fact and fiction, shows how past and present images of the future influence people’s actions.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Hawai‘i Politics
description: Introduction to political history, institutions, processes, and issues in Hawai‘i grounded in Native Hawaiian perspectives.

subject: POLS
title: Media and Politics
description: Influences and effects of media on politics. Setting public agendas, interpreting events, manipulating the political process, political learning through popular culture.

subject: POLS
title: Reading and Writing Politics
description: Develop skills needed to read and write political texts. Weigh competing views; read and analyze texts for what they do and do not say; craft and defend evidence-based arguments; practice writing mechanics and style. A-F only.

subject: POLS
title: Problems of War and Peace
description: Introduction to the problems individuals and political communities currently face with respect to war, peace, and international conflict. Includes questions of human nature, economy, morality, nuclear deterrence, arms control and disarmament, and alternatives to war.

subject: POLS
title: Political Design and Futuristics
description: Possible social and political alternatives for the future. Conditions likely if present trends continue, formulation of visions of better futures, means for their achievement.

subject: POLS
title: Race and Politics
description: Racial inequality in the U.S.; mechanisms of institutional racism in employment, education, criminal justice, electoral politics.

subject: POLS
title: Hawai‘i Politics
description: Introduction to and critical study of institutions, governments, and political processes in Hawai‘i. Attends to race, class, gender, sexuality, indigeneity and nationality. Grounded in Native Hawaiian perspectives, with an emphasis on comparative study and dialogue.
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Native Hawaiian Politics
description: Critical study of issues in contemporary Native Hawaiian politics, with an emphasis on application and active engagement.
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Hawai‘i Politics (Alpha)
description: Intensive examination of particular institutions, processes, and issues. (B) the military in Hawai‘i; (C) political thought in Hawaiian; Taught in Hawaiian; (D) politics of food. A-F only for (D). ((C) Cross-listed as HAW 428)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher or consent. Pre: HAW 302 (or concurrent) for (C) only. Otherwise, a 100 or 200 level POLS course is a prerequisite unless otherwise specified.

subject: POLS
title: Indigenous Politics
description: Conceptualizing politics from the perspective of indigenous epistemologies, philosophies, language, and social and political movement.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Global Politics/Comparative
description: Introduction to global politics with emphasis on concepts and theories developed from a comparative politics perspective.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Comparative Politics of Developing Countries
description: Political, economic, and social development in the Third World. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Comparative Politics: Country/Regional (Alpha)
description: Political, social, and economic processes in specific countries/regions. (B) Southeast Asia; (C) Pacific Islands; (F) Middle East; (G) Philippines; (H) Japan; (I) Europe; (J) India; (K) East Asia. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Chinese Political Economy
description: Interdisciplinary review and analysis of the social and political issues in contemporary China, the interchange between state and society in national policies, the relationship between cultural tradition and technological modernization in the social transformation process. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ASAN 308).
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Politics of Indigenous Language Revitalization
description: Study of the importance and processes of language revitalization for indigenous peoples in Hawai‘i, the Pacific, Asia, and North America. (Alt. years)

subject: POLS
title: Global Politics/International Relations
description: Introduction to global politics with emphasis on concepts and theories developed from an international relations perspective.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: International Relations
description: Decision-making behavior of international actors; strategies of peacemaking.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: International Law
description: Nature and function of international law in international politics.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Current Issues in International Law, Organization, and Culture
description: Principles, norms, cases, and their interaction with culture and organization in international politics.
prerequisites: Pre: any 100 level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: International Organization
description: International relations of governmental and nongovernmental organizations.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: International Migration
description: Political-cultural economy of international migration: post-colonial populations, refugees, and immigrants.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: American Foreign Policy
description: Purposes, methods, strengths, obstacles, prospects; factors affecting American foreign policy; impact abroad and at home.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Model United Nations
description: Simulation of United Nations organizations, especially General Assembly. Repeatable 4 times.
prerequisites: Pre: 315 (or concurrent) or 319 (or concurrent), or instructor consent.

subject: POLS
title: Global Environmental Politics
description: Evolution of international politics, law and decision-making on a variety of environmental concerns; from endangered species to pollution to climate change. Interaction of population, development, and environment in global governance. (Cross-listed as SUST 324)
prerequisites: Either a 100 level or 200 level course is a prerequisite, or consent of instructor.

subject: POLS
title: Religion and Law in the U.S.
description: Surveys church-state jurisprudence since the 1940s, with special attention to difficulty of defining religion, and applies the religion clauses to current issues. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as AMST 325)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Advanced Topics in Global Politics
description: Studies of political development in the context of increasingly integrated and globalized political economies. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: any 100 level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: History of Political Thought
description: Theories, approaches, concepts, and issues developed or raised in history of political philosophy and thought.
prerequisites: Pre: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: History of Political Thought
description: Theories, approaches, concepts, and issues developed or raised in history of political philosophy and thought.
prerequisites: Pre: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Political Theory (Alpha)
description: Significant works, historical continuities, themes, and issues in political theory. (B) classical political philosophy; (F) revolution and utopia; (G) contemporary political theory; (I) Marxist philosophy.
prerequisites: Pre: any 100- or 200- level POLS course; or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Feminist Theory
description: Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.” (Cross-listed as WGSS 439)
prerequisites: Pre: any 300 level POLS or WGSS course; or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Korean Politics and Society Through Film
description: E
prerequisites: Either a 100 level or 200 level course is a prerequisite, or consent of instructor.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Hypermedia
description: Basic issues of interactive access to information in various formats on computers. Available hardware and software: editing, integration, programming. Implementation of a sample information system.

subject: ICS
title: Design for Mobile Devices
description: Lecture introducing design issues, programming languages, operating systems and mark-up languages for internet-enabled mobile devices, such as cell phones and PDAs. A-F or Audit. (Spring only)

subject: ICS
title: Cognitive Science
description: Introduces basic concepts, central problems, and methods from cognitive science. Identifies contributions from disciplines such as cognitive psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosophy, and neuroscience.

subject: ICS
title: Probability, Statistics, and Queuing
description: A hands-on introduction to probability, statistical inference, regression, Markov chains, queuing theory. Use of an interactive statistical graphics environment such as R.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Sequences and Genomes Analysis
description: Introduction to bioinformatics to computer sciences students by focusing on how computer sciences techniques can be used for the storage, analysis, prediction and simulation of biological sequences (DNA, RNA and proteins). A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics Algorithms and Tool Development
description: Study of commonly used bioinformatic algorithms, with an emphasis on string, tree, and graph algorithms. Presentation of probabilistic and clustering methods. Implementation of the studied algorithms and design of applications. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
description: Fundamentals of computer graphics including graphics hardware, representation, manipulation, and display of two- and three-dimensional objects, use of commercial software.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Graphics
description: Review of selected graphics literature, with a software development project based on a topic of interest. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Vision
description: Introductory course in computer vision. Topics include image formation, image processing and filtering, edge detection, texture analysis and synthesis, binocular stereo, segmentation, tracking, object recognition and applications. A-F only. Once a year.
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as CINE 484 and DATA 484)

subject: ICS
title: Video Game Design and Development
description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as CINE 487)

subject: ICS
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course. (Cross-listed as CINE 419).

subject: ICS
title: Digital Content Creation I
description: Principles, techniques, and history of 3D computer graphics. Modeling and animation techniques will be covered, as well as basic lighting and rendering. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Content Creation II
description: Software development within a commercial 3D application with a focus on scripting and plugin development for procedural modeling, animation, and shading. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Software Techniques for Computer Visual Effects
description: Principles, techniques, and history of visual effects and underlying software techniques for computer visual effects. Project-based course involving the merging of computer generated imagery with live action footage. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics
description: Reflects special interests of faculty. Oriented toward juniors and seniors. Repeatable one time for BS/CS students.
prerequisites: at least two 300-level ICS classes or consent

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics in Security
description: Special topics in security oriented toward juniors and seniors. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: at least two 300-level ICS courses or consent

subject: ICS
title: Capstone Project
description: Project-based course where students work in teams on a software project. Knowledge acquired in the computer science curriculum will be applied to design and implement a software product with potential real-world applicability. Repeatable one time. CS majors only. Senior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Project
description: Individual or small group projects in system design or application under faculty supervision.

subject: ICS
title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ECE 606)
prerequisites: 313 or ECE 467 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Compiler Theory and Construction
description: Design and implementation of compilers, syntactic and semantic descriptions of programming languages, algorithms for syntactic analysis and object code generation.

subject: ICS
title: Theory of Operating Systems
description: Advanced study in operating systems theory and design with emphasis on case studies and distributed systems.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Software Engineering
description: Fundamental software engineering procedures, including planning, estimation, design, testing, process definition and improvement, and software quality assurance. Measurement techniques are used to support empirically-driven software process improvement throughout the course.

subject: ICS
title: Medical Informatics I
description: Introduction to the field of medical informatics, which is found at the intersection of clinical science, public health, information science, computer technology and communications technology. Concentration on current issues.

subject: ICS
title: Software Quality and Maintenance
description: Introduction to software quality concepts and the major activities involved in software maintenance. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Information Architecture and Web Design
description: User-centered design of websites; survey Information Architecture (IA) systems (organization, navigation, labeling, searching); gain experience in methodologies for creating IA, tools for IA, web standards and usability tests. ICS and LIS majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in ICS or LIS or related field or consent

subject: ICS
title: Analysis of Algorithms
description: Analysis and design of algorithms: modeling, comparison, measures, applications.

subject: ICS
title: Network Science
description: Modeling human-made and natural systems as networks to understand their structure and dynamics. Computational and statistical methods and research results they enabled. Use of network analysis software. Applications to topics of interest to students.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Cryptography
description: Taxonomy of security properties: methods for defining and proving security. Randomness, pseudorandomness, and indistinguishability. Functional encryption and obfuscation. Zero knowledge.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Data Management
description: Exploration of information retrieval and object-relational tools and methods for the management of distributed multimedia database systems.

subject: ICS
title: Principles of High Performance Computing
description: Principles of high performance computing for single-processor and parallel architectures. Detailed coverage of parallel architectures and exposure to shared-memory, distributed-memory, and hybrid parallelism. Hands-on experience with message-passing and multithreaded programming. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in computer science or closely related field, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning
description: Introduction to key theoretical concepts of machine learning. Practical experience with decision free methods, artificial neural networks. Bayesian belief networks and contemporary statistical methods including regression, clustering and classification. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Information Theory in Machine Learning
description: Basics of information processing and learning in the brain; neural networks; learning algorithms based on information maximization; applications in molecular biology and bioinformatics. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in computer science or mathematics background, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Deep Learning with Neural Networks
description: Graduate course on deep learning with artificial neural networks. Provides practical techniques for modeling image, video, text, and graph data with supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement

subject: NURS
title: Principles of Nursing Research and Evidence-Based Practice
description: Introduces the process for research application and evidence-based practice. Includes: EBP questions, evidence sources, literature search and synthesis, levels and quality of evidence, and determination of clinical significance. Focus on contemporary medical ethics issues. NURS majors only. A-F only..
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Directed Reading/Research I, II
description: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.
prerequisites: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Student Ambassador Program
description: Focuses on professional leadership development, mentorship, and professional skills for nurses. Students learn to be representatives between the Department of Nursing and alumni, prospective students, and the general public. NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: NCLEX Review
description: Overview of the NCLEX-RN licensure examination and regular, systematic practice in taking multiple choice examinations. Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
prerequisites: Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Cooperative Education in Nursing
description: A two-semester course with seminar in professional role development in addition to paid work experience in nursing at a local agency. Upper division NURS majors only. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only. Pre: 360, 360L, and faculty approval.
prerequisites: Upper division NURS majors only. Pre: 360, 360L, and faculty approval.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Summer Internship
description: Summer practicum experience for students to learn the role of the professional nurse by building on previously learned knowledge and skills in the nursing program. Repeatable two times. NURS majors only. CR/NC only. Pre: 360 and 360L, or consent. (Summer only)
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 360 and 360L, or consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies
description: Survey of complementary and alternative therapies used for health promotion of individuals and groups. NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Veteran Healthcare, Education, and Cultural Needs
description: Provides a broad overview of the Veteran-Military population and their unique culture, educational, and health care needs. Open to non-nursing majors. A-F only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as COA 449)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing
description: Theory course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing with an emphasis on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels. NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 360, 360L, and 363. Co-requisite: 450L, 465, and 465L.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 360, 360L, and 363. Co-requisite: 450L, 465, and 465L.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing emphasizing application of strategies to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local, national, and international levels. Emphasis on oral and writing instruction. NURS majors only. CR/NC only. Pre: 360, 360L, and 363. Co-requisite: 450, 465, and 465L.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 360, 360L, and 363. Co-requisite: 450, 465, and 465L.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Population Health Nursing
description: Theory on population and global health nursing with emphasis on analysis of strategies to address concepts of health disparities, inequity, social justice issues, and ethics which impact health outcomes of populations. Nursing majors only. Senior standing or higher. A-F only. Pre: 364 (or concurrent). Co-requisite: 451L.
prerequisites: Nursing majors only. Senior standing or higher. Pre: 364 (or concurrent). Co-requisite: 451L.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Population Health Nursing Lab

prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 360, 360L, and 363. Co-requisite: 465, 450, and 450L.

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis II
description: Continuation of 431. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 431. Emphasis on writing instruction continues.

subject: MATH
title: Vector Analysis
description: Vector operations, wedge product, differential forms, and smooth mappings. Theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss, both classically and in terms of forms. Applications to electromagnetism and mechanics.
prerequisites: Pre: 244 or 253A, and 307 or 311, or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Differential Geometry
description: Properties and fundamental geometric invariants of curves and surfaces in space; applications to the physical sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Complex Analysis
description: Analytic functions, complex integration, introduction to conformal mapping.

subject: MATH
title: Topics in Undergraduate Mathematics
description: Advanced topics from various areas: algebra, number theory, analysis, and geometry. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MATH
title: Axiomatic Set Theory
description: Sets, relations, ordinal arithmetic, cardinal arithmetic, axiomatic set theory, axiom of choice and the continuum hypothesis.
prerequisites: Pre: 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Logic
description: A system of first order logic. Formal notions of well-formed formula, proof, and derivability. Semantic notions of model, truth, and validity. Completeness theorem.
prerequisites: Pre: 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent. Recommended: 454.

subject: MATH
title: Probability
description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectations, moment-generating and characteristic functions, limit theorems. Continuous probability emphasized.
prerequisites: Pre: 244 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent), or consent. Recommended: 305 or 371 or 372; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Statistical Inference
description: Sampling and parameter estimation, tests of hypotheses, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, sequential analysis, rank order statistics.

subject: MATH
title: Combinatorial Mathematics
description: Finite configurations. Topics may include counting methods, generating functions, graph theory, map coloring, block design, network flows, analysis of discrete algorithms.

subject: MATH
title: Senior Seminar
description: Seminar for senior mathematics majors, including an introduction to methods of research. Significant portion of class time is dedicated to the instruction and critique of oral presentations. All students must give the equivalent of three presentations. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: one 400-level mathematics course or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: junior standing or higher and consent. (Cross-listed as BIOL 490)

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading
description: Repeatable one time, up to six credits.
prerequisites: Limited to advanced students who must arrange with an instructor before enrolling.

subject: MATH
title: Problem Solving for Teachers
description: Practicing teachers develop and improve their problem-solving skills by working on challenging mathematical tasks. Students improve their mathematics content knowledge by working on problems and learning to design challenge problems for their own classes. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Practicing teachers in grades K-12 only.

subject: MATH
title: (Alpha) Career Skills for Graduate Students in Mathematics
description: Seminar addresses issues important in the career of a mathematician, beginning from their time in graduate school, through navigating the job market and on to their eventual work in industry or academia. (B) teaching. Repeatable unlimited times, repeatable one time for (B).
prerequisites: MATH majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Dynamical Systems
description: Continuous and discrete dynamical systems; bifurcation theory; chaotic maps. Additional topics from PDEs and linear algebra.

subject: MATH
title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
description: Linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations. Topics include spectral theory, matrix exponentiation, initial-value problems, dynamical systems, bifurcation theory, first-order PDEs, characteristics, Sturm-Liouville theory, boundary-value problems, Green’s functions.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations
description: Classical existence and uniqueness theory for PDEs, qualitative properties, classification, boundary value and initial value problems, fundamental solutions, other topics.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical linear algebra including iterative methods, SVD, and other matrix factorizations, locating eigenvalues, discrete approximation to partial differential equations.
prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent. Recommended: 407, 411, or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Key Elements of Linear Algebra
description: Key concepts of linear algebra for graduate students in mathematics. Specific topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, multilinear forms, and Jordan decomposition.
prerequisites: May not receive credit for both MATH 411 and MATH 610. MATH majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Modules, Sylow theorems, Jordan-Holder theorem, unique factorization domains, Galois theory, algebraic closures, transcendence bases. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 611–612.)

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Continuation of 611. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 611.

subject: MATH
title: Group Theory
description: Sylow theorems, solvable groups, nilpotent groups, extension theory, representation theory, additional topics.

subject: MATH
title: Ring Theory
description: Ideal theory in Noetherian rings, localization, Dedekind domains, the Jacobson radical, the Wedderburn-Artin theorem, additional topics.

subject: MATH
title: Lattice Theory
description: Introduction with applications to general algebra. Partially ordered sets, decomposition theory, representations of lattices, varieties and free lattices, coordinatization of modular lattices.

subject: MATH
title: Universal Algebra
description: Introduction to basic techniques, including subalgebras, congruences, automorphisms and endomorphisms, varieties of algebras, Mal’cev conditions.

subject: MATH
title: Key Elements of Topology
description: Key concepts of Topology for graduate students in mathematics; topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; continuity.
prerequisites: MATH majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: Properties of topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; metrizability; convergence and continuity. Additional topics from general and algebraic topology. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 621–622.)

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: Continuation of 621. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 621.

subject: MATH
title: Geometric Group Theory
description: Geometric, topological, and dynamical methods in the study of finitely generated infinite groups.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: 621 (with a minimum grade of B-).

subject: MATH
title: Differentiable Manifolds I
description: Differentiable structures on manifolds, tensor fields, Frobenius theorem, exterior algebra, integration of forms, Poincare Lemma, Stoke’s theorem.

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
description: Lebesgue measure and integral, convergence of integrals, functions of bounded variation, Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral and more general theory of measure and integration. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 631–632.)

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
description: Continuation of 631. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 631.

subject: MATH
title: Functional Analysis
description: Linear topological spaces, normed spaces, Hilbert spaces, function algebras, operator theory.
prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent. Pre: consent.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus of Variations
description: Simple variational problems, first and second variation formulas. Euler-Lagrange equation, direct methods, optimal control.

subject: MATH
title: Analytic Function Theory
description: Conformal mapping, residue theory, series and product developments, analytic continuation, special functions. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 644–645.)

subject: MATH
title: Analytic Function Theory
description: Continuation of 644. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 644.

subject: MATH
title: (Alpha) Topics in Mathematics
description: (B) logic; (D) analysis; (E) commutative rings; (F) function theory; (G) geometric topology; (H) operator theory; ((I) probability; (J) algebra; (K) special; (M) lattice theory and universal algebra; (N) noncommutative rings; (O) transformation groups; (P) partial differential equations; (Q) potential theory; (R) algebraic topology; (S) functional analysis; (T) number theory and combinatorics; (U) differentiable manifolds II. Repeatable up to nine credits for (U); unlimited times for the other alphas.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Logic
description: Model theory, computability theory, set theory. In particular syntax and semantics of first order logic; incompleteness, completeness, and compactness theorems; Loewenheim-Skolem theorems; computable and computably enumerable sets; axioms of set theory; ordinals and cardinals.

subject: MATH
title: Set Theory
description: Axiomatic development, ordinal and cardinal numbers, recursion theorems, axiom of choice,

subject: MEDT

Repeatable one time for (C)–(E); not repeatable for (F); repeatable two times for (B), (C) and (H); repeatable three times for (G). CR/NC only.
prerequisites: MED 531 or MED 532 for (B), (C), and (O); MED 541 for (E) and (H).

subject: MICR
title: General Microbiology
description: DB. Role of microorganisms; how they affect people, property, and the environment. A basic survey course covering broad aspects of biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, and physiology; host-parasite relationships, public health, bacterial, mycotic and viral diseases; epidemiology; ecology of soils and water; environmental pollution; food microbiology; industrial applications at an introductory level. Not open to those with credit in 351 or equivalent.

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology Laboratory
description: DY. (2 2-hr Lab) Primarily for students in nursing and dental hygiene.

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology Laboratory

subject: MICR

description: DS. Introduction to the ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Based on case studies, students will discuss and write about ethical issues in research. Issues include humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data, genetic technologies and record keeping. This course is designed for students with majors in the natural sciences. A-F only. (Cross-listed as MCB 314)
prerequisites: BIOL 171 (or concurrent), or MATH 307 (or concurrent), or MATH 311 (or concurrent), or PHYS 170 (or concurrent), or CHEM 272 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MICR

subject: NREM

prerequisites: CEE 424 (or concurrent) or ERTH/SUST 425 (or concurrent) or BS degree from NREM, or consent.

subject: NREM

description: Study of coastal systems, estuaries, and coral reefs. Emphasis on interdisciplinary science and integration of coastal ecology, geoscience, and social science. Coastal and marine wildlife-human interactions, environmental pertubations, and management strategies will be discussed. (Spring only)
prerequisites: advanced undergraduate course work in marine biology, oceanography, geoscience, and sustainability recommended.

subject: NREM
title: Interdisciplinary Methods for Agrarian Systems
description: Interdisciplinary methodologies for conducting research and impact analyses on agrarian systems, sustainable development, and resource management. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: NREM

description: Analysis of trends and strategies in international agricultural research and development. International agricultural research centers (IARC), Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), university networks and consortia, and private voluntary organizations (PVOs).
prerequisites: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing, and consent.

subject: NREM
