description: Fundamentals, techniques, and applications of remote sensing for natural resource assessments and environmental monitoring. Lab consisting of field radiometric exercises, computer modeling of energymatter interaction, processing, and analysis of remotely sensed imagery. Recommended: either GEO 470 or ERTH 460 or one introductory remote sensing course. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: one physics course (e.g. PHYS 151), one calculus course (e.g. 203), and one statistics course (e.g. 310), or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Ecosystem Ecology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of ecosystem ecology with emphasis on tropical forests, human impacts, and global environmental change. Factors controlling ecosystem structure, productivity, nutrient cycling, plant-soil-atmosphere interactions, and energy balance. Field and laboratory methods in ecosystem science. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: advanced undergraduate coursework in ecology and soil science; graduate standing; and consent.

subject: NREM

description: Graduate seminar on foundations of restoration ecology, application of ecological theory to restoration practice. Emphasis on restoration of structure and function in degraded terrestrial ecosystems using case studies from Hawai‘i and around the world. Completion of 680 recommended, but not required. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: advanced undergraduate ecology course and graduate standing, or consent.

subject: NREM

description: Focuses on the history, theories, and contemporary views of landscapes; including scale, land cover, land use, landscape metrics, disturbance regimes, land management, landscape change, the relationship of landscapes to species, and modeling. (Alt. years)

subject: NREM

subject: NREM

subject: NREM
title: Research Seminar
description: Presentation and discussion of student research proposals, theses and dissertations, and research presentations by NREM faculty, students, and invited speakers. A-F only.

subject: NREM
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: NSCI
title: Natural Sciences and Life-Pulling the Puzzles Apart
description: Journey through the Natural Sciences finding fun, excitement, and success in science, mathematics, engineering, medicine, and all that is the natural sciences. Focus upon challenging worldviews of belief, invention, impact, and ethics. CR/NC only.

subject: NSCI
title: Seminar for Science Teachers
description: Seminar and discussions of current and significant topics and problems in science where teachers can exchange new and innovative teaching ideas and strategies. Repeatable one time.

subject: NSCI
title: Computers in Classroom
description: Combined lecture, laboratory and discussion on the use of computers as a teaching tool in the classroom. To be taught in a hands-on manner appropriate for the science teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: NSCI
title: Mathematics Workshop for Teachers
description: An in-depth study of topics from intermediate and high school mathematics. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: NSCI
title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as PHYS 505)

subject: NSCI
title: Seminar on Science Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods; organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audiovisual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ZOOL 619)

subject: NAVL
title: Leadership Laboratory
description: Laboratory instruction will include leadership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed for students pursuing Navy and Marine Corps commissions. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only

subject: NAVL
title: Introduction to Naval Science
description: Overview of the Navy’s mission, customs, traditions, and the duties required of Junior Officers. Provides students with a basic knowledge of damage control, shipboard organization, and safety procedures prior to their first summer training cruise. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NAVL
title: Seapower and Maritime Affairs
description: Study of the Navy and the influence of seapower upon history that incorporates both an historical and political perspective to explore major events and circumstances that have shaped a bold and proud history. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: NAVL
title: Navigation
description: Designed to provide midshipmen with an in-depth study of the theory, principles, procedures, and application of plotting, piloting, and electronic navigation, as well as an introduction to maneuvering boards. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Ships System I: Engineering
description: Will learn ship design and control, hydrodynamic forces, stability, electrical theory, and damage control coupled with design of steam, gas turbine and nuclear propulsion. Case studies merging both ethical and technical challenges. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Ship Systems II: Weapons
description: Outlines the theory and employment of naval warship weapons systems. Supplemented with review/ analysis of case studies involving the moral and ethical responsibilities of leaders in the employment of weapons. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: NAVL
title: Evolution of Warfare
description: Will imbue students with an understanding of the origins of modern warfighting theory through an analysis of historical philosophies, domains, tactics, and technology. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NAVL
title: Fund of Maneuver Warfare
description: Introduction to the foundational concepts and history of the USMC as the premiere Maneuver Warfighting Organization. Theoretical course that utilizes historical examples. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NAVL
title: United States Pacific Fleet Internship
description: Leadership development, teamwork, and activities designed for NROTC students. Learn how to write a federal resume, be a Federal Employee, and learn the skills needed to complete and present their U.S. Pacific Fleet capstone project. CR/NC only. (Summer only)

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Operations and Seamanship
description: Study of U.S. Navy ships professional and efficient operations. Lecture series on Fleet communications, tactical employment, relative motion plotting, seamanship, Joint Warfare, and employment of naval forces a

subject: KRS
title: Tumbling and Rebound Tumbling
description: Single and combination stunts on tumbling mats and trampoline, balancing stunts; techniques of spotting; safety procedures. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Heavy Apparatus
description: Single and combination stunts on side horse, horizontal bar, parallel bars, still rings; techniques of spotting; safety procedures. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Judo
description: Rules, etiquette, method of falling and breaking the fall, simple throws and their counters, simple holds and breaking of such holds, randori. (Student to provide own gi.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Aikido
description: Rules, etiquette, basic rolls, simple holds and the breaking of such holds, specific physical conditioning exercises. (Student to provide own gi.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: T’ai Chi Ch’uan
description: Classic forms of t’ai chi ch’uan. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Karate: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, basic stances, blocks, thrusts, kicks, ippon kumite, and selected kata. (Student to provide own gi.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Karate: Intermediate
description: Emphasis on improving the basic techniques (stances, punches, kicks, forms, and sparring); introduction to combination techniques. (Student to provide own gi.) Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Wrestling: Beginning
description: Rules: fundamental defensive and offensive maneuvers and competitive strategy, i.e., takedowns, reversals, escapes, and pinning combinations; conditioning exercises. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Yoga: Beginning
description: Experiencing yoga and its effects on body, mind and consciousness of individual. Encompasses exercise, breathing techniques, deep relaxation, meditation, practice in concentration, and yogic postures. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. KRS majors only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Yoga: Intermediate
description: Corrective work and improvement of basic techniques. Exercise sets and combinations designed to develop endurance, flexibility, muscle and nerve strength, meditation, and deep relaxation technique. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Water Polo
description: Fundamentals of basic water polo skills, namely, ball handling, passing, shooting, dribbling plus a brief introduction into beginning techniques of individual offense and defense. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Sport Proficiency I: Invasion
description: Knowledge, skill development, and strategy of various invasion type games and sports. Sports like basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee and/or others are introduced within a tactical framework. KRS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Sport Proficiency II: Net, Field, and Target
description: Knowledge, skill development, position, and strategy of net, field and target sports. Sports like volleyball, tennis, softball, and golf are introduced within a tactical framework. KRS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Floor Exercise Gymnastics
description: An entry-level course designed to develop students’ knowledge of men’s and women’s gymnastics floor exercise routines, including injury prevention, skill progression, spotting techniques, and routine choreography. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Track and Field for Physical Education
description: Knowledge, skills, and rules of various track and field events. Organization of track meets and strategy in competition. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Softball
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on basic skills, rules, etiquette, offensive and defensive strategies, position play, and game situations. Open to all students. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: School Health Problems: Elementary
description: Responsibilities of elementary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing teacher’s role in health instruction, health services, school health policies. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: School Health Problems: Secondary
description: Responsibilities of secondary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing health instruction, health services, healthful school living, school health policies. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Kinesiology
description: Kinesiology as a professional field. Overview of history, philosophy, and current trends in kinesiology. Survey of psychological and sociological foundations of kinesiology, exercise, fitness and sport. KRS majors or approval. A-F only. (Fall only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Recreation Services in Contemporary Society
description: Theories and philosophies in recreation: history; contemporary issues; roles in modern society; relationship to health, physical education, and exercise science. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Human Development
description: Developmental processes across the life span. Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Human growth and development from conception to death with major theories and related research on maintaining healthy lifestyles. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Safety and Risk Management
description: Understanding the fundamental principles and techniques of safety and accident-prevention programming emphasizing school, home, public places, on the job, and motor vehicle situations. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Outdoor Recreation Management
description: Objectives and values of outdoor recreation; characteristics and determinants of programs; planning, organization, leadership, and facilities for recreational uses of natural environments. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Health Education Curriculum
description: Objectives of school health program, emphasizing scope and sequence of health instruction; critical examination of health curriculum guides from various states. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Programming and Leadership
description: Factors in planning and leading recreation programs; characteristics and responsibilities of leadership in relation to nature, scope, and resources of a variety of programs. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Health and Physical Education
description: Introduction to foundational knowledge for effective teaching, history, philosophy, and current practices in physical education. Provides the basis for later coursework in K-12 physical education. Required field experience. A-F only. (Fall only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Performance Based Assessment in Health and Physical Education
description: Assessment and evaluative techniques applied to health and physical education, including test construction, performance-based assessment, measurement criteria and instruments, interpretation of data and content, as well as program evaluation.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
description: Understanding standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment in health with a focus on advocacy, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and prevention of disease within sub-topics of health (mental, social, emotional, environmental, financial, etc.). KRS majors only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Principles of Sports Medicine
description: Examines with some depth, principles of risk management and pathology of athletic injuries, major musculoskeletal structures, and concepts of evaluative skills, treatment, and rehabilitation for common athletic injuries. KRS majors only. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Football
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive football coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Basketball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive basketball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Baseball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive baseball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Volleyball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive volleyball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Music and Rhythm in Physical Education
description: Use of music in physical education programming (K-12), emphasizing selection of appropriate music for specific activities as expressive or creative movement, movement exploration, rhythmic gymnastics, and dancing. A variety of strategies for teaching dance will be shared. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Managing Recreation Services
description: Administrative framework and procedures pertinent to the operation of agencies providing recreational services to the various publics. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Water Safety Training
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: Cognitive, behavioral, and emotional effects of people: interpersonal relations, attribution, attitudes, group behavior, stereotypes, social roles, aggression, helping, self-concept; applications.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Personality
description: Scientific study of personality, its meaning, assessment, development, relation to cultural-social determinants.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: History, theories, nature of psychological problems, methods of assessment, forms of intervention, current developments.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Community Psychology
description: Examination of human functioning in social and ecological context. Topics include stress, health, intergroup relations, culture, ethnicity, social competence, and community empowerment.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research. Develops knowledge and written communication skills through and introduction to classroom, assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing. (Cross-listed as EDEP 311)

subject: PSY
title: Learning and Motivation
description: Theoretical interpretations; survey of major theorists and contemporary controversial issues; major influences in classical and instrumental conditioning.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Emotion
description: Survey of traditional views and leading theories, and research in related topics.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Psychology
description: Survey of cognitive processes involved in perception, attention, memory, language, problem-solving, reasoning, judgment, intelligence and consciousness, among others.

subject: PSY
title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Coverage of the relationship between the brain and body on learning and memory, stress, motivated and regulatory behavioral functions, and mental disorders. A-F only.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Coverage of the principles of pharmacology in relation to the effects of drug actions on the brain and behavior. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: PSY
title: Sensation and Perception
description: In-depth coverage of the basic principles involved in sensing and perceiving our environment. A-F only.

subject: PSY
title: Social Development of Children
description: Survey of the social and emotional development of children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Development and Aging
description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death. (Cross-listed as COA 342)

subject: PSY
title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Psychological theories and cultural systems; understanding of own and other cultures; psychological and cultural perception of social motivation; cultural similarities and differences in interpersonal relations.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
description: Psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, and societal regulation of intimate relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Abnormal Psychology
description: Nature and causes of psychological disorders.

subject: PSY
title: Consumer Behavior
description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects. (Cross-listed as MKT 311)

subject: PSY
title: History of Psychology
description: Origin and development of contemporary points of view.
prerequisites: PSY 100. Recommended: 9 credit hours in psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar on the Psychology of Knowledge
description: Selected topics in the psychology of knowledge and mind from Western and/or non-Western perspectives. Repeatable in different topics up to 9 credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Practicum in Psychology
description: Supervised psychological experience in school, clinic, hospital, industry, social welfare, government, etc.

subject: PSY
title: Teaching General Psychology
description: Supervised experience. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: PSY 100, at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology, and written consent

subject: PSY
title: General Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research. Repeatable to 6 credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Psychometrics: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory, research, or methodology relevant to individual differences, measurement, or aspects of psychometrics. Repeatable to six credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Experimental Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research, in cognitive psychology. Repeatable to six credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Psychobiology: Advanced Topics
description: Indepth coverage of some area of theory and research in psychobiology, physiological psychology, or sensory processes. Repeatable to six credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology
description: Social and emotional maladjustment in children and adolescents, developmental disabilities, pediatric psychology, psychological interventions with children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Development Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in developmental psychology. Repeatable to six credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in social psychology. Repeatable to six credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Health Psychology
description: Psychological principles for understanding and dealing with wellness and illness. Theories and research on stress-related disorders; prevention of stress through lifestyle and healthy behaviors.
prerequisites: PSY 100 or consent. Recommended: PSY 220 or PSY 322.

subject: PSY
title: Communicating Social Support
description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships. (Cross-listed as COMG 490)

subject: PSY
title: Teaching Personal Development
description: Supervised experience in leading a seminar in personal development.
prerequisites: PSY 170 and 12 additional credits in PSY and written consent

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Topics in Adjustment/ Treatment/Prevention
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in clinical psychology. Repeatable to six credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research. Repeatable to six credit hours. (Cross-listed as EDEP 489)

subject: PSY
title: Special Topics in Psychology
description: Covers topics of current or special interest not covered in regular course offerings or advanced topics seminars. Repeatable two times.

subject: PSY
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable eight times, up to nine credits.

subject: PSY
title: Methodologic Foundations of Psychology
description: Methods used in psychological research; observational, correlational, and experimental types of design.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Regression
description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences and the general linear model with a focus on regression. Topics include correlation, bivariate and multiple regression, mediation, and moderation. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: PSY
title: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Related Methods
description: Introduction to ANOVA and its extensions from both traditional and general linear model approaches. Topics include single and multi-factor ANOVA, multiple comparisons, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and repeated-measures ANOVA.

subject: PSY
title: Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Models (SEM)
description: Theories and applications to latent variables models. Topics include path analysis, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation models (SEM), multi-sample SEM, mean structure, latent growth curve models, and multilevel SEM.

subject: PSY
title: Multivariate Analysis
description: Analysis of multiple dependent variables. Topics include discriminant analysis, MANOVA, principal components, and canonical correlation.

subject: LATN
title: Seminar in Roman Studies
description: Study of an author or phase in Roman studies. Repeatable unlimited times with consent.
prerequisites: Pre: any two 300-level LATN courses, or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Islands/Islas/Ilhas and Global Exchange
description: Cross-cultural study of global issues of navigation, commerce, and the environment, as expressed by the arts, traditions, and narratives from 1492 to the present. Connections with Europe, Africa, Americas, Asia, Oceania. Oceania.

subject: LAIS
title: Vaqueros, Gauchos, Paniolo: Cowboy Legacies of the Americas and Hawai‘i
description: Histories and traditions (literature, music, dance, poetry, food, fashion) of the Hispanic cowboy, Americas to Hawai‘i. Examines symbolic interpretations of the vaquero concerning nation and identity, and the material consequences of ranching (colonialism, commerce, environment).
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Chocolate Tales & Culinary Cultures: Latin America to Hawai‘i
description: Traces evolution of uses, meanings, and cultural representations of chocolate and other food native to Latin America. Emphasis on how narratives of food and food practices engage with national, ethnic, social, and gender identity constructions.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Studies in Culture
description: Politics of culture and representation. Will consider issues, traditions, movements, texts, and cultural icons for their significance for national and regional identity formation, intercultural relations and global flows of images, people, and capital. (B) Latin America; (C) Iberian Peninsula.

subject: LAIS
title: U.S. Latino Culture and Literature
description: The culture and history of U.S. Latinos through an analysis of their literature and arts and their sociopolitical relationship to the U.S. mainstream culture.

subject: LAIS
title: Spanish Film
description: A chronological survey of films from Spain, from the Silent Era to the present. Conceptually, a cultural history of Spain in the 20th century, as seen through films.

subject: LAIS
title: Latin American Film
description: A survey of films from Latin America, the Silent Era to the present, and their representation of the cultural history of the region. Develops written communication skills.

subject: LAIS
title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households. (Cross-listed as ANTH 368)

subject: LAIS
title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America. Repeatable one time for different alphas. (Cross-listed as ANTH 372 (Alpha))

subject: LAIS
title: Studies in Culture: Portugal and Brazil
description: Surveys the cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world from pre-Lusitanian times, including connections with Africa, Asia, the U.S., and Hawai‘i.

subject: LAIS
title: Asians and Pacific Islanders in Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of Asian, Polynesian, and Pacific Islander communities in Latin America.

subject: LAIS
title: Colonial Latin American History
description: Pre-Columbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social and religious evolution to 1810; independence. (Cross-listed as HIST 478)

subject: LAIS
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ANTH 478 and REL 478)
prerequisites: Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites. Pre: LAIS 360, or consent. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LAIS
title: Topics in Latin American and Iberian Studies
description: Combined lecture-discussion on political, social, cultural themes of Iberia and Latin America; (B) Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama; (C) Luso-Hispanic pop culture. Repeatable one time for different alphas. (Once a year)
prerequisites: Pre: LAIS 360 or LAIS 363 or LAIS 368 or LAIS 372 or LAIS 380, and SPAN 351, and SPAN 352; or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Hispanic Cultural Studies
description: Critical overview of contemporary theories on Hispanic culture. Issues of identity such as mestizaje, hybridity, and pluralism will be discussed from a hemispheric perspective.

subject: LAW
title: Exchange Student Program
description: Designed for students accepted to participate in an exchange program while enrolled at William S. Richardson School of Law. Must obtain prior approval for the transfer credits. CR/NC only.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Organizing for Social Change
description: Examines conditions that lead people to become active, self-governing agents. Covered are strategies and tactics of organizers, history of social change movements, anti-subordination theories of justice and organizing case studies.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Historic Preservation Law
description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as HWST 653)
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Lawyering Fundamentals I
description: Comprehensive program that teaches students the analytical and presentational skills necessary for excellent legal writing. Introduces students to legal problem solving and writing through the types of documents lawyers prepare in practice.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Lawyering Fundamentals II
description: A comprehensive program that teaches students the analytical and presentational skills necessary for excellent legal writing. Introduces skills and strategies for preparing written legal arguments and oral advocacy.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Contracts
description: Law of private agreements. Focuses on common law doctrines with some attention to key Uniform Commercial Code provisions. Examines the bases of promissory liability, contract formation, defenses to enforcement, contract interpretation, breach, and remedies. (Fall only)
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Employment Discrimination
description: A study of the law of employment discrimination.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice- negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR. (Cross-listed as CEE 614)
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Contracts I
description: Law of private agreements. Explores the evolution and application of common law doctrines, and, where applicable, relevant provisions of the Uniform Commercial Code. Examines the bases of promissory liability, contract formation, mutual assent, defenses to enforcement, excuses, remedies and damages, and the rights and interests of third parties. Attention will be paid throughout the course to the role of contracts in a market society and the conflicting interests of certainty, freedom of contract and fairness.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Contracts II
description: Continuation of 509.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Professional Responsibility
description: Introductory consideration of selected topics relating to functions, structure, and responsibilities of the legal profession and its future role in society.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Reparations and Reconciliation
description: Seminar addresses a legally and socially important contemporary issue-healing present-day wounds of historic injustice. Considers how to repair the continuing social damage of injustice. (Once a year)
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Criminal Law
description: Examination of substantive rules, enforcement procedures, and rationales of criminal law in the U.S.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Children, Parents and the Law
description: Exploration of fundamental concepts of law relating to children, ethical issues, and the role of lawyers in assisting children, and how the child’s rights and obligations are balanced with those of parents and state. (Once a year)
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Business Reorganization in Bankruptcy
description: Examination of the rights and remedies available to a failing business and its creditors when the business seeks to reorganize its business and financial affairs under chapter 11 of the federal bankruptcy code. The course is structured as a “practicum,” which tracks a single business through restructuring and emphasizes the practical and strategic aspects of lawyering.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW
title: Civil Procedure I
description: Study of pre-trial, trial, and appellate procedures in the federal and Hawai‘i courts.

Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues. A-F only.

A-F only.

title: Assistive Technology in Rehabilitation Counseling
description: Study of application of assistive technologies to enhance the lives of people with disabilities. Case studies provide the vehicle in guiding students toward integration of available information into reality of actual situations. Special emphasis on the importance of using a consumer-centered approach in providing assistive technology services. A-F only.

department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

Student will gain experience in these roles with close supervision by the faculty mentor. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. KRS majors only. CR/NC only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to assume the role of director of a research project under the supervision of the faculty mentor. The research project will represent a piece of the ongoing line of research of the faculty mentor. Responsibilities will be comparable of a project director of research funded by a research grant. Repeatable three times or up to 12 credits. KRS majors only. CR/NC only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Doctoral Seminar IV in Kinesiology
description: Designed to enable PhD students to gain a perspective of the discipline, both historically and philosophically, prepare them for the issues they may face in the real world, particularly higher education and help them initiate their dissertation. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. KRS majors only. CR/NC only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

description: In-depth study of professional concerns in rehabilitation counseling. A-F only.
