subject: MBBE
title: Essential Biochemistry
description: Introduction to basic concepts of cellular biochemistry and metabolic pathways as applied to nutritional, medicinal and environmental biochemistry. A-F only.
prerequisites: (CHEM 152 or CHEM 272) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Biotechnology
description: DB. General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues. (Cross-listed as BIOL 401)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
description: DY. (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 401. Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as BIOL 401L)
prerequisites: MBBE 304, or MBBE 375, or BIOL 275L, or BIOL 375L; or consent. Co-requisite: MBBE 401.

subject: MBBE
title: Principles of Biochemistry
description: DB. Molecular basis of living processes in bacteria, plants and animals; emphasis on metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids. (Cross-listed as BIOL 402)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275/275L, CHEM 272 and CHEM 273; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Principles of Biochemistry Lab
description: DY. (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles and techniques of biochemical laboratory. Teaches biochemistry laboratory methods as well as technical writing in the form of experimental reports. A-F only.
prerequisites: (MBBE 402 (or concurrent), BIOL 402 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MBBE
title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as OCN 403)

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
description: DB. Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules. (Cross-listed as BIOL 408 and MCB 408)
prerequisites: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 407; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Food Engineering
description: DP. Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as BE 411 and FSHN 411)
prerequisites: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Environmental Biochemistry
description: DB. Biochemical and chemical principles of occurrence, distribution, biotic and abiotic conversion, fate, and impact of synthetic and natural molecules in the environment. Important pollutants will be used as case studies to illustrate the principles. A-F only.
prerequisites: CHEM 152 or CHEM 272, and CHEM 162 or CHEM 171; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: DY. Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems. (Cross-listed as BE 420 and ECE 422)
prerequisites: (MBBE 160, MBBE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Synthetic Biology
description: Introduction to principles, tools, and applications of synthetic biology; molecular techniques and design/analysis of synthetic gene circuits, synthetic-biology parts/devices, CRISPRbased systems, engineered microbial cell factories, for industrial, agricultural, medical applications. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall)
prerequisites: (PHYS 152 (or PHYS 272), BIOL 275/275L) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
description: DP. Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures. (Cross-listed as BE 460)
prerequisites: ME 322 (with a minimum grade of C-) or BE 373 or CEE 320; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Biotechnology for Teachers
description: Principles, methods, classical examples, recent development, benefits and concerns of modern biotechnology.

subject: MBBE
title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Topics for Biologists
description: Focuses on the use of computational tools and approaches to analyze the enormous amount of biological data (DNA, RNA, protein) available today. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as BIOL 483)
prerequisites: (BIOL 171 (or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Special Topics in MBBE
description: Study and discussion of special topics and problems in molecular biosciences and bioengineering.

subject: MBBE
title: Directed Research
description: Supervised individual instruction in laboratory research problems in biochemistry, molecular and cellular biology, genomics, and genetics. Repeatable 3 times or up to 16 credits. Limited to qualified undergraduate students. A-F only.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Cell Biology
description: Provide fundamental concepts and dynamic characteristics of the molecules of the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell, their biosynthesis and regulation, and the mechanisms that regulate cellular activities. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as MICR 601)
prerequisites: basic course in cell and molecular biology, or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Biology and Genetics
description: Graduate-level basic course on molecular biology and genetics. Prepares students to understand advanced concepts in related subjects such as biochemistry, cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, plant genetics, and genomics. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as MICR 602)
prerequisites: MBBE 402/BIOL 402 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or with consent from instructor.

subject: MBBE
title: Advanced Food Science I
description: Advanced topics in chemical and physical characteristics of foods as well as their role in human nutrition. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Basic knowledge of food science is expected. (Cross-listed as FSHN 607)
prerequisites: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics, and biochemistry; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Biosciences Seminar
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in plant physiology, biochemistry, and molecular biology. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: MBBE
title: Professional Development
description: Lecture/discussion targets students exiting from graduate degree programs and provides preparation as a career professional; topics include establishing a professional identity; CV and cover letters, job-seeking due diligence, and negotiation skills. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as PEPS 611 and TPSS 611)

subject: MBBE
title: Plant Biochemistry
description: Comprehensive study of chemical constituents and biochemical processes unique to the plant kingdom with emphasis on selected aspects of current interest. A-F only.
prerequisites: MBBE 402 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Metabolic Engineering
description: Principles and methodologies of metabolic engineering. Concepts of metabolic networks. Establishment of metabolic flux analysis and metabolic control analysis. Systems biology framework for integration of mathematical modeling and global measurements at metabolite, protein and transcription levels.
prerequisites: BIOL 275, MATH 311, and MICR 351; or consent.

subject: MBBE
title: Biological Instrumentation
description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers. (Cross-listed as BE 625)

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Diagnostics: Principles and Practices
description: Molecular diagnostics principles, comparative genomics, genome annotation and bio-informatics, phylogenetics, gene target selection, advanced primer, and probe design. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as PEPS 627)

subject: MBBE
title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to non-majors. (Cross-listed as ANSC 650 and FSHN 650)

subject: MBBE
title: Signal Transduction and Regulation of Gene Transcription
description: Lecture/discussion on molecular mechanisms involved in the transmission of regulatory signals from the cell surface to the nucleus. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: undergraduate level biochemistry, molecular biology, biology, nutrition; or override/ consent by professor.

subject: MBBE
title: Molecular Plant–Fungal Interactions
description: Focuses on the actions of plant pathogenic fungi/ oomycetes and their host responses at the molecular and cellular level. Current genetic and genomic approaches to study plant-fungal interactions will be discussed. Graduate standing only. (Every 2 years) (Cross-listed as PEPS 652)

subject: MBBE
title: Fermentation Biochemistry – Theory, Practice, Competency, and Application
description: Lecture/lab addresses fundamentals in fermentation biochemistry; theoretical and practical level. Explores the concepts of a start-up capital venture business as a project, moving a fermented product to production.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations.
prerequisites: 241 or 251A or a grade of B or better in 215; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus III
description: Vector algebra, vector-valued functions, differentiation in several variables, and optimization.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus IV
description: Multiple integrals; line integrals and Green’s Theorem; surface integrals, Stokes’s and Gauss’s Theorems.

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Compared to 241, topics are discussed in greater depth.
prerequisites: assessment and consent, or a grade of A in 140X and consent.

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations, introduction to vectors.
prerequisites: 251A (with a minimum grade of B) or 241 (with a minimum grade of A and consent).

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus III
description: Vector calculus; maxima and minima in several variables; multiple integrals; line integrals, surface integrals and their applications.

subject: MATH
title: History of Mathematics
description: The historical development of mathematical thought.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
description: Symbolic logic, sets and relations, algorithms, trees and other graphs. Additional topics chosen from algebraic systems, networks, automata. Recommended: one semester programming.
prerequisites: one semester of calculus from mathematics department; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Equations I
description: First order ordinary differential equations, constant coefficient linear equations, oscillations, Laplace transform, convolution, Green’s function.
prerequisites: 216 or 243 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Equations II
description: Constant coefficient linear systems, variable coefficient ordinary differential equations, series solutions and special functions, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models
description: Deterministic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include difference equations, qualitative behavior solutions of ODEs and reaction-diffusion equations. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models Lab
description: Optional laboratory for 304.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models
description: Probabilistic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include stochastic and Poisson processes, Markov models, estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models Lab
description: Optional laboratory for 305.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
description: Introduction to linear algebra, application of eigenvalue techniques to the solution of differential equations. Students may receive credit for only one of 307 or 311.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
description: Algebra of matrices, linear equations, real vector spaces and transformations. Emphasis on concepts and abstraction and instruction of careful writing. Students may receive credit for only one of 307 or 311.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Advanced Mathematics
description: Formal introduction to the concepts of logic, finite and infinite sets, functions, methods of proof and axiomatic systems. Learning mathematical expressions in writing is an integral part of the course.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: A rigorous axiomatic development of one variable calculus. Completeness, topology of the line, limits, continuity, differentiation, integration. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing.

subject: MATH
title: Foundation of Euclidean Geometry
description: Axiomatic Euclidean geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method.

subject: MATH
title: Non-Euclidean Geometries
description: Hyperbolic, other non-Euclidean geometries.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Euclidean and NonEuclidean Geometries
description: Axiomatic geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method; Euclidean geometry; hyperbolic geometry, and other nonEuclidean geometries. (Fall only)

subject: MATH
title: Financial Mathematics
description: Interest rate measurement, valuation of annuities, loan repayment, bond valuation, rate of return. Term structure of interest rates, cashflow duration, and immunization. Financial mathematics actuarial exam topics. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Probability Theory
description: Sets, discrete sample spaces, problems in combinatorial probability, random variables, mathematical expectations, classical distributions, applications.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Probability and Statistics
description: Problem-oriented introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics, providing a foundation for applications and further study.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Statistics
description: Estimation, tests of significance, the concept of power.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations I
description: Integral surfaces and characteristics of first and second order partial differential equations. Applications to the equations of mathematical physics. Recommended: 244 and 302.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations II
description: Laplace’s equation, Fourier transform methods for PDEs, higher dimensional PDEs, spherical harmonics, Laplace series, special functions and applications.

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Systems of linear ordinary differential equations, autonomous systems, and stability theory applications. Optional topics include series solutions, Sturm theory, numerical methods.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical solution of equations, interpolation, least-squares approximation, quadrature, eigenvalue problems, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 407–408.)
prerequisites: 243 or 253A, and 307 or 311, and one semester programming; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Continuation of 407. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 407.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Vector spaces over arbitrary fields, minimal polynomials, invariant subspaces, canonical forms of matrices; unitary and Hermitian matrices, quadratic forms.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Introduction to basic algebraic structures. Groups, finite groups, abelian groups, rings, integral domains, fields, factorization, polynomial rings, field extensions, quotient fields. Emphasis on writing instruction. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 412–413.)

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Continuation of 412. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 412. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: MATH
title: Optimization: Theory & Methods
description: Introduction to theory and methods for optimization. Topics may include least square analysis, search methods, conjugate direction methods, linear programming, integer programming, and constrained optimization.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
description: Congruences, quadratic residues, arithmetic functions, distribution of primes. Emphasis is on teaching theory and writing, not on computation.

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: General topology, including compactness and connectedness; the Jordan Curve Theorem and the classification of surfaces; first homotopy or homology groups.

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis I
description: Topology of Rn , metric spaces, continuous functions, Riemann integration, sequences and series, uniform convergence, implicit function theorems, differentials and Jacobians. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 431–432.)

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis II
description: Continuation of 431. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 431. Emphasis on writing instruction continues.

subject: MATH
title: Vector Analysis
description: Vector operations, wedge product, differential forms, and smooth mappings. Theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss, both classically and in terms of forms. Applications to electromagnetism and mechanics.

subject: MATH
title: Differential Geometry
description: Properties and fundamental geometric invariants of curves and surfaces in space; applications to the physical sciences.

subject: NURS
title: Psychobiology of Mental Health Disorders
description: Focuses on the psychological and biological factors that influence mental health and illness among diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Relevant biopsychosocial theories and research findings are applied.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
description: First of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
description: Repeatable one time, up to six credits. Complements NURS 684; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.

subject: NURS
title: Individual Psychotherapy for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioners
description: Major modalities of individual psychotherapy, such as psychodynamic, cognitive-behavioral, brief solution-focused, and multicultural approaches will be examined. Critical dialogue about race, gender, culture, sexuality and socioeconomic status will be applied to case studies and reenactments.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan II
description: The second of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan II
description: Repeatable one time, up to six credits. Complements NURS 686; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours. Repeatable one time or up to six credits.

subject: NURS
title: Family and Group Psychotherapy for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioners
description: Major approaches in family and group psychotherapy are examined in this course. The role of the PMHNP and issues in providing care across the lifespan, among diverse populations, in traditional and non-traditional settings are addressed.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan III
description: The final of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan III
description: Repeatable one time, up to six credits. Complements NURS 688; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours. Repeatable one time or up to six credits.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Research Methods
description: Nursing research methods for qualitative and quantitative studies, institutional review board procedures, and how to develop a research proposal.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Clinical for Clinical Nurse Specialists
description: Application of concepts and principles of education, consultation, research, and management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for adult health clinical nurse specialist students. Repeatable five times.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 612 (or concurrent), 612L (or concurrent), 613 (or concurrent), and 629 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Successful Aging: Physiologic
description: Advanced study of the functional, cultural, psychological, and socioeconomic phenomena that impact the physiology of normal and abnormal aging. Emphasis is on promoting successful aging among elder residents of the Pacific Basin and applications to primary health care.
prerequisites: NURS majors only or consent. Pre: consent.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Education Capstone
description: A culminating experience in nursing education program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program. (Spring only)
prerequisites: NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: consent.

subject: NURS
title: Directed Study or Research
description: Directed study of problems related to nursing theory and practice. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: NURS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Gerontology: Promotion and Maintenance
description: Analyze biologic, psychosocial, physiologic, and health disparity aspects with conceptual application to healthcare of the aging population. Demonstrate understanding and distinguish normal changes from common disease-related changes.

subject: NURS
title: Philosophical Thoughts
description: Introduces the major fields of philosophy for use in research. Frameworks for the evaluation and critique of philosophical approaches to research will be explored, debated, analyzed, and applied as relevant to the PhD student’s dissertation. (Fall only)

subject: NURS
title: Designing and Conducting Clinical Trials
description: Small group sections will guide students as they produce their own clinical trial protocol. Topics like ethics and statistical power will be addressed briefly. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: any graduate level statistics course.

subject: NURS
title: Instrument Development and Evaluation in Research
description: Theory of testing and evaluation applied to nursing research in culturally diverse populations. (Once a year)
prerequisites: NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: consent.

subject: NURS
title: Principles of Evidence-based Practice for Advanced Nursing
description: Evaluates conceptual models for use in evidence-based practice. Refines skills in searching and critiquing the literature for application to practice change. Synthesizes a body of literature to design interventions pertinent to a practice problem. (Fall only)

subject: NURS
title: Best Practices & Innovation in Teaching and Learning in Nursing Education
description: Current best practices and innovative teaching and learning strategies in nursing education.

subject: NURS
title: Effective Program Evaluation for Quality Improvement
description: Integration of program evaluation and translational science for assessment and communication of programmatic health impacts to improve well-being of patients, families, and stakeholders/communities at local, regional, national/ international levels.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Nursing Science
description: Provides opportunities to know and practice the process of theory development in nursing and to test concepts, relationships, and models about health behavior in culturally diverse populations.

subject: NURS
title: Health Policy and Economics
description: Evaluate the implications of policies on health care funding and regulations, provider payments, and other variables shaping the ability of health care systems (Western and other) on advanced practice.

subject: NURS
title: Quantitative Methods and Measures
description: Critical analysis of quantitative research methods used to analyze problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations. Repeatable three times.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 620 or equivalent course and an advanced statistics course; or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Qualitative Methods I
description: Introduction to qualitative research methods in the development of nursing disciplinary knowledge related to culturally diverse populations.

subject: NURS
title: Qualitative Methods II
description: Advanced in-depth exploration of the data collection, data analysis and methodological issues in the qualitative research traditions (ethnography, grounded theory, phenomenology and critical theory) used in nursing research. (Once a year)
prerequisites: NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 742 (or equivalent) or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar on Women and Health
description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care. (Cross-listed as SW 776)

subject: NURS
title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
description: Analysis of forces that affect adult learners. Concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities. (Cross-listed as EDEA 745 and EDEP 745)

subject: NURS
title: Methods of Program Evaluation & Quality Improvement
description: Principles of and frameworks for program evaluation. Students develop logic models and evaluation plans for a community program and collect and analyze evaluation data. (Spring only)

subject: NURS
title: Curriculum Development and Assessment Strategies in Nursing Education
description: Current theories, issues, and trends of curriculum development and assessment strategies in nursing education.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Education & Leadership Capstone Practicum
description: A culminating experience in nursing education and leadership program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: (732 and 747) with a minimum grade of B-.

subject: NURS
title: Curriculum Evaluation & Accreditation in Nursing Education
description: Current trends of planning for evaluation and critical analysis and application of curriculum evaluation in nursing curriculum.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. A-F only. Pre: 474 with a minimum grade of B-.

subject: NURS
title: Foundation of Health Systems and Translation Science
description: Integrate scientific findings from various fields of study to the leadership and management of healthc

subject: MBIO
title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research. (Cross-listed as OCN 682)

subject: MBIO
title: Behavioral Ecology of Coral Reef Fishes
description: Introduction to processes that affect animal behavior and their significance. Exploring a broad range of techniques for studying behaviors of fishes, students will use new techniques in their own research. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Respiratory Processes in Coral Reef Organisms
description: Multidisciplinary course introduces the respiratory system of fishes and other reef taxa and its significance for ecology and behavior. Students will learn theory, principles, and hot to design/execute experiments for their own research. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Remote Sensing Applications in Marine Science
description: Introduction to tools for the discover, access, and application of remote sensing for their own research in marine biology, including best practices for data collection, synthesis, and project management. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Coral Reef Structure and Function
description: Linking organismal traits and habitat features with ecosystem function. Hands-on course with coral reef fieldwork, exposure to new technology, and the potential to develop independent projects in publications. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Marine Mammal Science and Conservation
description: Will cover the most pressing conservation issues for marine mammals, and include a hands-on field component using traditional and novel techniques to inform their management. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Seminar in Marine Biology
description: Marine biology topics, literature, and concepts of current interest within one of several active fields considered in detail; (B) general marine biology; (C) marine fisheries and natural resource management; (D) marine conservation biology; (E) marine education, outreach and policy; (F) marine physiology, behavior and organismal biology; (G) marine population biology and ecology; (H) marine community and ecosystem ecology; (I) professional development for marine biologists; (J) seminar at HIMB. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MBIO
title: Place-Based Pedagogy for Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences
description: Introduces students to place-based science education with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi marine science classrooms. Includes discussions on inclusive teaching methods, CUREs, and effective instruction in laboratory and field environments. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: MBIO
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research and reading in various fields of marine biology. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MBIO
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis; (F) 1 credit. Repeatable unlimited times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Fisheries and Natural Resource Management
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to marine fisheries and natural resource management. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Conservation Biology
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to marine conservation biology. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Education, Outreach, and Policy
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to education, outreach, and policy of the marine environment. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Physiology, Behavior, and Organismal Biology
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to the physiology, behavior, and biology of marine organisms. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MBIO
title: Advanced Topics in Quantitative Biology
description: Reflects faculty expertise and needs for graduate training in quantitative methods for biology, including statistical, computational, and analytic approaches. Format (lecture/lab/discussion) will vary by topic. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: MBIO
title: Internship in College Teaching (Marine Science)
description: Introduction to college-level science teaching; masters or doctoral students serve as apprentices to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, planning and evaluation. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only. (Summer only)

subject: MBIO
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: MKT
title: Consumer Behavior
description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects. (Cross-listed as PSY 385)

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Research and Data Analytics
description: Use of marketing research and marketing management and data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: the research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; and digital media analytics.
prerequisites: Pre: BUS 310 and BUS 312, or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Communications
description: In-depth coverage of the major communication tools used in marketing such as advertising, sales promotion, public relations and the internet. Emphasis on integrated marketing communications.

subject: MKT
title: Integrated Communication Campaigns
description: Management of integrated marketing communications campaigns. Includes: conducting target market and competitor research, developing creative content and media strategies, production of communication materials and completion of major real world project.

subject: MKT
title: Retailing Management
description: Analysis of opportunities and challenges in physical and digital retailing management: physical layout and digital design; merchandise planning; organizational forms; expense analysis; integration of physical/digital programs.

subject: MKT
title: Professional Selling
description: Emphasis on selling technique, social-psychological principles of persuasion, and interpersonal communication. Lecture, discussion, and application of relevant principles and techniques. A-F only.

subject: MKT
title: Sales and Sales Management
description: Delves into selling and the sales management process. Through a variety of activities, students experience applying selling techniques, sales planning, recruiting and training salespeople, methods of motivating and compensating, territory management and sales team communications.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Marketing
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of marketing. May be repeated four times with change in topic.
prerequisites: Pre: consent and usually senior standing.

subject: MKT
title: Digital Marketing
description: Provides comprehensive understanding of digital marketing’s growing role in new product development; marketing research; direct sales; and marketing communications. Students learn multiple digital tools for analysis of customer behavior. Real-world projects provide opportunities for application.
prerequisites: Pre: BUS 311 and BUS 312, or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Customer Relationship Management
description: Focuses on the evolving field of customer relationship management. Students learn how to manage marketing information and decision-making systems that maximize customer retention and build long-term relationships. A-F only.

subject: MKT
title: Sustainable Marketing
description: Provides environmental knowledge and managerial tools that help for profit and not-for-profit organizations address pressing issues like global warming, plastic pollution, and fair trade while earning surplus revenue and remaining socially accountable.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing for New Ventures
description: Examines role of marketing in the formation and launch of entrepreneurial ventures within and outside of ongoing businesses. Emphasis on new product development and low cost, high impact marketing activities.

subject: MKT
title: International Marketing
description: Principles and topics related to international marketing, with emphasis on strategic planning and applications.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Strategies
description: Decision-making by the marketing executive; integration of all elements of the marketing program based on actual business situations.

subject: MKT
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Analytics
description: Introduces current quantitative techniques and analytical approaches to better marketing decis

subject: NAVL
title: Fund of Maneuver Warfare
description: Introduction to the foundational concepts and history of the USMC as the premiere Maneuver Warfighting Organization. Theoretical course that utilizes historical examples. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NAVL
title: United States Pacific Fleet Internship
description: Leadership development, teamwork, and activities designed for NROTC students. Learn how to write a federal resume, be a Federal Employee, and learn the skills needed to complete and present their U.S. Pacific Fleet capstone project. CR/NC only. (Summer only)

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Operations and Seamanship
description: Study of U.S. Navy ships professional and efficient operations. Lecture series on Fleet communications, tactical employment, relative motion plotting, seamanship, Joint Warfare, and employment of naval forces as an element of National Security. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NAVL
title: Leadership and Ethics
description: Introduces ethical theories in discussion-oriented formats to provide a solid foundation of various moral, ethical, and leadership philosophies. Serves to guide, refine, and strengthen moral character and increase awareness of different ethical decision-making tools. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Professional Nursing I
description: This first level course focuses on nursing practice and education. Professional responsibilities in the practice of nursing are emphasized. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Pre: admittance into HS-DEN program. NURS majors only.
degrees: High School Direct Entry in Nursing
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Professional Nursing II
description: This second level course builds on the knowledge and skills gained in the first level and focuses on professional responsibilities in nursing practice and education. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
degrees: High School Direct Entry in Nursing
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan
description: Focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. It introduces the nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent. Co-requisite: 210L, 211, and 212. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. Introduces nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice. NURS majors only. CR/NC only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Professionalism in Nursing
description: Professional responsibilities of nursing practice are examined through the history of nursing, practice and education, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, and nursing roles. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent. Co-requisite: 210, 210L, and 212. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Pathophysiology
description: Focus on pathophysiological concepts that are basic to understanding illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human responses, which serve as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent. Co-requisite: 210, 210L, and 211. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nursing
description: This course will help students to gain knowledge of the mechanism of action, toxicity, adverse reactions, side effects, therapeutic uses, and nursing implications of the major categories of drugs. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: Pre: 210, 210L, and 212. Co-requisites: 220 and 220L. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness I
description: Focuses on nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 210, 210L, 211, and 212, or departmental approval. Co-requisite: 213 and 220L. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness I Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on using nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness. Nursing skills are integrated into clinical experiences. NURS majors only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: 210, 210L, 211, and 212. Co-requisite: 213 and 220. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Health Promotion
description: Provides an introduction to the HSNC Competencies and spiraling of concepts and is based on the assumption of student responsibility for learning. Emphasis on writing instruction, and research evidence to support nursing care. NURS majors only. A-F only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Statistics in Nursing Research
description: Focuses on the basic concepts and applications of statistics as applied to nursing research. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Summer only)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health
description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools for providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 220 and 220L and 213. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health Lab
description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools when providing culturally sensitive, family-centered care. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: 220 and 220L and 213. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Child and Family Health
description: Nursing care and health promotion for children and families. Emphasis on concepts related to the delivery of familycentered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 213 and 220 and 220L. Co-requisite: 322L. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Child and Family Health Lab
description: Nursing care and health promotion lab for children and families. Application of concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 213 and 220 and 220L. Co-requisite: 322. NURS majors only. Sophomore standing or higher.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Contemporary Ethical Issues in Health Care
description: Explore contemporary ethical issues and their legal implications in health care. Focus on decision-making in professional practice and social policy formation.
prerequisites: Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Gerontology: Its Nursing Implications
description: Explores attitudes toward the aged, biological and psychological aspects, ethnicity, sexuality, nutritional problems, community resources, other related topics.
prerequisites: Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Nursing in the Multicultural Milieu
description: Relates values, beliefs, attitudes, family organization, lifestyles, and health practices in different ethnic groups to health-care and nursing practice.
prerequisites: Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness III
description: Focuses on complex situations requiring strong recognition skills, and rapid decision making. The evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 320 and 320L or departmental approval. Co-requisite: 360L. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness III Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on complex situations requiring application of strong recognition skills and rapid decision making. Evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored. NURS majors only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: 320 and 320L. Co-requisite: 360. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Health Education and Promotion
description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups, and the larger public. Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as DH 361)
prerequisites: Pre: open to non-nursing majors with consent.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Professionalism in Nursing II
description: Continuation of 211. Focus is on current issues in nursing and health care and nursing roles. Principles of organizational structure, leadership, decision-making, priority setting, and change will be discussed. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 320 and 320L, or departmental approval. Co-requisite: 360 and 360L. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Nursing Research
description: Introduction to the research process and an understanding of the applicability of the scientific approach to nursing. Analysis and resolution of contemporary medical ethics issues in research and general nursing practice are primary focuses. Repeatable one time. NURS majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: college-level statistics course. NURS majors only.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Principles of Nursing Research and Evidence-Based Practice
description: (Lec) Introduces the process for research application and evidence-based practice. Includes: EBP questions, evidence sources, literature search and synthesis, levels and quality of evidence, and determination of clinical significance. Focus on contemporary medical ethics issues. NURS majors only. A-F only..
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Directed Reading/Research I, II
description: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.
prerequisites: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: NURS
title: Student Ambassador Program
description: Focuses on professional leadership development, mentorship, and professional skills for nurses. Students learn to be representatives between the Department of
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene

subject: PUBA
title: The Political Environment of Public Organizations
description: Seminar on the role of public managers in shaping public opinion and public policy. Using evidence from theory and practice presents students with tools for understanding management roles within a political context.

subject: PUBA
title: Strategies of Change: Leaders and Leadership
description: Explores the key elements of leadership in public settings by examining what leaders actually do, looking at popular media portrayals of leadership, and talking together with guests about the challenges of leadership, effective followership, and positive change. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Law, Economics, and Public Administration
description: Explore U.S. law as applied to public institutions using economic lens. Rationale of property, contract, and tort law; evolution of administrative law, economic efficiency of common law system, effects of legal rules on economic behavior. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Collaboration for Public and Nonprofit Leaders
description: Theories, skills, and tools needed to effectively manage networks in government and nonprofit organizations; explores how to administer, assess performance, and evaluate success in these dynamic new partnerships. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Managing Workplace Diversity and Inclusion
description: Examines rationales, impacts, and various dimensions of diversity and inclusion beyond race and gender. Students learn and apply public management tools used to foster workplace diversity and inclusion. A-F only.
prerequisites: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: PUBA
title: ICT Policy and Planning
description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives. (Cross-listed as COM 660)

subject: PUBA
title: Public Policy and Advocacy
description: Designed to deepen students’ ability to understand and influence the policy process in Hawai‘i and the U.S. Topics include theories of the policy process, and advocacy strategies, legal constraints, and coalition building. PUBA majors only or approval of instructor. A-F only.
prerequisites: PUBA majors only or approval of instructor

subject: PUBA
title: Nonprofit Management
description: Fundamental aspects of managing a nonprofit organization: overview of the nonprofit sector; mission and scope of nonprofit organizations; organizational structures and functions; resource and volunteer development; major management issues. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PUBA
title: Nonprofit Management Practices and Tools
description: Skills and tools needed by nonprofit managers. Topics include but are not limited to grantwriting, strategic planning, business practices, program evaluation, and advocacy. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PUBA
title: International Perspectives on Public Administration
description: Key dimensions of public administration systems on a global scale; historic and contemporary forces shaping national systems; the dimensions that distinguish them, the opportunities and constraints for comparison and the transfer of knowledge and experience. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Indigenous Governance
description: Overview of indigenous governing systems, particularly in the Americas and the Pacific. Students will learn the legal frameworks and principles of these systems, and how services are provided to citizens. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Special Topics
description: Topics of current interest in the field of public service and public administration, taught by regular and visiting faculty. Repeatable for different topics up to six credit hours. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: MPA Practicum
description: Placement in public, private, and nonprofit organizations to observe and analyze organizational functions and processes while undertaking projects of use to the host agency. Repeatable one time. PUBA majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: with a minimum grade of B: 602, 603, and 604

subject: PUBA
title: Certificate Practicum
description: Students in the nonprofit management track of the certificate will learn by doing and observing in a nonprofit organization selected in consultation with the student’s advisor. PUBA graduate certificate students only. A-F only.

subject: PUBA
title: Capstone Seminar
description: Culminates public administration core courses by incorporating theoretical, analytical, and practicum observations into examination of public issues of importance to Hawai‘i and the region. A-F only.
prerequisites: (601, 602, 607) with a minimum grade of B

subject: PUBA
title: Directed Reading
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PUBA
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Public Health
description: DS. Introduces public health concepts with an emphasis on principles and tools for population health, disease prevention, health professions and healthcare systems, and public health professions and systems. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Public Health Issues in Hawai‘i
description: Application of general public health concepts and tools with broader public health issues as they relate to the State of Hawai‘i. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Global Health
description: Introduction to the basic principles of global PH. Topics include the application of these principles to global PH issues, exploration of links between health, economic, and social status, health disparities and global interventions. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Quantitative Reasoning for Public Health
description: FQ. Inductive and deductive reasoning; tabular, symbolic, verbal, and graphical forms of functions and relations; graphs and pictorial representations of data; interpretations of probabilistic data; surveys and statistical studies as related to public health. PH majors only. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Public Health Student Success in the College Experience
description: Required for entering PH majors to gain strategies for a successful college experience while studying public health. Students will examine academic and career goals and implement strategies to achieve them. PH majors only. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Public Health Issues
description: Seminar will explore current issues and case studies in epidemiology, issues and causes of chronic and infectious diseases, how the environment interacts with health, and how social and behavioral factors affect personal health.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
description: Seminar to work with faculty in applying evidence-based knowledge on social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians. A-F only. (Spring only)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Epidemiology
description: Lecture/discussion on the fundamental principles of epidemiology, exploring patterns of disease, threats to health and EPI methods for prevention, control, and treatment. PH majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: 201, and 210 or MATH 140X or MATH 161 or higher; or instructor approval
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Youth Risk and Protection–Public Health Research, Practice, and Policy
description: Application of public health, related to youth health risks and protective factors using an eco-developmental framework. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: The United States Health Care System

subject: PH

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

description: DB. Explores the biological basis of human disease and the role public health measures play in reducing both the extent and impact of chronic and acute diseases on individuals and society. A-F only.

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
description: Lecture/discussion. Examines a variety of issues associated with the effects of diet on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: IP
title: Study Abroad (Alpha)

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: IP

description: DH. Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as REL 373)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

description: DH. Study of major myths of Epic Sanskrit literature, primarily with focus of the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Literary sources will be tapped for appreciating myths and epics, especially with reference to dharma, karma, ways of life. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as REL 374)
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: IP

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures
