subject: JOUR
title: (Alpha) Journalism Workshops
description: Intensive workshops in practice-based journalism, focused on building skills and making public projects in: (B) emerging media; (C) reporting; (D) editing; (E) multimedia journalism; (F) public relations. Repeatable in different alphas up to 6 credits. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Photojournalism
description: Computer experience in the creation, manipulation, and editing of color news, feature, sports, and documentary images. Study of the ethical and legal dimensions of electronic imaging.

subject: JOUR
title: Publication Layout and Design
description: Visual display concepts and procedures for newsletters, brochures, newspapers, magazines.

subject: JOUR
title: Special Topics
description: Topics of interest to faculty and students; taught by regular and visiting faculty. Repeatable one time for different topics. JOUR majors only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: JOUR
title: Media Ethics
description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects through writing assignments. JOUR majors only. (Cross-listed as PACE 405)

subject: JOUR
title: Broadcast Projects/Production
description: Applied, problem-based application of skills and knowledge of visual story telling to the production of broadcast newscasts. JOUR majors only. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: JOUR 250, JOUR 300, JOUR 330; and ICS 101 or ICS 110 or ICS 111 or LTEC 112

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Multimedia Journalism
description: Advanced fundamentals of multimedia writing and reporting, including finding and developing journalistic story ideas, photojournalism, audio storytelling, design, infographics, and cross-platform digital convergence. JOUR majors only. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: JOUR
title: Global Communication
description: DS Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of international contexts, focused on journalistic issues. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Video Journalism
description: Advanced experience in field and studio production of short and long form video journalism; with emphasis on social media fundamentals and content distribution across multiple digital platforms. A-F only.

subject: JOUR
title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Journalism
description: Exploration of the leading edge of the journalistic ideology today as well as a projection of future forms, styles, and strategies, with writing skills as the foundation of such exploratory activities. JOUR majors only. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: JOUR 150, JOUR 200, JOUR 250, JOUR 300, and JOUR 330

subject: JOUR
title: Internship
description: Internship in media or PR operations under professional and faculty supervision. Repeatable two times. JOUR majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Public Health Practice
description: Observation, study, and supervised practical work in student’s area of specialization. A-F only.
prerequisites: public health degree candidate and completion of 15 PH credit hours and consent.

subject: PH
title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health
description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health. Repeatable unlimited times. PH majors only for (D) and (I).

subject: PH
title: Special Practicum/Project
description: Supervised practical training beyond the required practicum in an area of particular interest. Provides additional opportunity to synthesize, integrate, and apply practical skills and knowledge in a public health work environment. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Exploration in Public Health
description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health. Repeatable unlimited times. PH majors only.

subject: PPC
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as OCN 321 and SUST 323)
prerequisites: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.

subject: QHS
title: Mathematic Preparation for Quantitative Health Sciences
description: Mathematics preparation for quantitative health sciences. Includes selective topics in linear algebra, advanced calculus and probability theory. A-F only.

subject: QHS
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Directed reading/research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through quantitative methodologies and/or the process of conducting a research study. Repeatable three times or up to 12 credits. A-F only.

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistics Concepts for Clinical Researchers
description: Provide biostatistical concepts to clinical researchers. Students will obtain the ability to demonstrate an understanding of key biostatistical concepts in clinical research; and interpret statistical findings most commonly reported in clinical and healthcare literature. Graduate students only.

subject: QHS
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as TRMD 655)

subject: QHS
title: Generalized Linear Model
description: Statistical theory of Linear Model and Generalized Linear Model, algorithms use for estimation, inference concepts, and assessment of goodness-of-fit. Covers Proportional Hazard Model and Generalized Estimating Equations. A-F only.
prerequisites: 601 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: QHS
title: Data Management and Visualization for Health Sciences
description: Data management and visualization is essential to all aspects of health sciences. Through hands-on experiences in R, will introduce data processing, manipulation, visualization and reproducibility, with an emphasis on clinical, medical, and health science problems. A-F only.

subject: QHS
title: Bioinformatics I
description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis. Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only. Open to nonmajors. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed with TRMD 653)

subject: QHS
title: Bioinformatics II
description: Focus on bioinformatics approaches for functional genomics related to DNA, RNA, and protein. It will provide of virus, bacteria, and human genome and bioinformatics approaches to human disease. A-F only.
prerequisites: 610 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: QHS
title: Introduction to Clinical Trials
description: Introduction to clinical trials. Topics include history, definitions/terminology, adverse events, FDA and government regulatory agencies, ethics; monitoring committees, recruitment, introduction to protocol development, basis designs. A-F only.

subject: QHS
title: Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
description: Covers basic and advanced statistical methods utilized in clinical trials design, conduct, and data analysis. Topics cover statistician’s role in drug development and DSMB, statistical theory in phases I-IV clinical trial designs and analysis. A-F only.
prerequisites: 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent.

subject: QHS
title: Quantitative Health and Clinical Research Seminar
description: Provides overview of research related to health in Hawai‘i and advances in quantitative health and clinical research. Topics include ethnic disparities in health, social and cultural factors, ethics, biostatistics and bioinformatics. Repeatable six times. CR/NC only.

subject: QHS
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective. A-F only.

subject: QHS
title: Secondary Data Analysis
description: Will allow students who are new to using secondary data to become comfortable with accessing the data, forming hypotheses, and designing study proposals. Will introduce examples with basic and advanced techniques. A-F only.
prerequisites: 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B- .

subject: QHS
title: Secondary Data Analysis Practicum
description: Introduces students to issues in working with complex data sets and adds the hands-on experience needed to conduct individual research using secondary databases. A-F only.
prerequisites: (601 (or equivalent) and 650) with a minimum grade of B, which can be taken concurrently.

subject: QHS
title: Special Topics in Quantitative Health Sciences
description: Special topics in quantitative health sciences. Reflects special research interest of QHS faculty or guest lecturers. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistical Consulting
description: Investigate the roles and responsibilities of the biostatistician as both consultant and collaborator with biomedical researchers, guide students in enhancing problem-solving and communication skills, and provide opportunity to observe real-life biostatistical consultations. A-F only.
prerequisites: 601 and 602 (or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent.

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistical Consulting Practicum
description: Under the supervision of biostatistics faculty members, students will have the opportunity to provide statistical consultations to biomedical researchers and gain hands-on experience conducting biostatistical analysis in solving real-life analytic problems. Repeatable two times, up to six credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: 675 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: QHS
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through the process of conducting a research study. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: RE
title: Principles of Real Estate
description: Principles affecting the allocation and utilization of real estate resources, including legal, physical, economic elements; valuation; market analysis; finance; investments, and public and private externalities affecting the allocation and utilization of real estate resources.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate and Environmental Law
description: Property rights, land tenure, agency, contracts and negotiation theory, title conveyancing and escrow, mortgage instruments, fair housing, state and federal environmental policy.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate Appraisal/Analysis
description: Analysis of real property, including feasibility analysis, market analysis, income property capitalization, and general real estate valuation techniques.

subject: RE
title: Administration of Real Property Assets
description: How business firms and investors manage their real property assets in terms of the legal, financial, and physical dimensions of real property. Case studies in hotels, condominiums, and office buildings in the environment in Hawai‘i. Business majors only.

subject: RE
title: Current Topics in Real Estate Analysis
description: Consideration of various special concepts and problems in real estate. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: RE
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate Finance and Investment
description: Financial and investment techniques used to evaluate real property and real estate security investments.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate Investment Analysis
description: Development of strategic business plans for the optimization of a firm’s real property assets. Includes facilities utilization audits, contingency planning, and the impact of new techniques.

subject: KRS
title: Administration in Kinesiology
description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as EDEA 623)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Community Counseling
description: Philosophy, organization, and function of community service agencies, programs, and institutions as related to professional work in counseling.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Practicum
description: Pre-practicum training for supervised experiences in school, community, and human service organizations. Focus on the counseling relationship. Includes a specialty observation-participation field experience.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Career Development and Vocational Counseling
description: Theory and practice in career development and vocational counseling with individuals and groups; utilization of educational, vocational, and social resources in career counseling.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Research in Evaluation in Counseling
description: Framework for understanding basic statistics, methodology, and evaluation of research in counseling and related fields. Students will analyze research, conceptualize research, and apply research to practice.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Counseling: Group Theory and Practice
description: Theories and techniques of group counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Tests and Inventories in Guidance
description: Tests and inventories for the assessment of aptitudes, achievement, and interests. Applications to educational, instructional, and career guidance.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Problems of School Adjustment
description: Principles of behavior affecting interpersonal relationships in school with emphasis on application to actual situations.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Theory and Assessment of Intelligence
description: Theory and supervised experience in individual intelligence testing, psychological report writing; psychometric and social issues in intelligence testing.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Crisis Intervention
description: Professional concerns about crisis intervention strategies, and counseling skills development. Crisis theory as applied to suicide, sexual assault/rape, natural and man-made disasters, personal loss, terminal illness, life cycle crisis, and the like. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Inclusive Physical Activity
description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SPED 634)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Elementary Physical Education
description: Content and pedagogy for teaching preschool/ elementary physical education. Students will learn appropriate content and pedagogy for learners in elementary school. Bit teaching and field experiences are included. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Theory and Assessment of Personality
description: Personality testing; practice in administration and use of personality assessment; examination of psychometric and social issues.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Cross-Cultural Counseling
description: Significance of cultural factors in counseling relationships, delivery of counseling services in multicultural settings with attention to Hawai‘i. Emphasis on process of cultural learning and implications for counselor roles and functions.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Seminar in Physical Activity
description: Trends, research, and problems related to physical activity across the lifespan. A variety of topics and contexts will be addressed. Enrolled in KRS graduate program only. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Seminar: Health/Exercise Science
description: Review of selected current literature in exercise/sport science and leisure studies. Practice of presentation in group setting.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Secondary Physical Education
description: Detailed examination of effective physical education curriculum and instruction in middle and high schools. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: American College Student
description: Study of psychosocial characteristics of American college students and college environment, from viewpoint of student personnel work.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawai‘i and our global community. A-F only. (Summer only) (Cross-listed as DIS 650 and EDCS 650)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Sexuality & Health
description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health. (Cross-listed as DIS 651)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Marriage, Family, and Child Counseling
description: Theory/practice of marriage, family, and child counseling, including major model in clinical practice; supervised counseling project by each student. Liability insurance required.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Biomechanics of Human Motion
description: Principles of motion as applied to sport and physical rehabilitation. Introduction to the technology used in the analysis of motion.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Physiology of Exercise
description: Physiological bases of modern physical training methods and sports science. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Metabolic Analysis
description: Theory and practice of metabolic analysis of human performance examining each of the power systems used in energy production during exercise and how to use this information to prescribe exercise programs.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription
description: Provides knowledge of field and laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of testing results and individual exercise program/ prescription techniques. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Body Composition and Weight Management
description: Analysis of the theory and practice used in the assessment of body composition and human physique. Includes strategies for implementing changes in body composition.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Consultation: Theory and Practice
description: Consultation in educational, business, health, community, and human services agencies.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Research Methods in KRS
description: The use of experimental designs/models in physical education research with emphasis on understanding the concepts, applications, and interpretations of statistical analysis.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Assessment in Physical Activity
description: Overview of assessment purposes, types, practices and procedures used in physical education for those with disabilities. Frequently used motor assessments and practices in collection of data will be specifically addressed. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Transdisciplinary Approach to Teaching the Motor Domain
description: Highlights a trans-disciplinary approach for effectively teaching students with disabilities in the motor domain. Important characteristics and components of this approach will be shared. Strategies for its implementation will also be addressed. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Principles and Practice of Rehabilitation Counseling
description: Principles, practices of rehabilitation counseling; review of history and influence of legislation on vocational rehabilitation; current issues, developments, with emphasis on local situation.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Medical and Psychosocial Aspects of Disability
description: Functional implications of chronic illnesses and disabilities on psychological, social and vocational areas of an individuals life. Case studies and presentations will stimulate discussion and help students to apply theoretical information into practical everyday context.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Case Management in Rehabilitation
description: Knowledge and skills required in case and case-load management in public as well as private sector rehabilitation sites. Emphasis on professional/ client relationship, interviewing process, decision-making, goal-setting, recording/documentation, time management, and other tasks.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Psychopathology in Counseling
description: Discussion-oriented course (potentially Web-based). Examination of theory and practice of diagnosis in the assessment and treatment of mental disorders and the use of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) multi-axial system. Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues. A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Ethical Issues for the Helping Profession
description: Developing ethical reasoning capabilities for resolution of ethical dilemmas likely to be encountered in counseling, psychology, and specialty practices (e.g., community, rehabilitation, school, mental health, alcohol and substance abuse, marriage and family counseling, and the like). A-F only.
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: KRS
title: Vocational Evaluation and Assessment in Rehabilitation
description: Theory, process, and techniques of vocational evaluation and assessment. Assessment metho
department: Department of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science

subject: MICR
title: Immunology
description: DB. Structure and biological actions of antigens and antibodies; fundamentals of antibody synthesis; the relation of immunology to biology and medical sciences. Recommended: BIOL 275/275L. (Cross-listed as MCB 461)

subject: MICR
title: Immunology Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Basic exercises and experiments in immunology, immunochemistry, immuno-biology to illustrate principles of 461. (Cross-listed as MCB 461L)

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology of Pathogens
description: DB. Host-parasite relationships in microbial diseases of humans and animals with emphasis on bacterial pathogens.

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology of Pathogens Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Characterization of bacterial pathogens. Isolation, identification, and diagnosis.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Molecular Pathogenesis
description: DB. Fundamental mechanisms of bacterial infectious diseases or pathogenesis at the molecular level. Emphasis on bacterial virulence and host-pathogen interactions.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Molecular Pathogenesis Laboratory
description: DY. Modern techniques to study infectious diseases. Covers tissue culture and animal models to study virulence of extracellular and intracellular infecting bacteria, bacterial resistance mechanisms toward antibacterial drugs, and virulence factor assays. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Genetics
description: DB. Genetic analysis and molecular basis of transmission replication, mutation, and expression of heritable characteristics in prokaryotes. (Cross-listed as MCB 475)

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Genetics Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of transfer and expression of prokaryotic genes: transformation, conjugation, transposon mutagenesis, preparation and analysis of plasmid and chromosomal DNA. (Cross-listed as MCB 475L)

subject: MICR
title: Microbes and Their Environment
description: DB. Distribution, diversity, and roles of microorganisms in terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. Importance of bacteria in pesticide degradation, bioremediation of oil spills, sewage treatment, biocontrol, food fermentation.

subject: MICR
title: Microbes and Their Environment Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of interaction of microorganisms with and within their natural habitats; symbiosis between microorganisms and plants and animals; role of microorganisms in element cycling; food fermentation by bacteria.

subject: MICR
title: Virology
description: DB. Basic principles of virus biology. Topics include methods for virus study, virus structure, replication, gene expression, pathogenesis and host response.

subject: MICR
title: Virology Lab
description: DY. (2 3-hr Lab) General laboratory techniques and related theories in virology; including isolation, cell culture, assay, purification, and identification of viruses.
prerequisites: 351/351L or BIOL 275/275L and 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Molecular Cell Biology
description: Provide fundamental concepts and dynamic characteristics of the molecules of the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell, their biosynthesis and regulation, and the mechanisms that regulate cellular activities. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as MBBE 601)
prerequisites: basic course in cell and molecular biology, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Molecular Biology and Genetics
description: Graduate-level basic course on molecular biology and genetics. Prepares students to understand advanced concepts in related subjects such as biochemistry, cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, plant genetics, and genomics. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as MBBE 602)
prerequisites: MBBE 402/BIOL 402 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or with consent from instructor.

subject: MICR
title: Research Ethics
description: Introduction to ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Moral reasoning, humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data and genetic technologies. MICR graduates only. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: graduate standing in MICR or related field, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Immunology
description: Detailed reports and discussions on selected advanced topics and current research literature. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: MICR
title: Microbial Genome
description: Advanced studies of Microbial genome: relation to functional genomics, structural genomics, and proteomics. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 351 and one 400-level MICR course, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Microbial Physiology
description: Selected topics. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Marine Microbiology
description: Advanced studies of marine microorganisms in diverse habitats with consideration of applications of marine microbes, interactions with higher organisms, phylogeny and diversity, and past and current methods. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Virology
description: Detailed reports and discussions on selected advanced topics and current research literature. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: MICR
title: Regulations of Gene Expressions in Microorganisms
description: Use of bioinformatic tools to understand comparative genomics, metabolic pathways, and protein evolution. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 351 and one 400 level MICR course, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Genetics
description: Directed study and discussion of research literature on bacterial and bacterial virus mutation, genetic recombination, evolution and control mechanisms. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: graduate standing; undergraduates that have taken 475 may register with consent.

subject: MICR
title: Advances in Microbial Ecology
description: Highlights in microbial ecology; interaction of microorganisms with abiotic and biotic components of their environments. Modern techniques for study of autecology and synecology of microorganisms. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: MICR
title: Host-Parasite Relationships
description: Mechanisms of pathogenicity of microorganisms and defense mechanisms of human and animal hosts. Review of contemporary literature. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: MICR
title: Molecular and Cellular Bacterial Pathogenesis
description: Detailed examination of the molecular and cellular mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis. Overview of key literature, synthesis of scientific problems into research proposals. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: MICR
title: Seminar
description: Required of graduate students. Repeatable unlimited times; only one credit will count toward the degree.

subject: MICR
title: Research Literature Review
description: Review of primary literature in a selected area of microbiology. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: MICR
title: Directed Research
description: Selected problems in microbiology. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MICR
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts. (Cross-listed as PEPS 746)
prerequisites: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Special Topics in Microbiology
description: Selected topics in any aspect of microbiology. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MICR
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Physical Fitness
description: Hands-on participatory course following the Army’s physical fitness program. Classes conducted three days per week with Army ROTC cadets. Focus is on aerobic conditioning, muscular strength and endurance. Repeatable three times. A-F only.
department: Department of Military Science and Leadership

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science I
description: Introduces cadets to personal challenges and competencies critical for effective leadership; personal development of life skills such as goal setting, time management, physical fitness, and stress management related to leadership, officership, and the Army profession. Focus on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of Army Leadership Dimensions while understanding the ROTC program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student.
department: Department of Military Science and Leadership

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science I Lab
description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.
department: Department of Military Science and Leadership

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science II
description: Overviews leadership fundamentals such as setting direction, problem-solving, listening, presenting briefs, providing feedback and using effective writing skills. Explores leadership values, attributes, skills, and actions in the context of practical, hands-on, and interactive exercises. Cadre role models and building stronger relationships among cadets through common experience and practical interaction are critical.
department: Department of Military Science and Leadership

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science II Lab
description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.
department: Department of Military Science and Leadership

subject: MSL
title: Intermediate Military Science I
description: Explores creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles through historical case studies and engaging in interactive student exercises. Cadets practice aspects of personal motivation and team building by plannin
department: Department of Military Science and Leadership

subject: LTEC
title: LTEC Training and Evaluation Practicum
description: Practicum in educational technology training and evaluation in formal and informal settings, under close supervision, plus class meetings in hybrid format. Repeatable unlimited times. LTEC majors only or consent.
prerequisites: LTEC majors only or consent. Pre: instructor consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Seminar in Technology Leadership
description: Supervised activity in application of research in learning design and technology to teaching/training experiences. Repeatable three times. LTEC majors only and consent. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Practicum in E-learning
description: Practicum in e-learning in academic or non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings. Repeatable three times. LTEC majors only or consent. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable for 3 credit hours maximum each time.

subject: LTEC
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable nine times.

subject: LTEC
title: Instructional Design Studio
description: Covers multiple instructional design models within the context of theory and research. Studio approach to focus on facilitating learning and improving performance by creating, using, and managing appropriate technological processes and resources. A-F only.
prerequisites: LTEC PhD majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: LTEC
title: Special Topics in Educational Technology
description: Issues of topical interest in educational technology. Concentrates on a topic of current interest, including the new technologies for learning and teaching, and innovative strategies for design and delivery of instruction. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: LTEC
title: Seminar in Educational Technology Issues
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. (B) instructional development; (C) online communities; (D) the future; (E) research. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.
prerequisites: LTEC PhD majors only. Pre: consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Seminar in Educational Technology Theory
description: Doctoral level seminar for advanced students examining the theoretical foundations of research in the learning sciences and technology. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: LTEC PhD majors only. Pre: consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. Repeatable one time. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as EDCS 780 and DIS 780)

subject: LTEC
title: Advanced Qualitative Analysis in LTEC
description: Advanced research methods focused on management and analysis of qualitative data using technology. Reviews of different qualitative designs, data types, analytical methods, and software. Focused study of one qualitative design. Includes independent research project. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Summer only)
prerequisites: EDUC, LTEC PhD majors only. Pre: 667 or graduate level qualitative research course.

subject: LTEC
title: Design-Based Research in Education
description: Provides an introduction to design-based research in education. Reviews different design-based methods and guides students through the process of conducting original design-based research. Focuses on the gap between research and practice. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: 667 (with a minimum grade of B) and 668 (or concurrent).

subject: LTEC
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable five times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: LIS
title: Library and Information Studies Workshop
description: Designed for in-service librarians and other information specialists needing to update their professional skills, focus on a particular topic, or learn new approaches and concepts. Repeatable for credit. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: LIS
title: Introduction to Reference and Information Services
description: Philosophy, principles, and practice of reference services in libraries, information centers and information literacy. Bibliographic control, reference research, reference interview, online searching, evaluation of bibliographic and Webliographic material. Field component. MLISc degree required course.
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Resource Discovery
description: Techniques and strategies for discovery of information resources from professional online databases and the Web. Query formulation and use of advanced functions to match retrieved resources with user needs for research and reference work. A-F only.

subject: LIS
title: Metadata Creation for Information Organization
description: Theory and practice of metadata creation for organization of information resources, cataloging code for resource description and access, Library of Congress and Dewey Decimal Classification schemes, use of OCLC.
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Foundations of the Information Professions
description: Lecture/discussion/survey of the information professions, development of professional identity, professional values and ethics, historical development, current issues in the information professions.
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Intellectual Freedom
description: Seminar surveying the core philosophical principles and practices of intellectual freedom with special application to librarianship and information sciences. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: LIS majors only. Pre: departmental approval.

subject: LIS
title: History of Information
description: History of the recording, preservation, and transmission of knowledge. Development of libraries and other information organizations as instruments of cultural transmission.
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Navigating Information Organizations
description: Principles of effective management of information organizations, with emphasis on organizational information flows, team skills, communication, planning, resource allocation, assessment, outreach, and advocacy. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Collection Management
description: Principles and issues of collection management and care. Criteria and tools for selecting and deselecting materials. Relationships with publishers/producers.
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Preservation Management
description: Introduction to preservation management. Focus on management strategies for preservation of materials in libraries and archives. Covers preservation planning, condition surveys, disaster planning, grantsmanship, and basic issues relating to deterioration.
prerequisites: LIS majors only. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Community Engagement
description: Explores how information professionals in libraries and other settings collaborate with community members and organizations. Provides an overview of theory and practice emphasizing critical analysis of policies, services, and trends. Required course for CALIS. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Introduction to Hawai‘i and Pacific Librarianship
description: Overview of resources and issues concerning librarianship in Hawai‘i and the Pacific Islands. Reference strategies and materials to answer common research questions, collection development, and management issues. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Indigenous Librarianship
description: Development and delivery of information services with and for indigenous communities. Issues include cultural protocols, traditional knowledge organization and ethics of access. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Multicultural Resources for Diverse User Groups
description: Examines resources and materials targeted for diverse user populations in libraries and community organizations, locally and globally. Surveys issues and trends related to diversity initiatives affecting the publishing industry, libraries, and cultural institutions worldwide. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Traditional Literature and Oral Narration
description: Analysis of traditional literature including Asian and Pacific Island resources. Selection and evaluation of traditional literature emphasizing cultural values. Introduction to oral tradition, history and techniques of storytelling.
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Responding to Reading in Libraries
description: Research-intensive seminar that explores the reading process in library contexts and similar settings. Critical examination of ways in which library and literacy services impact reading engagement and interests of library users.
prerequisites: LIS majors only. Graduate students only. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Librarianship
description: Lecture with demonstrations to introduce the essential types of digital resources and the software tools for finding high quality and relevant information efficiently from digital journal archives and reference databases.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 or consent. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
description: Literature of Asia in Western and Asian languages; bibliography, reference tools, research methods, sources, published and archival repositories. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ASAN 705)
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Government Documents
description: Survey of government documents at the federal, state/local and international levels in all formats. Covers methods of acquisition and organization, including depository arrangements. Current issues of government information dissemination policies and practices discussed.
prerequisites: Pre: 601 or consent. Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: LIS
title: Management of Libraries and Information Centers
description: Theories and principles of administration for effective management of libraries and information centers, with emphasis on planning, resource allocation, team skills, project management,
prerequisites: Admitted to LIS Program or LIS Program Chair approval.

subject: MUS
title: Asian and Pacific Music in Education
description: DA Musical concepts in songs, dances, and instrumental music of Asia, Hawai‘i, and other Pacific Islands, appropriate for K–12.
prerequisites: 250, or 253, or 354, or 355, or 356, or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Vocal Pedagogy
description: Scientific studies of vocal mechanism; application to techniques of singing. Pedagogical methods for individual voice instruction; participation in applied music teaching.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Eras of Western Music History
description: Changing styles and forms in periods of European art music from 500 A.D. to the present. (B) medieval; (C) Renaissance; (D) Baroque; (E) Classic; (F) Romantic; (G) 20th century. Repeatable one time for different alphas.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Studies in Western Music History
description: (B) music of the United States.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Music Literature
description: (B) symphonic music; (C) concerto; (D) chamber music; (E) choral music; (F) solo song; (G) wind band literature; (H) guitar literature. Repeatable one time for different alphas.

subject: MUS
title: Opera
description: Historical study from Monteverdi to present.

subject: MUS
title: Music and Ethics
description: Studies music’s roles in religious traditions and politics, as identity formation, and music’s relationship with lyrics in a variety of forms. Readings approach these issues from the question of ethics. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: MUS
title: Chinese Music and Sound Culture
description: DH Situates the Chinese musical sound in the interdisciplinary field of sound culture. Students will learn to read music literature and listen to historical sounds critically and to analyze aspects of Chinese sound culture. (Cross-listed as THEA 469)

subject: MUS
title: Sound Systems of World Musics
description: Music-theoretical study of sound organization as defined by various cultures and development of aural analysis in world musics. Junior standing or higher.

subject: MUS
title: History of Rock and Roll
description: DH An examination of rock and roll from various perspectives including economics, regionalism, freedom of expression.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Musical Cultures
description: The study of a musical culture area. (B) Hawai‘i; (C) China; (D) Japan; (E) Korea; (F) Indonesia; (G) Philippines; (H) India; (I) Polynesia; (P) Africa; (Q) other. Repeatable one time for different alphas. Junior standing or higher. ((H) Cross-listed as ASAN 478)

subject: MUS
title: Topics in Ethnomusicology
description: DH Problem-oriented cross-cultural investigation of music and music organization. Junior standing or higher.

subject: MUS
title: Composition for Music Majors
description: Original composition; specific approaches to creative writing. Intended for music majors not majoring in composition. Repeatable one time. MUS majors only. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Intermediate Practicum in Music Composition
description: Creative writing beginning with smaller forms. Repeatable unlimited times. MUS majors only.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Practicum in Music Composition
description: Creative writing in larger forms. Composition majors only. Repeatable one time.

subject: MUS
title: Contemporary Techniques
description: Theoretical techniques in music of the 20th and 21st centuries; emphasis on writing as the synthesis of concepts. Investigation of important stylistic movements.

subject: MUS
title: Senior Project
description: Capstone project designed by student, who must find and work with faculty advisor before enrolling. Also subject to advance approval by departmental committee. Repeatable one time. Senior standing only. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Western Music History Review
description: Online course surveys representative composers, musical styles, and genres from the Western tradition. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Seminar
description: Selected problems in (B) composition; (C) ethnomusicology; (D) music literature; (E) performance repertory; (F) music education; (H) theory. Repeatable nine times. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Topics in Music
description: Advanced topics in history, literature, theory, applied music, music education, and ethnomusicology; some in intensive modular format. Repeatable nine times. MUS majors only.
prerequisites: appropriate lower division music courses or consent and graduate standing.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Ensemble
description: Projects in study and performance. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Conducting
description: Conducting instrumental and choral groups. Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Conducting
description: Continuation of 625.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Applied Music, Western
description: For nonmajors or music majors in secondary performance fields. Individual instruction in solo vocal or instrumental performance at an advanced level. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) organ; (E) conducting; (F) recorder; (G) guitar; (H) violin; (I) viola; (J) cello; (K) double bass; (M) flute; (N) oboe; (O) clarinet; (P) bassoon; (Q) saxophone; (R) trumpet; (S) french horn; (T) trombone; (U) tuba; (X) euphonium; (Y) percussion; (Z) other. Each alpha repeatable five times, up to 12 credits. MUS majors only, for majors in secondary performance fields. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Graduate-Level Applied Music
description: For students accepted for MMus in performance. Individual instruction in solo vocal or instrumental performance at graduate performance level. Representative works. (B) voice; (C) piano; (E) conducting; (G) guitar; (H) violin; (I) viola; (J) cello; (K) double bass; (M) flute; (N) oboe; (O) clarinet; (P) bassoon; (Q) saxophone; (R) trumpet; (S) French horn; (T) trombone; (U) tuba; (X) euphonium; (Y) percussion; (Z) other. Repeatable three times for (E), repeatable two times for all other alphas. MUS majors only for (E) and (G). Graduate students only for (E). A-F only for (E) and (G).

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Graduate Recital
description: For students accepted for MMus in performance. Individual instruction in solo vocal or instrumental performance at graduate level; full recital required. (B) voice; (C) piano; (E) conducting; (G) guitar (3 cr.); (H) violin; (I) viola; (J) cello; (K) bass; (M) flute; (N) oboe; (O) clarinet; (P) bassoon; (Q) saxophone; (R) trumpet; (S) French horn; (T) trombone; (U) tuba; (X) euphonium; (Y) percussion. Repeatable two times for (G); repeatable up to six credits per alpha for all other alphas. MUS majors only. Graduate students only for (E). A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: College Level Teaching Practicum
description: Practical experience teaching at the college level. Examination of elements for successful college teaching. Repeatable two times. MUS majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Foundations of Music Education
description: Music and music education in their philosophic, aesthetic, social, historical, and psychological dimensions. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Research in Music Education
description: Introduction to research techniques in music education, including topic selection, literature review, and presentation of information in written form. A-F only. MUS majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: Music Curriculum Theory and Design
description: Procedures for planning, teaching, evaluating, and administering music programs in elementary, secondary, and higher education. Evaluation of current programs; procedures for change. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: Music in Childhood Education
description: Principles and programs in teaching music to children in early childhood settings and elementary school. Curriculum development, analysis of research, and current approaches.
prerequisites: 353 or 354, teaching experience, and graduate standing.

subject: MUS
title: World Musics in Undergraduate Education
description: Concepts and materials at junior college and undergraduate levels. Preparation for structuring and teaching courses in non-Western musics.
prerequisites: graduate status in music and 107 or 407 (or concurrent).

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in College Music Teaching
description: Examines components of good teaching, adult learning theories, course organization, methodologies, evaluation, and other music issues. For students planning a college teaching career in music.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Studies in Music Literature
description: Detailed study by chronological period. (B) medieval; (C) Renaissance; (D) Baroque; (E) Classic; (F) Romantic; (G) 20th century. Repeatable in different alphas.

subject: MUS
title: Bibliography and Library Resources in Music
description: Basic materials and techniques; includes retrieval techniques from online computer catalog. MUS majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Regional Music
description: Musical content and historicosocial context of principal musical traditions. (B) Asia; (C) Oceania. Repeatable nine times.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Advanced Problems in Ethnomusicology
description: (B) transcription of music performance; (C) movement analysis; (D) other.

subject: MUS
title: (Alpha) Studies in Music Theory
description: (B) stylistic counterpoint to 1700; (C) stylistic counterpoint from 1700; (D) advanced analysis; (E) comparative theory; (F) history of theory; (G) contemporary techniques and resources; (H) atonal analysis and set theory; (I) Schenkerian analysis.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques.
prerequisites: Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory I
description: Relativistic wave equations and their solutions. Dirac’s theory of the electron, propagator techniques. Applications to quantum electrodynamics.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory II
description: Local gauge invariance, Yang-Mills theory: quantum chromodynamics, spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone bosons; the standard electroweak theory; grand unified theories.

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
description: Nuclear physics; electrodynamics; hadron structure and partons. Techniques of particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics II
description: Quantum chromodynamics; electroweak interactions; the standard model. Techniques of particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Theory
description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, electron-electron interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Theory
description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of dental hygiene students and others interested in pursuing health-related careers.

subject: PHYL
title: Physiology and Anatomy Lab
description: Laboratory to complement 103.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
description: Continuation of 141.
prerequisites: should have an understanding of basic physiology concepts as presented in 141 or equivalent

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

subject: PHYL
title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
description: Integrated presentation of human anatomy and physiology. An optional laboratory (PHYL 301L) is available separately.
prerequisites: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172, or any PHYL course; and CHEM 161 (or higher) or any BIOC course; or consent

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Laboratory study of human anatomy and physiology by means of models, histology slides, experiments, and demonstrations.

subject: PHYL
title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Continuation of 301L.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Physiology: Organ Systems
description: Basic function of the major organ systems in man. Covers cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, acid-base, and gastrointestinal physiology.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Physiology: Integrative Systems
description: Senior-level course in integrative systems (central nervous system and endocrinology). Complements 401.
prerequisites: 401 and either BIOC 341 or CHEM 152, or consent

subject: PHYL
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Students will learn fundamental concepts and multiple techniques in molecular biology, physiology, and histology for cardiovascular research through the projects in the lab. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned to two credits only.
prerequisites: Junior or senior standing only. CR/NC only.

subject: PEPS
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: The World of Insects
description: Biology/ecology of insects with emphasis on relationships to plants, animals, and especially people in Hawai‘i and the tropics. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: Environment and Agriculture
description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

subject: PEPS
title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawai‘i.
prerequisites: (BIOL 171 and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Invasive Pest Species
description: Ecological, economic and sociological impacts of invasive species on tropical ecosystems; characteristics of invasive species and vulnerability of habitats; ethical issues on impacts of management options on evolution, biodiversity and eco-stability and human life. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: General Entomology
description: Biology, diversity, and ecology of insects with emphasis on Hawaiian fauna. Classification to order level.
prerequisites: (BOT 101 or ZOOL 101 or BIOL 171) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: General Entomology Laboratory
description: Laboratory in the biology and classification to family level of Hawai‘i’s insects and arthropods.
prerequisites: (363 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production. Repeatable one time.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Pathogens and Diseases
description: Classification, morphology, ecology, and biology of bacteria, fungi, nematodes, and viruses that attack economic crops. Etiology and control of plant diseases.
prerequisites: 210/SUST 210 or BOT 101 or MICR 130, or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

subject: PEPS
title: Turfgrass Pest Management
description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawai‘i, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

subject: PEPS
title: Foundations of Pest Management
description: Principles and concepts of insect pest management using biological, ecological, cultural, behavioral, legislative, microbial and chemical methods.
prerequisites: one of the following: 250 or 363, BIOL 171, BIOL 172, or BOT 101; or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Disease Management
description: Diagnosis, epidemiology, and integrated management of important plant diseases and pathogens for key plants and cultivated crops in various agroecosystems in Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and the global tropics.

subject: PEPS
title: Environmental Law
description: Exploration of federal laws, regulations, and precedents that govern our interaction with the environment. Analysis of laws regulating air, water, toxins, pests, endangered species, and environmental justice.

subject: PEPS
title: Medical and Urban Entomology
description: Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Proficiency Through TV Drama
description: Increasing Korean proficiency to advanced level through TV drama, which provides culturally and situationally rich contexts. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: KOR
title: Directed Third-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Offered if staff available. CR/NC only. Repeatable three times.

subject: KOR
title: Fourth-Level Korean I
description: Continuation of 302. (Fall only)

subject: KOR
title: Fourth-Level Korean II
description: Continuation of 401. (Spring only)

subject: KOR
title: High-Advanced Korean: Korean Society
description: Emphasis on highest level of listening, speaking, reading and writing, with application to Korean society, using authentic materials. (Fall only)

subject: KOR
title: High-Advanced Korean II
description: Continuation of 402. Emphasis on highest level of listening, speaking, reading and writing, with application to Korean culture using authentic materials and focusing on training in oral presentation skills.

subject: KOR
title: Advanced Oral Communication in Korean
description: Fourth-year advanced Korean course to increase learners’ oral fluency and accuracy; with an emphasis on formal speaking. Covers linguistic proficiency as well as social and cultural proficiencies.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Composition
description: Training in modern structural and stylistic techniques; writing on designated themes. Repeatable one time.

subject: KOR
title: Media Analysis in Korean: Contemporary Korean Culture
description: Focus on analyzing, comparing, and evaluating current media materials in South Korea to develop professional language skills and to deepen knowledge and understanding of contemporary Korean society. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: KOR
title: Media Analysis in Korean: Contemporary Ethical Issues in Korea
description: Focus on analyzing, comparing, and evaluating current ethical issues in South Korea and North Korea using media materials to develop professional language skills and to deepen knowledge and understanding of contemporary North Korea. A-F only.

subject: KOR
title: Selected Readings in Korean
description: Selected readings in various disciplines. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: KOR
title: Structure of Korean: Phonology/Morphology
description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, and history.

subject: KOR
title: Structure of Korean: Syntax
description: Introduction to syntax and semantics.

subject: KOR
title: Language and Culture of Korea
description: DH Relation of Korean language to literature, history, philosophy, social structure, values, and interpersonal relationships; social and regional varieties. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Proficiency Through Film
description: Study of Korean culture through films to elevate students’ Korean proficiency level and improve their knowledge of Korea. Emphasis on writing instruction. Requires a minimum of 16 pages of graded writing.

subject: KOR
title: Korean for Academic Purposes: Humanities
description: Focus on expanding students’ Korean literacy and cultural knowledge in various Humanities disciplines, including history, religion, language, education, and literature. Taught entirely in Korean.

subject: KOR
title: Korean for Academic Purposes: Social Science & Others
description: Focus on expanding students’ Korean literacy and cultural knowledge in Social Science and other disciplines, including politics, economy, society, writing in Korean.

subject: KOR
title: Introduction to Traditional Korean Literature
description: DL Critical readings from earliest times and presentations that emphasize genre, style, and context.

subject: KOR
title: Introduction to Modern Korean Literature
description: DL Critical Korean-language readings of 20th-century literature that emphasize context and the development of style. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: KOR
title: Internship Program
description: Supervised internship with Korean professional hosts on O‘ahu or in Korea. Students will also attend an on-campus preparatory and follow-up language class. A-F only.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Abroad
description: Supervised internship with Korean professional hosts in Korea. Students also undergo a one-week training module designed to prepare them to maximize the benefits of the overseas internship. Repeatable up to 3 times. CR/ NC only.

subject: KOR
title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Primarily for graduate students from other departments. CR/NC only. Repeatable three times.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Verse
description: (Alpha) Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean lyric and didactic verse (e.g., hyangga, changga, hanshi, sijo, kasa, free form): (M) modern; (T) traditional. Repeatable one time with instructor consent for (M).
prerequisites: 494 or consent for (M), 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Narrative
description: (Alpha) Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean narrative (e.g., myth, p’ansori, shaman song, essay, biography, fiction): (M) modern; (T) traditional. Repeatable one time with instructor consent for (M).
prerequisites: 494 or consent for (M), 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Drama
description: (Alpha) Intensive and analytical reading of selected materials in Korean performing arts (e.g., spectacle, farce play, mask dance, staged narratives, theatrical drama): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prerequisites: 494 or consent for (M), 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Media Research in Korean
description: Focuses on searching, analyzing, and evaluating media data for research in areas of student specializations. Students are required to write short analysis papers and a final research paper. (Once a year)
prerequisites: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Comparative Studies of Contemporary South and North Korean Language
description: Comparing and analyzing language data to investigate language heterogeneity problems, its causes, and importance of comparative studies in NK/SK language differences; differences in language policy, grammar, and vocabulary, pronunciation, and discourse style. (Once a year)

subject: KOR
title: Interdisciplinary Research in Korean
description: Combined lecture-discussion on preparing students to be able to conduct interdisciplinary research in Korean. Require advanced-level Korean proficiency. (Once a year)
prerequisites: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse
description: (Alpha) Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: KOR
title: History and Dialects of Korean Language
description: Survey of various hypotheses on the genetic relationship of Korean; evolution of Korean from the 15th century to the present; Korean dialects.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Phonology and Morphology
description: Review of Korean vocalic and consonantal phonology. Phonological and morphological analysis of Korean derivation and inflection.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Syntax and Semantics
description: Review of theoretical problems in Korean syntax and semantics; different approaches; and contributions of Korean linguistic study to syntactic and semantic theory.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Sociolinguistics
