title: Introduction to Scripting
description: Introduction to scripting languages for the integration of applications and systems. Scripting in operating systems, web pages, server-side application integration, regular expressions, and event handling for languages such as Perl, JavaScript, PHP, Python, shell scripting. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Basic Concepts of Computer Science
description: What is the subject of computer science? What is a computer? Understand the basic models of computation and the concepts of computability, complexity, and network computation, and learn to use them in practice. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning Methods
description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as DATA 235)

subject: ICS
title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science II
description: Includes program correctness, recurrence relations and their solutions, relations and their properties, divide and conquer relations, graph theory, trees and their applications, Boolean algebra, introduction to formal languages and automata theory.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Science Careers: An Exploration of the Specialties of Computer Science
description: Exploration of the specialties of computer science. Meets every two week for 2.5 hours to explore specific areas in computer science. CR/NC only. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Sophomore Project
description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in a beginner-level design of a software project expected to be continued in ICS 396. CS majors only. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Algorithms
description: (4 1-hr Lec) Design and correctness of algorithms, including divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming methods. Complexity analyses using recurrence relations, probabilistic methods, and NP-completeness. Applications to order statistics, disjoint sets, B-trees and balanced trees, graphs, network flows, and string matching.
prerequisites: 211, and [(241 or ECE 362) and (MATH 216 or 242 or 252A)] or (MATH 301 and 372); or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Machine-Level and Systems Programming
description: Machine organization, machine instructions, addressing modes, assembler language, subroutine linkage, linking to higher-level languages, interface to operating systems, introduction to assemblers, loaders and compilers.
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205) (or concurrent), (311 or ECE 367), and 314; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Programming Language Theory
description: Syntax, semantics, control structures, variable binding and scopes, data and control abstractions. Programming in functional (LISP) and logic (Prolog) programming styles.
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205), (311 or ECE 367), and 314; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Software Engineering I
description: Problem analysis and design, team-oriented development, quality assurance, configuration management, project planning. These topics are covered in the sequence 314-414.
prerequisites: (211 or ECE 205) and [241 or ECE 362 or (MATH 301 and 372)]; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Database Systems I
description: Introduction to relational database systems, data modeling, query processing, transaction processing, storage, and indexing.

subject: ICS
title: Logic Design and Microprocessors
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Basic machine architecture, microprocessors, bus organization, circuit elements, logic circuit analysis and design, microcomputer system design.
prerequisites: (212 or ECE 205), (311 or ECE 367), and 314; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Operating Systems
description: Operating system concepts and structure, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, scheduling, file systems, inter-process communication, virtualization, popular operating systems. A-F only.

subject: ICS
title: Network Design and Management
description: Overview of the internet and its capabilities; introduction to HTTP, TCP/IP, ethernet, and wireless 802.11; routers, switches, and NAT; network and wireless security; practical experience in designing and implementing networks. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust I: Resource Protections
description: Security and trust in computers, networks, and society. Security models. Access and authorization. Availability and Denial-of-Service. Trust processes and network interactions.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Programming
description: Introduction to the theory of Artificial Intelligence and the practical application of AI techniques in Functional (Common LISP and/or Scheme) and Logic (Prolog) programming languages. Students gain practical experience through programming assignments and projects. A-F only.
prerequisites: (215 or 212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming w

subject: POLS
title: American Political Theory
description: DS. Origins and development of American political thought.
prerequisites: any 100 level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Political Theory
description: DS. Significant works, historical continuities, themes, and issues in political theory. (B) classical political philosophy; (F) revolution and utopia; (G) contemporary political theory; (I) Marxist philosophy.
prerequisites: any 100- or 200- level POLS course; or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Feminist Theory
description: DS. Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.” (Cross-listed as WGSS 439)
prerequisites: any 300 level POLS or WGSS course; or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Korean Politics and Society Through Film
description: DS. Examines modern Korean politics and society through films. Through movies and documentaries, students will learn major sociopolitical issues including military dictatorship, democratization, and globalization that Korea underwent for the last several decades. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: POLS
title: The Politics of Media
description: DS. Study of the political manipulation of aural and verbal images. Exercises to increase media literacy.
prerequisites: any 100 level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Political Design and Futuristics
description: DS. Alternative future social and political possibilities; design of means of realization of desirable futures.
prerequisites: any 100 level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: The Politics of Film
description: DS. Political, philosophical, and artistic dimensions of film; cross-cultural film genres; representational practices in films.
prerequisites: any 100 level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Nā Politika ma ka Nūhou Hawai‘i – Politics in Hawaiian Language Media
description: DH. Study of Hawaiian news media with emphasis on political content. Taught in Hawaiian. (Cross-listed as HAW 445)
prerequisites: HAW 302 (or concurrent) and one of 110, 120, 130, 170, or 171; or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Advanced Topics in Theory, Media, and Method
description: DS. Studies in political theory, media, and methods that analyze their interrelations in a globalized world.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Disability Law and Politics
description: DS. Introduction to the history and politics of U.S. disability law and activism. An analysis of disability politics as the result of the interaction between disability movement activism and the development of policy and law. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: DS. Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom. A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 436 and WGSS 436)
prerequisites: one of WGSS 151, WGSS 175, WGSS 176, WGSS 202, WGSS 360, WGSS 381, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: DS. History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory. (Cross-listed as AMST 438 and WGSS 462)
prerequisites: one of 339, AMST 310, AMST 316, AMST 318, AMST 373, AMST 455, WGSS 360, WGSS 361, WGSS 439; or consent.

subject: POLS
title: American Politics (Elections)
description: DS. Examination of voters and voting processes (participation, apathy, socialization, symbolic process, media, etc.); ideologies and belief systems.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Law, Politics and Society
description: DS. Relationships between law, politics, and society will be explored. Emphasis is placed on several dimensions of legality: legal “indeterminacy” and some of the many things that law does for us and to us; law’s response to violence; the connections between law and social change; access to the law and its sociological dimensions; how/why law fails and what happens when it does. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 374)
prerequisites: a 100 level or 200 level POLS course or SOC 100 or any 200 level SOC course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Constitutional Law I: Institutional Power
description: DS. Provides students with methods for interpreting U.S. Supreme Court decisions and analyzes the U.S. Supreme Court’s jurisprudence on institutional authority, including the Judiciary, Executive, and Legislative branches and their relationships to power.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Constitutional Law II: Rights and Liberties
description: DS. Analyzes the U.S. Supreme Court’s jurisprudence on civil rights and liberties.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Law and Politics
description: DS. Current issues; recent research findings; practical research undertaken by student.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in American Politics
description: DS. Specific institutions and processes of the American governmental system.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Power in America
description: DS. Analysis of sources of political, economic, and social power in the U.S. and the institutions through which it is exercised.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Environmental Law and Politics
description: DS. Focuses on theories, laws, policies, ethics, and sustainable futures of Hawai‘i and the U.S. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as SUST 380)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: any 100 or 200 level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Administration and Society
description: DS. Historical emergence of modern bureaucracy; mutual impact of administrative forms on social life; relation of bureaucracy to capitalism and patriarchy; constitution of the administered individual.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Political Leadership
description: DS. Exploration of concepts and theories of political leadership, partly through biography, as preparation for public service or advanced scholarly inquiry.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: POLS
title: Politics and Public Policy II
description: DS. Overview of the policy-making process in various political arenas (families, cities, nations, etc.); emphasis on conceptual and empirical analysis.
prerequisites: any 100 level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Women and Politics
description: DS. Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries. Female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions. (Cross-listed as WGSS 384)
prerequisites: any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent), WGSS 151 (or concurrent), or WGSS 362 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: POLS
title: American Politics
description: DS. Institutions (parties, interest groups, legislatures, executives, local government); policies (national defense, poverty, energy, etc.), politics (symbolism, inequality, race, and gender).

subject: POLS
title: Public Policy-Making
description: Students develop understanding of theory, practice, and ethical issues of public policy-making. Combines lecture/discussion and fieldtrips. Students develop policy analysis and strategic plans that identify issues, interests, and methods of influence. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as HON 301)
prerequisites: HON 101 or HON 291(Alpha), or departmental approval.

subject: POLS
title: Politics of the Ocean
description: DS. Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 387)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. Pre: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Health Politics
description: DS. Examines the politics of health care. Focus on institutional models to health care, the politics of health care reform, and contemporary health care issues and controversies. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. Pre: any 100-level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Political Inquiry and Analysis
description: DS. Introductory survey and analysis of methods used in empirical research, policy analysis, and social criticism.

subject: POLS
title: Advanced Topics in Law, Policy, and Society
description: DS. Studies integrating concerns of public law, public policy, public administration, and social movements.
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives
description: DS. Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 394)
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or 390 (or concurrent) or WGSS 151, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
description: DS. Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics. (Cross-listed as PACE 373)
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Teaching Political Science
description: Practicum for majors who serve as undergraduate teaching assistants. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: POLS 390 (or concurrent), senior standing; and consent.

subject: POLS
title: Legislative Internship
description: DS. Field placement at the Hawai‘i Legislature integrated with academic study of political institutions and practices. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: POLS
title: Community Internship
description: DS. Field placement integrated with academic study of political institutions and community organizations. Repeatable one time.

subject: POLS
title: Senior Thesis
description: Independent research and thesis writing with supervision of senior advisor.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Logic
description: Model theory, computability theory, set theory. In particular syntax and semantics of first order logic; incompleteness, completeness, and compactness theorems; Loewenheim-Skolem theorems; computable and computably enumerable sets; axioms of set theory; ordinals and cardinals. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Set Theory
description: Axiomatic development, ordinal and cardinal numbers, recursion theorems, axiom of choice, continuum hypothesis, consistency and independence results.

subject: MATH
title: Recursive Functions and Complexity
description: Recursive, r.e., Ptime, and Logspace classes. Nondeterminism, parallelism, alternation, and Boolean circuits. Reducibility and completeness.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Algebraic Number Theory
description: Number fields and rings of integers; primes, factorization, and ramification theory; finiteness of the class group; Dirichlet’s Unit Theorem; valuations, completions, and local fields. Further topics. Graduate students only.
prerequisites: Pre: MATH 611 (with a minimum grade of B-).

subject: MATH
title: Advanced Probability
description: Independence and conditioning, martingales, ergodic theory, Markov chains, central limit theorem. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Pre: MATH 631 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Stochastic Processes
description: Stationary, Gaussian, and Markov processes. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Pre: MATH 671 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Graph Theory
description: Connected graphs and digraphs. Graph embeddings. Connectivity and networks. Factors and factorizations. Coverings. Coloring. Applications.

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading and Research for Plan B Masters Students
description: Maximum of 3 credit hours. Repeatable two times. Graduate standing in MATH. A-F only.

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Maximum of 3 credit hours. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MATH
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MATH
title: Apprenticeship in Teaching
description: An experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation. Open to graduate students in mathematics only. Repeatable one time, up to six credits. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Pre: graduate standing in mathematics and consent.

subject: MATH
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Engineering Design I
description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Introductory experience in analysis, synthesis, and design. Teamwork and project required.
prerequisites: Pre: high school physics or consent.

subject: ME
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as EPET 201)

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Engineering Design
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Introductory experience in communication, presentation, professional ethics, social responsibility, engineering economics, quality control, and computer-aided drafting. Teamwork and project required.

subject: ME
title: Applied Mechanics II
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy. CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CEE 271)
prerequisites: Pre: C or better in CEE 270; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

subject: ME
title: Space Science and Instrumentation
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation. A-F only. Pre: EPET 201, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272. (Fall only) (Crosslisted as EPET 301)
prerequisites: Pre: EPET 201, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272.

subject: ME
title: Thermodynamics
description: (3 Lec, 1 Discussion) Basic laws, closed and open systems. Work, heat, concept of entropy. Properties of pure simple substances. Ideal gases. Introduction to power and refrigeration cycles.
prerequisites: Pre: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A), PHYS 170 and MATH 244 (or MATH 253A).

subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Fluids and Lab
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Incompressible and compressible ideal fluids, effects of viscosity. Similitude, boundary layer flow. Measurement techniques in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prerequisites: Pre: grade of C or better in all of ME 311 and CEE 271 (or ME 271).

subject: ME
title: Materials Science and Engineering
description: Electronic, atomic, and crystalline structure of materials and their effect on the mechanical, electrical, optical, and magnetic properties of engineering metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
prerequisites: Pre: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A), MATH 242 (or MATH 252A), and PHYS 170.

subject: ME
title: Manufacturing Processes and Lab
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Energy requirements for manufacturing methods. Manufacturing methods to obtain components with desired size/shape/properties. Conduct manufacturing experiments. Emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Manufacturing Processes Lab
description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Manufacturing laboratory: tension/ compression tests, cold rolling, welding, casting, statistical process control, programming and milling using a CNC machine. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Computer Methods in Engineering
description: Numerical solutions for algebraic and transcendental equations, simultaneous linear algebraic equations, integration and differentiation; integration of ordinary differential equations. Engineering applications.
prerequisites: Pre: grade of C or better in all of ECE 160 (or ECE 110 or ICS 111), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A), and MATH 302 (or MATH 307).

subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Solids
description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, consitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading. (Crosslisted as CEE 370)
prerequisites: Pre: C or better in all of the following: CEE 270; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

subject: ME
title: Component Design
description: Design, analysis, and selection of machine components: shafts, screws, fasteners, welds, rolling contact bearings, journal bearings, gears, clutches, brakes, belts, and roller chains.
prerequisites: Pre: ME 213, and either ME 371 or CEE 370.

subject: ME
title: Kinematics/Dynamics Machinery
description: Velocity and acceleration analysis of planar mechanisms; kinematic synthesis of linkages, cams, and gears; static and dynamic force analysis of mechanisms; balancing of machinery.
prerequisites: Pre: CEE 271 or ME 271 (C or better), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A) and either MATH 302 or MATH 307

subject: ME
title: Dynamics of Machines and Systems and Lab
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr. Lab) Lumped-parameter modeling of dynamic systems. Methods of analysis, including transform techniques. Time and frequency response. Feedback control. Engineering instrumentation. Data acquisition. Dynamic measurements. Design and testing. Lab report writing.
prerequisites: Pre: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (or ME 271) and MATH 302 (or MATH 307).

subject: ME
title: Space Mission Design
description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as EPET 400)

subject: ME
title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as EPET 401)

subject: ME
title: Dynamics Systems Laboratory
description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Analysis, design, fabrication, testing and characterization of engineering instrumentation. Computer-based data acquisition methods. Techniques and procedures associated with carrying out dynamic measurements within the constraints of cost, time and accuracy.
prerequisites: Pre: one of ME 360, MATH 407, or PHYS 305 (or concurrent for any); and ME 375 (or concurrent).

subject: ME
title: Advanced Mathematics for Engineers
description: Applications of ordinary differential equations, Laplace transform, vector field theory, matrices, line integrals.
prerequisites: Pre: MATH 244 (or MATH 253A), and MATH 302 (or MATH 307).

subject: ME
title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Basic computational fluid dynamics; four important partial differential equations; introduction to finite element method: Interpolation and Galerkin method; finite element method for transport phenomena; some algorithms for parallel computing. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: ME 422 (or concurrent ), and either ME 360, MATH 407 or PHYS 3

subject: OEST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Selected interdisciplinary ocean/earth-related topics involving science, technology, engineering, and/or policy. Repeatable one time.
program: Ocean and Earth Science and Technology
department: Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: OEST
title: Ocean Policy and Management
description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as SOCS 735)
program: Ocean and Earth Science and Technology
department: Ocean and Earth Science and Technology

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Technology—Man in the Sea
description: Survey of human activities in the ocean, from the most traditional to the most innovative technical and engineering accomplishments.

subject: ORE
title: Surf Science and Culture
description: Introduction to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the human interaction with the ocean using Western science and cultural perspectives. A-F only.

subject: ORE
title: Surf Science and Culture Lab
description: Practical laboratory dedicated to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the ocean environment through technology. A-F only.

subject: ORE
title: Mineral and Energy Resources
description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints. A-F only. (Cross-listed as OCN 330)

subject: ORE
title: Buoyancy and Stability
description: Ship nomenclature and geometry, hydrostatic principles of surface ships and underwater vehicles in free-floating, partially waterborne, and damaged conditions. Subdivision of ships. Launching.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean and Resources Engineering Laboratory
description: Design, construction, and evaluation of an engineering system. Laboratory and field experience and data analysis supplemented with appropriate theory.

subject: ORE
title: Oceanography for Ocean Engineers
description: Physical, chemical, biological, and geological ocean environments for ocean engineers. Introduction to ocean dynamical processes and general circulation. Ocean measurement techniques, theory of underwater acoustics. Sonar, swath bathymetry, and tomography applications.

subject: ORE
title: Water Wave Mechanics
description: Governing equations in free surface flow, deterministic and probabilistic wave theories, wave transformation, wave-induced coastal currents, tides, ocean engineering operational sea state, and design wave criteria.

subject: ORE
title: Probability and Statistics for Ocean Engineers
description: Probability and statistical analysis including distributions, multiple regression and correlation, autocovariance, cross-spectra, and practical applications in ocean engineering.

subject: ORE
title: Hydrodynamics of Fluid-Body Interaction
description: Hydrodynamics of ships, coastal and offshore structures. Wave forces by potential theory and by Morison’s equation. Method of source distribution for potential flow problems. Flows with prescribed body motion, fixed and freely floating bodies.

subject: ORE
title: Dynamics of Ocean Structures
description: Response of floating platforms and vessels to wave action, spectral analysis in sea keeping. Frequency and time domain analyses of rigid body motions in six degrees of freedom. A-F only.
prerequisites: ORE 411 or consent. Co-requisite: ORE 609 or consent.

subject: ORE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk. (Cross-listed as CEE 621 and SUST 621)
prerequisites: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable

subject: ORE
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change. (Cross-listed as CEE 624 and SUST 624)

subject: ORE
title: Structural Analysis in Ocean Engineering
description: Structural and finite element analyses and design of ocean structures to withstand hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loading of the sea. Considerations include material type, safety factor, stress concentration, and fatigue.

subject: ORE
title: Environmental Fluid Dynamics
description: Fluid dynamics for coastal and estuarine environments. Turbulent mixing processes in homogeneous and stratified fluids. Buoyancy driven flows, internal hydraulics, topographic effects and estuarine circulation. Spill and pollutant dispersal.

subject: ORE
title: Applications in Ocean Acoustics
description: Using sound to observe the ocean. Fundamentals of propagation. Topics include marine mammals, navigation and communication, seismics, ships, wind and rain, ocean dynamics, flow and biological imaging and measurement, seafloor mapping, and the forward/ inverse problem. (Once a year)

subject: ORE
title: Autonomous Marine Systems
description: Identifies the unique challenges faced by autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, and analyzes approaches to address those challenges. Topics include hydrodynamic vehicle modeling, propeller theory, subsystem integration, and motion control strategies. (Cross-listed as ME 657)
prerequisites: Graduate students only. MATH 307 or MATH 311 (or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 (or equivalent), or instructor consent.

subject: ORE
title: Coastal and Harbor Engineering
description: Planning and design of seawalls, groins, jetties, breakwaters, and layout of ports. Design requirements for harbor entrances and channels. Littoral drift and sedimentation problems. Navigation and mooring requirements.

subject: ORE
title: Nearshore Processes and Sediment Transport
description: coastal areas and its effect on morphological processes. Effect of man-made structures on littoral drift and shoreline.

subject: ORE
title: Marine Renewable Energy
description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power. (Cross-listed as SUST 677)
prerequisites: ORE 607; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable

subject: ORE
title: Marine Mineral Resources Engineering
description: Activities in marine minerals development are examined in a multidisciplinary systems approach involving engineering, Earth and environmental sciences and economics.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Engineering and Resilience in a Changing Climate
description: Focus on understanding the changing ocean conditions (e.g. waves and sea levels) relevant to the resilience of practical ocean engineering applications. (Spring only)
prerequisites: ORE 607 or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: ORE
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
degrees: MS in Ocean and Resources Engineering

subject: ORE
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: ORE
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for MS in ocean and resources engineering
degrees: MS in Ocean and Resources Engineering

subject: ORE
title: Nonlinear Water Wave Theories
description: Higher-order theories. Forced oscillations. Stoke’s theory. Nonlinear shallow-water wave equations and hydraulic jumps; effects of rotation. Internal waves. Analytical techniques necessary will be developed as course progresses.

subject: ORE
title: Numerical Methods in Ocean Engineering
description: Formulation and application of numerical methods for simulating and solving ocean engineering problems. Mathematical and computational fundamentals; accuracy and stability; numerical interpolation, differentiation, and integration; boundary element, finite difference, and finite element methods.

subject: ORE
title: (Alpha) Capstone Design Project
description: Major design experience based on knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work and incorporating realistic constraints that include economic, environmental, ethical, social, and liability considerations. description: FGC Foundations in Indigenous politics from diverse cultural perspectives.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Philosophy of Religion
description: Key issues in theory of religious experience, language, reasoning.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Aesthetics
description: Key issues in contemporary aesthetics, against background of traditional Western and Eastern theories. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Epistemology
description: Key issues in contemporary philosophical debates about knowledge. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophical Foundations of Cultural Criticism
description: A survey of the philosophical texts, thinkers, concepts, and theoretical approaches that are used in cultural criticism. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Hermeneutics
description: Important debates concerning the methodology of textual interpretation.

subject: PHIL
title: History and Theory of Science
description: Exploration of problems at the intersection of historical studies of science as a process and philosophical analysis of basic concepts of the sciences.
prerequisites: graduate standing or consent. Recommended: 308 or 316.

subject: PHIL
title: Confucianism
description: Ethical, social, institutional problems in classical theory. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Neo-Confucianism
description: Logic, epistemology, metaphysics, and ethics of major Chinese Neo-Confucian philosophers, 11th–16th century. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Daoism
description: Critical examination and evaluation of major philosophical ideas in Lao Zi, Zhuang Zi, and the Neo-Daoists. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable up to 30 credits.

subject: PHIL
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable up to six credits.
prerequisites: master’s Plan A candidate and consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar on Individual Philosophers
description: The most significant texts of an important philosopher. Repeatable three times in the MA program; an additional four times in the PhD program.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Philosophical Topics
description: Close study of a topic of important philosophical controversy. Repeatable two times in the MA program; an additional three times in the PhD program.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Islamic Philosophy
description: Major philosophical problems in Islamic thought. Focus either on a specific topic or one author. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar on Philosophical Periods
description: Close study of a period of significant and connected philosophical activity within a philosophic tradition. Repeatable two times with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Philosophical Texts
description: Reading, analysis, and critical discussion of one (or of several closely related) philosophical text in its original language (sometimes in conjunction with established translation). Repeatable two times with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Indian Philosophy
description: Major philosophical problems in the development of Indian thought during its formative period. Repeatable two times with consent of instructor and Graduate Chair.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Buddhist Philosophy
description: Major philosophical problems in the development of Buddhist thought during its formative period. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Chinese Philosophy
description: Fundamental issues, problems, movements, and schools of Chinese philosophy, such as classical Confucianism, Daoism, Legalism, Chinese logic, and Neo-Confucianism. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Yi Jing
description: Metaphysical, epistemological, ethical, and axiological views of Yi Jing and its claim as foundational work for classical Confucianism, Daoism, and Neo-Confucianism.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Japanese Philosophy
description: Various periods, movements, and thinkers in Japanese philosophy. Topic changes each semester. Consult department for more information. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Seminar in Comparative Philosophy
description: Comparison of widely differing philosophical traditions. Specific topic changes each semester. Consult department for more information. Repeatable two times with consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PHYS
title: Survey of Physics
description: DP. Mechanics, electricity and magnetism, waves, optics, atomic and nuclear physics. Only algebra and geometry used. For non-science majors.

subject: PHYS
title: Survey of Physics Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Hooke’s law, falling bodies, collisions, Boyle’s law, electric and magnetic fields, induction, waves, optics.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics in the Arts
description: DP. Introduction to physics of sound and light, with applications to music and visual arts: sound perception, harmony, musical scales, instruments; lenses, cameras, color perception and mixing. Uses algebra and geometry. Intended primarily for non-science majors.

subject: PHYS
title: How Things Work: Physics for Everyday Life
description: DP. Introduction to physics and science in everyday life. It considers objects from our daily environment, and focuses on the principles such as motion, forces, heat, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics. A-F only.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics I
description: DP. Non-calculus physics. Mechanics, wave motion, heat.
prerequisites: MATH 140X, or 215 or higher; or qualifying score on math placement exam.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics Lab I
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to experimental analysis, physical observation and measurement, experiments on conservation laws, fluid friction, oscillations.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics II
description: DP. Electricity, magnetism, optics, modern physics.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics Lab II
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Optics, electric and magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics I
description: DP. Calculus-based mechanics of particles and rigid bodies: kinematics, force, energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, fluids, oscillations and waves. Intended for physical science and engineering majors.
prerequisites: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Honors General Physics I
description: DP. Special format for topics: mechanics of particles and rigid bodies, wave motion, thermodynamics and kinetic theory.
prerequisites: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent. Co-requisite: 170L

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics I Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to 151L but at 170 level.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics II
description: DP. Electricity and magnetism and geometric optics.
prerequisites: 151 or 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A, MATH 216 may be substituted with consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Honors General Physics II
description: DP. Special format for topics: electricity and magnetism and geometric optics. A-F only.
prerequisites: 151 or 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A, MATH 216 may be substituted with consent. Co-requisite: 272L.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics II Lab
description: DY. (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to 152L but at 272 level.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics III
description: DP. Relativity, introduction to quantum mechanics, atomic and nuclear physics, and physical optics.
prerequisites: 152 or 272 and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics III Lab
description: DY. (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating selected concepts of 274, including diffraction and interference of light, wave nature of matter, photoelectric effect, atomic spectra, and semiconductors.

subject: PHYS
title: Computational Physics
description: DP. (3 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Analysis of physical systems and problem solving using computers and numerical methods. Development of scientific writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
prerequisites: 152 or 272 or 272A, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Theoretical Mechanics I
description: DP. Particle dynamics, rigid-body dynamics, planetary motion. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 170 or 170A; 272 or 272A; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: MATH 302 (or concurrent).

subject: PHYS
title: Theoretical Mechanics II
description: DP. Rigid-body mechanics continued, fluid dynamics, wave motion, theory of relativity.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity and Magnetism
description: DP. Electrostatic and magnetostatic fields in vacuum and in matter; induction; Maxwell’s equations; AC circuits. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 272 or 272A; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

subject: PHYS
title: Individual Work in Advanced Physics
description: Limited to students with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in physics.

subject: ME
title: Materials for Solar Energy Conversion
description: Atom structure, electromagnetic waves and energy, electronic and energetic properties of semi-conducting materials, junctions, solar cells operations, bulk and thin film materials synthesis, integration of solar cells into the electric grid. ECE and ME majors only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: (331 or ECE 324) with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: ME
title: Electrochemical Power Sources: Principles, Applications, and Sustainability
description: Electrochemistry, batteries, fuel cells, flow batteries, electrochemical capacitors, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage. ENGR majors only. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: 331, CHEM 162, CHEM 171, or CHEM 181A (with a grade of C- or better).

subject: ME
title: Experimental Stress Analysis
description: (1-3 hr Lab) Techniques of experimental stress analysis: strain and deflection measurement of beams and shafts, strain to stress conversion, principal and maximum shearing stresses, failure in biaxial stress states, stress concentrations, residual stresses, buckling, creep, electrical resistance strain gages, brittle coatings, photoelastic methods, transducers. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Vibrations
description: DP Response of machines and systems to transient and periodic excitation. Vibration isolation and transmissibility. Modal analysis of multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Applications to design.

subject: ME
title: Fundamentals of Acoustics
description: DP Plane and spherical acoustic waves. Transmission, reflection, radiation, and absorption. Near and far fields, radiation patterns. Applications to noise control. Instruments.

subject: ME
title: Thermofluid Measurements and Design
description: Measurement techniques in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Contemporary engineering ethics issues. Final report and presentation are required. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Design Project I
description: (2 1-hr Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Heuristic application of engineering design process and project planning via a significant, open-ended design project that includes realistic constraints involving economics, environmental sustainability, manufacturability, ethics, health, safety, society, and politics. Extensive written communication required. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Design Project II
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Continuation of design project initiated in ME 481. Extension of conceptual design to final design. Manufacturing of prototype: material and part selection, procurement, manufacturing specifications/ drawings. Testing of complex systems. Extensive oral communication required. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Research and Experiment Design
description: Introduction to research and experimentation via pursuit and reporting of an open-ended design project. Ethical issues in research and experimentation. Engineering, Biological Engineering, and Ocean & Resources Engineering majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: ME
title: System Engineering
description: Will cover system engineering design, analysis, and development concepts, requirements derivation/management, and program management processes, such as risk identification/ management and fiscal/schedule tools. ME majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: 213 (with a minimum grade of C). Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Pearl Harbor Co-op
description: Provides real-world engineering experience through project assignment and working alongside a practicing engineer at the Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard. ME majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: (322, 341, 372, and 375) with a minimum grade of C. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: (Alpha) Mentored Projects
description: Investigation of advanced problems, making use of faculty expertise for specific domains of work. (B) Design Project I; (C) Design Project II; (D) Research and Experiment Design. Junior or senior standing only. ME majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: instructor consent. Co-requisite: 481 for (B); 482 for (C); 483 for (D).

subject: ME
title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

subject: ME
title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

subject: ME
title: Project
description: Investigation of advanced problems in mechanical engineering design or development. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Renewable Energy Engineering and Sustainability
description: Analysis of principles of operation of renewable energy systems, and its interactions with sustainability. Fundamentals of renewable energy production, storage, and distribution.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Thermodynamics
description: Introduction to general principles of classical thermodynamics. Main topics include equilibrium conditions, thermodynamic relations, Legendre transformations, Maxwell relations, stability of thermodynamic systems, phase transitions, and critical phenomena. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics
description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics. Main topics include entropy, Boltzmann law, thermodynamic driving forces, statistical mechanics, chemical equilibria, solutions and mixtures, and applications of statistical thermodynamics in biology, chemistry, physics, and nanoscience. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Aerodynamics
description: Advanced topics in aerodynamics, two- and three-dimensional wing theory, slender-body theory, lifting surface methods, vortex and wave drag, analytical and numerical methods, for computing unsteady aerodynamic behavior and introduction to flightdynamics. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Thermal Environmental Engineering
description: Physiological response to thermal environment, designs of passive and active cooling systems, student project.

subject: ME
title: Boiling and Two-Phase Flow
description: Two-phase flow pattern and flow pattern maps; two-phase flow models (homogeneous, separate, drift flux, annular); laminar and turbulent film condensations; boiling incipience; pool boiling heat transfer; flow boiling heat transfer; critical heat flux (CHF). A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Biological Fluid Mechanics
description: Review of Newtonian fluid mechanics. Blood rheology and flow in elastic tubes. Murray’s Law and pulsatile flow propagation. Microcirculation dynamics and biological transport. Aquatic movement and comparative biological examples.

subject: ME
title: Conduction Heat Transfer
description: Steady and unsteady heat conduction with and without heat sources in solids. Analytical, numerical, graphical, analog methods for solving heat conduction problems.

subject: ME
title: Convection Heat Transfer
description: Heat transfer in laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Analogy between heat, momentum, mass transfer.

subject: ME
title: Radiation Heat Transfer
description: Radiant interchange among surfaces. Gaseous radiation. Combined conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer.

subject: ME
title: Microfluidics and Nanofluidics
description: Introduction to fundamental understanding of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena at micro-nanoscale; electrokinetics; chemical separation; colloids and emulsions; biophysics; micro-nanofabrication.

subject: ME
title: Numerical Methods in Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer
description: Integration of ordinary differential equations. Finite difference solutions of partial differential equations with applications to conduction and convection. Introduction to finite element methods.

subject: ME
title: Viscous Flows
description: Formulation and properties of the Navier-Stokes equations; exact solutions; creeping flows; lubrication theory; laminar boundary layers; laminar stability, and transition to turbulence; turbulent boundary layers.

subject: ME
title: Environmental Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transfer
description: Heat and mass transfer in Earth’s interior with applications to geothermal and petroleum reservoir engineering.

subject: ME
title: Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design
description: Chemical kinetics with heat and mass transfer. Balance equations applied to selected ideal reactors. Departures from ideality.

subject: ME
title: Renewable Energy Engineering I: Biomass
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Experimental methods and theory of thermochemical biomass conversion: static and dynamic temperature and mass measurements, thermogravimetry, differential scanning calorimetry, GCMS and HPLC techniques.

subject: ME
title: Rheology
description: Vector and tensor operations. Constutive equations. Generalized Newtonian fluids and linear viscoelastic fluids. Rheometry and experiments. Flow of suspensions. Advanced topics and rheology of polymers, food products, biomaterials and asphalt, laboratories.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Materials Science
description: Properties of materials interpreted from the atomistic viewpoint. Crystal structure and defects. Thermodynamics of solids; phase transformations; experimental techniques.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Transport Phenomena
description: Theory of momentum, heat, and mass transfer processes. Integral and differential conservation equations, constitutive laws, and interfacial boundary conditions. Dimensional analysis, perturbation theory, asymptotics, similarity, and Green’s fun

subject: POLS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Research Methods
description: Conceptual strategies, data collection approaches, and data analysis techniques appropriate to political inquiries. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Writing Politics
description: Seminar on the politics of writing, grammar, translation, argument, genre, and style with significant content on indigenous issues of oral traditions, alternative modes of writing and argument, and language continuance.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Political Thought
description: Pre-announced topics. Repeatable unlimited times. At least one section a year.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Indigenous Theory
description: Pre-announced topics may include gender and sexuality studies, postcolonial theory, colonial discourse analysis, globalization, historiography; emphasis on indigenous epistemologies and the work of native scholars. Repeatable one time.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: International Relations
description: Pre-announced problems of both international organization and politics. Repeatable unlimited times. At least one section a semester.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Comparative Government and Politics
description: Pre-announced topics. Repeatable unlimited times. At least one section a semester.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Public Administration
description: Pre-announced administrative theory, comparative and development administration, and functional aspects. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Public Policy
description: Pre-announced topics. Repeatable three times. At least one section a year.

subject: POLS
title: Indigenous Nations and the Problems of Sovereignty
description: Examines intersections of sovereignty and indigenity from comparative and critical perspectives. Engages indigenous studies of sovereignty and of alternative political frameworks. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: POLS
title: Decolonial Futures
description: Topic engages probable and preferable futures of indigenous struggles and resistances. Emphasis placed on the ethics and responsibilities used to move towards those futures.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Politics of Regions
description: Analysis of political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in regions and subregions of the world. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PORT
title: Elementary Portuguese
description: HSL Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: PORT
title: Elementary Portuguese
description: HSL Conversation, grammar and reading. Continuation of 101.

subject: PORT
title: Intensive Elementary Portugese
description: Intensive elementary Portuguese course covers content of 101 and 102 combined. Hybrid format combines 3 credits online and 3 credits face to face. HSL. (Fall only)

subject: PORT
title: Intermediate Portuguese
description: HSL Reading, conversation, writing, laboratory drill.

subject: PORT
title: Intermediate Portuguese
description: HSL Continuation of 201.

subject: PORT
title: Intensive Intermediate Portuguese
description: HSL Intensive Intermediate Portuguese course covers content of 201 and 202 combined. Hybrid format combines 3 credits online and 3 credits face to face. (Spring only)

subject: PORT
title: Conversation
description: Intensive practice in spoken Portuguese, focusing on the preparation and completion of oral tasks and presentations. 40% or more of the grade is based on 3-4 oral communication presentations.

subject: PORT
title: Third-Level Portuguese Abroad
description: Intensive, formal instruction at the third-year level in Portuguese language: reading, writing, pronunciation, grammar, or conversation in a Portuguese-speaking country. Repeatable one time.

subject: PORT
title: Fourth-Level Portuguese Abroad
description: Intensive formal instruction at the fourth-year level in Portuguese language, linguistics, culture, civilization, film, or literature in a Portuguese-speaking country. Repeatable one time.

subject: PRAK
title: Introduction to Prakrit I
description: Survey of principal Prakrit languages; selected readings and analysis.
prerequisites: PALI 381, PALI 382, SNSK 281, and SNSK 282; or equivalent.

subject: PRAK
title: Introduction to Prakrit II
description: Continuation of 481.

subject: PSTY
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individualized directed readings and/or research in mental health and psychiatry under the supervision of an instructor. Open to non-majors. Repeatable up to four times. A-F only.

subject: PSTY
title: Psychiatry Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, including knowledge, skills, attitudes for assessment, diagnosis, and management of psychiatric problems in medical practice, inpatient, and emergency room settings. Emphasis on development and application of psychosocial cultural formulations in all areas of psychiatric and medical practice. Repeatable two times. Co-requisites: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PEDS, SURG 532 and SURG 535.
prerequisites: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.

subject: PSTY
title: (Alpha) Electives in Psychiatry
description: Senior medical student elective providing advanced instruction on the theory and methods of mental health research as well as supervised participation in an assigned research project in the Department of Psychiatry. (B) adult inpatient PSTY; (C) child PSTY; (D) forensic PSTY; (E) journal editing; (F) community mental health; (G) PSTY aspects of OBGN, PED, MED, SURG; (H) sub-internship in adult PSTY; (I) substance abuse; (J) PSTY aspects of rehab medicine; (K) PSTY aspects of SURG; (M) PSTY consult liaison; (N) post-traumatic stress disorder; (O) extramural elective in PSTY; (Q) geriatric PSTY; (R) rural child PSTY; (S) public and rural PSTY; (T) mental health research. CR/NC only.

subject: PSTY
title: Philosophy & Human Suffering
description: To see how various philosophies and religions have tackled the question, “why is there suffering in the world?” Read short excerpts from “classic” texts and discuss in a welcoming atmosphere and draw own conclusions. Medical students only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Psychology
description: DS An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Psychology
description: DS An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Personal Development
description: DS The application of psychology to the understanding, management, and enhancement of one’s life.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Gender
description: DS Survey of topics in psychology relevant to gender and its impact on the lives of women and men: socialization of gender, mental health, racial identity, majority-minority status, sexual orientation, life-span issues and violence. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 202)

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Research Methods
description: DS (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Survey of standard methods and related conceptual issues employed in psychological research. Both experimental and non-experimental methods will be reviewed.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Behavioral Psychology
description: DS Outline of basic learning principles. A general, unified approach to study of human personality and behavior. Based upon a learning conception; various areas of psychology and the other social sciences are treated.

subject: PSY
title: Statistical Techniques
description: DS Frequency distributions; graphic methods; central tendency; variability; correlation; reliability; tests of significance.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Psychobiology
description: DB Survey of study of behavior from a natural sciences viewpoint. Evolution, ethological analysis of behavior genetics, neural mechanisms, drugs and behavior, biological development.

subject: PSY
title: Developmental Psychology
description: DS Emotional, mental, physical, social development from infancy to adulthood; interests and abilities at different age levels.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: DS Cognitive, behavioral, and emotional effects of people: interpersonal relations, attribution, attitudes, group behavior, stereotypes, social roles, aggression, helping, self-concept; applications.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Personality
description: DS Scientific study of personality, its meaning, assessment, development, relation to cultural-social determinants.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: DS History, theories, nature of psychological problems, methods of assessment, forms of intervention, current developments.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Community Psychology
description: DS Examination of human functioning in social and ecological context. Topics include stres

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Physical Oceanography
description: Near-shore processes, advanced mathematical techniques, recent developments, etc. Typically given by visiting professors in their specialties, or in response to student interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: OCN
title: Seminar
description: Oceanographic topics of current interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: OCN
title: Proposal Development
description: Introduction to the organization and functioning of oceanography funding agencies, the peer-review process, and the design and development of a research proposal. Repeatable one time. OCN majors only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: two of the following: 621, 626, 627 (or concurrent), or 628 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PAS
title: Overseas Study
description: Registration allows student to maintain enrolled status at UH Mānoa while taking courses abroad. CR/NC only.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Worlds: An Introduction to Pacific Islands Studies
description: DS. Introduces students to the geography, societies, histories, cultures, contemporary issues, and arts of Oceania, including Hawai‘i. Combines lectures and discussion that emphasize Pacific Islander perspectives and experiences. A-F only.

subject: PACS
title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Oceania
description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in the Pacific Islands through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions. A-F only.

subject: PACS
title: Islands of Globalization
description: DS. Combined lectures, service-learning. Examines the nature and impact of globalization on Pacific Island societies, viewed from the perspective of islanders who engage with global forces and processes, and create strategies to survive. Limit 20 students. A-F only.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Islands Movement and Migration
description: DS. Combined lecture and service-learning activities. Examines the diaspora of Pacific Islanders. Includes a service-learning activity examining cultural, political, and economic status of groups of Pacific Islanders living in other Pacific places. Limit of 20 students. A-F only.

subject: PACS
title: Arts in Oceania–An Introduction
description: DH. Practical and theoretical study of arts in Oceania in relevant cultural contexts. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Communities in Hawai‘i
description: DS. Examines Pacific Islander communities’ experiences in Hawai‘i through service learning, reading, writing, lecture, and discussion. Concerns about housing, employment, education, health, language, and culture are central. A-F only.

subject: PACS
title: Contemporary Issues in Oceania
description: DS. Combined lecture/discussion. Examination of critical political, social, and economic issues in the Pacific Islands region today.

subject: PACS
title: Thinking Through Pacific Arts, Ritual, and Performance
description: Lecture, discussion, and workshop series surveys arts, ritual, and performance practices throughout the Pacific. Engaging with Pacific traditions of thought, and creative approaches to research, students also return findings to Pacific communities. Repeatable one time.

subject: PACS
title: Islands and Archipelagos
description: DS. Applies an island studies perspective to critically evaluate the commonalities and differences across islands and archipelagos in several world regions. Examines how island geographies influence social identities and movements and are impacted by environmental conditions. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GEO 333)

subject: PACS
title: Literature of the Pacific
description: DL. Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the literature of the Pacific, including Pacific voyagers and contemporary writings in English by Pacific Islanders. (Cross-listed as ENG 371)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: PACS
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable up to 12 credits.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Islander Collaborative Research
description: Engage in intensive collaborative research with a Pacific Islander community in Hawai ʻi, culminating in a research paper and public presentation. Oral communication is an essential component of this course.

subject: PACS
title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
description: DH. Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawai‘i, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand. (Cross-listed as THEA 462)

subject: PACS
title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
description: DL. Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, writers, movements, or genres in the field of Pacific literature. Repeatable one time. (Crosslisted as ENG 474)
prerequisites: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course.

subject: PACS
title: Topics in Pacific Islands Studies
description: DS. Repeatable two times.

subject: PACS
title: Moving Images in the Pacific Islands
description: Critically examines indigenous and foreign representations of the Pacific Islands and is designed to make film a central focus of inquiry for students interested in the contemporary Pacific. Repeatable one time.

subject: PACS
title: Culture and Consumption in Oceania
description: Lecture on changing patterns of consumption in Oceania, and the historical, political, cultural, artistic, and economic forces shaping such practices.

subject: PACS
title: Learning Oceania
description: Graduate seminar. Introduction to the nature and origins of Pacific Studies as an organized field of study. Epistemological, conceptual, political and ethical issues facing students of the region today.

subject: PACS
title: Re/Presenting Oceania: Pacific and American Perspectives
description: Graduate seminar. Critical analysis of the way physical, social and cultural aspects of Oceania have been represented in scholarly and popular media.

subject: PACS
title: Researching Oceania: Creative and Conventional Methods of Inquiry
description: Graduate seminar. Literacy, theory and method in the creation of a Master’s research project.

subject: PACS
title: Women in Oceania
description: Will look at feminist theory, ethnography, culture, activism and globalization in the context of writing, research and film on or by Women in Oceania.

subject: PACS
title: Topics in Histories of Oceania
description: Reading and research on major issues, topics, and themes in the history of Oceania. Repeatable three times. (Cross-listed as HIST 675)

subject: PACS
title: Graduate Seminar: Change in the Pacific
description: Interrelationship of change in selected Pacific Islands regions, institutions, and processes. Repeatable two times.

subject: PACS
title: Master’s Portfolio Project
description: Independent study for students working on MA portfolio projects. A grade of satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: PACS
title: Directed Reading and Research

subject: PACS
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PALI
title: Elementary Pali I
description: Reading simple texts from Pali canon. Grammar taught as needed for the reading.

subject: PALI
title: Elementary Pali II
description: Continuation of 381.

subject: PALI
title: Intermediate Pali I
description: Continuation of 382. Reading various Hinayâna texts.

subject: PALI
