subject: PATH
title: Immunopathology Seminar
description: Autoimmune diseases and transplantation immunity.

subject: PATH
title: Directed Research
description: Pathology of aging, nutrition, alcoholism, and immunology. Open to selected undergraduate students. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PATH
title: Unit II Concurrent Elective
description: Elective course for first-year medical students. CR/NC only.

subject: PATH
title: Unit V Concurrent Elective
description: Elective course for second-year medical students. CR/NC only.

subject: PATH
title: Unit V Block Elective
description: Required elective for second-year medical students, objectives to be determined by contract. One option is a review of USMLE Part I. CR/NC only.

subject: PATH
title: Pathology Practicum
description: Required autopsy experience involving dissection and microscopic examination of tissues and detailed evaluation of disease process. CR/NC only.

subject: PATH
title: (Alpha) Unit VII Electives in Pathology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology. Repeatable four times. CR/NC only.

subject: PATH
title: Introduction to Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
description: Provides an introduction to the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine and the role pathologists and the laboratory play in the diagnosis and management of disease. MD students only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: PATH
title: Electives in Pathology
description: Individualized instruction in clinical and/or anatomic pathology. Third-year elective. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PACE
title: Survey of Conflict Management
description: DH. Survey of contemporary conflict management and resolution: negotiation, mediation, conciliation, ombuds, fact-finding, facilitation techniques, arbitration, and

subject: PHYS
title: Theoretical Mechanics I
description: Particle dynamics, rigid-body dynamics, planetary motion. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 170 or 170A; 272 or 272A; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: MATH 302 (or concurrent).

subject: PHYS
title: Theoretical Mechanics II
description: Rigid-body mechanics continued, fluid dynamics, wave motion, theory of relativity.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity and Magnetism
description: Electrostatic and magnetostatic fields in vacuum and in matter; induction; Maxwell’s equations; AC circuits. (Fall only)
prerequisites: 272 or 272A; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

subject: PHYS
title: Individual Work in Advanced Physics
description: Limited to students with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Applications of Mathematics in Physical Sciences
description: Mathematical methods, techniques; applications to problems in physical sciences. Recommended: upper division mathematics course.
prerequisites: MATH 244 or MATH 253A, and MATH 307 or 311; or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
description: Laws of thermodynamics, heat transfer, kinetic theory, statistical mechanics.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Physics I
description: Crystal structure: lattice vibrations; phonon effects; electronic processes in solids (metals, semiconductors, and superconductors).

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Physics II
description: Energy-band calculations, optical processes, Josephson effect, theories of dielectrics and magnetism, physics of color centers, order-disorder transformation.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetic Waves
description: Field equations, plane, spherical and guided waves.

subject: PHYS
title: Physical Optics
description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics. (Cross-listed as ECE 470)
prerequisites: 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C) or ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-), or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: General Relativity & Cosmology
description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation. Recommended: ASTR 242. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as ASTR 470)

subject: PHYS
title: Electronics for Physicists
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Investigation of Kirchoff’s Laws, electromagnetic circuit theory. Fourier analysis and stability theory with circuits. Applications to physical measurements are stressed. A-F only.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Electronics for Physicists
description: Introduction to high performance solid state instrumentation by means of practical research electronics: printed circuit board design/fabrication; complex programmable logic design/verification; integrated circuit SPICE simulation. Detector fabrication and test emphasis during final project. (Spring only)

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics I
description: Wave mechanics, Schroedinger equation, angular momenta, potential problems.
prerequisites: 274, 310, 350, 400 (or concurrent); either MATH 244 or 253A; and either MATH 311 or 307; or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory I
description: Advanced experiments involving nuclear spectroscopy, angular correlations in positronium annihilation, optical polarization, chaos, measurement of speed of light, numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics II
description: Continuation of 480; atomic physics, scattering, perturbation theory.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory II
description: Advanced experiments involving measurement of the muon lifetime, crystal x-ray diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance, the Mössbauer effect, and numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.

subject: PHYS
title: Professional Ethics for Physicists
description: Student seminar on ethical principles and their application to research in physics and astronomy and closely-related fields. Historical examples will be presented and discussed by the participants. PHYS, ASTP, and ASTR majors only. A-F only.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Physics
description: Introduction to nuclear and elementary-particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as NSCI 505)

subject: PHYS
title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Mathematical tools of theoretical physics. Continuation of 400 but with an independent selection of topics. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Analytical Mechanics
description: Dynamics of particles, particle systems; rigid bodies; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian equations; special relativity.

subject: PHYS
title: Electrodynamics I
description: Potential theory, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, boundary value problems. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Electrodynamics II
description: Relativistic electrodynamics, radiation by charged particles. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Optics
description: Contemporary advanced applications in optics including nonlinear optics and optical parametric oscillators, atomic lasers and laser systems, and free-electron lasers. (Alt. even years)

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar
description: Discussions and reports on physical theory and recent developments. CR/NC only.

subject: PHYS
title: Condensed Matter Seminar
description: Results and discussions of current topics in condensed matter physics. Repeatable six times with consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar on Atomic and Solid-State Physics
description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in atomic, surface, and solid-state physics. Repeatable five times with consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar on Elementary Particle Physics
description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in elementary particle physics. Repeatable four times.

subject: PHYS
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PHYS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PHYS
title: Topics in Particles and Fields
description: Topics in current theoretical research; e.g., unified field theories, general relativity, gravitation, and cosmology. Repeatable four times.

subject: PHYS
title: Special Topics: Experimental Physics
description: Topics in current experimental research in low-energy physics, high-energy physics, cross-disciplinary physics. Repeatable in different topics.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Topics in Condensed Matter Theory
description: Topics in condensed matter theory, e.g., group theory, many-body techniques, renormalization group, density functional theory, other topics of current interest. Repeatable four times.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Physics I
description: Equilibrium thermodynamics; Gibbs ensembles; quantum statistics; ideal and non-ideal Fermi; Bose and Boltzmann gases; phase transitions; and critical phenomena. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Physics II
description: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics, transport theory, fluctuation dissipation theorem, many-body Green’s function methods, normal Fermi and Bose liquids, superfluidity, superconductivity. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques. Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as ASTR 760)

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory I
description: Relativistic wave equations and their solutions. Dirac’s theory of the electron, propagator techniques. Applications to quantum electrodynamics. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory II
description: Local gauge invariance, Yang-Mills theory: quantum chromodynamics, spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone bosons; the standard electroweak theory; grand unified theories. (Alt. years)

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
description: Nuclear physics; electrodynamics; hadron structure and partons. Techniques of particle physics. (Alt. years)

subject: PACE
title: Research and Peace
description: Introduction to and survey of the interdisciplinary field of peace research, combining theory, methodology, and empirical aspects.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: any 200-level DS course.

subject: PACE
title: Topics in Peace and Conflict Resolution
description: Recent issues, practices in peace and conflict resolution. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Pre: any DS course, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Hiroshima & Peace
description: 10-day intensive course at Hiroshima City University, Japan, in the 2-weeks before the annual August 6 commemoration of the atomic bombing. Home-stay with Japanese family. Sophomore standing. A-F only.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing. Pre: any 200 level social science course, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Practicum and Internship
description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses. (Cross-listed as PUBA 495)
prerequisites: Pre: any two other PACE courses or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict. (Cross-listed as PLAN 621)

subject: PACE
title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills. (Cross-listed as PLAN 629)
prerequisites: Graduate standing only. Pre: one of the following courses with a minimum grade of B: 429, 447, 477, 647, 652, or 668; or PLAN 627; or COMG 455 or SOC 730; or LAW 508; or MGT 660.

subject: PACE
title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region. (Cross-listed as LAW 547 and WGSS 647)

subject: PACE
title: Seminar: Social Studies
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field. Repeatable two times. (Cross-listed as EDCS 640K)

subject: PACE
title: Mediation: Theory and Practice
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and mediation simulations. Theory of ADR field. Theory of major different models of mediation, both in the U.S. and internationally. Application of mediation process to categories of disputes, family, workplace, and international. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: Pre: graduate standing, or departmental approval.

subject: PACE
title: Dispute Resolution System Design
description: Conflict prevention, management and resolution in the workplace. Design and implementation of effective systems integrating ADR and recent advances in dispute resolution methodology to government, health, nonprofit, educational, private sector and other institutions.
prerequisites: Pre: graduate standing, or departmental approval.

subject: PACE
title: Conflict Management for Educators
description: Conflict resolution theory and practice for administrators, faculty and staff in educational organizations. K-12, community colleges and universities. Application and theory of negotiation, mediation, facilitation and hybrid ADR processes. (Cross-listed as EDEA 652)
prerequisites: Pre: EDEA 601 or EDEA 650, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Family Mediation
description: Theory and skills for practicing divorce and custody mediation. Negotiation and conflict intervention skills used by social workers, lawyers, and other intervenors in family conflict. Focus on Hawai‘i’s divorce and custody laws and practices. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: PACE
title: Collaboration Between Sectors
description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems. (Cross-listed as PLAN 661)

subject: PACE
title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as PLAN 668)
prerequisites: Graduate students only or departmental approval.

subject: PACE
title: Topics: Conflict Theory
description: Recent issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory. Repeatable up to 12 credits. A-F only.

subject: PACE
title: Conflict Resolution Practicum
description: Practice in conflict resolution skills. Open to candidates for Certificate in Conflict Resolution. Repeatable one time or up to three credits. A-F only.

subject: PACE
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable up to 9 credits. A-F only.

subject: PACE
title: Advanced Topics: Conflict Theory
description: Advanced seminar covering issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory. Repeatable one time.

subject: PED
title: Pediatric Seminars
description: Interactive weekly lecture/seminar designed to teach topics in pediatrics and supplemented by small group 2-hour encounters with faculty clinicians in pediatric emergency medicine, inpatient pediatric, and enonatology to gain exposure in pediatric hospital care. Repeatable one time. Medical students only. CR/NC only.

subject: PED
title: Pediatric Shadowing Encounters
description: Clinical Shadowing – Students are paired with Pediatric Subspecialists in chosen area(s) for 8-10 half days. Required: Log book file describing one concept that the student learned during each of the sessions. CR/ NC only. Field experience.

subject: PED
title: Introduction to Research Methodology, Biostatistics, and Epidemiology
description: Interactive seminar series to cover the following topics: data types, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, selecting a statistical test, data distributions, measures of data spread, statistical test assumptions, standard deviation vs. standard error, etc. Repeatable one time. Medical students only. CR/NC only.

subject: PED
title: Pediatrics Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, covering evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of childhood diseases. Emphasis on primary prevention, normal growth and development of the neonate to adolescent, and arrangement of pediatric care, including outpatient, inpatient, and emergency room experiences. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses. Co-requisite: MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, and SURG 532.

subject: PED
title: (Alpha) Electives in Pediatrics
description: Fourth-year elective in pediatric sub-specialty areas in which medical students may receive clinical experiences and an in-depth study of selected sub-specialty areas within the field of pediatrics. (B) adolescent medicine; (C) ambulatory pediatric care; (E) clinical genetics; (F) Sub-Internship in neonatology; (G) pediatric cardiology; (H) Sub-Internship in pediatric emergency medicine; (I) Sub-Internship in pediatric hematology/ oncology; (J) Sub-Internship in infectious diseases; (K) Sub-Internship in pediatrics–general ward in pediatrics; (M) extramural electives in pediatrics; (N) pediatric rheumatology; (P) developmental behavioral pediatrics; (Q) pediatric international preceptorship (3 cr.); (R) Sub-Internship in pediatric critical care;. (S) pediatric radiology; (T) pediatric ultrasound; (U) pediatric nephrology; (V) pediatric sports medicine. CR/NC only. Repeatable two times per alpha, up to 36 credits; not repeatable for (Q).
prerequisites: Fourth-year medical student standing. Pre: 531 or 532.

subject: PED
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: PHRM
title: Introduction to General Pharmacology
description: Drugs discussed with emphasis on sites and mechanism of action, toxicity, fate, and uses of major therapeutic agents.
prerequisites: Pre: mammalian physiology and dental hygiene major.

subject: PHRM
title: General Pharmacology
description: Similar to 201 but wider in scope of drugs discussed. Intended for undergraduates in the health sciences and related fields.

subject: PHRM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Directed reading and research in experimental pharmacology. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PHRM
title: Selected Topics in Pharmacology
description: Elective for medical students in Pharmacology. Repeatable up to 12 credits. CR/NC only.

subject: PHRM
title: Principles of Pharmacology
description: Pharmacology elective course for medical students. MD students only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: MD students only. Pre: MDED 554 or consent.

subject: PHRM
title: Research in Pharmacology
description: Pharmacology research elective for medical students. MD majors only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: MD majors only. Pre: MDED 551 or consent.

subject: PHRM
title: General Pharmacology
description: Pharmacodynamics, receptor theory, modeling, clinical trials and the FDA will be covered. Concepts in ADME/T and clinical research are also considered.

subject: PHRM
title: Systemic Pharmacology
description: Provides instruction at an organ systems/functional level covering major organ and functional systems of the human body. Concepts in pharmacological research at the animal, organ system and whole human level will also be considered. Repeatable one time.

subject: PHRM
title: Neuropharmacology
description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CMB 640)
prerequisites: Pre: CMB 606, or consent from the course director.

subject: PHRM
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MDED
title: Clinical Skills Assessment
description: Required comprehensive interdepartment multidisciplinary assessment program for fourth-year medical students. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532.

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Senior Interdisciplinary Electives
description: Fourth-year elective in which students study selected interdisciplinary topics. CR/NC only. (B) medical education elective; (C) complementary and alternative medicine; (D) leadership in underserved care; (E) Junior PBL course director. MED majors only for (D). CR/NC only for (D) and (E). (Spring only for (D) and (E))
prerequisites: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532.

subject: MDED
title: MD 1 Health and Illness
description: Introduction to concepts of health and disease through lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 1 health care problems in tutorials. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 1 Health and Illness Tutorials
description: Introductory series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on concepts of health and disease through MD 1 health care problems. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 2 CV/Pulmonary
description: Concepts focusing on cardiovascular and pulmonary systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 2 health care problems in tutorials. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 2 CV/Pulmonary Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on cardiovascular and pulmonary health care problems. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 3 Renal/Hematology
description: Concepts focusing on renal and hematologic systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 3 health care problems in tutorials. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 3 Renal/Hematology Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on renal and hematology health care problems. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 4 GI/Endocrine
description: Concepts focusing on gastrointestinal and endocrine systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 4 health care problems in tutorials. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 4 GI/Endocrine Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on gastrointestinal and endocrine health care problems. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 6 Locomotor System, Nervous System and Behavioral Problems
description: Concepts focusing on the locomotor/neurological systems and behavioral problems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 6 health care problems in tutorials. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 6 Locomotor System, Nervous System, and Behavioral Problems
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for second-year medical students focusing on neurological/ locomotor systems and behavioral health care problems. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 7 The Life Cycle
description: Concepts focusing on the life cycle through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 7 health care problems in tutorials. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: MD 7 The Life Cycle Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for second-year medical students focusing on the life cycle health care problems. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: Third Year Colloquia
description: A series of lecture-discussions intended to broaden the perspectives of the Unit VI experiences and healthcare problems. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Senior Seminars
description: Review of topics and issues that will prepare senior students for the end of their undergraduate training and the start of their internship. (B) Week 1; (C) Week 2; (D) Week 3. CR/ NC only. (Fall only for B); (Spring only for C and D)

subject: MDED
title: Introduction to Clinical Skills
description: Introductory lectures and laboratories on history taking and physical exam skills. Repeatable one time. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: Unit 2 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 2. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: Unit 3 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 3. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
