subject: MDED
title: Unit 7 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 7. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: Unit 1 Community Health
description: Field experience placing students in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients. Repeatable two times. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: Unit 2 Community Health
description: Field experience placing students in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients. Repeatable two times. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: Unit 3 Community Health
description: Field experience placing student in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: Unit 4 Community Health
description: Field experience placing student in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Preclinical Electives
description: Elective for first and second year medical students. (B) projects in medical education; (C) healer’s art; (D) introduction to student research; (E) health and wellness; (F) quality improvement; (G) introduction to ultrasound. Repeatable one time, up to two credits. MD majors only for (G). CR/NC only.

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Topics in Medical Education
description: Summer selectives in medical education for second-year medical students. (B) rural health preceptorship; (C) health issues of the Pacific Basin; (D) projects in medical education; (E) manikin simulations; (F) learning resources; (G) cardiovascular case maps; (H) pulmonary case maps; (I) clinical skills preceptors; (J) global health perspectives. Repeatable up to four credits. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: MDED
title: Research in Medical Education
description: An elective for medical students to work on research projects related to improving medical education, student wellness, and community health under the direction of a faculty member in the Office of Medical Education. Repeatable nine times, up to six credits.

subject: MDHX
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MEDT
title: Introduction to Medical Technology
description: Designed to acquaint students to the field of medical technology (clinical laboratory science). Repeatable one time.

subject: MEDT
title: Introduction to Medical Technology II
description: Basic principles and lab skills in medical technology (medical lab science). Required for second bachelor’s degree students (not MLT credentialed) wishing to major in medical technology. Second bachelor’s degree students only. A-F only.

subject: MEDT
title: The Clinical Laboratory
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Theory and clinical application of medical laboratory methods and healthcare professional relationships. MEDT majors only. Repeatable one time.

subject: MEDT
title: The Clinical Laboratory II
description: Theory and clinical application of medical technology methods and healthcare professional relationships. Companion course to MEDT 301; and required, for second bachelor’s degree students who were admitted to MEDT major. MEDT majors only. Second Bachelor’s degree standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Lab Management
description: Student will become familiar with fundamental administration of a clinical laboratory to include technical, personnel, and financial management areas. Repeatable one time. MEDT majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Parasitology
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Modern diagnostic practices in parasitology. Repeatable one time.

subject: MEDT
title: Hematology
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Fundame

subject: NREM
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors. (Cross-listed as PEPS 210 and SUST 210)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 220)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans. (Cross-listed as SUST 251 and TPSS 251)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Internship Preparation
description: Exploration of internship and career opportunities for NREM majors. Development of career-building skills, including resume, interview, and professional networking. NREM majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resources Management
description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 311)
prerequisites: Pre: (NREM/TPSS 251 or 210; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resources Management Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory and field methods covering biological and physical principles and concepts in natural resource management. Emphasis on basic field measurement techniques, computer skills commonly used in managing natural resources and writing scientific lab reports. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawai‘i state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 312)
prerequisites: Pre: NREM/PEPS/SUST 210 or NREM/SOCS/TPSS 251 or (BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or (ERTH 101 or higher); and 220/SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Fundamentals of Soil Science
description: Origin, development, properties, management of tropical soils; classification of Hawaiian soils. A-F only. Minimum prerequisite grade of C or consent. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as TPSS 304)
prerequisites: Pre: (CHEM 161 and 161L) with a minimum grade of C, or consent. Co-requisite: 304L.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Fundamentals of Soil Science Laboratory
description: Field and analytical methods for exploring the origin, development, properties, and management of soils, with an emphasis on tropical and Hawaiian soils. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as TPSS 304L)
prerequisites: Pre: (CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L) with a minimum grade of C. Co-requisite: 304.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Environmental Ethics
description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making. A-F only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as SUST 316)
prerequisites: Pre: 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Statistics in Agriculture and Human Resources
description: Theory, applications, and presentation of statistical reasoning. Descriptive, probability, and inferential reasoning for one-variable analysis with extensions to multiple variable cases. A-F only.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Current Topics in Plant Science
description: An undergraduate seminar that provides the presentation and discussion of topics of current relevance to students preparing for careers in applied plant sciences. Oral focus designation. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TPSS 311)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Managerial Accounting
description: Principles and methods of agricultural accounting. Preparing and interpreting financial statements. Sources and costs of credit, capital budgeting, tax management, estate planning. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TPSS 341)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Enterprise Management
description: Introduction of practical concepts and methods used in business management. Introduce broad range of business strategies. Understand the critical role each strategy plays. Facilitate student’s practice of analytical and critical thinking through case studies. (Cross-listed as TPSS 351)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies. (Cross-listed as SUST 358)
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Tropical Forestry/Agroforestry
description: Biophysical and socioeconomic description and analysis of major tropical forestry and agroforestry management systems, including Hawai‘i and the Pacific Basin. The role of traditional land use, pressures from regional and global development, and efforts to create sustainable, diverse systems for rural communities will be discussed. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: Pre: CHEM 151 or higher and BIOL 171 or higher.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Directed Study
description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students qualified to carry on advanced study.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management. Repeatable one time. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 411)
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 171. Junior standing or higher.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Community and Natural Resource Management
description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management. Pre: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as SUST 420)
prerequisites: Pre: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ECON 429)
prerequisites: Pre: NREM/SUST 220 or ECON 130, and 310 or ECON 321; or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawai‘i. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as SUST 451)
prerequisites: Pre: BIOL 172 (with a minimum grade of C-)or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies. (Cross-listed as HWST 458 and SUST 456)
prerequisites: Pre: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/ SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Sustainable Nutrient Management in Agroecosystems
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Biological, chemical, and physical processes governing the cycling of nutrients in agroecosystems, crop and livestock production, and the effects on surrounding unmanaged ecosystems. (Cross-listed as TPSS 450)
prerequisites: Pre: (TPSS 304 and CHEM 161) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Soil and Water Conservation
description: Past and present issues in soil and water conservation will be examined. Principles of erosion, conservation tillage, irrigation, and drainage will be discussed. Land-based threats to coastal zones and watershed management will also be covered.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Irrigation and Water Management
description: Basic soil-water-plant relationships, irrigation water requirements, irrigation efficiencies, different methods of irrigation, planning, design and management of an irrigation system, fertigation and impact of irrigation on soil and water quality. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as TPSS 463)
prerequisites: Pre: 203 (or equivalent) and NREM/TPSS 304 (or equivalent), or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resources Conservation Planning
description: Combined lecture and hands-on field course on theory and practice of natural resource conservation planning. Includes individual and group projects. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Pre: undergraduate junior or senior or graduate standing. Recommended: at least one upper division course in soils, natural resources, planning, physical geography, or related area; or consent.
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: NREM
title: Plant Nutrient Diagnosis in the Tropics
description: Desi
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management

subject: LING
title: Language Acquisition and Language Revitalization
description: Provides training relevant to the study and revitalization of heritage languages and endangered languages.

subject: LING
title: Data Science for Linguistic Research
description: Introduction to data science for linguistic research. Repeatable one time.

subject: LING
title: Practical Exercises in Data Science for Linguistic Research
description: Exercises in data science for linguistic research. Repeatable one time.

subject: LING
title: Phonology
description: Phonological theory and problems of analysis. (Fall only)

subject: LING
title: Grammar
description: Grammatical theory and problems of analysis.

subject: LING
title: Semantics and Pragmatics
description: Ways in which the interpretation of sentences in natural language depends upon the literal meaning of propositions and their logical (semantic) and conversational (pragmatic) inferences.

subject: LING
title: Discourse and Grammar
description: Usage-based examination of grammar in the context of spontaneous spoken language, including the role of discourse on synchronic and diachronic grammatical structure, discourse in interaction, and discourse in language documentation.

subject: LING
title: Field Methods
description: Work with native speakers of lesser-known languages to develop techniques for data collection and analysis. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: 421 and 422 and one of 621 or 622; or consent

subject: LING
title: Language Data Processing
description: Preparation of language data for computer processing; use ready-made programs; write simple language processing programs using SNOBOL4. Applications to student’s research.

subject: LING
title: Laboratory and Quantitative Research Methods
description: Laboratory and quantitative methods for research on language. Introduction to hardware, software, research designs, and basic analysis techniques commonly used in quantitative language research. Combines lecture, laboratory work ,and discussion.

subject: LING
title: Linguistics of Sign Languages
description: Universals and uniqueness in the phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures of sign languages, taught inductively with emphasis on hands-on analysis. Opportunities exist for skills development in American or Ho Chi Minh City sign languages. Graduate students only.

subject: LING
title: Hawai‘i Sign Language Linguistics: Documentation, Conservation, and Revitalization of HSL
description: Descriptive information on the phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures and lexicon of Hawai‘i Sign Language (HSL); language skills development in HSL; and guided research related to the documentation, conservation, and revitalization of HSL. Graduate students only.

subject: LING
title: Topics in Linguistics
description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc. Repeatable unlimited times. (E) English linguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (H) history of the discipline; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

subject: LING
title: Professionalism in Linguistics
description: Topics related to career development and professional/scholarly communication in linguistics, including CVs, abstracts, grant proposals, publications, conference planning. Topics vary by instructor. Repeatable two times.

subject: LING
title: The Comparative Method
description: Introduction to historical-comparative linguistics; attention to both Indo-European and languages with few or no written records.

subject: LING
title: Issues in Historical Linguistics
description: Continuation of 645. Addresses advanced topics in historical linguistics that have generated controversy rather than consensus. Repeatable two times.

subject: LING
title: Developmental Linguistics
description: Survey of the literature in language acquisition; emphasis on relation to linguistic theory.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Language Documentation
description: Covers history, method, and theory behind language documentation, and the role of language endangerment in the field. Discussion on skills required to undertake documentation; topics may vary depending on the emphases of the instructor.

subject: LING
title: Directed Research
description: CR/NC only. Repeatable unlimited times. Maximum six credit hours.

subject: LING
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable up to 12 credit hours.

subject: LING
title: Techniques of Language Documentation
description: Students learn to conduct best practice digital language documentation projects, from equipment purchase to data collection to data annotation to archiving and presentation.

subject: LING
title: Language Typology
description: Language typology deals with how and why the elements of language interact and function. Students acquire a broad overview of this grammatical make-up of languages in general and understanding of FunctionalTypological linguistics. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)

subject: LING
title: Advanced Laboratory Research
description: Advanced laboratory methods for research in linguistics. Specialized and/or advanced uses of hardware, software, research designs, and analysis techniques. Specific topic varies: check with department. Combines lecture, laboratory work and discussion. Repeatable four times.

subject: LING
title: Seminar
description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: LING
title: Areal Linguistics
description: Structures of languages of various areas of the world; diffusion. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: LING
title: Apprenticeship in Teaching Linguistics
description: Experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: admission to doctoral program and consent

subject: LING
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MGT
title: Fundamentals of Entrepreneurship
description: Covers the role of new ventures and entrepreneurship in the world economy, the formation, funding, marketing, structure and implementation of business ventures.

subject: MGT
title: Behavior in Organizations
description: DS Contributions made by sociology, psychology, and related behavioral sciences to the understanding and prediction of human behavior in organizations.

subject: MGT
title: Multinational Business Management
description: Introduction to the unique problems and challenges in managing multinational business enterprises. Systems approach to the management process in such multinational firms stressed.

subject: MGT
title: Comparative Management Systems: United States and Japan
description: Similarities and differences in managers, in process of management, and in relevant environmental constraints in Japan and the U.S.

subject: MGT
title: Seminar in Management
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration. May be repeated with change in topic.

subject: MGT
title: Entrepreneurial Ventures
description: Integrative course in entrepreneurship designed around the development of an original business concept and the completion of a comprehensive business plan for a new venture. Intended as final course for students completing entrepreneurship minor.

subject: MGT
title: History of American Business
description: DH The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development. (Cross-listed as HIST 378)

subject: MGT
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: MGT
title: Family Business
description: The exploration of business, personal, and interpersonal issues associated with a family owned and managed company. Topics include: family psychology and organizational structure, life cycles in family business, strategic family and business planning, succession planning, family business conflict resolution, estate planning, the role of professional managers, and others. This is not a course about how to become an entrepreneur or how to start or manage a business. It is most appropriate for those students who are part of a family that owns and manages a business.
prerequisites: BUS 315 or graduate status, or consent

subject: MGT
title: Asia Pacific Business Systems
description: Business systems in Asia Pacific countries including Japan, Korea, China, Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong in terms of particular organization strategies and how they relate to the industrial trade policies.
prerequisites: BBA core excluding BUS 345, or consent

subject: MGT
title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
description: Exploration of the nature and role of entrepreneurship behavior inside larger, established organizations. An examination of obstacles to entrepreneurial activity and approaches to creating work environments that foster entrepreneurship.

subject: MGT
title: Advanced Organizational Behavior
description: (B) ex

subject: PH
title: Promoting Physical Activity
description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as KRS 695)

subject: PH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PH
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PH
title: Health Communication
description: Skills-oriented course introduces the basic structure of health communication strategies in different settings, selected elements of communication theory, the development of health communication material, and a practical training in motivational counseling skills.

subject: PH
title: Health Promotion Research
description: Focus on research methods commonly used in health promotion. Topics will include randomized trials, quasi-experimental design, sampling, measurement, and correlational studies. Labwork will focus on the use of SPSS to analyze data for applied research problems. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Community-Based Participatory Research
description: Explores ways academic and lay communities collaborate on research, key theoretical perspectives in the development of CBPR, and the challenges in implementing CBPR approaches. Format includes lectures, discussions, readings, writing assignments, and a fieldwork project. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Systematic Literature Review in Public Health
description: Imparts skills in conducting a systematic review of the literature. Students provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work. Intended for doctoral students to complete their qualifying paper. Repeatable one time. PH majors only; doctoral students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: consent or PhD in PH or EPID only.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Applied Research Methods
description: Qualitative research methods design, implementation, and analysis with special focus on methodological, ontological, and ethical issues unique to conducting research with Indigenous communities. PH majors only. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Survey Methods for Indigenous People
description: Advanced application of health disparities research methodologies to address health and social injustices faced by Indigenous people. Grounded in survey design, implementation, and analyses through a public health and Indigenous lens. PH majors only or consent. Graduate students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: PH majors only or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Qualitative Research for Public Health Sciences
description: Provides a basic understanding of qualitative research approaches, methodologies, and techniques and for public health research and practice (needs assessment, program development, and evaluation strategies). Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Statistical Methods in Epidemiological Research
description: Multiple variable statistical methods currently used in chronic disease epidemiology. Logistic regression, conditional logistic regression, proportional hazards regression modelling, generalized estimating equation-based methods, delta method approximations, exact tests.

subject: PH
title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology
description: Will cover selected topics in chronic diseases with critical analysis of the current epidemiologic literature. Methodologic issues, contemporary findings and recommendations for future research will be discussed. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies. A-F only. (Cross-listed as FSHN 749)

subject: PH
title: Health Behavior Change
description: Provide an understanding of the relationship between health behaviors and outcomes including psychological, physiological, and quality of life aspects. It will also focus on the major theories of behavior and behavior change. Emphasis will be placed on understanding concepts, principles, explanations, and how these are translated into practical interventions for adoption and maintaining behavior change. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Social Epidemiology
description: Examine the epidemiologic study of the social distribution and social determinants of states of health, including the identification of social-environmental exposures and their relation to physical and mental health outcomes. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
description: Covers modern methods for longitudinal data analysis. Topics include random effects and growth curve models, generalized linear models for longitudinal data including generalized estimating equations, and generalized linear mixed models. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Survival Analysis
description: Construction and interpretation of various types of life tables, treatment of censored data, proportional hazards, relative risk regression models, and parametric survival analysis.

subject: PH
title: Neuroepidemiology
description: Lecture/discussion providing an overview of the epidemiology of neurological and neurodegenerative diseases and their risk factors, and methodological considerations for the study of these diseases. (Fall only)

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health. Repeatable unlimited times. (Cross-listed as TRMD 690)

subject: PH
title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health. Repeatable unlimited times. (Cross-listed as TRMD 705)

subject: PH
title: Evolution, Epidemiology, and Public Health
description: Will explore several aspects of human health through the perspective of how natural selection and evolution influence disease risk, with the aim of improving treatment and prevention. Graduate students only. A-F only.
prerequisites: PH 663 (with a minimum grade of B).

subject: PH
title: Health Program Evaluation
description: Examines advanced principles of and frameworks for evaluation. Students integrate utilization-focused evaluation methods to improve service delivery and quality, outcomes and impact to improve community and population health. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Doctoral Seminar in Translational Research
description: Required for students in the PhD PH program. (D) evidence-based public health; (E) health policy and leadership. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Teaching Practicum
description: Provide doctoral students with theoretical and practical teaching and course development experiences under the guidance of a faculty mentor. Students will have a portfolio documenting their accomplishments. Repeatable unlimited times. Graduate standing in PH only. A-F only.
prerequisites: PH 602 and PH 623 and PH 655 and PH 663 and PH 681 and PH 770(Alpha), or departmental approval.

subject: PH
title: Research Practicum
description: Hands-on research experience with a faculty mentor. Meet in small groups to discuss issues related to research in public health. Final project will be submission of a publishable quality paper. Graduate standing in PH only. A-F only.
prerequisites: PH 602 and PH 623 and PH 655 and PH 663 and PH 681 and PH 770(Alpha), or departmental approval.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Proposal and Dissertation Writing
description: Intended for doctoral students to complete and defend their proposals and dissertations. Research and presentation methods will be reviewed, and students will be provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work. Repeatable two times. A-F only.
prerequisites: consent or PhD in PH or EPID only.

subject: PH
title: Environmental Health Lab Methods
description: Hands-on training for laboratory methods used in monitoring and detecting environmental health risk factors; learning and application of immunological-, animal cell culture- and molecular biology-based techniques for studying environmental pathogens and toxic pollutants. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Public Health Sciences
description: Topics related to recent developments in major areas; student and faculty research activities. Sections: (1) biostatistics; (2) environmental health; (3) epidemiology; (4) public health nutrition. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PH
title: Integrative Seminar
description: Integrative seminar in public health required as part of the student capstone experience to bring together key aspects of their courses, competencies, and practicum. A-F only.
prerequisites: completed PH field practicum and consent.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Public Health Practice
description: Observation, study, and supervised practical work in student’s area of specialization. A-F only.
prerequisites: public health degree candidate and completion of 15 PH credit hours and consent.

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Current Issues and Topics in Public Health
description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health. Repeatable unlimited times. PH majors only for (D) and (I).

subject: PH
title: Special Practicum/Project
description: Supervised practical training beyond the required practicum in an area of particular interest. Provides additional opportunity to synthesize, integrate, and apply practical skills and knowledge in a public health work environment. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Mathematics for Engineers
description: Applications of ordinary differential equations, Laplace transform, vector field theory, matrices, line integrals.

subject: ME
title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Basic computational fluid dynamics; four important partial differential equations; introduction to finite element method: Interpolation and Galerkin method; finite element method for transport phenomena; some algorithms for parallel computing. A-F only.
prerequisites: 422 (or concurrent ), and either 360, MATH 407 or PHYS 305; or consent.

subject: ME
title: Orbital Mechanics
description: Basic theory of orbits of space objects, including spacecraft, small satellites, planets and small planets, and other fundamentals of astrodynamics and applications to aerospace engineering. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.
prerequisites: grade of C or better in all of the following: 271; 375; MATH 244 or MATH 253A; MATH 302 or MATH 307; ECE 160 or ICS 111.

subject: ME
title: Optimal Control for Aerospace Applications
description: Fundamentals of optimal control theory and calculus of variations. Application of this theory to aerospace engineering problems, including mission design problems and a wide range of space maneuvers. A-F only. Junior standing or higher.
prerequisites: grade of C or better in all of the following: 271; 375; MATH 244 or MATH 253A; MATH 302 or MATH 307; ECE 160 or ICS 111.

subject: ME
title: Applied Thermodynamics
description: DP Gas mixtures, generalized thermodynamic relationships, combustion and thermochemistry, chemical equilibrium, power and refrigeration cycles.
prerequisites: grade of C or better in 311.

subject: ME
title: Applied Thermal Engineering
description: DP Principles, design and analysis of practical thermal systems. Engineering applications. Valve, compressor, condenser and evaporator technologies. System integration and control. Thermal loads and thermal comfort. (Fall only)

subject: ME
title: Power and Propulsion
description: DP Principles, performance, and design of gas turbine power plants and propulsion systems.

subject: ME
title: Astronautics
description: The space environment (vacuum, neutral, radiation, and plasma); motion in gravitational fields; orbit transfers; Earth-satellite operations; rocketry; propulsion analysis and performance; reentry dynamics; interplanetary trajectories; attitude dynamics and stabilization. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Heat Transfer and Lab
description: DP (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Steady and unsteady conduction; steady convection and radiation; heat exchangers. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ME
title: Mass Transfer
description: DP Elementary mass diffusion; diffusion in a stationary medium; diffusion in a moving medium; low and high mass transfer theories; simultaneous heat and mass transfer; condensation, evaporation, and boiling; transpiration cooling; species boundary layers; engineering and design of heat and mass exchangers; current refrigerants and environmental regulations. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Gas Dynamics
description: DP One-dimensional compressible flow involving change of area, friction, heat transfer. Normal and oblique shocks. Prandtl-Meyer flow. Application to nozzles, diffusers, airfoils.

subject: ME
title: Thermal Management of Electronic Systems
description: To introduce concepts in the thermal management of electronics, and to develop sound technical tools to approach modern electronic packaging and cooling applications. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Scaling Methods in Engineering
description: Scaling methods and optimization under global constraints; multi-scale optimal design of mechanical, thermal, and natural systems; effectiveness of heat, fluid, and convective trees; theoretical design optimization of manmade and natural power systems; analysis of time dependent structures. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Solar Thermal Engineering
description: Fundamentals of solar energy, solar engineering material characteristics, and solar thermal and photovoltaic systems. Will learn solar thermal system components, and be able to perform simple system design. A-F only. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Failures in Materials
description: DP Analysis of component failures due to imperfections, fatigue, brittle fracture, wear, corrosion, bending, impact, and overload. Fracture mechanics. Case studies.

subject: ME
title: Materials Selection for Design
description: DP Methodology for the selection of materials for mechanical applications to prevent mechanical failure and environmental degradation. Design considerations associated with the use of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.

subject: ME
title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods—theory and hands-on experience. (Cross-listed as CHEM 435)

subject: ME
title: Corrosion Engineering
description: DP Basics of corrosion processes and emphasis on corrosion control. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosion, metal alloys and their behavior, corrosion control techniques (cathodic protection, anodic protection, coatings, and inhibitors).

subject: ME
title: Mechatronics
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Modern mechatronics components and design principles; functionality of products, processes and systems; electrical circuits and mechanical components; programming and control; hands on technology; application case studies. ME, ECE, CE, ICS majors only. (Fall only)

subject: ME
title: Advanced Materials Manufacturing
description: DP (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Introduction to anisotropic materials, advanced manufacturing techniques for composite and intelligent materials, joining of composites, thin film processing and stereolithography, computer aided manufacturing and rapid prototyping, manufacturing process optimization, open-ended manufacturing projects. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Nanotechnology
description: DP (3 Lec) Tools and techniques of micro- and nanotechnology in design, modeling, simulations, analysis, fabrication, testing and characterization; nano-materials, nano-structures, nano-composites, nano-coating, nano-optics, nano-electronics and nano-biotechnology. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Nanosystem and Microsystem Design
description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale. Microfabrication/nanofabrication, fabrication process design, electrostatistic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, measurements. Course work will focus on process and system design. ENGR majors only.
prerequisites: 331 (with a minimum grade of C-), 375 (with a minimum grade of C-), or consent.

subject: ME
title: Research Methods in Engineering
description: Introduces the basic skills of preparing and publishing scientific research. Students will learn how to prepare, write, publish, and present a scientific paper, while working on a research project related to thermofluids. A-F only. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Feedback-Control Systems
description: DP Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

subject: ME
title: Robotics
description: DP Principles and design methods for autonomous systems.

subject: ME
title: Energy Conversion Systems
description: DP Energy conversion and its impact on the environment. Conventional, hydroelectric, nuclear fission and fusion, solar, wind, ocean, geothermal, and biomass power; energy storage, transmission and conservation.

subject: ME
title: Nuclear Power Engineering
description: DP Nuclear reactor principles. Reactor heat transfer, heat generation and removal. Design and analysis of reactor power systems and plants.

subject: ME
title: Flow Visualization and Measurement
description: Overview of flow visualization and measurement techniques including high speed photography of wakes, jets, shear layer, particle motion. Experimental design, statistics, image processing and data analysis. Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: ME
title: Materials for Solar Energy Conversion
description: Atom structure, electromagnetic waves and energy, electronic and energetic properties of semi-conducting materials, junctions, solar cells operations, bulk and thin film materials synthesis, integration of solar cells into the electric grid. ECE and ME majors only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: (331 or ECE 324) with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: ME
title: Electrochemical Power Sources: Principles, Applications, and Sustainability
description: Electrochemistry, batteries, fuel cells, flow batteries, electrochemical capacitors, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage. ENGR majors only. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: 331, CHEM 162, CHEM 171, or CHEM 181A (with a grade of C- or better).

subject: ME
title: Experimental Stress Analysis
description: (1-3 hr Lab) Techniques of experimental stress analysis.

subject: NURS
title: Family Systems in Health and Illness
description: Family systems approach to include selected family theories, family research and family centered culturally sensitive clinical assessment and intervention in health and illness situations.

subject: NURS
title: Complementary and Traditional Care
description: A review of theoretical systems and approaches to complementary and traditional care in culturally diverse populations with a focus on wellness. Appropriate for all health-care professionals.

subject: NURS
title: Tests and Measurement in Nursing Education
description: Testing and evaluation applied to nursing education. (Once a year)

subject: NURS
title: (Alpha) Selected Topics in Nursing
description: Advanced study, exploration of special topics in clinical nursing. (D) developmentally disabled children and their families; (I) current issues in professional nursing.
prerequisites: NURS majors only or consent for (D).

subject: NURS
title: Human Resource Management in Healthcare Agencies
description: Analyze and critically evaluate basic issues, policies and trends in human resource management as it applies to health care agencies.

subject: NURS
title: Leadership, Role, Identity and Organizational/System Change
description: Seminar focused on theoretical and conceptual models of leadership and management as applied to relevant advanced nurses’ roles, their respective populations, and changing healthcare environments.

subject: NURS
title: Analysis of Healthcare Delivery Models
description: Analysis of various clinical management concepts and health-care delivery systems influencing outcomes, process, and costs in the delivery of care.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar and Practicum in Nursing Executive Leadership
description: Supervised practicum to build mid to senior level nursing leadership competencies and facilitate change in complex healthcare organizations.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 663 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Economics and Finance
description: Economic and financial concepts and tools for use in developing and managing patient care processes.

subject: NURS
title: Community Based Participatory Research (CBPR) for Advanced Practice Nurses
description: Online course focuses on use of CBPR methods by Advanced Practice Nurses to address population level issues amendable to nursing interventions; 15 hours of didactic and 90 hours of field experience are included. (Once a year)

subject: NURS
title: Evaluating Research for Evidencebased Practice
description: Introduces evidence-based practice methods for improving the quality of nursing practice. Develops skills in differentiating quantitative and qualitative research, statistical methods, and searching, critiquing, and synthesizing literature, pertinent to health care issues. (Fall only)

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Nursing During Public Health Disasters
description: The role of the advanced professional nurse in public health preparedness, planning and response. Includes 45 hours of field work where the student will practice emergency response functional roles. (Summer only)

subject: NURS
title: Biostatistics: Application in the Advanced Nursing Practice Setting
description: Includes basic bio-statistical techniques and the application of statistical findings to practice programmatic decisions. (Once a year)
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: graduate standing in the Department of Nursing or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Population Health Nursing Practicum
description: Student will conduct a complex service project for a public or community based agency. May be taken for 1-6 credits. (45 hours of practicum experience awarded for each one credit of the course) Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 24 credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing or consent.
degrees: MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Implementation and Evaluation Strategies for Evidence-Based Practice
description: Using knowledge of translational science, designs an implementation plan for a practice guideline. Determines evaluation methods and selects outcome variables that best measure success. Discusses institutionalization of, and identifies facilitators and barriers to, practice change. (Spring only)
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Graduate standing only. Pre: 669.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Clinical
description: Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: NURS majors only or consent. Pre: 612/612L, 613, and 629 (or concurrent)

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care I Seminar: Health Assessment
description: Seminar to discuss the evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management. Utilization of clinical cases and current literature on health care assessment.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: 612/612L, 613, and 629. Co-requisite: 676L.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care I Lab (beginning level): Health Assessment
description: Beginning level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients for advanced practice nursing students in primary care settings.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care II Seminar: Management of the Adult
description: Intermediate level seminar where students discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care II Lab (intermediate level): Acute & Chronic Conditions (Adult)
description: Intermediate level practicum. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management, and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing focusing on adults with acute or chronic diagnoses in primary care.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care III Seminar: Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
description: Intermediate level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care III Lab (intermediate level): Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
description: Intermediate level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients in a primary care setting for advanced practice nursing students focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women). Repeatable two times.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care IV Seminar: Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
description: Advanced level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management focusing on primary care of clients across the lifespan.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care IV Lab (advanced level): Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
description: Advanced level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients across the lifespan in primary care settings for advanced practice nursing students.

subject: NURS
title: Cultural Competency in Nursing Education
description: Evaluates the impact of history on the culture of nursing and nursing education. Explore strategies to provide education in a culturally sensitive manner to culturally diverse students.
prerequisites: NURS majors only. Pre: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Diagnosis & Management of Complex Care Across the Lifespan
description: Culminating seminar synthesizing and applying concepts from all APRN didactic course work, using case/problem-based learning via student and faculty-guided discussions.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Healing Practices of Populations with Health Disparities in Hawai‘i and Other Places
description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and the prevention of common conditions of disease among populations with health disparities in Hawai‘i and other places; includes didactic and 45 hours of field experience. (Spring only)

subject: NURS
title: Psychobiology of Mental Health Disorders
description: Focuses on the psychological and biological factors that influence mental health and illness among diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Relevant biopsychosocial theories and research findings are applied.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
description: First of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
description: Repeatable one time, up to six credits. Complements NURS 684; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.

subject: MUS
title: Bibliography and Library Resources in Music
description: Basic materials and techniques; includes retrieval techniques from online computer catalog. MUS majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: Regional Music
description: Musical content and historicosocial context of principal musical traditions. (B) Asia; (C) Oceania. Repeatable nine times.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Problems in Ethnomusicology
description: (B) transcription of music performance; (C) movement analysis; (D) other.

subject: MUS
title: Studies in Music Theory
description: (B) stylistic counterpoint to 1700; (C) stylistic counterpoint from 1700; (D) advanced analysis; (E) comparative theory; (F) history of theory; (G) contemporary techniques and resources; (H) atonal analysis and set theory; (I) Schenkerian analysis.

subject: MUS
title: Intercultural Composition
description: Examination of compositional approaches, techniques, and characteristics of works with East Asian influences in Western concert settings. Composing idiomatically for East Asian instruments. Repeatable one time. MUS majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Masters Composition Practicum
description: Original composition in all forms. Masters-level composition students only. Repeatable five times. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed. A maximum of 3 credits may be earned in MUS 695. Graduate standing in music education or music composition. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Directed Work
description: Reading and research in ethnomusicology, musicology, music education; reading and practice in theory, composition, or performance. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: consent of chair and department chair

subject: MUS
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: MUS
title: Topics in Music
description: Advanced topics in musicology; theory, ethnomusicology, and music education. (B) psychology of music; (C) research in music education; (D) research methods in musicology; (E) advanced diction for singers. Repeatable in different alphas. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Seminar for Doctoral Students
description: Selected topics centering on areas pertinent to the student’s degree needs and research interests. Repeatable nine times, up to 12 credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: admission to PhD program in music or consent

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in Music Education
description: Selected problems in music education. (B) childhood; (C) adolescence/adults; (D) major issues. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: MUS
title: Doctoral Composition Practicum
description: Original composition in all forms. Doctoral-level composition students only. Repeatable five times. A-F only.

subject: MUS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD degree and consent of dissertation chair

subject: NSEB
title: National Student Exchange
description: Study at another campus through National Student Exchange (NSE). Transfer credits earned upon successful completion of courses on exchange. Repeatable one time at the same host campus. Unlimited times at different host campuses. CR/NC only. Credits to be granted in transfer upon successful completion of course work at exchange institution.

subject: NHH
title: Applied Health Disparities Research
description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: NHH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable unlimited times. Junior standing or higher.

subject: NHH

description: Introduction to medical science stressing key historical figures and significant events to exemplify the development of scientific methods. Special emphasis on writing skills, health team concept, and culture and contributions of the Pacific. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

subject: NHH
title: Humanities in Medicine II
description: Continuation of 501. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only.

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biology I
description: (2 Lec, 2 Tutorial, 1 3-hr Lab) Foundation in medical sciences, including anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pathology, and pharmacology (focus on respiratory, cardiovascular, and urinary systems); develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Includes lectures, problembased tutorials, and histology and gross anatomy labs. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biology II
description: (2 Lec, 2 Tutorial, 1 3-hr Lab) Continuation of 503. CR/NC only.

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biochemistry I
description: Provide background knowledge of chemistry, biochemistry, and molecular biology with emphasis in principles of biochemical processes as well as clinical correlations to medical conditions; develop critical thinking, standardized test taking skills, and problem-solving skills. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: admission to Imi Ho‘ola Post-Baccalaureate Program

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biochemistry II
description: Continuation of 505. CR/NC only.

subject: NHH

description: Introduction to Native Hawaiian health issues and traditional healing practices. MD majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: NHH

description: Clinical experience in the Native Hawaiian Health Care System and community health care centers, incorporating both western and traditional Hawaiian medicine. Open to fourth year medical students interested in Native Hawaiian Health Care. CR/NC only.

subject: NHH

description: Social justice provides an analytical and prescriptive framework to understand health inequities; understand connections between social forces and health outcomes, and the role of the individual student in improving social justice in the health system. Graduate standing only. CR/NC only. (Spring only)

subject: NHH

description: Provides a focused experience in clinical medicine with opportunities to practice the history and physical examination in Lau Ola, the clinical setting of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health. Repeatable one time. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: NHH
title: Directed Reading/Research in Native Hawaiian Health
description: Instruction of medical students in the social determinants of health, issues of health equity, specifically in Native Hawaiians, Pacific Islanders and/or disadvantaged people and teach them how these issues can be addressed through research. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: NHH
title: Advanced Applied Health Disparities Research
description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research. Repeatable two times, or up to 27 credits.

subject: NHH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable unlimited times. Graduate standing only.

subject: NREM

subject: NREM

description: Introduction to NREM student learning outcomes and scholarly breadth within the department, exposure to on-campus resources, networking with current and former NREM students and external stakeholders, career skills development. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: NREM
title: Environmental Service Learning II
description: Experiential service learning course for students participating in the Hawai‘i Youth Conservation Corps summer program as Hana Hou members. Hawai‘i Youth Conservation Corps summer program students only. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: NREM

description: FQ (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Applications of calculus (limits, continuity, derivatives, exponential and logarithmic functions, partials, integrals) to problems in business management, social sciences, and life sciences. Applies symbolic techniques and quantitative methods in problem solving, utilizes concept of proof as a chain of inferences, and promotes development of reasoning skills and mathematical logic in bridging theory and practice. A-F only.

subject: NREM
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: DB Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors. (Cross-listed as PEPS 210 and SUST 210)

subject: NREM
title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: DS Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchang

subject: MUS

prerequisites: music majors or minors or consent

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Music Education
description: Survey of American education, with an emphasis on music learning, teaching and philosophy, school structure and governance, diversity and multi-cultural education, and professional ethics. Supervised clinical and field experiences required. MUS majors only. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: MUS

description: DA (3 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Musical concepts, philosophy and pedagogy: use of media, singing, movement, and instruments; as well as resources for an active elementary music classroom. A-F only.

subject: MUS

description: DH Students will study how the singing voice works in various styles, including classical, musical theater, jazz, choral, and pop/ rock. Students will learn historical contexts, aural characteristics, and musical vocabulary through lecture, discussion, and listening. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as THEA 259) DA

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music to 1750
description: DH Development of Western music from its origins to 1750. Styles, schools, composers.

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music After 1750
description: DH Development of Western music from 1750 to the present. Styles, schools, composers.

subject: MUS
title: World of Music: Asia/Pacific
description: DH Study of music as social process, sound system, aesthetics, and world view. Emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific and the ways music creates links across the region and among people. (Fall only)
prerequisites: ability to read music and one introductory music course with a minimum grade of C (MUS 108, 114, 121-126, 155-158) or consent

subject: MUS

description: Fundamentals of music theory, notation, sight-singing, and dictation. A-F only.

prerequisites: MUS 280 or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 283 or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Theory II
description: Continuation of 281.
prerequisites: MUS 281 or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 284 or consent.

subject: MUS

description: Perception, identification, and notation of musical sounds through dictation and sight singing.
prerequisites: MUS 280 and ability to sing diatonic melodies at sight, or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 281 or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Aural Training II
description: Continuation of 283.
prerequisites: MUS 283 or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 282 or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Theory III
description: Detailed study of theory: writing, analysis, keyboard application. MUS majors only.

subject: MUS
title: Theory IV
description: Continuation of 285.

subject: MUS
title: Aural Training III
description: Advanced level of perception, identification, and notation of musical sounds through dictation and sight-singing. MUS majors only.

subject: MUS
title: Aural Training IV
description: Continuation of 287.

subject: MUS

description: Original composition; specific approaches to creative writing. Repeatable five times, up to six credits. MUS majors only.

subject: MUS
title: Hula/Chant Ensemble I
description: DA Ancient style. Pre: upper division standing or consent. A-F only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 312)

subject: MUS
title: Diction for Singers
description: Diction and phonetics of English, Italian, liturgical Latin, German, and French for singers and conductors.

subject: MUS

description: Problems in directing instrumental and choral ensembles. Score reading, rehearsal techniques, and basic interpretive problems.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Conducting
description: Continuation of 325.

subject: MUS

description: Individual instruction in instrumental and dance performance at advanced level. (Alpha) (B) koto; (C) shamisen; (E) Hawaiian chant; (F) shakuhachi; (I) other. Repeatable for six semesters. A-F only.

subject: MUS

(Alpha) (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) organ; (E) conducting; (F) recorder; (G) classical guitar; (H) violin; (I) viola; (J) cello; (K) double bass; (M) flute; (N) oboe; (O) clarinet; (P) bassoon; (Q) saxophone; (R) trumpet; (S) French horn; (T) trombone; (U) tuba; (X) euphonium; (Y) percussion; (Z) other. Repeatable for six semesters for all other alphas; repeatable five times, up to 12 credits for (E). Juniors and seniors only for (E). A-F only.
prerequisites: advancement from MUS 231 or consent; any MUS 231 or consent for (E)

subject: MUS

Half recital required to complete junior level. (Alpha) (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) organ; (G) classical guitar; (H) violin; (I) viola; (J) cello; (K) double bass; (M) flute; (N) oboe; (O) clarinet; (P) bassoon; (Q) saxophone; (R) trumpet; (S) French horn; (T) trombone; (U) tuba; (X) euphonium; (Y) percussion; (Z) other. Repeatable for three semesters. A-F only.
prerequisites: four semesters of MUS 232 and promotion by board examination

subject: MUS

subject: MUS

subject: MUS
title: Digital Audio Synthesis and Multimedia Applications
description: Sound control through graphical interfaces. Advanced digital audio synthesis techniques. Audio control of graphics and video. Introduction of alternate controllers. (Once a year)

subject: MUS
title: Western Music and Japan
description: DH Historical survey of Western music in Japan from modernization through the Meiji Restoration up to the present. Topics include: Western-style symphonic music, J-pop, and Enka by Japanese artists; develops written communication skills.

subject: MUS
title: Marching Band Design and Techniques
description: Design and techniques for the modern field marching band. Repeatable one time, up to four credits. (Alt. years)

subject: MUS
title: Integrating World Music in Education
description: Application of musical concepts through an integrated approach. This includes strategies, world music, literature, materials and resources for the classroom curriculum.

subject: MUS

description: Required for K-12 music specialists. Scope and nature of music in the lives of children and adolescents; planning, teaching, learning, and evaluating in elementary, middle, and high school curriculum. A-F only.
prerequisites: MUS 250, MUS 286, and MUS 288, or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 354L.

subject: MUS

prerequisites: MUS 250, MUS 286, and MUS 288; or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 354.

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Music Methods
description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of instrumental music in schools. A-F only.
prerequisites: MUS 250, MUS 286, and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 355L.

subject: MUS

description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in instrumental settings. Supervised 30 hours of field experiences required. CR/NC only. (Every 3rd semester)
prerequisites: MUS 250, MUS 286, and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 355.

subject: MUS
title: Choral Music Methods
description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of choral music in schools. A-F only.
prerequisites: MUS 122B, MUS 250, MUS 286, and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 414.

subject: MUS
title: Choral Music Methods Lab

prerequisites: MUS 250, MUS 286, and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent. Co-requisite: MUS 356.

subject: MUS
title: Piano Pedagogy
description: Concepts, materials, and procedures for class and individual instruction in piano.

subject: MUS

description: Continuation of 358. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

subject: MUS

description: DH Lecture investigating the role of music in narrative film, and developing critical skills through close study of films and their music. Understanding styles and techniques of film music within larger aesthetic trends and historical contexts. (Once a year)

subject: MUS

description: DH Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the recent “Hamilton” phenomenon, and explores their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts. (Cross-listed as THEA 362)

subject: MUS
title: Superstars: A History of Musical Celebrity
description: DH

(Alt. years) (Cross-listed as TPSS 463)

department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

degrees: Natural Resources and Environmental Management MS
Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD
department: Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Management
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

Natural Resources and Environmental Management PhD

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

Frequently, compensatory damages cannot adequately protect clients or provide them with the relief they need. Topics include temporary restraining orders, preliminary and permanent injunctions, restitution and unjust enrichment, specific performance, and equitable defenses such as unclean hands, laches, and estoppel. Practice issues concerning appeal, jury trials, and the relationship of equity to law are also explored. Repeatable unlimited times.
department: William S. Richardson School of Law
college: William S. Richardson School of Law

subject: LAW

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

college: William S. Richardson School of Law

(Once a year)

subject: KRS
