subject: PSY
title: Principles of Learning
description: Survey of the principles of learning, including important discoveries in the development of the study of learning, major theories, and both basic and applied research in contemporary literature.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Psychology
description: In-depth survey of the computational and representational structures and processes of cognition. Special attention devoted to consideration of the relationship between brain, mind, and computation.

subject: PSY
title: Thinking
description: Provides an introduction to higher cognition (thinking and reasoning) and its foundations, particularly as they relate to the larger field of cognitive science. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: PSY
title: Comparative Cognition
description: Survey of the historical and contemporary study of cognition across species, including learning, memory, attention, navigation, reasoning, social interaction, and communication.

subject: PSY
title: Selected Topics in Comparative Psychology
description: Intensive review of comparative, communicative, sensory, or learning mechanisms in animals.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Basic principles of pharmacology as they apply to the brain and specific psychological disorders such as anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorders, schizophrenia, psychosis, memory, and drug use. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: PSY
title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Relation of central and peripheral nervous systems to behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Developmental Foundations
description: Historical, theoretical, and methodological foundations of developmental psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Development
description: Familiarizes students with current research and theory in cognitive development through readings of original journal articles and monographs.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: Theories and research in social cognition and behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Application of psychological theories to cross-cultural phenomena; assessment of cross-cultural processes and social motivations; culture and personality; research evaluation and design.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology and Social Issues
description: Conflict, dissent, community issues, problems; social change and its relation to mental disorder.

subject: PSY
title: Applied Social Psychology
description: Problems in use of social psychology principles in human affairs; multidisciplinary considerations.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology of Love and Sex
description: Seminar in psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of cognitive, emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, mate selection, and antecedents and consequences of intimate relationships. Pre: consent. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: Preparation for becoming a clinical psychologist with emphasis on scientist-practitioner model, professional ethics, diversity and professional development.
prerequisites: Pre: graduate student in psychology or consent of instructor.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Assessment I
description: Psychometric theory; ethics; diversity issues; principles and methods of cognitive-intellectual, neuropsychological, and personality assessment. A-F only.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Assessment II
description: Administration and interpretation of cognitive-intellectual and personality assessment devices. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 670 and 671 or consent and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program.

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Assessment
description: Conceptual and methodological foundations of clinical applications of assessment. PSY majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
prerequisites: Pre: 671 and 672 and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program, or consent.

subject: PSY
title: Treatment Research
description: Idiographic and nomothetic approaches to clinical treatment research methods and findings.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopathology
description: Comprehensive study of the mental disorders across the lifespan. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: PSY
title: Child Practicum
description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of children and adolescents. Repeatable ten times, up to 33 credits.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Practicum
description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of adults. Repeatable ten times, up to 33 credits.

subject: PSY
title: External Practicum
description: This supervision-style class will cover cases and issues related to student’s clinic work, supervision, or educational goals while training in external practicum sites. Repeatable ten times.

subject: PSY
title: Cultural Community Psychology
description: Graduate seminar on cultural considerations and issues in the history, methods, theories, interventions, and professional roles in community psychology. Small class size (up to 10). Open to graduate students.

subject: PSY
title: Practicum: Behavioral Change and Community
description: Supervised experience in educational, mental health, correctional, consulting, or community action agencies.

subject: PSY
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Minimum of six credit hours is required. Repeatable six times up to seven credits.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in History and Theory of Psychology

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Quantitative Psychology
description: Specific and newly emerging topics in statistics, including casual inference, analysis of missing data, and statistical machine learning. Content varies and focuses on advanced topics not covered in other PSY methods and statistics courses. Repeatable two times. PSY majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 610 (with a minimum grade of B) or instructor consent.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychometrics
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Experimental Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Experimental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Physiological Psychology
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Biostatistics
description: Basic biostatistics methods in public health and biomedical research. Topics covered include data collection, data analyses, and interpretation of statistical results. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Epidemiology
description: Students will gain a deeper understanding of the core concepts used in epidemiologic research and practice. Upon completion, students will have the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct an epidemiologic study. A-F only.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: PH 201 and PH 310.

subject: PH
title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
description: Lecture/discussion. Examines a variety of issues associated with the effects of diet on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Junior standing or higher.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: PH 310.

subject: PH
title: Social Behavioral Health I: Health Promotion for Individuals and Groups
description: Focus on the application of social and behavioral theory in health education, and how health promotion programs are constructed for various populations with an emphasis on cultural diversity and social determinants of health. A-F only.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: PH 202 and PSY 100.

subject: PH
title: Social Behavioral Health II: Health Promotion in Communities
description: Introduction to health education and health promotion programming in public health, and to social/behavioral theories used to develop health interventions that affect communities, institutions, and policies. Introduction to common program planning models. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Tobacco & Community Disparities
description: DS Assessing the facilitators and barriers of smoking initiation, cessation, and exposure to second-hand smoke within communities. Use of photovoice and its application to policy and addressing disparities. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Health Policy and Management
description: Examines the role that health policy and management plays in population-based public health practice, including the delivery, quality, and costs of health care and the structure, process, and outcomes of health services delivery. A-F only.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: PH 201 and PH 202.

subject: PH
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well. A-F only. (Cross-listed as COA 435 and SW 435)
prerequisites: Pre: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to One Health
description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health– an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections. A-F only.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: (PH 201, or ANSC 200, or BIOC 141, or BIOL 101, or BIOL 171, or BOT 101, or ERTH 101, or GES 102, or OEST 101, or OCN 102, or ATMO 150, or SOC 180) with a minimum grade of C or better; or consent.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Environmental Microbiology
description: Lecture/discussion. Will define the nature and biological activities of microorganisms in different environments and evaluate the effects of these microbes on human activities and health.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: MICR 130 or MICR 351 or BIOL 171.

subject: PH
title: Social Determinants of Indigenous Peoples’ Health
description: Examines indigenous peoples’ health inequities using social determinants of health framework: considers this approach within the historical, political, cultural, and social context of Indigenous population’s health status to generate solutions. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Application of Public Health Principles in Research and Practice
description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health projects and associated methods while working to develop a written applied learning project literature review. Students will present their findings at a public forum. A-F only.
prerequisites: PH majors only. Junior standing or higher. Pre: PH 203 and PH 310.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Applied Learning Experience
description: Allows students to execute an independent, mentor-supervised, applied learning project as implementation of skills learned in previous public health coursework. Applied project is a required component of the public health undergraduate degree program.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Undergraduate Capstone Seminar
description: Synthesis of public health knowledge, skills, and practice acquired during the public health undergraduate degree. Students also reflect on, finalize, and present written applied learning experience projects at a public form. A-F only.
prerequisites: Senior standing and higher. Pre: completed public health applied learning experience and consent.

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Current Issues and Topics in Public Health
description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health. Each alpha repeatable one time. Open to nonmajors. A-F only.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing and above. Pre: PH 201.

subject: PH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable up to six credits.
prerequisites: PH majors only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Foundations
description: Focus will provide a broad introduction to the field of public health and orientation to overarching issues in the field. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PH
title: U.S. Health Care Services and Policy
description: Overview of the historical, conceptual, ethical and political context for health care delivery in the U.S. Explores current trends, practices and issues in the delivery of health care services in both private and public sector.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Biology
description: Writing-intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as CMB 610)

subject: PH
title: Fundamentals to One Health
description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health– an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Health Promotion Theory and Methods
description: Individual and community health; implications for public health practice, individual and social change processes.

subject: PH
title: Health Economics
description: Integrated concepts in health economics and its application towards health policy issues; market failures in health care; factors affecting U.S. health care spending potential impact on equity/efficiency stemming from changes in health care delivery. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Cultural Competency in Health Care
description: Presents both analytical and practical approaches to cultural competency domains, concepts, models, frameworks, patterns and communication that occur in cross-cultural healthcare situations. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Health Activism
description: Examines how Indigenous Peoples and their allies (individually and collectively) accomplish social change in society. A-F only.
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: consent of instructor.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Health Seminar
description: Examines public health through an Indigenous lens, integrates competencies across all public health disciplines, and will apply them in context of working for and with Indigenous communities to improve health and wellness. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Topics in Health Policy
description: Examines major federal and local policies that impact health and health care delivery in the U.S. and other nations; considers effectiveness of these policy-making institutions for improving population health; covers methods in policy analysis. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Grant Writing in Public Health
description: Lecture/discussion on grant writing with public health focus. Includes basic components of grant proposals, assessing appropriate funding opportunities, data sources/resources for justifying grants, and the funder’s perspective. Student will prepare a brief foundation grant proposal. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Program Planning, Management, Evaluation, and Leadership
description: Foundation to inform, educate, and improve health for individuals, communities, and populations. Knowledge/acquisition of skills through program planning, management, evaluation and leadership that span the social-ecological range from individual-level to population-level programs. A-F only.

subject: PH
title: Needs Assessment
description: Knowledge and skills acquisition in conducting needs assessment in public health practice.

subject: PH
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as TRMD 650)

subject: PH
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
description: Topics such as contemporary issues in global health and population studies, international health programs, demographic methods, global economy and health, human right and humanitarian assistance, social justice, global environmental changes and health.

subject: PH
title: Global Health and Human Security
description: Provides the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to successfully manage health security crises and protect human vulner

subject: POLS
title: Political Alternatives
description: Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics. (Cross-listed as PACE 373)
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent

subject: POLS
title: Teaching Political Science
description: Practicum for majors who serve as undergraduate teaching assistants. Repeatable one time.

subject: POLS
title: Legislative Internship
description: Field placement at the Hawai‘i Legislature integrated with academic study of political institutions and practices. A-F only. Recommended: 390. (Spring only)

subject: POLS
title: Community Internship
description: Field placement integrated with academic study of political institutions and community organizations. Repeatable one time. Recommended: 390.

subject: POLS
title: Senior Thesis
description: Independent research and thesis writing with supervision of senior advisor.

subject: POLS
title: Executive Internship
description: Open to students awarded a Mānoa Undergraduate Political Fellowship for placement in the Governor’s or Lt. Governor’s Office, Prosecuting Attorney’s Office, or Public Defender’s Office. Field placement, integrated with academic study. A-F only. Recommended: 385, 390.

subject: POLS
title: Senior Seminar in Political Science
description: Exploration of themes in political science with emphasis on discussion, research, and substantial writing.
prerequisites: 390 (or concurrent) or senior standing or consent

subject: POLS
title: Mānoa Undergraduate Congressional Fellowship Internship Seminar
description: Hawai‘i Undergraduate Political Internship’s Congressional Fellowship. Award includes stipend and internship experience in a Hawai‘i congressional office. Students review policy processes, House and Senate procedures and produce a final paper. Restricted to fellowship awardees only. Junior and senior standing only. A-F only. Co-requisite: 386.

subject: POLS
title: Scope and Methods of Political Science
description: Main concepts delineating boundaries of discipline; approaches to knowledge employed by political scientists; empirical and normative theory; problems in theory-building; validity and reliability in research design; philosophy of science applied to political science.

subject: POLS
title: Political Analysis and Theory Building
description: Survey of theory-building, approaches and validation techniques.

subject: POLS
title: Research Techniques and Analytic Methods
description: Quantitative models and statistical inference techniques.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Methodology
description: Specific methodological techniques and practices introduced in 601 and 602. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Political Theory and Analysis
description: Major contemporary approaches and styles in political theory, philosophy, and analysis.

subject: POLS
title: Tradition of Political Philosophy
description: Discussion of texts and themes in the Western political tradition from Plato to Nietzsche. Repeatable one time.

subject: POLS
title: Hawaiian Political Thought: Theory and Method/Nā Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i
description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods. (Cross-listed as HAW 612)

subject: POLS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Political Thought
description: Specific traditions and individuals, or particular issues and problems. (C) feminist theory. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. ((C) Cross-listed as WGSS 615)

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Indigenous Politics
description: Historical treatment of the contact between state and indigenous peoples and a survey of contemporary indigenous political initiatives: social movements, media, indigenous studies programs, and events.

subject: POLS
title: Politics of Indigenous Representation
description: Politics of indigenous representations in media, literature, and academic scholarship.

subject: POLS
title: International Relations
description: Analysis of theories: actors, decisions, systems, conflict, integration, alternative approaches to validation. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: International Conflict Resolution
description: Analysis of international conflict and conflict resolution. Theory and practice of negotiation, mediation, conciliation, facilitation, and other “third-party” methods of peaceful settlement. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Teaching Model United Nations
description: Substantive and pedagogical approaches to using Model United Nations simulation for teaching and conflict resolution. Repeatable two times. Graduate students only. (Fall only)

subject: POLS
title: (Alpha) Topics in International Relations
description: (B) international relations and war; (E) international organization; (F) modeling international systems. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Comparative Politics
description: Emphasis on Asia, theories of development, and comparative methods. At least one section a semester.

subject: POLS
title: Indigenous Peoples and Western Imperialism
description: Historical examination of U.S. and European imperialisms, including national narratives, politics, and impacts upon indigenous peoples in the Americas, Pacific, and Asia. Repeatable one time.

subject: POLS
title: (Alpha) Politics and Development: Regional
description: Politics of particular regions; particular development processes. (C) China. ((C) cross-listed as ASAN 608 and PLAN 608)

subject: POLS
title: (Alpha) Politics and Development: Topical
description: (F) political ecology and development.

subject: POLS
title: American Political Institutions in Comparative Perspective
description: Consideration of American political institutions and development relative to American philosophical foundations and non-American political forms. Federalism as an expansive devise will be emphasized, as will American influence and penetration abroad. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: POLS
title: Public Administrative Theory
description: Focus varies among theoretical, comparative and developmental approaches to study of administration. One section each semester.

subject: POLS
title: Political Leadership
description: Exploration of political leadership as a focus for research, teaching, and applied political science.

subject: POLS
title: Comparative Public Administration
description: Detailed examination of implementation of governmental policy in different countries. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Law and Politics
description: Law, courts, and rights as a political resource; analyses of public law (including court decisions), other forms of dispute management, and judicial behavior and policy-making.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Public Law and Judicial System
description: Recent issues and practices in public law; particular judicial systems. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Public Policy
description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation. (Cross-listed as PLAN 607)

subject: POLS
title: Politics of the Future
description: Introduction to political futures studies; images of future, theories of social change, methods of social forecasting and designing preferred futures. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: The Future of Political Systems
description: Normative and descriptive forecasts of political institutions, systems, subsystems, and behaviors. Design of preferred systems.

subject: POLS
title: Topics in Public Policy
description: Particular political processes, specific political institutions, or particular policy area. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
description: Exploration of nonviolent, non-killing alternatives in political science research, teaching, and public service.

subject: POLS
title: Asian and/or Pacific Politics
description: Political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in all or part of Asia and/or the Pacific. Repeatable three times.

subject: POLS
title: Contemporary Native Hawaiian Politics
description: Study of political and social movements, political status, national and cultural identities, and issues of representation of Native Hawaiians.

subject: POLS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Asian and/or Pacific Politics
description: (C) Korean politics. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Politics of Hawai‘i
description: Examinations from several perspectives of the political, economic, and cultural forces that historically formed Hawai‘i and contemporary political themes, issues, and processes. Graduate students only.

subject: POLS
title: Teaching Initiative in Political Science
description: Combines the study of the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching political science with supervised classroom teaching of POLS 110. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: POLS
title: Colloquium
description: Specialized subjects in political science.

subject: POLS
title: Graduate Intern Seminar
description: Seminar for those seeking internship experience. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: 672 and 673 or consent for the alternative futures option; 620 or consent for the indigenous politics option; consent of advisor for all other options

subject: POLS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Research Methods
description: Conceptual strategies, data collection approaches, and data analysis techniques appropriate to political inquiries. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: POLS
title: Writing Politics
description: Seminar on the politics of writing, grammar, translation, argument, genre, and style with significant content on indigenous issues of oral traditions, alternative modes of writing and argument, and language continuance.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Political Thought
description: Pre-announced topics. Repeatable unlimited times. At least one section a year.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Indigenous Theory
description: Pre-announced topics may include gender and sexuality studies,

subject: LIS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable nine times.

subject: LIS
title: Seminar in International Librarianship
description: International and comparative librarianship; professional organizations; comparative methodology; research; periodicals; international agencies; influence of literacy and social, cultural, political factors.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to the Study of Language
description: Non-formal introduction to language, emphasizing the everyday use of language, its relevance to contemporary issues in society, and local language issues. Content studied through lecture, readings, and writing; emphasis on writing as a grading criterion

subject: LING
title: Language and Symbolic Reasoning
description: Introduction to language as a formal symbolic system and to the techniques of analysis and reasoning that reveal its workings. A-F only.

subject: LING
title: Language Endangerment, Globalization, and Indigenous Peoples
description: Focus on language endangerment and globalization. Students are introduced to case studies on language endangerment from around the world and throughout history. Offered through the distance-learning Unit Mastery program. A-F only.

subject: LING
title: Language as a Window to the Mind
description: Introduction to language-related phenomena, which gives insight into the organization of the human mind. Combines lecture, discussion and group projects.

subject: LING
title: Logic and Language
description: Introduces logic as a way of understanding the meanings of everyday words and sentences, as well as the inferences that humans draw from them. Topics include propositional logic, first-order logic, elementary set theory, and relations.

subject: LING
title: Language in Hawai‘i and the Pacific
description: Introduction to the study of language and language-related issues, with a focus on Hawai‘i and the Pacific; (B) unit mastery; (C) lecture discussion with focus on writing as a grading criterion. A-F only.

subject: LING
title: The Language of Children
description: Survey of findings about the child’s acquisition of language.

subject: LING
title: Language Documentation for NonLinguists
description: Provides training in the fundamentals of language documentation and conservation for non-linguists. Repeatable two times. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: proficiency in a lesser studied language and consent.

subject: LING
title: Bad Words
description: An examination of the link between language and society through the use and perception of taboo words.

subject: LING
title: General Linguistics
description: Introduction to the formal analysis of language, focusing on phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, historical linguistics, language acquisition, and related topics.

subject: LING
title: Computer Applications
description: Background; uses for machine translation, dictionary programs, speech synthesis, grammar modeling, etc.

subject: LING
title: Languages of the World
description: Survey of major language families; typological classification and language universals; writing systems, “contact” languages. Variety of grammatical structures illustrated by selected languages.

subject: LING
title: The Philippine Language Family
description: Introduction; phonological and grammatical systems; historical developments; emphasis on Filipino, Cebuano, and Ilokano.
prerequisites: grade of B or better in 102 or 320 and experience with a Philippine language, or consent.

subject: LING
title: Pidgin and Creole Languages
description: Nature, history, structure, and geographic distribution of pidgins and creoles. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as IS 347)

subject: LING
title: Philippine Sociolinguistics: Language Use, Ideologies, and Identities
description: Examines the intersection between language and society, specifically Philippine languages in various communities. Explores how language policies, discourses, and ideologies shape people’s use of language. Emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills. Sophomore standing or higher. (Cross-listed as IP 394)

subject: LING
title: Articulatory Phonetics
description: Intensive training in recognition, reproduction, and recording of human speech sounds; preparation for fieldwork with unrecorded languages and for clinical work in speech pathology.

subject: LING
title: Psycholinguistics
description: The mental processes involved in producing, understanding, and acquiring language. Students will conduct a small psycholinguistic experiment. Open to non-majors.
prerequisites: one of 102, 320, or PSY 100; or consent.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ANTH 414 and IS 414)

subject: LING
title: Language and Gender
description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ANTH 413)

subject: LING
title: Language as a Public Concern
description: How does language serve as a proxy for larger social questions? Focuses on four main themes: language revitalization, discrimination on the basis of accent, gender miscommunication and the English Only Movement. A-F only.

subject: LING
title: Language Endangerment and Revitalization
description: An overview of language endangerment, especially in the Pacific and Asia, and a critical examination of the strategies that are being developed to combat it.
prerequisites: one of LING 102, 150B, 150C, 105, 320, SLS 150, SLS 301, or consent.

subject: LING
title: Raciolinguistics
description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere. (Cross-listed as ES 451)

subject: LING
title: Morphology
description: Theory of word structure; analysis of a variety of morphological types.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Phonological Analysis
description: Phonological analysis and theory.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Grammatical Analysis
description: Syntactic analysis and grammatical theory.

subject: LING
title: Cognitive Linguistics
description: Conceptual systems and language from a cognitive science perspective. Linguistic evidence on conceptual structure, reasoning, categorization, and understanding. Open to non-majors.

subject: LING
title: Animal Communication
description: Investigates animal communication from the perspective of modern linguistics. Dispels common misconceptions about “talking animals” and shows how the cognitive, biological, and environmental needs and opportunities of animals determine what and how they communicate.

subject: LING
title: Computational Modeling
description: Hands-on introduction to modeling language. Focuses on connectionism, relations between language perception,and motor control. Requires no programming experience. Open to non-majors.

subject: LING
title: Topics in Linguistics
description: Variable topics in special areas of Linguistics, depending on instructor interest. Repeatable two times.

subject: LING
title: Meaning
description: Theories of how literal and figurative language encode meaning and processes of meaning encoding and decoding. Open to non-majors.

subject: LING
title: Polynesian Language Family
description: Introduction to the language family of Hawaiian, Samoan, Tahitian, Tongan, etc.; models of migration and settlement and linguistic evidence; subgrouping and reconstruction of Proto-Polynesian; linguistic characteristics of present-day languages; language endangerment and conservation in Polynesia.
prerequisites: 320 with a grade of B or better, or consent.

subject: LING
title: Induction of Linguistic Structure
description: Phonological and grammatical structures of a previously uncodified language are determined by linguistic analysis of data obtained from speakers of the language.

subject: LING
title: Children’s Speech
description: Child language acquisition, language milestones, multilingualism. Relation of cognitive development to language development. Emphasis on developing research skills, with an emphasis on written communication.

subject: LING
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable up to 3 credits. CR/NC only.

subject: LING
title: Acoustic and Auditory Phonetics
description: Principles of acoustics and audition as they relate to speech sounds, use of computer-based analysis tools to investigate acoustic properties of speech.

subject: LING
title: The Nature of Language
description: Language as a communication system, current theories of grammar, meaning, sociolinguistics, linguistic change and comparison.

subject: LING
title: Language Acquisition and Language Revitalization
description: Provides training relevant to the study and revitalization of heritage languages and endangered languages.

subject: LING
title: Data Science for Linguistic Research
description: Introduction to data science for linguistic research. Repeatable one time.

subject: LING
title: Practical Exercises in Data Science for Linguistic Research
description: Exercises in data science for linguistic research. Repeatable one time.

subject: LING
title: Phonology
description: Phonological theory and problems of analysis. (Fall only)

subject: LING
title: Grammar
description: Grammatical theory and problems of analysis.

subject: LING
title: Semantics and Pragmatics
description: Ways in which the interpretation of sentences in natural language depends upon the literal meaning of propositions and their logical (semantic)

subject: ORE
title: Capstone Design Project
description: Major design experience based on knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work and incorporating realistic constraints that include economic, environmental, ethical, social, and liability considerations. Emphasis is placed on teamwork and consultant-client relationship. (B) coastal engineering; (C) offshore engineering; (D) ocean resources engineering; (E) oceanic engineering. ORE majors only. (Fall only for (E)). (Alpha).
prerequisites: (ORE 411, ORE 603, and ORE 607) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: ORE
title: Special Topics in Ocean and Resources Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting and permanent faculty. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: ORE
title: Seminar in Ocean and Resources Engineering
description: Attendance at 15 approved seminars is required along with submission of notes.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: ORE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: candidacy for PhD in ocean and resources engineering.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST. Restricted to GES majors. CR/NC only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as GES 100)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: DB. Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GES 102 and SUST 112)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: DY. Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GES 102L and SUST 112L)
prerequisites: OCN 102 (or concurrent) or GES 102 (or concurrent) or SUST 112 (or concurrent).
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Sustainability in a Changing World
description: FGA. Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawai‘i/Oceania. Active learning environment. (Cross-listed as SUST 115)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Challenges
description: DP. Scientific approach to evaluating human-caused environmental challenges and their potential solutions. Open to non-majors. (Spring only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: FQ. Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ATMO 150 and ERTH 150)
prerequisites: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X).
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Research Experiences in Marine Science
description: Inquiry-driven and experimental marine biology summer program based on the expertise of HIMB researchers whose specialties demonstrate how human impacts and global change affect coral reef ecosystems. Emphases on student team research projects. Repeatable one time. High school or UG freshman only. (Summer only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Directed Research
description: Reading and research in any area of Oceanography under the direction of a faculty member. Repeatable up to six credits.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Science of the Sea
description: DP. Origin and features of ocean basins and seawater; global cycles of carbon and nutrients; currents; waves; tides; characteristics of marine organisms; marine ecological principles; marine pollution; climate change causes and consequences. Online asynchronous; synchronous format.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Science of the Sea Laboratory
description: DY. Experiments, computer exercises, and field trips demonstrating the geological, physical, chemical, and biological principles of earth and ocean sciences. A-F only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Change
description: DP. Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc. (Cross-listed as ATMO 310)
prerequisites: OCN 200, OCN 201, ERTH 101, ERTH 103, or ERTH 170; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods. (Cross-listed as ERTH 312)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models. Pre: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as PHIL 315)
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Introduction to environmental monitoring systems for earth science students. Students will learn how to construct, program, and deploy simple environmental monitoring systems to collect in-situ environmental data. OCN, ERTH, ATMO majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: OCN 201/201L or ERTH 101/101L, CHEM 161/161L, and MATH 241; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
description: DY. (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311. Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling. GES majors only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as GES 319L)
prerequisites: GES 311, MATH 242, PHYS 170/170L, and CHEM 161/161L; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Pollution
description: DP. Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives. (Cross-listed as GES 320)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: DS. Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as PPC 340 and SUST 323)
prerequisites: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Mineral and Energy Resources of the Sea
description: DP. Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration, and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints. (Cross-listed as ORE 330)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Living Resources of the Sea-Mai ke Kai Mai ke Ola
description: DB. Marine fisheries, aquaculture, and law of the sea. Principles of management of renewable resources. Political and scientific constraints and limitations. Sophomore standing or higher.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawai‘i. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as PEPS 340)
prerequisites: (BIOL 171 and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN

college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science. Repeatable up to 6 credits. (Cross-listed as GES 399)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Systems
description: DP. Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills. GES majors only. Senior standing only. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as GES 401)
prerequisites: OCN 201, GES 311, BIOL 172/172L, CHEM 162/162L, ERTH 101/101L, GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES/OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as MBBE 405)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Crosslisted as SUST 414)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Builds upon 318 using more advanced microprocessors and environmental sensors, 3D printing, programming, etc. to construct, program, and deploy environmental monitoring systems to collect and stream in-situ time-series env
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: STE
title: Home Economics Education

subject: STE
title: Managing Classrooms
description: Analysis of the factors that contribute to learning in the classroom and the development of teacher behaviors that promote such learning. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Student Teaching
description: Full-time supervised experience in school. (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary; (D) secondary; (M) dual preparation in elementary education and multilingual learning; (S) dual preparation in elementary and special education. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Completion of all other program requirements, passing Praxis II exam(s). Co-requisite for D: 391D.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Seminar for Student Teaching
description: With student teaching as context, examination of knowledge, skills, and dispositions for teaching; standards-based planning, teaching, assessment, and reflection; inclusive classroom management; professional growth and development; integration of research, theory, and practice. Emphasis on writing instruction and ethical issues in teaching. (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary (2); (D) secondary; (M) dual preparation in elementary education and multilingual learning (2); (S) dual preparation in elementary and special education (1). Repeatable nine times for (D). CR/NC only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Student Teaching Modified
description: Modified student teaching for individuals who have had prior extensive teaching experience or wish to repeat student teaching. CR/NC only. (C) elementary; (D) secondary.
prerequisites: Extensive teaching experience; requirements listed under “student teaching”; approval of review committee; consent. Co-requisite: 391.

subject: STE
title: Directed Study
description: Individual work supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, observation/participation, teaching, and/or projects. Repeatable up to 12 credits.

subject: STE
title: Principles & Methods of Literacies Within and Across the Disciplines
description: Examines different literacy strategies for learning content that will engage diverse adolescents across and within all disciplines. Includes a disciplinary literacies framework that influences lesson planning, classroom culture, and assessment practices. Emphasis on teaching writing. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Teaching Practicum
description: Observation, analysis, participation and teaching in middle or high school. A seminar accompanies the field experience. Subject field: (B) visual and performing arts; (C) business and marketing; (D) language arts; (E) physical education; (F) industrial arts/agriculture; (G) mathematics; (H) science; (I) social studies; (J) foreign language; (K) music; (M) home economics; (N) interdisciplinary; (O) elementary; (P) English as a Second Language. Repeatable two times. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Admission to COE Teacher Education Program and departmental consent.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Educational Inquiry
description: Study and discussion of general school-related topics and issues, e.g., dimensions of elementary and/ or secondary schooling, school governance, curriculum design and development, the student learner, classroom management; (B) service learning; (C) exploratory education; (D) international field study; (E) minor in education. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Teaching in the Subject Field
description: Purposes, procedures, curricula, evaluation in elementary or secondary school subject field. Develops written communication skills: (B) visual and performing art; (C) business and marketing; (D) language arts; (E) physical education; (F) industrial arts/agriculture; (G) mathematics; (H) science; (I) social studies; (J) foreign languages; (K) music; (M) home economics; (N) interdisciplinary; (P) English as a Second Language. Repeatable five times for different alphas. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Teaching Residency
description: Full-time student teaching experience in school. Student teachers will receive training and evaluation for oral communication, organization, and planning skills. Subject field: (B) visual and performing arts; (C) business and marketing; (D) language arts; (F) industrial arts; (G) mathematics; (H) science; (l) social studies; (J) foreign languages; (K) music; (M) home economics; (O) elementary education; (P) English as a second language. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: Successful completion of all required courses; departmental consent.

subject: STE
title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
description: Analysis and resolution of current ethical issues and practices in classrooms; teaching skills and strategies; curriculum planning, professional growth and development; and integration of teaching experiences with professional standards. Instruction in preparing an extensive written portfolio. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Supervision of the Observation-Participation Student
description: Basic guidelines for developing effective team relationships between the professional teacher and the observation-participation student.
prerequisites: Two years’ teaching experience and consent.

subject: STE

subject: STE

subject: STE
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
description: Continuation of 415L. CR/ NC only. (Cross-listed as EDCS 416L)

description: Planning child-centered, responsive programs for children. Focuses on play, learning environments, integrated thematic instructional design, guidance, assessment, and family engagement in early childhood and early elementary to promote enjoyment, growth, and development. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Supervision of Student Teaching
description: Principles and methods; role of supervisor; human resources supervision in student teaching. Open to teachers interested in pre-service teacher education.
prerequisites: Three years teaching experience and consent.

subject: STE

description: Knowledge and appreciation for the complex characteristics of children, families, and communities. Analysis and development of skills for creating respectful, reciprocal relationships with diverse children and families from diverse backgrounds. Lecture/lab.
prerequisites: 318 (or concurrent), or HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: STE

description: Advanced principles and methods: clinical supervision, observation recording, analysis, interpretation of classroom teaching; human resources supervision in student teaching.
prerequisites: 420, successful supervision of two or more student teachers, and consent.

subject: STE

description: Planned work-experience program for special areas of vocational technical education. Acceptable type of wage-earning employment. Minimum of six 40- hour weeks or 240 work hours required. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: STE

description: Historical and philosophical foundations of vocational technical education, overview of federal and state legislation and contemporary practices. Special emphasis on vocational education program in Hawai‘i.

subject: STE

description: Understanding and use of word processing, spreadsheet, and database software for business applications. Explore software across the office and marketing content areas.

subject: STE

description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawai‘i as our place of learning and teaching. (Cross-listed as EDCS 440)

subject: STE

description: Examination of issues in Hawaiian and U.S. views of education and their application to the teaching of Hawaiian studies. Field experience required. A-F only.
prerequisites: 312C, 312D; or consent. Co-requisite for BEd students: 317.

subject: STE
title: Education of Exceptional Children in Regular Classroom
description: Practices that facilitate teaching special needs students in regular classrooms. Techniques for meeting academic needs, managing behavior, motivating students, increasing peer interactions, communication between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms, Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

subject: KOR

subject: KOR

description: Integrating the conceptual aspects of statistics and scientific analysis of human language behavior into the study of Korean as a foreign language.

subject: KOR

description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature. Repeatable one time.

subject: KOR
title: Practicum: Teaching Korean as a Second Language
description: Designed for graduate students pursuing Korean language teaching, while developing practical teaching skills through class observation, action research and discussion under supervision.

subject: KOR
title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical sociocultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history. Repeatable one time.

subject: KOR
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: KOR
title: Research Seminar in Korean Literature
description: Advanced study of an author, school, period, genre, or problem leading to a research paper. Repeatable four times.

subject: KOR

description: Advanced study in history and dialects, phonology and morphology, syntax and semantics, sociolinguistics, or pedagogy, leading to a research paper. Repeatable four times.

department: Languages and Literatures of Europe and the Americas

subject: NURS
title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-B
description: Second of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Emerging Diseases & Implications for Advanced Nursing Practice
description: Selected emerging diseases are examined within historical context, known science (past and present) and societal factors that influence prevention, detection, treatment and containment strategies. Considerations for advanced public health nursing practice are identified and examined. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Research, Theory, and Evidence-Based Practice
description: Examination of theory, research, and evidence-based inquiry to support evidence-based practice among MS prepared nurses.
prerequisites: enrollment as a classified student in the graduate degree program in SONDH
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Acute and Episodic Care Management
description: Diagnosis and management of health and illness with emphasis on clients with common acute/episodic conditions seen in context of family and community. Advanced practice nurse-client relationship, practice roles, and culturally relevant care are included. NURS majors only or consent. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Issues and Roles
description: Exploration of major issues and roles in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Survey of biopsychological bases of and biotherapies for major mental disorders, including the schizophrenias, affective and personality disorders, pediatric and geriatric problems, and neurological dysfunctions with appropriate applications to health care. NURS majors only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Adolescent and Family PsychiatricMental Health Care
description: Seminar on theory/ research in advanced psychiatric-mental health nursing of adolescents and families representing diverse populations. Emphasis on developmental and nursing theories, evidence-based practice, therapeutic modalities and disease management of psychiatric illness. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Nursing Roles
description: Provides students with an understanding of different roles of the advanced professional nurse; an ability to proactively manage the environment of their specialty practice; includes 45 hours of field work experience. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Population Health Nursing
description: Introduction to the core competencies, key theoretical models and concepts that guide advanced population health nursing. The student will initiate their professional portfolio, which must be completed during the last semester of the MS program. NURS majors only. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Child/Family Health Assessment
description: (2 Sem, 8-hr Lab) Opportunity to develop specialized clinical competence in assessment of children as a basis for the development of clinical specialization. Development of the individual’s potential toward health maintenance functioning. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Child Health: Special Health Needs
description: Provides a theoretical basis required for specialized clinical competence in adapting recent findings on child/parent assessments, social and health risk indicators, the role of environment, and multidisciplinary settings in the care of pediatrics. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nurses in Advanced Practice
description: Prepares APNs to evaluate, monitor, and prescribe pharmaceuticals to treat acute and chronic illness across lifespan. Emphasis on drug indications, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, adverse effects, interactions, monitoring, education, and cost effectiveness. Enrollment as a classified student in a SONDH graduate degree program. Repeatable unlimited times. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Information Technology in Healthcare
description: Introduction to the use of information systems in healthcare. Selected information systems and data sets are explored with application of results to various patient populations and clinical practice settings.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Psychopharmacology Across the Lifespan
description: Examines the legal, ethical and therapeutic role of the psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioner (PMHNP) in prescribing psychotropic medications for diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Diverse biopsychosocial perspectives will be considered. NURS majors only. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Therapeutic Modalities
description: Therapeutic modalities used in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations. NURS majors only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Child Health: Promotion and Maintenance
description: Presents normal developmental, physiological and social needs of children within the context of family; then focuses on the management of common acute and chronic illnesses of children. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Child Health: Advanced Pediatric Acute/Chronic Care
description: Focuses on the evaluation of pediatric clients with higher acuity and more complex management issues. Emphasizes critical analysis of evidence based research in pediatric health care. NURS majors only or consent.
prerequisites: Admission into the PNP and FNP program; 612/612L, and 633
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Women’s Health: Promotion and Maintenance
description: Provides a foundation of concepts necessary to maintain and promote women’s health, including developmental, physiological and social needs of women of all ages and the management of common health problems and concerns specific to women. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Women’s Health: Special Problem
description: (2 Sem, 12-hr Lab) Focuses upon assessment and intervention of at-risk and high-risk women during pregnancy, interconception, and the menopausal years. Emphasizes critical analysis of research in pregnancy, family planning, and common gynecological problems. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Child and Adolescent PsychiatricMental Health
description: Theory and research in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing of children and adolescents representing culturally diverse populations. Emphasis on growth and development, assessment and diagnosis, and therapeutic modalities. NURS majors only. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Disciplinary Knowledge I
description: Exploration of a variety of philosophies of science and examination of factors influencing the development of nursing theory and the emergence of nursing as a discipline. NURS majors only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Chronic Illness Management
description: Management of chronic illness using selected health care systems in culturally diverse communities. Management includes practice, consultation, education, research, and evaluation. NURS majors only or consent.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Nursing in the Global Health Environment
description: Exploration and analysis of key global health topics of concern for APNs. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Health Care Technology and Informatics
description: Introduction to the field of health care technology and informatics for clinicians through the application of health care information systems. Open to students in other healthcare fields by permission. A-F only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Health Law
description: Introduction to medical jurisprudence, medical malpractice, informed consent, health care decisions, medical ethics, the health care industry, managed care, financing health care, and the role of government in health care. LAW majors only; NURS DNP majors only (Cross-listed as LAW 532)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Psychiatric-Mental Health Practicum
description: Supervised application of theories, research, and skills for advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations. Includes the program’s capstone experience. Repeatable five times. NURS majors only.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Family Systems in Health and Illness
description: Family systems approach to include selected family theories, family research and family centered culturally sensitive clinical assessment and intervention in health and illness situations.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Complementary and Traditional Care
description: A review of theoretical systems and approaches to complementary and traditional care in culturally diverse populations with a focus on wellness. Appropriate for all health-care professionals.
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: NURS
title: Tests and Measurement in Nursing Education
description: Testing and evaluation applied to nursing education. NURS majors only. A-F only. (Once a year)
department: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)
college: School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene (SONDH)

subject: OCN
title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as MBBE 405)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Crosslisted as SUST 414)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Builds upon 318 using more advanced microprocessors and environmental sensors, 3D printing, programming, etc. to construct, program, and deploy environmental monitoring systems to collect and stream in-situ time-series environmental measurements. OCN, ERTH, ATMO majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: OCN 318, MATH 242, PHYS 272/272L, and CHEM 162/162L; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Marine Geology
description: DP Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins. (Cross-listed as ERTH 423)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deepsea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction and global climate change. A-F only. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Climate Change and Urbanization
description: The following topics will be addressed: How are cities impacted by, and impacting climate change? How do urbanization, alteration of atmospheric processes, and extreme weather events affect urban systems and populations? A-F only. (Fall only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as CEE 441 and SUST 441)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015. Repeatable one time. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as SUST 442 and TIM 462)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Plate Tectonics
description: DP (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ERTH 444)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Aquaculture Production
description: DB Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics, and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery. (Cross-listed as ANSC 450)
prerequisites: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445: or BIOL 172/172L and CHEM 162/162L or higher.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Earth’s Microbiome
description: DB Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Alt years: Fall) (Cross-listed as GES 454)
prerequisites: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: DY Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Alt years: Fall) (Cross-listed as OCN 454L)
prerequisites: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ridge to Reef: Coastal Ecosystem Ecology and Connectivity
description: Watershed and coastal biogeochemistry/ecosystem science. Emphasis on field surveying and sampling of stream and reef habitats; laboratory chemical/biological analyses. Analysis of land use impacts on ecosystem health and ahupua‘a resource management. A-F only.
prerequisites: OCN 201/201L; and either OCN/ATMO 310, or GES 311; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: DP Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory. GES majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GES 463)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
description: Combined lecture and discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems. GES majors only. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: OCN 201/201L, GES 311, GES 319L, and PHYS 272/272L; and consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
description: Introduction to modeling biogeochemical and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on plankton blooms. Students learn ecosystem dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming. A-F only. GES majors only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: (OCN/ATMO 310 or GES 311 or PHYS 272, and OCN/ERTH 312) with a minimum grade of B-.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Communication of Research Results
description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material. GES majors only in their final semester. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GES 490)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Global Environmental Science
description: Lecture and discussion or seminar. Current topics in environmental science explored in detail. Typically offered by faculty in their specialties, or developed in response to student interest. GES majors only. Repeatable unlimited times, credits earned up to six credits.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article. Repeatable up to six credits. (Cross-listed as GES 499)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Physical Oceanography
description: Introduction to properties of seawater, oceanographic instruments and methods, heat budget, general ocean circulation, regional oceanography, waves, tides, sea level. Formation of water masses, dynamics of circulation. Repeatable one time.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Biological Oceanography
