description: Factors governing productivity, population dynamics, distribution of organisms in major ecosystems of the ocean, emphasis on ecology of pelagic zone. OCN majors only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Geological Oceanography
description: Marine geological processes, ocean basin structure and tectonics, sedimentation.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Chemical Oceanography
description: Chemical processes occurring in marine waters; why they occur and how they affect oceanic environment.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Photosynthesis
description: Biochemical and biophysical concepts of photosynthesis. Application and interpretation of ecological processes of photosynthesis in aquatic systems. Open to nonmajors. A-F only. (Spring only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Marine Microplankton Ecology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Distribution, abundance, and ecology of marine microplankton, including bacteria, algae, and protozoans, with an emphasis on metabolic rates and processes. Pre: consent. (Fall only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ecology of Pelagic Marine Animals
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ecology of pelagic animals including feeding, energetics, predation, and anti-predation tactics. Life-history strategies, vertical flux of materials, population dynamics, fisheries. (Spring only)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Benthic Biological Oceanography
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Processes controlling the structure and function of benthic communities, including organism-sediment-flow interactions, sediment geochemistry, feeding strategies, recruitment, succession, and population interactions. OCN and MB majors only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Molecular Methods in Marine Ecology
description: Molecular methods for studying marine functional ecology; emphasis on hand-on tools for ecological and biogeochemical processes of microbes; developing practical skills for research project in marine microbial ecology and biological oceanography. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: OCN 403, OCN 626, OCN 627, or OCN 628; or consent.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction, and global climate change. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Minerals
description: Distribution, origin, processes of formation. Sulfides, oxides, and placer minerals. Comparative studies of continental ore bodies. Submarine rift, subduction, and abduction.
prerequisites: one of OCN 622, OCN 623, ERTH 407, or ERTH 603.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Methods in Oceanography
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Current methods of analysis used in the ocean sciences, both in the field and in the laboratory. An ocean-going field trip provides students with hands-on training in sample collection and processing. The latter is followed by laboratory analyses
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: PH
title: Needs Assessment
description: Knowledge and skills acquisition in conducting needs assessment in public health practice.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as TRMD 650)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
description: Topics such as contemporary issues in global health and population studies, international health programs, demographic methods, global economy and health, human right and humanitarian assistance, social justice, global environmental changes and health.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Global Health and Human Security
description: Provides the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to successfully manage health security crises and protect human vulnerability in the global context with a special focus on problems with high likelihood and risk in the Pacific.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Biostatistics I
description: Introduction to statistical methods for public health sciences. Probability, experimental design, t tests and analysis of variance, 2X2 contingency tables, linear regression, introduction to life tables.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Biostatistics II
description: Poisson distribution, Fisher’s exact test, contrasts in ANOVA, two way ANOVA, multiple linear regression and analysis of covariance, path analysis, logistic regression, method of maximum likelihood, likelihood ratio tests.
prerequisites: 655, completion of one semester of calculus; or consent
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Computer Applications in Public Health
description: Applications of computers to problems common to public health. Emphasis on data analysis and processing using existing computer programs.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, and urbanization; projections and stable population theory. (Cross-listed as SOC 659)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Principles of Epidemiology I
description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods. Topics covered include: outbreak investigation, measures of morbidity and mortality, measurements of risk, biological variability, screening, measurements of error, sampling, statistical significance, study design, and association and causation.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Principles of Epidemiology II
description: Lecture/discussion on: design and interpretation of experimental and observational studies; causation and casual inference; biases in study design; random error and statistics role in epidemiology; and epidemiological data analysis. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TRMD 604)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Infectious Disease Control
description: Strategies for controlling important infectious diseases in the Pacific area. Emphasis on epidemiology, ecology, and public health principles.
prerequisites: 663 (or concurrent) and one semester in microbiology, or consent
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Infectious Disease Micro II
description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TRMD 605)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Epidemiological Study Design Critique
description: Critique of study design using published public health literature. Emphasis on exchange of ideas, alternative approaches; stresses epidemiology as science of public health. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Community and Public Health Practice
description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery. (Cross-listed as SW 674)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Leading and Managing Health Programs
description: Assess how to organize community partnerships to create and communicate a shared vision for a changing future; discuss solutions to organizational and community challenges; maximize motivation to reach public health goals. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as LAW 594)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Advanced Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
description: Applications of evidence-based knowledge about the social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Community Engaged Research and Practice
description: Explores collaborative and engaged approaches with communities in public health research and practice. With a focus on Indigenous Peoples’ health, we delve into Indigenous knowledge and empowerment in evaluation, needs assessment, intervention, and health promotion. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Hawai‘i Public Health Policies on Infectious Diseases
description: Examines quarantine/ isolation of patients infected with Hanson’s disease. Focus on PH policies before 1823 and after; analysis of other infections in Hawai‘i and the world to examine differences in policies and their effect on the public. Graduate students only. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Managing Global Health Service Delivery
description: Provides knowledge, skills, attitudes and resources that health managers require to manage and maintain the quality of partnerships, facilities, programs, community services, people, drugs, and information in limited resources settings. PH majors only. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Health Emergencies in Large Populations
description: Health Emergencies in Large Populations is run by the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance and the Red Cross. It provides knowledge, practical skills, and networking for global health practitioners. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Environmental Determinants of Health
description: Environmental factors in personal and community health; implications for public health practice. Consideration of major issues from local, U.S., and international perspectives.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Global Nutrition
description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall) (Cross-listed as FSHN 683)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. PH majors only. (Cross-listed as FSHN 684)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as FSHN 686)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as FSHN 688)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Nutritional Epidemiology
description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease. (Cross-listed as FSHN 689)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Global Health Challenges
description: Addresses critical, contemporary, and transnational issues best addressed by cooperative international action. Health issues are examined in the context of intersecting effects of limited resources, socioeconomics, politics, and environmental change. A-F only. (Once a year)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Fundamentals of Environmental Epidemiology
description: Examines the complex relationship between environmental contaminants and human health. Emphasis on environmental epidemiology study design, environmental exposure monitoring and risk assessment, disease and environmental exposure mapping, and spatial data analysis and modeling with GIS. A-F only. (Once a year)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Promoting Physical Activity
description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as KRS 695)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: PH
title: Health Communication
description: Skills-oriented course introduces the basic structure of health communication strategies in different settings, selected elements of communication theory, the development of health communication material
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SPAN
title: Reading Spain
description: Reading and discussion of narratives from and about Spain; (B) heroines, knights, witches; (C) love, loss, liberty. Repeatable one time for different alphas. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SPAN
title: Reading Latin America
description: Culture and history of Spanish America through literature; (B) warriors, nuns, and rebels; (C) the magical and the real. Repeatable one time for different alphas. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SPAN
title: Introduction to Hispanic Film
description: Introduction to the study and analysis of genres, techniques, and cinematic styles as used in Hispanic film.

subject: SPAN
title: Directed Reading
description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish Language in Society
description: Explores issues in Spanish language in society (media, communication, advertising, government, technology). Introduces and examines current sociolinguistic and sociopragmatic issues.

subject: SPAN
title: Building Advanced Fluency
description: Advanced practice; emphasis on building active vocabulary.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish-English Translation
description: Factors in the art of translation. Practice in translating material from Spanish to English and the reverse.

subject: SPAN
title: Historical Spanish Linguistics
description: Evolution of Spanish from Latin; modern social and geographical dialects.

subject: SPAN
title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics
description: Analysis of morphology, syntax, and semantics.

subject: SPAN
title: Fourth-Level Spanish Abroad
description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the fourth-year level in Spanish linguistics, civilization, culture, and literature in a Spanish-speaking country.

subject: SPAN
title: Fourth-Level Spanish Abroad
description: Continuation of 458.

subject: SPAN
title: Intensive Fourth-Level Spanish Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-year level in Spanish language and culture in a Spanish-speaking country. For semester programs only.

subject: SPAN
title: U.S. Latino Literature
description: Study of the literature of U.S. Hispanics written in Spanish or bilingually.

subject: SPAN
title: Hispanic Women’s Literature
description: Women’s literary and cultural expressions in Latin America and Spain.

subject: SPAN
title: Hispanic Theater
description: Study of representative authors and plays from Spain and Latin America. Repeatable one time.

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Hispanic Scholarship
description: Hispanic authors, periods, or themes. (B) literature and society; (D) literature and film. Repeatable for other topics, but not for the same topic.

subject: SPAN
title: Studies in Latin American and Iberian Film
description: Intensive study of selected topics in Latin American and/or Iberian cinemas; e.g. national or regional cinemas, periods, movements or issues, major filmmakers, film theory and criticism. Repeatable two times.

subject: SPAN
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision. A-F only. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and departmental approval.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish Translation Studies
description: Study of social, cultural, and pragmatic issues in Spanish Translation Studies. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPAN
title: Seminar in Spanish Applied Linguistics
description: Repeatable unlimited times with consent.

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Spanish Applied Linguistics
description: Supervised participation in online course at UNED University (Spain) relevant to student’s specialization for Second Language Studies or Spanish Applied Linguistics. Students also complete projects and meet with advisor to check progress. Repeatable two times for different topics. Graduate students only.
prerequisites: Spanish Proficiency assessment: B- (CERFL) or Advanced low (ACTFL).

subject: SPAN
title: Medieval Spanish Literature
description: Representative readings in prose and poetry, from origins through 15th century.

subject: SPAN
title: Golden Age Literature
description: Spanish literature from the 16th and 17th centuries. (B) theater; (C) prose; (D) poetry; (E) Cervantes.

subject: SPAN
title: 19th-Century Spanish Realism
description: Nineteenth-century Spanish realism in the novel. Authors include Galdós, Clarin, Alarcón, Pardo Bazán, Blasco-Ibáñez, Valera.

subject: SPAN
title: 20th-Century Spanish Literature
description: Representative works from 20th-century literature. Genres: poetry, theater, essay, novel. (B) generation of 1898; (C) pre-Civil War; (D) post-Civil War.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish-American Novel
description: Critical analysis of major Spanish-American novels.

subject: SPAN
title: Colonial Spanish-American Literature
description: Spanish-American literature from period of discovery to independence. Representative authors such as Sor Juana, Bernal Díaz del Castillo.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish-American Poetry
description: Study of representative poets from all periods: Martí, Darió, Mistral, Guillén, Neruda, Paz, etc.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish-American Short Story and Essay
description: Study of representative writers from various periods: Sor Juana, Palma, Quiroga, Reyes, Borges, etc.

subject: SPAN
title: Seminar in Hispanic Literature
description: A period, author, genre, or region. Repeatable unlimited times with consent.

subject: SPAN
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SPED
title: Disability and Diversity in the Media
description: Explores the changing disability experience as described in contemporary film, literature, advertising, news, sports and dialogue with persons with disabilities in the Pacific region and around the world. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Global and Historical Perspectives of Disability in the Media
description: Explores the history of disability representation across cultures. Emphasis is placed on examining evolving perceptions of disability as depicted in art, literature, print, film, and digital media. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Foundations of Inclusive Schooling
description: Foundations of “special education” exploring philosophies, diverse and historical viewpoints, laws, and service delivery. Students reflect upon texts, films and interviews with persons with disabilities, their families and professionals to understand the culture of disability. A-F only.
certificates: Post-Baccalaureate Special Education (PB-SPED) in mild/moderate disabilities

subject: SPED
title: Special Education Law and Compliance
description: Analysis of legislation, litigation, and administrative rulings in special education, with an emphasis on teaching expository writing and developing legally sound policies/procedures that ensure educationally meaningful and legally correct education for students with disabilities. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Special Education Assessment
description: Assessment methods and techniques to inform special education decisions, including the use of standardized assessments for initial eligibility, reevaluations, and annual reviews for special education services. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Specialized Instruction
description: Characteristics and educational programming for students with disabilities. Role and responsibilities of the special educator, founding principles and current practices in special education with an emphasis on teaching writing. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: SPED
title: Field Training – Blended ECE
description: Students spend 15 hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled classes; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as STE 315)

subject: SPED
title: Young Children with Communication Needs
description: Communication development of infants and young children, ages birth through age 8, with and without disabilities. Assessment and intervention to support the development of communication skills in inclusive community and school environments. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Student Teaching in Special Education
description: Full-time supervised experience in school. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one per alpha. A-F only. Co-requisite: 391B for (B); 391C for (C); 391D for (D).

subject: SPED
title: Seminar for Student Teachers in Special Education
description: Seminar relating current educational theories with experiences. (B) elementary/ special education; (C) early childhood education/ special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.

subject: PHIL
title: Critical Thinking: Pre-Medicine
description: Scientific and social perspectives on the nature of disease and their impact on medical practice. Exploration of these topics through reading, writing and critical inquiry.
prerequisites: any course in PHIL, 100 or above; or any two BIOL, CHEM or PHYS courses; or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as OCN 315)
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Science, Technology, and Society
description: Investigation of some of the complex interconnections between science, technology, and society. DH
prerequisites: any course 100 or above in PHIL or in a course with either DB or DP or DS designation, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Critical Thinking: Pre-Law
description: Introduction to concepts and techniques for evaluating arguments with special emphasis on their application both to questions of law and to issues in jurisprudence. DH
prerequisites: any course 100 or above in PHIL or POLS or SOC, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Law
description: Historical and contemporary issues in law and legal theory. Law and morality; legal responsibility, justice, rights, punishment, judicial reasoning. DH
prerequisites: any course 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in BLAW or POLS or SOC, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Ethical Issues in the Law
description: Exploration of ethical issues that have come before (mainly U.S.) courts, including but not confined to, medical and criminal justice ethics. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: 101 or a course numbered 200 or above in PHIL or HIST or ENG or with a DS designation; or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: American Philosophy
description: Survey of major philosophers and schools in development of American thought up to modern times. DH
prerequisites: any course 100 or above in PHIL, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Bodies, Minds, and Selves
description: Explores the nature of the mind. Questions addressed include: How does the mind relate to the body? What is the nature of consciousness? Are you the same person today as you were yesterday? DH
prerequisites: any 100-level PHIL course or above, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Critical Race Theory and Philosophy
description: (LED) Introduction to the work of philosophers whose writings aim to contribute to movements for racial justice. Repeatable one time. A-F only. DH

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Disability
description: Uses tools of philosophical inquiry to explore philosophical concepts emerging from the study of disability. Ethical issues of personhood and justice are discussed, with significant attention given to helping students express their thinking through writing. A-F only. DH

subject: PHIL
title: Islamic Philosophy
description: Survey of major Islamic philosophers and schools. DH
prerequisites: any course 100 or above in PHIL or ARAB, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Topics in Ancient Greek Thought
description: Explore a central aspect of ancient Greek philosophy and literature. This may be a theme, such as tragedy or emotions; a thinker, such as Aristotle; or a since monumental text, such as Plato’s Republic. (Cross-listed as CLAS 332). DH

subject: PHIL
title: Hawaiian Philosophy: Aloha ‘Āina
description: Introduction to Indigenous Hawaiian philosophy and how to engage with Aloha ‘Āina relying upon a methodology and pedagogy consistent with the philosophy being discussed. DH
prerequisites: 100 or above, HAW 100, HWST 107, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Indian Philosophy
description: Survey of major orthodox and heterodox systems: Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavadgita, Vedanta, Jainism, Buddhism. DH
prerequisites: any course 100 or above in PHIL or PALI or SNSK; or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Buddhist Philosophy
description: Survey of central thinkers and schools. (Cross-listed as ASAN 360). DH

subject: PHIL
title: Chinese Philosophy
description: Survey of important schools and thinkers in classical Chinese traditions: Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, Legalism. A significant emphasis will be placed on developing the ability to write clearly, critically, and coherently. DH

subject: PHIL
title: Japanese Philosophy
description: Survey of central thinkers and schools from ancient to modern. DH

subject: PHIL
title: The Meaning of War
description: Exploration of ethical questions related to the many facets of war–e.g., patriotism, tribalism, holy war, self-sacrifice, cowardice, media coverage, propaganda, torture, genocide, pillage, suicide tactics, battlefield immunity. (Cross-listed as PACE 387). DH

subject: PHIL
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable up to a maximum of 6 credits.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Phenomenology
description: Methods of analyzing the structures of experience, as developed by Husserl, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Sartre, etc. DH

subject: PHIL
title: Marxism and Critical Theory
description: Introduction to the philosophical works of Karl Marx and a historical overview of the development of the Frankfurt School of Critical Theory. A-F only. DH

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Zen (Ch’an) Buddhist Philosophy
description: Development and philosophical significance of basic precepts, explored through translations of Chinese and Japanese sources. DH

subject: PHIL
title: (Alpha) Western Movements and Periods
description: (B) Greek; (C) late antiquity; (D) medieval; (E) Renaissance; (F) continental rationalism; (G) British empiricism; (H) German idealism; (I) 19th century; (J) 20th century. Repeatable two times in different alphas, not in same alpha. DH
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy in Literature
description: Philosophical themes in the literary mode in world literature. DL

subject: PHIL
title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy
description: Examination of basic feminist issues in philosophy, and of responses to them. (Cross-listed as WGSS 419). DH
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophical Psychology
description: Classical and modern theories of mind, cognition, and action. DH

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Language
description: Contemporary theories in semantics and syntax; problems of meaning, reference, speech acts, etc. DH
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or LING, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Gender and Environmental Philosophy
description: Interdisciplinary approach to feminist perspectives on environmental issues; critical analysis of eco-feminism as political movement with reference to race and coloniality; cross-cultural comparison of differently-imagined relationships to non-human others, with emphasis on ethics and writing. (Cross-listed as WGSS 438). DH
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS or any course 200 or above with a DB or DP designation, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Symbolic Logic
description: Intermediate-level course covering proof techniques for classical, first-order predicate calculus, and an introduction to meta-theory. DH
prerequisites: 110 or any course 200 or above in ICS or MATH; or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Individual Philosophers/Topics
description: Examination of work of a major Eastern or Western philosopher, or topic of philosophical concern. Repeatable three times.

subject: PHIL
title: Undergraduate Capstone
description: Capstone seminar for undergraduate majors. Concentration on a topic of current philosophical concern. Repeatable one time with consent. DH
prerequisites: declared major in PHIL with at least six courses 200 or above in PHIL, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Understanding Place: Philosophical Inquiry and Community
description: Uses tools of philosophical inquiry, specifically p4cHI pedagogy, to develop a deep understanding of lived environment in a Hawaiian context while drawing on urban planning theories and methods to empower students as agents of change. Repeatable one time. (Fall only). DH
prerequisites: any course 100 or above in PHIL or PLAN, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy with Children
description: Experience theory and practice developing intellectually safe philosophical communities of inquiry in contexts from kindergarten through university and beyond.
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or EDUC, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Teaching Philosophy
description: Supervised work in elementary, middle, and high school classrooms, facilitating philosophical inquiry with students. Repeatable one time.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Ethics
description: Key issues in contemporary philosophical debates about ethics. Repeatable one time with consent. Recommended: 301.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Metaphysics
description: Key issues in ontological and cosmological theory. Problems of materialism, idealism, phenomenalism, etc. Repeatable one time with consent. Recommended: 304.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Philosophy of Religion
description: Key issues in theory of religious experience, language, reasoning. Recommended: 305.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Aesthetics
description: Key issues in contemporary aesthetics, against background of traditional Western and Eastern theories. Repeatable one time with consent. Recommended: 306.

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Epistemology
description: Key issues in contemporary philosophical debates about knowledge. Repeatable one time with consent. Recommended: 307.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophical Foundations of Cultural Criticism
description: A survey of the philosophical texts, thinkers, concepts, and theoretical approaches that are used in cultural criticism. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: PHIL
title: Studies in Hermeneutics
description: Important debates concerning the methodology of textual interpretation.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Psychology
description: DS Major principles; social attitudes, theories of conformity and change, person perception and attribution theory, social role, role conflict and role behavior, group structure, and behavior.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Happiness in Unsettled Times
description: DS Combines theoretical, scientific and ‘hands-on’ learning to explore how happiness and well-being can be cultivated, even in this challenging era of extreme global climate events.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Education
description: DS Formal education as one aspect of socialization. Emphasis on American system; business, military, and religious institutions.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
description: DS Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research. (cross-listed as COA 353)

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Medical Sociology
description: DS Social factors in disease and treatment; illness behavior, roles of patients and healers; nature of healing professions; use of medical services; alternative systems of medical organization.

subject: SOC
title: Chinese Society and Culture
description: DS Social institutions, family, community, education, stratification, government, economy; impact of modernization and revolution on their contemporary transformation. A-F only.

subject: SOC
title: Japanese Society and Culture
description: DS Persistence and change in economy, policy, religion, education, family, and other institutions of modern Japan.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Korea
description: DS Social institutions, family, education, religion, cultural values, social classes, economic development, social movements, gender relations, North-South relations, and unification issues. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Gender
description: DS Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems. (Cross-listed as WGSS 362)
prerequisites: Recommended: at least one WGSS course. Pre: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: DS Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society. A-F only. (Fall only) (Crosslisted as SUST 367 and WGSS 367)
prerequisites: Pre: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Law, Politics and Society
description: DS Relationships between law, politics, and society will be explored. Emphasis is placed on several dimensions of legality: legal “indeterminacy” and some of the many things that law does for us and to us; law’s response to violence; the connections between law and social change; access to the law and its sociological dimensions; how/why law fails and what happens when it does. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 374)
prerequisites: Pre: 100 or any 200 level SOC course, or a 100 level or 200 level POLS course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 394)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. Consent of instructor.

subject: SOC
title: Food, Body, and Women: Analysis of Biopolitics
description: DS Explores how food, body, and other “matter of life” are imbedded in biopolitics from the feminist perspectives. A-F only. (Spring only).
prerequisites: Pre: WGSS 300, or one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Urban Sociology
description: DS Urbanization in developed and developing countries, the rural-urban continuum, structure and process of metropolitan regions, theories of urban location and growth, housing and urban renewal.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Social Stratification
description: DS Approaches to research in social inequality: community studies; historical and cross-cultural analyses of poverty, working class, middle class, power structure, social mobility, etc.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Population and Society
description: DS Global and U.S. patterns of population growth; composition and distribution, elementary demographic techniques; development issues and population policy.

subject: SOC
title: Economy and Society
description: DS Study of the dominant trend of economic change and its impact on society; globalization of economic activities and transformation of industrial society to postindustrial one; corporate restructuring and downsizing and their impact on employment and income distribution; gender relations in workplaces; the impact of globalization on the newly industrializing countries.

subject: SOC
title: Technology and Society
description: DS Nature of technology, social forces that affect its adoption; impact on society; innovation.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Work
description: DS Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global. (Cross-listed as ES 418 and WGSS 418)
prerequisites: Pre: 300, or one 300-level WGSS or ES course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Organizations and Society
description: DS Schools, hospitals, industries, prisons, and government agencies analyzed in terms of self-actualization, alienation, human relations, communication, leadership, organizational conflicts.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Criminology & Juvenile Delinquency
description: DS Research in systematic social deviation. Scaling and measurement of delinquents/ criminals, official data, gangs, identification and measurement of delinquent/criminal value orientations, etc. DS

subject: SOC
title: Punishment & Society
description: DS Institutions, organizations, and individuals charged with carrying out punishment in the criminal justice system and beyond. DS

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Law and Social Change
description: DS Interrelationships between legal orders and other social institutions; use of “law” to change major status relationships, e.g., boss-worker, woman-man, child-adult.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Crime
description: DS Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system. (Cross-listed as WGSS 435)
prerequisites: Recommended: at least one WGSS course. Pre: 300, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Prisons
description: Prisons, jails, and other detention facilities across historical, social, and/or international contexts.

subject: SOC
title: Social Structure and the Individual
description: DS Effects of social institutions on individuals. Role of socioeconomic status, cultural background, family structure, peer group, schools, and occupational roles in socialization.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Gender Violence
description: DS Historical and structural theories of gender-based violence, including domestic and sexual abuse, prostitution, trafficking, cross-cultural perspectives, social policy and practices. (Once a year)
prerequisites: Junior standing or graduate standing only. Pre: 300 or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
description: DS Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives. (Cross-listed as WGSS 446)
prerequisites: Pre: 300, WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Marriage and the Family
description: DS Theory and methods of studying social interaction in marriage and the family; examination of marriage, mating, love, and choice. Empirical research emphasizing Hawai‘i.

subject: SOC
title: Marriage and Family: A Feminist Perspective
description: DS Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. (Cross-listed as WGSS 452)
prerequisites: Recommended: at least one WGSS course. Pre: 300, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sociology of Aging
description: DS Social and research issues significant to delivery of long-term care services to the elderly; cost, quality, availability of services, evaluation of programs, role of family, formal and informal care services.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Medical Sociology
description: DS Application of sociological theories and concepts to medical social situations and behavior; problems of obtaining data for research.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Religion
description: DS Seminar in research on sociological aspects of religious sectarianism; attention to Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as REL 452)

subject: SOC
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
description: DS The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as ES 456)
prerequisites: Pre: 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Arts
description: DS Relation of art to society; role of artist, audience, critic, patron, museum; Western and other societies; attitudes toward new styles.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sports and Society
description: DS Critical perspectives on sports and society. Topics include power and inequality; mobility, status, and economics; youth development; globalization; gender; and violence in sports and the wider society. (Spring only)

subject: SOC
title: Popular Culture
description: DS Popular culture as manifested in film, sports, TV, comics, magazines,

subject: SNSK
title: Introduction to Sanskrit II
description:
HSL
Continuation of 101.

subject: SNSK
title: Intermediate Sanskrit I
description:
HSL
Continuation of 102. Reading and analysis of classical texts with review of grammar.

subject: SNSK
title: Intermediate Sanskrit II
description:
HSL
Continuation of 201.

subject: SNSK
title: Third-Level Sanskrit
description: Continuation of 282. Reading and analysis of various classical texts.

subject: SNSK
title: Third-Level Sanskrit
description: Continuation of 381. Introduction to Veda.

subject: SNSK
title: Fourth-Level Sanskrit
description: Continuation of 382. Reading, analysis, and interpretation of various Vedic or Sanskrit texts selected according to students’ interests.

subject: SNSK
title: Fourth-Level Sanskrit
description: Continuation of 481.

subject: SNSK
title: Advanced Readings in Sanskrit
description: Advanced study of Sanskrit literature (kâvya) and systematic thought (sâstra), alongside reading and discussion of scholarship on these topics. Specific content will change each semester. Repeatable unlimited times for different topics.
prerequisites: intermediate-level SNSK (or equivalent). Contact instructor with questions.

subject: STE
title: Introduction to Teaching, Elementary
description: Standards-based planning, assessment, instruction, reflection; inclusive classroom management; unique multicultural environment; issues in education and curriculum. Developing knowledgeable, effective, caring professionals to support student’s academic, social, emotional, physical needs. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Principles and Methods of Reading Instruction
description: First of two methods courses focusing on theories and research-based practices related to reading instruction in elementary classrooms. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Principles and Methods of Writing Instruction
description: Second of two methods courses focusing on theories and research-based practices related to writing instruction in elementary classrooms. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Field Training – Blended ECE
description: Students spend 15 hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled classes; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SPED 315)

subject: STE
title: Field Experience
description: Supervised field experience in schools. Minimum of 8 hours per week in conjunction with professional education courses. Repeatable two times, up to three credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Field Experience
description: Supervised field experience in schools. Minimum of 2 full days per week in classrooms, plus mandatory seminar scheduled by UH Mānoa field supervisor. Taken in conjunction with professional education courses; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. Repeatable two times or up to 9 credits per alpha. CR/NC only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Child Development from Prenatal Through Age Eight
description: Growth and development of children from prenatal through age eight. Historical and current issues through a research-based ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on children’s optimal development and how this informs teaching practices in early education. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Children’s Literature
description:
DL
Acquaintance with wide range of children’s books; criteria for evaluation of literature; using literature in the classroom.

subject: STE
title: Instructional and Assessment Methods for Multilingual Learners
description: Introduction to language use and development as it relates to multilingual learners (MLL). Candidates analyze and apply strategies to create inclusive and collaborative classrooms for learners at various levels of English language development. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Social Studies and Science in Early Childhood Education
description: Assessment, instructional methods, and materials for teaching social studies and science to children in preschool through grade 3. Emphasis on developmentally appropriate practices and lesson planning for teaching social studies and science. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)
prerequisites: STE 417, and STE 315 (or concurrent) or SPED 315 (or concurrent)

subject: STE
title: Social Studies, Elementary
description: Purposes, methods, curriculum, and assessment in teaching social studies. Focus: enriching children’s understanding of the communities of which they are a part through inquiry, investigation, collaboration, and expository skills. Emphasis on writing instruction; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Science, Elementary
description: Science education in elementary school; methods and materials; laboratory activities selected from new science curricula; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. Each alpha repeatable one time, up to 3 credits. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Mathematics, Elementary
description: Inquiry-based approach to concepts and algorithms of whole numbers and introduction to geometry/ measurement. Laboratory experiences with appropriate manipulatives; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Mathematics, Elementary II
description: Inquiry-based approach to concepts and algorithms of fractions, decimals, graphing, and probability and statistics. Laboratory experiences with appropriate manipulatives; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
prerequisites: STE 324B or consent for (B); STE 324C or consent for (C)
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Visual Art, Elementary
description: Scope and organization of art in pK-6 school curriculum, creative use of art media through laboratory experience; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Curriculum, Materials, and Assessment Development for Multilingual Learners
description: Introduction to the development of curriculum materials, and assessments for diverse and multilingual learners. Teacher candidates will develop their ability to organize, develop, and assess learning around standards-based subject matter and language learning objectives. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Responsive Pedagogy for Multilingual Learners
description: Introduction to the teaching of multilingual learners (MLL) in an elementary school context. Teacher candidates will learn specific strategies and methods for teaching non-native speakers of English. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Performing Arts Expression, K-6
description: Standards-based teaching, with, in, through, and about music, dance, and drama. Developing verbal and non-verbal communication skills through creative expression with an emphasis on planning, teaching, and assessing preK-6 lessons that integrate the performing arts; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Personal and Social K-6 Health Skills
description: Standards-based planning, teaching, assessment in health education. Developing interactive learning opportunities to teach personal and social responsibility for health through curriculum integration. Training, practice and evaluation of oral communication skills; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. A-F only.
degrees: Dual Preparation in ECE and Elementary Education

subject: STE
title: Methods of Instruction, Industrial/ Agricultural Education
description: Techniques of individual and group instruction in laboratory and related classes, evaluation of various methods.

subject: STE
title: Management of Industrial/Agricultural Facilities
description: Organization of instruction; handling supplies; maintaining equipment and tools; purchasing materials; keeping records; making inventories.

subject: STE
title: Teaching Business and Office Education
description: Theory and methods of teaching business and office education courses.
prerequisites: ACC 201 and either ACC 200 or ACC 202

subject: STE
title: Teaching Marketing and Distribution
description: Theory and methods of teaching marketing and distribution courses.

subject: STE
title: Music in the Elementary School
description: Goals, concepts, literature, materials, procedures, and evaluation for teaching music in grades K–6. For students in elementary education. Not intended for elementary music majors.

subject: STE
title: Multicultural Perspectives in Education
description:
DS
Concepts and methods to develop sensitivity and awareness of cultural influences on behaviors related to schooling. Examines intersections of Native Hawaiian culture with Asian and/or Pacific Islanders fostering multicultural respect and understanding through cross-cultural analysis. A-F only. DS

subject: STE
title: Home Economics Education
description: Curriculum design. Current educational philosophies and practices in home economics education. Teaching materials and techniques.

subject: STE
title: Managing Classrooms
description: Analysis of the factors that contribute to learning in the classroom and the development of teacher behaviors that promote such learning. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Student Teaching
description: Full-time supervised experience in school. (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary; (D) secondary; (M) dual preparation in elementary education and multilingual learning; (S) dual preparation in elementary and special education. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: completion of all other program requirements, passing Praxis II exam(s). Co-requisite for (D): STE 391D.
degrees: Dual preparation in ECE and elementary education
Dual preparation in elementary education and multilingual learning
Dual preparation in elementary and special education

subject: STE
title: Seminar for Student Teaching
description: With student teaching as context, examination of knowledge, skills, and dispositions for teaching

subject: SPED
title: Young Children with Communication Needs
description: Communication development of infants and young children, ages birth through age 8, with and without disabilities. Assessment and intervention to support the development of communication skills in inclusive community and school environments. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Student Teaching in Special Education (Alpha)
description: Full-time supervised experience in school. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one per alpha. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar for Student Teachers in Special Education (Alpha)
description: Seminar relating current educational theories with experiences. (B) elementary/ special education; (C) early childhood education/ special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: requirements for registration listed under “student teaching.” Co-requisite: 390B for (B); 390C for (C); 390D for (D).

subject: SPED
title: Student Teaching in Special Education Modified
description: Modified student teaching for students from another institution completing student teaching at UH or for students who have prior extensive teaching experience. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: requirements for registration listed under “Student Teaching,” approval of review committee and consent.

subject: SPED
title: Field Training in Special Education (Alpha)
description: Students participate in classroom settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by department field supervisor; (B) first semester; (C) second semester, with ethical issues in education discussed and applied in field settings; (D) third semester, with emphasis on writing and oral communication for application in field settings. SPED majors only. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.
prerequisites: Pre: 304 (or concurrent) or consent for (B); 400B for (C); 400C for (D).

subject: SPED
title: Writing for Educational Professionals
description: Instruction on learning to write as professional educators. Strategies for developing and enhancing professional writing for the field of education. Peer and instructor feedback on writing throughout course. Technologies used to assist with writing. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Individuals with Severe Disabilities/ Autism
description: Etiology, characteristics, and development of individuals with severe disabilities and autism; historical, theoretical, and legal issues affecting individuals with severe disabilities and autism; multicultural, family, and consumer issues; professional and ethical issues in providing services. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Education of Gifted Students
description: Characteristics and educational provisions for gifted children and youth with particular attention to psychological aspects of creativity

subject: SPED
title: Education Program for the Gifted/ Talented
description: Utilization and evaluation of teaching/ learning models for gifted/talented students, including consideration of roles, expectancies for learning, and organizational procedures.

subject: SPED
title: Strategies for Reading Difficulties (Alpha)
description: Overview of methods, programs, and strategies for reading instruction designed to improve the performance of elementary students, grades K-6, who experience difficulties in reading acquisition, fluency, and comprehension. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Vocabulary Comprehension, Fluency & Writing Interventions for Students with Disabilities
description: Development of and intervention for fluent reading vocabulary acquisition, comprehension and writing in students with disabilities. Explicit and systematic instruction of core aspects of reading and writing. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: SPED
title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals (Alpha)
description: Knowledge and skills for relating effectively with families and professionals on behalf of the children and youth with and without disabilities. Coverage of the context in which family members and school personnel interact. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one time per alpha. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Elementary
description: Teaching elementary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SPED
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction. Collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Special Education
description: Study of issues, trends, and research into special education programming and service delivery. Repeatable two times.

subject: SPED
title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers including criteria for evaluation and planning. A-F only. (Cross-listed as EDCS 451)
prerequisites: Pre: HDFS 230 (or concurrent) and HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Preschool Children–Special Needs
description: Examination of application of current research and practices for serving preschool children with special needs.

subject: SPED
title: Physical and Medical Needs-Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Learning to teach children with physical and health impairments, with a focus on developing independence. Instructional and assistive strategies for meeting the student’s physical and medical needs as well as managing medical conditions. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: SPED
title: Non-School-Age Individuals with Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Effective planning, instruction, and support for non-school-age individuals (infants, toddlers, and adults) with severe disabilities or ASD across natural environments. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: SPED
title: Secondary Transition-Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for postsecondary education, employment, and community living. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Assessment and Instruction-Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Assessment methods and tools, instructional and assistive strategies, and special procedures to support the participation of students with severe disabilities and autism in inclusive settings. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: SPED
title: Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities (Alpha)
description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Stress on program development to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities into general education environment. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood elementary/special education; (D) unclassified; (E) secondary. BEd in SPED majors only for (E). A-F only. (Spring only for (E))

subject: SPED
title: Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Severe Disabilities/ Autism (Alpha)
description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with severe disabilities/autism. Focus on program development to facilitate the inclusion of students with disabilities into general education settings. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education, emphasis on writing instruction in teaching special education; (D) unclassified. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Inclusive Practices Across the Curriculum-Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Strategies for teaching science, math, and social studies to students with mild/moderate disabilities in secondary settings; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, and curriculum development. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: SPED
title: Assistant-Level Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis at the assistant level supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings. Repeatable nine times, up to 20 credits. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Instructional and Assistive Technology (Alpha)
description: Addresses instructional and assistive technologies for special education and general education settings; technology-based instructional strategies that support inclusion and address academic and behavioral objectives; and application of Universal Design for Learning to support access to the general curriculum for diverse students in the PreK-12 classroom setting. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one time per alpha; repeatable up to six credits for (B). A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Classroom Organization and Management (Alpha)
description: Knowledge and skills related to basic organizational management of an inclusive classroom.

subject: OCN
title: Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction, and global climate change. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Minerals
description: Distribution, origin, processes of formation. Sulfides, oxides, and placer minerals. Comparative studies of continental ore bodies. Submarine rift, subduction, and abduction.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Methods in Oceanography
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Current methods of analysis used in the ocean sciences, both in the field and in the laboratory. An ocean-going field trip provides students with hands-on training in sample collection and processing. The latter is followed by laboratory analyses of the collected samples throughout the remainder of the semester.
prerequisites: BIOL 171 and CHEM 161 and ERTH 101; or consent
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Chemistry
description: Chemical reactions support lie and stabilize Earth’s climate. We explore marine and fresh waters through chemical dquilibrium and reaction kinetics. Topics include mineral stability, ocean acidification, complexation/bioavailability, pollution, and quantitative approximation of natural systems. (Alt. years: spring)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Microbial Geochemistry
description: The synergy between the biogeochemistry of element cycling and the microbial organisms involved, interfacing across disciplines from the perspective of a practical blend of aquatic chemistry, microbiology, biogeochemistry, and molecular biology. (Alt years: fall)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Earth System Science and Global Change
description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmosphere-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ERTH 638)
prerequisites: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Observational Physical Oceanography
description: Application of the scientific method; physical regimes in the ocean; ocean processes and observational strategies; resolution, sampling, array design and observing systems; models and data assimilation; major field programs; operational oceanography and climate prediction.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ERTH 641) F
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Elemental Composition Changes
description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles. (Cross-listed as ERTH 642)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Marine Geochemistry
description: Seminar on a broad topic; discussion and critique of research papers. Repeatable one time.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions. (Cross-listed as ERTH 644)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Math Techniques for Oceanographers
description: (3 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Introduction to numerical methods, data analysis, error propagation, box models, linear and nonlinear least squares, perturbation theory, numerical integration.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Methods in Microbiology Oceanography
description: (1 8-hr Lab) Modern methods for sampling microbial populations from the sea and for quantifying biomass and in siturates of metabolism. Integrated field projects, theme varies. OCN majors only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Waves I
description: Survey of wave types-acoustic, capillary, gravity, inertial, vorticity. Basic wave concepts emphasized: phase and group velocities, standing waves, energy conservation, dispersion, refraction, diffraction. Rotation and boundary effects are covered: reflection, basin modes, trapping, tides.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Waves II
description: Baroclinic gravity waves, inertial waves, mid-latitude Rossby waves, topographic waves, equatorial waves.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Marine Hydrodynamics
description: Introduction to classical hydrodynamics and continuum mechanics. Techniques for solution of Navier Stokes equations on various scales of oceanic motion; potential theory, dynamic modeling, and viscous and rotational processes.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Satellite Oceanography
description: Techniques of satellite observations of the ocean, including temperature, pigment concentration, currents, and winds; analysis of a satellite data set as term project. A-F only. OCN majors only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Oceanographic Instrumentation and Technology
description: Measurement techniques in physical oceanography, including pressure, temperature, salinity, oxygen, optical sensors, current meters, navigation systems, ocean acoustics, and mooring structures. Includes a laboratory research project. A-F only. OCN majors only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ATMO 665)
prerequisites: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either 620 or ATMO 600, or consent
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Nino/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ATMO 666)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics I
description: Basic concepts and equations to describe large-scale ocean circulation; numerical models; boundary layers; models of wind-driven circulation of a homogeneous ocean.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics II
description: Thermodynamics of stratified fluids; convection; mixing; models of the thermohaline circulation; the role of eddies in the large-scale ocean circulation.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Paleoceanography
description: Study of the paloeceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere, and biosphere. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ERTH 674)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
description: Combined lecture/discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: previous course in marine science, or consent
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
description: Introduction to modeling biological and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on biological production. Students will learn biological-physical dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming. (Alt. years)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research. (Cross-listed as MBIO 612)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Statistics in R
description: (2 hr Lec, 1 hr Lab) In-depth introduction to the modern statistical methods necessary for analyzing biological/ecological data, including GLMs, GAMs, mixed models, ordination, etc. Students will learn how to perform these methods in R.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Directed Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Biological Oceanography
description: Seminar. Literature and concepts in one of several active fields considered in detail. Repeatable three times, credits earned up to 12 credits.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Physical Oceanography
description: Near-shore processes, advanced mathematical techniques, recent developments, etc. Typically given by visiting professors in their specialties, or in response to student interest. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Seminar in Chemical Oceanography
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Seminar
description: Oceanographic topics of current interest. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Proposal Development
description: Introduction to the organization and functioning of oceanography funding agencies, the peer-review process, and the design and development of a research proposal. Repeatable one time. OCN majors only. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: two of the following: 621, 626, 627 (or concurrent), or 628 (or concurrent); or consent
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: OCN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SPED
title: Instructional and Assistive Technology
description: Addresses instructional and assistive technologies for special education and general education settings; technology-based instructional strategies that support inclusion and address academic and behavioral objectives; and application of Universal Design for Learning to support access to the general curriculum for diverse students in the PreK-12 classroom setting. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable one time per alpha; repeatable up to six credits for (B). A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Classroom Organization and Management
description: Knowledge and skills related to basic organizational management of an inclusive classroom, including scheduling, grouping, and stress and time management; techniques of applied behavior management, emphasizing behavior change and practical implementation of learning principles. (B) elementary/special education, V credits; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified. Repeatable up to six credits for (B). A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Theoretical Basis for Teaching Special-Needs Students
description: Survey of biophysical, behavioral, social/ecological, psychodynamic/ psychoeducational, cognitive/developmental, counter-theoretical approaches to teaching exceptional students. Opportunity for the development and/ or strengthening of one’s own theoretical frame of reference.

subject: SPED
title: Characteristics/Strategies for Teaching At-Risk Students
