description: Survey of educational, behavioral, and emotional characteristics of students who are at-risk for school failure and strategies to work with such students. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Intensive Behavioral Interventions
description: Principles of behavior, emphasizing positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems and improving behavior and learning for students with severe disabilities and autism. BEd in SPED majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
degrees: Bachelor of Education in Special Education

subject: SPED
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading, research, and/or projects under direct supervision of instructors. Repeatable nine times.
prerequisites: Consent of instructor or department chair

subject: SPED
title: Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education Program Seminar
description: Mandatory program seminar for Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education (PBSPED) teacher candidates; access to tools and skills necessary for distance education program success; Introduction to the Special Education teaching profession. Post-Bac in SPED majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: SPED
title: Field Experience in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate
description: Students spend between 100-135 hours over a semester in settings appropriate to SPED-PCert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by participating teacher and/or college supervisor. Repeatable one time, up to 6 credits. Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Student Teaching in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate Programs
description: Supervised student teaching with a master teacher in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert emphasis (mildmoderate, severe/autism); minimum 280 hours in minimum 11 weeks. Supervision by master teacher and university supervisor. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Internship in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate Programs
description: Supervised teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by master teacher/university mentor, and university supervisor. Must enroll for two consecutive semesters. Repeatable two times, up to 14 credits. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Practicum in Special Education
description: For in-service school/community personnel to present new ideas, approaches, instructional methods, materials for teaching exceptional individuals. (B–E) general SPED; (F–G) secondary programming/ SPED; (H–I) bilingual/multicultural/special needs; (J–K) severe disabilities; (M–N) early childhood/ special needs; (O–P) career/vocational/special needs; (Q–R) computer/special needs; (S–T) arts/special needs; (U–W) computer training/special needs; (X–Y) consultant skills/special needs; (Z) Ho‘okoho. Repeatable nine times. CR/NC only.

subject: SPED
title: Practicum in Special Education
description: For in-service school/community personnel to present new ideas, approaches, instructional methods, materials for teaching exceptional individuals. (B–E) general SPED; (F–G) secondary programming/SPED; (H–I) bilingual/multicultural/special needs; (J–K) needs; (Q–R) computer/special needs; (S–T) arts/ special needs; (U–W) computer training/special needs; (X–Y) consultant skills/special needs; (Z) Ho‘okoho. Repeatable nine times. CR/NC only.

subject: SPED
title: Practicum in Special Education
description: For in-service school/community personnel to present new ideas, approaches, instructional methods, materials for teaching exceptional individuals. (B–E) general SPED; (F–G) secondary programming/ SPED; (H–I) bilingual/multicultural/special needs; (J–K) severe disabilities; (M–N) early childhood/ special needs; (O–P) career/vocational/special needs; (Q–R) computer/special needs; (S–T) arts/special needs; (U–W) computer training/special needs; (X–Y) consultant skills/special needs; (Z) Ho‘okoho. Repeatable eight times. CR/NC only.

subject: SPED
title: Internship, Special Education
description: Supervised field activities involving the programming and instruction of special-needs students within training programs in Hawai‘i and the Pacific Basin.

subject: SPED
title: Foundations of Exceptionality
description: Theoretical, legal and multicultural foundations for assessing, teaching and developing individual service plans across the lifespan for persons with disabilities. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Instructional/Assistive Technology and Universal Design for Learning
description: Strategies for using instructional and assistive technology, digital tools and media, and Universal Design for Learning to support learning needs of students with disabilities and other diverse learners in the K-12 classroom.

subject: SPED
title: Special Education Law and Compliance
description: Examination of the federal, state, and local government roles in special education with special emphasis on case and regulatory law. Focus on understanding special education law necessary in providing services to students with disabilities in a variety of placements. Appropriate for special/general education teachers, administrators, or related service providers.

subject: SPED
title: Principles of Behavior
description: Principles and laws governing behavior and methods that can be used to accomplish educationally relevant changes in student performance. Emphasis on the conceptual basis for changing behavior and use of technologies for changing behavior in school and community settings. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Collaboration in School and Community Settings
description: Collaboration skills necessary to function as team members and to ensure the success of students with disabilities in inclusive school and community settings. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Language Development for Deaf Children
description: General theories of first and second language development applied to development of ASL and English in deaf children. Relationship of theory to educational practice. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Admission into Deaf Education program or consent

subject: SPED
title: Audiology and Spoken English for Deaf Students
description: Developmental principles of audiology and speech (i.e., spoken English) will be used to examine assessment procedures and intervention strategies appropriate to deaf students in a variety of educational placements. Classroom applications will be presented. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Admission into Deaf Education program or consent

subject: SPED
title: Literacy Development for Deaf Students
description: Basic concepts related to language, language development and recognition of language-related learning problems of deaf students; strategies for teaching reading and writing to deaf students. Repeatable one times. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Bilingual Deaf Education
description: Study of issues, trends and methods in ASL/ English bilingual education for deaf students. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: SPED 606, SPED 607 and SPED 608; or consent

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development–Deaf
description: Assessment methods and techniques used with deaf students that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming through planning and providing cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Methods and Strategies for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Techniques for providing effective instruction including: best instructional practice, lesson planning, teacher-directed and student-mediated instructional strategies, and curricular approaches for working with students with mild/moderate disabilities. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Education of Exceptional Children in Regular Classroom
description: Practices that facilitate teaching special needs students in regular classrooms. Techniques for meeting academic needs, managing behavior, motivating students, increasing peer interactions, communication between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms, Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education. (Cross-listed as EDCS 480)

subject: STE
title: Directed Activity
description: Individual work supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, teaching, and/or projects.

subject: STE
title: Common Core State Standards in ELA: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of ELA content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the ELA practices of the Common Core State Standards. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: STE
title: Common Core State Standards in Mathematics: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of mathematics content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the mathematical practices of the Common Core State Standards. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Curriculum Development: Natural Science
description: For in-service teachers to upgrade subject matter and develop teaching methods and materials for instruction. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Curriculum Development: Natural Science
description: For in-service teachers to upgrade subject matter and develop teaching methods and materials for instruction. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: STE
title: Master of Education in Teaching Program Seminar
description: Mandatory program seminar for Master of Education in Teaching (MEdT) teacher candidates; access to tools and skills necessary for distance education program success, introduction to the teaching profession. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: admission into the MEdT program, or consent.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Professional Studies I
description: Development of theoretical and practical knowledge base and skills for understanding, analyzing, and responding to teaching issues and problems. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Clinical Partnership and Practice I
description: Supervised field study of a school. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to 12 credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Professional Studies II
description: Development of pedagogical skills in planning and implementing instruction for target subject area/grade level. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Clinical Partnership and Practice II
description: Team collaboration on responding to identified school need; supervised experience in mini-teaching. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to 12 credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Clinical Partnership and Practice III
description: Supervised experience in instructional planning and practice teaching. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Professional Studies III
description: Planning and methods seminar in conjunction with practice teaching. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Clinical Partnership and Practice IV
description: Full-time supervised teaching experience. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Professional Studies IV
description: Collaborative problem solving of issues and concerns encountered in current teaching experiences. (B) licensure; (C) non-licensure. Each alpha is repeatable one time, up to six credits. A-F only.

subject: STE
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: SLS
title: Introduction to Pidgin in Hawai‘i
description: Introduction to contemporary Pidgin in Hawai‘i, in relation to the role of Hawaiian and Languages of the Asia-Pacific region; language rights; sociolinguistics of Pidgin and Hawaiian in institutional, educational, and interpersonal contexts.

subject: SLS
title: Learning Languages and Communicating Interculturally in a Global Multilingual World
description: Historical/global perspective on being/becoming multilingual/multicultural, encompassing cases of second language learning, teaching, use, growth, change, loss across the world, ancient times to present, supporting individuals’ motivations and abilities concerning second languages and cultures.

subject: SLS
title: Language by the Numbers
description: Understanding quantitative information and analyses related to language and language learning/multilingualism. Topics include data description and visualization, basic statistics, and evaluating quantitative analyses. A-F only.

subject: SLS
title: Introduction to Second Language Learning and Technology
description: Introduction to the use of technology in second language learning; pros and cons of specific new applications and established technologies; project-based and oriented; developing multilingual/ multicultural understanding through technology. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SLS
title: Topics in Learning and Using Second Languages
description: Reviews practices of second language learning, use, and maintenance. Introductory exploration and analysis of selected topics with a specific theme indicated by course title listed in the class schedule. Repeatable one time for different topics, up to six credits with consent.

subject: SLS
title: Bilingualism: Cognition and Culture
description: Introduction to bi-/multilingualism as a phenomenon at the level of society and as a characteristic of individual speakers; discussion of recent media reports and popular myths about bilingualism in relation to research-based evidence.

subject: SLS
title: Basic Language Concepts for Second Language Learning, Teaching, and Use
description: Introduction to language structure and function in the domains of sound, words, sentences, and discourse, with specific focus on description, analysis, and research into learner language.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Learning
description: Theoretical foundations for the learning and teaching of second/ foreign languages. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Teaching
description: Survey of methodology; basic concepts and practices; emphasis on teaching second languages through oral instruction.

subject: SLS
title: Sociolinguistics of Multilingualism
description: Explores themes in sociolinguistics relevant to L2/ multilingual contexts, including language ideology, language variation, language and culture, and language and identity; how L2 users and multilingual people grapple with these issues. Includes emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Testing
description: Measurement and evaluation of achievement and proficiency in second language learning.
prerequisites: SLS 302 or SLS 303 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: SLS
title: Techniques in Second Language Teaching: Reading and Writing
description: Methods and materials. Issues in teaching; survey of available materials and practice in their adaptation. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

subject: SLS
title: Techniques in Second Language Teaching: Listening and Speaking
description: Methods and materials. Issues in teaching; survey of available materials and practice in their adaptation. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

subject: SLS
title: Multilingual Education
description: Survey and analysis of current thinking and practices in multilingual and multicultural education, including bilingual education; special emphasis on ESL/EFL. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SLS
title: Instructional Media
description: Theoretical foundation and practical applications of using electronic and audiovisual media in second language teaching.
prerequisites: SLS 303 (with minimum grade of C), or SLS 600 (with minimum grade of B or concurrent); or consent.

subject: SLS
title: Pidgin and Creole English in Hawai‘i
description: Major historical descriptive, pedagogical aspects; pidgin and creole languages, linguistic change, language variation. Work with actual language data. Laboratory work required.

subject: SLS
title: Learning and Teaching World Languages
description: Hybrid technology intensive course for pre- or in-service teachers of world languages. Topics: online learning, curriculum and lesson planning,

subject: SW
title: Community and Public Health Practice
description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery. (Cross-listed as PH 671)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: Current trends in field of social welfare. Recent courses have focused on forensic social work, immigrants and refugees, and leadership in human services. Meets seminar requirement. Repeatable one time in different topics.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Marriage and Family Therapy
description: Introduction to couple and family therapy offers an overview of family systems perspective, theory and technique relevant to informing effective social work case planning, case management, advocacy, and interaction with clients.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Generalist Field Education I
description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice. A-F only.
prerequisites: SW 606 (or concurrent)(with a minimum grade of C).
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Generalist Field Education II
description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice. A-F only.
prerequisites: SW 690 and SW 607 (or concurrent) and SW 631 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of C).
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Health and Aging
description: Biological and physiological changes associated with aging. Social and psychological factors associated with health maintenance. Major threats to health, changing patterns of morbidity and mortality of the aged.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Students, on the basis of special interest, select a faculty member to work with on a problem for which planned individualized study or research is deemed advisable. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Thesis Research
description: Independent research under supervision of a thesis committee. Includes formal proposal and defense of finished research. Repeatable unlimited times.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Methods of Group Psychotherapy
description: Designed specifically to train students in the theory and practice of leading psychotherapy groups; it includes historical developments, research, theories, and application of group psychotherapy, group techniques and exercises.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Therapeutic Strategies with the Older Adult
description: Focuses on interdisciplinary strategies with older adults: individual, family, and group therapy; eclectic mental health approaches; case management; and environmental intervention. Emphasis placed on the use of these strategies as preventive, as well as supportive, measures for the well, transition, and frail elderly. Meets seminar requirement.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Children and Families
description: Advanced practice course for students specializing in social work with children and families. Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of both theoretical formulations and therapeutic techniques for practice in the field of family and child welfare. Emphasis placed on the development of specialized knowledge and skills for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of a variety of common child and family practice situations.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice with Children and Families
description: Designed for students in the child and family concentration and builds upon past knowledge and skill development in practice classes and in the practicum. Students integrate, demonstrate, and extend earlier learning, acquire new knowledge, and learn and practice new skills. Organized around student case presentations in a consultation format. Meets seminar requirement.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Health Care
description: Didactic and experiential learning activity focuses on the major role functions of the social worker in the health field including assessment, contracting, counseling, advocacy, case management, discharge planning, family group work, community and team building. Covers health care policy, research directions in practice and social work management issues.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Health Care
description: Through the use of case studies developed by the students, social work practice is examined in three areas of health care: primary care provided in health departments and medical groups, hospital-based services, and long-term care. Meets seminar requirement.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Mental Health
description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings. Focused on engagement and assessment while emphasizing cultural, person in environment, and strengths-based approaches.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Mental Health
description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings, with a focus on history and policy in the U.S. and Hawai‘i, as well as culturally-grounded and evidence-based practice.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Older Adults
description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of theoretical formulations and intervention strategies for working with older adults and their families. Emphasis on diversity/justice.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work with Older Adults
description: Designed for gerontology specialization students to gain advanced knowledge for working with diverse older adults and their families. Emphasis on strength perspectives on aging.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Policy Analysis
description: Students pursue in-depth a specific topic in the areas of social planning, social policy analysis, evaluation of social programs, administration, supervision, and consultation. Selectively a comparative perspective is introduced and case studies used to illustrate concepts, principles, and techniques, with implications for practice. Meets seminar requirement.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work and the Law
description: Knowledge of judicial systems and law relevant to social work practice in corrections, child-family welfare, health, and mental health. Skills for effective participation in the legal process are acquired in moot court and in practice for testifying.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Review of Research in Social Work
description: In-depth study of research in a substantive area. Each seminar will be devoted to a particular topic: e.g., foster care of children, effectiveness of social work intervention, etc.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project— Plan B
description: Independent research (group of two to seven students or by an individual student) undertaken under the sponsorship of a faculty advisor. Elements are selection of a topic related to the practice of social work or knowledge relevant to that practice, utilization of empirical research methodology in collecting and analyzing original data, and preparation of a scholarly paper. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project– Plan B
description: Same as SW 743. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project– Plan B
description: Same as SW 743. A-F only
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Analysis and Development of Knowledge for Social Work
description: Focuses on developing an understanding of philosophy of science, theory development, social work epistemology, and the analysis and development of knowledge for social work practice. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Quantitative Methods II
description: Empirical research methodology with emphasis on design principles and measurement theory; design and measurement issues and problems in cross-cultural research. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Qualitative Research: Philosophical, Methodological and Analytic Approaches
description: Theories and methods of qualitative research; problem formulation, informant selection, study design, data collection and analysis utilizing qualitative approaches. Repeatable three times. A-F only.
prerequisites: SW 640 or SW 651 or equivalent; departmental approval.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Dissertation Seminar
description: Culminating experience in social welfare doctoral specialization; integration of PhD core and specialization course work.
prerequisites: classified student in PhD in social welfare program or consent.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Seminar in International Social Work
description: Approaches to social problems and trends in the profession in international, cross-cultural perspectives. Emphasis on developmental aspects of social work. Political, economic, social, and cultural forces shaping social welfare in national development. Meets seminar requirement.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Hawaiian culture, past and present. Explores and examines possible approaches to working with Hawaiians and part-Hawaiians. Special emphasis on supports in the Hawaiian system that may promote maximal functioning
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SLS
title: Multilingual Education
description: DS. Survey and analysis of current thinking and practices in multilingual and multicultural education, including bilingual education; special emphasis on ESL/EFL. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SLS
title: Instructional Media
description: Theoretical foundation and practical applications of using electronic and audiovisual media in second language teaching.
prerequisites: 303 (with minimum grade of C), or 600 (with minimum grade of B or concurrent); or consent.

subject: SLS
title: Pidgin and Creole English in Hawai‘i
description: DS. Major historical descriptive, pedagogical aspects; pidgin and creole languages, linguistic change, language variation. Work with actual language data. Laboratory work required.

subject: SLS
title: Learning and Teaching World Languages
description: Hybrid technology intensive course for pre- or in-service teachers of world languages. Topics: online learning, curriculum and lesson planning, assessment, language teaching approaches, technology for learning world languages. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as LLEA 455)

subject: SLS
title: English Phonology
description: DH. Introduction to English phonetics and phonology. Includes an emphasis on the oral presentation of key phonological concepts and provides experience in English pronunciation tutoring.

subject: SLS
title: Practicum for Future Language Professionals
description: Students observe and assist mentor teachers (minimum of 40 hours) at cooperating schools in multilingual contexts, examining the intersection of theory and practice in language learning and teaching and applying knowledge from other SLS courses. A-F only.

subject: SLS
title: Topics in Second Language Studies
description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research; (U) second language use. Repeatable three times in different topics. Not applicable toward graduate degrees offered within SLS.

subject: SLS
title: Professionalism in SLS
description: Capstone for SLS majors. Reflection on experiences via the major, articulation of professional values, exploration of diverse approaches to professionalism in SLS, and formal compilation of a professional portfolio. SLS majors only. Senior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: SLS
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: For interdisciplinary studies majors. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major, or consent of department chair.

subject: SLS
title: Introduction to Second Language Studies
description: Introduction to basic professional and research issues in second language studies; integration of theory, research, and practice for prospective second or foreign language teachers and researchers. (Fall only)

subject: SLS
title: Language Concepts for Second Language Learning and Teaching
description: Language analysis— phonology, syntax, semantics, discourse for teaching second languages.

subject: SLS
title: Introduction to Teaching Second Languages
description: Survey and analysis of second language teaching traditions and perspectives.

subject: SLS
title: Introduction to Second Language Assessment
description: Assessment of second language knowledge and skills. Topics include design, use, and analysis of assessments. Graduate standing only or consent.

subject: SLS
title: Alternative Approaches to Second Language Teaching
description: Examination, comparison with conventional approaches; interpersonal relationships in language teaching.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Listening and Speaking
description: Key issues; overview and critique of published materials; practice in developing syllabi and other materials.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Writing
description: Problems in teaching second language composition. Survey materials; use, modification, and development. Error analysis.

subject: SLS
title: Language and Learning Technologies
description: A wide range of emerging technologies for language learning and research will be explored. Online/faceto-face discussions and hands-on experiential learning are integrated with learner’s goals, best practices, and theoretical foundations. (Once a year)

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Reading
description: Survey of research in reading process; teaching methodology; psycholinguistic investigations; comparison of reading in first and second languages.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Program Development
description: Designing, implementing, and evaluating language programs; systems-based approach to program and curriculum development.

subject: SLS
title: English Grammar
description: Descriptive English grammar in relation to second language learning and teaching.

subject: SLS
title: Comparative Grammar and Second Languages
description: Comparative study of two or more languages. Consideration of language transfer in second language learning, role of typological features.

subject: SLS
title: Multilingual/EL Pedagogy
description: Examines practices, theories, research, and perspectives on multilingual/EL teaching approaches. Topics include culturally and linguistically responsive approaches, collaboration, lesson planning, and adapting materials to promote the growth and development of multilingual/ EL learners. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as EDCS 644)

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Acquisition
description: Survey of theories and research on second language learning by children and adults, learning naturalistically and in formal settings. Relationships are explored between SLA research and language teaching.

subject: SLS
title: Sociolinguistics and Second Languages
description: Theoretical and applied aspects of language, culture, and society, and research methods in sociolinguistics, as they relate to second and foreign language issues.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Quantitative Research
description: Quantitative research methods; design of research studies; techniques in collecting data; statistical inference; and analysis and interpretation of data.

subject: SLS
title: Research in Language Testing
description: Advanced issues in language testing research including recent developments in the following areas: language testing hypotheses, item analysis, reliability, dependability, and validity.

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Classroom Research
description: Survey of research on second language classrooms and analysis of methodological issues.

subject: SLS
title: Applied Psycholinguistics and Second Language Acquisition
description: Theory and research in psycholinguistics as related to second language perception, production, acquisition, and instruction.

subject: SLS
title: Survey Research Methods in Second Language Studies
description: Hands-on experience in language survey research including planning and creating survey instruments (both interviews and questionnaires), administering, compiling and analyzing survey data (quantitatively and qualitatively), and reporting the results. (Once a year)

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Qualitative Research
description: Philosophical and theoretical approaches, methodology, and ethics in second language qualitative research.

subject: SLS
title: Discourse Analysis in Second Language Research
description: Survey of approaches to discourse; microanalytic qualitative research; theory and methodology.

subject: SLS
title: Topics in Second Language Studies
description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research methodology; (U) second language use. Repeatable one time for different alphas.
prerequisites: 650 for (E); consent for (N) and (P); 660 or consent for (U).

subject: SLS
title: Second Language Teaching Practicum
description: Student teaching in a language learning classroom. Repeatable one time in a different instructional context.

subject: SLS
title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
description: Enrollment for degree completion. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned up to six credits. CR/NC only.
prerequisites: master’s Plan B or C candidate and consent.

subject: SLS
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading in various fields of second language studies. CR/ NC only. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SLS
title: Thesis Research
description: Individual research in the various fields of second language studies. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: SLS
title: Seminar in Second Language Education
description: Current issues and problems. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SLS
title: Seminar in Second Language Acquisition
description: Issues in theory and research in second language acquisition of child and adult. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SLS
title: Seminar in Second Language Use
description: Second language/dialect use in multilingual communities. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SLS
title: Seminar in Second Language Research
description: Research methodologies in second language and multilingual contexts. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SLS
title: Apprenticeship in Teaching
description: An experienced-based introduction to college-level teaching; graduate students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, and participation in planning and evaluation. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: SLS
title: Dissertation Research
description: One credit is necessary for dissertation writing. Repeatable unlimited times. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Statistics
description: Dealing with advanced statistical methods beyond multiple linear regression, such as logit, event history analysis, and multi-level analysis. Emphasis is on applications of the techniques to social science research. Repeatable one time only.

subject: SOC
title: Cultural Analysis
description: Contemporary issues in cultural sociology, covering key theoretical perspectives, analytic methods and substantive areas for empirical research. A-F only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Sociology of Knowledge
description: Sociological theory applied to bases of knowledge in everyday life, professional communities, and the sciences. Research and theory-building activities of sociologists; ethnomethodology; construction of social structure, culture, and consciousness. Repeatable one time only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Current Issues in Sociology
description: Substantive areas that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other courses. Repeatable two times.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Medical Sociology
description: Application of theoretical paradigms and methodologies to the examination of selected research topics in the field of medical sociology. Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Aging, Culture, and Health
description: Overview of the major theories, perspectives, and empirical findings relating to aging in various cultural contexts. SOC, PSY, NURS, SW, PH majors only.
prerequisites: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: SOC
title: Comparative Family and Gender
description: Discusses the major perspectives on family and gender relations and examines related empirical research. Emphasis is on the cross-cultural comparisons across the U.S. and Asia in the context of globalizing economies and cultures. A-F only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as GHPS 719)

subject: SOC
title: Comparative Study of East Asia
description: Comparative analysis of social organization, social processes, and change of both capitalist and communist countries of East Asia, with each other and other areas of the world. Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC
title: Social Change–Pacific Islands
description: Analysis of social change; transformation from subsistence societies to commodified, wage-labor societies with participation in world economy.

subject: SOC
title: Modern Japanese Society
description: Social and behavioral studies of Japanese values, social organization, and personality development. Problems of value conflict, political protest, world role, tradition, and social change. Repeatable one time only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Modern Chinese Society
description: Developmental policies, social change, and impact on modern Chinese social institutions. Includes China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. May include social and demographic change, population, social stratification, gender, and family problems. Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Race and Ethnicity
description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) antiracism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality. Repeatable up to two times in different alphas. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)

subject: SOC
title: Conflict Analysis/Resolution
description: Seminar on the analysis of conflict resolution. Faculty from law, planning, political science and guest practitioners will present multidisciplinary analysis and intervention strategies on contemporary conflicts. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Structure and the Individual
description: Intensive study and individual research projects in a selected topic. Theoretical and methodological issues in relating social and individual levels of analysis.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Movements
description: Study of sociology of social movements, plus independent student research. Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC

Focus on culturally and linguistically diverse students diversity, non-traditional students and students with disabilities. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Transition/Supported Employment

subject: SPED
title: Reading Assessment & Tiered Intervention for Students with Disabilities
description: Selection and administration of formal and informal assessments within a problem-solving model for designing robust reading instruction for struggling readers. Guiding planning and reading intervention using data-based decision-making. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Diagnostic-Prescriptive Reading Intervention
description: Structural and functional features of reading development using diagnostic-prescriptive reading intervention. Advanced diagnostic-prescriptive intervention selection and design for students with reading disabilities using tool-component-composite analysis. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)
description: Focuses on the definitions and characteristics of applied behavior analysis and the concepts, principles, and processes. Concepts related to ethics and behavior change procedures will also be introduced. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Ethics and Professional Conduct
description: Focuses on content on the Behavior Analysis Certification Board’s code for ethical conduct as well as advanced concepts, principles, and processes of applied behavior analysis. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings. Repeatable nine times, up to 20 credits. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Research Practicum in Special Education
description: Directed research experience to demonstrate mastery of research skills and techniques through developing and writing research proposals. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: SPED
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading/research. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and department chair

subject: SPED
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Exceptionalities

subject: SPED
title: Doctoral Internship
description: Supervised internship (minimum 18 hours per week) in program development and administration or research in the student’s area of emphasis. EDUC majors only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Professional Seminar in Exceptionalities
description: Professional norms, duties, and expectations of leaders in exceptionalities; transitioning from practitioner to researcher and leadership roles; familiarity with current research and trends in the field of exceptionalities. Repeatable five times. PhD in EDUC majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Single-Case Experimental Design
description: Advanced single-case experimental design; examines the logic of internal and external validity of small “N” design and its functionalist foundations.

subject: SPED
title: Special Topics in Exceptionalities
description: Critical examination and discussion of historical or current topic in early intervention, special education, and/or developmental disabilities. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: SPED
title: Grant Development/Procurement
description: Overview of grant development and procurement processes related to special education personnel preparation and research and demonstration programs. Students design a grant proposal related to a particular problem or need within their employment settings.

subject: SURG
title: Surgery Longitudinal Clerkship
description: A clinically based, year-long, introductory in general surgery and selected subspecialties. Outpatient-conducted one day per week for six months in a community-based, ambulatory care facility. Inpatient-conducted for four weeks in an acute-care hospital facility. Repeatable one time.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: SURG

description: Clinical experiences in management of medical, surgical, and psychiatric problems requiring urgent care.
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: SURG

description: Advanced clinical experience in: (B) urology; (C) ophthalmology; (D) otolaryngology; (E) plastic surgery; (F) neurosurgery; (G) orthopaedics; (H) anesthesia; (I) surgical intensive care; (J)Sub-I –general surgery; (K) Sub-I –pediatric surgery; (M) diagnostic radiology; (N) radiation oncology; (O) EM Sub-I; (P) extramural elec in surg; (Q) Sub-I –cardiovascular; (R) surgical research; (S) surgical anatomy; (T) preceptorship in Asia; (U) biomedical technology design; (X) transplant surgery; (Y) bedside ultrasounds; (Z) laparoscopic skills. Repeatable one time for all except (U), (X), (Y), and (Z); repeatable two times for (U) and (X). Medical students only for (U), (X), (Y), and (Z). CR/NC only.
prerequisites: 532 for all except (M), (U), and (Y); and consent for (R) and (S); admission into JABSOM for (U) and (Y)
college: John A. Burns School of Medicine

subject: SUST
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip. (Cross-listed as ERTH 101) DP
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: The Natural Environment
description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards. (Cross-listed as GEO 101) DP
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: The Natural Environment Lab
description: DY A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers. Pre: GEO 101 (or concurrent). (Cross-listed as GEO 101L)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
description: DB Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as OEST 103)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: Biology & Society Laboratory
description: DY (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawai‘i. Not a BIOL major elective. (Cross-listed as BIOL 101L)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST

description: DB Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GES 102 and OCN 102)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: DY Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GES 102L and OCN 102L)
prerequisites: 112 (or concurrent) or GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: FQ Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ERTH 102)
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Cities
description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.
college: School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST)

subject: ZOOL

description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques. BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as BOT 670)

(B) general zoology; (C) zoology literature; (D) animal behavior; (E) ecology; (F) animal physiology; (G) development biology; (H) marine biology; (I) systematics and evolution. Each alpha is repeatable five times.

subject: ZOOL

description: Selected advanced topics in experimental design or data analysis for biologists. Repeatable unlimited times. ZOOL majors only.

subject: ZOOL

description: Advanced treatment of selected topics under current active investigation. Repeatable unlimited times. ZOOL majors only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Animal Behavior
description: Lecture-discussion of selected topics. Repeatable three times, up to nine credits. ZOOL majors only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Invertebrate Zoology
description: Comparative morphology, development, taxonomy, phylogeny. Repeatable three times, up to nine credits.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Fish and Fisheries Biology
description: Lecture-discussion of various aspects. Repeatable up to nine credits. ZOOL majors only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Animal Physiology
description: Selected problems in environmental physiology, electro-physiology, or neurophysiology. Basic concepts and measurements of function at the organismic or cellular level. Repeatable three times, up to nine credits.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Systematics and Evolution
description: Selected problems of current or historic interest. Repeatable three times, up to nine credits.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Ecology
description: Advanced topics in ecology; discussion of literature and in depth survey of specific areas. Repeatable three times up to nine credits. Graduate students only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Conservation Biology
description: Advanced topics in conservation and environmental biology. Repeatable three times, up to twelve credits. A-F only. (Cross-listed as BOT 750)

subject: ZOOL
title: Foundations of Evolution and Ecology I
description: Graduate level introduction to evolution and ecology emphasizing foundational literature, modern models and inference, and major questions in evolution and ecology. Topics include population ecology, community ecology, the genetics of populations, systematics, and speciation. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: ZOOL
title: Foundations of Evolution and Ecology II
description: Graduate level introduction to evolution and ecology emphasizing foundational literature, modern models and inference, and major questions in evolution and ecology. This is the second semester continuation of 780. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: SW
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well. A-F only. (Cross-listed as COA 435 and PH 435)
prerequisites: Pre: 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Research Development in Social Welfare
description: DS Introduction to and application of language of research, theoretical concepts underlying advancement of knowledge, practical steps in research.
prerequisites: SW majors only. Pre: completion of required junior-level SW courses (i.e., 302, 303, 325, 326, 360, 361, and 391) with C or better. Co-requisite: 402 and 490.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Native Hawaiian Perspectives: A Cultural Context for Well-Being
description: To preserve the cultural knowledge of kupuna as it relates to health and wellbeing. Disseminate cultural knowledge of health and well-being to social work students and students in allied health professions.
prerequisites: SW or Social Welfare students only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Ke A‘o Mau: Learning Preserved
description: To provide a holistic examination of issues and to explore culturally-anchored resolutions and practices to achieve social justice and health and well-being.
prerequisites: SW, Social Welfare, or PH students only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Provides students with a body of knowledge, skills, and values that facilitate social work with Native Hawaiians.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare Concepts and Issues in Gerontology
description: DS Aging and its effect on the individual, family groups, associations, and communities. Impact of aging on social service delivery systems, public policy and role of social work.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: An examination of current trends and issues in social work.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education II
description: Intermediate instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prerequisites: Pre: 391 complete with C or better, and majors only. Co-requisite: 402 and 440.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education III
description: Advanced instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prerequisites: Pre: 490 complete with C or better, and majors only. Co-requisite: 403.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Directed Reading and Research

prerequisites: Pre: majors only, senior standing, and consent of program chair and faculty advisor.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Individuals
description: Beginning practice course introduces students to the basic processes of social work and the roles and skills needed for generalist practice. Relevant theories of social work practice with individuals are explored for the efficacy with various problems and for their applicability to practice with various ethnocultures, social classes, and oppressed populations. Interviewing and interpersonal skill development are incorporated. A-F only. (Fall only)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Families and Groups
description: Practice course builds upon the generalist framework and foundation content presented in 606. Special emphasis is given on models for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of practice with families and groups. Relevant theories of groups and the principles of group dynamics and group work methods are examined in regard to task, therapeutic, psychoeducational, and social development groups. Family content includes structural, behavioral, communication/experiential, and culturally-specific theories of intervention. A-F only.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare Policy and Services
description: Examines in a historical and comparative framework the economic, social, political, organizational, and administrative factors influencing the development, formulation, and implementation of social welfare policies in the U.S. Provides opportunity for the application of various models of social policy analysis in major areas of social welfare programming and service delivery. SW majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Communities and Organizations
description: Community conceptualization; organized roles of developer, enabler, broker, mediator, and advocate; diagnostic and problem-solving technology; the special characteristics of the social worker as community organizer; matrix of structural objectives; sources and use of power; how to build an organization; and interorganizational negotiation. SW majors only. A-F only. (Spring only)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

description: Introduction to formal organization theory. Social service administration examined and implications for service delivery systems developed.
prerequisites: SW majors only. Pre: graduate standing.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

description: Overview of aging from the biopsycho, socioeconomic and cultural perspectives. Explores common theories of aging. Emphasis on bridging the gap between the realm of concepts and theories, and the world of practice in gerontology.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: SW

SW majors only. A-F only. (Fall only)
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

description: Emphasis on the developments in child welfare; issues, concerns with regard to needs and rights, and the application of social work services to problems associated with needs for protection. prerequisites: SW majors only. Pre: graduate standing.
college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

college: Thompson School of Social Work & Public Health

subject: TIM
title: Geography of Global Tourism
description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. (Cross-listed as GEO 324)
prerequisites: DS. Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: TIM
title: Travel Distribution Management
description: History, development, operations, and management of travel distribution organizations including: travel agents, tour operators and wholesalers, specialty channelers, meeting planners, incentive houses, travel associations, and other destination management organizations. Evolution and economics of the distribution of travel products through destination databases and electronic commerce.

subject: TIM
title: Hotel/Resort Facilities and Design
description: Comprehensive understanding of facilities management and design including maintenance systems, sustainable development options and design and environmental management.
prerequisites: TIM majors only. A-F only. Pre: 313 and 314.

subject: TIM
title: Hospitality Sales & Negotiation
description: Personal selling by hospitality and tourism firms engaged in business-to-business marketing. Emphasis will be placed on negotiation case studies, exercises, and role-plays.
prerequisites: TIM majors only. A-F only. Pre: 101. Recommended: 304.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Tourism Transportation
description: Introduction to managerial and operational issues related to all modes of transportation used by tourists into or within a tourist destination. Passenger behavior; transport infrastructure; transport networks; regulation; sustainable transport.

subject: TIM
title: Principles of Logistics
description: Management of logistics systems: inventory control, warehousing, materials management, physical distribution, transportation. Emphasis on Hawai‘i’s location and unique problems.

subject: TIM
title: Air Transportation Management
description: Marketing, management and strategies used by airlines, airports, catering, and aircraft manufacturers.

subject: TIM
title: Surface Transportation Management
description: Management of surface transportation such as cars, buses, and intercity rail, etc. Includes marketing, ownership and financing, supply chain, operations, regulation and promotion, human resources.

subject: TIM
title: Economics in Travel Industry
description: Microeconomic theory of consumer behavior and demand production cost analysis, market structure and pricing in travel companies. Economic impact of tourism.
prerequisites: Students may not earn credit for 365 and BUS 313. TIM majors only. Pre: either ECON 120 or ECON 130.

subject: TIM
title: TIM Study Abroad
description: Study abroad instructional experience emphasizing international travel, tourism and hospitality-related topics at equivalent, accredited programs. Content varies depending on locus of instruction and instructor. Course qualifies as either a TIM or general elective with pre-approval or department. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: TIM
title: Current Topics in Travel Industry Management (Alpha)
description: (B) resort development; (C) assets management; (D) transportation and public policy; (E) management by cultural values; (F) travel industry management; (G) hospitality management; (H) hotel management; (I) restaurant entrepreneurship; (J) tourism management; (K) recreation management; (M) leisure management; (N) transportation management; (O) travel industry management education; (P) travel industry management technology; (Q) meetings, incentives, conventions, and exhibition management. Repeatable five times with consent.
prerequisites: TIM majors only for (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), (G), (H), (I), (J), (K), (M), (N). Pre: 101 and 313 for (I).

subject: TIM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research into problems in hotel, restaurant, transportation or tourism sectors of the travel industry.
prerequisites: TIM majors only. Junior standing or above. Pre: a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and consent of dean’s office and instructor based upon student’s written proposal of content and objectives of course program.

subject: TIM
title: Internship IV (Alpha)
description: Requires a minimum of 150 hours of internship, a business presentation, and an analytical report synthesizing experience and related theories. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, which will enhance and improve students’ writing skills. (B) executive internship; (C) community service internship.
prerequisites: Restricted to majors. CR/NC only. Pre: 200 and consent.

subject: TIM
title: Resort, Spa and Wellness Management
description: Principles of resort and spa development. Essential aspects of understanding the leadership and interrelationships of managing/operating and marketing resorts, spas, and wellness.

subject: TIM
title: Resort Mixed Use Development
description: Critical and essential aspects of developing and managing resort mixed use facilities. Includes multidimensional and dynamic interrelationships of site development and facilities, business mix, management structures and systems, and industry practices. (Fall only)
prerequisites: A-F only. Pre: 313 or 369; and 314. Recommended: 333 and 401.

subject: TIM
title: Revenue Management in Travel Industry
description: An in-depth comprehensive introduction to the theory and practice of revenue management and provides recognition of thorough knowledge of the fundamental metrics and methodologies used within the hotel industry.
prerequisites: TIM majors only. Pre: 101, ECON 130, and ACC 210.

subject: TIM
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. (Cross-listed as GEO 415 and SUST 415)
prerequisites: DS. Junior standing or higher. Pre: 101 or 324/ GEO 324.

subject: TIM
title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects. (Cross-listed as SUST 421)
prerequisites: A-F only. Pre: 101 and departmental approval.

subject: TIM
title: Destination Development and Marketing
description: Analysis of key factors in the marketing and management of tourism destinations, including destination branding, product development, integrated marketing, stakeholder relations, and the role of destination marketing/marketing organizations. Emphasis on written communication.

subject: TIM
title: Strategic Management for the Travel/ Hospitality Industry
description: Strategic management in the travel/hospitality industry. Case study analysis, discussion and written reports, covering strategies, management problems and industry issues. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prerequisites: A-F only. Pre: 301, 302, 303, 304, 305 and graduating senior.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Transportation
description: Advanced level of discussion in terms of transportation, including management, economics, strategy, regulation, operating performance, fleet management, and network management.

subject: TIM
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015. Repeatable one time. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as OCN 442 and SUST 442)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Travel Industry Management (Alpha)
description: (B) tourism planning; (C) advanced travel industry management; (D) advanced hospitality management; (E) advanced hotel management; (F) advanced restaurant management; (G) advanced tourism management; (H) advanced recreation management; (I) advanced leisure management; (J) advanced transportation management; (K) advanced travel industry management education; (M) advanced travel industry management technology; (N) advanced meetings, incentives, conventions, and exhibition management; (O) advanced food and beverage management; (P) leadership and advanced human resources; (Q) advanced assets management. Repeatable five times with consent for (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), (G), (H), (I), (J), (K), (M), (N); repeatable six times for (O), (P), and (Q).
prerequisites: TIM majors only. A-F only for (O), (P), and (Q).

subject: TIM
title: Research Application in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Analysis of methodologies appropriate for research in travel industry management. Survey of the literature of applied techniques and approaches including exploratory approaches. Familiarization with research design and implementation of development of research proposals.

subject: TIM
title: Strategic Marketing in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: In-depth study of marketing principles and problems related to travel industry organizations. Emphasis on strategic marketing. Research applications, international and domestic marketing of travel industry services.

subject: SW
title: Dissertation Seminar
description: Culminating experience in social welfare doctoral specialization; integration of PhD core and specialization course work.
prerequisites: classified student in PhD in social welfare program or consent.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in International Social Work
description: Approaches to social problems and trends in the profession in international, cross-cultural perspectives. Emphasis on developmental aspects of social work. Political, economic, social, and cultural forces shaping social welfare in national development. Meets seminar requirement. SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Hawaiian culture, past and present. Explores and examines possible approaches to working with Hawaiians and part-Hawaiians. Special emphasis on supports in the Hawaiian system that may promote maximal functioning for those Hawaiians experiencing problems in today’s society. Meets seminar requirement. A-F only.

subject: SW
title: Seminar on Women and Health
description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care. (Cross-listed as NURS 744)

subject: SW
title: Specialist Field Education I
description: Instruction in the field is continued. The field experience in the second year provides an opportunity for the student to test out concepts, principles, theories, and alternate approaches in actual practice settings. SW majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: 717 (or concurrent) or 722 (or concurrent) or 724 (or concurrent) or 726 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B -).

subject: SW
title: Specialist Field Education II
description: Continuation of 790. A-F only.
prerequisites: 790 and; 718 (or concurrent); or 723 (or concurrent); or 725 (or concurrent); or 727 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B-).

subject: SW
title: Advanced Social Welfare Policy Analysis and Change
description: Builds on 630 and emphasizes a more thorough and comprehensive examination of major policies, programs, and populations central to a concentration (Health, Mental Health, Gerontology, Child and Family). Students learn a more focused and applied analysis of the relationship between social policy, research, and social work practice. SW majors only. A-F only.

subject: SW
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology
description: DS. Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology
description: DS. Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Data Analysis
description: FQ. Basic analytic skills widely used in quantitative analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, rates and probability, comparison of groups, introduction to causal relationships, and application of these techniques to real life examples. A-F only.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
description: FGB. Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawai‘i and the Asia-Pacific region. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 160)

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
description: DS. Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society. (Cross-listed as ES 214)

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Social Problems
description: DS. Theoretical and substantive survey of the nature and causes of social problems; selected types: poverty, inequality, deviance, etc

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: DS. Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues. (Cross-listed as SUST 250 and TAHR 250)

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Juvenile Delinquency
description: DS. Forms of juvenile deviance; conditions and processes that result in alienation and deviance of youth. Juvenile corrections as institutionalized societal responses.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to the Sociology of Punishment
description: DS. Multiple social theories about different forms of formal and informal punishments and social control across different societies and times.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology of the Family
description: DS. Family patterns, mate selection, parent-child interaction, socialization of roles, legal sanctions, trends in organization, functions.

subject: SOC
title: East Asian Popular Cultures
description: DS. East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ASAN 259)

subject: SOC
title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
description: DS. (3 Lec, 2 50-min Lab) Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
description: DS. (3 Lec, 2 50-min Lab) Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics. Restricted to students in the honors program and required for students taking the honors track in sociology. A-F only.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Urban Sociology
description: DS. Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as PLAN 301)
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Health
description: DS. Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women. (Cross-listed as WGSS 305)
prerequisites: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or WGSS 202, or POLS 110; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Inequality and Stratification
description: DS. Introduction to social stratification theory and research; definition and measurement of socioeconomic status; racial, ethnic and gender inequality; differences in lifestyles and life chances; social mobility.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Work
description: DS. Work from viewpoint of individuals; meaningfulness versus productivity; how work, economics, and the industrial system affect individual goals.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Change
description: Causes, processes, and effects of social change, using single and multi-cause models in simple and complex industrialized societies.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Social Policy
description: DS. Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women. (Cross-listed as WS 318)
prerequisites: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociological Theory
description: DS. Major theorists and their influences, from Comte to today.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Law
description: DS. Law as a political enforcement of the social order; how it is organized and operates; determinants of effectiveness; ways it adapts to and facilitates changing social conditions.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Criminology
description: DS. Concepts used in crime, law enforcement, criminal justice, and corrections. Types of criminal behavior; costs and effects of control.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Drugs and Society
description: DS. Use of mood- and mind-altering drugs in America among adults, youth, and cross-culturally. Illicit drug culture, psychedelics, and perception; social norms and deviant behavior.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Deviance and Social Control
