description: DS. Interrelations of deviance, criminology, juvenile delinquency, corrections, social control, sociology of law. Key concepts, theories.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Criminal Justice Organizations
description: DS. Examines major criminal justice organizations–police, courts, and prisons. Using organizational theory, identifies the role of organizational goals, structure, resources, legitimacy, culture, and front-line workers in shaping criminal justice policy and practice.
prerequisites: 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Psychology
description: DS. Major principles; social attitudes, theories of conformity and change, person perception and attribution theory, social role, role conflict and role behavior, group structure, and behavior.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Happiness in Unsettled Times
description: DS. Combines theoretical, scientific and ‘hands-on’ learning to explore how happiness and well-being can be cultivated, even in this challenging era of extreme global climate events.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Education
description: DS. Formal education as one aspect of socialization. Emphasis on American system; business, military, and religious institutions.
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
description: DS. Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing
prerequisites: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Religion
description: Seminar in research on sociological aspects of religious sectarianism; attention to Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as REL 452)

subject: SOC
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
description: The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as ES 456)
prerequisites: Prerequisite: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Arts
description: Relation of art to society; role of artist, audience, critic, patron, museum; Western and other societies; attitudes toward new styles.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sports and Society
description: Critical perspectives on sports and society. Topics include power and inequality; mobility, status, and economics; youth development; globalization; gender; and violence in sports and the wider society. (Spring only)

subject: SOC
title: Popular Culture
description: Popular culture as manifested in film, sports, TV, comics, magazines, etc.; relation to sociological theories and studies.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Survey Research
description: Survey research design and analysis, including theory selection instrument construction, sampling techniques, data collection, computerized data analysis, and writing up research reports of the findings.

subject: SOC
title: Social Statistics
description: Common statistical procedures emphasizing univariate and bivariate description; some attention to multivariate techniques and statistical inference, within context of research procedures.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: SOC 300 or consent. Co-requisite: SOC 476L

subject: SOC
title: Social Statistics Laboratory
description: Required lab for computer applications for analysis of sociological data. CR/NC only.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Field Research Methods
description: Techniques for collecting and analyzing qualitative data. Participant observation; small groups in natural settings; community studies. Grounded theory; theories of everyday life; reality construction.

subject: SOC
title: Discussion Group Leader–Freshman Seminar
description: A unique opportunity for students to gain leadership, teaching, and public speaking skills as a SOC 100 leader for a section of 10 freshmen students while being mentored weekly by a faculty course coordinator.

subject: SOC
title: Politics of Multiculturalism
description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ES 492)
prerequisites: Prerequisite: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. Consent of instructor. (Cross-listed as SOCS 489 and WGSS 489)

subject: SOC
title: Topics in Sociology
description: Topics course that explore current issues and try new ideas. Repeatable two times.

subject: SOC
title: Topics in Sociology: Student Projects
description: Students create their own study group and solicit an advisor from faculty. Consult department for assistance.

subject: SOC
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: SOC 300 and consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Statistics for Regression Analysis
description: Dealing with the multiple linear regression and logistic regression models, focusing on modeling, i.e., specification of the explanatory variables to answer different research questions. Emphasis on applications using statistical package programs. SOC 605L is required.

subject: SOC
title: Regression Analysis Laboratory
description: Lab for computer analysis skills is required for students taking 605. CR/NC only.

subject: SOC
title: Research Methods and Design
description: Emphasis on theory selection, theory construction, and choice of research strategies.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Methods of Content Analysis
description: Content analysis combines quantitative and qualitative methods to analyze text systematically. Covers sampling and case selection; manual and computer-assisted methods of coding and analyzing textual data; writing reports using content analysis data. Repeatable one time. (Once a year)

subject: SOC
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models. (Cross-listed as EDEA 608 and EDEP 602)

subject: SOC
title: Seminar Qualitative Research
description: Advanced seminar on conducting fieldwork in natural social settings with emphasis on qualitative techniques, political and ethical considerations, data management and assessment, interpretation and reflexive writing. Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC
title: Classical Sociological Theory
description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociological theory from 19th- century to the 1960s, including intellectual contexts and historical development. A-F only. Graduate students only. (Fall only)

subject: SOC
title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociology theory from the 1960s to the present, including intellectual contexts and historical development. A-F only. Graduate students only. (Spring only)

subject: SOC
title: Organizational Analysis
description: Theoretical approaches to organizations; organizational structure and process; organizational pathologies and effectiveness; the organization and its environment.

subject: SOC
title: Medical Sociology
description: Covers the major paradigms in medical sociology for analyzing social epidemiology, the political economy of health systems, health service organizations, health and wellness behaviors illness perception and help-seeking, doctor-patient interaction, and adaptations to illness. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Stress and Health
description: Analysis of current theory and empirical research on relationship of stress and health; sociological, psychological, and community psychiatry models and current issues.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Mental Health and Illness
description: Examines sociological research and theories about mental health and illness. A key question in medical sociology will be addressed: What is the relationship between society and mental health? Repeatable one time.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Stratification
description: Classical theories of social class, contemporary developments; crucial research issues, appropriate methodologies. Repeatable one time only. Classified graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Feminist Criminology
description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls. A-F only. (Cross-listed as WGSS 625)

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Criminology
description: Major current theories, history of their development, elaborations of typologies, implications for treatment modalities.

subject: SOC
title: Criminal Justice System
description: Examination of the criminal justice system; the exercise of discretion and limits placed upon it.

subject: SOC
title: American Punishment
description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison- industrial complex. A-F only. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as AMST 638)

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Human Population
description: Comparative analysis of quantitative and qualitative aspects of population; factors affecting size, distribution, and composition; impact of population size and composition on society.

subject: SOC
title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, urbanization; projections and stable population theory. (Cross-listed as PH 659)

subject: SOC
title: Teaching Seminar
description: Examines research on teaching, learning, and ethics, as well as practical skills for teaching at the university level. Syllabi and teaching philosophies are developed, which are useful for the academic job market. Graduate standing only.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Sustainability
description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives. Graduate students only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as SUST 670)

subject: SOC
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SOC
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Evaluation Research
description: Research design, data collection, field problems and analysis in the evaluation of social programs. Examples from criminal justice, corrections, drug treatment, mental health, and public health.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Statistics
description: Dealing with advanced statistical methods beyond multiple linear regression, such as logit, event history analysis, and multi-level analysis. Emphasis is on applications of the techniques to social science research. Repeatable one time only.

subject: SOC
title: Cultural Analysis
description: Contemporary issues in cultural sociology, covering key theoretical perspectives, analytic methods and substantive areas for empirical research. A-F only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Sociology of Knowledge
description: Sociological theory applied to bases of knowledge in everyday life, professional communities, and the sciences. Research and theory-building activities of sociologists; ethnomethodology; construction of social structure, culture, and consciousness. Repeatable one time only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Current Issues in Sociology
description: Substantive areas that ar

subject: EA
title: Lighting III: Advanced Lighting Design
description: Workshop dealing with special topics in theatrical lighting design and related skills. Repeatable two times. THEA or DNCE majors only.

subject: THEA
title: Professional Advancement in Entertainment Design
description: Directed study designed to help MFA candidates in Design acquire the tools helpful in obtaining future employment. Portfolios, resumes, and related application tools will be developed along with other necessary skills. Must be current MFA candidate in theatre. Repeatable six times. THEA majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: THEA
title: Scenic II: Intermediate Scene Design
description: Workshop in advanced techniques and skills of scenic design; research, presentation, rendering, drafting, and model making.
prerequisites: 353 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Scenic III: Advanced Scenic Design
description: Workshop dealing with special topics in scenic design, related skills, and portfolio preparation. Repeatable two times with consent. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Topics in Costume Construction
description: Advanced costume production techniques for entertainment design. Topics may include corset, draping, patterning, tailoring, dye work, fabric modification, millinery, leatherwork, and crafts. Topics presented within the context of both current entertainment industry and traditional practices. Repeatable three times for different topics.
prerequisites: 354 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Costumes III: Advanced Costume Design
description: Workshop dealing with special topics in costume design and related skills. Repeatable one time with consent. A-F only.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Design
description: Research, design, and discussion exploring collaborative design problems and solutions. Repeatable two times. A-F only.

subject: THEA
title: Business for the Arts
description: Seminar offering overview and foundation for launching or advancing enterprises in the arts. A focus on the processes and method for creating economically successful grants and project development applications. (Cross-listed as DNCE 658)

subject: THEA
title: Field Research Methods
description: Goals and methods. Grant writing, interview, questionnaire, observation, and performance study as research techniques. Practical application by designing a research project.

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Topics in Asian Theatre
description: Comparative and cross-cultural examination. (B) origins; (C) theories and systems; (D) modern Asian drama. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Topics in Performance in Hawai‘i
description: Analysis of Hawai‘i’s indigenous performance traditions, the contemporary multicultural landscape of theatre in Ko Hawai‘i Pae ‘āina, and the representation of Kanaka Maoli and settler voices on Hawai‘i’s stages. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 668)

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Advanced Creative Dramatics
description: Advanced seminar in applied methods and theories of creative dramatics. Repeatable one time. THEA or DNCE majors only.

subject: THEA
title: Interdisciplinary Collaborations
description: Hybrid performance works for dancers, musicians, actors, visual artists, poets, and writers to explore the nature of the collaboration process in various settings. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. THEA, DNCE, MUS, ART, ENG majors only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 674)

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Topics in Theatre for Young Audiences
description: Creative movement/drama, puppetry, and theatre/dance; (B) production concepts. Repeatable when topics change.

subject: THEA
title: Directing Asian Theatre
description: Directing traditional Asian theatre pieces and Western plays performed with Asian techniques; development of new performance styles based on Asian examples; directing of scenes and one-act plays. Repeatable one time with consent.
prerequisites: graduate theatre major and one Asian theatre course, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Directing Multicultural Theatre
description: Directing multicultural/intercultural theatre; development of new performance styles based on the study of diverse theatre traditions from around the world; directing of scenes and one-act plays. A-F only. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: graduate theatre major and one directing course with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Topics in Theatre Directing
description: Readings, discussion, research, and/or performance and scene work. Repeatable five times, up to nine credits. THEA majors only.

subject: THEA
title: Graduate Workshop in Directing
description: Direction of scenes and major one-act plays. Pre-thesis production. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Workshop in Directing Process
description: Methods class in theatre production for the director. Covers organization and techniques such as rehearsal planning, scheduling, and execution. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Directing Western Styles
description: Students direct scenes in classic or non-realistic western theatre styles or genres. Repeatable one time with consent. THEA majors only. A-F only. Graduate student in theatre program. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Graduate Theatre Workshop
description: Practical and supervisory theatre work pertinent to professional degree objectives on productions being done in Kennedy Theatre or in other venues, by approval. Repeatable eight times, up to 9 credits. THEA majors only.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Teaching Dance/Theatre
description: Pedagogy and classroom experience in teaching technique and theory. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as DNCE 691)

subject: THEA
title: Practicum in Teaching
description: Supervised teaching experience at the introductory or undergraduate level. Students will teach an appropriate level course in their field of expertise under faculty supervision. Repeatable up to nine credits. THEA or DNCE majors only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 692)

subject: THEA
title: Internship: Youth Theatre/Dance
description: Supervised leadership experiences in theatre/dance program with children. Students spend nine hours per week in supervised setting and three hours in weekly class meeting. (Cross-listed as DNCE 693)
prerequisites: one of 470, 476, or DNCE 490; or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Creative Projects
description: MFA play or dance productions, design projects, original full-length plays. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Professional Internship
description: Internship program where students will work for or with a professional theatre company under supervision of a UH faculty member, plus possible supervisor(s) from the theatre company. Students must participate hands-on in production activities of that company and receive a satisfactory (or better) review from their supervisor(s); (B) entertainment design: costume, lighting, scenery, props, sound, or other related disciplines; (C) performance: acting, directing, dance, choreography, or other related disciplines. Repeatable eight times per alpha, up to nine credits per alpha. A-F only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 696 (Alpha))
prerequisites: 345 or 353 or 356 for (B); 621 or 682 or DNCE 371 for (C).

subject: THEA
title: Directed Research
description: Reading or research in theatre theory or history; reading and practice in particular areas of dramatic production. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: THEA
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Drama and Theatre
description: Special topics. Repeatable when topics change.

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Asian Theatre
description: (B) Southeast Asia and India; (C) China; (D) Japan. Repeatable two times.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Hawaiian & Indigenous Performance
description: Exploration, analysis, and application of Kanaka Maoli and Indigenous research methodologies, epistemologies, performance theory, methods, and praxis. Repeatable two times. Graduate students only.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Theatre for Young Audiences
description: Theories and methods applied in theatrical experiences with and for young audiences: creative movement/drama, puppetry, and theatre/ dance.

subject: THEA
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: TONG
title: Beginning Tongan
description: HSL. Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

subject: TONG
title: Beginning Tongan
description: HSL. Continuation of 101.

subject: TONG
title: Intermediate Tongan
description: HSL. Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

subject: TONG
title: Intermediate Tongan
description: HSL. Continuation of 201.

subject: TI
title: Court Interpreting I
description: Introduction to the legal system, as well as theoretical principles, ethics, practical techniques, and current issues surrounding the practice and profession of court and other legal interpreting. Repeatable one time.

subject: TI
title: Community Interpreting
description: Basic principles, ethics and skills involved in community interpreting in medical, legal, and social service settings; practical information about the community interpreter’s role and profession; practice of various community interpreting situations and techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: TI
title: Court Interpreting II
description: Combined lecture/discussion/practice. Continuation of 405 Court Interpretation, diving deeper into the practical side of oral interpreting for various proceedings, including arraignmen

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as GEO 302)

subject: SUST
title: Water and Society
description: DS. Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives. Pre: sophomore standing or higher, or consent. (Cross-listed as GEO 305)
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Ethics
description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making. A-F only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as NREM 306)
prerequisites: SUST 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103.

subject: SUST
title: Malama ‘Āina Resource Management Visual Technologies
description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies. (Cross-listed as HWST 307)

subject: SUST
title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
description: DS. Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity. (Cross-listed as ES 308)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environment and Agriculture
description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed. (Cross-listed as PEPS 310)

subject: SUST
title: Hawai‘i and the Pacific
description: DH. Hawai‘i as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples. (Cross-listed as ES 320)

subject: SUST
title: Globalization and Environment
description: DS. Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change. (Cross-listed as GEO 322)

subject: SUST
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: DS. Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as OCN 321 and PPC 340)
prerequisites: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Politics
description: DS. Evolution of international politics, law and decision-making on a variety of environmental concerns; from endangered species to pollution to climate change. Interaction of population, development, and environment in global governance. (Cross-listed as POLS 324)

subject: SUST
title: Communicating Sustainability
description: Application of scientific communication theory, strategic communication, and multimedia techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability. A-F only. (Cross-listed as COM 325)
prerequisites: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent. COM majors only.

subject: SUST
title: Geography, Environment, and Society
description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems. (Cross-listed as GEO 325)

subject: SUST
title: Culture and Environment
description: DS. Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures. (Cross-listed as GEO 330)

subject: SUST
title: Economics of Global Climate Change
description: DS. Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ECON 332)
prerequisites: SUST 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
description: DS. Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as ANTH 333)

subject: SUST
title: Society and Environment
description: DS. Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems. (Cross-listed as ANTH 335)

subject: SUST
title: Energy Economics and Policy
description: DS. Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources. (Cross-listed as ECON 336)

subject: SUST
title: Inter-woven Structures
description: DA. Studio investigation of threads under tension. Thematic lens of environmental vulnerability and resiliency. Explores art practice as embodied knowledge. Specific attention to weaving as meaning and place-making. Engages writing as a significant tool for analysis. A-F only. (Cross-listing as ART 338)

subject: SUST
title: Human Values and the Environment
description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts–literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics–in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature. A-F only. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as IS 340)
prerequisites: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawai‘i
description: DH. Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities. (Cross-listed as ES 340)

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Development
description: DS. Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawai‘i. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ECON 350)
prerequisites: SUST 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Economic Change and Hawai‘i’s People
description: DS. Hawai‘i’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy. (Cross-listed as ES 350)

subject: SUST
title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. (Cross-listed as HWST 356)

subject: SUST
title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: DS. Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies. (Cross-listed as NREM 358)

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: DS. Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society. A-F only. (Fall only) (Crosslisted as SOC 367 and WS 367)
prerequisites: WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PEPS 371 and TPSS 371)

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Law and Politics
description: DS. Focuses on theories, laws, policies, ethics, and sustainable futures of Hawai‘i and the U.S. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as POLS 380)
prerequisites: any 100 or 200 level POLS course, or consent. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Politics of the Ocean
description: DS. Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 387)
prerequisites: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 394)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. Consent of instructor.

subject: SUST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: DH. Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women,

subject: SUST
title: Politics of the Ocean
description: DS Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 387)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 394)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. Consent of instructor.

subject: SUST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: DH Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as HIST 401)

subject: SUST
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: DS Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control. (Cross-listed as GEO 404)
prerequisites: Pre: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as PEPS 410 and TPSS 410)

subject: SUST
title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as NREM 410)

subject: SUST
title: The Ocean Economy
description: DS Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ECON 409)

subject: SUST
title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
description: DP Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes. (Cross-listed as GEO 411)
prerequisites: Pre: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as OCN 411)

subject: SUST
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: DS Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. (Cross-listed as GEO 415 and TIM 415)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: TIM 101 or GEOG/TIM 324.

subject: SUST
title: Community and Natural Resource Management
description: DS Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as NREM 420)
prerequisites: Pre: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TIM 420)

subject: SUST
title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
description: DB Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management. (Cross-listed as PEPS 422)

subject: SUST
title: Agriculture, Food and Society
description: DS Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to nonmajors. (Cross-listed as GEO 422)
prerequisites: Pre: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Geochemistry
description: DP Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ERTH 425)
prerequisites: Pre: CHEM 161 and CHEM 162, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environment, Resources and Society
description: DS Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues. (Cross-listed as GEO 426)

subject: SUST
title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
description: DP Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ERTH 420)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as EDCS 433)

subject: SUST
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: DA Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ART 436)

subject: SUST
title: Installation/Performance–Material in Context
description: DA Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ART 439)

subject: SUST
title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as CEE 440)

subject: SUST
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as CEE 441 and OCN 441)

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as OCN 442 and TIM 462)

subject: SUST
title: Infrastructure: Project Impacts, Policy and Sustainability
description: Evaluation of infrastructure impacts. Impacts regulation and mitigation. Effects of environmental and other policies on infrastructure. Infrastructure relations to sustainability. Energy consumption, transportation efficiency and infrastructure recycling. Lectures and presentations by experts and enrolled students. A-F only. (Cross-listed as CEE 444)
prerequisites: Pre: senior standing, open to engineering, science, urban planning, and economics majors.

subject: SUST
title: Ethnoecology and Conservation
description: DB Ecological implications of cultural uses of plants. Examines the biological basis for, and ecological effects of traditional and local resource management systems. (Cross-listed as BOT 444)
prerequisites: Pre: BOT 305 or BIOL 265/265L or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: DS (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork. (Cross-listed as BOT 446)

subject: SUST
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ATMO 449 and CEE 449)
prerequisites: Senior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific B

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Journal Club
description: Students gain experience in the presentation and discussion of topics of current interest in the fields of tropical medicine and infectious diseases. Repeatable unlimited times. Graduate students only.

subject: TRMD
title: Laboratory Methods in Tropical Medicine
description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety. Repeatable one time. Graduate standing only. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Microbiology I: Medical Parasitology
description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: TRMD
title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PH 665)

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Micro II
description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PH 667)

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Laboratory Rotations
description: Practical experience in use of equipment and procedures in infectious disease and immunology research; introduction to research in tropical medicine. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: TRMD
title: Neurovirology
description: Seminar on neuroinvasive viruses giving basics of viruses causing nervous system diseases and discussing recent advances in the research field of neurovirology. (Fall only)

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Microbiology III
description: Basic structure, physiology, epidemiology, and genetics of pathogenic bacteria as well as the host response to these organisms. Correlation of these characteristics to disease pathogenesis in humans and animal models. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: TRMD
title: Advances In Medical Immunology
description: Presentations/discussions of current literature concerning recent advances in immunology relevant to disease and to disease processes. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: TRMD
title: Infection and Immunity
description: Combined lecture/discussion of interactions of pathogens with the innate and acquired immune systems. Topics will include the role of novel receptors in pathogen detection, inflammation in disease pathogenesis, pathogen immune evasion, and neuroimmunology. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: TRMD
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as PH 650)

subject: TRMD
title: Vaccinology
description: History/evolution of vaccines, current and next generation vaccines, vaccine immunology, adjuvants, vaccine strategies, vaccines for viral, bacterial, and parasitic diseases, vaccine-proof-of-concept and downstream developmental studies; vaccine safety production processes. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Spring only
prerequisites: (604 and 605) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Genetics and Evolution of Infectious Diseases
description: An evolutionary perspective to examine the interactive responses between infectious agents and the immune system. Topics will include natural selection, life history evolution, population genetics of pathogens and hosts, and anti-microbial resistance. A-F only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: TRMD
title: Bioinformatics I
description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis. Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only. Open to nonmajors. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed with QHS 610)

subject: TRMD
title: Advances in HIV/AIDS
description: History of HIV, basic biology and virology, epidemiology, HIV pathogenesis and immunology, clinical features, and co-morbidities. Treatment and prevention of HIV/ AIDS, including research methods, statistics, cultural competence, genetics, pathophysiology, drug and vaccine development. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Fall only)

subject: TRMD
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as QHS 601)

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Parasitology
description: Consideration of ultrastructure, physiology, biochemistry, in-vitro cultivation and host-parasite relationship of parasites of medical importance. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Virology
description: In-depth study of the major groups of viruses pathogenic for human; virus replication, host range, pathogenesis, immunology, and epidemiology. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Bacteriology
description: Role of bacteria in infectious diseases, with emphasis on clinical aspects and identification of etiological agents.

subject: TRMD
title: Epidemiology of Tropical Infectious Diseases
description: Epidemiology of infectious diseases as it relates to tropical medicine. Lecture/seminar format. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: TRMD
title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health. Repeatable unlimited times. (Cross-listed as PH 755)

subject: TRMD
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed. A-F only.

subject: TRMD
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research in medical microbiology (bacteriology, parasitology, virology). Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: TRMD
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Approval of department faculty required. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: TRMD
title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PH 756)

subject: TRMD
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral thesis. Approval of department faculty is required. Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: Approval of department faculty is required.

subject: TPSS
title: (Alpha) Plants for People
description: DB The origins: social, cultural, and ceremonial traditions; culture; food and nutritional properties. Processing of a variety of tropical horticultural plants are presented, with tasting sessions and optional field trips. Topics will rotate among (B) beverage crops (e.g., coffee, tea, chocolate, kava, fruit juices); (C) herbs, spices, and flavoring (selection of examples to be determined); (D) tropical fruits (assortment offered depends on availability during semester); (E) ornamental plants (flowers, houseplants, popular landscape plans, bonsai, ethnic ornamentals). Does not count towards TPSS major.

subject: TPSS
title: Sustainable Food and Energy (Field Course)
description: DB Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawai‘i for sustainable development. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits. (Cross-listed as SUST 156)

subject: TPSS
title: Natural History Field Trips on Hawai‘i Island
description: DY Field trips for Natural history and Conservation of the Hawaiian Islands. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: TPSS
title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
description: DB Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawai‘i as a model system. (Cross-listed as SUST 211)

subject: TPSS
title: Aquaponics
description: DB DY Basic online course integrates aquaculture (raising fish and prawns) with hydroponics plant cultivation in water. Includes the basic design and construction of an aquaponics feed system. Repeatable one time. (Summer only)

subject: TPSS
title: Organic Food Crop Production
description: DY Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as SUST 221)

subject: TPSS
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: DB Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of hum

subject: TIM
title: Research Application in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Analysis of methodologies appropriate for research in travel industry management. Survey of the literature of applied techniques and approaches including exploratory approaches. Familiarization with research design and implementation of development of research proposals. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Strategic Marketing in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: In-depth study of marketing principles and problems related to travel industry organizations. Emphasis on strategic marketing. Research applications, international and domestic marketing of travel industry services. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Information Technology, e-Commerce, and Travel Industry in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Planning, implementation, management, evaluation, and impact of information and electronic communication technologies, including e-commerce applications in the travel industry. Analysis of new information technology use as an area of research and strategic application. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Managerial Accounting for Travel Industry
description: Advanced study of management accounting within travel industry: responsibility accounting, pricing decisions, concepts and application of central systems, financial planning, price level impacts, performance evaluation. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Hospitality Management
description: Advanced human relations and operating issues; use of accounting, behavioral, financial, marketing, and informational systems in managing hospitality organizations. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Managerial Economics in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Advanced study analysis of economics and management of passenger transportation systems serving the travel industry. Emphasis on topics such as government policy, transport economics, marketing and management, and the relationships between transportation systems and tourism development. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Global Tourism Analysis
description: International trade theory and regional analysis methodologies applied to tourism and the service industry, including travel balance account, inter-regional transactions flow, economic impacts, environmental economics, demand theory and forecasting. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Financial Management in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Applications of financial analysis to both the domestic and international travel industry. TIM majors only. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation Field Studies
description: Integration of concepts and application of knowledge and skills from other courses to a selected field study project.
prerequisites: any two 600-level TIM courses completed and a third concurrent; or consent

subject: TIM
title: Professional Paper
description: Independent project or paper under faculty supervision in lieu of Plan A, TIM 700 thesis. Requires proposal approved by supervisor and graduate chair prior to registration. A-F only.
prerequisites: three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent

subject: TIM
title: Seminar: Travel Industry Management Policy
description: Integration of learning through analysis of policy issues, trends, and problems in the travel industry. A-F only.
prerequisites: three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent

subject: TIM
title: Directed Reading
description: Independent study of approved, advanced reading with faculty supervision. Requires proposal prepared by student and approved by supervisor and graduate chair before registration. Repeatable one time.

subject: TIM
title: Thesis Research
description: Independent supervised research. Formal and oral written presentation of research findings. Repeatable up to six credits.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Global Tourism Management
description: Sustainable management of global tourism to minimize its negative impacts and optimize its positive ones. Deliberation and analysis of major issues related to global tourism from the perspectives of ethics and sustainability. PhD students only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Global Hospitality Management
description: Advanced hospitality management aims to critically explore the key areas that comprise hospitality management, integrate theories and practice, and explore the linkages between hospitality research, management, and business strategies. PhD students only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Global Transportation Management
description: Transport economics and management, and their applications for the travel and tourism industry. Focuses on analytical thinking, problem-solving. and research skills using transportation issues. PhD students only. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B

subject: TAHR
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international or similar exchange program. CR/NC only.

subject: TAHR
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: DS. Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues. (Cross-listed as SOC 230 and SUST 250)

subject: TAHR
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: TAHR
title: Extension Education & Outreach
description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program development and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as TPSS 415)

subject: TRMD
title: One Health: Preparing for the Next Pandemic
description: DB. Focuses on the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study of a global health problem that is optimally approached from a One Health perspective. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as IS 350)
prerequisites: ANSC 200, BIOL 101, MICR 130, PH 201, or consent of instructor

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Journal Club
description: Students gain critical reading skills in the presentation and discussion of published literature on One Health-related topics. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as IS 395)

subject: TRMD
title: Health Disparities
description: Overview of biosciences research related to health and health disparities in a global setting as well as in Hawai‘i. Workshop topics include health research, Native Hawaiian health, global health, and cultural competency. MHIRT cohort only. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: TRMD
title: Medical and Urban Entomology
description: DB. (2 Lec, 1-3-hr hybrid Lab) Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases. (Cross-listed as PEPS 463)
prerequisites: (PEPS 363 or BIOL 265) with a minimum grade of C, or consent

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Practicum
description: Provide certificate students with real-world experience and opportunity to integrate and apply classroom learning in a professional environment. Intended for students who prefer to pursue a supervised, practical experience rather than a research-based project. A-F only. (Cross-listed as IS 485)

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Seminar
description: Weekly presentations and discussions on current events and research in the field of One Health. Presentation topics may include research progress, literature reviews, or research proposals. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as IS 490)

subject: TRMD
title: Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Elective for fourth-year medical students for advanced study of selected topics within the field of tropical medicine and medical microbiology.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases
description: Elective for medical students in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases. Repeatable six times, up to 12 credits. Medical students only. CR/NC only.

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only. CR/NC only.

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only. CR/NC only. (Fall only)

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Journal Club
description: Students gain experience in the presentation and discussion of topics of current interest in the fields of tropical medicine and infectious diseases. Repeatable unlimited times. Graduate students only.
degrees: Tropical Medicine and Medical Microbiology MS/PhD

subject: TRMD
title: Laboratory Methods in Tropical Medicine
description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety. Repeatable one time. Graduate standing only. A-F only. (Fall only)
degrees: Tropical Medicine and Medical Microbiology MS/PhD

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Micr
description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety. Repeatable one time. Graduate standing only. A-F only. (Fall only)
degrees: Tropical Medicine and Medical Microbiology MS/PhD

subject: REL
title: Women and Religion
description: DH. Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through autobiographies, films, and primary texts. (Cross-listed as WGSS 356)
prerequisites: 149 or WGSS 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151.

subject: REL
title: Love, Sex, and Religion
description: DH. Love and sex as themes in religions of Asia and the West.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Art
description: DH. The uses of art in religion are studied with historical examples.

subject: REL
title: Prophecies of the Last Days
description: DH. In-depth look at ancient Judeo-Christian apocalyptic texts and the communities in which they originated, followed by a survey of the medieval and modern day heirs of apocalyptic traditions.

subject: REL
title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
description: DH. Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as IP 373)
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: REL
title: Classical Hindu Mythology
description: DH. Study of major myths of Epic Sanskrit literature, primarily with focus of the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Literary sources will be tapped for appreciating myths and epics, especially with reference to dharma, karma, ways of life. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as IP 374)

subject: REL
title: Mysticism East and West
description: DH. Mystic traditions of the West from desert monasticism to Renaissance mystics compared with those of South and East Asia. Focuses on the ethical lives of these mystics, and developing oral communication skills.

subject: REL
title: Hawaiian Gods
description: DH. The traditions and practices related to one or more major indigenous gods, or class of gods, will be studied by the interpretation and analysis of primary texts. Develops written communication skills. Repeatable one time.

subject: REL
title: On Death and Dying
description: DH. Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves. (Crosslisted as COA 394)

subject: REL
title: Life and Teachings of Jesus
description: DH. Critical study of synoptic gospels and of extra-Biblical sources.

subject: REL
title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
description: DH. Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies. (Cross-listed as ANTH 422)

subject: REL
title: Health/Medicine in Religion
description: DH. Issues of health and disease in the light of religious beliefs and practices with a focus on ethical matters shaping policies in the U.S. and the world. A-F only.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Food
description: DH. Writing-based seminar exploring foodways as a basic component in the practice of religions. Examines theoretical issues, foodways as creators of community and identity, sustainability, and other ethical issues, abstinence and fasting, and healing. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: REL
title: Anthropology of Buddhism
description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ANTH 443)

subject: REL
title: Spiritual Ecology
description: DS. Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ANTH 444)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: REL
title: Sacred Places
description: DS. Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ANTH 445)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: REL
title: Sociology of Religion
description: DS. Seminar on research in sociological aspects of religious sectarianism, historical and current; special reference to Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as SOC 455)

subject: REL
title: Seminar on Buddhism
description: DH. Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Buddhism; topics and geographical focus to be announced each semester.

subject: REL
title: Daoism: Philosophy and Religion
description: DH. Seminar on religious Taoism, its historical development and its role in the present-day context.

subject: REL
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: DH. Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as ANTH 478 and LAIS 478)

subject: REL
title: Field Methods in Religion
description: Introduction to theoretical and methodological approaches to doing fieldwork in the study of religion. Application of these in studying Hawai‘i’s diverse religious environment.

subject: REL
title: Buddhism in Japan
description: DH. Major features and trends in thought, institutions, and practices in the context of Japanese history and culture, 6th–20th century.

subject: REL
title: Polynesian Religions
description: DH. Introduction to field, comparison of several traditions; beliefs and practices from analysis of texts. Historical interactions with Christianity.

subject: REL
title: Seminar in Religion
description: DH. Topics pre-announced each semester. Repeatable one time.

subject: REL
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Repeatable up to six credits. A-F only.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and department chair.

subject: REL
title: History and Theory of the Study of Religion
description: Survey of development of history of religions; application of methodologies from anthropology, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, and sociology.

subject: REL
title: Sacred Space
description: Introduces ways that sacred sites are used by religious adherents in Asia and the Pacific. Students will survey different methodologies, and develop a final project on a single sacred site. Graduate students only. (Alt years)
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: instructor consent.

subject: REL
title: The Study of the Ways Religion is Practiced
description: The study of rituals and practices in the religious traditions of Asia and the Pacific, with a focus on the importance and significance they play in people’s lives. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: instructor consent.

subject: REL
title: The Study of New Religious Movements
description: Seminar exploring methods developed for the study of New Religions, particularly in the U.S., Asia, and the Pacific. Considers implications of these methodologies for studies of other religious traditions. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: instructor consent.

subject: REL
title: Indigenous Religions & Decolonial Theories and Methods
description: Surveys decolonial approaches to the study of religion(s) and focuses on a specific Indigenous religion of Asia and the Pacific to examine the ways that historical paradigms have adversely influenced the study of Indigenous religions. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: instructor consent.

subject: REL
title: Healing in the Religious Traditions of Asia and the Pacific
description: Seminar focused on approaches to healing in the religious traditions of Asia and the Pacific. Explores commonalities between religious traditions, geographical areas, historical periods, and disciplines. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Graduate students only. Pre: instructor consent.

subject: REL
title: (Alpha) Seminar on East Asian Religions
description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in East Asian religions and traditions: (B) Chinese religions; (C) Japanese religions; (D) East Asian Buddhism. Repeatable up to six credits for (D), up to nine credits for (B) and (C). A-F only.

subject: REL
title: (Alpha) Seminar on South Asian Religions
description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Indian religious traditions: (B) Indian religions; (D) Indian Buddhism. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits for (B). A-F only

subject: REL
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Polynesian Religions
description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Polynesian and Hawaiian religious traditions: (B) Polynesian religions; (C) Hawaiian religion. Each alpha repeatable up to nine credits. A-F only.

subject: REL
title: (Alpha) Pedagogy in Religion
description: Theory, preparation, and practice in the teaching of religious studies at the community college level: (B) teaching religion; (C) teaching religion practicum. REL majors only. A-F only.

subject: REL
title: Plan B Research
description: Research for master’s degree Plan B. Restricted to students in the Religion Masters Program in Plan B. Enrollment must be approved by student’s project committee. A-F only.

subject: REL
title: Topics in Religious Studies
description: Topics in the study of religion with special emphasis on theoretical approaches and concerns. Specific topics to be preannounced. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years)

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: DS (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork. (Cross-listed as BOT 446)

subject: SUST
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ATMO 449 and CEE 449)
prerequisites: Senior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
description: DB (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota. (Cross-listed as BIOL 454)
prerequisites: one semester of biological sciences at college level.

subject: SUST
title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawai‘i. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as NREM 450)
prerequisites: BIOL 172 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Sovereignty in Pacific Context
description: DS Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context. (Cross-listed as ES 455C)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies. (Cross-listed as HWST 458 and NREM 458)
prerequisites: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/ SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356

subject: SUST
title: ‘Āina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as HWST 457)

subject: SUST
title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
description: DS Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources. (Cross-listed as ECON 458)

subject: SUST
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research. A-F only. (Cross-listed as HWST 459).

subject: SUST
title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawai‘i. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as HWST 460)

subject: SUST
title: Global Ethnic Conflict
description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. (Cross-listed as ES 460)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Pre: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Applied Forest Ecology
description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources). A-F only. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as NREM 480)
prerequisites: (SUST 311/NREM 310 and NREM 380) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: American Environmental History
description: DH Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present. (Cross-listed as AMST 425 and HIST 480)

subject: SUST
title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
description: DS Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ANTH 482)

subject: SUST
title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
description: DH Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ART 484)

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Problem Solving
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Senior-level capstone for NREM and related majors. Ecosystem management within problem-solving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications. NREM majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as NREM 494)

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability Capstone
description: Capstone for undergraduate students in interdisciplinary studies focusing on sustainability. The capstone experience provides an opportunity for students to gain knowledge and research experience in an applied setting. Repeatable one time. IS majors only. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: SUST
title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Crosslisted as EDCS 608)

subject: SUST
title: Seminar on Water in History
description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history. (Cross-listed as HIST 608)

subject: SUST
title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as NREM 611)
prerequisites: grade of C or above in ECON 130 or NREM/SUST 220, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings. A-F only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as NREM 612)
prerequisites: NREM 301/ SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600. Recommended NREM 461, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation.
