In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management. A-F only. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as NREM 610)

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Planning and Policy
description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PLAN 620)

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk. (Cross-listed as CEE 621 and ORE 621)
prerequisites: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

subject: SUST
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as EDCS 623)

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change. (Cross-listed as CEE 624 and ORE 624)

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the As

subject: SUST
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as EDCS 623)

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change. (Cross-listed as CEE 624 and ORE 624)

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via videoconferencing. (Cross-listed as PLAN 625)

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Geology
description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning. Repeatable one time, credit earned one time. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as ERTH 620)

subject: SUST
title: Urban Environmental Problems
description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems. (Cross-listed as PLAN 628)

subject: SUST
title: Planning in Hawai‘i and Pacific Islands
description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawai‘i, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as PLAN 632)

subject: SUST
title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options. (Cross-listed as ECON 636)
prerequisites: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development. (Cross-listed as ECON 637 and NREM 637)

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Resource Economics
description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development. (Cross-listed as ECON 638)

subject: SUST
title: Land Systems Science
description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socio-ecological system function. (Alt. years: Fall) (Cross-listed as NREM 640)
prerequisites: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461.

subject: SUST
title: Seminar
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field. (P) place-based education. Each alpha repeatable two times. COE-related majors only. (Cross-listed as EDCS 640P)
prerequisites: graduate and/or undergraduate courses in education and/ or social sciences or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as PLAN 647)

subject: SUST
title: Kānāwai Lawai‘a: Hawa‘i’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance. (Alt. years: Fall) (Cross-listed as HWST 652)

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate. (Cross-listed as NREM 658)

subject: SUST
title: He Ali‘i Ka ‘Āina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ‘Āina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ‘Āina future. (Cross-listed as HWST 659)

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips. (Cross-listed as BOT 661)

subject: SUST
title: Sociology of Sustainability
description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives. Graduate students only. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as SOC 670)

subject: SUST
title: Marine Renewable Energy
description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power. (Cross-listed as ORE 677)
prerequisites: ORE 607; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable.

subject: SUST
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ARCH 695)

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.

subject: SUST
title: Research Seminar: Agricultural Geography
description: (Cross-listed as GEO 763)

subject: TAHT
title: First Year Tahitian I
description: HSL Basic core skills of listening, speaking and grammar of spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

subject: TAHT
title: First Year Tahitian II
description: HSL Continuation of 101.

subject: TAHT
title: Second Year Tahitian I
description: HSL Intermediate core skills of listening, speaking and knowledge of grammar for spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

subject: TAHT
title: Second Year Tahitian II
description: HSL Continuation of 201.

subject: TAHT
title: Third-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of 202. Conversation, advanced reading, composition.

subject: TAHT
title: Third-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of 302. Advanced conversation, reading, and writing with focus on modern formal and colloquial Tahitian styles. The language in the realms of storytelling, radio, folklore, traditional and modern writing. Survey of modern and classical language.

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of 401.

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian Abroad
description: Full-time formal instruction at the University of French Polynesia in Tahiti. Fourth-year level in Tahitian language and culture. A-F only.

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian Abroad
description: Continuation of 458. A-F only.

subject: THAI
title: Elementary Thai I
description: HSL First semester of elementary Thai. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Thailand.

subject: THAI
title: Elementary Thai II
description: HSL Continuation of 101. Emphasizes reading, writing, listening, and speaking modern standard Thai. Structural points are introduced inductively. Regular on-line lab work and review of audiovisual materials.

subject: THAI
title: Second-Level Thai I
description: HSL Continuation of 102. Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Thai script.

subject: THAI
title: Second-Level Thai II
description: HSL Continuation of 201. Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading and writing in Thai script.

subject: THAI
title: Intensive Intermediate Thai
description: HSL

subject: THAI
title: Third-Level Thai I
description: Continuation of 202. Advanced conversation and reading, emphasis on modern written texts. Regular on-line lab work.

subject: THAI
title: Third-Level Thai II
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Third-Level Thai
description: Continuation of 202. Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading; emphasis on modern written texts. Lab work.

subject: THAI
title: Fourth-Level Thai I
description: Continuation of 302/303. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

subject: THAI
title: Fourth-Level Thai II
description: Continuation of 401.

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Thai
description: Continuation of 303. Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and r

subject: TI
title: Court Interpreting I
description: Introduction to the legal system, as well as theoretical principles, ethics, practical techniques, and current issues surrounding the practice and profession of court and other legal interpreting. Repeatable one time.

subject: TI
title: Community Interpreting
description: Basic principles, ethics and skills involved in community interpreting in medical, legal, and social service settings; practical information about the community interpreter’s role and profession; practice of various community interpreting situations and techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: TI
title: Court Interpreting II
description: Combined lecture/ discussion/practice. Continuation of 405 Court Interpretation, diving deeper into the practical side of oral interpreting for various proceedings, including arraignments, trials, witness testimonies, etc. Must be bilingual. Real courtroom observations required. Repeatable one time.

subject: TI
title: Medical Interpreting
description: Healthcare interpreting requires students to understand basic biosystems, common illnesses and treatments, as well as interpreting skills. Students must have 402 or above equivalency of second language skills (or instructor approval). Repeatable one time.

subject: TI
title: Consecutive Interpretation
description: Extensive note-taking and note-reading in a bilingual context. Focuses on the translation of numbers, acronyms, initials, and economic and financial information. (J) Japanese; (K) Korean; (M) Mandarin; (O) other; (S) Spanish. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: TI
title: Simultaneous Interpretation
description: Simultaneous interpretation of speeches. Focus on the study of formulaic and frozen language characteristically used in international meetings. (J) Japanese; (K) Korean; (M) Mandarin; (O) other; (S) Spanish. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: TI
title: Sight Translation
description: Focus on the ability to translate orally information from a written text. Emphasis on improving linguistic (discourse analysis) and communicative (public speaking) skills. (J) Japanese; (K) Korean; (M) Mandarin; (O) other; (S) Spanish. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: TI
title: Directed Reading/Studies
description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: International Exchange Programs
description: UH Mānoa School of Travel Industry Management majors participating in approved international exchange programs. CR/NC only.

subject: TIM
title: Internship I
description: Introduction to travel industry. Discussion of job search strategies, TIM internship requirements, career and academic planning. CR/NC only.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Travel Industry Management
description: Overview of travel industry and related major business components. Analysis of links between hotel, food, transportation, recreation, and other industries comprising tourism.

subject: TIM
title: Food and World Cultures
description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Food and World Cultures
description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Internship II
description: A minimum of four hundred hours of travel industry experience. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required. CR/NC only.

subject: TIM
title: Internship III
description: A minimum of four hundred hours of travel industry experience. Position must be different from TIM 200 position and of a more responsible nature or in a different organization. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required. CR/NC only.

subject: TIM
title: Legal Environment of the Travel Industry
description: Origin, development, and principles of common, statutory, constitutional, international, and maritime law relating to hospitality industry. TIM majors only. Recommended: BLAW 200.

subject: TIM
title: Information Systems Technology
description: Computer applications in the travel industry; operation and evaluation of specific travel industry systems and applied business systems. TIM majors only.
prerequisites: 101; and either ICS 101, or both LTEC 112 and LTEC 113

subject: TIM
title: Management of Service Enterprises
description: Principles and philosophies of management with special emphasis on those principles and theories that are most relevant to management in service-based industries. Students may not earn credit for 303 and BUS 315. TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Principles of Travel Industry Marketing
description: Concepts, problems, processes of marketing within the travel industry; development of marketing strategies including product, place, promotion, and price for travel institutions. Students may not earn credit for 304 and BUS 312. TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Financial Management for the Travel Industry
description: Cash flow determination and management strategies for financing hospitality ventures and expansion. Determining the financial viability of proposed and existing operations through traditional and state-of-the-art techniques. TIM majors only.
prerequisites: 101, ACC 200 and ACC 210; and NREM 203, MATH 203, MATH 215, MATH 241, or BUS 250.

subject: TIM
title: Human Resource Management: Travel Industry
description: Comprehensive overview of human resources management (HRM) with emphasis on the supervision in the travel industry, including HRM as a firm’s strategic asset, contemporary theories, issues and developments, to improve employee recruitment productivity and retention. TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Institutional Purchasing
description: Procurement responsibilities in hospitality management. Emphasis on institutions supplying hospitality operations and legislation which controls standards of industrial supplies and goods. TIM and FSHN majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Club Management
description: Introduction to club and institutional management, including operations, services, and facilities. TIM majors only. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Foodservice Management
description: Critical and essential aspects of managing foodservice operations including principles of food safety and sanitation, procedural knowledge in front and back of the house and guest relations. TIM majors only. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Hotel Management
description: Comprehensive understanding of hotel management and functional departments including front office, accounting, housekeeping, food and beverage, marketing, security and safety. Simulation of management trainee programs by hotel chains. Synthesis of concepts, tools and theories of decision-making relevant to hotel operations. TIM majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: 101, 302, and 303 (with a minimum grade of C- in 302 and 303).

subject: TIM
title: Quality Food Management
description: Explore various aspects of the quality in foodservice operations and develop strategies to measure and improve the quality. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Events Planning and Marketing
description: Introduction to special event planning processes and techniques. Emphasis on designing, planning, marketing, management, staging events, legal compliances, risk management, financial control, and successful event evaluation. TIM majors only. A-F only.

subject: TIM
title: Quantity Foods and Institutional Purchasing
description: Quantity food and beverage operations, menu development and costing, dietary menu claims, purchasing procedures, inventory control, procurement, transportation, legislation. Institutional foodservice sanitation, Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and National Restaurant Association Certification. TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development. TIM majors only. (Cross-listed as ECON 320)

subject: TIM
title: Sociocultural Issues in Tourism
description: Issues arising from the impacts of tourism on societies and cultures. Class discussions of the ethical dimensions of such impacts. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction. TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Geography of Global Tourism
description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. (Cross-listed as GEO 324)

subject: TIM
title: Travel Distribution Management
description: History, development, operations, and management of travel distribution organizations including: travel agents, tour operators and wholesalers, specialty channelers, meeting planners,

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment. A-F only.
prerequisites: 112 (or concurrent) or GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent)

subject: SUST
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Cities
description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability in a Changing World
description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawai‘i/Oceania. Active learning environment.

subject: SUST
title: Humans and the Environment
description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. A-F only. Students who successfully completed CHEM 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 120/CHEM 110 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 120/CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Food and Energy Field Course
description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawai‘i for sustainable development. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits.

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental History
description: Explores the influence of nature–climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms–on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

subject: SUST
title: Religion and the Environment
description: Examines the roles contemporary religious groups play in ground movements for sustainability. Introduces students to key scholars, religious leaders, and activists who are implementing sustainable solutions to pressing environmental problems. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change
description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors. (Fall only)
prerequisites: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Historical Ecology of Hawai‘i
description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: SUST
title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawai‘i as a model system.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupua‘a
description: Examination of the ahupua‘a system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the malama ‘aina track designed to build critical writing skills. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included. A-F only.

subject: SUST
title: Organic Food Crop Production
description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors. (Fall only)

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiians
description: The sustainable social system, culture, spirituality, language, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians. Transformation of the sustainable Hawaiian social system by a capitalist economy. Resiliency, land issues, and Native Hawaiian quest for sovereign governance.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

subject: SUST
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Environmental Humanities
description: Introduction to the environmental humanities, which rests at the intersection of the arts, humanities, and environmental studies.

subject: SUST
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawai‘i. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only. A-F only. (Alt years: Spring)

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Issues
description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
prerequisites: one of BIOL 101, BIOL 123, or GEO 101; or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Conservation Ethics
description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resources Management
description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife. A-F only. (Spring only)
prerequisites: (NREM/TPSS 251 or 210; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawai‘i state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues. A-F only.
prerequisites: SUST/ NREM/PEPS 210 or or NREM/SOCS/TPSS 251 or (BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or (ERTH 101 or higher); and NREM/SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses.

subject: SUST
title: Plant Conservation Biology
description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-inpractice in Hawai‘i and elsewhere. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components. A-F only. Co-requisite: BOT 301. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. A-F only. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Water and Society
description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
prerequisites: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Ethics
description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental problems.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development–Deaf
description: Assessment methods and techniques used with deaf students that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming through planning and providing cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Methods and Strategies for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Techniques for providing effective instruction including: best instructional practice, lesson planning, teacher-directed and student-mediated instructional strategies, and curricular approaches for working with students with mild/moderate disabilities. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development
description: Assessment methods and techniques that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming. Planning and cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment. SPED majors only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Assessment and Instruction—Severe Disabilities and Autism
description: Basic principles of assessment, instruction, and curriculum development; application of formal and informal assessment procedures for goal selection, formulating instructional plans, and adapting instructional materials to accommodate learning needs of students with severe disabilities and autism.

subject: SPED
title: Family-Centered Approaches in Deaf Education
description: Prepare teachers to deliver family-centered home-based services to families of deaf children using the SKI-HI model. Course will be taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Collaboration–Working with Deaf Students in Inclusive Settings
description: Collaboration skills for working with general education teachers, specialists, paraprofessionals, families and community members to support the success of deaf students in inclusive settings. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Transition Strategies for Deaf Students
description: Collaborative model for facilitating the transition of deaf and hard-of-hearing students to develop appropriate transition plans and effective plans of study. Taught in ASL and English. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Adaptations and Special ProceduresStudents/Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Adaptations and special intervention procedures to support the participation of individuals with severe motor, communication, and/or adaptive behavior disabilities in inclusive school and community settings. Includes lab work. SPED majors only. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Strategies Across Content Area
description: Strategies for teaching math, science, and social sciences to students of all ages with mild/moderate disabilities; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, curriculum development.

subject: SPED
title: Language Arts Strategies: Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Basic concepts related to language, language development, and recognition of language-related learning problems of students with mild/moderate disabilities; strategies for teaching language arts curricula (listening, speaking, reading, writing) to students of all ages with learning problems. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Children’s Literature for Deaf Students
description: Introduction to English literature translated into American Sign Language (ASL) including discussion of ASL literature genres, the importance of translation, selection of literature; story reading, book reading, and retelling. Taught in ASL. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: SPED
title: Teaching Skills for Social Competence
description: Issues in social development, self-determination, and social skills competence training for children and youth with disabilities; experience in group social skills training and development of individualized programs.
prerequisites: either 485 or 630, and either 611 or 614; or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Field Experiences in Special Education
description: Students spend a minimum of nine hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor. Repeatable three times. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Practicum
description: Supervised education/community experiences; minimum of 20 hours weekly with special-needs population (MR, LD, SED, SMH); pre-school through postsecondary settings (public/private). Related seminar or equivalent and completion of SPED core required. Repeatable one time.

subject: SPED
title: Internship
description: Supervised education/ community experiences with special needs populations, preschool through postsecondary settings. A-F only. Repeatable two times, up to six credits.

subject: SPED
title: Clinical Practice Special Projects
description: Development and implementation of a field-based research professional development project under the direction of the student’s advisor; limited to students enrolled in the interdisciplinary program. Repeatable up to 9 credits. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Positive Behavioral Support-Severe Disabilities and Autism
description: Principles and laws governing human behavior and positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems for students with severe disabilities and autism. Emphasis on the functions of behavior, experimental techniques for documenting behavior change, and the use of technologies for improving behavior in school and community settings. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Early Intervention for Special Populations
description: Issues important to early childhood special education. Early screening and assessment, working with families, curriculum options/models, program evaluation.

subject: SPED
title: Language/Communication Intervention- Communication Disorders/Autism
description: Current research in normal language learning, assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation of language delayed/disordered children, including children with autism. Procedures for attaining language/functional communication objectives using ongoing routines/activities.

subject: SPED
title: Motor Development/Intervention for Students with Severe Disabilities
description: Normal/ abnormal motor development; description/etiology of physically disabling conditions influencing motor development; analysis/application of assessment/intervention strategies to promote motor development; positioning and handling skills.

subject: SPED
title: Inclusive Physical Activity
description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan. A-F only. (Cross-listed as KRS 634)

subject: SPED
title: Procedures for Early Childhood Special Education
description: Assessment and intervention strategies to promote behavior change with young children with disabilities. Promoting child skill gains and integrated programming options. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Topics and Issues in Reading Difficulties
description: Introduction of foundational knowledge of language and literacy development. Current topics and issues related to literacy development in students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
description: Introduction of basic linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for beginning or struggling readers. Covers evidence-based practices for teaching literacy to students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
description: Advanced linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for older students. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with Dyslexia or related reading difficulties. Repeatable one time. A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Study of issues, research, program development in the area of mild/moderate disabilities. Repeatable two times.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Issues in Special Education
description: Seminar on issues, trends, research, and program development in the field of special education. (B) current issues and trends; (C) technology; (D) foundations; (E) developmental disabilities; (F) cultural and linguistic diversity; (G) evidence-based practices; (H) single case research. Repeatable one time per alpha, repeatable two times for (H). A-F only.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Applied Research/Special Education
description: Study and development of applied research topics in special education. Repeatable two times.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Severe/Multiple Disabilities
description: Research, program development trends/issues in the area of severe/multiple disabilities (birth through adulthood). College of Education majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Early Childhood Special Education
description: Study of issues/trends. Research and program development in early childhood special education. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: (631 and 635) with a minimum grade of B- or better, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Community-Based Planning
description: Planning and programmatic aspects of community-based development projects. East-West and local planning perspectives on participatory development and intentional communities.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Community Economic Development
description: Community-based economic development approaches and methods explored with an emphasis on low income communities. Repeatable one time.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Multiculturalism in Planning and Policy
description: Graduate seminar focuses on issues of governance, policy and planning in diverse multicultural societies. Differences in backgrounds, languages, privilege, preferences and values are often expressed in planning and policy controversies such as affirmative action and land use planning. Will examine these controversies and explore theories of governance in a multicultural setting.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Planning and Policy
description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 620)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as PACE 621)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment. (Cross-listed as GEO 622)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Coastal Planning and Management
description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture. Repeatable one time with consent. (Crosslisted as GEO 621)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Valuation and Policy
description: Build valuation skills to assess best use, conservation, and policies relating to environmental amenities. Provides an overview of policy solutions to environmental degradation used by planners.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via videoconferencing. (Cross-listed as SUST 625)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Topics in Resource Management
description: for different resource systems including land, water, energy, coastal resources, forests and fisheries. Course focus varies from year to year. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Negotiation and Mediation in Planning
description: Applicability and limitations of selected approaches; role of planners; impact on planning.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Environmental Problems
description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems. (Cross-listed as SUST 628)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills. Graduate standing only. Pre: one of the following courses with a minimum grade of B: 627; or PACE 429, PACE 447, PACE 477, PACE 647, PACE 652, or PACE 668; or COMG 455 or SOC 730; or LAW 508; or MGT 660. (Cross-listed as PACE 629)
prerequisites: one of the following courses with a minimum grade of B: 627; or PACE 429, PACE 447, PACE 477, PACE 647, PACE 652, or PACE 668; or COMG 455 or SOC 730; or LAW 508; or MGT 660
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia
description: Key issues and policies in urban planning, rural-urban relations, rural regional planning, and frontier settlement in Asia and the Pacific. Repeatable one time.
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Planning in Hawai‘i and Pacific Islands
description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawai‘i, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as SUST 632)
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Globalization and Urban Policy
description: Urbanization and urban policies in the Asia and Pacific region with focus on the international dimension of national and local spatial restructuring.
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Shelter and Services in Asia
description: Examines government and non-government organizations’ responses to urban and rural shelter issues and services in Asia.
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals. Pre: 310, 600, or ASAN 312. (Cross-listed as ARCH 687 and ASAN 636)
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Environment and Development
description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era. (Cross-listed as GEO 637)
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy. Graduate students only. (Cross-listed as GEO 639)
program: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia and the Pacific
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Land Use Policies and Programs
description: Land use public policy planning in urban and regional settings. Growth management and land use guidance systems. A-F only.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Neighborhood and Community Land Use Planning
description: Land use planning for urban neighborhoods and small towns. Theory and practice of neighborhood planning. Neighborhood and community dynamics, reinvestment, and stabilization.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Urban Infrastructure
description: Introduction to the planning of various urban infrastructures. Explores approaches and tools to plan, evaluate, and regulate urban infrastructure systems in support of sustainable and resilient cities and communities.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Project Planning and Management
description: Examines project management in theory and practice and the roles and responsibilities of the project manager. Focuses on planning, organizing, and controlling the efforts of projects. A-F only.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Land Use Planning
description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ARCH 641)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 647)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Transportation Policy and Planning
description: Theory and practice of urban transportation planning in developed and developing countries with an emphasis on the U.S., Asia, and Pacific region. A-F only.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form. Pre: 310 or ASAN 312. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ASAN 649)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Research Design Seminar
description: Research design and preparation of thesis proposal. Normally taken after admission to candidacy in MURP. Pre: (600 or 601 or 603) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.
prerequisites: (600 or 601 or 603) with a minimum grade of B, or consent
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Policy Implementation and Program Evaluation
description: Implementation and evaluation in public policy analysis; philosophical and methodological issues; impact of policies and plans; use of evaluation research in program implementation.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Applied Geographic Information Systems: Public Policy and Spatial Analysis
description: Use of advanced and specialized spatial methods and models in urban and regional planning. Uses GIS software and builds upon 601. Skills are useful applied to planning, economic development, and environmental planning and resource management. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only or consent.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Research Methods
description: Advanced methods and deterministic and stochastic models used in urban and regional planning.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: UNIV
title: Collaborative Learning: Foundations of Tutoring
description: Theory and practice of collaborative learning in academic contexts.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing or higher. Pre: consent.

subject: UNIV
title: Passages
description: Interactive course develops mentoring skills and relationships with peers, mentors, and “elders.” A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: UNIV
title: Topics in Major and Career Exploration
description: Major and career development for Exploratory students, using written and oral communication to facilitate learning across varied topics. A-F only.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. Exploratory students only. Pre: UNIV 340 or consent.

subject: UNIV
title: Mānoa Peer Advisor Leader Training and Leadership Practicum
description: A reflective apprenticeship in which Peer Advisor Leaders solidify their understanding of advising and learn more about leadership and deepen their facilitation, communication, collaboration, and leadership skills by mentoring a cohort of peer advisor trainees. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Summer only)
prerequisites: Pre: UNIV 350 (or equivalent course) (with a minimum grade of B).

subject: PLAN
title: Sustainable Cities
description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SUST 114)

subject: PLAN
title: Survey of Urban Sociology
description: DS Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawai‘i. (Cross-listed as SOC 301)
prerequisites: Pre: SOC 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Introduction to Planning
description: DS Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawai‘i planning–research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Directed Reading in Planning
description: Independent research on topics in urban and regional planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
description: Examines resilience thinking as it relates to making cities resilient to environmental hazards in the context of climate change. Draws on relevant theories, policy, and case studies in urban planning. Emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Geography
description: DS Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities. (Cross-listed as GEO 421)
prerequisites: Pre: GEO 102 or GEO 151 or GEO 330, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
description: DS Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning. (Cross-listed as ASAN 438)
prerequisites: Pre: PLAN 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Principles of Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015. Repeatable one time. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Spring only)

subject: PLAN
title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape. (Cross-listed as ASAN 449)
prerequisites: Pre: PLAN 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: GIS for Community Planning
description: Exploration of geographic information systems (GIS) area analysis techniques for spatial information management in community planning. Students will learn the basic concepts and principles, and practical skills of GIS through lectures, discussions, and labs. Repeatable one time.

subject: PLAN
title: Housing, Land, and Community
description: DS Analyzes availability for housing, particularly affordable housing, and its relationship to use of land and building of community. Examines public policies impacting housing, land use, and community development and ways they can be improved.

subject: PLAN
title: Public Policy and Planning Theory
description: Designed to a) impart a historic and comparative perspective on the evolution of urban and regional planning in public policy; b) explore the spatial and built environment dimensions of society, planning and policy; c) assess the justifications for planning and differing processes of planning in the U.S. and AsiaPacific with a focus on the role of the planner in policy formulation and implementation. Graduate students only or with permission. A-F only. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: Graduate students only or with permission.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Methods
description: Introduction of the basic methods in planning, including problem definition, research design, hypothesis testing, statistical reasoning, forecasting and fundamental data analysis techniques required by the planning program and the planning profession. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: PLAN and ARCH majors only. Pre: one of ECON 321, GEO 380, or SOC 476.

subject: PLAN
title: Advanced Planning Theory
description: Advanced planning theory for PhD students (others by petition) to prepare for careers in planning education and/or high level professional practice. Covers key contemporary planning policy issues and themes from the perspective of values, explanations of the real world, policy alternatives and implementation. Students must have passed 600 or equivalent (by petition) with a B or better. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: PhD students only or by consent. Pre: PLAN 600 (or equivalent) with a B or better, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Economics
description: Reviews and builds skills in applying basic theories and principles of urban and regional economics in contemporary U.S., Hawai‘i and Asia-Pacific. Repeatable one time.

subject: PLAN
title: Qualitative Methods in Planning
description: Provides a general introduction to qualitative research methods for planning and planning research. Includes data collection methods (focus groups, interviews, ethnography, participant observation, and participatory action research) and various analytic methods and approaches.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Models
description: Allocation, decision, derivation, and forecasting models used in the analysis of demographic, economic, land use, and transportation phenomena in urban and regional planning. Repeatable one time.

subject: PLAN
title: Comparative Planning Histories
description: Provides students with an overview of the history of urban and regional planning in the U.S., Europe, and Asia, and the role that planning has played in shaping contemporary urban settlements. Graduate standing only. A-F only.

subject: PLAN
title: Introduction to Public Policy
description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation. (Cross-listed as POLS 670)

subject: PLAN
title: Politics and Development: China
description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice. (Cross-listed as ASAN 608 and POLS 645C)

subject: PLAN
title: Causality in the Social Sciences: A Relatively Gentle Introduction
description: An introduction to the statistical methods used to identify plausibly causal effects with non-experimental data. A-F only. Pre: 601 or equivalent. (Alt. years)

subject: PLAN
title: Community Planning and Social Policy
description: Social issues and conditions; consequences of social policies experienced by different groups; community social plans and programs organized by various kinds of agencies and organizations. Repeatable one time.

subject: PLAN
title: Housing
description: Housing delivery systems as an aspect of urban and regional planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Community-Based Planning
description: Planning and programmatic aspects of community-based development projects. East-West and local planning perspectives on participatory development and intentional communities.

subject: PLAN
title: Community Economic Development
description: Community-based economic development approaches and methods explored with an emphasis on low income communities. Repeatable one time.

subject: PLAN
title: Multiculturalism in Planning and Policy
description: Graduate seminar focuses on issues of governance, policy and planning in diverse multicultural societies. Differences in backgrounds, languages, privilege, preferences and values are often expressed in planning and policy controversies such as affirmative action and land use planning. Will examine these controversies and explore theories of governance in a multicultural setting.

subject: TPSS
title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawai‘i and the tropics. TPSS majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ARCH 634)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Advanced Soil Chemistry
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Physio-chemical processes in soils and soil solutions, with emphasis on ionic equilibria, mineral stability, organic complexation, and surface sorption of major plant nutrients and heavy metals. A-F only.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Soil Plant Nutrient Relations
description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Soil-plant interactions, emphasis on characteristics of tropical soils and plants influencing nutrient uptake by plants. Diagnostic methods to identify nutrient deficiencies and element toxicity. (Cross-listed as NREM 650)
prerequisites: 450 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Information Research Skills
description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences. (Cross-listed as ANSC 652, FSHN 652, and NREM 652)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Communications in the Sciences
description: (3-hr Lec/Lab combination) Laboratory-type course for improving communication abilities in the sciences and engineering. Presentations to lay audiences are emphasized. Hands-on experience in techniques and methods is provided.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design. TPSS and LAND majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ARCH 656)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent. (Cross-listed as ANSC 657 and FSHN 657)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes. TPSS majors only. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ARCH 658)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Orchidology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Classification, culture, cytogenetics, breeding of orchids. Recommended: 200/SUST 211 and 402.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Graduate Seminar
description: Presentation of research reports; reviews of current literature in plant and soil sciences. Repeatable four times.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Sustainability of Food Systems
description: Explores sustainability and resilience of food systems with an emphasis on Hawai ʻi, using interdisciplinary approaches to assess impacts. Repeatable one time. Pre: consent. (Alt. years: fall)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Growth and Development
description: Contemporary literature is used as the basis for understanding the physiology for whole plant growth and development. Aspects covered include vegetative and reproductive development, seed dormancy, senescence, abscission, and relevant biochemical and molecular processes.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included. A-F only. (Cross-listed as GEO 680)
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed. A-F only.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Directed Research
description: In-depth study of specialized problems. Repeatable unlimited times. CR/ NC only.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Thesis Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Special Topics
description: Specialized topics from various areas of plant and soil research such as experimental techniques, growth regulation, morphogenesis, genetics and breeding, culture and nutrition of tropical crops. A-F only.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times. CR/NC only.
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: UROP
title: Transformational Research Experiences for Early Undergraduates
description: Introduction to exploring discover-based investigation, with hands-on experiences in a wide range of science fields. Divided into 4-week learning modules led by researchers at several UH Mānoa research facilities on and off campus. Repeatable one time. CR/NC only. (Cross-listed as HON 299)

subject: UROP
title: Faculty Mentored Research and Creative Work Project
description: Directed research for undergraduate students conducting faculty-mentored research or creative work projects. Repeatable three times, up to ten credits. CR/NC only. (Summer only)
prerequisites: consent of UROP director and student faculty mentor.

subject: UNIV
title: University Experience
description: An introduction to the university community; topics include critical thinking, the value of higher education, cultural and transition issues. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Academic and Personal Exploration
description: Seminar introduces students to goal setting, time management, major exploration, academic planning, service-learning opportunities, student/faculty meetings, financial literacy, and encourages frequent self-reflection. Instructor approval required. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Academic and Career Exploration
description: Seminar introduces exploratory students to major and career exploration resources, guides students in developing personal, academic, and career goals and plans, and encourages frequent self-reflection. Develops written communication skills. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Introduction to Majors and UH Mānoa
description: Major exploration providing incoming students with an understanding of the tools to navigate UH Mānoa and explore the programs of study available. Introduction to career development, goal setting, and action planning. Freshmen only. Exploratory majors only. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Topics in Learning Techniques & Technologies
description: Student-centered topics on techniques and technologies used for successful learning. Emphasizes the cultivation of learning dispositions and strategies for achievement in higher education and beyond. Repeatable unlimited times. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Your Academic Journey
description: Provides exploratory students with the knowledge/skills to thrive in college and beyond. Utilizes writing as a tool for research, analysis, exploration, and reflection. Topics include major and career exploration, personal interests, and goal-setting. May not be taken concurrently or after UNIV 340. Freshmen and sophomores only. Exploratory designations only. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: ACE Mentoring: Facilitating Student Development
description: Theoretical foundations in student learning and holistic development. Practical leadership skills acquisition and application through the facilitation of a seminar for new freshmen. Emphasis on developing proficiency in writing and public speech. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Pre: consent. (Fall only)

subject: UNIV
title: Metacognitive Strategies for College Success
description: Theories of the memory processes and the application of the Information Processing Systems in developing metacognitive strategies for college classroom success. Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Academic Exploration Through Advising
description: Major exploration designed to assist exploratory students in the process of researching personal, career, and educational goals through writing and the impact of these goals on the decision-making process. Emphasis on written self-reflection and identity. Sophomore standing. A-F only.

subject: UNIV
title: Mānoa Peer Advisor Training Course
description: Intensive course designed for peer advisor trainees to learn General Education requirements, university policies and procedures, and campus resources. Trainees also develop skills and strategies necessary to provide quality advising to their fellow students. A-F only (Summer only)

subject: UNIV
title: Collaborative Learning: Foundations of Tutoring
description: Theory and practice of collaborative learning in academic contexts. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: UNIV
title: Passages
description: Interactive course develops mentoring skills and relationships with peers, mentors, and “elders.” Sophomore standing or higher. A-F only. (Summer only)

subject: UNIV
title: Topics in Major and Career Exploration
description: Major and career development for Exploratory students, using written and oral communication to facilitate learning across varied topics. Junior standing or higher. Exploratory students only. A-F only.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course. (Cross-listed as ASAN 336)

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Topics in Theatre Production
description: DA Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing exercises, color theory, and practical projects; (E) props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre. Repeatable one time for different alphas, each alpha can be taken one time. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: any course in THEA or DNCE, or production experience; or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Lighting I: Beginning Lighting Design
description: DA Basic principles of lighting design and associated technologies. Includes functions and properties of light, lighting and control equipment, working procedures, and drafting and paperwork techniques. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as DNCE 345)

subject: THEA
title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
description: DA Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process. (Consent required for production experience option) (Cross-listed as CINE 353 and DNCE 353)
prerequisites: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Costume Construction
description: DA Workshop on basic principles of costume construction for theatre and dance. Professional practices, materials, and methods. (Cross-listed as DNCE 354)

subject: THEA
title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
description: DA Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as CINE 356 and DNCE 356)

subject: THEA
title: Stage Makeup Workshop
description: DA Western and traditional Asian makeup theory and application practice. Western corrective, period, and old age makeup. Asian may include Jingju, Kabuki, Wayang. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Performance and Medicine
description: DS Survey of key texts on medicine and performance, and on how these two areas intersect, including representations of medicine and illness in contemporary drama and performance-based practices within medicine. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Curtain Up! Broadway Musicals, Then and Now
description: DH Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the recent “Hamilton” phenomenon, and explores their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts. (Cross-listed as MUS 362)

subject: THEA
title: Movement Improvisation
description: Introduces movement improvisation to all levels and disciplines. Movement studies will explore improvisation approaches, devices, elements, exercises, and implications to gain skills in and appreciation for the art of improvisation. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as DNCE 370)

subject: THEA
title: Beginning Directing
description: DA Basic practical course in how to direct a play. Students will direct scenes. Emphasis on writing instruction. THEA and DNCE majors only.
prerequisites: upper division theatre majors or consent.

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Advanced Practicum
description: Advanced workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography. Repeatable up to four credits per alpha. (Cross-listed as DNCE 400)
prerequisites: audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production for (B); 200C for (C); 200D for (D); 200E for (E); 200B or 200C or 200F, and consent for (F).

subject: THEA
title: World Theatre: Elite and Popular
description: DL Interplay between elite and popular forms to 1900. Develops written communication skills. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: World Theatre: Modern
description: DL Pluralism in modern theatre, 1900–present. Reactions to realism and current international theatre forms, develops written communication skills. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Approaches to Dramatic Texts
description: DL Intensive analysis and discussion of dramatic texts from a variety of authors. Understanding trends and variations in dramatic form and content. (B) contemporary British and American drama; (C) political drama in the West.

subject: THEA
title: Women, Gender, & Sexuality in Performance
description: DH Feminist and performance studies approaches to performances by women and other genders; focus on the representation and status of women Pre: 311 or consent. (Cross-listed as WGSS 414) DH

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Playwriting
description: DA Workshop in experimental writing in dramatic form; full-length plays. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Intermediate Voice for the Actor
description: DA Training in proper and dynamic use of the voice for the actor. (B) Western traditions; (C) Asian traditions. Repeatable two times.

subject: THEA
title: Musical Theatre
description: DA Training in skills required to perform in musicals. Students present scenes from musical comedies for criticism and review. Repeatable two times with consent. (Cross-listed as MUS 421)
prerequisites: one of 321, 322, MUS 231B, or consent; and/or audition.

subject: THEA
title: Period Styles in Acting
description: DA Presentational acting in comedy and tragedy; emphasis on performance styles in Elizabethan, Restoration, and 18th-century drama. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Acting Shakespeare
description: DA Techniques for acting in Shakespearean and heightened language texts. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Hawaiian Performance Workshop
description: DA Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Hawaiian performance forms and Hawaiian medium theatre. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Crosslisted as DNCE 424)
prerequisites: one of: 101, 221, 224, 468, HAW 202, HAW 321, HAW 384, HAW 486, DNCE 312, DNCE 411, DNCE 412; or consent.

subject: THEA
title: South/Southeast Asian Acting Workshop
description: DA Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional south and southeast Asian theatre forms. Emphasis on movement and vocal techniques. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Chinese Acting Workshop
description: DA Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Chinese theatre forms. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique. Repeatable to six credits. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Japanese Acting Workshop
description: DA Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Japanese theatre forms. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique. Repeatable to six credits. (Alt. years) DA

subject: THEA
title: Contemporary Performance Practices
description: DA Focus on individual training in the skills and techniques of contemporary experimental theatre including acting, directing, and self-scripting. Repeatable two times.
