subject: THEA
title: Stage Combat
description: DA Techniques for performing unarmed and armed stage combat. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Movement Workshop
description: DA Special workshops in movement relating to specific departmental theatrical productions beyond the scope of movement taught in 437 and 438. Repeatable one time. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as DNCE 433)

subject: THEA
title: Taiji (T’ai Chi) for Actors II
description: DA Intermediate-level Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) movement training. Repeatable two times. (Cross-listed as DNCE 434)

subject: THEA
title: Movement for Actors
description: DA Training actors to discover experientially the sources of movement; to teach skills for analyzing movement for its mechanical, anatomical, spatial, and dynamic content; and then to apply these skills in a role. (Cross-listed as DNCE 435)

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Movement for Actors
description: DA Detailed development of material presented in 435. Focus on Bartenieff fundamentals and movement analysis as it applies to the physical interpretation of theatrical roles. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as DNCE 436)

subject: THEA
title: Musical Theatre Dance Forms
description: DA Theatrical dance forms used in 20th-century musical theatre. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as DNCE 439)
prerequisites: 100 level or above dance technique class, 421, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Topics in Costume Construction
description: DA Costume production techniques, both Western and Asian, for theatre and dance. Topic rotation includes: understructures and armatures, patterning, tailoring, dyeing, fabric modification, millenery and crafts, within the context of current industry practice. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 446)

subject: THEA
title: Stage Management
description: Business, organization and management for theatre and dance productions. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: DS Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society. A-F only. (Fall only) (Crosslisted as SOC 367 and SUST 367)
prerequisites: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: DH Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as ES 391)
prerequisites: one DS or DH course, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Women and the Media
description: DS Media portrayal of women and men; role of the media in reproducing gender inequality. Women as producers and consumers of media. Feminist alternatives to mainstream media.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality and Literature
description: DL Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literary constructions of gender and sexuality; emphasis on teaching gender and sexuality through writing and oral communication. (Cross-listed as ENG 382)
prerequisites: one ENG DL course or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Island Feminisms: Art, Literature, and Culture
description: DH Examines island feminisms and explores ways women have engaged in various forms of cultural production (art, literature, film). Interdisciplinary, intersectional, and transnational. Key themes discussed: settler-colonialism, race, gender, and sexuality.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Politics
description: DS Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries; female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions. (Cross-listed as POLS 384)
prerequisites: 151 (or concurrent) or 362 (or concurrent) or any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent); or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: DS Historical and sociological studies of race and gender in U.S. society; grassroots feminist and racial/justice activism on the continent and in Hawai‘i. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ES 390)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Sexualities
description: DS Multi-disciplinary course draws from psychology, sociology, biology, history, cultural anthropology, law, Hawaiian, ethnic, feminist, gender, and queer studies to explore human sexualities with emphasis on the U.S., Hawai‘i and the AsiaPacific regions. A-F only.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives
description: DS Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change. A-F only. (Cross-listed as POLS 394)
prerequisites: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or POLS 390 (or concurrent) or WS 151, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Directed Reading
description: Repeatable eight times, up to 45 credits.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ASAN 410)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Women, Gender, & Sexuality in Performance
description: DH Feminist and performance studies approaches to performances by women and other genders; focus on the representation and status of women. (Cross-listed as THEA 414)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Work
description: DS Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global. (Cross-listed as ES 418 and SOC 418)
prerequisites: one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or SOC 300; or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy
description: DH Examination of basic feminist issues in philosophy, and of responses to them. (Cross-listed as PHIL 418)
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WS, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality and Digital Media
description: DH Students learn how gender and sexuality are constructed online and produce a website to post their analysis and contribute to knowledge production about gender and sexuality in cyberspace. A-F only.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
description: DS Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ANTH 426)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Seminar in the Biology of Women
description: DB Embryological, anatomical, and physiological development of human female; hormonal, neural, and behavioral determinants of female sexual behavior; psychobiology of pregnancy, ovariectomy, and menopause.
prerequisites: 350 or BIOL 172 or BIOL 350, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
description: DS Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication. A-F only. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as GEO 433)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Madness
description: DS Interdisciplinary critical examination of the relationship between gender and mental health. Psychological research, feminist theory, autobiography, literature, and cinema.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Crime
description: DS Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system. Recommended: at least one WS course. (Cross-listed as SOC 435)
prerequisites: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: DS Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom. A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 436 and POLS 368)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Violence
description: DS Interdisciplinary course will examine western constructs of gender violence on its correlates with ethnicity, class, sexuality, nation, and empire. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Environmental Philosophy
description: DH Interdisciplinary approach to feminist perspectives on environmental issues; critical analysis of eco-feminism as political movement with reference to race and coloniality; cross-cultural comparison of differently-imagined relationships to non-human others, with emphasis on ethics and writing. (Cross-listed as PHIL 438)
prerequisites: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS or any course 200 or above with a DB or DP designation, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Theory
description: DS Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.” (Crosslisted as POLS 339)
prerequisites: any 300 level WS or POLS course, or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Methods and Research
description: DS Overview of feminist issues with dominant theories of knowledge and major methodologies employed in the social sciences; and exploration of role of gender theory and feminist politics in feminist research.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Queer Theory
description: DH Intensive survey of the key theories, texts, and questions of the interdisciplinary fields that make up queer theory.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Consumption in a Global World
description: DH Students learn theories of the global economy, histories of consumerism, constructions of gendered public spaces, and how the cultural production of consumers and consumer culture functions in the process of globalization. A-F only.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: DL Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities. (Cross-listed as AMST 455 and ENG 455)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
description: DS Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives. (Cross-listed as SOC 446)
prerequisites: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, SOC 300; or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
description: DS Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 448 and ES 450)
prerequisites: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Marriage and Family: Feminist Perspective
description: DS Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. Recommended: at least one WS course. (Cross-listed as SOC 452)
prerequisites: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

description: DS Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close a
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: THAI
title: Intensive Intermediate Thai
description: HSL. listening, speaking, reading and writing in Thai script.

subject: THAI
title: Third-Level Thai I
description: Continuation of 202. Advanced conversation and reading, emphasis on modern written texts. Regular on-line lab work.

subject: THAI
title: Third-Level Thai II
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Third-Level Thai
description: Continuation of 202. Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading; emphasis on modern written texts. Lab work.

subject: THAI
title: Fourth-Level Thai I
description: Continuation of 302/303. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

subject: THAI
title: Fourth-Level Thai II
description: Continuation of 401.

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Thai
description: Continuation of 303. Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

subject: THAI
title: Thai Language in the Media
description: Development of reading and aural comprehension of authentic Thai language used in print and broadcast media through reading Thai newspapers, viewing and listening to Thai television and radio programs. Oral and written reports. Repeatable one time.

subject: THAI
title: Structure of Thai
description: DH Introduction to information structure of Thai as a basis for developing reading skills. Analysis of rhetorical, sentence, and word structure from different types of written texts.

subject: THAI
title: Structure of Thai
description: DH Continuation of 451.

subject: THAI
title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Short Story
description: DL Selected readings in Thai short stories from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970- present. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THAI
title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Novel
description: DL Selected readings in Thai novels from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews. (B) 1930–1969; (C) 1970– present. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Stage, Screen, and New Media Writing
description: FW Introduction to college level writing and information literacy for and about the stage (theatre, dance, performance), the screen (film, television), and new media (digital platforms, social media). A-F only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 100)

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to World Drama and Theatre
description: DA (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Performance traditions of Africa, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and the Pacific from the 5th century B.C. to the present. Analysis of political, religious, and technological conditions of theatre. Includes practical theatre workshop. Emphasis on writing instruction. A-F only.

subject: THEA
title: Live on Stage
description: DH Students view locally produced theatre and dance productions and write performance reviews. Readings, writing, and class discussion will guide students to understand each performance. Performances include theatre, dance, musical theatre, opera, and performance art. Repeatable one time. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as DNCE 152)

subject: THEA
title: Beginning Practicum
description: DA Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography. Repeatable up to four credits in each alpha. (Cross-listed as DNCE 200)
prerequisites: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to the Art of the Film
description: DH Introduction to the aesthetics of silent and sound movies. Technical subjects analyzed only as they relate to theme and style.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Long-Form Improvisation
description: DA Introduction to long-form improvisation as developed by companies such as Second City and iO Chicago. Focus will be on games, situations, creating characters, and forming narratives from those elements. Repeatable two times.

subject: THEA
title: Development of the Sound Film
description: DH Growth and changes in aesthetics of the sound film from 1929 to present; films by Renoir, Welles, Eisenstein, etc. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Beginning Voice and Movement
description: DA Introduction to vocal and movement techniques to increase self-awareness and potential for self-expression. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Acting for Stage and Screen
description: DA Beginning acting techniques for theatre and screen media including exercises, improvisations, monologues, and scenes. Focus on voice, relaxation, body awareness, and freedom from self-consciousness. Emphasis on writing instruction as appropriate to discipline. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Acting I: Foundations and Techniques for Stage and Screen
description: DA Fundamentals of contemporary acting styles for stage and screen, including self-awareness, character, and scene work. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Pidgin/HCE Drama
description: DA Introduction to Hawaiian Creole English (HCE) multicultural comedy and drama in Hawai‘i. Emphasis on acting exercises, local dialects, and the performance of Pidgin/HCE plays. Repeatable one time with consent. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Stage Production
description: DA Survey class introducing theater management, lighting, costuming, scenery, and other aspects of theatre that relate to producing stage performances. (Cross-listed as DNCE 240)

subject: THEA
title: Theatre Production Lab
description: Lab observations and projects illustrating basic principles of theatre production. A-F only. Co-requisite: 240.

subject: THEA
title: Film/TV Production Process
description: DA Entry-level course details three phases of the production process for film and video projects: pre-production, production, and post-production. A-F only.

subject: THEA
title: Principles of Design
description: DA Introduction to general design principles as applied to theatre. Will introduce the language and tools of visual literacy and visual communications via individual projects and collaboration. Repeatable two times. (Cross-listed as DNCE 245)

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Voice Function and Singing Styles
description: DH, DA Students will study how the singing voice works in various styles, including classical, musical theater, jazz, choral, and pop/ rock. Students will learn historical contexts, aural characteristics, and musical vocabulary through lecture, discussion, and listening. (Fall only) (Cross-listed as MUS 259)

subject: THEA
title: World Theatre I: Script Analysis
description: DL Script analysis methods for world drama. Develops written and oral communication skills. Required of all majors.

subject: THEA
title: World Theatre II: Myth to Drama
description: DL Myth and ritual into drama, 1000 BCE–1700 CE. Development of secular drama from sacred and ritual beginnings. Required of all majors. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Playwriting
description: DA One-act plays; practice in writing in dramatic form. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: grade of B or better in composition or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Screenplay Writing
description: DA Characterization, structure, theme, image, and other components of writing for film. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: 201 and grade of B or better in composition, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Auditioning
description: DA Preparation of material from different audition situations, including monologues, cold readings, dance, singing, and TV/ film. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Acting II: Advanced Scene Study
description: DA Further exploration of character development and dramatic action through textual analysis. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Film/TV Acting
description: DA Acting techniques for film and TV production. Students appear in scenes from TV and film scripts. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 101 or 221 or 222 or COM 201 or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Film/TV Acting
description: DA Advanced acting techniques for film and TV production. Taping/filming of scenes and full-length scripts. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Asian Acting Styles
description: DA Principles of acting based on traditional Asian models. Voice, movement exercises.

subject: THEA
title: Taiji (T’ai Chi) for Actors I
description: DA Basic Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) movement training. Repeatable two times. Sophomore standing or higher. (Cross-listed as DNCE 334)

subject: THEA
title: Taiji Round Form for Actors
description: DA Introduction to basic Asian movement skills through learning the Wu-style taijiquan round form, a faster and more fluid version of the full 108 taiji sequence of forms. Open to non-majors. Repeatable two times. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course. (Cross-listed as ASAN 336)

subject: THEA
title: Topics in Theatre Production
description: DA Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre

subject: WGSS
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher. A-F only. (Cross-listed as AMST 448 and ES 450)
prerequisites: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Marriage and Family: Feminist Perspective
description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. Recommended: at least one WS course. (Cross-listed as SOC 452)
prerequisites: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper. (Cross-listed as EDCS 453 and EDEF 453)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and Global Popular Culture
description: A study of gender, race, and sexuality as constructed in contemporary global popular culture, including music, films, novels, television shows, and internet culture. A-F only. Junior standing or higher.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries. A-F only. (Cross-listed as ES 457)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Feminism, Nation and Empire
description: Examines U.S. feminist movements in the 19th and 20th century by exploring how U.S. racism, nationalism and imperialism have provided the context from which feminism emerged. A-F only.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory. (Crosslisted as AMST 438 and POLS 372)
prerequisites: one of 360, 361, 439, AMST 310, AMST 316, AMST 318, AMST 373, AMST 455, POLS 339; or consent.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g. with class, religion, ethnicity). (Cross-listed as ASAN 463)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as ANTH 465)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Gender in Action Cinema
description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. (Cross-listed as AMST 446)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Film
description: Exploration of film as a philosophical and artistic form in the context of gender, race, and sexuality.
prerequisites: one of 151, 175, 176, or THEA 201; or consent.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Indigenous Feminisms
description: Examines the origins and futures of Indigenous feminist theory and praxis. Topics explored include cultural revitalization, colonialism, and sexual violence in Indigenous communities, citizenship and sovereignty, and contemporary Native gender roles and identity.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
description: Intensive study of selected problems and issues in the construction and representation of sexuality and gender in specific genres, social and cultural contexts, thematic or figurative clusters. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as ENG 482)
prerequisites: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Disasters
description: Explores disasters and their consequences for women, with attention to gender, race, sexuality, and class. A-F only. Junior standing or higher.
prerequisites: at least one course in WS, or consent of instructor.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; repeatable two times, up to 12 credits. (Cross-listed as SOC 494 and SOCS 489)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons. (Cross-listed as ASAN 492 and HIST 492)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/masculine/ gender nonconforming/sexual)
description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration. Junior standing or higher. (Cross-listed as AMST 437)
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Selected Topics
description: Problems and issues for reading and research: feminist theory, criticism, affirmative action, etc. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: any WS course in appropriate area.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Teaching Women’s Studies
description: Strategies for teaching women’s studies; addressing complex issues of gender, race, nation, class, sexuality and culture in a contemporary multiethnic campus environment. Emphasis on classroom techniques, teaching pedagogies, and hands-on experience. Repeatable one time. A-F only.
prerequisites: 151 and one or more WS course with a grade of B or better in all relevant courses, instructor recommendation; or consent.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable one time, up to six credits. WS students only.
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Transnational Feminist Teaching and Research
description: Introductory graduate seminar designed to develop common vocabulary and explore the core debates in transnational feminist teaching and research to encourage critical reflection about teaching assumptions, approaches, and techniques in the contemporary college or university environment. A-F only. Graduate students only.

description: Seminar/discussion to introduce students pursuing the Graduate Certificate to the Woman’s Studies faculty and their areas of research, and to initiate student’s graduate studies in a woman’s studies field. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only.
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method. (Cross-listed as AMST 612)
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Research and Methods of Inquiry
description: Examination of an emergent body of literature about how to shape questions concerning gender, sex, race, class, colonialism, and other vectors of power. Includes methods from social sciences and humanities and debates in the philosophy of science. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only.
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts. (Cross-listed as AMST 615)
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Theory
description: Selected ideas from contemporary feminist theory concerning power, knowledge, and self; articulating women’s voice; deconstructing gender. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as POLS 615C)
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Writing and Publishing in an Interdisciplinary Field
description: Writing-intensive and publishing-focused class, students learn how to publish in an interdisciplinary field. Readings and assignments are designed to help students succeed in academic publishing. Graduate students only. A-F only.
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Feminism and Its “Others”
description: Relationship between feminist and other sites of critical insight and scholarship that have contributed to creating anticolonial, antiracist, antihomophobic theory, method and action. Questions the legacy of feminist coalition practices and engages the ongoing transformations that have begun to produce new alliances and coalitions that disrupt traditional boundaries of identity and power. A-F only. Graduate students only.
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Topics in Feminist Social Policy Research
description: Feminist social scientists from a variety of fields have explored issues of gender, social change and social justice. Draws from their work to critically examine strategies for conducting social policy research that is feminist in values and impact. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Graduate students only.
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Criminology
description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 625)
certificates: Graduate Certificate in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
department: Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Department

Draws from their work to critically examine strategies for conducting social policy research that is feminist in values and impact. Repeatable one time. A-F only. Graduate students only.

description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls. A-F only. (Cross-listed as SOC 625)

description: Advanced graduate seminar on the key ideas within queer theory. Students will become familiar with theories of queer relationality, queer of color critique, globalization of sexuality, disability and transgender studies, and queer indigeneities.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region. (Cross-listed as LAW 547 and PACE 637)

subject: WGSS
title: Research in Feminist Studies: Capstone Experience
description: Provide women’s studies graduate certificate students with an opportunity to design, develop and complete a research project culminating in a publishable quality work and a professional quality seminar presentation. A-F only. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Literature
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional. Repeatable one time for (M). A-F only for (M). (Cross-listed as CHN 753 (Alpha))
prerequisites: WGSS 613, WGSS 615, WGSS 650, or EALL 611; or consent for (M); CHN 612 or consent for (T).

subject: ZOOL
title: Principles of Zoology
description: Structure, development, physiology, reproduction, evolution, behavior, and ecology of animals.

subject: ZOOL
title: Principles of Zoology Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany 101.

subject: ZOOL
title: Marine Biology
description: Biology and ecology of marine plants and animals; coral reefs, the deep sea, rocky shores, marine mammals, fisheries, aquaculture, pollution, and conservation of marine resources.

subject: ZOOL
title: Marine Biology Lab
description: Laboratory, field trips to accompany 200.

subject: ZOOL
title: Parasitology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany 340.

subject: ZOOL
title: Developmental Biology
description: Fundamental principles, methods, concepts, and significance of developmental biology, emphasizing experimental methods.

subject: ZOOL
title: Developmental Biology Lab
description: Analysis of animal development by experimental methods, using local organisms.
prerequisites: ZOOL 420 (or concurrent) and BIOL 275, or consent. Recommended: BIOL 407.

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Physiology
description: Lecture/laboratory introduction to animal physiology, especially vetebrates. Topics include nerve and muscle physiology, metabolism, circulation, respiration, excretion, thermoregulation in a project-driven format. Labs develop skills in experimental biology, morphology, data analysis, and scientific writing. A-F only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Comparative Physiology
description: Physicalchemical cellular mechanisms underlying function of organ systems; general principles inferable from study of adaption to diverse environments.
prerequisites: BIOL 171 and 172, and MBBE 402 (or concurrent) or BIOC 441 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Introduction to Neuroscience
description: Nerve cells, their signaling capabilities and the developmental organization of nervous systems, both invertebrate and vertebrate, for sensory reception, integration, behavioral command and learning;insights from on-going research using molecular, genetic, biophysical, and imaging methods. (Spring only)

subject: ZOOL
title: Avian Biology
description: Broad coverage of the morphology, physiology, ecology, behavior, and evolution of birds, emphasizing the relation of birds to general theory in biology.

subject: ZOOL
title: Biology of the Invertebrates Lab
prerequisites: BIOL 172 and CHEM 161, or consent. Co-requisite: ZOOL 475.

subject: ZOOL
title: Biogeography
description: Distribution of plants and animals and processes that cause, maintain, and modify them. Approach is synthetic and dynamic.

subject: ZOOL
title: Seminar in Zoology
description: Reports on research, reviews of literature, or research experience. Required of students majoring in zoology or entomology. (B) general zoology; (D) animal behavior; (E) ecology; (F) physiology; (G) developmental biology; (H) marine biology. Repeatable 2 times per alpha, credits earned for 3 credits only.
prerequisites: ZOOL 306 or equivalent or consent for (D).

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Behavior
description: Lectures and critical discussions on the mechanisms of animal behavior, social and interspecific behaviors, behavioral ecology, and evolutionary theory. Graduate students only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Principles of Animal Behavior Lab
description: Group or individual research projects depending on interest of students.

subject: ZOOL
title: Genetics of Behavior and Evolution
description: Introduction to concepts and techniques in the genetics of behavior. Techniques include next gen sequencing, GWAS, and more. Students may use real data to analyze associations between genotype and phenotype. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only. (Fall only)

subject: ZOOL
title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology
description: Lectures, readings and presentations on sensory systems and behavior of fishes. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: ZOOL 430, ZOOL 606, BIOL 306, BIOL 465; or consent. Co-requisite: ZOOL 608L.

subject: ZOOL
title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology Laboratory
description: Laboratory study of fish sensory systems and behavior. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: ZOOL 430, ZOOL 606, BIOL 306, BIOL 465; or consent. Co-requisite: ZOOL 608.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Development and Reproductive Biology
description: Discussion and survey of literature on specific topics; some field and lab work may be required. Repeatable three times.

subject: ZOOL
title: Seminar on Science Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audiovisual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines. Repeatable one time. (Cross-listed as NSCI 619)

subject: ZOOL
title: Marine Ecology
description: Principles of ecology of marine biota and environment.
prerequisites: graduate standing in zoology, oceanography, or botany; or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Quantitative Field Ecology
description: Formal quantitative approach in identifying, designing, performing, analyzing, and interpreting ecological field problems. A-F only. (Alt. years)
prerequisites: ZOOL 439, ZOOL 439L, and ZOOL 631; or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Evolution in Marine Systems
description: Fundamental elements of modern evolutionary theory and research, with a strong focus on marine organisms and ecosystems. A-F only. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: ZOOL
title: Introduction to Statistical Modeling in Biology
description: Statisticalmethods for biological research. Covers: probability; likelihood-based inference; hypothesis testing; linear and generalized linear models; common statistical tests; statistical programming.
prerequisites: MATH 215 or 216 or 241 or 251A or NREM 203 (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Advanced Biometry
description: Multivariate statistical methods: multiple regression and correlation; multiway anova; general linear models; repeated measures and multivariate anova; loglinear analysis and logistic regression.

subject: ZOOL
title: Cellular Neurophysiology
description: Biophysical and membrane mechanisms of conduction, synaptic transmission, and other electrical responses of nerve cells. (Alt years: spring)

subject: ZOOL
title: Population Biology
description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology. (Cross-listed as BOT 652)
prerequisites: one of the following: ZOOL 620, ZOOL 623, BOT 456, NREM 680, PEPS 671; or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques. BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring) (Cross-listed as BOT 670)

subject: ZOOL
title: Conservation Biology
description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions. (Cross-listed as BOT 690 and NREM 690)

subject: ZOOL
title: Seminar in Zoology
description: Reports on research or reviews of literature. Graduate students required to take this or one

subject: PLAN
title: Policy Implementation and Program Evaluation
description: Implementation and evaluation in public policy analysis; philosophical and methodological issues; impact of policies and plans; use of evaluation research in program implementation.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Applied Geographic Information Systems: Public Policy and Spatial Analysis
description: Use of advanced and specialized spatial methods and models in urban and regional planning. Uses GIS software and builds upon 601. Skills are useful applied to planning, economic development, and environmental planning and resource management. Repeatable one time. Graduate students only or consent.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Research Methods
description: Advanced methods and deterministic and stochastic models used in urban and regional planning.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Collaboration Between Sectors
description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems. (Cross-listed as PACE 661)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations. A-F only. Graduate students only or departmental approval. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as PACE 668)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
description: Overview to the field of disaster management and humanitarian assistance with a specific focus on risk reduction. Includes background knowledge and skills for preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and adaptation to hazards and threats. Graduate students only or consent. (Once a year)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
description: Combined lecture/ discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and and planning. (Once a year) (Cross-listed as ERTH 604)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Humanitarian Assistance: Principles, Practices and Politics
description: Combined lecture/ discussion aimed at understanding the theoretical basis and working structure of humanitarian assistance programs and international responses to natural and human-induced disasters. (Once a year)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Information Systems for Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
description: Combined lecture/laboratory in disaster management focusing on essential methodological and practical issues that are involved in spatial analyses using GIS and other information technologies to inform decision making related to natural hazards, disasters, and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning activities.
prerequisites: PLAN 473 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Disaster Recovery: Theory and Practice
description: How do communities recover from disaster? Provides students with an overview of recovery theory and an understanding of how planners, policy makers, and ordinary citizens rebuild communities, cities, and nations following catastrophic events. A-F only. Graduate standing only.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy. (Cross-listed as ARCH 628)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures. Graduate students only or consent. (Cross-listed as ANTH 676 and ARCH 676)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Historic Preservation Planning
description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building. (Cross-listed as ARCH 677)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Site Planning
description: Fundamental principles that guide site planning, including planning and design determinants of the site taking into account its regional context, site-specific characteristics and applicable codes, ordinances, and standards. PLAN and ARCH majors only. (Fall only)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Land Use Management and Control
description: Survey course of public land use management. (Cross-listed as LAW 580)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises. LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only. Graduate students only. A-F only. (Crosslisted as ARCH 682)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
prerequisites: consent of instructor and department chair
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Thesis Research
description: Limited to MURP students under Plan A. Repeatable unlimited times.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Homeland Security: Terrorism
description: Combined lecture/discussion in disaster management and humanitarian assistance track focusing on developing a multidisciplinary understanding of international terrorism and anti-terrorism planning and response. (Once a year)
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Seminar in Planning Theory
description: Special topics in theory, history, analysis.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Seminar in Planning Practice
description: Project planning, programming, and similar topics.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Practicum
description: Team experience in defining and addressing a current planning problem; identification, substantive review, research design, preparation and presentation of analysis. Topic varies. Limited to 10 students.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Directed Project
description: Individual project in analysis, plan preparation and evaluation, and policy/ program evaluation. PLAN majors only.
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Design Studio
description: Group experience in defining urban and regional design problems and potentials, developing and evaluating alternatives, formulating strategies for implementation. PLAN and ARCH majors only. A-F only.
prerequisites: (PLAN 600 and 601) with a minimum grade of B, or consent
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: PLAN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Repeatable unlimited times. S/U only. PhD student only.
degrees: PhD in Urban and Regional Planning
department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

subject: URDU
title: Reading and Writing in Urdu
description: Introduces students to the Nastaliq (Urdu) script, alphabets, their various forms, and combination rules. Reading and writing is emphasized. A-F only. (Fall only)
prerequisites: HNDI 102 or consent. Co-requisite: HNDI 201 or consent.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Elementary Vietnamese I
description: HSL Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets one hour, three times a week.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Elementary Vietnamese II
description: HSL Continuation of 101.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Intermediate Vietnamese I
description: HSL Continuation of 102. After completion, most students should be able to use all major sentence patterns to produce sounds, combinations of sounds, tones, and intonation and have some understanding of Vietnamese culture.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Intermediate Vietnamese II
description: HSL Continuation of 201.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Third-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of 202. Emphasis on increased proficiency and cultural understanding through interaction with Vietnamese media, including newspapers, radio, film, etc.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Third-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of 301.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Fourth-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of 302. Emphasis on cultural understanding through modern literary Vietnamese.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Fourth-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of 401.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Introduction to Vietnamese Literature
description: DL Selected readings in major genres; emphasis on analysis. Modern literature.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: VIET
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times.
department: Department of Indo-Pacific Languages and Literatures

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to LGBTQ+ Studies
description: DH Introduction to a survey of the key terms, texts, and histories of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities with special attention to Hawai‘i and Oceania. A-F only
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
description: FGA Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E. (Cross-listed as REL 149)
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
description: DS Introduction to feminist scholarship and methods across a range of academic disciplines; historical and cross-cultural perspectives on women's experiences and status in family, work, and society.
department: Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies

subject: THEA
title: Musical Theatre Dance Forms
description: DA. Theatrical dance forms used in 20th-century musical theatre. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as DNCE 439)
prerequisites: 100 level or above dance technique class, 421, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Topics in Costume Construction
description: DA. Costume production techniques, both Western and Asian, for theatre and dance. Topic rotation includes: understructures and armatures, patterning, tailoring, dyeing, fabric modification, millenery and crafts, within the context of current industry practice. Repeatable two times. A-F only. (Cross-listed as DNCE 446)

subject: THEA
title: Stage Management
description: Business, organization and management for theatre and dance productions.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design for the Theatre
description: Basic concepts and techniques of 2D computer-aided design. Lecture/ workshop covers language and commands common to most CAD packages with a focus on drafting specific to theatre. A laptop with Vectorworks installed is required. (Once a year)

subject: THEA
title: Costumes II: Intermediate Costume Design
description: DA. Advanced costume design for theatre and dance. Introduction to collaborative process in costume. Intensive work on rendering skills, applied to various design problems. Cost analysis and organizational techniques. (Cross-listed as DNCE 456)

subject: THEA
title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
description: DH. Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawai‘i, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand. (Cross-listed as PACS 462)

subject: THEA
title: Drama and Theatre of Southeast Asia and India
description: DH. Court, folk, popular traditions, and the manner of their production.

subject: THEA
title: Drama and Theatre of China
description: DH. Yuan, southern, spoken drama; Beijing opera and the manner of their production.

subject: THEA
title: Drama and Theatre of Japan
description: DH. Survey of Japanese theatre forms, from traditional to contemporary. Includes examination of dramatic texts, performance elements, and historical context, utilizing written, aural, and visual materials.
prerequisites: Junior standing or above. 311 or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Drama and Theatre of Hawai‘i
description: DH. Survey of indigenous theatre forms of Hawai‘i, Native Hawaiian, and other ethnic playwrights, and contemporary multicultural landscape of drama and theatre in Hawai‘i. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: THEA
title: Chinese Music and Sound Culture
description: DH. Situates the Chinese musical sound in the interdisciplinary field of sound culture. Students will learn to read music literature and listen to historical sounds critically and to analyze aspects of Chinese sound culture. (Cross-listed as MUS 469)

subject: THEA
title: Creative Drama
description: DA. Dramatic activities for young people. For teachers, group workers, recreation majors, and others dealing with children. Supervised field activities.

subject: THEA
title: Masked Performance
description: DA. History, techniques, construction, and performance of theatrical masks. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Junior standing or higher. 221 or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Storytelling
description: DA. Storytelling development through focused activities on personal artistic practice, story content, and public performative techniques. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Theatre for Young Audiences
description: DA. Theories and principles of formal theatre for young audiences. Study of and practice in the selection, direction, and production of plays.

subject: THEA
title: Puppetry for Young Children
description: DA. Methods of constructing puppets and stages with and for children 3 to 8 years of age. Use of puppets in the creative arts. Fieldwork.

subject: THEA
title: Puppetry
description: DA. History and scope of puppetry. Construction and presentation of puppets for adult and child audiences. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Giant Puppetry
description: DA. History, construction, and performance techniques for large-scale and giant puppets. For teachers, recreation directors, and others working with students aged 10 to 18 and adults

subject: THEA
title: Hula Ki‘i: Hawaiian Puppetry and Image Dancing
description: DA. History, techniques, construction, and performance of Hawaiian puppetry and traditional image dancing. Repeatable one time.

subject: THEA
title: Intermediate Directing
description: DA. Workshop; students direct one-act plays. Repeatable one time with consent. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Experimental Theatre Studio
description: DA. Working collectively, students research, write, design, develop, and perform a full-length production. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: 6 credits above the 200 level in acting, directing, playwriting, dancing; or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Topics in Drama and Theatre
description: (B) theatre traditions; (D) contemporary theatre. Repeatable two times each for (B) and (D).

subject: THEA
title: Directed Work
description: Individual projects; tutorial. Repeatable two times.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Theatre Research
description: Bibliography and research methods; preparation for thesis and dissertation writing. Required of many graduate theatre majors.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Major Theatre Theory
description: Major theatre theories from antiquity to the present and across a broad range of cultures. Repeatable one time with consent. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Theatre in Europe: Classical to 1700
description: Theatre as a cultural and social institution in the West, from ancient Greece to Restoration England. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Theatre in Europe and the U.S., 1700-Present
description: Theatre as a cultural and social institution in Europe and the U.S., from the 18th century to the present. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Topics in Dramaturgy
description: (B) role of the dramaturg; covers history, theory, and practice; (C) dramaturgy workshop; accompanies specific Kennedy Theatre productions. Repeatable one time per alpha. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Performance Theory
description: Introduction to key texts and concepts of performance studies. (Cross-listed as DNCE 615)

subject: THEA
title: Script Analysis
description: Theory and practical application of script analysis with reference to dramatic texts from various cultural traditions.

subject: THEA
title: Seminar in Performance Studies
description: Special topics. Repeatable up to two times when topics change. (Cross-listed as DNCE 617)

subject: THEA
title: Digital Multimedia Tools for Performance Research
description: A-F only. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: Dance, Theatre, Music Majors only. consent.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Topics: Playwriting and Dramatic Theory
description: Readings, research, writing, and seminar discussions.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Voice for the Actor
description: Training at advanced level in speaking and vocal skills and techniques in preparation for a solo performance. Repeatable one time. A-F only. (Alt. years)

subject: THEA
title: Great Roles in Acting
description: Great roles from the Western theatre repertory; focus on the individual actor and performance styles. Repeatable one time with consent.

subject: THEA
title: Experimental Asian Acting
description: Integration of movement, vocal technique, and concepts of traditional Asian genres into the actor’s repertory. Exploration of application to contemporary Asian and non-Asian texts. Workshop format. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: THEA and DNCE majors only. consent.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Topics in Performance
description: Readings, discussion, research, and/or performance work. Repeatable two times, up to nine credits. (Cross-listed as DNCE 626)
prerequisites: THEA and DNCE majors only. consent.

subject: THEA
title: Taiji Weapons for Actors
description: Advanced level Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) weapons training. Repeatable two times.

subject: THEA
title: Historic Costume and Decor
description: Overview of visual styles in fashion, textiles, architecture, ornament, and furniture for production and entertainment design through lecture, lab, and discussion.

subject: THEA
title: Lighting II: Intermediate Lighting Design
description: Workshop in intermediate techniques and skills of lighting design; storytelling, analysis, research, envisioning, and communicating a design plan, execution of successful design projects. Use of communication tools such as mini-plots, light renderings, LightWright, and VectorWorks. Repeatable one time.
prerequisites: 345 (with a minimum grade of B) or equivalent experience.

subject: THEA
title: Lighting III: Advanced Lighting Design
description: Workshop dealing with special topics in theatrical lighting design and related skills. Repeatable two times.
prerequisites: THEA or DNCE majors only. 644 or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Professional Advancement in Entertainment Design
description: Directed study designed to help MFA candidates in Design acquire the tools helpful in obtaining future employment. Portfolios, resumes, and related application tools will be developed along with other necessary skills. Repeatable six times.
prerequisites: Must be current MFA candidate in theatre. THEA majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: THEA
title: Scenic II: Intermediate Scene Design
description: Workshop in advanced techniques and skills of scenic design; research, presentation, rendering, drafting, and model making.
prerequisites: 353 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Scenic III: Advanced Scenic Design
description: Workshop dealing with special topics in scenic design, related skills, and portfolio preparation. Repeatable two times.

subject: TPSS
title: Nursery Management
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices in production and operations of commercial nurseries in Hawai‘i.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems. Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only. Junior standing or higher.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as BIOL 430 and BOT 430)
prerequisites: (BOT 201, BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens. (Spring only) (Cross-listed as BIOL 430L and BOT 430L)
prerequisites: (BOT 430 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Environmental Soil Chemistry
description: Study of soil chemical processes such as weathering, adsorption, precipitation, and ion exchange; causes of soil acidity, alkalinity, and salinity; reactions between soils and fertilizers, pesticides, or heavy metals. Management strategies to minimize environmental contamination by nitrate, phosphate, and trace elements such as As, Pb, and Se. A-F only. (Fall only)
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Tissue Culture/Transformation
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of plant tissue culture for plant scientists; study of the growth and development of plant tissues in culture as influenced by chemical and environmental factors, and the regeneration of plants following plant transformation by biolistics and other molecular approaches.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Sustainable Nutrient Management in Agroecosystems
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Biological, chemical, and physical processes governing the cycling of nutrients in agroecosystems, crop and livestock production, and the effects on surrounding unmanaged ecosystems. (Cross-listed as NREM 460)
prerequisites: (TPSS 304 and CHEM 161) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Breeding and Genetics
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Unique aspects of plant genetics and applications to crop improvement, with emphasis on breeding plants in Hawai‘i.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Soil Plant Environment
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Bio-physical processes in the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum that influence crop growth and development. Methods to estimate the impact of soil and climate on crop performance. Use of crop models to simulate effects of planting date, plant spacing and density, fertilizer rate, rainfall or irrigation, and daily weather on crop yield and farm income.
prerequisites: TPSS 304 and either PHYS 151 or PHYS 170, or consent.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
title: Irrigation and Water Management
description: Basic soil-water-plant relationships, irrigation water requirements, irrigation efficiencies, different methods of irrigation, planning, design and management of an irrigation system, fertigation and impact of irrigation on soil and water quality. (Alt. years) (Cross-listed as NREM 463)
prerequisites: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and NREM/TPSS 304 (or equivalent), or consent.
department: Department of Tropical Plant and Soil Sciences
college: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources

subject: TPSS
